> ### 1. Repo bootstrap (main loop, Phase 0)
> 1. `git init -b main`, then `git config user.name "Kristiyan Dimitrov"` and `git config user.email kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com` (repo-local).
> 2. `.gitignore`: `.temp/ .DS_Store .vscode/ .venv/ __pycache__/ .*_cache/ .coverage htmlcov/ node_modules/ frontend/.next/ frontend/out/ frontend/test-results/ frontend/playwright-report/ evals/data/private/ .env`. `evals/data/private/` holds gold bodies, raw HTML, FPB zip and HF caches.
> 3. `LICENSE`: MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Kristiyan Dimitrov".
> 4. Run `gh auth status` and confirm the active account is cleverjobs. Then `gh repo create cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics --public -d "..."` (no `--source`), then `git remote add origin [redacted-email]:cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics.git`, then `git push -u origin main`.
> 5. Every milestone commit message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
> 6. Declare every Python and Node dependency up front, then run `uv lock` and `pnpm install` once. This makes the Phase 2 parallel agents safe.
> 7. `scripts/check.py` is the single gate command. `--fast` runs ruff, `ruff format --check`, mypy, unit pytest and `pnpm lint typecheck test`. `--full` adds integration tests, `pnpm build` and the openapi/type drift checks.
> 
> ### 2. Native setup (`scripts/dev_setup.py`)
> - `stop-containers`: run `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'` and append the names, with a timestamp, to `.temp/setup/stopped-containers.txt`. Then `docker stop` all of them. Eight are running today.
> - `restart-containers` reads that file and runs `docker start` on each name.
> - `native`:
>   - `brew install ollama`. Stable is 0.40.4, which meets the >= 0.40.4 requirement for decision models.
>   - `brew services start ollama`. The formula's service already sets `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` and `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`. The script verifies this with `launchctl print`.
>   - `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=3` is applied with `launchctl setenv` followed by `brew services restart`. This does not survive a reboot, so the script re-applies it idempotently.
>   - keep_alive is sent per request by the app (`VT_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m`).
> - `pull --set {serve,ci,eval}` pulls the model lists from `env/*.txt` and prints the disk delta.
> 
> ### 3. Docker
> - **`docker/app.Dockerfile`** has three stages:
>   1. `node:24-alpine` with corepack pnpm builds the static export to `out/`.
>   2. `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim` runs `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package veritrade-backend`.
>   3. `python:3.13-slim-bookworm` copies `.venv` and `out` to `/app/static`, runs as a non-root user, and starts `uvicorn veritrade.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`.
>   - The healthcheck is the `veritrade-healthcheck` console script, so no inline Python is needed.
> - **`compose.yaml`**:
>   - `app`:
>     - Has both `build` and `image: veritrade-app:${TAG:-local}`, and publishes `8000:8000`.
>     - `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=${OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}`, `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway`.
>     - Passes `VT_MODEL_ALLOWLIST` and `SEC_USER_AGENT`.
>     - `depends_on: {ollama-pull: {condition: service_completed_successfully, required: false}}`.
>   - `ollama` (profile `bundled`):
>     - Image `ollama/ollama:0.40.5`, named volume `ollama-models:/root/.ollama`.
>     - Environment: keep_alive 30m, max loaded models 2, flash attention, q8_0 KV cache.
>     - Healthcheck `["CMD","ollama","list"]`. No host port, to avoid clashing with native :11434 and to avoid exposing Ollama.
>   - `ollama-pull` (profile `bundled`): same image, `OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434`, runs `/scripts/ollama-pull.sh` over the comma-separated `VT_PULL_MODELS`, `restart: "no"`.
>   - `env/bundled.env` sets `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434` and `VT_PULL_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-<R8 winners>}`.
> - **`compose.gpu.yaml`**: adds a `deploy.resources.reservations.devices` nvidia/all/[gpu] block to `ollama`.
> - **`compose.e2e.yaml`**:
>   - `fixture-site`: `nginx:1.27-alpine` serves `backend/tests/fixtures/skeletons` read-only, with network alias `fixtures.local`.
>   - The app runs with `VT_ENV=test`, `VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS=fixtures.local` and the CI allowlist.
>   - The ollama volume is a bind mount to `${OLLAMA_CACHE_DIR}` so `actions/cache` can save it.
>   - `settings.py` refuses to start if `VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS` is set while `VT_ENV != test`.
> 
> ### 4. Test strategy per altitude
> 
> | Altitude | Where | What (PoC-balanced) |
> |---|---|---|
> | BE unit | `backend/tests/unit/` | **Extractors** (`test_extract.py`): every skeleton x {jsonld, profile, density, cascade} x 4 parsers must reach `VTB` body-marker recall >= 0.9 with zero `VTX` leakage. JSON-LD cases are skipped when `expected.jsonld_body` is false. Third-party extractors get a smoke test only (non-empty, no exception). **`test_skeleton_purity.py`**: every text node matches the synthetic vocabulary. **`test_ssrf.py`**: schemes; v4/v6 private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA and v4-mapped addresses; DNS resolving to a private IP through an injected resolver; per-hop redirect checks; redirect cap; size cap; content type; the test-allow env refused outside test. **`test_detect.py`**: Yahoo consent form, Cloudflare/DataDome challenges and paywall markers each map to the typed error with its hint. The reject-all POST is checked with respx and the cookie cached. **`test_prompts.py`**: golden files in `unit/golden/prompts/<id>.txt`, untrusted-content fencing, lede vs full truncation, both field orders. **`test_policies.py`**: logprob threshold, ordinal \|score\| threshold, decision probabilities, neutral-first ties, `abstained`. **`test_stream_parser.py`**: 6 canned payloads split at every byte offset (escapes, unicode, both orders, malformed input). **`test_schemas.py`**: models, allowlist, enums, SSE event payloads, plus `export_openapi.py --check`. |
> | BE integration | `backend/tests/integration/` | Runs `httpx.AsyncClient(ASGITransport)` with `asgi-lifespan`. **respx** mocks publisher hosts and lets the fake Ollama pass through (`respx.route(host="127.0.0.1").pass_through()`). The resolver is overridden with a static public-IP map. **Fake Ollama** is a Starlette app on a uvicorn thread (session fixture, random port) serving `/api/chat` (stream and non-stream), `/v1/systemone`, `/api/tags`, `/api/version` and `/api/embed` from cassettes, with a configurable chunk delay. Each cassette stores `prompt_sha256`; a mismatch fails with "run scripts/record_cassettes.py". **Cases**: signal (decision and generative models); summary and analyze, both JSON and SSE; event order `meta -> sentiment -> summary_delta* -> done`; single-flight (2 concurrent requests, 1 upstream hit); result-cache hit; typed errors mapped to status codes; model outside the allowlist returns 422; Ollama down returns 503; health; models endpoint merges `/api/tags`. |
> | BE coverage | CI | `--cov=veritrade --cov-fail-under=75` |
> | FE unit | `frontend/tests/unit` | Vitest + RTL + jsdom: `lib/sse.ts` chunk splitting; SentimentBadge (including abstained), TimingBreakdown, Parser/Extractor selects, ErrorBanner per typed error. |
> | FE integration | `frontend/tests/integration` | MSW 3 `setupServer` with handlers in `src/mocks/handlers.ts`. SSE is streamed through a `ReadableStream`. Checks that sentiment renders before the summary completes, that done timings appear, errors, model dropdown contents, and the Benchmarks page rendered from `public/benchmarks`. `pnpm gen:api --check` (openapi-typescript) catches contract drift. |
> | E2E | `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts` | Playwright chromium against the compose stack on :8000. Specs: analyze happy path, signal-only with the tiny decision model, consent fixture shows the `consent_required` banner, extractor switch. Assertions are model-agnostic: schema, event order, one of 3 labels or abstained, non-empty summary, timings. |
> | Live smoke | `backend/tests/live` (`-m live`, excluded by default) | For each source, take the newest RSS/listing item from `live/sources.toml` and run the production fetcher plus cascade. Expect >= 150 words and no typed block error. No LLM. |
> 
> ### 5. Skeleton capture (`scripts/capture_skeletons.py`)
> - Input: one URL per source from the probe output.
> - Fetches once live, then rewrites with lxml:
>   - Removes script and style contents (JSON-LD is kept, with its text fields synthesized) and comments.
>   - Body paragraphs, located by the per-domain profile and cross-checked with trafilatura, become prose-like synthetic sentences of the same length carrying `VTB-k` markers. All other text becomes `VTX-k`.
>   - `alt`, `title` and `aria-*` values are synthesized. `href` and `src` point to `https://example.invalid/`.
>   - Classes, ids and `data-*` attributes are kept.
> - Writes `.expected.json` with: source, captured_at, url_sha256, headline marker, body markers, `jsonld_body`, profile.
> - Also captures the Yahoo consent page and any challenge page it meets.
> - Prints per-source marker stats; an Opus agent spot-checks one fixture per source.
> 
> ### 6. GitHub Actions
> **`ci.yml`** runs on push and PR. It has `concurrency: ${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress.
> - `backend`:
>   - `astral-sh/setup-uv` (enable-cache, glob `uv.lock`), then `uv sync --all-packages --frozen`, then `uv run python scripts/check.py --backend --full`.
>   - Then `export_transcript.py --scan-only` as a regression guard.
> - `frontend`: `pnpm/action-setup` and `setup-node@v4` (Node 24, `cache: pnpm`, `cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`), then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, gen:api check, lint, typecheck, `vitest run`, build.
> - `e2e` (needs both, `timeout-minutes: 30`):
>   1. Free disk by removing dotnet, ghc and android directories. The runner has 14 GB; the ollama image, about 2 GB of models, the app image and chromium fit after this.
>   2. `docker/build-push-action` with `load: true` and `cache-from/to: type=gha,mode=max`.
>   3. `actions/cache` for `~/.ollama-ci`, keyed on `ollama-0.40.5-${{ hashFiles('env/ci-models.txt') }}`, and for `~/.cache/ms-playwright`.
>   4. `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml --profile bundled up -d`, then `docker compose wait ollama-pull`, then poll `/api/health`, then send one warm-up `/api/signal`.
>   5. `pnpm exec playwright test`.
>   6. Run `sudo chown -R` on the model dir before the cache post-step.
>   7. On failure, upload the report and `compose logs`.
> 
> **`live-smoke.yml`** runs on `schedule: '23 5 * * *'` and `workflow_dispatch`. It is a single uv job that writes a results table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. It is never a required check, and runner-IP blocks are labelled informational.
> 
> ### 7. Probe (`scripts/probe_sources.py`, first real step)
> - Built on `veritrade/fetch/{headers,detect}.py`, written in Phase 1 and later reused by the fetcher.
> - Covers the 10 candidate sources plus the 4 backups. For each it fetches the RSS or section page and 2 recent articles over http2 with the browser header set.
> - Records: status, final URL, typed detection, latency, JSON-LD presence, word estimate, and 2 article URLs. No text is stored.
> - Outputs `evals/data/source_probe.json` and `.context/docs/design/02-source-probe.md`, which states the final top 10.
> 
> ### 8. Transcript export (`scripts/export_transcript.py`, very last step)
> 1. **Collect** from `--projects-root` (default `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, otherwise `~/.claude4/projects`), folder `-~-veritrade-analytics/`:
>    - `0024648c-....jsonl`
>    - `0024648c-.../subagents/**`: agent JSONL, meta and workflow `journal.jsonl`
>    - `0024648c-.../workflows/*.json` and `workflows/scripts/*.js`
>    - Excluded: `tool-results/` and other sessions.
> 2. **Filter by allowlist** into `.temp/transcript/staging/`:
>    - Record types: `user, assistant, system{turn_duration,informational,away_summary}, mode, permission-mode, custom-title, ai-title, agent-name`.
>    - Attachments: `plan_mode, ultra_effort_enter, model, date, skill_mention, queued_command`.
>    - Everything else is dropped, including `api request blob`, `instructions`, `session context`, `credential_org`, hooks, listings and `cost-state`. Usage is harvested before dropping.
>    - Thinking `signature` is stripped. `[system reminder]` blocks are stripped from user and tool_result text. Image and document blocks become `[omitted]`.
> 3. **Redact**:
>    - `~` becomes `~`, and the project slug becomes `<project>`.
>    - Every email except `kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com` and `noreply@anthropic.com` is replaced.
>    - Secret regexes: `sk-`, `gh[pousr]_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, `-----BEGIN`, `xox[bp]-`, `eyJ` JWT-like strings.
>    - Terms from a gitignored `.temp/transcript/denylist.txt`. Seed it with the work domain and the stopped container/project names, which appear in tool output.
> 4. **Render**: `uvx claude-code-log@1.7.0` on the staging copy, producing HTML and MD into `.context/transcript/rendered/`.
> 5. **`meta.json`**:
>    - Harness: Claude Code 2.1.301.
>    - Model set from `message.model`: `claude-opus-5-5`. Effort xhigh, ultracode true, plan_mode true.
>    - Skills, workflows (run id, name, agent count), and subagents (type, model).
>    - Token usage deduped by keeping the last record per `(file, message.id)` (up to 4 per id were seen), summed per model, and cross-checked against `cost-state`.
>    - Date range and redaction counts.
> 6. **Gate**: zero hits across staging, rendered output and meta for `~`, `kristiyandimitrov`, the redacted emails, denylist terms, secret regexes, `api request blob`, `session context`, `"instructions"`, `system reminder`, and any file over 50 MB. Any hit exits 1 with file:line. Only then are files moved to `.context/transcript/{raw,rendered,meta.json,README.md}`. After that: commit and push.

> ### 9. README outline
> 1. What and why
> 2. Quickstart: native Mac, bundled, GPU, dev mode
> 3. Architecture and endpoints, with the SSE protocol
> 4. Design decisions and latency trade-offs
> 5. Measured latency vs R7 budgets, including the Pareto knee, labelled by backend
> 6. Sentiment eval: F0.5, inversions, abstention
> 7. Summary eval

> 9. Security and scraping ethics

> ### 10. Orchestration (build sequence)
> Every `agent()` call sets `model: 'opus'`. Each agent brief lists the paths it owns and the paths it may not touch (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and other agents' paths), plus the coding rules. Each agent reports back: files changed, dependencies it needs, open issues. The main loop commits after every gate.
> 
> | Phase | Units | Mode | Gate / commit |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | P0 | Bootstrap; deps declared and locked; contracts (`schemas.py`, `Extractor`/`LLMClient` Protocols, `openapi.json`); ci.yml backend and frontend jobs; `dev_setup stop-containers` + `native` + model pulls (in the background) | main loop | `check.py --fast`, push M0 |
> | P1 | Probe | 1 agent | Design doc 02 with >= 10 usable sources, M1 |
> | P2 | (a) `fetch/` (b) `extract/` + skeleton capture (c) `llm/` + fake Ollama + recorder (d) `frontend/` against the contract and MSW (e) `evals` loaders and metrics | 5 agents in parallel, shared tree, file-disjoint | `check.py --fast`, M2 |
> | P3 | (a) `api/`, `main.py`, caches, integration tests, cassettes (b) R5 article-set sub-workflow (labellers isolated from each other, then adjudicator) writing `evals/data/articles/` | 2 parallel | `--full`, plus one manual analyze per source on native Ollama, M3 |
> | P4 | (a) Docker, compose, CI e2e, Playwright (b) accuracy evals: prompt grid, knobs, scope, field order, extraction matrix accuracy (c) gold bodies and the Opus summary judge on finalists from (b) | (a) runs in a worktree on branch `ci/e2e`, iterates by pushing, then is squash-merged into main; (b) and (c) run in the main tree | CI and e2e green on main (`gh run watch`), M4 |
> | P5 | Latency benchmarks, holdout once, freeze, `public/benchmarks`, design docs, README | Exclusive: no Docker builds or other agents running | Budgets reported, M5 |
> | P6 | Verification checklist, then transcript export | main loop | Scan gate, M6, push |
> 
> ### 11. End-to-end verification checklist
> 1. `git log` shows the correct author and trailer on every commit, and `git status` is clean.
> 2. `check.py --full` passes.
> 3. Native path: `brew services list` shows ollama running; `docker compose up -d`; `/api/health` reports `backend=native-metal`; analyze succeeds on one URL per source; typed errors are recorded.
> 4. Bundled path: `--profile bundled --env-file env/bundled.env` comes up healthy and one analyze succeeds.
> 5. Latency budget script prints p50 against the R7 budgets.
> 6. `ci.yml` is green on HEAD. `gh workflow run live-smoke.yml` was dispatched once and its result noted.
> 7. `git ls-files` contains nothing from `evals/data/private`, and the skeleton purity test passes.
> 8. All README links resolve.
> 9. Remind the user that `dev_setup restart-containers` exists.
> 10. Transcript export is the very last step.
> 
> ### Open details I defaulted
> - CI tiny decision model is `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` with scope=lede. If it is unusable, e2e tests the signal endpoint with the generative model only.
> - E2E fixtures depend on JSON-LD and generic cascade. Per-domain profiles are covered only in unit tests, because the e2e host is `fixtures.local`.
> - The bundled profile uses `env/bundled.env`, since a compose profile cannot change app env by itself. The ollama service publishes no host port.
> - Backend coverage floor is 75. The frontend is reported only.
> - OpenAPI plus openapi-typescript drift checks are the contract gate.
> - `.context/openai-research.md` and the brief are committed.
> - The final export and push turns will not appear in the exported transcript. This is stated in the transcript README.
> - The claude-code-log MD flag needs to be checked with `--help` at build time.
> - CI workflow iteration happens on a temporary branch that is squash-merged, so main still gets milestone commits only.
> 
> ### Risks
> - **Env name collision**: `OLLAMA_MODELS` is also Ollama's own storage-dir variable. Passing it to the `ollama` service would move model storage, which is why it is mapped to `VT_PULL_MODELS`.
> - **Linux native path**: Ollama listens on 127.0.0.1 by default, so `host-gateway` cannot reach it. It needs `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`.
> - **Docker Desktop memory**: the VM has 15.6 GiB, and clef-flash alone is 11 GB, so the bundled models must stay at or below ~10 GB.
> - **CI runner limits**: disk and RAM are tight, model pulls are slow on a cold cache, and the GitHub cache limit is 10 GB.
> - **Live smoke results are noisy**: runner IPs get blocked differently from the user's IP.
> - **Transcript size and privacy**: subagent JSONL may push files toward the 50 MB gate, and redaction still needs a manual skim of the rendered HTML.
> - **Latency noise**: concurrent agents or Docker builds would skew P5 numbers, which is why that phase runs alone.
>

### Verdict

The three sections each work on their own but don't fit together.
- **Biggest gaps:**
  - The transcript would leak publisher text.
  - Serving config and thresholds have three competing sources, and evals uses a different Ollama code path, which would invalidate the claim that evals measure the served system.
  - The Delivery build order breaks Q7 (freeze before holdout) and R5 (gold bodies before labellers).
- **Biggest over-scope:** Evals ignores the trimmed roster: a 13-model screen and 6 hours of compute against a PoC principle. Delivery adds a cassette recorder and a GPU compose file that cannot be verified here.
- **Checked against settled decisions:** Q1-Q20 and R1-R10 are otherwise covered. The partial ones are Q1 (backend labels), Q3 (label-token), Q15 (Prettier), R3 (summary-first ordering), R6 (lead-fact), R7 (early sanity gate), R8 (exact restart command), R10 (decisions doc and backlog list), all fixed above.
- **Suggested merge:** use Delivery's phase table as the master sequence, Architecture's module and contract layout, and Evals' metrics and Opus pipeline, cut to the trimmed roster.

### Open details I defaulted
- Naming picks in fix 2.
- Status codes: 400 for `model_not_allowed`, 503 for `llm_unreachable`.
- `top_logprobs=20`.
- tev1 default thresholds: ordinal t=1, decision min_p=0.5.
- docker-cpu latency sample: n=10, winners only.
- Live smoke weekly.
- Fallback `benchmarks.sample.json`.
- 12-word shingle redaction gate.

### Risks
- The tokenizer may make label first tokens ambiguous, forcing the score-sign fallback.
- Grammar may ignore property order, which makes the field-order dimension moot.
- Small article sets give wide CIs.
- Docker Desktop restarts can revive containers with restart policies.
- FPB and tweet text can reach the transcript through the error pass; the shingle gate covers FPB.
- Brew Ollama 0.40.4 vs container 0.40.5 drift; record versions with the benchmarks.

  Evals import `veritrade.fetch/extract/prompts/inference` directly, so evals and the server run the same code. Only the end-to-end latency suite goes through HTTP.
  
  ### 2. Backend modules
  
  - **config.py**: `Settings(BaseSettings, env_prefix="VT_")`. Fields:
    - `ollama_base_url` (also reads `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`), `ollama_models` (CSV restriction), `sec_user_agent`
    - Timeouts: connect 3 s, read 6 s, deadline 8 s. Limits: `max_body_bytes` 5 MB, `max_redirects` 5
    - Cache TTLs, `cors_origins=[]`, `static_dir`, `ssrf_host_allowlist=[]` (CI only)
  - **models_registry.py**: loads `models.toml` into `ModelSpec(name, kind: generative|decision, endpoints, num_ctx, max_input_tokens, policy, threshold)` plus a default model per endpoint. `resolve(endpoint, model|None)` raises `ModelNotAllowed`.
  - **errors.py**: `VtError(code, http_status, message, hint, retryable)`. Codes: `invalid_url, blocked_destination, source_blocked, paywalled, consent_required, upstream_timeout, upstream_http, unsupported_content, too_large, extraction_empty, model_not_allowed, model_unavailable, inference_timeout, schema_violation`.
  
  **fetch/**
  - `ssrf.check_target(url)`: accepts http/https only, ports 80/443, no userinfo. It resolves every A/AAAA record with `getaddrinfo` and rejects any address that is not `is_global` (this also catches IPv4-mapped v6). It runs on the initial URL and again on every redirect hop.
  - `client.Fetcher.get(url) -> FetchResult(final_url, status, html, timings)`:
    - one `httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, follow_redirects=False, limits=Limits(100, 20))`
    - manual redirect loop, streamed body with a byte cap, HTML content-type gate
  - `headers.py`: a standard Chrome header set (UA, Accept, Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding gzip/br, Sec-Fetch-*). For `sec.gov`, the UA is replaced with `SEC_USER_AGENT`.
  - `consent.py` (Yahoo):
    - On a redirect to `consent.yahoo.com` or `guce.yahoo.com`, parse the form, POST "reject all", keep the cookies in the client jar, and retry the original request once.
    - If that fails, raise `ConsentRequired`.
  - `detect.classify(resp, html)`:
    - 401/403/429 or challenge markers (cf-chl, captcha, DataDome, PerimeterX) raise `SourceBlocked`.
    - JSON-LD `isAccessibleForFree:false`, or a profile paywall selector plus a short body, raises `Paywalled`.
  - `cache.SingleFlightCache[K,V]`:
    - OrderedDict LRU + TTL, plus an in-flight `dict[K, asyncio.Task]`; waiters `await asyncio.shield(task)`.
    - Typed source errors get a 60 s negative TTL. Other errors are not cached.
  
  **extract/**
  - `dom.py`: a `Dom` protocol (`select, text, attr, remove, iter_blocks, json_ld`) implemented by `SelectolaxDom`, `LxmlDom` (cssselect) and `BsDom(html.parser|lxml)`.
  - Own strategies run on `Dom`, so each one works with all 4 parsers (16 matrix cells):
    - `jsonld` (articleBody)
    - `profiles` (`DomainProfile(domains, body, drop, lede, paywall)` for the 10 sources + backups; selectors filled from probe output)
    - `density` (text/link density)
    - `cascade` (jsonld if ≥400 chars, then profile, then density)
  - `third_party.py`: lazy-imported trafilatura {default, favor_precision}, readability-lxml, newspaper4k, justext and strip-tags. These ignore the parser, so their matrix cells are N/A.
  - `registry.extract(html, url, parser, extractor) -> Article(title, paragraphs, published_at, method, parse_ms, extract_ms)`.
  - `scope.build_input(article, scope, cap)`:
    - lede = title + paragraphs up to about 200 tokens; full = title + body
    - cap = min(request cap, model `max_input_tokens`); tokens estimated as chars/4
  
  **prompts/registry.get(endpoint, model) -> PromptSpec(version, system, user_template, criteria, schema_variant)**
  - Stored as TOML per (endpoint, model slug), with `active="vN"`, versioned tables and a `default` fallback.
  - `prompt_version = "{endpoint}/{model}/{vN}@{sha8}"`, so cache keys change whenever the content changes.
  
  **inference/**
  - `schemas.py`: `OrdinalOut(score -2..2)`, `LabelOut(label)`, `SummaryOut`, `AnalyzeSentimentFirst(score, entity, summary)`, `AnalyzeSummaryFirst(...)`. Their `model_json_schema()` is passed as Ollama's `format`.
  - `ollama_chat.OllamaChat` (httpx, its own pool, no SSRF guard):
    - `complete(...) -> ChatResult(content, logprobs, ollama_timings)` and `stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[str]`
    - every call sends `think:false, format, options{temperature:0, seed, num_ctx, num_predict}, keep_alive:"30m"`
    - non-streaming label calls add `logprobs:true, top_logprobs:5`
    - a client disconnect closes the Ollama stream
  - `ollama_decision.DecisionClient.decide(model, state, spec) -> DecisionResult(choice, probabilities, confidence, usage, wall_ms)`: httpx `POST /v1/systemone`, criteria in the order neutral, bullish, bearish.
  - `adapters.py`:
    - `SignalAdapter.classify -> RawSignal`, implemented by `DecisionSignal`, `OrdinalSignal`, `LabelLogprobSignal`
    - `Summarizer.complete/stream`, `Analyzer.complete/stream`
  - `confidence.py`:
    - Three policies: `ProbabilityPolicy(min_p)`, `LabelLogprobPolicy(min_p)` (first-token probabilities of the 3 labels, renormalised) and `OrdinalPolicy(min_abs)`.
    - Each produces `-> Verdict(sentiment, abstained, confidence?, score?)`.
    - `select(spec, streaming)` forces Ordinal when a stream carries no logprobs.
  - `incremental.JsonFieldScanner.feed(delta) -> list[ScoreClosed|SummaryText]`: a character state machine that handles escape sequences (`\"`, `\\`, `\uXXXX`) split across chunks.
  
  **services/**
  - `ArticleService` keys the fetch cache by normalised URL (lowercase host, no fragment, no `utm_*`) and memoises extraction per (url, parser, extractor).
  - The result cache key is `(url, model, prompt_version, extractor, parser, scope)`. It stores raw model output, and the confidence policy is applied when reading.
  - A stream that hits the cache replays its events immediately with `cached:true`.
  - `timing.StageTimer` builds `Timings`.
  
  ### 3. API contracts (`api/contracts.py`)
  
  **Requests**
  - `SignalRequest(url: HttpUrl, model?, parser="selectolax", extractor="cascade", scope="lede", no_cache=False)`
  - `SummaryRequest`: no `scope` field; always full, capped
  - `AnalyzeRequest`: `scope` defaults to `full`
  
  **Shared response parts**
  - `ArticleMeta(url, final_url, title, source, model, prompt_version, parser, extractor, scope, cached)`
  - `Timings(total_ms, fetch_ms, consent_ms?, parse_ms, extract_ms, inference{wall_ms, ttft_ms?, load_ms?, prompt_eval_ms?, eval_ms?, prompt_tokens?, eval_tokens?}, cache{fetch: hit|miss|joined, result: hit|miss})`
  
  **Responses**
  - `SignalResponse(meta, sentiment, abstained, confidence?, score?, probabilities?, policy, timings)`
  - `SummaryResponse(meta, summary, timings)`
  - `AnalyzeResponse(meta, signal fields, entity, summary, timings)`
  - `ErrorResponse(error{code, message, hint?, retryable, upstream_status?})`
  
  **SSE** (`fastapi.sse.EventSourceResponse`, named events, JSON data)
  - `/analyze/stream` sends `meta` -> `sentiment` (when the score closes) -> `summary_delta{text}` -> `done{result}`.
  - `/summary/stream` sends `meta` -> `summary_delta` -> `done`.
  - `error{error}` is sent for failures mid-stream. Fetch and extraction run before the stream opens, so failures there return a normal HTTP error.
  
  **Routes** (prefix `/api`)
  - `POST /signal`, `/summary`, `/summary/stream`, `/analyze`, `/analyze/stream`
  - `GET /models`: the allowlist ∩ `OLLAMA_MODELS`, with an `installed` flag from `/api/tags` and the per-endpoint defaults
  - `GET /health`: Ollama reachable and version ≥0.40.4
  
  **Status codes**
  
  | Status | Errors |
  |---|---|
  | 400 | invalid URL, blocked destination, model not allowed |
  | 422 | paywalled, consent required, extraction empty, unsupported content |
  | 502 | source blocked, upstream HTTP error |
  | 503 | model unavailable |
  | 504 | timeouts |
  
  **`api/app.create_app()`** (run with uvicorn `--factory`)
  - The lifespan creates both clients and the caches.
  - CORS is added only when `cors_origins` is set.
  - `app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=static_dir, html=True))` is registered after the routers.
  
  ### 4. Evals
  
  Commands run as `uv run python -m veritrade_evals <cmd>`:
  - `datasets fetch`
  - `articles verify|merge|split`
  - `extraction`
  - `signal --suite dev|holdout`
  - `grid`, `thresholds`, `summary`, `analyze`, `latency`
  - `judge export|ingest`
  - `report`
  
  The Opus steps run as Claude Code subagents, each spawned with `model: "opus"`. The instruction files are in `evals/opus/`.
  1. Discovery writes `data/articles/candidates.jsonl`.
  2. Labellers A and B plus the adjudicator write `labels_{a,b,adj}.jsonl`, which are merged into `articles.jsonl(id, url, source, fetched_at, sha256, label, score, entity, ticker, rationale, key_facts, split, agreement)`.
  3. Gold bodies go to `.local/gold/<id>.txt` (gitignored).
  4. Judge verdicts go to `results/summary/judge/*.jsonl`.
  
  `report` writes `results/*.json`, `results/README.md` and `frontend/src/data/benchmarks.json`.
  
  ### 5. Frontend
  
  Next 16 App Router, strict TS, CSS modules, `output:'export'`, `trailingSlash:true`.
  
  - **`app/page.tsx`**:
    - `AnalyzeForm`: url, mode (split|combined), streaming toggle, model pickers from `/api/models`, extractor, parser, scope
    - `SignalCard`, `SummaryStream`, `ErrorBanner` (code + hint)
    - `LatencyBar`: stacked stages; in split mode two lanes on one client `performance.now()` axis
  - **`app/benchmarks/page.tsx`**: imports `src/data/benchmarks.json` at build time.
  - **`src/lib/sse.ts`**: fetch + `TextDecoderStream` + an SSE frame parser that yields typed events, with an AbortController.
  - **`src/lib/api.ts`**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` (empty in prod, `http://localhost:8000` in dev).
  - **`src/lib/api-schema.d.ts`**: generated by `openapi-typescript` from `scripts/export_openapi.py`. CI checks it for drift.
  
  Split mode calls `/api/signal` and `/api/summary/stream` at the same time; single-flight on the backend makes them share one article fetch.
  
  Tests: Vitest + RTL + MSW (SSE via ReadableStream), and Playwright `e2e/analyze.spec.ts` against `:8000`.
  
  ### 6. Docker / compose / setup
  
  **`docker/Dockerfile`** (three stages)
  1. `fe`: node:24-slim, pnpm build -> `out/`
  2. `py`: `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim`, `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package veritrade-backend`
  3. `runtime`: python:3.13-slim with the venv and `out/` at `/app/static`; non-root; HEALTHCHECK on `/api/health`; `uvicorn veritrade.api.app:create_app --factory --port 8000`
  
  **`compose.yaml`**
  - `app`: `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` defaults to `http://host.docker.internal:11434`.
  - Profile `bundled`: `ollama` (ollama/ollama:0.40.5, volume) and `ollama-pull` (pulls `${OLLAMA_MODELS}`). `app` depends on it with `condition: service_completed_successfully, required: false`.
  - Profile `ci`: a `fixtures` static server for the skeleton HTML; `docker/ci.env` sets `VT_SSRF_HOST_ALLOWLIST=fixtures`.
  
  **`scripts/setup.sh`**
  - Records the names of running containers to `.temp/setup/stopped-containers.txt` and runs `docker stop` on them (R8). `restore-containers.sh` restarts them later.
  - `brew install ollama`, `brew services start ollama`, then pulls the models.
  
  ### 7. CI
  
  **`ci.yml`**
  - `backend`: ruff, mypy, pytest with respx-mocked Ollama and the skeleton fixtures, `check_redaction.py`
  - `frontend`: lint, tsc, vitest, build, OpenAPI drift check
  - `e2e`: compose with `bundled` and `ci` profiles, `OLLAMA_MODELS=qwen3.5:0.8b,tev1:0.8b-q8_0`, models cached with `actions/cache`, Playwright
  
  **`live-smoke.yml`**: weekly cron plus manual dispatch. Fetches and extracts one fresh RSS URL per source and writes a summary table to the job. No LLM.
  
  ### 8. Build sequence (milestone commits straight to main)
  
  1. **scaffold**
     - `gh repo create cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics --public`, repo-local identity
     - workspace pyprojects, `.gitignore`, Next skeleton
     - `setup.sh` (stop containers, native Ollama), `.context/docs/design/00-overview.md`
  2. **fetch + extraction**
     - fetch modules
     - run `probe_sources.py`, then lock in the 10 sources
     - Dom facade, strategies, profiles, third-party extractors, scope
     - skeleton fixtures via `make_skeleton_fixture.py`, unit tests
  3. **inference**
     - models.toml, prompts v1, both Ollama clients, adapters, confidence, scanner (tests with chunks split mid-escape)
     - `.temp/` probes against real Ollama to check two things: whether streams carry logprobs, and whether the schema's field order is followed
  4. **API**: contracts, services, caches, timings, SSE, static mount; integration tests (ASGI + respx).
  5. **evals**
     - datasets; Opus discover/label/adjudicate/gold bodies; extraction matrix
     - baseline run, then check latency against R7 and report it to you if the budget is unrealistic
     - grid -> error analysis -> freeze -> thresholds -> holdout once
     - summary/analyze evals plus the Opus judge
     - pick the bundled models, update the defaults, run `report`
  6. **frontend**: pages, SSE client, components, Vitest/MSW, Playwright.
  7. **docker + CI**: Dockerfile, compose, workflows; first green run.
  8. **docs + transcript**
     - README; design records `NN-*.md`; `90-optional-backlog.md`
     - `export_transcript.py`: session 0024648c only (main, subagents, workflows); strips the instructions attachment, `session context`, `api request blob`, emails and home paths; output to `.context/transcript/{raw,rendered,meta.json}`
     - `check_redaction.py`, then the final commit
  
  ### Open details I defaulted
  
  - **Package structure:** evals depend on the backend package. There is no third "core" package.
  - **Ollama client:** httpx for both `/api/chat` and `/v1/systemone` (one pool, mockable with respx). The `ollama` library is not a runtime dependency.
  - **Streaming routes:** separate `/stream` paths instead of content negotiation. Errors before the stream opens come back as plain HTTP errors.
  - **Prompts and thresholds:** prompts are TOML data; thresholds live in `models.toml`.
  - **Scope defaults:** `/signal` defaults to lede, `/analyze` to full, `/summary` is always full.
  - **Abstention:** `sentiment` keeps the model's label and `abstained:true` marks it as below threshold. Evals count an abstained result as no directional call.
  - **Caches:** fetch 10 min, results 1 h, 512 entries, all in memory. Yahoo consent cookies are kept per process only.
  - **CI decision model:** `tev1:0.8b-q8_0`.
  - **Frontend:** CSS modules, generated TS types.
  - **Node:** pinned to 24 via `.nvmrc`; the local machine runs 26.5.
  
  ### Risks
  
  - **SSRF:** a DNS-rebinding gap exists between the check and httpx's own resolve. Documented; the fix would be a custom transport that pins the IP.
  - **Field order:** Ollama's grammar may not follow the schema's property order. If so, sentiment-first streaming gains nothing. Checked in M3.
  - **Label logprobs:** labels split into several tokens, and the JSON prefix tokens get in the way, so the policy matches on first-token prefixes.
  - **Memory:** split mode keeps two models loaded at once. The Docker VM's 15.6 GiB limits the bundled profile.
  - **Ollama settings:** `brew services` needs `launchctl setenv` for KEEP_ALIVE and MAX_LOADED_MODELS.
  - **Source drift:** publisher DOMs and Yahoo's consent form change over time. Live smoke catches it.
  - **Image size:** newspaper4k makes the image larger. It is lazy-imported and its install size is reported.
  - **Ollama bugs:** there are open think+format bugs. Mitigated with `think:false` and one retry after validation fails.
  - **SSE API:** FastAPI's native SSE is new; sse-starlette is the fallback.
  - **Labels:** labels are Opus-only with no human check. The agreement rate is reported.
  - **Transcript timing:** redaction must be the last step, and CI runs a denylist check.

  - ~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/backend/src/veritrade/api/contracts.py
  - ~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/backend/src/veritrade/fetch/client.py
  - ~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/backend/src/veritrade/extract/registry.py
  - ~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/backend/src/veritrade/inference/incremental.py
  - ~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/evals/src/veritrade_evals/__main__.py

  ## Evaluation and benchmarking harness
  
  All paths are relative to `~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/`. `evals/` is a uv workspace member: package `vt_evals`, CLI `uv run vt-evals <cmd>`. It depends on the backend package (I assumed the name `veritrade`). That way prompts, extractors, `build_lede`, the incremental stream parser and the fetcher come from the serving code itself, not copies.
  
  ### 1. Layout
  ```
  evals/src/vt_evals/
    cli.py paths.py schema.py            # Example, RunConfig, PredRecord, BenchmarksV1 (pydantic)
    datasets/{twitter_fns,fpb,finentity,articles,splits}.py
    runner/{session,cache,generative,decision,embed,stages}.py
    metrics/{signal,selective,bootstrap,summary,extraction}.py
    bench/{latency,extraction_matrix}.py
    opus/{prepare,ingest}.py   select.py   report.py
  evals/configs/{roster,grid,budgets,sources}.toml   frozen.toml (written by freeze)
  evals/opus_prompts/{discover,gold_body,label,adjudicate,judge}.md
  evals/tests/                            # synthetic fixtures, no network, runs in CI
  ```
  Gitignored: `evals/.cache/` (hf, preds, emb), `evals/.work/`, `evals/data/articles/_local/`, `.temp/`.
  
  ### 2. Datasets, label maps, splits
  | Loader | Fetch (pinned revision, `cache_dir=evals/.cache/hf`) | Label map | Id |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `twitter_fns.load(split)` | `hf_hub_download("zeroshot/twitter-financial-news-sentiment", f"default/{split}/0000.parquet", repo_type="dataset", revision=<sha of refs/convert/parquet>)`, cols `text,label` | 0 bearish, 1 bullish, 2 neutral | `tfns:{split}:{row}` |
  | `fpb.load("AllAgree")` | `hf_hub_download("takala/financial_phrasebank", "data/FinancialPhraseBank-v1.0.zip")`. Read `FinancialPhraseBank-v1.0/Sentences_AllAgree.txt` via `zipfile`, `.decode("iso-8859-1")`, `line.rsplit("@", 1)`, dedupe exact duplicates | positive bullish, negative bearish | `fpb:{sha1[:12]}` |
  | `finentity.load()` | `FinEntity.json` (`content`, `annotations[].label`). Keep rows with at least one annotation and exactly one distinct label | Positive / Negative / Neutral | `fin:{idx}` |
  | `articles.load_articles(split, text="extracted"\|"gold", scope="lede"\|"full")` | Local HTML, checked against `html_sha256`. "extracted" means the serving default extractor | native | `{source}-{nn}` |
  
  - **Committed:** `evals/data/sources.lock.json` (HF revisions) and `evals/data/splits/*.json` (ids plus text sha1, which the loader verifies).
  - **Never committed:** dataset text (FPB is NC-SA, and tweets carry content rights).
  - **Dev split:** `splits.stratified_sample(seed=20261018)` builds `tfns_dev300` from Twitter train as a balanced 100/100/100 sample.
    - It excludes texts whose normalised hash appears in validation.
    - Dev metrics use prevalence weights (train prior divided by sample prior), so neutral false positives keep their real weight.
  - **Holdouts:** `tfns_val` (2,388), `fpb_allagree` (~2,264), `finentity_single` (n reported), `articles_test` (60).
  - `articles_dev` (30) is used only for scope, field-order and summary selection.
  - **Few-shot:** 4 synthetic headline-style shots (bullish, bearish, neutral, mixed) live in the backend prompt registry. No dataset text goes into prompts, and dev data cannot leak.
  
  ### 3. Runner
  - **`session.ModelSession(model)`** is an async context manager. On entry it:
    - calls `ps()` and unloads every other model (`generate(keep_alive=0)`, falling back to `ollama stop` for decision models);
    - loads the model with an empty generate and records `load_duration`, plus digest and format (gguf or mlx) from `/api/show`;
    - sends 3 warmup calls with the real prompt prefix.
  
    On exit it unloads. `stages.py` sorts configs by model, so each model loads once per stage.
  - **Fixed options:** `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, `think=False`, `num_ctx=8192` on every call (changing `num_ctx` reloads the model). `num_predict` is 16 for signal, 192 for analyze and 160 for summary.
  - **Concurrency:** accuracy stages use `asyncio.Semaphore(4)`; the latency harness always uses 1.
  - **Cache:**
    - Files are `evals/.cache/preds/{model_slug}/{hash16}.jsonl` with a `.config.json` sidecar.
    - `hash16 = sha256(canonical_json(RunConfig, model_digest, rendered_prompt_sha, HARNESS_VERSION))[:16]`, so editing a prompt or re-pulling a model invalidates the cache automatically.
    - A single writer task appends and flushes each line. Resume skips ids already present without a retryable error.
    - Line format: `{id, gold, raw, score, label, p_dir{bullish,neutral,bearish}|null, probs, conf, error, t{client_ms, load_ms, prompt_ms, prompt_tokens, eval_ms, eval_tokens}}`. No text is stored.
  - **Generative calls:** `generative.predict(...)` calls `chat(format=schema, logprobs=True, top_logprobs=20)`.
  - **Decision calls:** `decision.predict(...)` calls `systemone(state=text, questions={"sentiment": {"type": "choice", "instructions": ..., "criteria": {"neutral": ..., "bullish": ..., "bearish": ...}}})`. Neutral comes first, and timing is client-side only.
  
  ### 4. Lean prompt grid and the two confidence knobs
  The generative signal schema is `{"score": int in [-2, 2]}`. Both knobs come from the same call:
  - `extract_dir_probs(logprobs)` finds the first token after the `score` key and strips the top-20 tokens. It maps `-` to bearish, `0` to neutral, and `1`/`2` to bullish, then renormalises into `p_dir`.
  - **Knob L (logprob):** abstain if `max(p_dir) < τ`, with τ swept from 0.50 to 0.99 in steps of 0.01.
  - **Knob O (ordinal):** abstain if `|score| < t`, with t in {1, 2}.
  - Each model keeps the knob with the higher dev F0.5. On a tie, O wins because it also works for SSE streaming (stream chunks carry no logprobs).
  
  | Stage | Models | Configs | Data |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | screen | all roster generative models | rubric A, k=0 | dev300 |
  | tune | top 4 by dev F0.5 with warm lede p50 ≤ 1 s, plus `qwen3.5:0.8b` always (R2 baseline) | rubric {A compact, B edge-case rules} × k {0, 4} = 4 | dev300 |
  | decision | clef-flash:9b-q8_0, nimble:9b-q4_K_M | instructions {plain, rubric} × criteria {null, one-line} = 4. τ on the chosen-class probability | dev300 |
  | field order | top 2 tuned | best (rubric, k) × {score_first, summary_first}, combined schema | dev300 + articles_dev |
  | scope | best generative + both decision models | lede, full | articles_dev |
  | error pass | each finalist | `vt-evals errors <hash>` writes `.temp/error-analysis/<hash>.md`, one manual rubric revision, rerun | dev300 |
  
  `vt-evals freeze` writes `evals/configs/frozen.toml`, with per-model `prompt_id, rubric, k, field_order, knob, tau, scope`.
  
  ### 5. Metrics
  - **`signal.signal_metrics(gold, pred, abstained, w=None)`** (numpy only):
    - The effective label is `none` when the model abstains.
    - Weighted one-vs-rest P, R and F0.5 for bullish and bearish; `f05_macro` is their mean.
    - `inversion_rate` = opposite-direction signals / directional signals emitted.
    - `coverage` = 1 − abstain rate; `signal_rate` = share of items that get a directional signal.
    - A 3×4 confusion matrix (the fourth column is abstain).
  - **`selective`:**
    - `sweep` returns risk-coverage points (coverage vs 1 − directional precision).
    - `select_operating_point(points, inversion_cap=0.02)` picks the maximum F0.5 under the inversion cap.
  - **`bootstrap`:**
    - `bootstrap_ci` is a stratified percentile bootstrap with B=1000 and seed 0.
    - `paired_delta` compares finalists and reports P(Δ>0).
  - **Holdout once:** thresholds are selected on dev300 only. `run --stage holdout` refuses any frozen hash already listed in `evals/results/holdout_runs.json`. `--force` overrides this, and the override is recorded.
  
  ### 6. Latency harness (`bench/latency.py`)
  - **Preflight:** abort if `docker ps -q` is non-empty (R8), unless `--allow-containers` is passed. Records Ollama version, backend `native-metal|docker-cpu`, chip/RAM and git sha.
  - **Per model × kind × scope:**
    - Cold: n=3, all models unloaded first; wall time plus `load_duration`.
    - Warm: 3 warmups, then n=30 cycling through articles_dev. Reports p50/p95 client ms, server `prompt_eval`/`eval` ms, tokens/s and prompt tokens.
  - **Streaming:**
    - TTFT is the first non-empty chunk.
    - Time-to-signal is when the backend's incremental parser closes `score`, compared across the two field orders.
    - systemone timing is client-side only.
  - **Pipeline stages:** the FastAPI app runs in-process (`httpx.ASGITransport`) with the fetcher bound to local HTML, and the harness reads the backend's per-stage timing. Live fetch times from the probe step are reported separately.
  
  ### 7. Extraction matrix (`bench/extraction_matrix.py`)
  It runs over the backend extractor registry (22 combinations) and the 90 local HTML files and reports:
  - **Speed:** median of 5 repetitions per article, then p50/p95 across articles.
  - **Token P/R/F1:** multiset overlap of lowercased `\w+` tokens against the Opus gold body.
  - **Leakage:** share of extracted lines with less than 50% token overlap with the gold body.
  - **Tokens to LLM:** `prompt_eval_count` minus the template-only count.
  - **Failure:** an exception, fewer than 50 tokens, or recall below 0.2.
  - **Downstream agreement:** frozen signal winner on the lede of each extraction vs on the gold body.
  - **Install MB:** from `importlib.metadata` file sizes.
  
  ### 8. Opus steps
  These run as Claude Code subagents, and every spawn sets `model: "opus"`.
  - Python prepares the batches (`vt-evals opus prepare <step>`). Agents write per-item JSON to `evals/.work/opus/<step>/out/`. `vt-evals opus ingest <step>` validates the output and merges it.
  
  The steps:
  1. **discover:** 10 agents, one per source (`sources.toml` RSS/sections, last 60 days), oversampling 5 per class. Only URLs where `uv run vt-evals articles probe <url>` returns ok are kept; the probe saves `_local/html/<id>.html`.
  2. **gold_body + key_facts** (one fused pass, batches of 10):
     - The verbatim body goes to `_local/gold/<id>.txt`.
     - Each article gets 3-5 paraphrased key facts with numbers verbatim.
     - `articles validate-gold` checks that at least 95% of gold lines are substrings of the HTML text.
  3. **label:** labellers A and B are separate agents. They see only the gold body, blind to the proposed label and to each other. Output: `{id, labeller, label, score, entity, ticker, aliases, rationale, ambiguous}`.
  4. **adjudicate:** triggered by a label mismatch or an ambiguous flag. Ambiguous articles are replaced from the same source/class pool, and steps 2-4 repeat for the replacements.
  5. **finalize:**
     - Enforces 3/3/3 per source (±1 allowed, 30/30/30 overall).
     - Assigns a seeded split: 1/1/1 dev and 2/2/2 test per source.
     - `articles agreement` reports raw agreement and Cohen's κ.
  6. **judge:** finalist summaries are anonymised, shuffled and judged in batches of 10. Scores are faithfulness 1-5 and coverage 1-5, plus hallucination flags.
  
  Committed:
  - `evals/data/articles/{candidates,labels,articles}.jsonl`, with url, fetched_at, html/gold sha256, label, score, entity, ticker, rationale, key_facts and split.
  - `evals/data/judgements/{summary_judge.jsonl, judge_key.json}`.
  - `evals/opus_prompts/`.
  
  ### 9. Summary eval (`metrics/summary.py`)
  - `numeric_faithfulness` normalises %, $, k/m/bn and commas; every number in the summary must appear in the source.
  - `entity_named` checks the entity, ticker or an alias.
  - `length_ok`: at most 3 sentences and 60 words.
  - `keyfact_coverage` uses `runner/embed.py` with Ollama `embed` and `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`. A fact counts as covered if its best cosine against the summary sentences is ≥ 0.75. Vectors are cached in `.cache/emb/`, and this runs as a separate single-model pass.
  - **Flow:** top 4 generative models plus the analyze finalists run on articles_dev. The top 3 by (deterministic pass rate, coverage) go to the Opus judge on dev for selection. Only the winner is judged on test60 for the report.
  
  ### 10. Selection and serving
  `select.select(endpoint)`:
  - **Filters:** inversion ≤ 2% on dev, plus the `budgets.toml` budgets: signal lede warm p50 ≤ 500 ms; summary/analyze TTFT ≤ 1.5 s and complete p50 ≤ 4 s.
  - **Signal and analyze:** maximum dev F0.5 among the survivors.
  - **Summary:** best judge faithfulness, then coverage, gated on a deterministic pass rate of at least 0.8.
  - **No survivors:** take the Pareto front on min-max-normalised (F0.5, p50). The knee is the point with the largest perpendicular distance to the chord, and the README says so.
  
  `vt-evals select --write` produces two committed files, reviewed in the diff:
  - **`backend/config/serving.toml`:** the default model per endpoint, plus the frozen settings for every tuned model, because the `model` param must use that model's own prompt and τ. The allowlist is tuned plus screened models.
  - **`deploy/ollama-models.txt`:** the winners if their total size (from `/api/tags`) is ≤ 10 GB. Otherwise the largest is swapped for the next finalist that fits; clef-flash q8 alone is 11 GB, so it can never be bundled. A CI tiny list is included.
  
  ### 11. Results artifacts
  `vt-evals report` writes:
  - `evals/results/benchmarks.json` (`BenchmarksV1`: env, signal{dev, holdout, risk_coverage, knobs}, latency, extraction, summary, selection, articles);
  - `evals/results/predictions/<hash>.jsonl` for finalists (ids and outputs only);
  - `REPORT.md`;
  - the README blocks between `<!-- evals:<table> -->` markers.
  
  The frontend prebuild copies `benchmarks.json` to `frontend/public/` (the copy is gitignored). The Docker frontend stage does the same copy.
  
  ### 12. Build sequence
  1. Scaffold the package, gitignore and configs.
  2. Build loaders, splits and metrics with unit tests, running in CI.
  3. Build session, cache and runners. Run `vt-evals smoke` (qwen3.5:0.8b plus clef-flash, 20 items) to verify:
     - where the score token sits in the logprobs, and whether grammar masking affects the reported logprobs;
     - logprobs on MLX vs GGUF tags;
     - the systemone response shape;
     - whether stream chunks carry logprobs (R3).
  4. Run the baseline on dev300 plus a latency probe, then the R7 sanity check: if the budgets look unrealistic, surface it rather than move them.
  5. Run the Opus article pipeline. It needs the backend fetcher and can run in parallel with step 4.
  6. Run screen, tune, decision, field order, scope and the error pass, then freeze.
  7. Run the extraction matrix.
  8. Run latency for all candidates.
  9. Run the summary eval and the Opus judge.
  10. Run `select --write`.
  11. Run the holdout once.
  12. Run `report`.
  
  ### 13. Compute estimate (M4 Pro, Metal, warm, prefix cache hot)
  | Step | Calls | Time |
  |---|---|---|
  | Model pulls (~55-65 GB) | - | 15-40 min |
  | Screen (13 × 300) | 3.9k | ~25 min |
  | Tune (5 × 4 × 300) | 6k | ~25 min |
  | Decision (8 × 300) | 2.4k | ~10 min |
  | Field order (2 × 2 × 330, ~1.7 s each) | 1.3k | ~40 min |
  | Scope + summaries + embeddings | ~0.9k | ~25 min |
  | Latency (15 models + streaming) | - | ~50 min |
  | Extraction matrix | ~2k | ~15 min |
  | Holdout, signal (3 configs × ~5.4k) | 16k | ~65 min |
  | Holdout, analyze (Twitter val + test60) | 2.45k | ~70 min |
  | **Total** | | **~6 h machine time + ~2 h Opus wall time** |
  
  Trims, to get to about 3.5-4 h:
  - Run the latency gate before the screen and skip the accuracy screen when warm lede p50 is over 1 s. This also saves disk.
  - Set `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4` (`launchctl setenv` plus `brew services restart`) for accuracy stages, about 1.5x faster.
  - Limit the signal holdout to the winner plus the 0.8b baseline.
  - Run field order on the top 1 model only.
  
  Every stage is resumable, so this can run overnight in chunks.
  
  ### Open details I defaulted
  - Names and paths: backend package `veritrade`; `backend/config/serving.toml`; `deploy/ollama-models.txt`.
  - dev300 is balanced 100/100/100 with prevalence weights, rather than a proportional sample.
  - The model emits an integer score from -2 to +2, and direction probability comes from the first score token.
  - Few-shot examples are synthetic rather than drawn from the datasets.
  - Finalists are the top 4 plus the 0.8b baseline; the latency gate is 2× the budget.
  - The τ grid is 0.50-0.99 in 0.01 steps; a knob tie goes to the ordinal knob.
  - Article thresholds are inherited from dev300; there is no tuning on articles.
  - `num_ctx` is 8192 everywhere; `think` off; temperature 0 and seed 0.
  - Concurrency is 4 for accuracy and 1 for latency.
  - Embedding model `qwen3-embedding:0.6b` with a 0.75 cosine threshold.
  - Gold body and key facts are produced in one fused Opus pass.
  - Bootstrap B=1000; seed 20261018.
  - Holdout-once guard.
  - Twitter texts are not committed, only ids and hashes (MIT notwithstanding).
  - Raw caches are gitignored; finalist predictions are committed without text.
  - The summary judge runs on dev for selection and on test for the winner only.
  - The frontend copies `benchmarks.json` at prebuild.
  
  ### Risks
  - **Logprobs:** constrained decoding may report distributions from before the grammar mask, add whitespace tokens, or be unavailable on MLX tags. The smoke test decides. Fallbacks are an explicit GGUF tag, or knob O only.
  - **Latency budget:** 9B decision models may miss 500 ms on full ledes, which leads to the Pareto knee.
  - **Disk:** the roster plus decision models (55-70 GB) against 75 GB free, plus the Docker volume. Pull sequentially and `ollama rm` models that do not make the final cut.
  - **Small article sets:** 30/60 articles give wide CIs, so the field-order and scope decisions have low statistical power. This is stated in the README.
  - **Domain shift:** thresholds tuned on tweets may not transfer to articles. The articles_dev numbers are reported, with no re-tuning.
  - **Labels and gold bodies:** Opus-only labels likely produce inflated agreement (same-model correlation). Gold bodies cannot be reproduced from a clone, and articles can drift or vanish. Hash drift is reported by `articles refetch`.
  - **Measurement noise:** parallel batching makes temperature-0 outputs slightly non-deterministic, and the hot prefix cache flatters warm latency. Both are recorded.
  - **Key-fact threshold:** 0.75 is uncalibrated. Spot-check 20 pairs during the error pass.

  ### 1. Repo bootstrap (main loop, Phase 0)
  1. `git init -b main`, then `git config user.name "Kristiyan Dimitrov"` and `git config user.email kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com` (repo-local).
  2. `.gitignore`: `.temp/ .DS_Store .vscode/ .venv/ __pycache__/ .*_cache/ .coverage htmlcov/ node_modules/ frontend/.next/ frontend/out/ frontend/test-results/ frontend/playwright-report/ evals/data/private/ .env`. `evals/data/private/` holds gold bodies, raw HTML, FPB zip and HF caches.
  3. `LICENSE`: MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Kristiyan Dimitrov".
  4. Run `gh auth status` and confirm the active account is cleverjobs. Then `gh repo create cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics --public -d "..."` (no `--source`), then `git remote add origin [redacted-email]:cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics.git`, then `git push -u origin main`.
  5. Every milestone commit message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
  6. Declare every Python and Node dependency up front, then run `uv lock` and `pnpm install` once. This makes the Phase 2 parallel agents safe.
  7. `scripts/check.py` is the single gate command. `--fast` runs ruff, `ruff format --check`, mypy, unit pytest and `pnpm lint typecheck test`. `--full` adds integration tests, `pnpm build` and the openapi/type drift checks.
  
  ### 2. Native setup (`scripts/dev_setup.py`)
  - `stop-containers`: run `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'` and append the names, with a timestamp, to `.temp/setup/stopped-containers.txt`. Then `docker stop` all of them. Eight are running today.
  - `restart-containers` reads that file and runs `docker start` on each name.
  - `native`:
    - `brew install ollama`. Stable is 0.40.4, which meets the >= 0.40.4 requirement for decision models.
    - `brew services start ollama`. The formula's service already sets `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` and `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`. The script verifies this with `launchctl print`.
    - `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=3` is applied with `launchctl setenv` followed by `brew services restart`. This does not survive a reboot, so the script re-applies it idempotently.
    - keep_alive is sent per request by the app (`VT_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m`).
  - `pull --set {serve,ci,eval}` pulls the model lists from `env/*.txt` and prints the disk delta.
  
  ### 3. Docker
  - **`docker/app.Dockerfile`** has three stages:
    1. `node:24-alpine` with corepack pnpm builds the static export to `out/`.
    2. `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim` runs `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package veritrade-backend`.
    3. `python:3.13-slim-bookworm` copies `.venv` and `out` to `/app/static`, runs as a non-root user, and starts `uvicorn veritrade.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`.
    - The healthcheck is the `veritrade-healthcheck` console script, so no inline Python is needed.
  - **`compose.yaml`**:
    - `app`:
      - Has both `build` and `image: veritrade-app:${TAG:-local}`, and publishes `8000:8000`.
      - `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=${OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}`, `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway`.
      - Passes `VT_MODEL_ALLOWLIST` and `SEC_USER_AGENT`.
      - `depends_on: {ollama-pull: {condition: service_completed_successfully, required: false}}`.
    - `ollama` (profile `bundled`):
      - Image `ollama/ollama:0.40.5`, named volume `ollama-models:/root/.ollama`.
      - Environment: keep_alive 30m, max loaded models 2, flash attention, q8_0 KV cache.
      - Healthcheck `["CMD","ollama","list"]`. No host port, to avoid clashing with native :11434 and to avoid exposing Ollama.
    - `ollama-pull` (profile `bundled`): same image, `OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434`, runs `/scripts/ollama-pull.sh` over the comma-separated `VT_PULL_MODELS`, `restart: "no"`.
    - `env/bundled.env` sets `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434` and `VT_PULL_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-<R8 winners>}`.
  - **`compose.gpu.yaml`**: adds a `deploy.resources.reservations.devices` nvidia/all/[gpu] block to `ollama`.
  - **`compose.e2e.yaml`**:
    - `fixture-site`: `nginx:1.27-alpine` serves `backend/tests/fixtures/skeletons` read-only, with network alias `fixtures.local`.
    - The app runs with `VT_ENV=test`, `VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS=fixtures.local` and the CI allowlist.
    - The ollama volume is a bind mount to `${OLLAMA_CACHE_DIR}` so `actions/cache` can save it.
    - `settings.py` refuses to start if `VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS` is set while `VT_ENV != test`.
  
  ### 4. Test strategy per altitude
  
  | Altitude | Where | What (PoC-balanced) |
  |---|---|---|
  | BE unit | `backend/tests/unit/` | **Extractors** (`test_extract.py`): every skeleton x {jsonld, profile, density, cascade} x 4 parsers must reach `VTB` body-marker recall >= 0.9 with zero `VTX` leakage. JSON-LD cases are skipped when `expected.jsonld_body` is false. Third-party extractors get a smoke test only (non-empty, no exception). **`test_skeleton_purity.py`**: every text node matches the synthetic vocabulary. **`test_ssrf.py`**: schemes; v4/v6 private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA and v4-mapped addresses; DNS resolving to a private IP through an injected resolver; per-hop redirect checks; redirect cap; size cap; content type; the test-allow env refused outside test. **`test_detect.py`**: Yahoo consent form, Cloudflare/DataDome challenges and paywall markers each map to the typed error with its hint. The reject-all POST is checked with respx and the cookie cached. **`test_prompts.py`**: golden files in `unit/golden/prompts/<id>.txt`, untrusted-content fencing, lede vs full truncation, both field orders. **`test_policies.py`**: logprob threshold, ordinal \|score\| threshold, decision probabilities, neutral-first ties, `abstained`. **`test_stream_parser.py`**: 6 canned payloads split at every byte offset (escapes, unicode, both orders, malformed input). **`test_schemas.py`**: models, allowlist, enums, SSE event payloads, plus `export_openapi.py --check`. |

The resolver is overridden with a static public-IP map. **Fake Ollama** is a Starlette app on a uvicorn thread (session fixture, random port) serving `/api/chat` (stream and non-stream), `/v1/systemone`, `/api/tags`, `/api/version` and `/api/embed` from cassettes, with a configurable chunk delay. Each cassette stores `prompt_sha256`; a mismatch fails with "run scripts/record_cassettes.py". **Cases**: signal (decision and generative models); summary and analyze, both JSON and SSE; event order `meta -> sentiment -> summary_delta* -> done`; single-flight (2 concurrent requests, 1 upstream hit); result-cache hit; typed errors mapped to status codes; model outside the allowlist returns 422; Ollama down returns 503; health; models endpoint merges `/api/tags`. |

Checks that sentiment renders before the summary completes, that done timings appear, errors, model dropdown contents, and the Benchmarks page rendered from `public/benchmarks`. `pnpm gen:api --check` (openapi-typescript) catches contract drift. |

Specs: analyze happy path, signal-only with the tiny decision model, consent fixture shows the `consent_required` banner, extractor switch. Assertions are model-agnostic: schema, event order, one of 3 labels or abstained, non-empty summary, timings. |

  ### 5. Skeleton capture (`scripts/capture_skeletons.py`)
  - Input: one URL per source from the probe output.
  - Fetches once live, then rewrites with lxml:
    - Removes script and style contents (JSON-LD is kept, with its text fields synthesized) and comments.
    - Body paragraphs, located by the per-domain profile and cross-checked with trafilatura, become prose-like synthetic sentences of the same length carrying `VTB-k` markers. All other text becomes `VTX-k`.
    - `alt`, `title` and `aria-*` values are synthesized. `href` and `src` point to `https://example.invalid/`.
    - Classes, ids and `data-*` attributes are kept.
  - Writes `.expected.json` with: source, captured_at, url_sha256, headline marker, body markers, `jsonld_body`, profile.
  - Also captures the Yahoo consent page and any challenge page it meets.
  - Prints per-source marker stats; an Opus agent spot-checks one fixture per source.
  
  ### 6. GitHub Actions
  **`ci.yml`** runs on push and PR. It has `concurrency: ${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress.
  - `backend`:
    - `astral-sh/setup-uv` (enable-cache, glob `uv.lock`), then `uv sync --all-packages --frozen`, then `uv run python scripts/check.py --backend --full`.
    - Then `export_transcript.py --scan-only` as a regression guard.
  - `frontend`: `pnpm/action-setup` and `setup-node@v4` (Node 24, `cache: pnpm`, `cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`), then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, gen:api check, lint, typecheck, `vitest run`, build.
  - `e2e` (needs both, `timeout-minutes: 30`):
    1. Free disk by removing dotnet, ghc and android directories. The runner has 14 GB; the ollama image, about 2 GB of models, the app image and chromium fit after this.
    2. `docker/build-push-action` with `load: true` and `cache-from/to: type=gha,mode=max`.
    3. `actions/cache` for `~/.ollama-ci`, keyed on `ollama-0.40.5-${{ hashFiles('env/ci-models.txt') }}`, and for `~/.cache/ms-playwright`.
    4. `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml --profile bundled up -d`, then `docker compose wait ollama-pull`, then poll `/api/health`, then send one warm-up `/api/signal`.
    5. `pnpm exec playwright test`.
    6. Run `sudo chown -R` on the model dir before the cache post-step.
    7. On failure, upload the report and `compose logs`.
  
  **`live-smoke.yml`** runs on `schedule: '23 5 * * *'` and `workflow_dispatch`. It is a single uv job that writes a results table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. It is never a required check, and runner-IP blocks are labelled informational.

  - Built on `veritrade/fetch/{headers,detect}.py`, written in Phase 1 and later reused by the fetcher.

  - Records: status, final URL, typed detection, latency, JSON-LD presence, word estimate, and 2 article URLs. No text is stored.
  - Outputs `evals/data/source_probe.json` and `.context/docs/design/02-source-probe.md`, which states the final top 10.

Any hit exits 1 with file:line. Only then are files moved to `.context/transcript/{raw,rendered,meta.json,README.md}`. After that: commit and push.

  Every `agent()` call sets `model: 'opus'`. Each agent brief lists the paths it owns and the paths it may not touch (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and other agents' paths), plus the coding rules. Each agent reports back: files changed, dependencies it needs, open issues. The main loop commits after every gate.
  
  | Phase | Units | Mode | Gate / commit |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | P0 | Bootstrap; deps declared and locked; contracts (`schemas.py`, `Extractor`/`LLMClient` Protocols, `openapi.json`); ci.yml backend and frontend jobs; `dev_setup stop-containers` + `native` + model pulls (in the background) | main loop | `check.py --fast`, push M0 |
  | P1 | Probe | 1 agent | Design doc 02 with >= 10 usable sources, M1 |
  | P2 | (a) `fetch/` (b) `extract/` + skeleton capture (c) `llm/` + fake Ollama + recorder (d) `frontend/` against the contract and MSW (e) `evals` loaders and metrics | 5 agents in parallel, shared tree, file-disjoint | `check.py --fast`, M2 |
  | P3 | (a) `api/`, `main.py`, caches, integration tests, cassettes (b) R5 article-set sub-workflow (labellers isolated from each other, then adjudicator) writing `evals/data/articles/` | 2 parallel | `--full`, plus one manual analyze per source on native Ollama, M3 |
  | P4 | (a) Docker, compose, CI e2e, Playwright (b) accuracy evals: prompt grid, knobs, scope, field order, extraction matrix accuracy (c) gold bodies and the Opus summary judge on finalists from (b) | (a) runs in a worktree on branch `ci/e2e`, iterates by pushing, then is squash-merged into main; (b) and (c) run in the main tree | CI and e2e green on main (`gh run watch`), M4 |
  | P5 | Latency benchmarks, holdout once, freeze, `public/benchmarks`, design docs, README | Exclusive: no Docker builds or other agents running | Budgets reported, M5 |
  | P6 | Verification checklist, then transcript export | main loop | Scan gate, M6, push |
  
  ### 11. End-to-end verification checklist
  1. `git log` shows the correct author and trailer on every commit, and `git status` is clean.
  2. `check.py --full` passes.
  3. Native path: `brew services list` shows ollama running; `docker compose up -d`; `/api/health` reports `backend=native-metal`; analyze succeeds on one URL per source; typed errors are recorded.
  4. Bundled path: `--profile bundled --env-file env/bundled.env` comes up healthy and one analyze succeeds.
  5. Latency budget script prints p50 against the R7 budgets.
  6. `ci.yml` is green on HEAD. `gh workflow run live-smoke.yml` was dispatched once and its result noted.
  7. `git ls-files` contains nothing from `evals/data/private`, and the skeleton purity test passes.
  8. All README links resolve.
  9. Remind the user that `dev_setup restart-containers` exists.
  10. Transcript export is the very last step.
  
  ### Open details I defaulted
  - CI tiny decision model is `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` with scope=lede. If it is unusable, e2e tests the signal endpoint with the generative model only.
  - E2E fixtures depend on JSON-LD and generic cascade. Per-domain profiles are covered only in unit tests, because the e2e host is `fixtures.local`.
  - The bundled profile uses `env/bundled.env`, since a compose profile cannot change app env by itself. The ollama service publishes no host port.
  - Backend coverage floor is 75. The frontend is reported only.
  - OpenAPI plus openapi-typescript drift checks are the contract gate.
  - `.context/openai-research.md` and the brief are committed.
  - The final export and push turns will not appear in the exported transcript. This is stated in the transcript README.
  - The claude-code-log MD flag needs to be checked with `--help` at build time.
  - CI workflow iteration happens on a temporary branch that is squash-merged, so main still gets milestone commits only.
  
  ### Risks
  - **Env name collision**: `OLLAMA_MODELS` is also Ollama's own storage-dir variable. Passing it to the `ollama` service would move model storage, which is why it is mapped to `VT_PULL_MODELS`.
  - **Linux native path**: Ollama listens on 127.0.0.1 by default, so `host-gateway` cannot reach it. It needs `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`.
  - **Docker Desktop memory**: the VM has 15.6 GiB, and clef-flash alone is 11 GB, so the bundled models must stay at or below ~10 GB.
  - **CI runner limits**: disk and RAM are tight, model pulls are slow on a cold cache, and the GitHub cache limit is 10 GB.
  - **Live smoke results are noisy**: runner IPs get blocked differently from the user's IP.
  - **Transcript size and privacy**: subagent JSONL may push files toward the 50 MB gate, and redaction still needs a manual skim of the rendered HTML.
  - **Latency noise**: concurrent agents or Docker builds would skew P5 numbers, which is why that phase runs alone.

financial-news URL, fetches + extracts the article, and returns an LLM summary + Bullish/Bearish/Neutral

# Real-Time Financial News Analysis Service

## Overview
VeriTrade Analytics is a fintech firm providing high-speed market intelligence to day traders and quantitative analysts. Our analysts currently waste precious minutes manually reading breaking news articles, press releases, and earnings reports to gauge market sentiment. In a world where milliseconds matter, this manual process introduces critical delays, leading to missed opportunities. To solve this, VeriTrade needs a tool that can ingest a news article and provide an instant, AI-powered summary and sentiment analysis.

Your task is to build a prototype for this internal tool. You will create a web service that accepts a URL to a public financial news article. The service should then fetch the article's content, use a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate a concise summary and a sentiment analysis (e.g., Bullish, Bearish, Neutral), and return this information via an API. The core business constraint is speed; the system must be designed for low latency to be useful for traders making time-sensitive decisions. You will also build a simple frontend interface to interact with this service.

A successful submission will demonstrate thoughtful system design focused on performance, effective use of an LLM for a specific task, and clear communication of your design trade-offs. The frontend UI does not need to be visually polished; a functional interface that clearly presents the workflow and results is sufficient.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository or a single public GitHub gist URL containing your complete solution.
- A backend service written in Python that exposes an API to analyze a given news article URL.
- A basic frontend web application (e.g., React, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JS) that consumes the backend API and displays the results.
- A `README.md` file explaining your design decisions, trade-offs (especially regarding latency optimization), instructions on how to run the application and any tests, and a brief note on which AI tools you used.
- The conversation log from any AI assistants used during development (e.g., VS Code Copilot Chat export, Claude conversation history) committed to the repository.

## Suggested tools / libraries
- Backend Framework: FastAPI, Flask
- LLM Integration: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, Groq, or a local model via Ollama
- Web Scraping: BeautifulSoup, requests
- Frontend Framework: React + Vite, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- API Client: `fetch` API, Axios
- Containerization: Docker (optional)

## On AI assistants & follow-up
- We expect and encourage the use of AI assistants. Your goal is to deliver a great solution, not to memorize APIs.
- Please commit the conversation log from your AI assistant (e.g., Copilot Chat export, Claude history) to your repository and briefly describe its role in your README.
- Be prepared to walk through your code and justify your design decisions, especially regarding performance and architectural trade-offs, in the follow-up interview.
- The focus is on your design judgment, problem decomposition, and verification, not on writing every line of code from scratch.

## How to submit
Reply to this email with **one** public GitHub repository or gist URL containing your solution.

<!-- AI-EVALUATOR:PRESCREEN-META {"language":"Python","dueDays":10,"timeBudgetHours":8} -->

### Twitter Financial News Sentiment

**Dataset:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/zeroshot/twitter-financial-news-sentiment

Contains approximately 11.9K financial short texts labeled:

- Bearish
- Bullish
- Neutral

Best for:

- Directional sentiment classification.
- Model comparison.
- Cross-domain evaluation.
- Testing prediction thresholds.

The dataset provides predefined training and validation partitions. Use these rather than introducing unnecessary leakage through ad hoc splitting.

The published license is MIT, although underlying social-media content rights may require separate consideration.

### SEntFiN

**Paper:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12257

A dataset of approximately 10.7K financial headlines with entity-specific sentiment annotations.

Particularly useful for cases involving multiple companies with different financial implications.

Best for:

- Entity-specific sentiment.
- Multiple entities per article.
- Mixed sentiment scenarios.

### FinEntity

**Dataset:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/yixuantt/FinEntity

Financial-news annotations focused on sentiment toward individual entities.

Best for:

- Entity extraction and attribution.
- Financial context sensitivity.
- Company-specific sentiment evaluation.

### Custom full-article dataset
## 12. Reliability and Security

Because the backend accepts arbitrary public URLs, URL handling is a security-sensitive part of the design.

Minimum protections:

- Reject non-HTTP(S) URL schemes.
- Block loopback, private, link-local, and internal network destinations.
- Validate resolved IP addresses and redirects.
- Apply strict fetch timeouts and response-size limits.
- Restrict unsupported content types.
- Avoid unrestricted redirect chains.
- Apply rate limits where appropriate.
- Treat retrieved web content as untrusted data.
- Prevent article instructions from overriding the model's system instructions.
- Validate structured model responses with Pydantic.
- Return explicit errors for extraction and inference failures.
- Never expose local Ollama APIs publicly without suitable access controls.

Respect website access policies and content licensing.

For a production financial-news service, licensed data feeds would generally be preferable to arbitrary public-web scraping.
