````
---
title: How to create a static export of your Next.js application
nav_title: Static Exports
description: Next.js enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application (SPA), then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

Next.js enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application (SPA), then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server.

When running `next build`, Next.js generates an HTML file per route. By breaking a strict SPA into individual HTML files, Next.js can avoid loading unnecessary JavaScript code on the client-side, reducing the bundle size and enabling faster page loads.

Since Next.js supports this static export, it can be deployed and hosted on any web server that can serve HTML/CSS/JS static assets.

## Configuration

To enable a static export, change the output mode inside `next.config.js`:

```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={5}
/**
 * @type {import('next').NextConfig}
 */
const nextConfig = {
  output: 'export',

  // Optional: Change links `/me` -> `/me/` and emit `/me.html` -> `/me/index.html`
  // trailingSlash: true,

  // Optional: Prevent automatic `/me` -> `/me/`, instead preserve `href`
  // skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true,

  // Optional: Change the output directory `out` -> `dist`
  // distDir: 'dist',
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

After running `next build`, Next.js will create an `out` folder with the HTML/CSS/JS assets for your application.

<PagesOnly>

You can utilize [`getStaticProps`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/get-static-props) and [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/get-static-paths) to generate an HTML file for each page in your `pages` directory (or more for [dynamic routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes)).

</PagesOnly>

<AppOnly>

## Supported Features

The core of Next.js has been designed to support static exports.

### Server Components

When you run `next build` to generate a static export, Server Components consumed inside the `app` directory will run during the build, similar to traditional static-site generation.

The resulting component will be rendered into static HTML for the initial page load and a static payload for client navigation between routes. No changes are required for your Server Components when using the static export, unless they consume [dynamic server functions](#unsupported-features).

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
export default async function Page() {
  // This fetch will run on the server during `next build`
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/...')
  const data = await res.json()

  return <main>...</main>
}
```

### Client Components

If you want to perform data fetching on the client, you can use a Client Component with [SWR](https://github.com/vercel/swr) to memoize requests.

```tsx filename="app/other/page.tsx" switcher
'use client'

import useSWR from 'swr'

const fetcher = (url: string) => fetch(url).then((r) => r.json())

export default function Page() {
  const { data, error } = useSWR(
    `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1`,
    fetcher
  )
  if (error) return 'Failed to load'
  if (!data) return 'Loading...'

  return data.title
}
```

```jsx filename="app/other/page.js" switcher
'use client'

import useSWR from 'swr'

const fetcher = (url) => fetch(url).then((r) => r.json())

export default function Page() {
  const { data, error } = useSWR(
    `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1`,
    fetcher
  )
  if (error) return 'Failed to load'
  if (!data) return 'Loading...'

  return data.title
}
```

Since route transitions happen client-side, this behaves like a traditional SPA. For example, the following index route allows you to navigate to different posts on the client:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <>
      <h1>Index Page</h1>
      <hr />
      <ul>
        <li>
          <Link href="/post/1">Post 1</Link>
        </li>
        <li>
          <Link href="/post/2">Post 2</Link>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <>
      <h1>Index Page</h1>
      <p>
        <Link href="/other">Other Page</Link>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

</AppOnly>

<PagesOnly>

## Supported Features

The majority of core Next.js features needed to build a static site are supported, including:

- [Dynamic Routes when using `getStaticPaths`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes)
- Prefetching with `next/link`
- Preloading JavaScript
- [Dynamic Imports](/docs/pages/guides/lazy-loading)
- Any styling options (e.g. CSS Modules, styled-jsx)
- [Client-side data fetching](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/client-side)
- [`getStaticProps`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/get-static-props)
- [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/get-static-paths)

</PagesOnly>

### Image Optimization

[Image Optimization](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image) through `next/image` can be used with a static export by defining a custom image loader in `next.config.js`. For example, you can optimize images with a service like Cloudinary:

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  output: 'export',
  images: {
    loader: 'custom',
    loaderFile: './my-loader.ts',
  },
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

This custom loader will define how to fetch images from a remote source. For example, the following loader will construct the URL for Cloudinary:

```ts filename="my-loader.ts" switcher
export default function cloudinaryLoader({
  src,
  width,
  quality,
}: {
  src: string
  width: number
  quality?: number
}) {
  const params = ['f_auto', 'c_limit', `w_${width}`, `q_${quality || 'auto'}`]
  return `https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/${params.join(
    ','
  )}${src}`
}
```

```js filename="my-loader.js" switcher
export default function cloudinaryLoader({ src, width, quality }) {
  const params = ['f_auto', 'c_limit', `w_${width}`, `q_${quality || 'auto'}`]
  return `https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/${params.join(
    ','
  )}${src}`
}
```

You can then use `next/image` in your application, defining relative paths to the image in Cloudinary:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Image from 'next/image'

export default function Page() {
  return <Image alt="turtles" src="/turtles.jpg" width={300} height={300} />
}
```

```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
import Image from 'next/image'

export default function Page() {
  return <Image alt="turtles" src="/turtles.jpg" width={300} height={300} />
}
```

<AppOnly>

### Route Handlers

Route Handlers will render a static response when running `next build`. Only the `GET` HTTP verb is supported. This can be used to generate static HTML, JSON, TXT, or other files from cached or uncached data. To ensure Route Handlers are prerendered, you must explicitly mark the handler as static by adding `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` when a static export is enabled. For example:

```ts filename="app/data.json/route.ts" switcher
export const dynamic = 'force-static'

export async function GET() {
  return Response.json({ name: 'Lee' })
}
```

```js filename="app/data.json/route.js" switcher
export const dynamic = 'force-static'

export async function GET() {
  return Response.json({ name: 'Lee' })
}
````

````
If you need to read dynamic values from the incoming request, you cannot use a static export.

### Browser APIs

Client Components are prerendered to HTML during `next build`. Because [Web APIs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API) like `window`, `localStorage`, and `navigator` are not available on the server, you need to safely access these APIs only when running in the browser. For example:

```jsx
'use client';

import { useEffect } from 'react';

export default function ClientComponent() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // You now have access to `window`
    console.log(window.innerHeight);
  }, [])

  return ...;
}
```

</AppOnly>

## Unsupported Features

Features that require a Node.js server, or dynamic logic that cannot be computed during the build process, are **not** supported:

<AppOnly>

- [Dynamic Routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) with `dynamicParams: true`
- [Dynamic Routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) without `generateStaticParams()`
- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) that rely on Request
- [Cookies](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies)
- [Rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites)
- [Redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/redirects)
- [Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers)
- [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)
- [Incremental Static Regeneration](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration)
- [Image Optimization](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image) with the default `loader`
- [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode)
- [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data)
- [Intercepting Routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes)

Attempting to use any of these features with `next dev` will result in an error, similar to setting the [`dynamic`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) option to `error` in the root layout.

```jsx
export const dynamic = 'error'
```

</AppOnly>

<PagesOnly>

- [Internationalized Routing](/docs/pages/guides/internationalization)
- [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes)
- [Rewrites](/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites)
- [Redirects](/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/redirects)
- [Headers](/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers)
- [Proxy](/docs/pages/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)
- [Incremental Static Regeneration](/docs/pages/guides/incremental-static-regeneration)
- [Image Optimization](/docs/pages/api-reference/components/image) with the default `loader`
- [Draft Mode](/docs/pages/guides/draft-mode)
- [`getStaticPaths` with `fallback: true`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths#fallback-true)
- [`getStaticPaths` with `fallback: 'blocking'`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths#fallback-blocking)
- [`getServerSideProps`](/docs/pages/building-your-application/data-fetching/get-server-side-props)

</PagesOnly>

## Deploying

With a static export, Next.js can be deployed and hosted on any web server that can serve HTML/CSS/JS static assets.

When running `next build`, Next.js generates the static export into the `out` folder. For example, let's say you have the following routes:

- `/`
- `/blog/[id]`

After running `next build`, Next.js will generate the following files:

- `/out/index.html`
- `/out/404.html`
- `/out/blog/post-1.html`
- `/out/blog/post-2.html`

If you are using a static host like Nginx, you can configure rewrites from incoming requests to the correct files:

```nginx filename="nginx.conf"
server {
  listen 80;
  server_name acme.com;

  root /var/www/out;

  location / {
      try_files $uri $uri.html $uri/ =404;
  }

  # This is necessary when `trailingSlash: false`.
  # You can omit this when `trailingSlash: true`.
  location /blog/ {
      rewrite ^/blog/(.*)$ /blog/$1.html break;
  }

  error_page 404 /404.html;
  location = /404.html {
      internal;
  }
}
```

To deploy to GitHub Pages, use our [template](https://github.com/nextjs/deploy-github-pages) to create a new project or as a reference for configuring an existing project.

## Version History

| Version   | Changes                                                                                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v14.0.0` | `next export` has been removed in favor of `"output": "export"`                                                      |
| `v13.4.0` | App Router (Stable) adds enhanced static export support, including using React Server Components and Route Handlers. |
| `v13.3.0` | `next export` is deprecated and replaced with `"output": "export"`                                                   |
````

```
12:- [Bundle environment variables for the browser by prefixing with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`](#bundling-environment-variables-for-the-browser)
156:Non-`NEXT_PUBLIC_` environment variables are only available in the Node.js environment, meaning they aren't accessible to the browser (the client runs in a different _environment_).
158:In order to make the value of an environment variable accessible in the browser, Next.js can "inline" a value, at build time, into the js bundle that is delivered to the client, replacing all references to `process.env.[variable]` with a hard-coded value. To tell it to do this, you just have to prefix the variable with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. For example:
161:NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_ID=abcdefghijk
164:This will tell Next.js to replace all references to `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_ID` in the Node.js environment with the value from the environment in which you run `next build`, allowing you to use it anywhere in your code. It will be inlined into any JavaScript sent to the browser.
166:> **Note**: After being built, your app will no longer respond to changes to these environment variables. For instance, if you use a Heroku pipeline to promote slugs built in one environment to another environment, or if you build and deploy a single Docker image to multiple environments, all `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables will be frozen with the value evaluated at build time, so these values need to be set appropriately when the project is built. If you need access to runtime environment values, you'll have to set up your own API to provide them to the client (either on demand or during initialization).
171:// 'NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_ID' can be used here as it's prefixed by 'NEXT_PUBLIC_'.
```

````
title: How to set up Vitest with Next.js
nav_title: Vitest
description: Learn how to set up Vitest with Next.js for Unit Testing.
---

Vitest and React Testing Library are frequently used together for **Unit Testing**. This guide will show you how to set up Vitest with Next.js and write your first tests.

> **Good to know:** Since `async` Server Components are new to the React ecosystem, Vitest currently does not support them. While you can still run **unit tests** for synchronous Server and Client Components, we recommend using **E2E tests** for `async` components.

## Quickstart

You can use `create-next-app` with the Next.js [with-vitest](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-vitest) example to quickly get started:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app
```

```bash package="npm"
npx create-next-app@latest --example with-vitest with-vitest-app
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app
```

```bash package="bun"
bun create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app
```

## Manual Setup

To manually set up Vitest, install `vitest` and the following packages as dev dependencies:

```bash package="pnpm"
# Using TypeScript
pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths
# Using JavaScript
pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom
```

```bash package="npm"
# Using TypeScript
npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths
# Using JavaScript
npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom
```

```bash package="yarn"
# Using TypeScript
yarn add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths
# Using JavaScript
yarn add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom
```

```bash package="bun"
# Using TypeScript
bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths
# Using JavaScript
bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom
```

Create a `vitest.config.mts|js` file in the root of your project, and add the following options:

```ts filename="vitest.config.mts" switcher
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [tsconfigPaths(), react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
  },
})
```

```js filename="vitest.config.js" switcher
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
  },
})
```

For more information on configuring Vitest, please refer to the [Vitest Configuration](https://vitest.dev/config/#configuration) docs.

Then, add a `test` script to your `package.json`:

```json filename="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev",
    "build": "next build",
    "start": "next start",
    "test": "vitest"
  }
}
```

When you run `npm run test`, Vitest will **watch** for changes in your project by default.

## Creating your first Vitest Unit Test

Check that everything is working by creating a test to check if the `<Page />` component successfully renders a heading:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Home</h1>
      <Link href="/about">About</Link>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Home</h1>
      <Link href="/about">About</Link>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx filename="__tests__/page.test.tsx" switcher
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import Page from '../app/page'

test('Page', () => {
  render(<Page />)
  expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Home' })).toBeDefined()
})
```

title: use client
description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.
---

The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.

> **Good to know:**
>
> You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.

## Usage

To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:

```tsx filename="app/components/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0)

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Count: {count}</p>
      <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/components/counter.js" highlight={1} switcher
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0)

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Count: {count}</p>
      <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

When using the `'use client'` directive, the props of the Client Components must be [serializable](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types). This means the props need to be in a format that React can serialize when sending data from the server to the client.

```tsx filename="app/components/counter.tsx" highlight={4} switcher
'use client'

export default function Counter({
  onClick /* ❌ Function is not serializable */,
}) {
  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={onClick}>Increment</button>

title: How to set up Playwright with Next.js
nav_title: Playwright
description: Learn how to set up Playwright with Next.js for End-to-End (E2E) Testing.
related:
  description: Learn more about testing instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
---

Playwright is a testing framework that lets you automate Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API. You can use it to write **End-to-End (E2E)** testing. This guide will show you how to set up Playwright with Next.js and write your first tests.

## Quickstart

The fastest way to get started is to use `create-next-app` with the [with-playwright example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-playwright). This will create a Next.js project complete with Playwright configured.

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
```

```bash package="npm"
npx create-next-app@latest --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
```

```bash package="bun"
bun create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
```

## Manual setup

To install Playwright, run the following command:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm create playwright
```

```bash package="npm"
npm init playwright
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn create playwright
```

```bash package="bun"
bun create playwright
```

This will take you through a series of prompts to set up and configure Playwright for your project, including adding a `playwright.config.ts` file. Please refer to the [Playwright installation guide](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#installation) for the step-by-step guide.

## Creating your first Playwright E2E test

Create two new Next.js pages:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Home</h1>
      <Link href="/about">About</Link>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>About</h1>
````

```
import type {
  DefaultBodyType,
  RequestHandlerOptions,
  ResponseResolver,
} from '#core/handlers/request-handler'
import {
  HttpMethods,
  HttpHandler,
  type HttpRequestResolverExtras,
  type HttpRequestPredicate,
} from './http-handler'
import type { PathParams } from '#core/utils/matching/match-request-url'

export type HttpRequestHandler = <
  Params extends PathParams<keyof Params> = PathParams,
  RequestBodyType extends DefaultBodyType = DefaultBodyType,
  // Response body type MUST be undefined by default.
  // This is how we can distinguish between a handler that
  // returns plain "Response" and the one returning "HttpResponse"
  // to enforce a stricter response body type.
  ResponseBodyType extends DefaultBodyType = undefined,
>(
  predicate: HttpRequestPredicate<Params>,
  resolver: HttpResponseResolver<Params, RequestBodyType, ResponseBodyType>,
  options?: RequestHandlerOptions,
) => HttpHandler

export type HttpResponseResolver<
  Params extends PathParams<keyof Params> = PathParams,
  RequestBodyType extends DefaultBodyType = DefaultBodyType,
  ResponseBodyType extends DefaultBodyType = DefaultBodyType,
> = ResponseResolver<
  HttpRequestResolverExtras<Params>,
  RequestBodyType,
  ResponseBodyType
>

function createHttpHandler<Method extends HttpMethods | RegExp>(
  method: Method,
): HttpRequestHandler {
  return (predicate, resolver, options = {}) => {
    return new HttpHandler(method, predicate, resolver, options)
  }
}

/**
 * A namespace to intercept and mock HTTP requests.
 *
 * @example
 * http.get('/user', resolver)
 * http.post('/post/:id', resolver)
 *
 * @see {@link https://mswjs.io/docs/api/http `http` API reference}
 */
export const http = {
  all: createHttpHandler(/.+/),
  head: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.HEAD),
  get: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.GET),
  post: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.POST),
  put: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.PUT),
  delete: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.DELETE),
  patch: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.PATCH),
  options: createHttpHandler(HttpMethods.OPTIONS),
}
```

```
import { isAbsoluteUrl } from './is-absolute-url'

/**
 * Returns an absolute URL based on the given path.
 */
export function getAbsoluteUrl(path: string, baseUrl?: string): string {
  // already absolute URL
  if (isAbsoluteUrl(path)) {
    return path
  }

  // Ignore path with pattern start with *
  if (path.startsWith('*')) {
    return path
  }

  // Resolve a relative request URL against a given custom "baseUrl"
  // or the document baseURI (in the case of browser/browser-like environments).
  const origin = baseUrl || (typeof location !== 'undefined' && location.href)

  return origin
    ? // Encode and decode the path to preserve escaped characters.
      decodeURI(new URL(encodeURI(path), origin).href)
    : path
}
```

110-> - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.

2:title: usePathname
3:description: API Reference for the usePathname hook.
6:`usePathname` is a **Client Component** hook that lets you read the current URL's **pathname**.
11:import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
14:  const pathname = usePathname()
22:import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation'
25:  const pathname = usePathname()
30:`usePathname` intentionally requires using a [Client Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). It's important to note Client Components are not a de-optimization. They are an integral part of the [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) architecture.
32:For example, a Client Component with `usePathname` will be rendered into HTML on the initial page load. When navigating to a new route, this component does not need to be re-fetched. Instead, the component is downloaded once (in the client JavaScript bundle), and re-renders based on the current state.
37:> - If your page is being statically prerendered and your app has [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites) in `next.config` or a [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) file, reading the pathname with `usePathname()` can result in hydration mismatch errors, because the initial value comes from the server and may not match the actual browser pathname after routing. See our [example](#avoid-hydration-mismatch-with-rewrites) for a way to mitigate this issue.
43:If you have components that use `usePathname` and they are imported into routes within the Pages Router, be aware that `usePathname` may return `null` if the router is not yet initialized. This can occur in cases such as [fallback routes](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths#fallback-true) or during [Automatic Static Optimization](/docs/pages/building-your-application/rendering/automatic-static-optimization) in the Pages Router.
45:To enhance compatibility between routing systems, if your project contains both an `app` and a `pages` directory, Next.js will automatically adjust the return type of `usePathname`.
52:const pathname = usePathname()
55:`usePathname` does not take any parameters.
59:`usePathname` returns a string of the current URL's pathname. For example:
72:When [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, `usePathname` may require a [`Suspense`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary. This depends on whether the pathname can be resolved during prerendering.
74:- **Static routes and routes with [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)**: every route segment, including dynamic params, is known at build time. The pathname can be resolved during prerendering, so `usePathname` resolves on the server and no `Suspense` boundary is required.
75:- **Routes with dynamic params not covered by `generateStaticParams`**: the param is a [fallback param](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params#all-paths-at-build-time) that is not known until request time. The pathname cannot be resolved during prerendering, so `usePathname` suspends. Wrap the component (or a parent) in a `Suspense` boundary so its fallback can be rendered during prerendering; otherwise, the build fails.
77:This applies even when the component that calls `usePathname` is itself static. For example, a sidebar with active links rendered in a layout suspends on any page below it that has an unknown dynamic param. To keep the rest of the layout prerendered, wrap the component that calls `usePathname` (or a parent) in a `Suspense` boundary with a fallback.

```typescript
import type { components } from "./api-schema";

type Schemas = components["schemas"];

export type SignalRequest = Schemas["SignalRequest"];
export type SummaryRequest = Schemas["SummaryRequest"];
export type AnalyzeRequest = Schemas["AnalyzeRequest"];
export type SignalResponse = Schemas["SignalResponse"];
export type SummaryResponse = Schemas["SummaryResponse"];
export type AnalyzeResponse = Schemas["AnalyzeResponse"];
export type ModelsResponse = Schemas["ModelsResponse"];
export type HealthResponse = Schemas["HealthResponse"];
export type ModelInfo = Schemas["ModelInfo"];
export type ArticleMeta = Schemas["ArticleMeta"];
export type SignalResult = Schemas["SignalResult"];
export type Timings = Schemas["Timings"];
export type InferenceTimings = Schemas["InferenceTimings"];
export type CacheInfo = Schemas["CacheInfo"];
export type ErrorBody = Schemas["ErrorBody"];
export type ErrorCode = Schemas["ErrorCode"];

export type ParserName = SignalRequest["parser"];
export type ExtractorName = SignalRequest["extractor"];
export type Scope = SignalRequest["scope"];
export type Endpoint = ArticleMeta["endpoint"];
export type Sentiment = SignalResult["sentiment"];
export type PolicyName = SignalResult["policy"];

// The generated request types mark defaulted fields as required; callers only need the url.
type Body<T extends { url: string }> = Pick<T, "url"> & Partial<Omit<T, "url">>;
export type SignalBody = Body<SignalRequest>;
export type SummaryBody = Body<SummaryRequest>;
export type AnalyzeBody = Body<AnalyzeRequest>;

export const PARSERS: readonly ParserName[] = ["selectolax", "lxml", "bs4", "bs4-lxml"];
export const EXTRACTORS: readonly ExtractorName[] = [
  "cascade",
  "jsonld",
  "profile",
  "density",
  "trafilatura",
  "trafilatura-precision",
  "readability",
  "newspaper",
  "justext",
  "strip-tags",
];
export const SCOPES: readonly Scope[] = ["lede", "full"];

const SERVER_ERROR_CODES: Record<ErrorCode, true> = {
  invalid_url: true,
  blocked_destination: true,
  model_not_allowed: true,
  paywalled: true,
  consent_required: true,
  extraction_empty: true,
  unsupported_content: true,
  too_large: true,
  source_blocked: true,
  upstream_http: true,
  schema_violation: true,
  model_unavailable: true,
  llm_unreachable: true,
  upstream_timeout: true,
  inference_timeout: true,
};
export const ERROR_CODES = Object.keys(SERVER_ERROR_CODES) as ErrorCode[];

/** Failures detected in the browser rather than reported by the API envelope. */
export type ClientErrorCode = "network_error" | "invalid_request" | "http_error" | "bad_response";
export type ApiErrorCode = ErrorCode | ClientErrorCode;

export function isErrorCode(value: unknown): value is ErrorCode {
  return typeof value === "string" && Object.hasOwn(SERVER_ERROR_CODES, value);
}

export interface ApiErrorInit {
  code: ApiErrorCode;
  message: string;
  hint?: string | null;
  status?: number | null;
  retryable?: boolean;
  upstreamStatus?: number | null;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly code: ApiErrorCode;
  readonly hint: string | null;
  readonly status: number | null;
  readonly retryable: boolean;
  readonly upstreamStatus: number | null;

  constructor(init: ApiErrorInit) {
    super(init.message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.code = init.code;
    this.hint = init.hint ?? null;
    this.status = init.status ?? null;
    this.retryable = init.retryable ?? false;
    this.upstreamStatus = init.upstreamStatus ?? null;
  }

  static fromBody(body: ErrorBody, status: number | null = null): ApiError {
    return new ApiError({
      code: body.code,
      message: body.message,
      hint: body.hint,
      status,
      retryable: body.retryable,
      upstreamStatus: body.upstream_status,
    });
  }
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function asErrorBody(value: unknown): ErrorBody | null {
  if (!isRecord(value) || !isErrorCode(value.code) || typeof value.message !== "string") return null;
  return {
    code: value.code,
    message: value.message,
    hint: typeof value.hint === "string" ? value.hint : null,
    retryable: value.retryable === true,
    upstream_status: typeof value.upstream_status === "number" ? value.upstream_status : null,
  };
}

/** Maps any error payload (our envelope, FastAPI validation detail, or junk) to an ApiError. */
export function errorFromPayload(status: number, payload: unknown): ApiError {
  const envelope = isRecord(payload) ? asErrorBody(payload.error) : null;
  if (envelope) return ApiError.fromBody(envelope, status);

  // FastAPI request validation runs before our handlers and answers {"detail": [...]}.
  if (isRecord(payload) && Array.isArray(payload.detail)) {
    const first: unknown = payload.detail[0];
    const msg = isRecord(first) && typeof first.msg === "string" ? first.msg : "Request validation failed.";
    const loc = isRecord(first) && Array.isArray(first.loc) ? first.loc.slice(1).join(".") : "";
    return new ApiError({
      code: "invalid_request",
      message: loc ? `${loc}: ${msg}` : msg,
      status,
    });
  }

  return new ApiError({
    code: "http_error",
    message: `The API answered with HTTP ${status}.`,
    status,
    retryable: status >= 500,
  });
}

export async function readError(res: Response): Promise<ApiError> {
  let text = "";
  try {
    text = await res.text();
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
  }
  let payload: unknown = null;
  try {
    payload = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
  } catch {
    payload = null;
  }
  return errorFromPayload(res.status, payload);
}

export function isAbortError(err: unknown): boolean {
  return isRecord(err) || err instanceof Error
    ? (err as { name?: unknown }).name === "AbortError"
    : false;
}

export function toApiError(err: unknown): ApiError {
  if (err instanceof ApiError) return err;
  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
  return new ApiError({ code: "bad_response", message });
}

/** Empty base means same origin, which is how FastAPI serves the static export in production. */
export function apiUrl(path: string): string {
  const base = (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE ?? "").replace(/\/+$/, "");
  if (base) return `${base}${path}`;
  return typeof window === "undefined" ? path : new URL(path, window.location.origin).toString();
}

/** fetch() that turns network failures and non-2xx answers into ApiError; aborts pass through. */
export async function apiFetch(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> {
  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(apiUrl(path), init);
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
    throw new ApiError({
      code: "network_error",
      message: "Could not reach the API.",
      retryable: true,
    });
  }
  if (!res.ok) throw await readError(res);
  return res;
}

async function readJson<T>(res: Response): Promise<T> {
  try {
    return (await res.json()) as T;
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
    throw new ApiError({ code: "bad_response", message: "The API returned invalid JSON.", status: res.status });
  }
}

export function jsonPost(body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal, accept = "application/json"): RequestInit {
  return {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: accept },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
    signal,
  };
}

async function postJson<T>(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
  return readJson<T>(await apiFetch(path, jsonPost(body, signal)));
}

export async function getHealth(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<HealthResponse> {
  return readJson<HealthResponse>(await apiFetch("/api/health", { signal }));
}

export async function getModels(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ModelsResponse> {
  return readJson<ModelsResponse>(await apiFetch("/api/models", { signal }));
}

export function postSignal(body: SignalBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SignalResponse> {
  return postJson<SignalResponse>("/api/signal", body, signal);
}

export function postSummary(body: SummaryBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SummaryResponse> {
  return postJson<SummaryResponse>("/api/summary", body, signal);
}

export function postAnalyze(body: AnalyzeBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<AnalyzeResponse> {
  return postJson<AnalyzeResponse>("/api/analyze", body, signal);
}
```

```typescript
}

export interface ErrorEventData {
  error: ErrorBody;
}

export type StreamEvent<R> =
  | { type: "meta"; data: MetaEventData }
  | { type: "sentiment"; data: SentimentEventData }
  | { type: "summary_delta"; data: SummaryDeltaEventData }
  | { type: "done"; data: DoneEventData<R> }
  | { type: "error"; data: ErrorEventData };

export type StreamEventType = StreamEvent<unknown>["type"];
const EVENT_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<StreamEventType>([
  "meta",
  "sentiment",
  "summary_delta",
  "done",
  "error",
]);

export interface SseFrame {
  event: string;
  data: string;
  id: string | null;
}

/**
 * Incremental text/event-stream parser (WHATWG rules): any of CRLF/LF/CR ends a line, a blank
 * line dispatches, ":" lines are comments, repeated data lines join with "\n".
 */
export class SseParser {
  private buffer = "";
  private skipLeadingLf = false;
  private eventType = "";
  private dataLines: string[] = [];
  private lastId: string | null = null;

  push(chunk: string): SseFrame[] {
    if (!chunk) return [];
    let text = chunk;
    // A CR that ended the previous chunk may be the first half of a CRLF.
    if (this.skipLeadingLf) {
      this.skipLeadingLf = false;
      if (text.startsWith("\n")) text = text.slice(1);
    }
    this.buffer += text;

    const frames: SseFrame[] = [];
    let start = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < this.buffer.length; i++) {
      const ch = this.buffer[i];
      if (ch !== "\n" && ch !== "\r") continue;
      const line = this.buffer.slice(start, i);
      if (ch === "\r") {
        if (i + 1 === this.buffer.length) this.skipLeadingLf = true;
        else if (this.buffer[i + 1] === "\n") i++;
      }
      start = i + 1;
      const frame = this.processLine(line);
      if (frame) frames.push(frame);
    }
    this.buffer = this.buffer.slice(start);
    return frames;
  }

  private processLine(line: string): SseFrame | null {
    if (line === "") return this.dispatch();
    if (line.startsWith(":")) return null;

    const colon = line.indexOf(":");
    const field = colon === -1 ? line : line.slice(0, colon);
    let value = colon === -1 ? "" : line.slice(colon + 1);
    if (value.startsWith(" ")) value = value.slice(1);

    if (field === "event") this.eventType = value;
    else if (field === "data") this.dataLines.push(value);
    else if (field === "id" && !value.includes("\0")) this.lastId = value;
    return null;
  }

  private dispatch(): SseFrame | null {
    const lines = this.dataLines;
    const event = this.eventType || "message";
    this.dataLines = [];
    this.eventType = "";
    if (lines.length === 0) return null;
    return { event, data: lines.join("\n"), id: this.lastId };
  }
}

/** Yields parsed frames; an unterminated trailing frame is dropped, as the SSE spec requires. */
export async function* readSseFrames(body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>): AsyncGenerator<SseFrame> {
  const reader = body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  const parser = new SseParser();
  let finished = false;
  try {
    for (;;) {
      const { value, done } = await reader.read();
      if (done) {
        finished = true;
        return;
      }
      yield* parser.push(value);
    }
  } finally {
    // Early exit (consumer break or abort) must release the network stream.
    if (!finished) await reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
  }
}

export function toStreamEvent<R>(frame: SseFrame): StreamEvent<R> | null {
  if (!EVENT_TYPES.has(frame.event)) return null;
  let data: unknown;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(frame.data);
  } catch {
    throw new ApiError({ code: "bad_response", message: `Malformed "${frame.event}" event from the API.` });
  }
  return { type: frame.event, data } as StreamEvent<R>;
}

export interface StreamOptions {
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}

/**
 * POSTs and yields typed events until `done` or `error`. Errors raised before the stream opens
 * arrive as a JSON envelope and are thrown as ApiError.
 */
export async function* streamEvents<R>(
  path: string,
  body: unknown,
  { signal }: StreamOptions = {},
): AsyncGenerator<StreamEvent<R>> {
  const res = await apiFetch(path, jsonPost(body, signal, "text/event-stream"));
  if (!res.body) throw new ApiError({ code: "bad_response", message: "The API returned an empty stream." });

  for await (const frame of readSseFrames(res.body)) {
    const event = toStreamEvent<R>(frame);
    if (!event) continue;
    yield event;
    if (event.type === "done" || event.type === "error") return;
  }
  throw new ApiError({
    code: "bad_response",
    message: "The stream closed before it finished.",
    retryable: true,
  });
}

export function streamSummary(body: SummaryBody, options?: StreamOptions) {
  return streamEvents<SummaryResponse>("/api/summary/stream", body, options);
}

export function streamAnalyze(body: AnalyzeBody, options?: StreamOptions) {
  return streamEvents<AnalyzeResponse>("/api/analyze/stream", body, options);
}
```

```typescript
  agreement: number | null;
  kappa: number | null;
}

  generatedAt: string | null;

  latency: LatencyBenchmark[];
  summary: SummaryBenchmark[];
  extraction: ExtractionBenchmark[];
  selection: Record<SelectionEndpoint, Selection>;
  articles: ArticleSetStats;
}

function isObject(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/** Structural check at the top level only; the eval report owns row-level correctness. */
export function isBenchmarksV1(value: unknown): value is BenchmarksV1 {
  if (!isObject(value) || value.version !== 1 || typeof value.sample !== "boolean") return false;
  const arrays = ["signal", "latency", "summary", "extraction"] as const;
  return (
    isObject(value.environment) &&
    arrays.every((key) => Array.isArray(value[key])) &&
    isObject(value.selection) &&
    isObject(value.articles)
  );
}

/** Latency budgets settled in the design decisions (native, warm, excluding fetch). */
export const LATENCY_BUDGETS = {
  signalLedeP50Ms: 500,
  ttftMs: 1500,
  completeP50Ms: 4000,
} as const;

export function withinBudget(row: LatencyBenchmark): boolean | null {
  if (row.endpoint === "signal") {
    return row.scope === "lede" ? row.p50Ms <= LATENCY_BUDGETS.signalLedeP50Ms : null;
  }
  if (row.endpoint === "summary" || row.endpoint === "analyze") {
    const ttftOk = row.ttftP50Ms === null || row.ttftP50Ms <= LATENCY_BUDGETS.ttftMs;
    return ttftOk && row.p50Ms <= LATENCY_BUDGETS.completeP50Ms;
  }
  return null;
}
```

```typescript
export function formatMs(ms: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (ms === null || ms === undefined || !Number.isFinite(ms)) return "-";
  if (ms >= 10_000) return `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`;
  if (ms >= 1000) return `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(2)} s`;
  return `${Math.round(ms)} ms`;
}

export function formatPct(value: number | null | undefined, digits = 1): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return `${(value * 100).toFixed(digits)}%`;
}

export function formatNum(value: number | null | undefined, digits = 3): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return value.toFixed(digits);
}

export function formatInt(value: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return Math.round(value).toLocaleString("en-US");
}

export function capitalize(value: string): string {
  return value ? value[0].toUpperCase() + value.slice(1) : value;
}
```

```typescript
import type { ApiError, ArticleMeta, SignalResult, Timings } from "./api";

export type Mode = "split" | "combined";
export type LaneId = "signal" | "summary" | "analyze";
export type LaneStatus = "pending" | "streaming" | "done" | "error" | "cancelled";

export interface Lane {
  id: LaneId;
  status: LaneStatus;
  meta: ArticleMeta | null;
  timings: Timings | null;
  error: ApiError | null;
  // Client clock: milliseconds since the run started, from performance.now().
  signalAtMs: number | null;
  firstTokenAtMs: number | null;
  endAtMs: number | null;
}

export interface RunState {
  runId: number;
  mode: Mode;
  streaming: boolean;
  running: boolean;
  lanes: Lane[];
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity: string | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on the combined stream. */
  serverSignalMs: number | null;
  summary: string;
}

interface Tagged {
  runId: number;
  lane: LaneId;
  atMs: number;
}

export type RunAction =
  | { type: "start"; runId: number; mode: Mode; streaming: boolean; lanes: LaneId[] }
  | ({ type: "meta"; meta: ArticleMeta } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "signal"; signal: SignalResult; entity: string | null; serverMs: number | null } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "delta"; text: string } & Tagged)
  | ({
      type: "done";
      meta: ArticleMeta;
      timings: Timings;
      summary?: string;
      signal?: SignalResult;
      entity?: string | null;
    } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "error"; error: ApiError } & Tagged)
  | { type: "cancel"; runId: number; atMs: number };

export const initialRunState: RunState = {
  runId: 0,
  mode: "split",
  streaming: true,
  running: false,
  lanes: [],
  signal: null,
  entity: null,
  serverSignalMs: null,
  summary: "",
};

function newLane(id: LaneId): Lane {
  return {
    id,
    status: "pending",
    meta: null,
    timings: null,
    error: null,
    signalAtMs: null,
    firstTokenAtMs: null,
    endAtMs: null,
  };
}

const isActive = (lane: Lane) => lane.status === "pending" || lane.status === "streaming";

function patchLane(state: RunState, id: LaneId, patch: (lane: Lane) => Partial<Lane>): RunState {
  const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) => (lane.id === id ? { ...lane, ...patch(lane) } : lane));
  return { ...state, lanes, running: lanes.some(isActive) };
}

export function runReducer(state: RunState, action: RunAction): RunState {
  if (action.type === "start") {
    return {
      ...initialRunState,
      runId: action.runId,
      mode: action.mode,
      streaming: action.streaming,
      running: true,
      lanes: action.lanes.map(newLane),
    };
  }
  // Late events from a superseded run must not leak into the current one.
  if (action.runId !== state.runId) return state;

  switch (action.type) {
    case "meta":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        meta: lane.meta ?? action.meta,
        status: lane.status === "pending" ? "streaming" : lane.status,
      }));
    case "signal":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({ signalAtMs: lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs })),
        signal: action.signal,
        entity: action.entity,
        serverSignalMs: action.serverMs,
      };
    case "delta":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
          firstTokenAtMs: lane.firstTokenAtMs ?? action.atMs,
          status: "streaming",
        })),
        summary: state.summary + action.text,
      };
    case "done": {
      const next = patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        status: "done",
        meta: action.meta,
        timings: action.timings,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
        signalAtMs: action.signal ? (lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs) : lane.signalAtMs,
      }));
      return {
        ...next,
        // The final payload is authoritative over the concatenated deltas.
        summary: action.summary ?? next.summary,
        signal: action.signal ?? next.signal,
        entity: action.entity !== undefined ? action.entity : next.entity,
      };
    }
    case "error":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, () => ({
        status: "error",
        error: action.error,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
      }));
    case "cancel": {
      const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) =>
        isActive(lane) ? { ...lane, status: "cancelled" as const, endAtMs: action.atMs } : lane,
      );
      return { ...state, lanes, running: false };
    }
  }
}

export function laneById(state: RunState, id: LaneId): Lane | undefined {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.id === id);
}

/** Article-level meta from whichever lane reported first. */
export function articleMeta(state: RunState): ArticleMeta | null {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.meta)?.meta ?? null;
}

/** One banner per distinct failure; split lanes often fail identically on a shared fetch. */
export function distinctErrors(state: RunState): { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] {
  const out: { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] = [];
  for (const lane of state.lanes) {
    if (!lane.error) continue;
    const same = out.find((e) => e.error.code === lane.error?.code && e.error.message === lane.error.message);
    if (same) same.lanes.push(lane.id);
    else out.push({ lanes: [lane.id], error: lane.error });
  }
  return out;
}
```

```typescript
import { useCallback, useEffect, useReducer, useRef, type Dispatch } from "react";

import {
  ApiError,
  isAbortError,
  postAnalyze,
  postSignal,
  postSummary,
  toApiError,
  type AnalyzeBody,
  type AnalyzeResponse,
  type ExtractorName,
  type ParserName,
  type Scope,
  type SignalBody,
  type SummaryBody,
  type SummaryResponse,
} from "@/lib/api";
import { initialRunState, runReducer, type LaneId, type Mode, type RunAction } from "@/lib/run-state";
import { streamAnalyze, streamSummary, type StreamEvent } from "@/lib/sse";

export interface RunParams {
  url: string;
  mode: Mode;
  streaming: boolean;
  parser: ParserName;
  extractor: ExtractorName;
  /** Signal scope in split mode; /analyze keeps its server default. */
  scope: Scope;
  /** Empty string lets the server pick the endpoint default. */
  signalModel: string;
  summaryModel: string;
  analyzeModel: string;
}

interface LaneContext {
  runId: number;
  dispatch: Dispatch<RunAction>;
  signal: AbortSignal;
  at: () => number;
}

const withModel = (model: string) => (model ? { model } : {});

async function guarded(ctx: LaneContext, lane: LaneId, work: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await work();
  } catch (err) {
    if (ctx.signal.aborted || isAbortError(err)) return;
    ctx.dispatch({ type: "error", runId: ctx.runId, lane, atMs: ctx.at(), error: toApiError(err) });
  }
}

function handleEvent(
  ctx: LaneContext,
  lane: LaneId,
  event: StreamEvent<SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse>,
): void {
  const tag = { runId: ctx.runId, lane, atMs: ctx.at() };
  switch (event.type) {
    case "meta":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "meta", ...tag, meta: event.data.meta });
      return;
    case "sentiment":
      ctx.dispatch({
        type: "signal",
        ...tag,
        signal: event.data.signal,
        entity: event.data.entity ?? null,
        serverMs: event.data.elapsed_ms,
      });
      return;
    case "summary_delta":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "delta", ...tag, text: event.data.text });
      return;
    case "done": {
      const result = event.data.result;
      const combined = "signal" in result ? result : null;
      ctx.dispatch({
        type: "done",
        ...tag,
        meta: result.meta,
        timings: result.timings,
        summary: result.summary,
        signal: combined?.signal,
        entity: combined ? (combined.entity ?? null) : undefined,
      });
      return;
    }
    case "error":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "error", ...tag, error: ApiError.fromBody(event.data.error) });
      return;
  }
}

function runSignal(ctx: LaneContext, body: SignalBody) {
  return guarded(ctx, "signal", async () => {
    const res = await postSignal(body, ctx.signal);
    ctx.dispatch({
      type: "done",
      runId: ctx.runId,
      lane: "signal",
      atMs: ctx.at(),
      meta: res.meta,
      timings: res.timings,
      signal: res.signal,
    });
  });
}

function runSummary(ctx: LaneContext, body: SummaryBody, streaming: boolean) {
  return guarded(ctx, "summary", async () => {
    if (streaming) {
      for await (const event of streamSummary(body, { signal: ctx.signal })) handleEvent(ctx, "summary", event);
      return;
    }
    const res = await postSummary(body, ctx.signal);
    handleEvent(ctx, "summary", { type: "done", data: { result: res } });
  });
}

function runAnalyze(ctx: LaneContext, body: AnalyzeBody, streaming: boolean) {
  return guarded(ctx, "analyze", async () => {
    if (streaming) {
      for await (const event of streamAnalyze(body, { signal: ctx.signal })) handleEvent(ctx, "analyze", event);
      return;
    }
    const res = await postAnalyze(body, ctx.signal);
    handleEvent(ctx, "analyze", { type: "done", data: { result: res } });
  });
}

/** Owns one in-flight run; starting a new run aborts the previous one. */
export function useAnalysis() {
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(runReducer, initialRunState);
  const controllerRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null);
  const runIdRef = useRef(0);
  const startedAtRef = useRef(0);

  useEffect(() => () => controllerRef.current?.abort(), []);

  const start = useCallback((params: RunParams) => {
    controllerRef.current?.abort();
    const controller = new AbortController();
    controllerRef.current = controller;
    const runId = ++runIdRef.current;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    startedAtRef.current = t0;
    const ctx: LaneContext = { runId, dispatch, signal: controller.signal, at: () => performance.now() - t0 };
    const base = { url: params.url, parser: params.parser, extractor: params.extractor };

    if (params.mode === "split") {
      dispatch({ type: "start", runId, mode: "split", streaming: params.streaming, lanes: ["signal", "summary"] });
      // Fired together on purpose: the backend single-flight shares one fetch between them.
      void runSignal(ctx, { ...base, scope: params.scope, ...withModel(params.signalModel) });
      void runSummary(ctx, { ...base, ...withModel(params.summaryModel) }, params.streaming);
    } else {
      dispatch({ type: "start", runId, mode: "combined", streaming: params.streaming, lanes: ["analyze"] });
      void runAnalyze(ctx, { ...base, ...withModel(params.analyzeModel) }, params.streaming);
    }
  }, []);

  const cancel = useCallback(() => {
    controllerRef.current?.abort();
    controllerRef.current = null;
    dispatch({ type: "cancel", runId: runIdRef.current, atMs: performance.now() - startedAtRef.current });
  }, []);

  return { state, start, cancel };
}
```

```typescript
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

import { getModels, isAbortError, toApiError, type ApiError, type ModelsResponse } from "@/lib/api";

export type ModelsState =
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "ready"; data: ModelsResponse }
  | { status: "error"; error: ApiError };

export function useModels(): ModelsState {
  const [state, setState] = useState<ModelsState>({ status: "loading" });

  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    getModels(controller.signal).then(
      (data) => setState({ status: "ready", data }),
      (err: unknown) => {
        if (!isAbortError(err)) setState({ status: "error", error: toApiError(err) });
      },
    );
    return () => controller.abort();
  }, []);

  return state;
}

```

```typescript
"use client";

import Link from "next/link";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";

import styles from "./SiteHeader.module.css";

const LINKS = [
  { href: "/", label: "Analyze" },
  { href: "/benchmarks/", label: "Benchmarks" },
] as const;

const normalize = (path: string) => path.replace(/\/+$/, "") || "/";

export function SiteHeader() {
  const current = normalize(usePathname() ?? "/");
  return (
    <header className={styles.header}>
      <div className={styles.inner}>
        <Link href="/" className={styles.brand}>
          VeriTrade Analytics
        </Link>
        <nav aria-label="Primary">
          <ul className={styles.links}>
            {LINKS.map(({ href, label }) => (
              <li key={href}>
                <Link
                  href={href}
                  className={styles.link}
                  aria-current={normalize(href) === current ? "page" : undefined}
                >
                  {label}
                </Link>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </nav>
      </div>
    </header>
  );
}
```

```typescript
import type { ApiErrorCode } from "@/lib/api";

import styles from "./ErrorBanner.module.css";

export interface ErrorLike {
  code: ApiErrorCode;
  message: string;
  hint?: string | null;
  status?: number | null;
  retryable?: boolean;
  upstreamStatus?: number | null;
}

export const ERROR_TITLES: Record<ApiErrorCode, string> = {
  invalid_url: "Invalid URL",
  blocked_destination: "Destination not allowed",
  model_not_allowed: "Model not allowed",
  paywalled: "Paywalled article",
  consent_required: "Consent wall",
  extraction_empty: "No article text found",
  unsupported_content: "Unsupported content",
  too_large: "Page too large",
  source_blocked: "Blocked by the source",
  upstream_http: "Source returned an error",
  schema_violation: "Malformed model output",
  model_unavailable: "Model unavailable",
  llm_unreachable: "Ollama unreachable",
  upstream_timeout: "Source timed out",
  inference_timeout: "Model timed out",
  network_error: "API unreachable",
  invalid_request: "Invalid request",
  http_error: "Unexpected HTTP error",
  bad_response: "Unexpected response",
};

// Used only when the server sent no hint of its own.
const FALLBACK_HINTS: Partial<Record<ApiErrorCode, string>> = {
  invalid_url: "Paste a full http(s) article URL.",
  blocked_destination: "Only public hosts on ports 80 and 443 can be fetched.",
  model_not_allowed: "Pick a model from the list; it mirrors the server allowlist.",
  paywalled: "The article is behind a paywall. Try a free source.",
  consent_required: "The site demands a consent choice the fetcher could not make. Try another source.",
  extraction_empty: "Try another extractor or parser.",
  unsupported_content: "The URL must point to an HTML article page.",
  too_large: "The page is larger than the fetch cap.",
  source_blocked: "The publisher refused automated access. Try another source.",
  upstream_http: "The source answered with an error status. Retry later.",
  schema_violation: "Retry; the model output did not match the expected schema.",
  model_unavailable: "Pull the model in Ollama or pick another one.",
  llm_unreachable: "Start Ollama or check OLLAMA_BASE_URL on the backend.",
  upstream_timeout: "The source was too slow to answer. Retry.",
  inference_timeout: "The model took too long. Try a smaller model.",
  network_error: "Start the backend (http://localhost:8000 in development) and retry.",
};

interface ErrorBannerProps {
  error: ErrorLike;
  /** Which request(s) failed, e.g. "Signal and summary". */
  context?: string;
}

export function ErrorBanner({ error, context }: ErrorBannerProps) {
  const hint = error.hint || FALLBACK_HINTS[error.code];
  const status = error.upstreamStatus ?? null;
  return (
    <div role="alert" className={styles.banner} data-code={error.code}>
      <p className={styles.title}>
        {context ? <span className={styles.context}>{context}: </span> : null}
        {ERROR_TITLES[error.code]} <code className={styles.code}>{error.code}</code>
        {error.status ? <span className={styles.status}>HTTP {error.status}</span> : null}
      </p>
      <p className={styles.message}>{error.message}</p>
      {hint ? <p className={styles.hint}>{hint}</p> : null}
      {status !== null || error.retryable ? (
        <p className={styles.extra}>
          {status !== null ? `Upstream status ${status}. ` : ""}
          {error.retryable ? "Retrying may help." : ""}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import type { PolicyName, Sentiment, SignalResult } from "@/lib/api";
import { capitalize, formatMs, formatPct } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./SignalCard.module.css";

const POLICY_NOTES: Record<PolicyName, string> = {
  probability: "threshold on the decision model's class probability",
  "label-logprob": "threshold on the label token probability",
  ordinal: "threshold on |score| of the -2..+2 scale",
};

const ORDER: readonly Sentiment[] = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

/** Direction the model leaned before the threshold turned it into an abstention. */
export function leaning(signal: SignalResult): Sentiment {
  if (signal.probabilities) {
    let best: Sentiment = signal.sentiment;
    for (const s of ORDER) {
      if ((signal.probabilities[s] ?? 0) > (signal.probabilities[best] ?? 0)) best = s;
    }
    return best;
  }
  if (typeof signal.score === "number" && signal.score !== 0) return signal.score > 0 ? "bullish" : "bearish";
  return signal.sentiment;
}

function formatScore(score: number): string {
  return score > 0 ? `+${score}` : String(score);
}

interface SignalCardProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity?: string | null;
  model?: string | null;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the signal arriving. */
  timeToSignalMs?: number | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on a combined stream. */
  serverMs?: number | null;
}

export function SignalCard({ status, signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: SignalCardProps) {
  const busy = !signal && (status === "pending" || status === "streaming");
  return (
    <section className={styles.card} aria-labelledby="signal-heading" aria-busy={busy}>
      <h2 id="signal-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Signal
      </h2>
      {signal ? (
        <SignalBody
          signal={signal}
          entity={entity}
          model={model}
          timeToSignalMs={timeToSignalMs}
          serverMs={serverMs}
        />
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.placeholder}>
          {busy
            ? "Waiting for the signal..."
            : status === "cancelled"
              ? "Cancelled."
              : "No signal: the request failed."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

function SignalBody({ signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: Omit<SignalCardProps, "status">) {
  if (!signal) return null;
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <span
          className={styles.badge}
          data-sentiment={signal.sentiment}
          data-abstained={signal.abstained || undefined}
          data-testid="signal-badge"
        >
          {capitalize(signal.sentiment)}
        </span>
        {signal.abstained ? <span className={styles.abstainTag}>Abstained</span> : null}
        {entity ? <span className={styles.entity}>{entity}</span> : null}
      </div>
      {signal.abstained ? (
        <p className={styles.abstainNote}>
          Below confidence threshold: the call is not confident enough to trade on, so treat it as no
          directional signal.
          {lean !== signal.sentiment ? ` The model leaned ${capitalize(lean)}.` : null}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <dl className={styles.stats}>
        {typeof signal.confidence === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Confidence</dt>
            <dd>{formatPct(signal.confidence)}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof signal.score === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Score</dt>
            <dd>{formatScore(signal.score)} on -2..+2</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <div>
          <dt>Policy</dt>
          <dd>
            <code>{signal.policy}</code> <span className={styles.note}>({POLICY_NOTES[signal.policy]})</span>
          </dd>
        </div>
        {model ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Model</dt>
            <dd>
              <code>{model}</code>
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof timeToSignalMs === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Time to signal</dt>
            <dd>
              {formatMs(timeToSignalMs)}
              {typeof serverMs === "number" ? (
                <span className={styles.note}> (server {formatMs(serverMs)})</span>
              ) : null}
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </dl>
      {signal.probabilities ? (
        <ul className={styles.probs} aria-label="Class probabilities">
          {ORDER.map((s) => {
            const p = signal.probabilities?.[s] ?? 0;
            return (
              <li key={s} className={styles.prob}>
                <span className={styles.probLabel}>{capitalize(s)}</span>
                <span className={styles.probTrack} aria-hidden="true">
                  <span
                    className={styles.probFill}
                    data-sentiment={s}
                    style={{ width: `${Math.max(0, Math.min(1, p)) * 100}%` }}
                  />
                </span>
                <span className={styles.probValue}>{formatPct(p)}</span>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import { formatMs } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./SummaryPanel.module.css";

interface SummaryPanelProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  text: string;
  model?: string | null;
  streaming: boolean;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the first summary token. */
  firstTokenMs?: number | null;
}

function statusLabel(status: LaneStatus, text: string, streaming: boolean): string {
  switch (status) {
    case "pending":
      return streaming ? "Waiting for the first token..." : "Waiting for the summary...";
    case "streaming":
      return text ? "Streaming..." : "Waiting for the first token...";
    case "done":
      return "Complete";
    case "error":
      return "Failed";
    case "cancelled":
      return "Cancelled";
  }
}

export function SummaryPanel({ status, text, model, streaming, firstTokenMs }: SummaryPanelProps) {
  const active = status === "pending" || status === "streaming";
  return (
    <section className={styles.panel} aria-labelledby="summary-heading" aria-busy={active}>
      <div className={styles.header}>
        <h2 id="summary-heading" className={styles.heading}>
          Summary
        </h2>
        <span className={styles.status} data-status={status} data-testid="summary-status">
          {statusLabel(status, text, streaming)}
        </span>
      </div>
      {text ? (
        <p className={styles.text} data-testid="summary-text">
          {text}
          {active ? <span className={styles.caret} aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
        </p>
      ) : status === "done" ? (
        <p className={styles.empty}>The model returned an empty summary.</p>
      ) : null}
      {model || typeof firstTokenMs === "number" ? (
        <p className={styles.footer}>
          {model ? (
            <>
              Model <code>{model}</code>
            </>
          ) : null}
          {model && typeof firstTokenMs === "number" ? " · " : null}
          {typeof firstTokenMs === "number" ? `first token ${formatMs(firstTokenMs)}` : null}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}

```

```typescript
    </section>
  );
}
```

```typescript
import type { CSSProperties } from "react";

import type { Timings } from "@/lib/api";
import { formatMs } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./LatencyBar.module.css";

export type StageKey =
  | "fetch"
  | "consent"
  | "parse"
  | "extract"
  | "load"
  | "prompt"
  | "generation"
  | "inference"
  | "other";

export const STAGE_LABELS: Record<StageKey, string> = {
  fetch: "fetch",
  consent: "consent",
  parse: "parse",
  extract: "extract",
  load: "model load",
  prompt: "prompt eval",
  generation: "generation",
  inference: "inference",
  other: "network + overhead",
};

export interface Segment {
  key: StageKey;
  ms: number;
}

/**
 * Server stages laid end to end; whatever the client waited beyond them is "other". Decision
 * models report only wall time, so they get a single inference segment.
 */
export function stageSegments(timings: Timings, clientTotalMs: number | null): Segment[] {
  const segments: Segment[] = [];
  const push = (key: StageKey, ms: number | null | undefined) => {
    if (typeof ms === "number" && ms > 0) segments.push({ key, ms });
  };
  push("fetch", timings.fetch_ms);
  push("consent", timings.consent_ms);
  push("parse", timings.parse_ms);
  push("extract", timings.extract_ms);
  const inference = timings.inference;
  if (inference) {
    const { load_ms, prompt_eval_ms, eval_ms } = inference;
    const split = [load_ms, prompt_eval_ms, eval_ms].some((ms) => typeof ms === "number");
    if (split) {
      push("load", load_ms);
      push("prompt", prompt_eval_ms);
      push("generation", eval_ms);
    } else {
      push("inference", inference.wall_ms);
    }
  }
  const staged = segments.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.ms, 0);
  push("other", (clientTotalMs ?? timings.total_ms) - staged);
  return segments;
}

export function niceStep(raw: number): number {
  if (raw <= 0) return 1;
  const pow = 10 ** Math.floor(Math.log10(raw));
  const n = raw / pow;
  const mult = n <= 1 ? 1 : n <= 2 ? 2 : n <= 2.5 ? 2.5 : n <= 5 ? 5 : 10;
  return mult * pow;
}

export interface LaneMark {
  kind: "signal" | "token";
  label: string;
  atMs: number;
}

export interface LatencyLane {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  status: LaneStatus;
  timings: Timings | null;
  /** Client-observed completion, ms since submit. */
  endMs: number | null;
  marks: LaneMark[];
}

function laneExtent(lane: LatencyLane): number {
  const markMax = Math.max(0, ...lane.marks.map((m) => m.atMs));
  return Math.max(lane.endMs ?? lane.timings?.total_ms ?? 0, markMax);
}

const pct = (ms: number, axis: number) => `${Math.min(100, (ms / axis) * 100)}%`;

export function LatencyBar({ lanes }: { lanes: LatencyLane[] }) {
  const axis = Math.max(1, ...lanes.map(laneExtent));
  const step = niceStep(axis / 4);
  const ticks: number[] = [];
  for (let t = 0; t <= axis; t += step) ticks.push(t);

  const laneSegments = lanes.map((lane) => (lane.timings ? stageSegments(lane.timings, lane.endMs) : []));
  const usedKeys = new Set(laneSegments.flat().map((s) => s.key));

  return (
    <section className={styles.wrap} aria-labelledby="latency-heading" data-testid="latency">
      <h2 id="latency-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Latency
      </h2>
      <p className={styles.caption}>
        Server stage timings placed on one client time axis, measured from submit with performance.now().
      </p>
      <div className={styles.chart}>
        {lanes.map((lane, i) => {
          let left = 0;
          return (
            <div key={lane.id} className={styles.lane} data-testid={`lane-${lane.id}`}>
              <div className={styles.laneLabel}>{lane.label}</div>
              <div className={styles.track} aria-hidden="true">
                {laneSegments[i].map((segment) => {
                  const style: CSSProperties = { left: pct(left, axis), width: pct(segment.ms, axis) };
                  left += segment.ms;
                  return (
                    <span
                      key={segment.key}
                      className={styles.segment}
                      data-stage={segment.key}
                      data-testid={`segment-${lane.id}-${segment.key}`}
                      style={style}
                      title={`${STAGE_LABELS[segment.key]} ${formatMs(segment.ms)}`}
                    />
                  );
                })}
                {lane.marks.map((mark) => (
                  <span
                    key={mark.kind}
                    className={styles.mark}
                    data-kind={mark.kind}
                    data-testid={`mark-${lane.id}-${mark.kind}`}
                    style={{ left: pct(mark.atMs, axis) }}
                    title={`${mark.label} ${formatMs(mark.atMs)}`}
                  />
                ))}
                {!lane.timings && (lane.status === "pending" || lane.status === "streaming") ? (
                  <span className={styles.running}>running...</span>
                ) : null}
              </div>
            </div>
          );
        })}
        <div className={styles.axis} aria-hidden="true">
          <div />
          <div className={styles.ticks}>
            {ticks.map((t) => (
              <span key={t} className={styles.tick} style={{ left: pct(t, axis) }}>
                {formatMs(t)}
              </span>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <ul className={styles.legend} aria-hidden="true">
        {[...usedKeys].map((key) => (
          <li key={key}>
            <span className={styles.swatch} data-stage={key} />
            {STAGE_LABELS[key]}
          </li>
        ))}
        {lanes.some((l) => l.marks.some((m) => m.kind === "signal")) ? (
          <li>
            <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="signal" />
            signal arrived
          </li>
        ) : null}
        {lanes.some((l) => l.marks.some((m) => m.kind === "token")) ? (
          <li>
            <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="token" />
            first token
          </li>
        ) : null}
      </ul>

      <div className={styles.details}>
        {lanes.map((lane, i) => (
          <div key={lane.id} className={styles.detail}>
            <h3 className={styles.detailHeading}>{lane.label}</h3>
            <dl className={styles.values}>
              {lane.marks.map((mark) => (
                <div key={mark.kind}>
                  <dt>{mark.label}</dt>
                  <dd>{formatMs(mark.atMs)}</dd>
                </div>
              ))}
              {lane.endMs !== null ? (
                <div>
                  <dt>complete (client)</dt>
                  <dd>{formatMs(lane.endMs)}</dd>
                </div>
              ) : null}
              {lane.timings ? (
                <div>
                  <dt>server total</dt>
                  <dd>{formatMs(lane.timings.total_ms)}</dd>
                </div>
              ) : null}
              {typeof lane.timings?.inference?.ttft_ms === "number" ? (
                <div>
                  <dt>TTFT (server)</dt>
                  <dd>{formatMs(lane.timings.inference.ttft_ms)}</dd>
                </div>
              ) : null}
              {laneSegments[i].map((segment) => (
                <div key={segment.key}>
                  <dt>{STAGE_LABELS[segment.key]}</dt>
                  <dd>{formatMs(segment.ms)}</dd>
                </div>
              ))}
              {lane.timings ? (
                <div>
                  <dt>cache</dt>
                  <dd>
                    fetch {lane.timings.cache.fetch}, result {lane.timings.cache.result}
                  </dd>
                </div>
              ) : null}
            </dl>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

```
</details>
