```python
"""One small DOM protocol over four HTML parsers, so every own strategy runs unchanged on each backend."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import json
import re
import time
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Any, Protocol

import lxml.html
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from bs4.element import NavigableString, PreformattedString, Tag
from lxml.cssselect import CSSSelector
from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser, LexborNode

from veritrade.extract.types import ParserName

# Text inside these never reaches a reader.
SKIP_TAGS = frozenset(
    {"script", "style", "noscript", "template", "svg", "math", "iframe", "object", "head", "select", "textarea"}
)
# Phrasing content joins without a separator; every other element (block, custom, SGML) separates text.
INLINE_TAGS = frozenset(
    {
        "a", "abbr", "acronym", "b", "bdi", "bdo", "big", "cite", "code", "data", "del", "dfn", "em", "font",
        "i", "img", "ins", "kbd", "label", "mark", "nobr", "picture", "q", "s", "samp", "small", "source",
        "span", "strike", "strong", "sub", "sup", "time", "tt", "u", "var", "wbr",
    }
)  # fmt: skip

_INVISIBLE = dict.fromkeys(map(ord, "​‌‍⁠﻿\xad"), None)
_XML_DECL = re.compile(r"^﻿?\s*<\?xml[^>]*\?>", re.IGNORECASE)
_LD_OPEN = re.compile(r"<script\b[^>]*application/ld\+json[^>]*>", re.IGNORECASE)
_SCRIPT_CLOSE = re.compile(r"</script", re.IGNORECASE)
_LD_WRAPPER = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:<!--|<!\[CDATA\[)|(?:-->|\]\]>)\s*$")
_META_TITLE = re.compile(
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name)\s*=\s*["'](?:og:title|twitter:title)["'][^>]*>""", re.IGNORECASE
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_TITLE_TAG = re.compile(r"<title\b[^>]*>(.*?)</title\s*>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse all whitespace (incl. nbsp) and drop zero-width characters."""
    return " ".join(text.translate(_INVISIBLE).split())


def scan_json_ld(html: str) -> list[Any]:
    """Parse every JSON-LD script straight from the source string; no DOM needed, same on every parser."""
    out: list[Any] = []
    pos = 0
    while (opening := _LD_OPEN.search(html, pos)) is not None:
        closing = _SCRIPT_CLOSE.search(html, opening.end())
        if closing is None:
            break
        pos = closing.end()
        payload = _LD_WRAPPER.sub("", html[opening.end() : closing.start()]).strip()
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(payload, strict=False))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return out


def head_title(html: str) -> str:
    """og:title, twitter:title or <title> read from the raw string, for paths that never build a DOM."""
    if (meta := _META_TITLE.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        if text := normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")):
            return text
    if title := _TITLE_TAG.search(html):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", title.group(1))))
    return ""


class Node(Protocol):
    @property
    def tag(self) -> str: ...

    def text(self) -> str: ...

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None: ...


class Container:
    """A non-inline element on the path of a text block; density scores these."""

    __slots__ = ("_hint", "_hint_of", "depth", "native", "tag")

    def __init__(self, tag: str, native: Any, depth: int, hint_of: Callable[[Any], str]) -> None:
        self.tag = tag
        self.native = native
        self.depth = depth
        self._hint_of = hint_of
        self._hint: str | None = None

    @property
    def hint(self) -> str:
        """Lowercased class and id, computed only for the few containers density inspects."""
        if self._hint is None:
            self._hint = self._hint_of(self.native)
        return self._hint


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Block:
    text: str
    link_chars: int
    tag: str
    path: tuple[Container, ...]  # nearest container first

    @property
    def link_density(self) -> float:
        return self.link_chars / len(self.text) if self.text else 0.0


class Dom(Protocol):
    @property
    def parser(self) -> ParserName: ...

    @property
    def parse_ms(self) -> float: ...

    def select(self, css: str) -> list[Node]: ...

    def remove(self, css: str) -> int: ...

    def iter_blocks(self) -> Iterator[Block]: ...

    def json_ld(self) -> list[Any]: ...

    def title(self) -> str: ...


class _Node[E]:
    __slots__ = ("_dom", "native")

    def __init__(self, dom: _TreeDom[E], native: E) -> None:
        self._dom = dom
        self.native = native

    @property
    def tag(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._tag(self.native)

    def text(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._text(self.native)

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        return self._dom._attr(self.native, name)


class _TreeDom[E](ABC):
    """Shared walkers; a backend only supplies parse, select, drop and child iteration."""

    name: ParserName

    def __init__(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._html = html
        self._parse_ms = 0.0
        self._built = False
        self._json_ld: list[Any] | None = None

    # --- backend primitives ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    @abstractmethod
    def _build(self, html: str) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[E]: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _drop(self, el: E) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _tag(self, el: E) -> str: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _attr(self, el: E, name: str) -> str | None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _content(self, el: E) -> Iterator[E | str]:
        """Children in order: plain text as str, elements as E; comments and doctypes are skipped."""

    @abstractmethod
    def _body(self) -> E | None: ...

    # --- protocol -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def parser(self) -> ParserName:
        return self.name

    @property
    def parse_ms(self) -> float:
        return self._parse_ms

    def _ensure(self) -> None:
        # Lazy so a JSON-LD hit never pays for a parse; the build time is reported separately.
        if not self._built:
            start = time.perf_counter()
            self._build(self._html)
            self._parse_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
            self._built = True

    def select(self, css: str) -> list[Node]:
        self._ensure()
        return [_Node(self, el) for el in self._select(css)]

    def remove(self, css: str) -> int:
        self._ensure()
        matches = self._select(css)
        # Reverse document order detaches nested matches before their ancestors are destroyed.
        for el in reversed(matches):
            self._drop(el)
        return len(matches)

    def json_ld(self) -> list[Any]:
        if self._json_ld is None:
            self._json_ld = scan_json_ld(self._html)
        return self._json_ld

    def title(self) -> str:
        self._ensure()
        for css in ('meta[property="og:title"]', 'meta[name="twitter:title"]'):
            for el in self._select(css):
                if content := normalize(self._attr(el, "content") or ""):
                    return content
        for el in self._select("title"):
            return self._text(el)
        return ""

    def iter_blocks(self) -> Iterator[Block]:
        self._ensure()
        root = self._body()
        if root is None:
            return iter(())
        return iter(self._blocks(root))

    # --- shared walkers -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _hint(self, el: E) -> str:
        return f"{self._attr(el, 'class') or ''} {self._attr(el, 'id') or ''}".lower()

    def _text(self, el: E) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        self._collect(el, parts)
        return normalize("".join(parts))

    def _collect(self, el: E, parts: list[str]) -> None:
        for item in self._content(el):
            if isinstance(item, str):
                parts.append(item)
                continue
            tag = self._tag(item)
            if tag in SKIP_TAGS:
                continue
            if tag in INLINE_TAGS:
                self._collect(item, parts)
            else:
                parts.append(" ")
                self._collect(item, parts)
                parts.append(" ")

    def _blocks(self, root: E) -> list[Block]:
        """Split visible text at every non-inline boundary; each run remembers its container path."""
        out: list[Block] = []
        buffer: list[str] = []
        link_chars = 0
        stack: list[Container] = [Container(self._tag(root), root, 0, self._hint)]

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal link_chars
            if buffer:
                text = normalize("".join(buffer))
                if text:
                    path = tuple(reversed(stack))
                    out.append(Block(text, min(link_chars, len(text)), stack[-1].tag, path))
                buffer.clear()
            link_chars = 0

        def walk(el: E, in_link: bool) -> None:
            nonlocal link_chars
            for item in self._content(el):
                if isinstance(item, str):
                    buffer.append(item)
                    if in_link:
                        link_chars += len(item.strip())
                    continue
                tag = self._tag(item)
                if tag in SKIP_TAGS:
                    continue
                if tag in INLINE_TAGS:
                    walk(item, in_link or tag == "a")
                elif tag == "br":
                    buffer.append(" ")
                else:
                    flush()
                    stack.append(Container(tag, item, len(stack), self._hint))
                    walk(item, in_link)
                    flush()
                    stack.pop()

        walk(root, False)
        flush()
        return out


# --- selectolax (Lexbor) --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SelectolaxDom(_TreeDom[LexborNode]):
    name: ParserName = "selectolax"

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._tree = LexborHTMLParser(html)

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[LexborNode]:
        return list(self._tree.css(css))

    def _drop(self, el: LexborNode) -> None:
        el.decompose()

    def _tag(self, el: LexborNode) -> str:
        return el.tag or ""

    def _attr(self, el: LexborNode, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.attrs.get(name)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: LexborNode) -> Iterator[LexborNode | str]:
        for child in el.iter(include_text=True):
            tag = child.tag
            if tag == "-text":
                yield child.text_content or ""
            elif tag and tag[0] != "-" and tag[0] != "!":
                yield child

    def _body(self) -> LexborNode | None:
        return self._tree.body or self._tree.root


# --- lxml -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@lru_cache(maxsize=256)
def _lxml_selector(css: str) -> CSSSelector:
    return CSSSelector(css, translator="html")


class LxmlDom(_TreeDom[lxml.html.HtmlElement]):
    name: ParserName = "lxml"

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        # lxml refuses str input that still declares an encoding (XHTML pages).
        source = _XML_DECL.sub("", html, count=1)
        try:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(source)
        except lxml.etree.ParserError:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring("<html><body></body></html>")

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[lxml.html.HtmlElement]:
        return list(_lxml_selector(css)(self._root))

    def _drop(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> None:
        if el.getparent() is not None:
            el.drop_tree()

    def _tag(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> str:
        tag = el.tag
        return tag if isinstance(tag, str) else ""

    def _attr(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.get(name)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> Iterator[lxml.html.HtmlElement | str]:
        if el.text:
            yield el.text
        for child in el:
            if isinstance(child.tag, str):
                yield child
            if child.tail:
                yield child.tail

    def _body(self) -> lxml.html.HtmlElement | None:
        body = self._root.find("body")
        return body if body is not None else self._root


# --- BeautifulSoup (html.parser or lxml tree builder) ---------------------------------------------


class _SoupDom(_TreeDom[Tag]):
    features: str

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._soup = BeautifulSoup(html, self.features)

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[Tag]:
        return list(self._soup.select(css))

    def _drop(self, el: Tag) -> None:
        el.decompose()

    def _tag(self, el: Tag) -> str:
        return el.name

    def _attr(self, el: Tag, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.attrs.get(name)
        if isinstance(value, list):
            return " ".join(value)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: Tag) -> Iterator[Tag | str]:
        for child in el.children:
            if isinstance(child, Tag):
                yield child
            elif isinstance(child, NavigableString) and not isinstance(child, PreformattedString):
                yield child

    def _body(self) -> Tag | None:
        body = self._soup.body
        return body if body is not None else self._soup


class SoupDom(_SoupDom):
    name: ParserName = "bs4"
    features = "html.parser"


class SoupLxmlDom(_SoupDom):
    name: ParserName = "bs4-lxml"
    features = "lxml"


BACKENDS: dict[ParserName, type[_TreeDom[Any]]] = {
    "selectolax": SelectolaxDom,
    "lxml": LxmlDom,
    "bs4": SoupDom,
    "bs4-lxml": SoupLxmlDom,
}


def parse(html: str, parser: ParserName = "selectolax") -> Dom:
    """A Dom over `html`; the tree is built on first use and its build time lands in `parse_ms`."""
    return BACKENDS[parser](html)
```

```python
"""Per-source profiles from sources.toml and the paragraph rules every own strategy applies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from functools import cache
from importlib import resources
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, Node, normalize

# Unambiguous press-release tails; they end the body on any page, on top of a profile's own markers.
GENERIC_STOPS = (
    "Forward-Looking Statement",
    "Forward Looking Statement",
    "Cautionary Statement",
    "Safe Harbor",
    "Media Contact",
    "Investor Contact",
    "Investors Contact",
    "Investor Relations Contact",
)
# Whole-line UI leftovers that sit between body paragraphs.
BOILERPLATE_LINES = frozenset(
    {
        "advertisement", "continue reading", "read more", "read next", "recommended stories",
        "related articles", "related content", "related stories", "scroll to continue", "share this article",
        "show less", "show more", "sign up", "skip advertisement", "story continues", "subscribe",
        "view comments",
    }
)  # fmt: skip
_BOILERPLATE_TRAIL = " .:»›>…"
# "About Acme" ends a release, "About 40% of" does not: name-style markers need a capital or a short line.
_HEADING_WORDS = 8


class Fate(StrEnum):
    KEEP = "keep"
    EMPTY = "empty"
    NESTED = "nested"
    SHORT = "short"
    BOILERPLATE = "boilerplate"
    STOP = "stop"
    AFTER_STOP = "after_stop"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Verdict:
    fate: Fate
    phrase: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Profile:
    source: str
    body: str
    drop: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    title: str | None = None
    lede_paragraphs: int = 2
    min_words: int = 1
    stop_markers: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    paywall: str | None = None

    @property
    def stops(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return self.stop_markers + tuple(m for m in GENERIC_STOPS if m not in self.stop_markers)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Source:
    key: str
    name: str
    domains: tuple[str, ...]
    status: str
    kind: str
    profile: Profile | None


def _profile(key: str, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Profile:
    return Profile(
        source=key,
        body=str(raw["body"]),
        drop=tuple(str(s) for s in raw.get("drop", ())),
        title=raw.get("title"),
        lede_paragraphs=int(raw.get("lede_paragraphs", 2)),
        min_words=int(raw.get("min_words", 1)),
        stop_markers=tuple(str(s) for s in raw.get("stop_markers", ())),
        paywall=raw.get("paywall"),
    )


@cache
def sources() -> dict[str, Source]:
    text = resources.files("veritrade").joinpath("data/sources.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    out: dict[str, Source] = {}
    for key, raw in tomllib.loads(text).get("sources", {}).items():
        profile = raw.get("profile")
        out[key] = Source(
            key=key,
            name=str(raw.get("name", key)),
            domains=tuple(str(d).lower() for d in raw.get("domains", ())),
            status=str(raw.get("status", "")),
            kind=str(raw.get("kind", "")),
            profile=_profile(key, profile) if isinstance(profile, dict) else None,
        )
    return out


@cache
def _domain_index() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {domain: key for key, source in sources().items() for domain in source.domains}


def source_for_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """Source key for the URL's host or its closest listed parent domain (uk.finance.yahoo.com -> yahoo)."""
    host = (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").rstrip(".").lower()
    index = _domain_index()
    while host:
        if (key := index.get(host)) is not None:
            return key
        _, _, host = host.partition(".")
    return None


def profile_for(source_key: str | None) -> Profile | None:
    source = sources().get(source_key) if source_key else None
    return source.profile if source else None


# --- paragraph rules --------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def stop_marker(text: str, markers: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
    lowered = text.lower()
    for marker in markers:
        if not lowered.startswith(marker.lower()):
            continue
        rest = text[len(marker) :]
        if marker.endswith(" ") and rest and not rest[0].isupper() and len(text.split()) > _HEADING_WORDS:
            continue
        return marker
    return None


def boilerplate_line(text: str) -> str | None:
    line = text.lower().rstrip(_BOILERPLATE_TRAIL)
    return line if line in BOILERPLATE_LINES else None


def triage(texts: Sequence[str], profile: Profile | None) -> list[Verdict]:
    """Fate of every candidate paragraph, in order; the skeleton capture replays these to stay in sync."""
    min_words = profile.min_words if profile else 1
    lede = profile.lede_paragraphs if profile else 2
    stops = profile.stops if profile else GENERIC_STOPS
    verdicts: list[Verdict] = []
    anchor = ""
    kept = 0
    stopped = False
    for text in texts:
        if stopped:
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.AFTER_STOP))
            continue
        if not text:
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.EMPTY))
            continue
        # A selector list can match an <li> and the <p> inside it; the outer text already holds the inner.
        if anchor and len(text) < len(anchor) and text in anchor:
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.NESTED))
            continue
        anchor = text
        if len(text.split()) < min_words:
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.SHORT))
        elif phrase := boilerplate_line(text):
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.BOILERPLATE, phrase))
        elif kept >= lede and (marker := stop_marker(text, stops)):
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.STOP, marker))
            stopped = True
        else:
            verdicts.append(Verdict(Fate.KEEP))
            kept += 1
    return verdicts


def refine(texts: Sequence[str], profile: Profile | None) -> list[str]:
    return [text for text, v in zip(texts, triage(texts, profile), strict=True) if v.fate is Fate.KEEP]


# --- strategy -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def select_body(dom: Dom, profile: Profile) -> list[Node]:
    """Body candidates in document order after the profile's drop selectors ran."""
    for css in profile.drop:
        dom.remove(css)
    return dom.select(profile.body)


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    profile = profile_for(source_key)
    if profile is None:
        return []
    return refine([normalize(node.text()) for node in select_body(dom, profile)], profile)

```

```python
"""schema.org Article metadata and body from JSON-LD, including @graph containers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import re
from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, normalize, split_sentences
from veritrade.extract.profiles import Profile, profile_for, refine

ARTICLE_TYPES = frozenset(
    {
        "AnalysisNewsArticle", "Article", "BackgroundNewsArticle", "BlogPosting", "NewsArticle",
        "OpinionNewsArticle", "Report", "ReportageNewsArticle", "ReviewNewsArticle", "TechArticle",
    }
)  # fmt: skip
# Bodies that arrive as one blob are regrouped so "first N paragraphs" still means an opening.
_GROUP_SENTENCES = 3
_GROUP_WORDS = 90
_BLOCK_TAG = re.compile(r"</?(?:p|div|li|h[1-6]|blockquote|ul|ol)\b[^>]*>|<br\s*/?>", re.IGNORECASE)
_ANY_TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")


def nodes(objects: list[Any]) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    stack: list[Any] = list(reversed(objects))
    while stack:
        item = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            yield item
            stack.extend(reversed(list(item.values())))
        elif isinstance(item, list):
            stack.extend(reversed(item))


def types_of(node: dict[str, Any]) -> set[str]:
    raw = node.get("@type")
    values = [raw] if isinstance(raw, str) else raw if isinstance(raw, list) else []
    # "https://schema.org/NewsArticle" and "schema:NewsArticle" name the same type.
    return {re.split(r"[/:#]", v)[-1] for v in values if isinstance(v, str)}


def article_nodes(objects: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [node for node in nodes(objects) if types_of(node) & ARTICLE_TYPES]


def _text_field(node: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> str | None:
    value = node.get(key)
    if isinstance(value, list) and value:
        value = value[0]
    if isinstance(value, str) and (text := normalize(html_lib.unescape(value))):
        return text
    return None


def headline(objects: list[Any]) -> str | None:
    for node in article_nodes(objects):
        if text := _text_field(node, "headline") or _text_field(node, "name"):
            return text
    return None


def date_published(objects: list[Any]) -> str | None:
    for node in [*article_nodes(objects), *nodes(objects)]:
        if text := _text_field(node, "datePublished"):
            return text
    return None


def is_paywalled(objects: list[Any]) -> bool:
    """True when any node says isAccessibleForFree false; the body may still be complete (metered sites)."""
    for node in nodes(objects):
        value = node.get("isAccessibleForFree")
        if value is False or (isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().lower() == "false"):
            return True
    return False


def article_body(objects: list[Any]) -> str:
    bodies = [b for node in article_nodes(objects) if isinstance(b := node.get("articleBody"), str)]
    if not bodies:
        bodies = [b for node in nodes(objects) if isinstance(b := node.get("articleBody"), str)]
    return max(bodies, key=len, default="")


def split_body(body: str) -> list[str]:
    if "<" in body and _BLOCK_TAG.search(body):
        body = _ANY_TAG.sub("", _BLOCK_TAG.sub("\n\n", body))
    body = html_lib.unescape(body)
    chunks = re.split(r"\n\s*\n", body) if "\n\n" in body else body.split("\n")
    out: list[str] = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        if not (text := normalize(chunk)):
            continue
        if len(text.split()) <= _GROUP_WORDS:
            out.append(text)
        else:
            out.extend(_group(split_sentences(text)))
    return out


def _group(sentences: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    words = 0
    for sentence in sentences:
        n = len(sentence.split())
        if current and (len(current) >= _GROUP_SENTENCES or words + n > _GROUP_WORDS):
            out.append(" ".join(current))
            current, words = [], 0
        current.append(sentence)
        words += n
    if current:
        out.append(" ".join(current))
    return out


def paragraphs(objects: list[Any], profile: Profile | None) -> list[str]:
    return refine(split_body(article_body(objects)), profile)


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return paragraphs(dom.json_ld(), profile_for(source_key))
```

```python
"""Generic body finder for pages without a profile: the tightest container that holds most of the prose."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from veritrade.extract.dom import Block, Container, Dom
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for, refine

# Never article text. <form> stays: ASP.NET pages wrap the whole document in one.
JUNK = (
    "script, style, noscript, template, iframe, svg, nav, header, footer, aside, figure, figcaption, "
    "button, input, select, textarea, dialog"
)
HEADINGS = frozenset({"h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6"})
PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 6  # blocks that vote for a container
MAX_LINK_DENSITY = 0.5
# Tightest container still holding this share of the voted words; looser lets teasers in, tighter cuts ledes.
SHARE = 0.85
HINT_DEPTH = 5  # class/id hints only count close to the text, so a page-level "has-sidebar" class is harmless
NEGATIVE_HINT = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[\s_-])(?:ads?|advert\w*|banner|breadcrumbs?|byline|caption|comments?|cookie\w*|credits?|"
    r"disclaimer|footer|menu|modal|nav\w*|newsletter\w*|outbrain|popular|promo\w*|recirc\w*|recommend\w*|"
    r"related\w*|share|sharing|sidebar|signup|social|sponsor\w*|subscri\w*|taboola|trending)(?=$|[\s_-])"
)


def _negative(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> bool:
    for container in block.path[:HINT_DEPTH]:
        if container is until or container.tag in ("body", "html"):
            return False
        if NEGATIVE_HINT.search(container.hint):
            return True
    return False


def _votes(block: Block) -> int:
    words = len(block.text.split())
    if words < PROSE_MIN_WORDS or block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > MAX_LINK_DENSITY:
        return 0
    return 0 if _negative(block, None) else words


def best_container(blocks: list[Block]) -> Container | None:
    totals: dict[Container, int] = {}
    for block in blocks:
        if votes := _votes(block):
            for container in block.path:
                totals[container] = totals.get(container, 0) + votes
    if not totals:
        return None
    top = max(totals.values())
    # Candidates above the share lie on one ancestor chain, so the deepest is the tightest.
    return max((c for c, words in totals.items() if words >= SHARE * top), key=lambda c: c.depth)


def _is_content(block: Block, container: Container) -> bool:
    if block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > MAX_LINK_DENSITY or _negative(block, container):
        return False
    words = len(block.text.split())
    return words >= 5 or (words >= 2 and block.text[-1] in ".!?:\"”")


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    dom.remove(JUNK)
    blocks = list(dom.iter_blocks())
    container = best_container(blocks)
    if container is None:
        return []
    texts = [b.text for b in blocks if container in b.path and _is_content(b, container)]
    return refine(texts, profile_for(source_key))
```

```python
"""Cheapest trustworthy strategy first: JSON-LD, then the source profile, then text density."""

from __future__ import annotations

from veritrade.extract import density, jsonld, profiles
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom

JSONLD_MIN_CHARS = 400
PROFILE_MIN_WORDS = 80


def _words(paragraphs: list[str]) -> int:
    return sum(len(p.split()) for p in paragraphs)


def run(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """(winning method, paragraphs); a JSON-LD hit returns before the DOM is ever built."""
    tried: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    body = jsonld.extract(dom, url, source_key)
    if sum(len(p) for p in body) >= JSONLD_MIN_CHARS:
        return "jsonld", body
    tried.append(("jsonld", body))
    if profiles.profile_for(source_key) is not None:
        body = profiles.extract(dom, url, source_key)
        if _words(body) >= PROFILE_MIN_WORDS:
            return "profile", body
        tried.append(("profile", body))
    tried.append(("density", density.extract(dom, url, source_key)))
    # A short release beats an empty density pass; ties go to the more specific method.
    return max(reversed(tried), key=lambda item: _words(item[1]))


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return run(dom, url, source_key)[1]

```

```python
"""Off-the-shelf extractors behind one signature; each is imported on first use and brings its own parser."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Callable

from veritrade.extract.dom import normalize, parse
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName

_XML_DECL = re.compile(r"^﻿?\s*<\?xml[^>]*\?>", re.IGNORECASE)


def _lines(text: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return [line for raw in (text or "").splitlines() if (line := normalize(raw))]


def _trafilatura(html: str, url: str, *, precision: bool) -> list[str]:
    import trafilatura

    text = trafilatura.extract(
        html,
        url=url,
        favor_precision=precision,
        include_comments=False,
        include_tables=False,
        deduplicate=False,
        with_metadata=False,
        output_format="txt",
    )
    return _lines(text)


def _readability(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    from readability import Document

    fragment = Document(_XML_DECL.sub("", html, count=1), url=url).summary(html_partial=True)
    return [block.text for block in parse(fragment, "lxml").iter_blocks()]


def _newspaper(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    from newspaper import Article

    # Parse the given HTML only: no download, no image probing, no on-disk URL memo.
    article = Article(url, language="en", fetch_images=False, follow_meta_refresh=False, memorize_articles=False)
    article.download(input_html=html)
    article.parse()
    return _lines(article.text)


def _justext(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    import justext

    found = justext.justext(html.encode("utf-8"), justext.get_stoplist("English"), encoding="utf-8")
    return [text for p in found if not p.is_boilerplate and (text := normalize(p.text))]


def _strip_tags(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    """Baseline: every visible text run on the page, scripts and styles removed."""
    return [block.text for block in parse(html, "selectolax").iter_blocks()]


ADAPTERS: dict[ExtractorName, Callable[[str, str], list[str]]] = {
    "trafilatura": lambda html, url: _trafilatura(html, url, precision=False),
    "trafilatura-precision": lambda html, url: _trafilatura(html, url, precision=True),
    "readability": _readability,
    "newspaper": _newspaper,
    "justext": _justext,
    "strip-tags": _strip_tags,
}


def extract(name: ExtractorName, html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    return ADAPTERS[name](html, url)

```

```python
"""Single entry point from HTML to Article; parse and extract time are measured separately."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from veritrade.errors import ExtractionEmpty
from veritrade.extract import cascade, density, jsonld, profiles, third_party
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, head_title, normalize, parse, scan_json_ld
from veritrade.extract.profiles import source_for_url
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS, Article, ExtractorName, ParserName

__all__ = ["MIN_WORDS", "extract", "source_for_url"]

MIN_WORDS = 40

OWN: dict[ExtractorName, Callable[[Dom, str, str | None], list[str]]] = {
    "jsonld": jsonld.extract,
    "profile": profiles.extract,
    "density": density.extract,
}
_PUBLISHED_META = re.compile(
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name|itemprop)\s*=\s*["']"""
    r"""(?:article:published_time|datePublished|pubdate|publishdate)["'][^>]*>""",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)


def _published_meta(html: str) -> str | None:
    if (meta := _PUBLISHED_META.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")) or None
    return None


def _dom_title(dom: Dom, source: str | None) -> str:
    profile = profiles.profile_for(source)
    if profile is not None and profile.title:
        for node in dom.select(profile.title):
            if text := node.text():
                return text
    return dom.title()


def extract(
    html: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax",
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade",
) -> Article:
    """Raises ExtractionEmpty when fewer than MIN_WORDS words come out."""
    source = source_for_url(url)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    if extractor in PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS:
        dom = parse(html, parser)
        if extractor == "cascade":
            method, paragraphs = cascade.run(dom, url, source)
        else:
            method, paragraphs = extractor, OWN[extractor](dom, url, source)
        objects = dom.json_ld()
        title = jsonld.headline(objects) or _dom_title(dom, source)
        used_parser: ParserName | None = parser
    else:
        method, paragraphs = extractor, third_party.extract(extractor, html, url)
        objects = scan_json_ld(html)
        title = jsonld.headline(objects) or head_title(html)
        dom, used_parser = None, None
    published_at = jsonld.date_published(objects) or _published_meta(html)
    paywalled = jsonld.is_paywalled(objects)
    total_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    parse_ms = dom.parse_ms if dom is not None else 0.0

    article = Article(
        url=url,
        title=title,
        paragraphs=tuple(paragraphs),
        published_at=published_at,
        source=source,
        method=method,
        parser=used_parser,
        extractor=extractor,
        parse_ms=parse_ms,
        extract_ms=total_ms - parse_ms,
        paywalled=paywalled,
    )
    if article.word_count < MIN_WORDS:
        host = urlsplit(url).hostname or url
        raise ExtractionEmpty(
            f"The {extractor} extractor found {article.word_count} words on {host}; "
            f"at least {MIN_WORDS} are needed",
            hint="Try another extractor (for example trafilatura), or check that the URL is a single "
            "article rather than a section or video page.",
        )
    return article
```

```python
"""What the model reads: the headline plus the lede or the whole body, cut to a token budget."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Sequence

from veritrade.extract.dom import split_sentences
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for
from veritrade.extract.types import Article, Scope

CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
LEDE_PARAGRAPHS = 2
LEDE_MIN_TOKENS = 60  # a dateline-only first paragraph is topped up with the next one
LEDE_MAX_TOKENS = 200
_SEP = "\n\n"


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return math.ceil(len(text) / CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def lede_paragraphs(article: Article) -> list[str]:
    profile = profile_for(article.source)
    count = profile.lede_paragraphs if profile else LEDE_PARAGRAPHS
    out = list(article.paragraphs[:count])
    for paragraph in article.paragraphs[count:]:
        if estimate_tokens(_SEP.join(out)) >= LEDE_MIN_TOKENS:
            break
        out.append(paragraph)
    return out


def _cut(paragraph: str, room: int, *, mid_sentence: bool) -> str:
    kept = ""
    for sentence in split_sentences(paragraph):
        candidate = f"{kept} {sentence}" if kept else sentence
        if len(candidate) > room:
            break
        kept = candidate
    if kept or not mid_sentence:
        return kept
    head = paragraph[: room + 1]
    return head[:room] if " " not in head else head.rsplit(" ", 1)[0]


def fit(paragraphs: Sequence[str], budget_chars: int) -> list[str]:
    """Whole paragraphs, then whole sentences; words are cut only when not even one sentence fits."""
    out: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for paragraph in paragraphs:
        sep = len(_SEP) if out else 0
        if used + sep + len(paragraph) <= budget_chars:
            out.append(paragraph)
            used += sep + len(paragraph)
            continue
        if partial := _cut(paragraph, budget_chars - used - sep, mid_sentence=not out):
            out.append(partial)
        break
    return out


def build_input(article: Article, scope: Scope, max_tokens: int) -> str:
    """'TITLE: ...' then a blank line and the body; the estimate (chars / 4) never exceeds max_tokens."""
    if max_tokens <= 0:
        raise ValueError("max_tokens must be positive")
    budget = max_tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN
    head = f"TITLE: {article.title}" if article.title else ""
    if len(head) > budget:
        return fit([head], budget)[0] if fit([head], budget) else ""
    room = budget - len(head) - (len(_SEP) if head else 0)
    if scope == "lede":
        body = fit(lede_paragraphs(article), min(room, LEDE_MAX_TOKENS * CHARS_PER_TOKEN))
    else:
        body = fit(article.paragraphs, room)
    return _SEP.join([head, *body] if head else body)

```

```python
"""One small DOM protocol over four HTML parsers, so every own strategy runs unchanged on each backend."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import json
import re
import threading
import time
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Protocol

import lxml.etree
import lxml.html
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from bs4.element import NavigableString, PreformattedString, Tag
from lxml.cssselect import CSSSelector
from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser, LexborNode

from veritrade.extract.types import ParserName

# Text inside these never reaches a reader.
SKIP_TAGS = frozenset(
    {"script", "style", "noscript", "template", "svg", "math", "iframe", "object", "head", "select", "textarea"}
)
# Phrasing content joins without a separator; every other element (block, custom, SGML) separates text.
INLINE_TAGS = frozenset(
    {
        "a", "abbr", "acronym", "b", "bdi", "bdo", "big", "cite", "code", "data", "del", "dfn", "em", "font",
        "i", "img", "ins", "kbd", "label", "mark", "nobr", "picture", "q", "s", "samp", "small", "source",
        "span", "strike", "strong", "sub", "sup", "time", "tt", "u", "var", "wbr",
    }
)  # fmt: skip

_INVISIBLE = dict.fromkeys(map(ord, "​‌‍⁠﻿\xad"), None)
_XML_DECL = re.compile(r"^﻿?\s*<\?xml[^>]*\?>", re.IGNORECASE)
_LD_OPEN = re.compile(r"<script\b[^>]*application/ld\+json[^>]*>", re.IGNORECASE)
_SCRIPT_CLOSE = re.compile(r"</script", re.IGNORECASE)
_LD_WRAPPER = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:<!--|<!\[CDATA\[)|(?:-->|\]\]>)\s*$")
_META_TITLE = re.compile(
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name)\s*=\s*["'](?:og:title|twitter:title)["'][^>]*>""", re.IGNORECASE
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_TITLE_TAG = re.compile(r"<title\b[^>]*>(.*?)</title\s*>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse all whitespace (incl. nbsp) and drop zero-width characters."""
    return " ".join(text.translate(_INVISIBLE).split())


_SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"""[.!?]["'”’)\]]*(?=\s+["'“‘(\[]?[A-Z0-9])""")
_LAST_TOKEN = re.compile(r"(\S+)$")
_ABBREVIATIONS = frozenset(
    {
        "approx", "apr", "aug", "co", "corp", "dec", "dr", "e.g", "est", "feb", "fig", "gen", "gov", "i.e",
        "inc", "jan", "jr", "jul", "jun", "llc", "ltd", "mar", "mr", "mrs", "ms", "no", "nov", "oct", "plc",
        "prof", "rep", "sen", "sep", "sept", "sr", "st", "u.k", "u.s", "vs",
    }
)  # fmt: skip


def split_sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Rule-based splitter: good enough to cut at a boundary, not a linguistic tool."""
    out: list[str] = []
    start = 0
    for match in _SENTENCE_END.finditer(text):
        if match.group(0)[0] == "." and (token := _LAST_TOKEN.search(text, start, match.start())):
            word = token.group(1)
            if word.lower().rstrip(".") in _ABBREVIATIONS or (len(word) == 1 and word.isupper()):
                continue
        out.append(text[start : match.end()].strip())
        start = match.end()
    if tail := text[start:].strip():
        out.append(tail)
    return out


def scan_json_ld(html: str) -> list[Any]:
    """Parse every JSON-LD script straight from the source string; no DOM needed, same on every parser."""
    out: list[Any] = []
    pos = 0
    while (opening := _LD_OPEN.search(html, pos)) is not None:
        closing = _SCRIPT_CLOSE.search(html, opening.end())
        if closing is None:
            break
        pos = closing.end()
        payload = _LD_WRAPPER.sub("", html[opening.end() : closing.start()]).strip()
        try:
            out.append(json.loads(payload, strict=False))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return out


def head_title(html: str) -> str:
    """og:title, twitter:title or <title> read from the raw string, for paths that never build a DOM."""
    if (meta := _META_TITLE.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        if text := normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")):
            return text
    if title := _TITLE_TAG.search(html):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", title.group(1))))
    return ""


class Node(Protocol):
    @property
    def tag(self) -> str: ...

    def text(self) -> str: ...

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None: ...


class Container:
    """A non-inline element on the path of a text block; density scores these."""

    __slots__ = ("_hint", "_hint_of", "depth", "native", "tag")

    def __init__(self, tag: str, native: Any, depth: int, hint_of: Callable[[Any], str]) -> None:
        self.tag = tag
        self.native = native
        self.depth = depth
        self._hint_of = hint_of
        self._hint: str | None = None

    @property
    def hint(self) -> str:
```

```
    def hint(self) -> str:
        """Lowercased class and id, computed only for the few containers density inspects."""
        if self._hint is None:

def _lxml_selector(css: str) -> CSSSelector:
    # Compiled XPath objects are not safe to share across threads, so the cache is per thread.
    cache: dict[str, CSSSelector] | None = getattr(_local, "selectors", None)
    if cache is None:
        cache = _local.selectors = {}
    if (selector := cache.get(css)) is None:
        selector = cache[css] = CSSSelector(css, translator="html")
    return selector


class LxmlDom(_TreeDom[lxml.html.HtmlElement]):
    name: ParserName = "lxml"

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        # lxml refuses str input that still declares an encoding (XHTML pages).
        source = _XML_DECL.sub("", html, count=1)
        try:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(source)
        except lxml.etree.ParserError:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring("<html><body></body></html>")
```

```bash
"""Rewrite invisible/non-ASCII control characters in source files as \\uXXXX escapes."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

INVISIBLE = {0x200B, 0x200C, 0x200D, 0x2060, 0xFEFF, 0x00AD, 0x00A0}

for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    path = Path(name)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    fixed = "".join(f"\\u{ord(c):04x}" if ord(c) in INVISIBLE else c for c in text)
    if fixed != text:
        path.write_text(fixed, encoding="utf-8")
        print("fixed", name)
EOF
```

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Block:
    text: str
    link_chars: int
    tag: str
    path: tuple[Container, ...]  # nearest container first

    @property
    def link_density(self) -> float:
        return self.link_chars / len(self.text) if self.text else 0.0


class Dom(Protocol):
    @property
    def parser(self) -> ParserName: ...

    @property
    def parse_ms(self) -> float: ...

    def select(self, css: str) -> list[Node]: ...

    def remove(self, css: str) -> int: ...

    def iter_blocks(self) -> Iterator[Block]: ...

    def json_ld(self) -> list[Any]: ...

    def title(self) -> str: ...


class _Node[E]:
    __slots__ = ("_dom", "native")

    def __init__(self, dom: _TreeDom[E], native: E) -> None:
        self._dom = dom
        self.native = native

    @property
    def tag(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._tag(self.native)

    def text(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._text(self.native)

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        return self._dom._attr(self.native, name)


class _TreeDom[E](ABC):
    """Shared walkers; a backend only supplies parse, select, drop and child iteration."""

    name: ParserName

    def __init__(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._html = html
        self._parse_ms = 0.0
        self._built = False
        self._json_ld: list[Any] | None = None

    # --- backend primitives ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    @abstractmethod
    def _build(self, html: str) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[E]: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _drop(self, el: E) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _tag(self, el: E) -> str: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _attr(self, el: E, name: str) -> str | None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def _content(self, el: E) -> Iterator[E | str]:
        """Children in order: plain text as str, elements as E; comments and doctypes are skipped."""

    @abstractmethod
    def _body(self) -> E | None: ...

    # --- protocol -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def parser(self) -> ParserName:
        return self.name

    @property
    def parse_ms(self) -> float:
        return self._parse_ms

    def _ensure(self) -> None:
        # Lazy so a JSON-LD hit never pays for a parse; the build time is reported separately.
        if not self._built:
            start = time.perf_counter()
            self._build(self._html)
            self._parse_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
            self._built = True

    def select(self, css: str) -> list[Node]:
        self._ensure()
        return [_Node(self, el) for el in self._select(css)]

    def remove(self, css: str) -> int:
        self._ensure()
        matches = self._select(css)
        # Reverse document order detaches nested matches before their ancestors are destroyed.
        for el in reversed(matches):
            self._drop(el)
        return len(matches)

    def json_ld(self) -> list[Any]:
        if self._json_ld is None:
            self._json_ld = scan_json_ld(self._html)
        return self._json_ld

    def title(self) -> str:
        self._ensure()
        for css in ('meta[property="og:title"]', 'meta[name="twitter:title"]'):
            for el in self._select(css):
                if content := normalize(self._attr(el, "content") or ""):
                    return content
        for el in self._select("title"):
            return self._text(el)
        return ""

    def iter_blocks(self) -> Iterator[Block]:
        self._ensure()
        root = self._body()
        if root is None:
            return iter(())
        return iter(self._blocks(root))

    # --- shared walkers -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _hint(self, el: E) -> str:
        return f"{self._attr(el, 'class') or ''} {self._attr(el, 'id') or ''}".lower()

    def _text(self, el: E) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        self._collect(el, parts)
        return normalize("".join(parts))

    def _collect(self, el: E, parts: list[str]) -> None:
        for item in self._content(el):
            if isinstance(item, str):
                parts.append(item)
                continue
            tag = self._tag(item)
            if tag in SKIP_TAGS:
                continue
            if tag in INLINE_TAGS:
                self._collect(item, parts)
            else:
                parts.append(" ")
                self._collect(item, parts)
                parts.append(" ")

    def _blocks(self, root: E) -> list[Block]:
        """Split visible text at every non-inline boundary; each run remembers its container path."""
        out: list[Block] = []
        buffer: list[str] = []
        link_chars = 0
        stack: list[Container] = [Container(self._tag(root), root, 0, self._hint)]

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal link_chars
            if buffer:
                text = normalize("".join(buffer))
                if text:
                    path = tuple(reversed(stack))
                    out.append(Block(text, min(link_chars, len(text)), stack[-1].tag, path))
                buffer.clear()
            link_chars = 0

        def walk(el: E, in_link: bool) -> None:
            nonlocal link_chars
            for item in self._content(el):
                if isinstance(item, str):
                    buffer.append(item)
                    if in_link:
                        link_chars += len(item.strip())
                    continue
                tag = self._tag(item)
                if tag in SKIP_TAGS:
                    continue
                if tag in INLINE_TAGS:
                    walk(item, in_link or tag == "a")
                elif tag == "br":
                    buffer.append(" ")
                else:
                    flush()
                    stack.append(Container(tag, item, len(stack), self._hint))
                    walk(item, in_link)
                    flush()
                    stack.pop()

        walk(root, False)
        flush()
        return out


# --- selectolax (Lexbor) --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SelectolaxDom(_TreeDom[LexborNode]):
    name: ParserName = "selectolax"

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._tree = LexborHTMLParser(html)

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[LexborNode]:
        return list(self._tree.css(css))

    def _drop(self, el: LexborNode) -> None:
        el.decompose()

    def _tag(self, el: LexborNode) -> str:
        return el.tag or ""

    def _attr(self, el: LexborNode, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.attrs.get(name)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: LexborNode) -> Iterator[LexborNode | str]:
        for child in el.iter(include_text=True):
            tag = child.tag
            if tag == "-text":
                yield child.text_content or ""
            elif tag and tag[0] != "-" and tag[0] != "!":
                yield child

    def _body(self) -> LexborNode | None:
        return self._tree.body or self._tree.root


# --- lxml -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


_local = threading.local()


def _lxml_selector(css: str) -> CSSSelector:
    # Compiled XPath objects are not safe to share across threads, so the cache is per thread.
    cache: dict[str, CSSSelector] | None = getattr(_local, "selectors", None)
    if cache is None:
        cache = _local.selectors = {}
    if (selector := cache.get(css)) is None:
        selector = cache[css] = CSSSelector(css, translator="html")
    return selector


class LxmlDom(_TreeDom[lxml.html.HtmlElement]):
    name: ParserName = "lxml"

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        try:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(strip_xml_declaration(html))
        except lxml.etree.ParserError:
            self._root = lxml.html.document_fromstring("<html><body></body></html>")

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[lxml.html.HtmlElement]:
        return list(_lxml_selector(css)(self._root))

    def _drop(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> None:
        if el.getparent() is not None:
            el.drop_tree()

    def _tag(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> str:
        tag = el.tag
        return tag if isinstance(tag, str) else ""

    def _attr(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.get(name)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: lxml.html.HtmlElement) -> Iterator[lxml.html.HtmlElement | str]:
        if el.text:
            yield el.text
        for child in el:
            if isinstance(child.tag, str):
                yield child
            if child.tail:
                yield child.tail

    def _body(self) -> lxml.html.HtmlElement | None:
        body = self._root.find("body")
        return body if body is not None else self._root


# --- BeautifulSoup (html.parser or lxml tree builder) ---------------------------------------------


class _SoupDom(_TreeDom[Tag]):
    features: str

    def _build(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._soup = BeautifulSoup(html, self.features)

    def _select(self, css: str) -> list[Tag]:
        return list(self._soup.select(css))

    def _drop(self, el: Tag) -> None:
        el.decompose()

    def _tag(self, el: Tag) -> str:
        return el.name

    def _attr(self, el: Tag, name: str) -> str | None:
        value = el.attrs.get(name)
        if isinstance(value, list):
            return " ".join(value)
        return value if isinstance(value, str) else None

    def _content(self, el: Tag) -> Iterator[Tag | str]:
        for child in el.children:
            # Comments, doctypes and CDATA are PreformattedString subclasses of NavigableString.
            if isinstance(child, Tag) or not isinstance(child, PreformattedString):
                yield child

    def _body(self) -> Tag | None:
        body = self._soup.body
        return body if body is not None else self._soup


class SoupDom(_SoupDom):
    name: ParserName = "bs4"
    features = "html.parser"


class SoupLxmlDom(_SoupDom):
    name: ParserName = "bs4-lxml"
    features = "lxml"


BACKENDS: dict[ParserName, type[_TreeDom[Any]]] = {
    "selectolax": SelectolaxDom,
    "lxml": LxmlDom,
    "bs4": SoupDom,
    "bs4-lxml": SoupLxmlDom,
}


def parse(html: str, parser: ParserName = "selectolax") -> Dom:
    """A Dom over `html`; the tree is built on first use and its build time lands in `parse_ms`."""
    return BACKENDS[parser](html)
```

```python
"""Generic body finder for pages without a profile: the tightest container that holds most of the prose."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from veritrade.extract.dom import Block, Container, Dom
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for, refine

# Never article text. <form> stays: ASP.NET pages wrap the whole document in one.
JUNK = (
    "script, style, noscript, template, iframe, svg, nav, header, footer, aside, figure, figcaption, "
    "button, input, select, textarea, dialog"
)
HEADINGS = frozenset({"h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6"})
PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 6  # blocks that vote for a container
MAX_LINK_DENSITY = 0.5
# Tightest container still holding this share of the voted words; looser lets teasers in, tighter cuts ledes.
SHARE = 0.85
HINT_DEPTH = 5  # class/id hints only count close to the text, so a page-level "has-sidebar" class is harmless
NEGATIVE_HINT = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[\s_-])(?:ads?|advert\w*|banner|breadcrumbs?|byline|caption|comments?|cookie\w*|credits?|"
    r"disclaimer|footer|menu|modal|nav\w*|newsletter\w*|outbrain|popular|promo\w*|recirc\w*|recommend\w*|"
    r"related\w*|share|sharing|sidebar|signup|social|sponsor\w*|subscri\w*|taboola|trending)(?=$|[\s_-])"
)


def _negative(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> bool:
    for container in block.path[:HINT_DEPTH]:
        if container is until or container.tag in ("body", "html"):
            return False
        if NEGATIVE_HINT.search(container.hint):
            return True
    return False


def _votes(block: Block) -> int:
    words = len(block.text.split())
    if words < PROSE_MIN_WORDS or block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > MAX_LINK_DENSITY:
        return 0
```

```python
"""Generic body finder for pages without a profile: the tightest container that holds most of the prose."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from functools import lru_cache

from veritrade.extract.dom import Block, Container, Dom
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for, refine

# Never article text. <form> stays: ASP.NET pages wrap the whole document in one.
JUNK = (
    "script, style, noscript, template, iframe, svg, nav, header, footer, aside, figure, figcaption, "
    "button, input, select, textarea, dialog"
)
HEADINGS = frozenset({"h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6"})
PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 6  # blocks that vote for a container
MAX_LINK_DENSITY = 0.5
# Tightest container still holding this share of the voted words; looser lets teasers in, tighter cuts ledes.
SHARE = 0.85
HINT_DEPTH = 5  # class/id hints only count close to the text, so a page-level "has-sidebar" class is harmless
NEGATIVE_TOKEN = re.compile(
    r"ads?|advert\w*|banner|breadcrumbs?|byline|caption|comments?|cookie\w*|credits?|disclaimer|footer|menu|"
    r"modal|nav\w*|newsletter\w*|outbrain|popular|promo\w*|recirc\w*|recommend\w*|related\w*|share|sharing|"
    r"sidebar|signup|social|sponsor\w*|subscri\w*|taboola|trending"
)
POSITIVE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"(?:article|body|content|entry|main|post|prose|story|text)\w*")
# Tailwind variants such as "xl:group-[:has(#rail-recirc)]" describe layout, not the element's role.
_UTILITY_CLASS = re.compile(r"[:\[\]()/#&!@]")


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def negative_hint(hint: str) -> bool:
    """A class or id names a non-article role: by its first word, or anywhere with no article-ish word."""
    for name in hint.split():
        if _UTILITY_CLASS.search(name):
            continue
        tokens = [t for t in re.split(r"[-_]+", name) if t]
        if not tokens:
            continue
        if NEGATIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(tokens[0]):
            return True
        if any(NEGATIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(t) for t in tokens) and not any(
            POSITIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(t) for t in tokens
        ):
            return True
    return False


def _negative(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> bool:
    for container in block.path[:HINT_DEPTH]:
        if container is until or container.tag in ("body", "html"):
            return False
        if negative_hint(container.hint):
            return True
    return False


def _votes(block: Block) -> int:
    words = len(block.text.split())
    if words < PROSE_MIN_WORDS or block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > MAX_LINK_DENSITY:
        return 0
    return 0 if _negative(block, None) else words


def best_container(blocks: list[Block]) -> Container | None:
    totals: dict[Container, int] = {}
    for block in blocks:
        if votes := _votes(block):
            for container in block.path:
                totals[container] = totals.get(container, 0) + votes
    if not totals:
        return None
    top = max(totals.values())
    # Candidates above the share lie on one ancestor chain, so the deepest is the tightest.
    return max((c for c, words in totals.items() if words >= SHARE * top), key=lambda c: c.depth)


def _is_content(block: Block, container: Container) -> bool:
    if block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > MAX_LINK_DENSITY or _negative(block, container):
        return False
    words = len(block.text.split())
    return words >= 5 or (words >= 2 and block.text[-1] in '.!?:"”')


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    dom.remove(JUNK)
    blocks = list(dom.iter_blocks())
    container = best_container(blocks)
    if container is None:
        return []
    texts = [b.text for b in blocks if container in b.path and _is_content(b, container)]
    return refine(texts, profile_for(source_key))

```

```python
"""Generic body finder for pages without a profile: the tightest container that holds most of the prose."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from functools import lru_cache

from veritrade.extract.dom import Block, Container, Dom
from veritrade.extract.profiles import GENERIC_STOPS, profile_for, refine, stop_marker

# Never article text. <form> stays: ASP.NET pages wrap the whole document in one.
JUNK = (
    "script, style, noscript, template, iframe, svg, nav, header, footer, aside, figure, figcaption, "
    "button, input, select, textarea, dialog"
)
HEADINGS = frozenset({"h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6"})
CELLS = frozenset({"td", "th"})
VOTE_MIN_WORDS = 6
VOTE_MAX_LINK_DENSITY = 0.25  # teaser cards and link lists must not pull the container towards them
KEEP_MAX_LINK_DENSITY = 0.5
# Tightest container still holding this share of the votes; looser lets teasers in, tighter cuts ledes.
SHARE = 0.85
HINT_DEPTH = 5  # hints only count close to the text, so a page-level "has-sidebar" class is harmless
NEGATIVE_TOKEN = re.compile(
    r"ads?|advert\w*|banner|breadcrumbs?|byline|caption|comments?|cookie\w*|credits?|disclaimer|footer|menu|"
    r"modal|nav\w*|newsletter\w*|outbrain|popular|promo\w*|recirc\w*|recommend\w*|related\w*|share|sharing|"
    r"sidebar|signup|social|sponsor\w*|subscri\w*|taboola|trending|video\w*"
)
POSITIVE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"(?:article|body|content|entry|main|post|prose|story|text)\w*")
# Tailwind variants such as "xl:group-[:has(#rail-recirc)]" describe layout, not the element's role.
_UTILITY_CLASS = re.compile(r"[:\[\]()/#&!@]")
_CAMEL = re.compile(r"(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])")


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def negative_hint(hint: str) -> bool:
    """A class or id names a non-article role: by its first word, or anywhere with no article-ish word."""
    for name in hint.split():
        if _UTILITY_CLASS.search(name):
            continue
        tokens = [t for t in re.split(r"[-_]+", _CAMEL.sub("-", name).lower()) if t]
        if not tokens:
            continue
        if NEGATIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(tokens[0]):
            return True
        if any(NEGATIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(t) for t in tokens) and not any(
            POSITIVE_TOKEN.fullmatch(t) for t in tokens
        ):
            return True
    return False


def _below(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> list[Container]:
    """Containers between the text and `until` (exclusive), nearest first."""
    out: list[Container] = []
    for container in block.path:
        if container is until:
            break
        out.append(container)
    return out


def _negative(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> bool:
    for container in _below(block, until)[:HINT_DEPTH]:
        if container.tag in ("body", "html"):
            return False
        if negative_hint(container.hint):
            return True
    return False


def _in_cell(block: Block, until: Container | None) -> bool:
    return any(c.tag in CELLS for c in _below(block, until))


def _votes(block: Block, *, cells: bool) -> int:
    words = len(block.text.split())
    if words < VOTE_MIN_WORDS or block.tag in HEADINGS or block.link_density > VOTE_MAX_LINK_DENSITY:
        return 0
    if _negative(block, None) or (not cells and _in_cell(block, None)):
        return 0
    return words


def best_container(blocks: list[Block]) -> Container | None:
    # Data tables never vote, unless the whole page is laid out in one (old EDGAR filer agents).
    for cells in (False, True):
        totals: dict[Container, int] = {}
        for block in blocks:
            if votes := _votes(block, cells=cells):
                for container in block.path:
                    totals[container] = totals.get(container, 0) + votes
        if totals:
            top = max(totals.values())
            # Candidates above the share lie on one ancestor chain, so the deepest is the tightest.
            return max((c for c, n in totals.items() if n >= SHARE * top), key=lambda c: c.depth)
    return None


def _keep(block: Block, container: Container, stops: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    if block.link_density > KEEP_MAX_LINK_DENSITY or _negative(block, container) or _in_cell(block, container):
        return False
    words = len(block.text.split())
    if block.tag not in HEADINGS and (words >= 5 or (words >= 2 and block.text[-1] in '.!?:"”')):
        return True
    # Short "About Acme" headings are not prose, but they must reach the rules to end the body.
    return stop_marker(block.text, stops) is not None


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    dom.remove(JUNK)
    blocks = list(dom.iter_blocks())
    container = best_container(blocks)
    if container is None:
        return []
    profile = profile_for(source_key)
    stops = profile.stops if profile else GENERIC_STOPS
    texts = [b.text for b in blocks if container in b.path and _keep(b, container, stops)]
    return refine(texts, profile)

```

```bash
from pathlib import Path

p = Path("backend/src/veritrade/extract/density.py")
s = p.read_text()
old = '''    for cells in (False, True):
        totals: dict[Container, int] = {}
        for block in blocks:
            if votes := _votes(block, cells=cells):
                for container in block.path:
                    totals[container] = totals.get(container, 0) + votes
        if totals:
            top = max(totals.values())
            # Candidates above the share lie on one ancestor chain, so the deepest is the tightest.
            best = max((c for c, n in totals.items() if n >= SHARE * top), key=lambda c: c.depth)
            # Disclosures and pitches outside the story can hold more than 15%; a named body still wins.
            named = [
                c
                for c, n in totals.items()
                if c.depth > best.depth and n >= POSITIVE_SHARE * totals[best] and positive_hint(c.hint)
            ]
            return max(named, key=lambda c: c.depth) if named else best
    return None'''
new = '''    for cells in (False, True):
        totals: dict[Container, int] = {}
        voters: dict[Container, int] = {}
        for block in blocks:
            if votes := _votes(block, cells=cells):
                for container in block.path:
                    totals[container] = totals.get(container, 0) + votes
                    voters[container] = voters.get(container, 0) + 1
        if totals:
            top = max(totals.values())
            # Candidates above the share lie on one ancestor chain, so the deepest is the tightest.
            best = max((c for c, n in totals.items() if n >= SHARE * top), key=lambda c: c.depth)
            # Disclosures and pitches outside the story can hold more than 15%; a named body still wins.
            named = [
                c
                for c, n in totals.items()
                if c.depth > best.depth
                and voters[c] > 1
                and n >= POSITIVE_SHARE * totals[best]
                and positive_hint(c.hint)
            ]
            return max(named, key=lambda c: c.depth) if named else best
    return None'''
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
EOF
```

```python
def extract(
    html: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax",
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade",
) -> Article:
    """Raises ExtractionEmpty when fewer than MIN_WORDS words come out."""
    source = source_for_url(url)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    if extractor in PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS:
        dom = parse(html, parser)
        if extractor == "cascade":
            method, paragraphs = cascade.run(dom, url, source)
        else:
            method, paragraphs = extractor, OWN[extractor](dom, url, source)
        objects = dom.json_ld()
        title = jsonld.headline(objects) or _dom_title(dom, source)
        used_parser: ParserName | None = parser
    else:
        method, paragraphs = extractor, third_party.extract(extractor, html, url)
        objects = scan_json_ld(html)
        title = jsonld.headline(objects) or head_title(html)
        dom, used_parser = None, None
    published_at = jsonld.date_published(objects) or _published_meta(html)
    paywalled = jsonld.is_paywalled(objects)
    total_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    parse_ms = dom.parse_ms if dom is not None else 0.0

    article = Article(
        url=url,
        title=title,
        paragraphs=tuple(paragraphs),
        published_at=published_at,
        source=source,
        method=method,
        parser=used_parser,
        extractor=extractor,
        parse_ms=parse_ms,
        extract_ms=total_ms - parse_ms,
        paywalled=paywalled,
    )
    if article.word_count < MIN_WORDS:
        host = urlsplit(url).hostname or url
        raise ExtractionEmpty(
            f"The {extractor} extractor found {article.word_count} words on {host}; "
            f"at least {MIN_WORDS} are needed",
            hint="Try another extractor (for example trafilatura), or check that the URL is a single "
            "article rather than a section or video page.",
        )
    return article

```

```
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name|itemprop)\s*=\s*["']"""
    r"""(?:article:published_time|datePublished|pubdate|publishdate)["'][^>]*>""",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)


def _published_meta(html: str) -> str | None:
    if (meta := _PUBLISHED_META.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")) or None
    return None


def _dom_title(dom: Dom, source: str | None) -> str:
    profile = profiles.profile_for(source)
    if profile is not None and profile.title:
        for node in dom.select(profile.title):
            if text := node.text():
                return text
    return dom.title()
```

```python
"""Turn one probe capture per source into a publisher-text-free skeleton fixture for the extractor tests.

The DOM (tags, classes, ids, data-*, JSON-LD shape) is kept; every text node, text attribute and JSON-LD
string is replaced from a small fixed vocabulary, so the fixtures can be committed. Body paragraphs carry
VTB-<k> markers, all other text VTX-<k>, which lets tests measure recall and leakage per extractor.

    uv run python scripts/capture_skeletons.py                 # every primary/backup source, capture 1
    uv run python scripts/capture_skeletons.py --pick sec=2    # another capture for one source
"""

    "second", "series", "service", "several", "shared", "staff", "system", "team", "that", "the", "this",
    "to", "update", "visitor", "was", "week", "were", "while", "will", "with", "would", "year",

URL_ATTRS = frozenset(
```
