# 01 - Design decisions

Every decision below was settled with Kris in a `/grill-me` interview (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-18) before any code
was written. Background facts came from read-only research agents (local machine, Ollama library, Docker/CI, news
sources, datasets, transcript format) and were re-verified against primary sources where they were surprising
(the Ollama decision-model API). The full conversation is in `.context/transcript/`.

Guiding principle (Kris, R2): **this is a PoC - balance the level of rigor per aspect**, no exhaustive sweeps.

## Round 1

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Where does the Ollama server run? | Native Ollama on the host is the documented default on macOS; a `bundled` compose profile runs `ollama/ollama` (CPU) for Linux/CI; `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` switches; benchmarks are labelled `native-metal` / `docker-cpu` | Docker Desktop cannot pass Apple's GPU into Linux containers (~0.2x prompt-eval, ~0.4x generation vs native); reviewers on Macs will have Ollama anyway |
| Q2 | What does "precision" mean, how is a winner picked? | Positives are directional calls (bullish/bearish); neutral is the safe default. Selection metric F0.5 macro over {bullish, bearish}; bullish<->bearish inversions capped at 2%; winner = best F0.5 inside the latency budget, else the Pareto knee | A wrong call costs a trade, a missed call costs little; F0.5 cannot be gamed by "always neutral" |
| Q3 | Sentiment output contract | 3-class `sentiment` + `abstained`; compare two precision knobs for generative models (label-token logprob threshold vs ordinal -2..+2 \|score\| threshold) and keep the better one; decision models threshold their native class probabilities | Ollama emits logprobs, but only for non-streaming calls; the ordinal knob also works when streaming |
| Q4 | What does the quick signal read? | `scope=lede` (headline + opening paragraphs) by default, `scope=full` available; both evaluated for accuracy and speed | Lede matches headline-level datasets and decision-model context limits; prompt length drives latency |
| Q5 | Article-level gold set | 90 real articles (10 sources x 3 classes x 3), labelled by Opus subagents, no human check | Public datasets are sentences/headlines; real requests are full articles |
| Q6 | Public datasets and splits | Dev: stratified 300 from Twitter Financial News train. Holdout: full Twitter validation + Financial PhraseBank AllAgree (downloaded at eval time, never committed, CC BY-NC-SA) + FinEntity single-label paragraphs | Twitter FNS already uses Bearish/Bullish/Neutral and has official splits; FPB is the cleanest cross-domain check |
| Q7 | Prompt tuning method | Automated grid per model, then one manual error-analysis pass, freeze, run holdout once. Optional backlog starts with a DSPy-style optimizer loop | Reproducible and explainable within a PoC budget |
| Q8 | API surface | `/api/signal`, `/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`, `/api/models`, `/api/health`; model allowlist; per-URL fetch cache with single-flight; result cache; timing breakdown in every response; SSE **and** JSON variants for `/summary` and `/analyze` | Streaming improves perceived latency; both variants make the comparison measurable |
| Q9 | How the UI is served | Reopened in round 2 (R1) | - |
| Q10 | Extraction | Full parser x extractor comparison matrix, switchable from the UI, results published | Extraction quality and speed both feed end-to-end latency |
| Q11 | Fixtures and publisher rights | Skeleton fixtures (real DOM structure, synthetic text) + scheduled live smoke; article texts never committed (URL + hash + labels only) | Respect each publisher's content rights in a public repo |
| Q12 | CI | Everything on GitHub Actions, including e2e with a real tiny model | Free for public repos |
| Q13 | Transcript | Redacted raw JSONL + rendered Markdown/HTML + `meta.json` under `.context/transcript/`, stripped of anything not suitable for a public repo | The brief asks for the AI log; Kris wants reviewers to read it |
| Q14 | Git workflow | Milestone commits straight to `main`, no feature branches; repo-local author Kristiyan Dimitrov; public repo `cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics` | Solo PoC |
| Q15 | Tooling | Python 3.13 uv workspace (`backend`, `evals`), ruff + mypy; Node 24 + pnpm, Next.js 16 strict TS, ESLint + Prettier, Vitest + RTL + MSW, Playwright | Conventional, fast |
| Q16 | Native Ollama install | `brew install ollama` + `brew services` | Metal acceleration for evals and the native path |
| Q17 | Model roster | See R2 and the follow-ups | - |
| Q18 | Top-10 sources | Yahoo Finance, CNBC, AP News, Investing.com, Motley Fool, Benzinga, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business; backups Fortune, Business Wire, Guardian, BBC; the live probe decides | Reviewer likelihood x accessibility; the brief names earnings reports, EDGAR is their primary source |
| Q19 | Fetch identity | Standard browser header set, no evasion (no captcha solving, proxies or TLS impersonation); typed `source_blocked` / `paywalled` / `consent_required` errors with hints; `SEC_USER_AGENT` for EDGAR | Neither end of the spectrum |
| Q20 | Yahoo EU consent wall | Submit "reject all" and cache the cookie; fall back to `consent_required` | Gets the article without granting tracking consent on anyone's behalf |

## Round 2

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | UI serving topology | FastAPI serves the static Next.js export from the same origin (multi-stage Docker build); dev uses `pnpm dev` + CORS for localhost | No proxy hop on the latency path, no nginx, no Node at runtime; the brief requires a Python backend anyway |
| R2 | Decision models | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` + `nimble:9b-q4_K_M`, with `qwen3.5:0.8b` as the generative baseline | PoC balance; clef-flash by request, nimble best published accuracy among the rest |
| R3 | Streaming `/analyze` | Typed SSE events `meta` -> `sentiment` -> `summary_delta*` -> `done`; JSON field order (sentiment-first vs summary-first) is an eval dimension | Sentiment arrives after a handful of output tokens when it is generated first |
| R4 | Extraction matrix + reference | 4 parsers x 4 own strategies + trafilatura (default, precision), readability-lxml, newspaper4k, justext, strip-tags; reference bodies produced by Opus, kept local (gitignored) | Comparable quality metric without publishing article text |
| R5 | Article-set procedure | Opus discovery via RSS/sections (last ~60 days, fetchable by our fetcher); two independent Opus labellers + adjudicator, ambiguous articles replaced; agreement reported; split 30 dev / 60 test | Stand-in for a human check |
| R6 | Summary evaluation | Deterministic checks (numbers grounded in source, entity named, length) + key-fact coverage via a local embedding model + Opus-as-judge on finalists | Cheap reproducible signal plus a strong judge where it matters |
| R7 | Latency budgets (native, warm, excl. fetch) | `/signal` lede p50 <= 500 ms; `/summary` and `/analyze` TTFT <= 1.5 s, complete p50 <= 4 s; unrealistic budgets are surfaced, not silently moved | Concrete selection gate |
| R8 | Bundled models | Per-endpoint winners if they total <= ~10 GB, else the best finalist that fits; all other Docker containers stopped during setup | Docker Desktop VM has 15.6 GiB |
| R9 | Transcript scope | Only this build session (main + subagents + workflows) | No other relevant sessions |
| R10 | Docs layout | `.context/docs/design/NN-*.md`, backlog in `90-optional-backlog.md`, eval reports in `evals/results/` | Book-order reading |

## Follow-ups

- Generative roster trimmed: summary {`qwen3.5:2b`, `qwen3.5:4b`}; combined {`qwen3.5:4b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`,
  `ministral-3:3b`}; `qwen3.5:9b` only as a holdout quality ceiling; Gemma 4 dropped (open think+format bug).
- Lean prompt grid: 2 rubric styles x few-shot {0, 4} x field order where relevant (<= 8 configs per model).
- Stopped Docker containers stay stopped; the restart command is handed back at the end.
- `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` is used only in CI to exercise the real decision-model path in containers; it is not evaluated.

## Build-time findings that adjusted the plan

Measured during P1/P2, recorded here so the deviations are traceable. Inputs for the Ollama probe were synthetic
(`evals/results/ollama_probe.json`, native Metal, warm, n=5).

- **Sources** (`02-source-probe.md`): AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
  their CDN (Cloudflare / Akamai), so all four backups were promoted. Final 10: Yahoo Finance, CNBC, Motley Fool,
  PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune, Guardian Business, BBC Business.
- **R7 sanity gate passed**: each endpoint has at least one candidate inside its budget, so no budget moved.
  - `/signal`: `qwen3.5:0.8b` answers in 190 ms at ~510 prompt tokens. The 9B decision models take 1.3-1.5 s
    at the same size, so they are reported against the budget rather than the budget relaxed for them.
  - `/summary`: `qwen3.5:2b` shows first text at 0.93 s and finishes at 2.2 s on ~1.6k-token articles;
    `qwen3.5:4b` misses the 1.5 s TTFT budget at that size (2.4 s).
  - `/analyze`: `ministral-3:3b` reaches the score at 1.47 s and finishes at 3.5 s on ~1.75k tokens; the 4B
    qwen models miss TTFT at full-article size.
- **Logprobs**: Ollama 0.40.6 also returns logprobs on streamed chunks (undocumented). The knob comparison stays
  on non-streaming `/signal`; `/analyze` keeps the ordinal knob. Logprob-weighted streaming confidence goes to
  the backlog.
- **Field order**: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` ignores schema property order (always entity, score, summary) and
  ignores `think:false` when a schema is set, so the field-order dimension runs on `qwen3.5:4b` and
  `ministral-3:3b` only.
- **Fetch cap** raised from 5 MB to 10 MB: CNN article pages are 5.7-6.6 MB decompressed.

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


def _csv(value: str) -> list[str]:
    return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="VT_", extra="ignore")

    env: Literal["dev", "test", "prod"] = "dev"

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import StrEnum
from typing import ClassVar


class ErrorCode(StrEnum):
    INVALID_URL = "invalid_url"
    BLOCKED_DESTINATION = "blocked_destination"
    MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED = "model_not_allowed"
    PAYWALLED = "paywalled"
    CONSENT_REQUIRED = "consent_required"
    EXTRACTION_EMPTY = "extraction_empty"
    UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT = "unsupported_content"
    TOO_LARGE = "too_large"
    SOURCE_BLOCKED = "source_blocked"
    UPSTREAM_HTTP = "upstream_http"
    SCHEMA_VIOLATION = "schema_violation"
    MODEL_UNAVAILABLE = "model_unavailable"
    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
    UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT = "upstream_timeout"
    INFERENCE_TIMEOUT = "inference_timeout"


ERROR_STATUS: dict[ErrorCode, int] = {
    ErrorCode.INVALID_URL: 400,
    ErrorCode.BLOCKED_DESTINATION: 400,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED: 400,
    ErrorCode.PAYWALLED: 422,
    ErrorCode.CONSENT_REQUIRED: 422,
    ErrorCode.EXTRACTION_EMPTY: 422,
    ErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT: 422,
    ErrorCode.TOO_LARGE: 422,
    ErrorCode.SOURCE_BLOCKED: 502,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_HTTP: 502,
    ErrorCode.SCHEMA_VIOLATION: 502,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT: 504,
    ErrorCode.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT: 504,
}


class VtError(Exception):
    code: ClassVar[ErrorCode]
    retryable_default: ClassVar[bool] = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        hint: str | None = None,
        retryable: bool | None = None,
        upstream_status: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.hint = hint
        self.retryable = self.retryable_default if retryable is None else retryable
        self.upstream_status = upstream_status

    @property
    def http_status(self) -> int:
        return ERROR_STATUS[self.code]


class InvalidUrl(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.INVALID_URL


class BlockedDestination(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.BLOCKED_DESTINATION


class ModelNotAllowed(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED


class Paywalled(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.PAYWALLED


class ConsentRequired(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.CONSENT_REQUIRED


class ExtractionEmpty(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.EXTRACTION_EMPTY


class UnsupportedContent(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT


class TooLarge(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.TOO_LARGE


class SourceBlocked(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.SOURCE_BLOCKED


class UpstreamHttp(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_HTTP
    retryable_default = True


class SchemaViolation(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.SCHEMA_VIOLATION
    retryable_default = True


class ModelUnavailable(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE


class LlmUnreachable(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE
    retryable_default = True


class UpstreamTimeout(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT
    retryable_default = True


class InferenceTimeout(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT
    retryable_default = True
from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager


class StageTimer:
    """Wall-clock stage timings in milliseconds, measured from construction."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._t0 = time.perf_counter()
        self.stages: dict[str, float] = {}

    @contextmanager
    def stage(self, name: str) -> Iterator[None]:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self.stages[name] = self.stages.get(name, 0.0) + (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000

    def elapsed_ms(self) -> float:
        return (time.perf_counter() - self._t0) * 1000
"""Model allowlist and per-endpoint defaults loaded from `data/models.toml`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from functools import lru_cache
from importlib import resources
from typing import Any, Literal, get_args

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator

from veritrade.config import Settings, get_settings
from veritrade.errors import ModelNotAllowed
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint, FieldOrder, ModelKind, PolicyName

ENDPOINTS: tuple[Endpoint, ...] = get_args(Endpoint)
SignalSchema = Literal["label", "ordinal"]


class ModelSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    name: str
    kind: ModelKind
    endpoints: tuple[Endpoint, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
    num_ctx: int | None = Field(None, gt=0)
    max_input_tokens: int = Field(gt=0)
    num_predict: dict[Endpoint, int] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    signal_schema: SignalSchema | None = None
    policy: PolicyName
    min_p: float | None = Field(None, gt=0, le=1)
    ordinal_t: int = Field(1, ge=1, le=2)
    field_order: FieldOrder | None = None
    evaluated: bool = True

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _default_field_order(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(data, dict) and "analyze" in data.get("endpoints", ()) and not data.get("field_order"):
            return {**data, "field_order": "sentiment-first"}
        return data

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_consistency(self) -> ModelSpec:
        if self.kind == "decision":
            if self.endpoints != ("signal",) or self.policy != "probability":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{self.name}: decision models serve only /signal with the probability policy"
                )
        else:
            if self.policy == "probability":
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: generative models have no native class probabilities")
            if self.num_ctx is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: generative models need num_ctx")
            missing = [e for e in self.endpoints if e not in self.num_predict]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: num_predict missing for {missing}")
            if "signal" in self.endpoints and self.signal_schema is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: generative /signal models need signal_schema")
            if "signal" in self.endpoints and self.policy == "ordinal" and self.signal_schema != "ordinal":
                raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: the ordinal policy needs signal_schema = 'ordinal'")
        if self.policy in ("probability", "label-logprob") and self.min_p is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: policy {self.policy} needs min_p")
        return self

    def serves(self, endpoint: Endpoint) -> bool:
        return endpoint in self.endpoints


def parse_models_toml(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, ModelSpec], dict[Endpoint, str]]:
    raw = tomllib.loads(text)
    specs = {name: ModelSpec(name=name, **body) for name, body in raw.get("models", {}).items()}
    defaults: dict[Endpoint, str] = {}
    for endpoint, name in raw.get("defaults", {}).items():
        if endpoint not in ENDPOINTS:
            raise ValueError(f"models.toml: unknown endpoint in [defaults]: {endpoint}")
        defaults[endpoint] = name
    return specs, defaults


def read_models_toml() -> str:
    return resources.files("veritrade.data").joinpath("models.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def allowlist() -> Mapping[str, ModelSpec]:
    """Every model in models.toml, ignoring VT_MODELS (prompts and evals need the full roster)."""
    return parse_models_toml(read_models_toml())[0]


class Registry:
    def __init__(
        self,
        specs: Mapping[str, ModelSpec],
        defaults: Mapping[Endpoint, str],
        *,
        restriction: Iterable[str] = (),
        overrides: Mapping[Endpoint, str | None] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        restricted = list(restriction)
        unknown = [name for name in restricted if name not in specs]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"VT_MODELS names models outside models.toml: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        keep = set(restricted) if restricted else set(specs)
        self._all = dict(specs)
        self._specs = {name: spec for name, spec in specs.items() if name in keep}
        self._defaults: dict[Endpoint, str] = {}
        for endpoint in ENDPOINTS:
            override = (overrides or {}).get(endpoint)
            if override:
                if not self._is_allowed(endpoint, override):
                    raise ValueError(f"default model override {override!r} is not allowed for /{endpoint}")
                self._defaults[endpoint] = override
                continue
            configured = defaults.get(endpoint)
            if configured and self._is_allowed(endpoint, configured):
                self._defaults[endpoint] = configured
            elif fallback := self.allowed(endpoint):
                self._defaults[endpoint] = fallback[0].name

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, settings: Settings | None = None, *, toml_text: str | None = None) -> Registry:
        settings = settings or get_settings()
        specs, defaults = parse_models_toml(toml_text if toml_text is not None else read_models_toml())
        overrides: dict[Endpoint, str | None] = {
            "signal": settings.default_model_signal,
            "summary": settings.default_model_summary,
            "analyze": settings.default_model_analyze,
        }
        return cls(specs, defaults, restriction=settings.model_restriction, overrides=overrides)

    def _is_allowed(self, endpoint: Endpoint, name: str) -> bool:
        spec = self._specs.get(name)
        return spec is not None and spec.serves(endpoint)

    @property
    def models(self) -> list[ModelSpec]:
        return list(self._specs.values())

    @property
    def defaults(self) -> dict[Endpoint, str]:
        return dict(self._defaults)

    def allowed(self, endpoint: Endpoint) -> list[ModelSpec]:
        return [spec for spec in self._specs.values() if spec.serves(endpoint)]

    def resolve(self, endpoint: Endpoint, model: str | None) -> ModelSpec:
        allowed = ", ".join(spec.name for spec in self.allowed(endpoint)) or "none"
        hint = f"Allowed for /{endpoint}: {allowed}."
        if model is None:
            default = self._defaults.get(endpoint)
            if default is None:
                raise ModelNotAllowed(f"No model is configured for /{endpoint}.", hint=hint)
            return self._specs[default]
        spec = self._specs.get(model)
        if spec is None:
            reason = "is disabled by VT_MODELS" if model in self._all else "is not on the allowlist"
            raise ModelNotAllowed(f"Model {model!r} {reason}.", hint=hint)
        if not spec.serves(endpoint):
            raise ModelNotAllowed(f"Model {model!r} does not serve /{endpoint}.", hint=hint)
        return spec


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_registry() -> Registry:
    return Registry.load()

from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from veritrade import __version__
from veritrade.api.contracts import ErrorBody, ErrorResponse
from veritrade.api.routes import router
from veritrade.config import Settings, get_settings
from veritrade.errors import VtError


def error_response(exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
    body = ErrorResponse(
        error=ErrorBody(
            code=exc.code,
            message=exc.message,
            hint=exc.hint,
            retryable=exc.retryable,
            upstream_status=exc.upstream_status,
        )
    )
    return JSONResponse(status_code=exc.http_status, content=body.model_dump(mode="json"))


def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    app = FastAPI(title="VeriTrade Analytics", version=__version__)
    app.state.settings = settings

    @app.exception_handler(VtError)
    async def _vt_error(_: Request, exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
        return error_response(exc)

    if settings.cors_origin_list:
        app.add_middleware(
            CORSMiddleware,
            allow_origins=settings.cors_origin_list,
            allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
            allow_headers=["*"],
        )
    app.include_router(router)
    # Mounted last so /api routes win; html=True serves the static export's index.html files.
    if settings.static_dir and settings.static_dir.is_dir():
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=settings.static_dir, html=True), name="static")
    return app

"""Public API contract: request/response bodies, SSE event payloads and the error envelope."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from veritrade.errors import ErrorCode
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName, ParserName, Scope
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint, FieldOrder, ModelKind, PolicyName, Sentiment


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


# --- requests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _ArticleRequest(_Strict):
    url: AnyHttpUrl
    model: str | None = Field(None, description="Allowlisted Ollama tag; endpoint default when omitted.")
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax"
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade"
    no_cache: bool = Field(False, description="Bypass fetch and result caches (used by latency benchmarks).")


class SignalRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = Field("lede", description="lede = headline + opening paragraphs; full = whole article.")


class SummaryRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    pass


class AnalyzeRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = "full"


# --- shared response parts ------------------------------------------------------------------


class CacheInfo(_Strict):
    fetch: Literal["hit", "miss", "joined", "bypass"]
    result: Literal["hit", "miss", "bypass"]


class InferenceTimings(_Strict):
    wall_ms: float
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    load_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_eval_ms: float | None = None
    eval_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    eval_tokens: int | None = None


class Timings(_Strict):
    total_ms: float
    fetch_ms: float
    consent_ms: float | None = None
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    inference: InferenceTimings | None = None
    cache: CacheInfo


class ArticleMeta(_Strict):
    url: str
    final_url: str
    title: str
    source: str | None = Field(None, description="Key from sources.toml when the domain is a known source.")
    published_at: str | None = None
    endpoint: Endpoint
    model: str
    model_kind: ModelKind
    prompt_version: str
    parser: ParserName
    extractor: ExtractorName
    extraction_method: str = Field(description="Strategy that produced the body (cascade resolves to one).")
    scope: Scope
    input_chars: int
    word_count: int
    field_order: FieldOrder | None = None
    cached: bool
    backend: str = Field(description="Inference backend label, e.g. native-metal or docker-cpu.")


class SignalResult(_Strict):
    sentiment: Sentiment
    abstained: bool = Field(description="True when the call fell below the frozen confidence threshold.")
    policy: PolicyName
    confidence: float | None = None
    score: int | None = Field(None, ge=-2, le=2)
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float] | None = None


# --- responses ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SignalResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    timings: Timings


class SummaryResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    summary: str
    timings: Timings


class AnalyzeResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    summary: str
    timings: Timings


class ErrorBody(_Strict):
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str
    hint: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    upstream_status: int | None = None


class ErrorResponse(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


class ModelInfo(_Strict):
    name: str
    kind: ModelKind
    endpoints: list[Endpoint]
    installed: bool
    size_bytes: int | None = None
    evaluated: bool = Field(True, description="False for plumbing-only models (e.g. the CI decision model).")


class ModelsResponse(_Strict):
    models: list[ModelInfo]
    defaults: dict[Endpoint, str]
    parsers: list[ParserName]
    extractors: list[ExtractorName]
    scopes: list[Scope]


class HealthResponse(_Strict):
    status: Literal["ok", "degraded"]
    ollama_reachable: bool
    ollama_version: str | None = None
    backend: str
    version: str


# --- SSE event payloads (event name -> data model) ------------------------------------------
# /summary/stream: meta -> summary_delta* -> done
# /analyze/stream: meta -> sentiment (exactly once, position follows field order) + summary_delta* -> done
# Any failure after the stream opens emits a single `error` event and closes.


class MetaEvent(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    fetch_ms: float
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    cache: CacheInfo


class SentimentEvent(_Strict):
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    elapsed_ms: float = Field(description="Milliseconds since the request was received.")


class SummaryDeltaEvent(_Strict):
    text: str


class SummaryDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: SummaryResponse


class AnalyzeDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: AnalyzeResponse


class ErrorEvent(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


SSE_EVENT_NAMES = ("meta", "sentiment", "summary_delta", "done", "error")

"""In-process LRU + TTL cache whose concurrent misses for one key share a single in-flight task."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Hashable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal
from urllib.parse import unquote_plus, urlsplit, urlunsplit

from veritrade.errors import VtError

CacheStatus = Literal["hit", "miss", "joined"]
TRACKING_PARAMS = frozenset({"fbclid", "gclid"})
DEFAULT_PORTS = {"http": ":80", "https": ":443"}


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CacheResult[V]:
    value: V
    status: CacheStatus


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Value[V]:
    value: V
    expires_at: float
    weight: int


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Failure:
    error: VtError
    expires_at: float
    weight: int = 0


class SingleFlightCache[K: Hashable, V]:
    """Typed VtErrors are cached for error_ttl_s so a refusing publisher is not hammered; others are not.

    weigh/max_weight bound memory as well as entry count, since one cached page can be several MB.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        max_entries: int,
        ttl_s: float,
        error_ttl_s: float,
        weigh: Callable[[V], int] | None = None,
        max_weight: int | None = None,
        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
    ) -> None:
        if max_entries < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_entries must be at least 1")
        self._max_entries = max_entries
        self._ttl_s = ttl_s
        self._error_ttl_s = error_ttl_s
        self._weigh = weigh
        self._max_weight = max_weight
        self._clock = clock
        self._entries: OrderedDict[K, _Value[V] | _Failure] = OrderedDict()
        self._inflight: dict[K, asyncio.Task[V]] = {}
        self._weight = 0

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._entries)

    @property
    def weight(self) -> int:
        return self._weight

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self._entries.clear()
        self._weight = 0

    async def get_or_create(self, key: K, factory: Callable[[], Awaitable[V]]) -> CacheResult[V]:
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry is not None:
            if entry.expires_at > self._clock():
                self._entries.move_to_end(key)
                if isinstance(entry, _Failure):
                    raise entry.error.with_traceback(None)
                return CacheResult(entry.value, "hit")
            self._drop(key)
        status: CacheStatus = "joined"
        task = self._inflight.get(key)
        if task is None:
            task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(key, factory))
            self._inflight[key] = task
            status = "miss"
        # Shielded so a caller that gives up does not cancel work others wait on; shield also marks the
        # error of a task every caller abandoned as retrieved, so asyncio does not log it.
        return CacheResult(await asyncio.shield(task), status)

    async def _run(self, key: K, factory: Callable[[], Awaitable[V]]) -> V:
        try:
            value = await factory()
        except VtError as exc:
            if self._error_ttl_s > 0:
                self._store(key, _Failure(exc, self._clock() + self._error_ttl_s))
            raise
        finally:
            self._inflight.pop(key, None)
        weight = self._weigh(value) if self._weigh else 0
        if self._ttl_s > 0 and (self._max_weight is None or weight <= self._max_weight):
            self._store(key, _Value(value, self._clock() + self._ttl_s, weight))
        return value

    def _store(self, key: K, entry: _Value[V] | _Failure) -> None:
        self._drop(key)
        self._entries[key] = entry
        self._weight += entry.weight
        while len(self._entries) > self._max_entries or (
            self._max_weight is not None and self._weight > self._max_weight
        ):
            _, evicted = self._entries.popitem(last=False)
            self._weight -= evicted.weight

    def _drop(self, key: K) -> None:
        if (entry := self._entries.pop(key, None)) is not None:
            self._weight -= entry.weight


def normalize_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Cache key: lowercase scheme and host, no default port, fragment or click-tracking parameters."""
    parts = urlsplit(url.strip())
    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
    userinfo, at, hostport = parts.netloc.rpartition("@")
    hostport = hostport.lower()
    if (default := DEFAULT_PORTS.get(scheme)) and hostport.endswith(default):
        hostport = hostport.removesuffix(default)
    query = "&".join(part for part in parts.query.split("&") if part and not _is_tracking(part))
    return urlunsplit((scheme, f"{userinfo}{at}{hostport}", parts.path or "/", query, ""))


def _is_tracking(param: str) -> bool:
    name = unquote_plus(param.partition("=")[0]).lower()
    return name.startswith("utm_") or name in TRACKING_PARAMS
"""The serving fetcher: one HTTP/2 client, manual SSRF-checked redirects, capped bodies, typed failures."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import codecs
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Mapping
from typing import NoReturn
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit

import httpcore
import httpx

from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.errors import (
    ConsentRequired,
    InvalidUrl,
    TooLarge,
    UnsupportedContent,
    UpstreamHttp,
    UpstreamTimeout,
)
from veritrade.fetch import detect
from veritrade.fetch.consent import REDIRECT_STATUSES, is_consent_url, reject_all
from veritrade.fetch.headers import browser_headers, is_sec_host
from veritrade.fetch.ssrf import GuardedBackend, Resolver, check_target, system_resolver
from veritrade.fetch.types import FetchResult

LIMITS = httpx.Limits(max_connections=64, max_keepalive_connections=32, keepalive_expiry=60.0)
# EDGAR's fair-access policy allows 10 requests per second per client; every sec.gov host shares it.
RATE_LIMITS: Mapping[str, float] = {"sec.gov": 10.0}
HTML_TYPES = frozenset({"text/html", "application/xhtml+xml"})
SEC_DOCUMENT_SUFFIXES = (".htm", ".html", ".txt")
# Error pages are only read for detect.classify, which scans the first 64 KB.
ERROR_BODY_BYTES = 65_536
SNIFF_BYTES = 4096

_META_CHARSET = re.compile(rb"""<meta[^>]{0,512}?charset\s*=\s*["']?\s*([a-z0-9_.:-]+)""", re.IGNORECASE)
# WHATWG decodes these labels as windows-1252; the 0x80-0x9F smart quotes in old filings depend on it.
_WINDOWS_1252_ALIASES = frozenset({"iso8859-1", "ascii"})


class HostRateLimiter:
    """Spaces request starts evenly per rate-limited host group; other hosts pass straight through."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        rates: Mapping[str, float] = RATE_LIMITS,
        *,
        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
        sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep,
    ) -> None:
        self._intervals = {suffix: 1.0 / rate for suffix, rate in rates.items()}
        self._next: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._clock = clock
        self._sleep = sleep

    def _group(self, host: str) -> str | None:
        host = host.lower().rstrip(".")
        for suffix in self._intervals:
            if host == suffix or host.endswith("." + suffix):
                return suffix
        return None

    async def acquire(self, url: str) -> None:
        group = self._group(urlsplit(url).hostname or "")
        if group is None:
            return
        # Slots are reserved before sleeping, so concurrent callers queue without a lock.
        now = self._clock()
        slot = max(now, self._next.get(group, now))
        self._next[group] = slot + self._intervals[group]
        if slot > now:
            await self._sleep(slot - now)


class _GuardedTransport(httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport):
    """httpx takes no network backend argument, so the pool is rebuilt around the SSRF-guarded one."""

    def __init__(self, backend: httpcore.AsyncNetworkBackend) -> None:
        super().__init__(http2=True, limits=LIMITS)
        self._pool = httpcore.AsyncConnectionPool(
            ssl_context=httpx.create_ssl_context(),
            max_connections=LIMITS.max_connections,
            max_keepalive_connections=LIMITS.max_keepalive_connections,
            keepalive_expiry=LIMITS.keepalive_expiry,
            http1=True,
            http2=True,
            network_backend=backend,
        )


class HttpFetcher:
    """Fetcher protocol over one shared client whose cookie jar keeps Yahoo's reject-all answer."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Settings,
        *,
        resolver: Resolver = system_resolver,
        limiter: HostRateLimiter | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._settings = settings
        self._resolver = resolver
        self._allow_hosts = settings.ssrf_allow_hosts
        self._limiter = limiter or HostRateLimiter()
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            transport=_GuardedTransport(GuardedBackend(resolver=resolver, allow_hosts=self._allow_hosts)),
            follow_redirects=False,
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(settings.fetch_deadline_s, connect=settings.fetch_connect_timeout_s),
            # User-supplied URLs must never pick up .netrc credentials.
            trust_env=False,
        )

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self._client.aclose()

    async def get(self, url: str) -> FetchResult:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        host = _host(url)
        deadline = self._settings.fetch_deadline_s
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(deadline):
                return await self._fetch(url, started)
        except (TimeoutError, httpx.TimeoutException) as exc:
            raise UpstreamTimeout(
                f"{host} did not deliver the page within {deadline:g} s",
                hint="The publisher is slow or unreachable; retry, or try the story from another source.",
            ) from exc
        except httpx.InvalidURL as exc:
            raise InvalidUrl(f"malformed URL: {exc}") from exc
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise UpstreamHttp(
                f"request to {host} failed: {type(exc).__name__}",
                hint="The publisher could not be reached; retry shortly.",
            ) from exc

    async def _check(self, url: str) -> None:
        await check_target(url, resolver=self._resolver, allow_hosts=self._allow_hosts)

    async def _fetch(self, url: str, started: float) -> FetchResult:
        current, redirects = url, 0
        consent_ms: float | None = None
        while True:
            await self._check(current)
            await self._limiter.acquire(current)
            async with self._client.stream("GET", current, headers=browser_headers(current)) as response:
                location = response.headers.get("location")
                if response.status_code not in REDIRECT_STATUSES or not location:
                    html, content_type = await self._read(response, current)
                    fetch_ms = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000 - (consent_ms or 0.0)
                    return FetchResult(
                        requested_url=url,
                        final_url=current,
                        status=response.status_code,
                        html=html,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        fetch_ms=fetch_ms,
                        consent_ms=consent_ms,
                        redirects=redirects,
                    )
                status, headers = response.status_code, response.headers
            target = urljoin(current, location)
            if is_consent_url(target):
                if consent_ms is not None:
                    _consent_wall(status, headers, target)
                # Reject-all once, then retry the hop that hit the wall with the consent cookie set.
                outcome = await reject_all(self._client, target, guard=self._check)
                consent_ms = outcome.elapsed_ms
                continue
            redirects += 1
            if redirects > (cap := self._settings.fetch_max_redirects):
                raise UpstreamHttp(
                    f"{_host(url)} redirected more than {cap} times",
                    hint="The URL redirects in a loop; open it in a browser and use the final address.",
                    retryable=False,
                    upstream_status=status,
                )
            current = target

    async def _read(self, response: httpx.Response, url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        status = response.status_code
        content_type = response.headers.get("content-type", "")
        host = _host(url)
        if not 200 <= status < 300:
            prefix = await _read_body(response, ERROR_BODY_BYTES, host=host, truncate=True)
            detect.classify(status, response.headers, decode_html(prefix, content_type), url)
            raise UpstreamHttp(
                f"{host} answered HTTP {status}",
                hint=_status_hint(status),
                retryable=status >= 500 or status == 408,
                upstream_status=status,
            )

        media = content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
        if media and not _accepted(media, url):
            raise _unsupported(host, media)
        limit = self._settings.fetch_max_bytes
        declared = response.headers.get("content-length", "")
        if declared.isdigit() and int(declared) > limit:
            raise _too_large(host, limit)
        body = await _read_body(response, limit, host=host, truncate=False)
        if not media:
            if not _looks_like_html(body):
                raise _unsupported(host, "an undeclared non-HTML type")
            content_type = "text/html"
        html = decode_html(body, content_type)
        detect.classify(status, response.headers, html, url)
        return html, content_type


def _host(url: str) -> str:
    """Host for messages; malformed input (e.g. an unclosed IPv6 bracket) is left to check_target."""
    try:
        return urlsplit(url).hostname or url
    except ValueError:
        return url


async def _read_body(response: httpx.Response, limit: int, *, host: str, truncate: bool) -> bytes:
    """Decoded bytes, so a small compressed body cannot inflate past the cap."""
    body = bytearray()
    async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
        body += chunk
        if len(body) > limit:
            if truncate:
                return bytes(body[:limit])
            raise _too_large(host, limit)
    return bytes(body)


def decode_html(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> str:
    """BOM, then header charset, then <meta> charset, then UTF-8 if valid, else windows-1252."""
    if body.startswith(codecs.BOM_UTF8):
        return body[len(codecs.BOM_UTF8) :].decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if body.startswith((codecs.BOM_UTF16_LE, codecs.BOM_UTF16_BE)):
        return body.decode("utf-16", "replace")
    for label in (_header_charset(content_type), _meta_charset(body[:SNIFF_BYTES])):
        if (encoding := _codec(label)) is None:
            continue
        try:
            return body.decode(encoding, "replace")
        except LookupError:
            # codecs also registers bytes-to-bytes transforms (base64, zlib) that str decoding refuses.
            continue
    try:
        return body.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return body.decode("cp1252", "replace")


def _header_charset(content_type: str) -> str | None:
    for param in content_type.split(";")[1:]:
        key, _, value = param.partition("=")
        if key.strip().lower() == "charset":
            return value.strip().strip("'\"")
    return None


def _meta_charset(head: bytes) -> str | None:
    match = _META_CHARSET.search(head)
    return match.group(1).decode("ascii") if match else None


def _codec(label: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not label:
        return None
    try:
        name = codecs.lookup(label).name
    except LookupError:
        return None
    return "cp1252" if name in _WINDOWS_1252_ALIASES else name


def _accepted(media: str, url: str) -> bool:
    if media in HTML_TYPES:
        return True
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    # EDGAR serves .txt exhibits and some filer-agent .htm files as text/plain.
    return (
        media == "text/plain"
        and is_sec_host(parts.hostname or "")
        and parts.path.lower().endswith(SEC_DOCUMENT_SUFFIXES)
    )


def _looks_like_html(body: bytes) -> bool:
    head = body[:SNIFF_BYTES].lstrip().lower()
    return head.startswith((b"<!doctype html", b"<html")) or b"<html" in head


def _unsupported(host: str, media: str) -> UnsupportedContent:
    return UnsupportedContent(
        f"{host} returned {media}, not an HTML article",
        hint="Only HTML article pages are supported; link the article page rather than a PDF, image or feed.",
    )


def _too_large(host: str, limit: int) -> TooLarge:
    return TooLarge(
        f"{host} sent more than {limit / 1_000_000:g} MB",
        hint="Article pages are far smaller; the URL probably points at a file download.",
    )


def _status_hint(status: int) -> str:
    if status in (404, 410):
        return "The page does not exist; check the URL or whether the article was taken down."
    if status >= 500:
        return "The publisher had a server error; retry shortly."
    return "The publisher refused the request; try the story from another source."


def _consent_wall(status: int, headers: Mapping[str, str], url: str) -> NoReturn:
    """A second consent redirect after reject-all means the cookie did not stick."""
    detect.classify(status, headers, "", url)
    raise ConsentRequired(f"{urlsplit(url).hostname} demands cookie consent")

"""SSRF guard: only public http(s) destinations, vetted per redirect hop and again at connect time."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import ipaddress
import re
import socket
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpcore

from veritrade.errors import BlockedDestination, InvalidUrl, UpstreamHttp

Resolver = Callable[[str, int], Awaitable[Sequence[str]]]
IpAddress = ipaddress.IPv4Address | ipaddress.IPv6Address

ALLOWED_SCHEMES = frozenset({"http", "https"})
ALLOWED_PORTS = frozenset({80, 443})
NAT64 = ipaddress.IPv6Network("64:ff9b::/96")
# Dotted, decimal, octal or hex numerals that resolvers read as IPv4 (2130706433, 0x7f.1, 0177.0.0.1).
_NUMERIC_HOST = re.compile(r"(?:0x[0-9a-f]*|[0-9]+)(?:\.(?:0x[0-9a-f]*|[0-9]+)){0,3}\.?")
_HINT = "Only public http(s) article URLs on ports 80 and 443 can be fetched."


async def system_resolver(host: str, port: int) -> list[str]:
    infos = await asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(host, port, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(str(info[4][0]) for info in infos))


def blocked_reason(address: IpAddress) -> str | None:
    """Why an address is not a public unicast destination, or None when it is."""
    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if (mapped := address.ipv4_mapped) is not None:
            return blocked_reason(mapped)
        # DNS64 networks answer every IPv4-only host inside 64:ff9b::/96, so judge the embedded address.
        if address in NAT64:
            return blocked_reason(ipaddress.IPv4Address(int(address) & 0xFFFF_FFFF))
        if address.is_site_local:
            return "site-local"
    if address.is_unspecified:
        return "unspecified"
    if address.is_loopback:
        return "loopback"
    if address.is_link_local:
        return "link-local"
    if address.is_multicast:
        return "multicast"
    if address.is_reserved:
        return "reserved"
    if address.is_private:
        return "private"
    if not address.is_global:
        return "non-global"
    return None


def _host_key(host: str) -> str:
    return host.lower().rstrip(".")


def _literal(host: str) -> IpAddress | None:
    try:
        return ipaddress.ip_address(host)
    except ValueError:
        if _NUMERIC_HOST.fullmatch(host):
            raise InvalidUrl(f"'{host}' is not a canonical IP address or host name", hint=_HINT) from None
        return None


async def public_addresses(host: str, port: int, *, resolver: Resolver) -> list[str]:
    """Every address the host resolves to; one non-public answer refuses the whole host."""
    if (literal := _literal(host)) is not None:
        candidates: Sequence[str] = [str(literal)]
    else:
        try:
            candidates = await resolver(host, port)
        except socket.gaierror as exc:
            if exc.errno == socket.EAI_AGAIN:
                raise UpstreamHttp(f"DNS lookup for {host} failed for now", hint="Retry shortly.") from exc
            raise InvalidUrl(f"{host} does not resolve", hint="Check the domain name in the URL.") from exc
    if not candidates:
        raise InvalidUrl(f"{host} does not resolve", hint="Check the domain name in the URL.")
    for candidate in candidates:
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(candidate)
        if (reason := blocked_reason(address)) is not None:
            raise BlockedDestination(f"{host} resolves to a {reason} address", hint=_HINT)
    return list(candidates)


async def check_target(
    url: str, *, resolver: Resolver = system_resolver, allow_hosts: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
) -> None:
    """Raise InvalidUrl or BlockedDestination unless the URL may be fetched; allow_hosts is test-only."""
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        port = parts.port
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise InvalidUrl(f"malformed URL: {exc}", hint=_HINT) from exc
    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
    if scheme not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES:
        raise InvalidUrl(f"unsupported URL scheme '{scheme or '(none)'}'", hint=_HINT)
    if parts.username is not None or parts.password is not None:
        raise InvalidUrl("URLs with embedded credentials are not fetched", hint=_HINT)
    host = parts.hostname
    if not host or "%" in host:
        raise InvalidUrl("URL has no usable host", hint=_HINT)
    if _host_key(host) in allow_hosts:
        return
    if port is not None and port not in ALLOWED_PORTS:
        raise BlockedDestination(f"port {port} is not allowed", hint=_HINT)
    await public_addresses(host, port or (443 if scheme == "https" else 80), resolver=resolver)


class GuardedBackend(httpcore.AsyncNetworkBackend):
    """Connects only to vetted addresses, pinning the IP so DNS cannot change between check and connect."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        resolver: Resolver = system_resolver,
        allow_hosts: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
        inner: httpcore.AsyncNetworkBackend | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._resolver = resolver
        self._allow_hosts = allow_hosts
        self._inner = inner or httpcore.AnyIOBackend()

    async def connect_tcp(
        self,
        host: str,
        port: int,
        timeout: float | None = None,  # noqa: ASYNC109 - httpcore's backend signature
        local_address: str | None = None,
        socket_options: Iterable[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> httpcore.AsyncNetworkStream:
        if _host_key(host) in self._allow_hosts:
            return await self._inner.connect_tcp(host, port, timeout, local_address, socket_options)
        addresses = await public_addresses(host, port, resolver=self._resolver)
        # TLS still verifies the certificate against `host`: httpcore passes it as SNI to start_tls.
        for address in addresses[:-1]:
            try:
                return await self._inner.connect_tcp(address, port, timeout, local_address, socket_options)
            except httpcore.ConnectError:
                continue
        return await self._inner.connect_tcp(addresses[-1], port, timeout, local_address, socket_options)

    async def connect_unix_socket(
        self,
        path: str,
        timeout: float | None = None,  # noqa: ASYNC109 - httpcore's backend signature
        socket_options: Iterable[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> httpcore.AsyncNetworkStream:
        raise BlockedDestination("unix sockets are not a fetch destination", hint=_HINT)

    async def sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        await self._inner.sleep(seconds)
"""Yahoo EU consent wall: answer "reject all" so the article loads without granting tracking consent."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit

import httpx

from veritrade.errors import ConsentRequired
from veritrade.fetch.detect import CONSENT_HOSTS
from veritrade.fetch.headers import browser_headers

MAX_CONSENT_HOPS = 6
REDIRECT_STATUSES = frozenset({301, 302, 303, 307, 308})

# Lets the fetch layer apply its SSRF policy to every consent hop.
Guard = Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]


def is_consent_url(url: str) -> bool:
    return (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").lower() in CONSENT_HOSTS


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ConsentForm:
    action: str
    fields: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ConsentOutcome:
    done_url: str | None
    elapsed_ms: float


@dataclass
class _RawForm:
    action: str
    classes: frozenset[str]
    hidden: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    submits: list[tuple[str, str, frozenset[str]]] = field(default_factory=list)


class _FormCollector(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.forms: list[_RawForm] = []
        self._open: _RawForm | None = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]) -> None:
        attr = {key: value or "" for key, value in attrs}
        classes = frozenset(attr.get("class", "").split())
        if tag == "form":
            self._open = _RawForm(action=attr.get("action", ""), classes=classes)
            self.forms.append(self._open)
            return
        if self._open is None or not (name := attr.get("name", "")):
            return
        kind = attr.get("type", "submit" if tag == "button" else "text").lower()
        if tag == "input" and kind == "hidden":
            self._open.hidden.append((name, attr.get("value", "")))
        elif tag in ("button", "input") and kind == "submit":
            self._open.submits.append((name, attr.get("value", ""), classes))

    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
        if tag == "form":
            self._open = None


def _reject_button(form: _RawForm) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    for name, value, classes in form.submits:
        if name.lower() == "reject" or "reject-all" in classes:
            return name, value
    return None


def parse_consent_form(html: str, page_url: str) -> ConsentForm:
    """Hidden fields plus the reject-all button of the consent form; accept-all is never selected."""
    collector = _FormCollector()
    collector.feed(html)
    collector.close()
    candidates = sorted(collector.forms, key=lambda form: "consent-form" not in form.classes)
    for form in candidates:
        reject = _reject_button(form)
        if reject is None:
            continue
        action = urljoin(page_url, form.action) if form.action else page_url
        if not is_consent_url(action):
            break
        return ConsentForm(action=action, fields=(*form.hidden, reject))
    raise ConsentRequired(
        "consent page has no reject-all form we can submit",
        hint="Yahoo changed its consent page; open the article in a browser or try another source.",
    )


async def reject_all(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient, consent_url: str, *, guard: Guard | None = None
) -> ConsentOutcome:
    """Walk the consent redirects, POST reject-all and stop where the chain leaves the consent hosts.

    Cookies land in the client's jar so the caller retries the original URL once; transport errors propagate.
    """
    if not is_consent_url(consent_url):
        raise ValueError(f"not a consent URL: {consent_url}")
    started = time.perf_counter()
    response, exit_url = await _follow(client, "GET", consent_url, guard=guard)
    if exit_url is not None:
        return ConsentOutcome(exit_url, _ms(started))

    page_url = str(response.url)
    form = parse_consent_form(response.text, page_url)
    action = urlsplit(form.action)
    headers = browser_headers(form.action) | {
        "Origin": f"{action.scheme}://{action.netloc}",
        "Referer": page_url,
        "Sec-Fetch-Site": "same-origin",
    }
    response, exit_url = await _follow(
        client, "POST", form.action, guard=guard, data=dict(form.fields), headers=headers
    )
    if exit_url is None:
        raise ConsentRequired(
            f"consent submission was not accepted (HTTP {response.status_code})",
            hint="Yahoo kept showing its consent page; open the article in a browser or try another source.",
            upstream_status=response.status_code,
        )
    return ConsentOutcome(exit_url, _ms(started))


async def _follow(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient,
    method: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    guard: Guard | None,
    data: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[httpx.Response, str | None]:
    """Follow redirects while they stay on consent hosts; the URL is set once the chain leaves them."""
    for _ in range(MAX_CONSENT_HOPS):
        if guard is not None:
            await guard(url)
        response = await client.request(
            method,
            url,
            data=data,
            headers=headers or browser_headers(url),
            follow_redirects=False,
        )
        location = response.headers.get("location")
        if response.status_code not in REDIRECT_STATUSES or not location:
            return response, None
        next_url = urljoin(url, location)
        if not is_consent_url(next_url):
            return response, next_url
        method, url, data, headers = "GET", next_url, None, None
    raise ConsentRequired(
        "consent flow redirected too many times",
        hint="Yahoo's consent flow looped; open the article in a browser or try another source.",
    )


def _ms(started: float) -> float:
    return (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000

}


def classify(status: int, headers: Mapping[str, str], html: str, final_url: str) -> None:
    """Raise SourceBlocked, ConsentRequired or Paywalled; other 4xx/5xx statuses are the caller's to map."""
    host = (urlsplit(final_url).hostname or "").lower()
    lowered = {key.lower(): value for key, value in headers.items()}
    window = html[:SCAN_WINDOW].lower()

    if host in CONSENT_HOSTS or any(marker in window for marker in _CONSENT_MARKERS):
        raise ConsentRequired(
            f"{host or final_url} answered with a cookie-consent wall",
            hint=_hint(ConsentRequired, host),
            upstream_status=status,
        )

    vendor = _challenge_vendor(lowered, window)
    if status in BLOCK_STATUSES or vendor:
        edge = _edge_vendor(lowered)
        by = f", {vendor} bot protection" if vendor else f", {edge} edge" if edge else ""
        raise SourceBlocked(
            f"{host or final_url} refused the request (HTTP {status}{by})",
            hint=_hint(SourceBlocked, host),
            retryable=status == 429,
            upstream_status=status,
        )

    if "isAccessibleForFree" in html:
        free, body_words = jsonld_access(html)
        # Metered sites flag every article as not free yet serve it whole; only a short body is a paywall.
        if free is False and body_words < PAYWALL_MIN_WORDS and paragraph_words(html) < PAYWALL_MIN_WORDS:
            raise Paywalled(
                f"{host or final_url} marks the article as not free and serves only a teaser",
                hint=_hint(Paywalled, host),
                upstream_status=status,
            )


def _challenge_vendor(headers: Mapping[str, str], window: str) -> str | None:
    if headers.get("cf-mitigated", "").lower() == "challenge":
        return "Cloudflare"
    if "x-dd-b" in headers:
        return "DataDome"
    if "<title>access denied</title>" in window and "reference #" in window:
        return "Akamai"
    for vendor, needle in _BODY_MARKERS:
        if needle in window:
            return vendor
    return None


def _edge_vendor(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> str | None:
    """Which CDN answered, so a bare 403 still says who refused it."""
    server = headers.get("server", "").lower()
    if "cf-ray" in headers or server == "cloudflare":
        return "Cloudflare"
    if "akamai" in server:
        return "Akamai"
    if "x-datadome" in headers:
        return "DataDome"
    return None


def _hint(kind: type[VtError], host: str) -> str:
    default, by_host = _HINTS[kind]
    for suffix, hint in by_host.items():
        if host == suffix or host.endswith("." + suffix):
            return hint
    return default


def jsonld_blocks(html: str) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """Yield every parseable JSON-LD payload; plain str.find keeps multi-MB pages at a few ms."""
    pos = 0
    while (start := html.find("application/ld+json", pos)) != -1:
        open_end = html.find(">", start)
        close = html.find("</script", open_end)
        if open_end == -1 or close == -1:
            return
        pos = close
        try:
            yield json.loads(html[open_end + 1 : close])
        except ValueError:
            continue


def _walk(node: Any) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        yield node
        for value in node.values():
            yield from _walk(value)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            yield from _walk(item)


def jsonld_nodes(html: str) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every JSON object nested anywhere in the page's JSON-LD (covers @graph and arrays)."""
    for block in jsonld_blocks(html):
        yield from _walk(block)


def jsonld_access(html: str) -> tuple[bool | None, int]:
    """isAccessibleForFree across JSON-LD (False wins) and the longest articleBody word count."""
    free: bool | None = None
    words = 0
    for node in jsonld_nodes(html):
        value = node.get("isAccessibleForFree")
        if value is not None:
            parsed = value if isinstance(value, bool) else str(value).strip().lower() == "true"
            free = parsed if free is None else free and parsed
        body = node.get("articleBody")
        if isinstance(body, str):
            words = max(words, len(body.split()))
    return free, words


_P_RE = re.compile(r"<p[\s>].*?</p>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")


def paragraph_words(html: str) -> int:
    """Rough visible word count of <p> elements; only used on the rare not-free path."""
    return sum(len(_TAG_RE.sub(" ", match).split()) for match in _P_RE.findall(html))

Kept import-free so `extract.types`, which the API contract imports, does not pull in the parsers.
"""

"""Single entry point from HTML to Article; parse and extract time are measured separately."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from veritrade.errors import ExtractionEmpty
from veritrade.extract import cascade, density, jsonld, profiles, third_party
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, head_title, normalize, parse, scan_json_ld
from veritrade.extract.profiles import source_for_url
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS, Article, ExtractorName, ParserName

__all__ = ["MIN_WORDS", "extract", "source_for_url"]

MIN_WORDS = 40

OWN: dict[ExtractorName, Callable[[Dom, str, str | None], list[str]]] = {
    "jsonld": jsonld.extract,
    "profile": profiles.extract,
    "density": density.extract,
}
_PUBLISHED_META = re.compile(
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name|itemprop)\s*=\s*["']"""
    r"""(?:article:published_time|datePublished|pubdate|publishdate)["'][^>]*>""",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)


def _published_meta(html: str) -> str | None:
    if (meta := _PUBLISHED_META.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")) or None
    return None


def _dom_title(dom: Dom, source: str | None) -> str:
    profile = profiles.profile_for(source)
    if profile is not None and profile.title:
        for node in dom.select(profile.title):
            if text := node.text():
                return text
    return dom.title()


def extract(
    html: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax",
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade",
) -> Article:
    """Raises ExtractionEmpty when fewer than MIN_WORDS words come out."""
    source = source_for_url(url)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    dom: Dom | None = None
    if extractor in PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS:
        dom = parse(html, parser)
        if extractor == "cascade":
            method, paragraphs = cascade.run(dom, url, source)
        else:
            method, paragraphs = extractor, OWN[extractor](dom, url, source)
        objects = dom.json_ld()
    else:
        method, paragraphs = extractor, third_party.extract(extractor, html, url)
        objects = scan_json_ld(html)
    words = sum(len(p.split()) for p in paragraphs)
    if words < MIN_WORDS:
        raise ExtractionEmpty(
            f"The {extractor} extractor found {words} words on {urlsplit(url).hostname or url}; "
            f"at least {MIN_WORDS} are needed",
            hint="Try another extractor (for example trafilatura), or check that the URL is a single "
            "article rather than a section or video page.",
        )
    title = jsonld.headline(objects) or (_dom_title(dom, source) if dom is not None else head_title(html))
    published_at = jsonld.date_published(objects) or _published_meta(html)
    total_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    parse_ms = dom.parse_ms if dom is not None else 0.0
    return Article(
        url=url,
        title=title,
        paragraphs=tuple(paragraphs),
        published_at=published_at,
        source=source,
        method=method,
        parser=parser if dom is not None else None,
        extractor=extractor,
        parse_ms=parse_ms,
        extract_ms=total_ms - parse_ms,
        paywalled=jsonld.is_paywalled(objects),
    )
"""What the model reads: the headline plus the lede or the whole body, cut to a token budget."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Sequence

from veritrade.extract.dom import split_sentences
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for
from veritrade.extract.types import Article, Scope

CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
LEDE_PARAGRAPHS = 2
LEDE_MIN_TOKENS = 60  # a dateline-only first paragraph is topped up with the next one
LEDE_MAX_TOKENS = 200
_SEP = "\n\n"


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return math.ceil(len(text) / CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def lede_paragraphs(article: Article) -> list[str]:
    profile = profile_for(article.source)
    count = profile.lede_paragraphs if profile else LEDE_PARAGRAPHS
    out = list(article.paragraphs[:count])
    for paragraph in article.paragraphs[count:]:
        if estimate_tokens(_SEP.join(out)) >= LEDE_MIN_TOKENS:
            break
        out.append(paragraph)
    return out


def _cut(paragraph: str, room: int, *, mid_sentence: bool) -> str:
    kept = ""
    for sentence in split_sentences(paragraph):
        candidate = f"{kept} {sentence}" if kept else sentence
        if len(candidate) > room:
            break
        kept = candidate
    if kept or not mid_sentence:
        return kept
    head = paragraph[: room + 1]
    return head[:room] if " " not in head else head.rsplit(" ", 1)[0]


def fit(paragraphs: Sequence[str], budget_chars: int) -> list[str]:
    """Whole paragraphs, then whole sentences; words are cut only when not even one sentence fits."""
    out: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for paragraph in paragraphs:
        sep = len(_SEP) if out else 0
        if used + sep + len(paragraph) <= budget_chars:
            out.append(paragraph)
            used += sep + len(paragraph)
            continue
        if partial := _cut(paragraph, budget_chars - used - sep, mid_sentence=not out):
            out.append(partial)
        break
    return out


def build_input(article: Article, scope: Scope, max_tokens: int) -> str:
    """'TITLE: ...' then a blank line and the body; the estimate (chars / 4) never exceeds max_tokens."""
    if max_tokens <= 0:
        raise ValueError("max_tokens must be positive")
    budget = max_tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN
    head = f"TITLE: {article.title}" if article.title else ""
    if len(head) > budget:
        return _SEP.join(fit([head], budget))
    room = budget - len(head) - (len(_SEP) if head else 0)
    if scope == "lede":
        body = fit(lede_paragraphs(article), min(room, LEDE_MAX_TOKENS * CHARS_PER_TOKEN))
    else:
        body = fit(article.paragraphs, room)
    return _SEP.join([head, *body] if head else body)

"""Thin async adapters from (model spec, prompt, article text) to validated outputs and verdicts."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import aclosing
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

from veritrade.errors import SchemaViolation
from veritrade.inference.confidence import (
    LabelLogprobPolicy,
    OrdinalPolicy,
    ProbabilityPolicy,
    policy_for,
)
from veritrade.inference.incremental import JsonFieldScanner, ScanEvent
from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.inference.schemas import (
    ANALYZE_MODELS,
    AnalyzeOut,
    LabelOut,
    OrdinalOut,
    SummaryOut,
    ollama_format,
)
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, DecisionResult, Endpoint, OllamaTimings, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec, SignalSchema
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptSpec

CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
TOP_LOGPROBS = 20


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SummaryResult:
    output: SummaryOut
    chat: ChatResult


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AnalyzeResult:
    output: AnalyzeOut
    verdict: Verdict
    chat: ChatResult

    @property
    def entity(self) -> str | None:
        return self.output.entity.strip() or None


def fit_input(text: str, max_input_tokens: int) -> str:
    """Cap at max_input_tokens (chars/4), cutting at the last whitespace so no word is split."""
    limit = max_input_tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    cut = max(text.rfind(" ", 0, limit), text.rfind("\n", 0, limit))
    return text[: cut if cut > limit // 2 else limit].rstrip()


def chat_options(spec: ModelSpec, endpoint: Endpoint) -> dict[str, Any]:
    options: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if spec.num_ctx is not None:
        options["num_ctx"] = spec.num_ctx
    if endpoint in spec.num_predict:
        options["num_predict"] = spec.num_predict[endpoint]
    return options


def score_verdict(spec: ModelSpec, score: int) -> Verdict:
    """Verdict for a streamed or /analyze score; both always use the ordinal policy."""
    return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t).decide(score)


def _sum(a: float | None, b: float | None) -> float | None:
    return None if a is None and b is None else (a or 0) + (b or 0)


def _sum_int(a: int | None, b: int | None) -> int | None:
    return None if a is None and b is None else (a or 0) + (b or 0)


def _combine(first: ChatResult, second: ChatResult) -> ChatResult:
    # The fallback call's output decides; the reported cost covers both calls.
    t1, t2 = first.timings, second.timings
    return ChatResult(
        content=second.content,
        wall_ms=first.wall_ms + second.wall_ms,
        timings=OllamaTimings(
            load_ms=_sum(t1.load_ms, t2.load_ms),
            prompt_eval_ms=_sum(t1.prompt_eval_ms, t2.prompt_eval_ms),
            eval_ms=_sum(t1.eval_ms, t2.eval_ms),
            prompt_tokens=_sum_int(t1.prompt_tokens, t2.prompt_tokens),
            eval_tokens=_sum_int(t1.eval_tokens, t2.eval_tokens),
            total_ms=_sum(t1.total_ms, t2.total_ms),
        ),
        logprobs=second.logprobs,
    )


async def _signal_call(
    client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str, schema: SignalSchema
) -> tuple[LabelOut | OrdinalOut, ChatResult]:
    out_type: type[LabelOut] | type[OrdinalOut] = LabelOut if schema == "label" else OrdinalOut
    return await client.chat_json(
        spec.name,
        prompt.messages(text, schema),
        out_type,
        options=chat_options(spec, "signal"),
        logprobs=True,
        top_logprobs=TOP_LOGPROBS,
    )


async def classify_signal(
    client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str
) -> tuple[Verdict, ChatResult | DecisionResult]:
    """Label-logprob falls back label -> ordinal call (score sign) -> ordinal policy on the score."""
    text = fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens)
    policy = policy_for(spec, endpoint="signal")
    if isinstance(policy, ProbabilityPolicy):
        decision = await client.decide_sentiment(
            spec.name, prompt.state(text), prompt.instructions, prompt.criteria_map
        )
        return policy.decide(decision.probabilities), decision
    out, chat = await _signal_call(client, spec, prompt, text, spec.signal_schema or "ordinal")
    if isinstance(policy, LabelLogprobPolicy):
        verdict = policy.decide(out, chat)
        if verdict is None and isinstance(out, LabelOut):
            out, second = await _signal_call(client, spec, prompt, text, "ordinal")
            chat = _combine(chat, second)
            verdict = policy.decide(out, chat)
        if verdict is not None:
            return verdict, chat
    if not isinstance(out, OrdinalOut):
        raise SchemaViolation(f"{spec.name}: a label output needs the label-logprob policy")
    return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t).decide(out.score), chat


def _validate[T: BaseModel](out_type: type[T], content: str, model: str) -> T:
    try:
        return out_type.model_validate_json(content)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise SchemaViolation(
            f"{model} streamed output that does not match {out_type.__name__}", hint=str(exc)[:300]
        ) from exc


async def summarize(client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str) -> SummaryResult:
    messages = prompt.messages(fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens), "default")
    out, chat = await client.chat_json(spec.name, messages, SummaryOut, options=chat_options(spec, "summary"))
    return SummaryResult(out, chat)


async def summarize_stream(
    client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str
) -> AsyncGenerator[ScanEvent | SummaryResult]:
    """Summary text deltas as they decode, then the validated result (no retry once tokens are out)."""
    messages = prompt.messages(fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens), "default")
    scanner = JsonFieldScanner()
    stream = client.chat_stream(
        spec.name, messages, format=ollama_format(SummaryOut), options=chat_options(spec, "summary")
    )
    async with aclosing(stream):
        async for item in stream:
            if isinstance(item, ChatResult):
                scanner.close()
                yield SummaryResult(_validate(SummaryOut, item.content, spec.name), item)
                return
            for event in scanner.feed(item):
                yield event


async def analyze(client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str) -> AnalyzeResult:
    order = spec.field_order or "sentiment-first"
    messages = prompt.messages(fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens), order)
    out, chat = await client.chat_json(
        spec.name, messages, ANALYZE_MODELS[order], options=chat_options(spec, "analyze")
    )
    return AnalyzeResult(out, score_verdict(spec, out.score), chat)


async def analyze_stream(
    client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str
) -> AsyncGenerator[ScanEvent | AnalyzeResult]:
    """Scanner events in generation order (ScoreClosed first when sentiment-first), then the result."""
    order = spec.field_order or "sentiment-first"
    out_type = ANALYZE_MODELS[order]
    messages = prompt.messages(fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens), order)
    scanner = JsonFieldScanner()
    stream = client.chat_stream(
        spec.name, messages, format=ollama_format(out_type), options=chat_options(spec, "analyze")
    )
    async with aclosing(stream):
        async for item in stream:
            if isinstance(item, ChatResult):
                scanner.close()
                out = _validate(out_type, item.content, spec.name)
                yield AnalyzeResult(out, score_verdict(spec, out.score), item)
                return
            for event in scanner.feed(item):
                yield event
