from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from veritrade.fetch.types import FetchResult
from veritrade.inference.types import SENTIMENTS, Sentiment
from veritrade_evals import __main__ as cli
from veritrade_evals import articles_cli
from veritrade_evals.articles import (
    ArticlePaths,
    ArticleRow,
    ArticlesError,
    Candidate,
    FetchRecord,
    article_id,
    load_articles,
    read_jsonl,
    write_json,
)
from veritrade_evals.articles_candidates import merge, select_found, write_view
from veritrade_evals.articles_fetch import fetch_articles, pick_top
from veritrade_evals.articles_finalize import (
    ShortfallError,
    build_ledger,
    choose,
    finalize,
    plan_quotas,
    publisher_text_problems,
    split_cell,
    status,
    verify,
    write_finalized,
)
from veritrade_evals.articles_validate import adjudicate_requested, ingest, shingles
from veritrade_evals.discovery import ArchiveClient, Found, Link, Politeness
from veritrade_evals.paths import ARTICLES_DIR

SOURCES = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
SCORES: dict[Sentiment, int] = {"bullish": 2, "bearish": -1, "neutral": 0}


@pytest.fixture
def paths(tmp_path: Path) -> ArticlePaths:
    return ArticlePaths(private=tmp_path / "private", committed=tmp_path / "committed")


def body_lines(tag: str) -> list[str]:
    return [
        f"{tag} sentence {n} reports that the {tag} unit shipped {n * 11} crates while costs held near "
        f"{n * 3} percent overall"
        for n in range(1, 8)
    ]


def seed(
    paths: ArticlePaths,
    article: str,
    source: str,
    label: Sentiment,
    *,
    b_label: Sentiment | None = None,
    ambiguous: bool = False,
    title: str | None = None,
    published: str = "2026-10-01",
) -> None:
    html = f"<html><body>{article}</body></html>".encode()
    paths.html(article).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths.html(article).write_bytes(html)
    from veritrade_evals.articles import sha256_bytes

    record = FetchRecord(
        id=article,
        source=source,
        url=f"https://{source}.example.com/{article}",
        fetched_at="2026-10-18T09:00:00+00:00",
        status=200,
        html_sha256=sha256_bytes(html),
        words=150,
        method="profile",
        published_date=published,
        published_from="page",
    )
    write_json(paths.fetched(article), record.model_dump())
    lines = ["Menu", title or f"{article} headline about {label} news", *body_lines(article)]
    write_json(paths.lines(article), {"id": article, "lines": lines})
    gold = {
        "id": article,
        "usable": True,
        "title_line": 2,
        "body_ranges": [[3, 9]],
        "key_facts": ["The unit shipped 77 crates.", "Costs held near 21 percent.", "Shipments began at 11 crates."],
        "entity": f"{source} holdings",
        "ticker": None,
        "provisional_label": label,
    }
    write_json(paths.out("gold", article), gold)
    for stage, value, flag in (("label_a", label, False), ("label_b", b_label or label, ambiguous)):
        write_json(
            paths.out(stage, article),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            {
                "id": article,
                "label": value,
                "score": SCORES[value],
                "entity": f"{source} holdings",
                "ticker": "ABC" if stage == "label_b" else None,
                "rationale": f"The news points {value} for the company in our reading.",
                "ambiguous": flag,
                "confidence": 4,
            },
        )


def adjudicate(paths: ArticlePaths, article: str, decision: str, label: Sentiment) -> None:
    write_json(
        paths.out("adjudicate", article),
        {
            "id": article,
            "decision": decision,
            "label": label,
            "score": SCORES[label],
            "entity": "adjudicated entity",
            "ticker": "ADJ",
            "rationale": "The adjudicator weighed both readings.",
        },
    )


def ingest_all(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    for stage in ("gold", "label_a", "label_b"):
        ingest(paths, stage)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def seed_pool(paths: ArticlePaths, per_cell: int = 4) -> None:
    for source in SOURCES:
        for label in SENTIMENTS:
            for n in range(per_cell):
                seed(paths, f"art-{source}{label}{n:02d}", source, label)
    # One disagreement per source, kept by the adjudicator, and one replaced.
    for source in SOURCES:
        seed(paths, f"art-{source}disputed", source, "bullish", b_label="neutral")
        seed(paths, f"art-{source}replaced", source, "bearish", ambiguous=True)
    ingest_all(paths)
    for source in SOURCES:
        adjudicate(paths, f"art-{source}disputed", "keep", "bullish")
        adjudicate(paths, f"art-{source}replaced", "replace", "bearish")
    ingest(paths, "adjudicate")


# --- ingest -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_gold_ingest_writes_bodies_and_drops_stale_ones(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed(paths, "art-one", "alpha", "bullish")
    report = ingest(paths, "gold")
    assert [(r.id, r.ok) for r in report.results] == [("art-one", True)]
    assert paths.gold("art-one").read_text() == "\n\n".join(body_lines("art-one"))
    raw = json.loads(paths.out("gold", "art-one").read_text())
    write_json(paths.out("gold", "art-one"), raw | {"body_ranges": [[3, 99]]})
    report = ingest(paths, "gold")
    assert report.results[0].codes == ("range_out_of_bounds",)
    assert not paths.gold("art-one").exists()


def test_label_ingest_lists_disagreements_and_ambiguity(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed(paths, "art-agree", "alpha", "bullish")
    seed(paths, "art-split", "alpha", "bullish", b_label="bearish")
    seed(paths, "art-unsure", "alpha", "neutral", ambiguous=True)
    ingest(paths, "gold")
    ingest(paths, "label_a")
    report = ingest(paths, "label_b")
    assert report.agreement is not None
    assert report.agreement.n == 3
    assert report.agreement.agreed == 2
    assert adjudicate_requested(paths) == {"art-split", "art-unsure"}


# --- quotas, selection, split -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def avail(**overrides: tuple[int, int, int]) -> dict[str, dict[Sentiment, int]]:
    out = {s: dict(zip(SENTIMENTS, overrides.get(s, (5, 5, 5)), strict=True)) for s in SOURCES}
    return out  # type: ignore[return-value]


def test_quotas_default_to_three_each() -> None:
    quota = plan_quotas(avail(), SOURCES)
    assert all(q == 3 for per in quota.values() for q in per.values())


def test_quotas_rebalance_a_short_class_across_sources() -> None:
    quota = plan_quotas(avail(alpha=(5, 2, 5)), SOURCES)
    assert quota["alpha"]["bearish"] == 2
    assert quota["beta"]["bearish"] == 4
    assert {c: sum(quota[s][c] for s in SOURCES) for c in SENTIMENTS} == dict.fromkeys(SENTIMENTS, 9)


def test_quotas_prefer_sources_that_lost_a_slot() -> None:
    # alpha is short of bearish, beta of neutral: each makes up the other's class.
    quota = plan_quotas(avail(alpha=(5, 2, 5), beta=(5, 5, 2), gamma=(3, 3, 3)), SOURCES)
    assert quota["alpha"] == {"bullish": 3, "bearish": 2, "neutral": 4}
    assert quota["beta"] == {"bullish": 3, "bearish": 4, "neutral": 2}
    assert sum(quota["alpha"].values()) == sum(quota["beta"].values()) == 9


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("overrides", "message"),
    [
        ({"alpha": (5, 1, 5)}, "alpha bearish: 1 eligible, at least 2 needed"),
        ({"alpha": (5, 2, 5), "beta": (5, 2, 5)}, "bearish: at most 8 of 9"),
        ({"alpha": (3, 3, 3), "beta": (3, 3, 3), "gamma": (2, 3, 3)}, "bullish: at most 8 of 9"),
    ],
)
def test_quotas_report_impossible_sets(overrides: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]], message: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ShortfallError) as exc:
        plan_quotas(avail(**overrides), SOURCES)
    assert any(message in problem for problem in exc.value.problems)


def test_choose_prefers_agreed_and_is_seeded() -> None:
    cell = {"art-a": "agreed", "art-b": "adjudicated", "art-c": "agreed", "art-d": "agreed"}
    picked = choose(cell, 3, seed=1, source="alpha", label="bullish")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert sorted(picked) == ["art-a", "art-c", "art-d"]
    assert choose(cell, 4, seed=1, source="alpha", label="bullish")[-1] == "art-b"  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert picked == choose(cell, 3, seed=1, source="alpha", label="bullish")  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_split_cell_puts_exactly_one_in_dev() -> None:
    splits = split_cell(["art-a", "art-b", "art-c"], seed=7, source="alpha", label="bearish")
    assert sorted(splits.values()) == ["dev", "test", "test"]
    assert splits == split_cell(["art-c", "art-b", "art-a"], seed=7, source="alpha", label="bearish")


# --- finalize end to end ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_finalize_selects_splits_and_is_deterministic(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths)
    first = finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES, seed=11)
    again = finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES, seed=11)
    assert first == again
    rows = first.rows
    assert len(rows) == 27
    assert first.stats["classes"] == dict.fromkeys(SENTIMENTS, 9)
    assert first.stats["splits"] == {"dev": 9, "test": 18}
    for source in SOURCES:
        for label in SENTIMENTS:
            cell = [r for r in rows if r.source == source and r.label == label]
            assert len(cell) == 3
            assert [r.split for r in cell].count("dev") == 1
    assert not any(r.id.endswith("replaced") for r in rows)
    pool = first.stats["pool"]
    assert isinstance(pool, dict)
    assert pool["adjudicated"] == 6
    assert pool["replaced"] == 3
    assert pool["sent_to_adjudication"] == 6
    other = finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES, seed=12)
    assert [(r.id, r.split) for r in other.rows] != [(r.id, r.split) for r in rows]


def test_finalize_row_fields_follow_the_labels(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=2)
    rows = {r.id: r for r in finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES, seed=3).rows}
    disputed = rows["art-alphadisputed"]
    assert disputed.label == "bullish"
    assert disputed.entity == "adjudicated entity"
    assert disputed.labels.adjudicated is not None
    assert disputed.labels.adjudicated.decision == "keep"
    agreed = rows["art-alphabullish00"]
    assert agreed.score == 2.0
    assert agreed.ticker == "ABC"
    assert agreed.labels.adjudicated is None
    assert agreed.labels.final == "bullish"


def test_finalize_ignores_articles_outside_the_window(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=3)
    seed(paths, "art-old", "alpha", "bullish", published="2026-08-18")
    ingest_all(paths)
    assert "art-old" not in {r.id for r in finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES).rows}


def test_finalize_fails_loudly_with_a_shortfall(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    for source in SOURCES:
        for label in SENTIMENTS:
            seed(paths, f"art-{source}{label}", source, label)
    ingest_all(paths)
    with pytest.raises(ShortfallError, match="eligible, at least 2 needed"):
        finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES)


def test_verify_and_loader_catch_drift(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=3)
    write_finalized(finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES), paths)
    assert all(not problems for _, problems in verify(paths))
    dev = load_articles("dev", paths=paths)
    assert len(dev) == 9
    assert dev[0].gold_text == paths.gold(dev[0].id).read_text()
    assert len(load_articles("all", paths=paths)) == 27
    paths.gold(dev[0].id).write_text("edited")
    paths.html(dev[1].id).unlink()
    found = dict(verify(paths))
    assert found[dev[0].id] == ["gold_drifted"]
    assert found[dev[1].id] == ["html_missing"]
    with pytest.raises(ArticlesError, match="missing or drifted"):
        load_articles("dev", paths=paths)


# --- no publisher text --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_committed_output_carries_no_publisher_text(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=3)
    result = finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES)
    write_finalized(result, paths)
    committed = paths.rows.read_text() + paths.stats.read_text()
    for row in result.rows:
        lines = json.loads(paths.lines(row.id).read_text())["lines"]
        assert lines[1] not in committed
        assert all(line not in committed for line in lines[2:])
    bodies = {r.id: paths.gold(r.id).read_text() for r in result.rows}
    titles = {r.id: json.loads(paths.lines(r.id).read_text())["lines"][1] for r in result.rows}
    assert publisher_text_problems(result.rows, bodies, titles) == []


def test_publisher_text_guard_flags_copied_text(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=3)
    row = finalize(build_ledger(paths), SOURCES).rows[0]
    body = paths.gold(row.id).read_text()
    title = "A distinctive invented headline about crates"
    copied = " ".join(body.split()[:12])
    bad = row.model_copy(update={"key_facts": [copied], "rationale": f"See: {title}"})
    problems = publisher_text_problems([bad], {row.id: body}, {row.id: title})
    assert f"{row.id}:key_facts[0]:verbatim_body" in problems
    assert f"{row.id}:rationale:headline" in problems


def test_committed_article_rows_are_publisher_free() -> None:
    """Runs on the real committed set once it exists; the schema forbids any title or body field."""
    path = ARTICLES_DIR / "articles.jsonl"
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip("article set not finalized yet")
    rows = read_jsonl(path, ArticleRow)
    assert rows
    real = ArticlePaths()
    for row in rows:
        assert all(len(fact.split()) <= 25 for fact in row.key_facts)
        assert len(row.rationale.split()) <= 50
        gold = real.gold(row.id)
        if gold.exists():
            assert publisher_text_problems([row], {row.id: gold.read_text()}, {}) == []

# --- candidates and fetch -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def found(url: str, *, title: str | None = None, published: str | None = None, via: str = "sitemap") -> Found:
    return Found(Link(url, title, published), via, "https://example.com/sitemap.xml", "loss" if via == "search" else None)


def test_select_found_applies_window_query_and_cap() -> None:
    from veritrade_evals.articles_candidates import SourceReport

    items = [
        found("https://example.com/2026/10/01/acme-widens-loss.html"),
        found("https://example.com/2026/07/01/acme-widens-loss-again.html"),
        found("https://example.com/b", title="Acme posts record profit", published="2026-10-02"),
        found("https://example.com/c", via="search"),
        found("https://example.com/d", title="Acme narrows losses"),
    ]
    report = SourceReport("wire")
    picked = select_found(
        report, items, since=date(2026, 8, 19), until=date(2026, 10, 18), queries=["loss"], max_new=2, known=set()
    )
    assert [c.url for c in picked] == ["https://example.com/2026/10/01/acme-widens-loss.html", "https://example.com/c"]
    assert picked[0].published_at == "2026-10-01"
    assert picked[1].query == "loss"
    assert (report.out_of_window, report.query_miss, report.capped) == (1, 1, 1)


def test_merge_keeps_order_and_fills_missing_fields() -> None:
    old = Candidate(id="art-1", source="s", url="https://e/1", via="feed", via_url="u")
    new = Candidate(id="art-1", source="s", url="https://e/1", title="T", published_at="2026-10-01", via="x", via_url="v")
    other = Candidate(id="art-2", source="s", url="https://e/2", via="feed", via_url="u")
    merged, added = merge([old], [new, other])
    assert added == 1
    assert [c.id for c in merged] == ["art-1", "art-2"]
    assert merged[0].title == "T"
    assert merged[0].via == "feed"


def candidate(n: int, published: str | None) -> Candidate:
    url = f"https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/0{n}/story-{n}.html"
    return Candidate(id=article_id(url), source="cnbc", url=url, published_at=published, via="feed", via_url="u")


def test_view_and_pick_top_respect_the_window(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    pool = [candidate(1, "2026-10-01"), candidate(2, None), candidate(3, "2026-07-01"), candidate(4, "2026-10-04")]
    from veritrade_evals.articles import write_jsonl

    write_jsonl(paths.candidates("cnbc"), pool)

    assert (rows, total) == (3, 4)
    assert paths.view("cnbc").read_text().splitlines()[0].startswith("id\t")
    top = pick_top(pool, paths, 3, since=date(2026, 8, 19), until=date(2026, 10, 18))
    assert [c.published_at for c in top] == ["2026-10-04", "2026-10-01", None]


ARTICLE_HTML = (
    '<html><head><script type="application/ld+json">{"@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "Synthetic", '
    '"datePublished": "2026-10-05T10:00:00Z", "articleBody": "'
    + " ".join(["Synthetic body sentence about invented companies."] * 20)
    + '"}</script></head><body><p>Visible.</p></body></html>'
)


class FakeFetcher:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.urls: list[str] = []

    async def get(self, url: str) -> FetchResult:
        self.urls.append(url)
        if url.endswith("blocked.html"):
            from veritrade.errors import SourceBlocked

            raise SourceBlocked("blocked", upstream_status=403)
        return FetchResult(url, url, 200, ARTICLE_HTML, "text/html", 12.0)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        return None


class AllowAll(ArchiveClient):
    async def allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        return True


async def test_fetch_records_status_words_and_dates(paths: ArticlePaths, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    from veritrade_evals import articles_fetch

    monkeypatch.setattr(articles_fetch, "Politeness", lambda: Politeness(0.0, 0.0))
    ok, blocked = candidate(5, "2026-10-04"), candidate(6, None)
    blocked = blocked.model_copy(update={"url": "https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/blocked.html"})
    fetcher = FakeFetcher()
    robots = AllowAll(paths.cache)
    results = await fetch_articles([ok, blocked], paths=paths, fetcher=fetcher, robots=robots)
    good, bad = (record for _, record in results)
    assert good is not None
    assert good.ok
    assert good.method == "jsonld"
    assert good.words > 40
    assert good.published_date == "2026-10-05"
    assert good.published_from == "page"
    assert paths.html(ok.id).read_text() == ARTICLE_HTML
    assert bad is not None
    assert (bad.error, bad.status, bad.ok) == ("source_blocked", 403, False)
    again = await fetch_articles([ok], paths=paths, fetcher=fetcher, robots=robots)
    assert again[0][1] is None
    assert len(fetcher.urls) == 2
    await robots.aclose()


def test_status_counts_each_stage(paths: ArticlePaths) -> None:
    seed_pool(paths, per_cell=2)
    rows = {r.source: r for r in status(paths, SOURCES)}
    alpha = rows["alpha"]
    assert alpha.fetched_ok == 8
    assert alpha.gold_usable == {"bullish": 3, "bearish": 3, "neutral": 2}
    assert (alpha.labelled_a, alpha.labelled_b, alpha.agreed) == (8, 8, 6)
    assert (alpha.adjudicated_keep, alpha.adjudicated_replace, alpha.pending_adjudication) == (1, 1, 0)
    assert alpha.eligible == {"bullish": 3, "bearish": 2, "neutral": 2}

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize` and `verify`. `status` is safe for anyone to run.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b    # prints agreement, writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 10 - Discover candidates for one source

You are the discovery agent for **one source** (its key is in the message that spawned you, for example `cnbc`).
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read titles only through the Read
tool on the private view file, never quote a headline or any article text in your messages or final report,
never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Goal

End with **at least 6 fetched articles per class** (bullish, bearish, neutral) for your source, published
between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-18, so that at least 5 per class survive the gold step. You judge the likely
class from the headline only; the real labels come later from independent labellers, so aim for clear cases.

A good candidate is one news story, press release or filing exhibit mainly about **one primary entity**: a
company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy. Skip live blogs, videos, galleries, opinion
roundups, newsletters, market wraps that list many stocks, "best stocks to buy" lists, quote pages, and law-firm
"class action" or "investor alert" releases (advertising, not issuer news).

What the classes mean (same rubric as the labellers, `30-label.md`): **bullish** = clear, material positive
economic impact on the primary entity (results or guidance above expectations, a major contract or approval, a
takeover at a premium); **bearish** = clear, material negative impact (results or guidance below expectations,
large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades, layoffs tied to weakness); **neutral** = no clear
material direction (scheduled announcements, routine appointments and dividends, conference-call notices,
explainers, balanced or minor news). Emotional wording is not a signal.

## Commands

All from the repository root. Output is ids, URLs, counts and paths only.

```bash
# 1. broad sweep with the source's feeds and deeper archives (sitemaps, archive pages, listings, EDGAR)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE

# 2. targeted sweeps: --query is a keyword search where the archive supports it (PR Newswire search,
#    EDGAR full-text search) and a headline/URL-slug filter everywhere else; repeat --query freely
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE --query "lowered guidance" --query "net loss"

# 3. extra listing pages on the source's own domain (Yahoo quote news pages, section pages)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source yahoo \
  --listing-url https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TICKER/news/

# 4. write a compact private view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) and Read it
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles candidates --source SOURCE --unfetched [--query WORD] [--limit 300]
#    -> evals/data/private/articles/views/SOURCE.tsv   (Read it with the Read tool; it is private)

# 5. fetch your picks through the serving fetcher; list ids one per line in a private file
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles fetch --source SOURCE --ids-file evals/data/private/articles/picks/SOURCE.txt

# progress for your source
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status --source SOURCE
```

Archive responses are cached for 6 hours, so repeating `discover` with new queries is cheap and polite.
`--pages N` deepens paged listings, search and EDGAR (default 3 to 40 depending on the archive).

## Query ideas

- Bearish: `lowered guidance`, `cuts forecast`, `profit warning`, `net loss`, `misses`, `downgrade`, `layoffs`,
  `recall`, `investigation`, `impairment`, `going concern`, `delisting`, `shares fall`, `plunge`, `default`.
- Bullish: `raises guidance`, `record revenue`, `beats`, `upgrade`, `to acquire`, `approval`, `contract`,
  `surges`, `dividend increase`, `buyback`.
- Neutral: `conference call`, `to present`, `appoints`, `annual meeting`, `declares quarterly dividend`,
  `launches`, `explainer`, `what to know`.

Source notes:

- **sec**: discovery uses EDGAR full-text search over 8-K filings and keeps the EX-99.1 exhibit. The view's
  `edgar_items` column helps: `2.02` is results of operations (earnings, either direction), `5.02` officer
  changes (usually neutral), `1.01` material agreements, `2.05`/`2.06` restructuring and impairments (often
  bearish), `8.01` other events. Search phrases such as `"third quarter"`, `net loss`, `record`, `lowered`.
- **prnewswire**, **globenewswire**: wires carry many non-US issuers and many law-firm ads; prefer issuer
  releases with numbers (results, guidance, deals). Bearish releases are rarer: search for losses, impairments,
  restructuring, going-concern and guidance cuts.
- **yahoo**, **bbc**, **cnn**, **guardian**: listings carry no or few dates; the publish date comes from the page
  at fetch time and out-of-window pages are dropped later, so prefer recent pages and check the fetch output.
- **fool**: much of the output is evergreen "should you buy" commentary; prefer news-driven articles about one
  company (earnings reactions, guidance, deals).

## Procedure

1. Run the broad sweep, then 2-4 targeted sweeps per class. Stop sweeping when the window holds plenty of
   plausible candidates per class (dozens), or after about 12 discover runs.
2. Write the view and Read it. Pick about **8 per class** (24 in total) by headline, preferring clear cases
   and a spread of companies. Put the ids, one per line, into
   `evals/data/private/articles/picks/<source>.txt` (create the folder if needed; only ids go in it).
3. Fetch them. For each printed line check: `ok` (not an error such as `source_blocked`, `paywalled`,
   `consent_required`, `upstream_http`), `words` of at least about 200, a `published` date inside the window, and
   `method` other than an `extract_error`. Replace failures with new picks and fetch again until you reach at
   least 6 good fetches per class.
4. Do not prepare packets, label or edit anything else; the main loop takes it from here.

## Final report (counts only, no headlines or article text)

- Fetched OK per intended class, and fetch errors by code.
- Which archive kinds and queries were productive (query strings are fine, they are yours).
- Any class that looks hard to fill for this source, and why in general terms.

````markdown
# 20 - Gold body, key facts and a provisional label

You turn fetched pages into reference ("gold") article bodies. The gold body is the yardstick for the
extraction benchmark (which parser and extractor recover the article best) and the text the labellers read.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read pages only with the Read tool
on the packet files you are given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/`, never quote article
text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Input

The message that spawned you lists gold packet paths, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/gold/<id>.md`.

A packet shows the page's visible text as numbered lines (`L0001 ...`), one per text block. Lines are
folded into marker rows that keep their numbers, for example `L0012-L0040 [29 lines hidden: short lines
(menus, buttons, tickers)]` or `L0001-L0140 [140 lines hidden: before the located article]`. Folding is only
for compactness: every line number stays valid. If the headline is not visible, the story looks cut off, or a
folded run might be part of the article (a short bulleted list), Read the full packet named in the header
(`<id>.full.md`), which shows every line.

## Decide: usable or not

Usable means one news story, press release or filing exhibit, in English, mainly about **one primary entity**
(a company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy), with at least 120 words of body text.
Otherwise set `usable: false` and one `reject_reason`:

| reject_reason | when |
|---|---|
| `not_article` | index or section page, quote page, data-only page, error, consent or login page |
| `live_blog` | rolling live coverage with timestamps |
| `paywalled_stub` | only a teaser; the rest is behind a wall |
| `roundup` | several unrelated items or companies with no primary entity (market wraps, newsletters, lists) |
| `video_only` | the story is a video with a caption |
| `too_short` | under 120 words of body text |
| `non_english` | not in English |
| `duplicate` | the same story as another packet in your batch (keep the better one) |
| `other` | anything else (say why in your final report, in general terms) |

## For usable pages

- `title_line`: the line holding the headline (normally the `h1` just above the story).
- `body_ranges`: inclusive `[start, end]` line ranges that together cover exactly the article body, in order and
  not overlapping. Include: the dateline lede, body paragraphs, in-body subheadings, bulleted or numbered lists
  that belong to the story, quotes. Exclude: the headline, standfirst or dek, editor key-points boxes, bylines,
  dates, image captions and credits, "read more" and related links, ads and their labels, newsletter and app
  promos, share buttons, author bios, comment prompts, financial tables, and press-release boilerplate after
  the story (About the company, forward-looking or safe-harbor statements, contacts, "SOURCE" lines, "View
  original content"). Split a range to skip a promo or a folded run of menu lines in the middle of a story.
  The title line must not fall inside a body range.
- `key_facts`: 3 to 5 statements, at most 25 words each, most market-moving first, in your own words. Copy
  numbers exactly as the body writes them ("$1.25 billion", "28%", "third quarter"), and only use numbers that
  appear in the body: no sums, differences or conversions. Never copy 10 or more consecutive words.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written ("Nvidia", "Brent crude", "UK economy").
- `ticker`: the ticker if the article states it or it is unambiguous, else `null`.
- `provisional_label`: your quick read with the rubric in `30-label.md` (bullish, bearish or neutral). It is
  only used to balance the selection; the real labels come from two independent labellers.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json` with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "usable": true,
  "reject_reason": null,
  "title_line": 41,
  "body_ranges": [[44, 61], [64, 70]],
  "key_facts": [
    "Fact in your own words with numbers copied exactly from the body.",
    "Second fact.",
    "Third fact."
  ],
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "provisional_label": "bearish"
}
```

For a rejected page: `{"id": "...", "usable": false, "reject_reason": "live_blog"}` (other fields may be
omitted).

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs of your batch, run:

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage gold
```

It prints one line per id: `PASS` (with your provisional label and the body word count, or `rejected:<reason>`)
or `FAIL` with codes. Fix every `FAIL` among your ids and run it again until they all pass.

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `schema:<field>:<type>` | field missing, misspelled, wrong type, or an unknown field |
| `missing:<field>` | usable outputs need `title_line`, `body_ranges`, `entity`, `provisional_label` |
| `range_inverted`, `range_out_of_bounds`, `ranges_overlap` | ranges must be `[start, end]`, start <= end, within the page, disjoint |
| `title_out_of_bounds`, `title_in_body` | the headline line must exist and sit outside the body ranges |
| `body_too_short` | under 120 words: widen the ranges if you cut too much, else reject as `too_short` |
| `key_facts_count`, `key_fact_too_long`, `key_fact_empty` | 3 to 5 facts, each 1 to 25 words |
| `key_fact_number_ungrounded` | a number in a fact does not appear in the body text; copy it exactly |
| `key_fact_verbatim` | a fact shares 10 consecutive words with the body; rephrase |
| `missing_packet_lines` | the packet was not prepared; tell the main loop |

## Final report (counts only)

Usable vs rejected (by reason), provisional labels (bullish / bearish / neutral), any ids that still fail
and their codes. No headlines, quotes or article text.

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). The agreement line it prints may include the other labeller's progress; ignore it.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# 40 - Adjudicate disagreements and ambiguous articles

You resolve the articles where the two labellers disagreed or at least one flagged the article as ambiguous.
The message that spawned you lists adjudication packets, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/adjudicate/<id>.md`.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read
tool on the packets you were given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/`, never quote
article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

A packet holds both labellers' outputs (label, score, entity, ticker, ambiguous flag, confidence, rationale)
followed by the headline and article body, the same text they read. Do not open other files.

## Rubric

Use exactly the rubric in `evals/opus_prompts/30-label.md`: the economic impact of the news on its primary
entity, not the tone; bullish or bearish only for a clear, material implication; mixed news follows the
dominant material driver, or neutral if balanced. Form your own reading from the article first, then weigh
the two rationales as arguments, not votes.

## Decide

- `keep`: the article has one defensible label under the rubric, and the disagreement came from a misreading,
  a materiality threshold, or a different primary entity that the article settles. Your label, score, entity
  and ticker become final.
- `replace`: the article stays genuinely ambiguous: balanced mixed news, no clear primary entity, materiality
  that depends on facts the article does not give, or a direction a careful analyst could reasonably dispute.
  Replaced articles leave the set and the main loop finds others. The set is only useful if its labels are
  defensible, so do not keep an article just to fill a quota.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/<id>.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "decision": "keep",
  "label": "neutral",
  "score": 0,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": null,
  "rationale": "Your own words, at most 50: why this label, and what settled the disagreement."
}
```

For `replace`, still give your best label and score (their sign must agree) and say in the rationale why the
article is too ambiguous to keep.

## Validate and fix

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage adjudicate
```

Fix every `FAIL`: `schema:<field>:<type>`, `score_label_mismatch`, `rationale_too_long`, `rationale_verbatim`
(rephrase), `not_requested` (the id is not in `adjudicate_ids.txt`; tell the main loop), `gold_missing`.

## Final report (counts only)

Kept by final label, replaced, and for kept articles whether you sided with labeller A, labeller B or neither.
No headlines, quotes or article text.

````

# --- source registry and archives ------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Archive:
    kind: ArchiveKind
    url: str
    pages: int = 1
    select: IndexSelect = "all"


GNW_PATTERN = r"^https://www\.globenewswire\.com/news-release/20\d\d/\d\d/\d\d/\d+/\d+/en/[^/]+\.html$"
# Archive pages link to sibling day pages and other nav that the article pattern would accept.
ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE = re.compile(r"/(?:all|altdate)$")

# Verified live on 2026-10-18; feeds and sections from sources.toml run first.
ARCHIVES: dict[str, tuple[Archive, ...]] = {
    "yahoo": (
        Archive("listing", "https://finance.yahoo.com/topic/earnings/"),
        Archive("listing", "https://finance.yahoo.com/topic/latest-news/"),
        Archive("listing", "https://finance.yahoo.com/topic/economic-news/"),
        Archive("listing", "https://finance.yahoo.com/topic/tech/"),
    ),
    "cnbc": (
        Archive("sitemap", "https://www.cnbc.com/sitemap_news.xml"),
        Archive("sitemap", "https://www.cnbc.com/sitemapAll.xml", select="newest"),
    ),
    "fool": (
        Archive("sitemap", "https://www.fool.com/news-sitemap.xml"),
        Archive("monthly", "https://www.fool.com/sitemap/{yyyy}/{mm}"),
    ),
    "prnewswire": (
        Archive("sitemap", "https://www.prnewswire.com/sitemap-news.xml"),
        Archive(
            "paged",
            "https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/financial-services-latest-news/earnings-list/"
            "?page={page}&pagesize=100",
            pages=10,
        ),
        Archive(
            "paged",
            "https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/news-releases-list/?page={page}&pagesize=100",
            pages=5,
        ),
        Archive(
            "search",
            "https://www.prnewswire.com/search/news/?keyword={query}&page={page}&pagesize=100",
            pages=3,
        ),
    ),
    "globenewswire": (
        Archive("sitemap", "https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/GoogleSitemap"),
        Archive("monthly", "https://sitemaps.globenewswire.com/news/en/{yyyy}-{mm}.xml"),
    ),
    "sec": (Archive("edgar-fts", EDGAR_FTS, pages=5),),
    "cnn": (Archive("monthly", "https://edition.cnn.com/sitemap/article/business/{yyyy}/{mm}.xml"),),
    "fortune": (
        Archive("sitemap", "https://fortune.com/feed/googlenews/articles.xml"),
        Archive("monthly", "https://fortune.com/articles-{yyyy}-{mm}.xml"),
        Archive("paged", "https://fortune.com/section/finance/page/{page}/", pages=10),
    ),
    "guardian": (Archive("daily", "https://www.theguardian.com/business/{yyyy}/{mon}/{dd}/all"),),
    "bbc": (Archive("paged", "https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business?page={page}", pages=40),),
}
# The feed links releases under org id 0, the sitemaps under the issuer's id; both resolve.
PATTERN_OVERRIDES: dict[str, str] = {"globenewswire": GNW_PATTERN}


def load_sources() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    text = resources.files("veritrade").joinpath("data/sources.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    sources: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = tomllib.loads(text)["sources"]
    return sources


def primary_sources(sources: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    registry = sources if sources is not None else load_sources()
    keys = [k for k, cfg in registry.items() if cfg.get("status") == "primary"]
    return sorted(keys, key=lambda k: int(registry[k].get("rank", 99)))


def source_archives(key: str, cfg: Mapping[str, Any], listing_urls: Sequence[str] = ()) -> list[Archive]:
    archives = [Archive("feed", url) for url in cfg.get("feeds", [])]
    archives += [Archive("listing", url) for url in cfg.get("sections", [])]
    archives += ARCHIVES.get(key, ())
    archives += [Archive("listing", url) for url in listing_urls]
    return archives


def on_source_domain(url: str, cfg: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    host = (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").lower()
    return any(host == d or host.endswith("." + d) for d in cfg.get("domains", []))


def expand(
    archive: Archive, since: date, until: date, queries: Sequence[str]
) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """Concrete (url, query) requests for one archive over the window."""
    template = archive.url
    if archive.kind == "monthly":
        return [(template.format(yyyy=y, mm=f"{m:02d}"), None) for y, m in months_between(since, until)]
    if archive.kind == "daily":
        return [
            (
                template.format(
                    yyyy=d.year, mm=f"{d.month:02d}", mon=MONTH_ABBR[d.month - 1], dd=f"{d.day:02d}"
                ),
                None,
            )
            for d in reversed(days_between(since, until))
        ]
    if archive.kind == "paged":
        return [(template.format(page=p), None) for p in range(1, archive.pages + 1)]
    if archive.kind == "search":
        return [
            (template.format(query=quote_plus(q), page=p), q)
            for q in queries
            for p in range(1, archive.pages + 1)
        ]
    return [(template, None)]


def edgar_fts_url(query: str | None, since: date, until: date, offset: int) -> str:
    params = {"forms": "8-K", "dateRange": "custom", "startdt": since.isoformat(), "enddt": until.isoformat()}
    if query:
        # Multi-word queries are phrases ("net loss"), which is what directional keywords need.
        params["q"] = f'"{query}"' if " " in query and not query.startswith('"') else query
    if offset:
        params["from"] = str(offset)
    return f"{EDGAR_FTS}?{urlencode(params)}"


_STEM_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


def query_matches(query: str, haystack: str) -> bool:
    """Every query word, loosely stemmed, starts some word of the title or URL slug."""
    words = _STEM_TOKEN.findall(haystack.lower())
    for token in _STEM_TOKEN.findall(query.lower()):
        stem = token if len(token) <= 4 else token[: max(4, len(token) - 2)]
        if not any(word.startswith(stem) for word in words):
            return False
    return True


def slug_text(url: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(_STEM_TOKEN.findall(urlsplit(url).path.lower()))

    def pattern(self, key: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
        return re.compile(PATTERN_OVERRIDES.get(key) or self._sources[key]["article_pattern"])

    def keep(self, key: str, url: str) -> bool:
        cfg = self._sources[key]
        exclude = cfg.get("exclude_pattern")
        if not self.pattern(key).match(url) or ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE.search(url):
            return False
        return not (exclude and re.search(exclude, url))

    async def run(
        self,
        key: str,
        *,
        since: date,
        until: date,
        queries: Sequence[str] = (),
        listing_urls: Sequence[str] = (),
        pages: int | None = None,
    ) -> DiscoverRun:
        cfg = self._sources[key]
        run = DiscoverRun(key)
        for archive in source_archives(key, cfg, listing_urls):
            if archive.kind == "search" and not queries:
                continue
            if pages is not None and archive.kind in PAGED_KINDS:
                archive = replace(archive, pages=pages)
            stats = ArchiveStats(archive.kind, archive.url)
            run.archives.append(stats)
            if archive.kind == "edgar-fts":
                await self._edgar_fts(run, stats, archive, since, until, queries)
            elif archive.kind == "feed" and cfg.get("discovery") == "edgar-8k-ex99":
                await self._edgar_feed(run, stats, archive.url)
            else:
                for url, query in expand(archive, since, until, queries):
                    await self._collect(run, stats, archive, url, query)
        return run

    async def _fetch(self, stats: ArchiveStats, url: str) -> Response | None:
        stats.requests += 1
        got = await self._client.get(url)
        if got.error or got.status != 200:
            stats.failed(got.error or f"http_{got.status}")
            return None
        stats.ok += 1
        return got

    async def _collect(
        self, run: DiscoverRun, stats: ArchiveStats, archive: Archive, url: str, query: str | None
    ) -> None:
        got = await self._fetch(stats, url)
        if got is None:
            return
        kind, links = parse_any(got.body, got.final_url)
        if kind == "sitemapindex":
            children = [link.url for link in links]
            if archive.select == "newest":
                children = sorted(children, key=_trailing_number)[-1:]
            for child in children:
                await self._collect(run, stats, Archive("sitemap", child), child, query)
            return
        self._add(run, stats, links, archive.kind, url, query)

    def _add(
        self,
        run: DiscoverRun,
        stats: ArchiveStats,
        links: Sequence[Link],
        kind: str,
        url: str,
        query: str | None,
        *,
        count: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        if count:
            stats.links += len(links)
        for link in links:
            canonical = normalize(link.url)
            if self.keep(run.source, canonical):
                stats.matched += 1
                run.found.append(
                    Found(Link(canonical, link.title, link.published, link.extra), kind, url, query)
                )

    async def _edgar_fts(
        self,
        run: DiscoverRun,
        stats: ArchiveStats,
        archive: Archive,
        since: date,
        until: date,
        queries: Sequence[str],
    ) -> None:
        exhibits: dict[str, Link] = {}
        main_docs: dict[str, tuple[EdgarHit, str | None]] = {}
        searches: list[str | None] = [*queries] or [None]
        for query in searches:
            for page in range(archive.pages):
                url = edgar_fts_url(query, since, until, page * EDGAR_PAGE)
                got = await self._fetch(stats, url)
                if got is None:
                    break
                try:
                    hits = edgar_fts_hits(json.loads(got.body))
                except ValueError:
                    stats.failed("bad_json")
                    break
                stats.links += len(hits)
                for hit in hits:
                    if hit.file_type.upper().startswith("EX-99.1"):
                        if hit.adsh not in exhibits:
                            exhibits[hit.adsh] = hit.link()
                            self._add(run, stats, [exhibits[hit.adsh]], "edgar-fts", url, query, count=False)
                    elif hit.file_type.upper() == "8-K":
                        main_docs.setdefault(hit.adsh, (hit, query))
                if len(hits) < EDGAR_PAGE:
                    break
        # A query can match the 8-K cover text rather than the exhibit; resolve those filings via the index.
        pending = [found for adsh, found in main_docs.items() if adsh not in exhibits][:MAX_EDGAR_RESOLVE]
        for hit, hit_query in pending:
            got = await self._fetch(stats, hit.index_url)
            if got is not None and (
                found := edgar_exhibit(got.body.decode("utf-8", "replace"), got.final_url)
            ):
                link = hit.link(found[0])
                self._add(run, stats, [link], "edgar-fts", hit.index_url, hit_query, count=False)

    async def _edgar_feed(self, run: DiscoverRun, stats: ArchiveStats, feed_url: str) -> None:
        got = await self._fetch(stats, feed_url)
        if got is None:
            return
        entries = feed_items(got.body)
        stats.links += len(entries)
        for entry in entries[:MAX_EDGAR_RESOLVE]:
            index = await self._fetch(stats, normalize(entry.url))
            if index is not None and (
                found := edgar_exhibit(index.body.decode("utf-8", "replace"), index.final_url)
            ):
                link = Link(found[0], entry.title, entry.published, {"form": "8-K", "file_type": "EX-99.1"})
                self._add(run, stats, [link], "feed", feed_url, None, count=False)


def _trailing_number(url: str) -> int:
    m = re.search(r"(\d+)\D*$", url)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else -1


def utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")

def test_expand_templates_over_the_window() -> None:

        "https://x/2026-10.xml",

        "https://x/2026/oct/02/all",

    search = expand(Archive("search", "https://x/?q={query}&p={page}", pages=1), since, until, ["net loss"])

    async def _raw_get(self, url: str) -> Response:

async def test_archive_client_retries_a_timeout_once(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    attempts: list[str] = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        attempts.append(request.url.path)
        if request.url.path == "/slow" and attempts.count("/slow") == 1:
            raise httpx.ReadTimeout("slow", request=request)
        return httpx.Response(200, text="ok" if request.url.path == "/slow" else "")

    http = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    client = ArchiveClient(tmp_path / "cache", polite=Politeness(0.0, 0.0), client=http)
    got = await client.get("https://example.com/slow")
    assert (got.status, got.body) == (200, b"ok")
    assert attempts == ["/robots.txt", "/slow", "/slow"]
    await client.aclose()
EOF

```python
"""Structural check of gold packets; prints numbers and booleans only, never packet text."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections import Counter

from veritrade.errors import VtError
from veritrade.extract import registry
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, iter_fetched

ROW = re.compile(r"^L(\d+) (.*)$")
FOLD = re.compile(r"^L(\d+)-L(\d+) \[(\d+) lines hidden: (.+)\]$")
HEADER_KEYS = ("id", "source", "url", "published_at", "lines", "every line, nothing folded", "follow",
               "write your output to")


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for record in iter_fetched(paths):
        packet = paths.packet("gold", record.id)
        if not packet.exists():
            continue
        text = packet.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        lines = json.loads(paths.lines(record.id).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["lines"]
        header_ok = all(any(t.startswith(f"- {k}:") for t in text) for k in HEADER_KEYS)
        body = text[text.index("## Lines") + 2 :]
        expected, problems, folds, visible = 1, 0, Counter[str](), []
        for row in body:
            if m := FOLD.match(row):
                start, end, size = int(m[1]), int(m[2]), int(m[3])
                problems += start != expected or size != end - start + 1
                folds[m[4].split(" (")[0]] += size
                expected = end + 1
            elif m := ROW.match(row):
                n = int(m[1])
                problems += n != expected or m[2] != lines[n - 1]
                visible.append(n)
                expected = n + 1
            else:
                problems += 1
        complete = expected == len(lines) + 1
        full = paths.full_packet(record.id).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        full_rows = sum(1 for t in full if ROW.match(t))
        html = paths.html(record.id).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            article = registry.extract(html, record.final_url or record.url)
            paragraphs = list(article.paragraphs)
            shown_text = {lines[n - 1] for n in visible}
            found = sum(any(p[:60] in s for s in shown_text) for p in paragraphs)
            title_shown = any(article.title and article.title.casefold() in s.casefold() for s in shown_text)
        except VtError:
            paragraphs, found, title_shown = [], 0, False
        print(
            f"{record.source:13} {record.id} lines={len(lines)} visible={len(visible)} "
            f"folded={dict(folds)} header_ok={header_ok} contiguous={problems == 0 and complete} "
            f"full_rows={full_rows == len(lines)} body_paragraphs_visible={found}/{len(paragraphs)} "
            f"title_visible={title_shown}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

"""Where do non-visible body paragraphs and headlines land in the packet? Numbers only, never text."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from veritrade.extract import registry
from veritrade.extract.dom import parse
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, iter_fetched
from veritrade_evals.articles_packets import compact_rows, is_tiny, locate, page_lines


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for record in iter_fetched(paths):
        if record.source not in ("cnn", "cnbc", "fool", "bbc"):
            continue
        html = paths.html(record.id).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        url = record.final_url or record.url
        lines = json.loads(paths.lines(record.id).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["lines"]
        assert lines == page_lines(html, url)
        article = registry.extract(html, url)
        span = locate(lines, article.title, article.paragraphs)
        rows = compact_rows(lines, span)
        hidden = {n: row.note for row in rows if row.text is None for n in range(row.start, row.end + 1)}
        h1 = [i + 1 for i, b in enumerate(parse(html, "selectolax").iter_blocks()) if b.tag == "h1"]
        print(f"{record.source} {record.id} span={span} h1_lines={h1[:5]} lines={len(lines)}")
        for k, p in enumerate(article.paragraphs):
            hits = [i + 1 for i, line in enumerate(lines) if p[:60] in line]
            if not hits or all(n in hidden for n in hits):
                where = [(n, hidden.get(n, "visible"), len(lines[n - 1].split()), is_tiny(lines[n - 1])) for n in hits]
                print(f"   paragraph {k} words={len(p.split())} hits={where}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The real bug is Fool's h1 sitting after the body in DOM order, so I'll fix this by tracking each block's tag, never folding h1 lines, anchoring the title to the nearest h1 above the body when text doesn't match, and listing h1 line numbers in the packet header.

```python
"""Agent packets: numbered page lines for gold selection, capped gold bodies for labelling and adjudication.

Gold packets list every visible text block of the page (strip-tags) as an addressable line; menus and the
page chrome far from the extracted article are folded into marker lines that keep their numbers.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from veritrade.errors import VtError
from veritrade.extract import registry, third_party
from veritrade.extract.dom import normalize, split_sentences
from veritrade_evals.articles import (
    LABEL_PACKET_WORDS,
    PROMPTS,
    ArticlePaths,
    FetchRecord,
    rel,
    write_json,
)
from veritrade_evals.articles_validate import (
    LabelCheck,
    adjudicate_requested,
    gold_body,
    gold_check,
    label_check,
)

TINY_WORDS = 3
TINY_CHARS = 32
TINY_RUN = 3
MARGIN_LINES = 12
TITLE_REACH = 200
LONG_LINE_WORDS = 250
CHUNK_WORDS = 120
ANCHOR_CHARS = 60
MIN_PARTIAL_CHARS = 40


def split_long(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Very long blocks (unparagraphed filings) become sentence chunks so ranges stay fine-grained."""
    if len(text.split()) <= LONG_LINE_WORDS:
        return [text]
    chunks: list[list[str]] = [[]]
    count = 0
    for sentence in split_sentences(text):
        size = len(sentence.split())
        if chunks[-1] and count + size > CHUNK_WORDS:
            chunks.append([])
            count = 0
        chunks[-1].append(sentence)
        count += size
    out: list[str] = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        words = " ".join(chunk).split()
        # A run-on "sentence" (a flattened table) is cut by words.
        out += [" ".join(words[i : i + LONG_LINE_WORDS]) for i in range(0, len(words), LONG_LINE_WORDS)]
    return out


def page_lines(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    return [line for block in third_party.extract("strip-tags", html, url) for line in split_long(block)]


def is_tiny(line: str) -> bool:
    return len(line.split()) <= TINY_WORDS and len(line) <= TINY_CHARS


def _key(text: str) -> str:
    return normalize(text).casefold()


def _matches(line: str, paragraph: str, anchor: str) -> bool:
    return anchor in line or (len(line) >= MIN_PARTIAL_CHARS and line in paragraph)


def locate(lines: Sequence[str], title: str | None, paragraphs: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """0-based (first, last) lines of the extracted article, widened up to its headline when it is near."""
    if not paragraphs:
        return None
    keys = [_key(line) for line in lines]
    first = next(
        (
            i
            for p in paragraphs[:3]
            for i, k in enumerate(keys)
            if _matches(k, _key(p), _key(p)[:ANCHOR_CHARS])
        ),
        None,
    )
    if first is None:
        return None
    last = next(
        (
            i
            for p in reversed(paragraphs[-3:])
            for i in range(len(keys) - 1, first - 1, -1)
            if _matches(keys[i], _key(p), _key(p)[-ANCHOR_CHARS:])
        ),
        None,
    )
    if last is None:
        return None
    start = first
    if title and (wanted := _key(title)):
        for i in range(first - 1, max(-1, first - TITLE_REACH), -1):
            if keys[i] == wanted or (len(keys[i]) >= 20 and (wanted in keys[i] or keys[i] in wanted)):
                start = i
                break
    return start, last


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Row:
    """One packet row: a visible line (text set) or a folded run of lines (text None)."""

    start: int
    end: int
    text: str | None = None
    note: str = ""


def compact_rows(lines: Sequence[str], span: tuple[int, int] | None) -> list[Row]:
    if not lines:
        return []
    last = len(lines) - 1
    lo, hi = (max(0, span[0] - MARGIN_LINES), min(last, span[1] + MARGIN_LINES)) if span else (0, last)
    rows: list[Row] = []
    if lo > 0:
        rows.append(Row(1, lo, note="before the located article"))
    i = lo
    while i <= hi:
        j = i
        while j + 1 <= hi and is_tiny(lines[i]) and is_tiny(lines[j + 1]):
            j += 1
        if j - i + 1 >= TINY_RUN:
            rows.append(Row(i + 1, j + 1, note="short lines (menus, buttons, tickers)"))
            i = j + 1
            continue
        rows.append(Row(i + 1, i + 1, lines[i]))
        i += 1
    if hi < last:
        rows.append(Row(hi + 2, last + 1, note="after the located article"))
    return rows


def _num(n: int, width: int) -> str:
    return f"L{n:0{width}d}"


def render_rows(rows: Sequence[Row], total: int) -> list[str]:
    width = max(4, len(str(total)))
    out = []
    for row in rows:
        if row.text is not None:
            out.append(f"{_num(row.start, width)} {row.text}")
        else:
            size = row.end - row.start + 1
            out.append(f"{_num(row.start, width)}-{_num(row.end, width)} [{size} lines hidden: {row.note}]")
    return out


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class GoldPacket:
    id: str
    lines: tuple[str, ...]
    rows: tuple[Row, ...]
    text: str
    full_text: str
    body_words: int
    located: bool

    @property
    def visible_words(self) -> int:
        return sum(len(row.text.split()) for row in self.rows if row.text is not None)


def build_gold_packet(record: FetchRecord, html: str, paths: ArticlePaths) -> GoldPacket:
    url = record.final_url or record.url
    lines = page_lines(html, url)
    try:
        article = registry.extract(html, url, parser="selectolax", extractor="cascade")
    except VtError:
        article = None
    span = locate(lines, article.title, article.paragraphs) if article else None
    rows = compact_rows(lines, span)
    full = paths.full_packet(record.id)
    header = [
        f"# Gold packet {record.id}",
        "",
        f"- id: {record.id}",
        f"- source: {record.source}",
        f"- url: {record.url}",
        f"- published_at: {record.published_date or 'unknown'}",
        f"- lines: {len(lines)}; folded runs keep their numbers and every line stays addressable",
        f"- every line, nothing folded: {rel(full)}",
        f"- follow: {rel(PROMPTS['gold'])}",
        f"- write your output to: {rel(paths.out('gold', record.id))}",
        "",
        "## Lines",
        "",
    ]
    width = max(4, len(str(len(lines))))
    full_lines = [f"{_num(n, width)} {line}" for n, line in enumerate(lines, start=1)]
    full_header = [
        f"# Full gold packet {record.id} (every line)",
        "",
        f"- compact packet: {rel(paths.packet('gold', record.id))}",
        "",
    ]
    return GoldPacket(
        id=record.id,
        lines=tuple(lines),
        rows=tuple(rows),
        text="\n".join(header + render_rows(rows, len(lines))) + "\n",
        full_text="\n".join(full_header + full_lines) + "\n",
        body_words=article.word_count if article else 0,
        located=span is not None,
    )


def write_gold_packet(packet: GoldPacket, paths: ArticlePaths) -> Path:
    path = paths.packet("gold", packet.id)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(packet.text, encoding="utf-8")
    paths.full_packet(packet.id).write_text(packet.full_text, encoding="utf-8")
    write_json(paths.lines(packet.id), {"id": packet.id, "lines": list(packet.lines)})
    return path


# --- label and adjudication packets -----------------------------------------------------------------------

```

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, FetchRecord
from veritrade_evals.articles_packets import (
    LONG_LINE_WORDS,
    Row,
    build_gold_packet,
    cap_paragraphs,
    compact_rows,
    is_tiny,
    locate,
    render_label,
    render_rows,
    split_long,
    write_gold_packet,
)

PARAGRAPHS = [
    f"Paragraph {n} of the synthetic story explains how Quillon Freight moved {n * 7} containers through "
    f"the harbour while rivals waited, according to figures the company shared with analysts this week."
    for n in range(1, 9)
]
NAV = "".join(f'<li><a href="/s{n}">Section {n}</a></li>' for n in range(30))
PROMOS = "".join(f"<p>Unrelated promo block number {n} with a few more words to read.</p>" for n in range(40))
FOOTER = "".join(f'<li><a href="/f{n}">Footer link {n}</a></li>' for n in range(30))
HTML = f"""<html><head><title>Quillon Freight story</title></head><body>
<nav><ul>{NAV}</ul></nav>
<main><article><h1>Quillon Freight clears the backlog</h1>
<div class="byline">By A. Writer</div>
{"".join(f"<p>{p}</p>" for p in PARAGRAPHS)}
</article></main>
<aside>{PROMOS}</aside>
<footer><ul>{FOOTER}</ul></footer>
</body></html>"""


def record() -> FetchRecord:
    return FetchRecord(
        id="art-0123456789ab",
        source="cnbc",
        url="https://news.example.com/2026/10/16/quillon.html",
        fetched_at="2026-10-18T10:00:00+00:00",
        status=200,
        html_sha256="0" * 64,
        published_date="2026-10-16",
    )


def covered(rows: list[Row]) -> list[int]:
    return [n for row in rows for n in range(row.start, row.end + 1)]


def test_split_long_keeps_text_and_caps_line_length() -> None:
    assert split_long("short line") == ["short line"]
    sentence = " ".join(["word"] * 29) + "."
    text = " ".join([sentence] * 40)
    parts = split_long(text)
    assert len(parts) > 1
    assert " ".join(parts) == text
    assert all(len(p.split()) <= LONG_LINE_WORDS for p in parts)
    run_on = " ".join(["cell"] * (LONG_LINE_WORDS * 2 + 5))
    assert [len(p.split()) for p in split_long(run_on)] == [LONG_LINE_WORDS, LONG_LINE_WORDS, 5]


def test_is_tiny() -> None:
    assert is_tiny("Sign in")
    assert is_tiny("Markets")
    assert not is_tiny("Shares fell 4% after the results")
    assert not is_tiny("Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious-and-more")


def test_compact_rows_fold_tiny_runs_and_keep_every_number() -> None:
    lines = [
        "Home",
        "Markets",
        "Tech",
        "A long headline about the company today",
        "Body one is long enough here",
        "Share",
        "Body two",
    ]
    rows = compact_rows(lines, None)
    assert covered(rows) == list(range(1, len(lines) + 1))
    assert rows[0] == Row(1, 3, note="short lines (menus, buttons, tickers)")
    # Runs shorter than three stay visible.
    assert Row(6, 6, "Share") in rows
    rendered = render_rows(rows, len(lines))
    assert rendered[0].startswith("L0001-L0003 [3 lines hidden")
    assert rendered[1].startswith("L0004 A long headline")


def test_compact_rows_fold_far_regions_around_the_span() -> None:
    lines = [f"line number {n} has several words in it" for n in range(100)]
    rows = compact_rows(lines, (40, 50))
    assert covered(rows) == list(range(1, 101))
    assert rows[0] == Row(1, 28, note="before the located article")
    assert rows[-1] == Row(64, 100, note="after the located article")
    assert rows[1].start == 29


def test_locate_finds_headline_first_and_last_paragraph() -> None:
    lines = ["Menu", "The headline", "By someone", *PARAGRAPHS, "Related stories"]
    assert locate(lines, "The headline", PARAGRAPHS) == (1, 2 + len(PARAGRAPHS))
    assert locate(lines, None, PARAGRAPHS) == (3, 2 + len(PARAGRAPHS))
    assert locate(lines, "x", ["not on the page at all, anywhere, in any form whatsoever"]) is None
    assert locate(lines, "x", []) is None


def test_gold_packet_is_compact_addressable_and_names_its_files(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths(private=tmp_path / "private", committed=tmp_path / "committed")
    packet = build_gold_packet(record(), HTML, paths)
    assert packet.located
    assert packet.body_words == sum(len(p.split()) for p in PARAGRAPHS)
    # Only the margin lines around the located article stay visible besides the body itself.
    assert packet.visible_words < 2 * packet.body_words
    assert covered(list(packet.rows)) == list(range(1, len(packet.lines) + 1))
    assert "Quillon Freight clears the backlog" in packet.text
    assert all(p in packet.text for p in PARAGRAPHS)
    assert "Footer link 29" not in packet.text
    assert "Footer link 29" in packet.full_text
    assert f"out/gold/{record().id}.json" in packet.text
    assert "opus_prompts/20-gold.md" in packet.text
    write_gold_packet(packet, paths)
    assert paths.packet("gold", record().id).exists()
    assert paths.full_packet(record().id).exists()
    assert paths.lines(record().id).exists()


def test_gold_packet_without_an_extractable_article_shows_every_line(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths(private=tmp_path / "private", committed=tmp_path / "committed")
    packet = build_gold_packet(record(), "<html><body><p>Too short.</p></body></html>", paths)
    assert not packet.located
    assert packet.rows == (Row(1, 1, "Too short."),)


def test_cap_paragraphs_stops_at_a_boundary() -> None:
    paras = ["a " * 500, "b " * 500, "c " * 500]
    kept, omitted = cap_paragraphs([p.strip() for p in paras], 1200)

> 
> ## Files created/changed
> - **New in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/`:** `discovery.py`, `articles.py`, `articles_candidates.py`, `articles_fetch.py`, `articles_packets.py`, `articles_validate.py`, `articles_finalize.py`, `articles_cli.py`.

> - **Tests:** `evals/tests/unit/test_discovery.py`, `test_articles_validate.py`, `test_articles_packets.py`, `test_articles_pipeline.py` (synthetic data only, no network).
> - **Prompts:** `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md`, `10-discover.md`, `20-gold.md`, `30-label.md`, `40-adjudicate.md`.
> 
> ## What works
> - `articles discover --source all` finished in 2m46s, then I re-ran Yahoo and SEC with new archives (4m28s).
> - **Politeness:** every archive request is checked against robots.txt, sequential per domain with a 1 s gap (EDGAR 0.2 s), and cached for 6 h so repeated query runs don't hit publishers again.
> - **Search:** `--query "net loss" --query "raises guidance"` added 78 SEC exhibits, and PR Newswire search returned 100 matches.
> - **Domain guard:** a `--listing-url` off the source's domain is rejected.
> - **Fetch:** `articles fetch --top 1` per source returned 10 of 10 OK through the serving `HttpFetcher`.
> 
> ## Discovery per source (candidates total / dated in window / undated)
> | Source | Counts | Archive types that worked |
> |---|---|---|
> | yahoo | 6232 / 6080 / 152 | daily HTML archive `/sitemap/YYYY_MM_DD/` + cursor pages, topic pages |
> | cnbc | 3274 / 3274 / 0 | RSS, news sitemap, newest `CNBCsitemapAll*.xml` |
> | fool | 6857 / 6857 / 0 | RSS, news sitemap, monthly sitemaps |
> | prnewswire | 1323 / 1257 / 66 | RSS, news sitemap, earnings and all-releases listings, keyword search |
> | globenewswire | 16747 / 16747 / 0 | RSS, Google news sitemap, monthly sitemaps |

> | cnn | 377 / 377 / 0 | section page, monthly business sitemaps |
> | fortune | 2170 / 2170 / 0 | RSS, Google news sitemap, monthly sitemaps, finance section pages |

> The SEC page has only 18 lines, and the extractor under-reads its body (109 words), which inflates its ratio. On all 10 packets a numbers-only check confirmed:
> - every line number is present and in order;
> - the full packet contains every line;
> - every `h1` line is visible;
> - the extracted body sits inside the visible region.
> 
> ## Deviations and why
> - **GlobeNewswire:** its keyword search is disallowed by robots.txt, so I use monthly sitemaps instead. Their URLs carry the issuer's id rather than `/0/`, so discovery uses a relaxed URL pattern for this source.
> - **CNBC:** the HTML site-map is rendered in the browser, so I use the newest XML sitemap instead.
> - **EDGAR phrase search:** spaces must be sent as `%20`; a `+` caused HTTP 500.
> - **Added commands and flags:**
>   - `articles candidates` writes a private TSV view for agents to read.
>   - `ingest --agreement` shows the running agreement to the main loop only, so labellers stay independent.
>   - Archive requests retry once after a timeout.
> - **Headlines in packets:** `h1` lines are never folded. Fool puts its `h1` after the body in the page source, which hid the headline before this fix.
> - **`reject_reason` is a fixed list of reasons:** this keeps it countable and safe to print.
> - **Committed `score`:** the adjudicator's score when there was adjudication, otherwise the mean of the two labellers' scores (so it can be x.5).
> - **Rebalancing:** each source/class count stays between 2 and 4 and each class totals 30. A source can then hold 8 to 10 articles; I chose fewer deviations from 3 over equal source totals. The algorithm text is written into `stats.json`.
> 
> ## Open issues
> - **Bearish will be hardest on the wires:** PR Newswire and GlobeNewswire are flooded with law-firm "class action" ads (the prompts exclude them), and SEC needs directional queries.
> - **Fool and Yahoo:** Fool has a lot of evergreen "should you buy" content, and Yahoo republishes partner copy from Fool, so the same story can turn up from two sources.
> - **BBC and Guardian:** both lean towards macro stories (allowed as long as there is one primary entity). BBC dates are only known after fetch.
> - **SEC exhibits:** some are financial-statement tables or under 120 words.
> - **PR Newswire:** occasionally slow, with a few timeouts in the news sitemap.
> 
> ## Requests
> - Whoever owns `backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml`: widen the GlobeNewswire `article_pattern` to accept any numeric id in place of `/0/` (`.../\d+/\d+/en/...`), so the registry matches the sitemap URLs.
