```
"""The serving fetcher: one HTTP/2 client, manual SSRF-checked redirects, capped bodies, typed failures."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import codecs
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Mapping
from typing import NoReturn
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit

import httpcore
import httpx

from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.errors import (
    ConsentRequired,
    InvalidUrl,
    TooLarge,
    UnsupportedContent,
    UpstreamHttp,
    UpstreamTimeout,
)
from veritrade.fetch import detect
from veritrade.fetch.consent import REDIRECT_STATUSES, is_consent_url, reject_all
from veritrade.fetch.headers import browser_headers, is_sec_host
from veritrade.fetch.ssrf import GuardedBackend, Resolver, check_target, system_resolver
from veritrade.fetch.types import FetchResult

LIMITS = httpx.Limits(max_connections=64, max_keepalive_connections=32, keepalive_expiry=60.0)
# EDGAR's fair-access policy allows 10 requests per second per client; every sec.gov host shares it.
RATE_LIMITS: Mapping[str, float] = {"sec.gov": 10.0}
HTML_TYPES = frozenset({"text/html", "application/xhtml+xml"})
SEC_DOCUMENT_SUFFIXES = (".htm", ".html", ".txt")
# Error pages are only read for detect.classify, which scans the first 64 KB.
ERROR_BODY_BYTES = 65_536
SNIFF_BYTES = 4096

_META_CHARSET = re.compile(rb"""<meta[^>]{0,512}?charset\s*=\s*["']?\s*([a-z0-9_.:-]+)""", re.IGNORECASE)
# WHATWG decodes these labels as windows-1252; the 0x80-0x9F smart quotes in old filings depend on it.
_WINDOWS_1252_ALIASES = frozenset({"iso8859-1", "ascii"})


class HostRateLimiter:
    """Spaces request starts evenly per rate-limited host group; other hosts pass straight through."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        rates: Mapping[str, float] = RATE_LIMITS,
        *,
        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
        sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep,
    ) -> None:
        self._intervals = {suffix: 1.0 / rate for suffix, rate in rates.items()}
        self._next: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._clock = clock
        self._sleep = sleep

    def _group(self, host: str) -> str | None:
        host = host.lower().rstrip(".")
        for suffix in self._intervals:
            if host == suffix or host.endswith("." + suffix):
                return suffix
        return None

    async def acquire(self, url: str) -> None:
        group = self._group(urlsplit(url).hostname or "")
        if group is None:
            return
        # Slots are reserved before sleeping, so concurrent callers queue without a lock.
        now = self._clock()
        slot = max(now, self._next.get(group, now))
        self._next[group] = slot + self._intervals[group]
        if slot > now:
            await self._sleep(slot - now)


class _GuardedTransport(httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport):
    """httpx takes no network backend argument, so the pool is rebuilt around the SSRF-guarded one."""

    def __init__(self, backend: httpcore.AsyncNetworkBackend) -> None:
        super().__init__(http2=True, limits=LIMITS)
        self._pool = httpcore.AsyncConnectionPool(
            ssl_context=httpx.create_ssl_context(),
            max_connections=LIMITS.max_connections,
            max_keepalive_connections=LIMITS.max_keepalive_connections,
            keepalive_expiry=LIMITS.keepalive_expiry,
            http1=True,
            http2=True,
            network_backend=backend,
        )


class HttpFetcher:
    """Fetcher protocol over one shared client whose cookie jar keeps Yahoo's reject-all answer."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Settings,
        *,
        resolver: Resolver = system_resolver,
        limiter: HostRateLimiter | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._settings = settings
        self._resolver = resolver
        self._allow_hosts = settings.ssrf_allow_hosts
        self._limiter = limiter or HostRateLimiter()
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            transport=_GuardedTransport(GuardedBackend(resolver=resolver, allow_hosts=self._allow_hosts)),
            follow_redirects=False,
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(settings.fetch_deadline_s, connect=settings.fetch_connect_timeout_s),
            # User-supplied URLs must never pick up .netrc credentials.
            trust_env=False,
        )

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self._client.aclose()

    async def get(self, url: str) -> FetchResult:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        host = _host(url)
        deadline = self._settings.fetch_deadline_s
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(deadline):
                return await self._fetch(url, started)
        except (TimeoutError, httpx.TimeoutException) as exc:
            raise UpstreamTimeout(
                f"{host} did not deliver the page within {deadline:g} s",
                hint="The publisher is slow or unreachable; retry, or try the story from another source.",
            ) from exc
        except httpx.InvalidURL as exc:
            raise InvalidUrl(f"malformed URL: {exc}") from exc
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise UpstreamHttp(
                f"request to {host} failed: {type(exc).__name__}",
                hint="The publisher could not be reached; retry shortly.",
            ) from exc

    async def _check(self, url: str) -> None:
        await check_target(url, resolver=self._resolver, allow_hosts=self._allow_hosts)

    async def _fetch(self, url: str, started: float) -> FetchResult:
        current, redirects = url, 0
        consent_ms: float | None = None
        while True:
            await self._check(current)
            await self._limiter.acquire(current)
            async with self._client.stream("GET", current, headers=browser_headers(current)) as response:
                location = response.headers.get("location")
                if response.status_code not in REDIRECT_STATUSES or not location:
                    html, content_type = await self._read(response, current)
                    fetch_ms = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000 - (consent_ms or 0.0)
                    return FetchResult(
                        requested_url=url,
                        final_url=current,
                        status=response.status_code,
                        html=html,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        fetch_ms=fetch_ms,
                        consent_ms=consent_ms,
                        redirects=redirects,
                    )
                status, headers = response.status_code, response.headers
            target = urljoin(current, location)
            if is_consent_url(target):
                if consent_ms is not None:
                    _consent_wall(status, headers, target)
                # Reject-all once, then retry the hop that hit the wall with the consent cookie set.
                outcome = await reject_all(self._client, target, guard=self._check)
                consent_ms = outcome.elapsed_ms
                continue
            redirects += 1
            if redirects > (cap := self._settings.fetch_max_redirects):
                raise UpstreamHttp(
                    f"{_host(url)} redirected more than {cap} times",
                    hint="The URL redirects in a loop; open it in a browser and use the final address.",
                    retryable=False,
                    upstream_status=status,
                )
            current = target

    async def _read(self, response: httpx.Response, url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        status = response.status_code
        content_type = response.headers.get("content-type", "")
        host = _host(url)
        if not 200 <= status < 300:
            prefix = await _read_body(response, ERROR_BODY_BYTES, host=host, truncate=True)
            detect.classify(status, response.headers, decode_html(prefix, content_type), url)
            raise UpstreamHttp(
                f"{host} answered HTTP {status}",
                hint=_status_hint(status),
                retryable=status >= 500 or status == 408,
                upstream_status=status,
            )

        media = content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
        if media and not _accepted(media, url):
            raise _unsupported(host, media)
        limit = self._settings.fetch_max_bytes
```

```
class Registry:
    def __init__(
        self,
        specs: Mapping[str, ModelSpec],
        defaults: Mapping[Endpoint, str],
        *,
        restriction: Iterable[str] = (),
        overrides: Mapping[Endpoint, str | None] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        restricted = list(restriction)
        unknown = [name for name in restricted if name not in specs]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"VT_MODELS names models outside models.toml: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        keep = set(restricted) if restricted else set(specs)
        self._all = dict(specs)
        self._specs = {name: spec for name, spec in specs.items() if name in keep}
        self._defaults: dict[Endpoint, str] = {}
        for endpoint in ENDPOINTS:
            override = (overrides or {}).get(endpoint)
            if override:
                if not self._is_allowed(endpoint, override):
                    raise ValueError(f"default model override {override!r} is not allowed for /{endpoint}")
                self._defaults[endpoint] = override
                continue
            configured = defaults.get(endpoint)
            if configured and self._is_allowed(endpoint, configured):
                self._defaults[endpoint] = configured
            elif fallback := self.allowed(endpoint):
                self._defaults[endpoint] = fallback[0].name

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, settings: Settings | None = None, *, toml_text: str | None = None) -> Registry:
        settings = settings or get_settings()
        specs, defaults = parse_models_toml(toml_text if toml_text is not None else read_models_toml())
```

```
"""Opt-in smoke against real publishers: `uv run pytest -m live backend/tests/live/test_fetch_live.py`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tomllib
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

import veritrade
from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.fetch.client import HttpFetcher

pytestmark = pytest.mark.live

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PROBE = REPO / "evals" / "data" / "source_probe.json"
SOURCES = Path(veritrade.__file__).parent / "data" / "sources.toml"


def primary_urls() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """First article per primary source that the probe fetched successfully."""
    sources: dict[str, Any] = tomllib.loads(SOURCES.read_text())["sources"]
    probed: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(PROBE.read_text())["sources"]
    picks = []
    for key, source in sorted(sources.items(), key=lambda item: item[1].get("rank", 99)):
        if source["status"] != "primary":
            continue
        ok = [
            a["fetch"]["url"]
            for a in probed.get(key, {}).get("articles", [])
            if a["fetch"]["outcome"] == "ok"
        ]
        if ok:
            picks.append((key, ok[0]))
    return picks

"""Single quality gate for local runs and CI: lint, types, tests, build and contract drift."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FRONTEND = ROOT / "frontend"


def backend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    backend_tests = "backend/tests" if full else "backend/tests/unit"
    tests = [backend_tests, "evals/tests", "scripts/tests"]
    steps = [
        ("ruff", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "."], ROOT),
        ("ruff-format", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", "."], ROOT),
        ("mypy", ["uv", "run", "mypy"], ROOT),
        ("openapi-drift", ["uv", "run", "python", "scripts/export_openapi.py", "--check"], ROOT),
        ("pytest", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q", *[t for t in tests if (ROOT / t).exists()]], ROOT),
    ]
    # The floor only means something once the API is wired and integration tests exist.
    if full and (ROOT / "backend" / "tests" / "integration").exists():
        steps[-1][1].extend(["--cov", "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered", "--cov-fail-under=75"])
    return steps


def frontend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    steps = [
        ("fe-lint", ["pnpm", "lint"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-format", ["pnpm", "format:check"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-typecheck", ["pnpm", "typecheck"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-test", ["pnpm", "test"], FRONTEND),
    ]
    if full:
        steps.append(("fe-build", ["pnpm", "build"], FRONTEND))
    return steps


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--fast", action="store_true", help="unit tests only, no build (default)")
    mode.add_argument("--full", action="store_true", help="integration tests, coverage floor, build")
    parser.add_argument("--backend", action="store_true", help="only backend + evals")
    parser.add_argument("--frontend", action="store_true", help="only frontend")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    run_be = not args.frontend or args.backend
    run_fe = not args.backend or args.frontend
    steps = (backend_steps(args.full) if run_be else []) + (frontend_steps(args.full) if run_fe else [])

    failed = []
    for name, cmd, cwd in steps:
        print(f"\n== {name}: {' '.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
        if subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd).returncode != 0:
            failed.append(name)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"\nFAILED: {', '.join(failed)}")
    print("\nall checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.13-slim-bookworm
ARG UV_IMAGE=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.10.9

FROM ${UV_IMAGE} AS uv

# Static Next.js export: FastAPI serves it from the same origin, so no Node runs in production.
FROM node:24-slim AS frontend
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /src/frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --store-dir /pnpm/store
COPY frontend/ ./
# The glob lets the build pass before evals publish results; the prebuild step then uses the sample.
COPY evals/results/benchmarks.jso[n] /src/evals/results/
RUN pnpm build

# Third-party dependencies only, so backend edits do not invalidate this layer.
FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS deps
COPY --from=uv /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/
COPY evals/pyproject.toml evals/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-workspace --package veritrade-backend

FROM deps AS wheel
COPY backend/src backend/src
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv build --wheel --package veritrade-backend --out-dir /dist

FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS runtime
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/.venv /app/.venv
# A small layer of its own: only the app wheel changes between backend edits.
RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=from=wheel,source=/dist,target=/dist \
    uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python --no-deps --compile-bytecode --no-cache /dist/*.whl
COPY --from=frontend /src/frontend/out /app/static
ENV PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    VT_ENV=prod \
    VT_STATIC_DIR=/app/static
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=5s --start-period=30s --retries=5 CMD ["veritrade-healthcheck"]
CMD ["uvicorn", "veritrade.api.app:create_app", "--factory", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

###### ✍️  Write `ollama-pull.sh`

`15:10:56`

<details>
<summary><code>~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/docker/ollama-pull.sh</code></summary>

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# One-shot init for the bundled profile: pulls VT_PULL_MODELS (comma-separated) plus the lines of
# VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE into the ollama service's model store, skipping models it already holds.
set -eu

models=$(printf '%s\n' "${VT_PULL_MODELS:-}" | tr ',' '\n')
if [ -n "${VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE:-}" ]; then
  models="${models}
$(sed 's/#.*//' "${VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE}")"
fi

count=0
for model in $(printf '%s\n' "${models}" | tr -d ' \r' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u); do
  # A model already in the store needs no registry round-trip, so cached re-runs work offline.
  if ollama show "${model}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "present ${model}"
  else
    echo "pulling ${model}"
    ollama pull "${model}"
  fi
  count=$((count + 1))
done

if [ "${count}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no models requested: set VT_PULL_MODELS or VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "models ready (${count})"

```
</details>

```yaml
# Default: the app uses native Ollama on the host (Metal on macOS; on Linux start it with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0).
#   docker compose up -d
# Bundled: CPU Ollama in a container, models pulled on first start (Linux, CI, no native install).
#   docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
# Either way the UI and API answer on http://localhost:8000 (VT_PORT changes the host port).
name: veritrade

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/app.Dockerfile
    image: veritrade-app:local
    ports:
      - "${VT_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL:-native-metal}
      # Empty values keep the models.toml allowlist and defaults.
      VT_MODELS: ${VT_MODELS:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE:-}
      # Passed through only when set on the host; otherwise the app's public contact default applies.
      SEC_USER_AGENT:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      ollama-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
        required: false

  ollama:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    volumes:
      # OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR swaps the named volume for a host directory (CI caches it between runs).
      - ${OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR:-ollama-models}:/root/.ollama/models
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: 30m
      OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: "2"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
      OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: q8_0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 30

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      OLLAMA_HOST: http://ollama:11434
      VT_PULL_MODELS: ${VT_PULL_MODELS:-qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0,tev1:0.8b-q8_0}
    volumes:
      - ./docker/ollama-pull.sh:/ollama-pull.sh:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/ollama-pull.sh"]
    restart: "no"

volumes:
  ollama-models:

```
</details>

```
# Serves skeleton pages under their real publisher hostnames, so the extractor picks each source profile.
map $host $vt_source {
    hostnames;
    default "";
    finance.yahoo.com yahoo;
    www.cnbc.com cnbc;
    www.fool.com fool;
    www.prnewswire.com prnewswire;
    www.globenewswire.com globenewswire;
    www.sec.gov sec;
    www.cnn.com cnn;
    fortune.com fortune;
    www.theguardian.com guardian;
    www.bbc.com bbc;
}

server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    access_log /dev/stdout;

    location = /healthz {
        access_log off;
        default_type text/plain;
        return 200 "ok\n";
    }

    location ~ ^/vt-skeleton/(?<slug>[a-z0-9-]+)/?$ {
        if ($vt_source = "") {
            return 404;
        }
        try_files /$vt_source/$slug.html =404;
    }

    location / {
        return 404;
    }
}
```

```yaml
# e2e stack: bundled CPU Ollama with the CI models, a fixture site posing as the publishers, app in test mode.
#   docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait
#   (cd frontend && pnpm exec playwright test)
#   docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml down
# Article URLs look like http://www.cnbc.com/vt-skeleton/article-1 and never leave the compose network.
services:
  app:
    environment:
      VT_ENV: test
      # Lifts the private-address block for exactly the fixture hostnames (refused outside VT_ENV=test).
      VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS: >-
        finance.yahoo.com,www.cnbc.com,www.fool.com,www.prnewswire.com,www.globenewswire.com,
        www.sec.gov,www.cnn.com,fortune.com,www.theguardian.com,www.bbc.com
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://ollama:11434
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: docker-cpu
      # The models listed in deploy/ci-models.txt.
      VT_MODELS: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0,tev1:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
    depends_on:
      fixture-site:
        condition: service_healthy

  ollama:
    profiles: !reset []

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: !reset []
    environment:
      VT_PULL_MODELS: ""
      VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE: /ci-models.txt
    volumes:
      - ./deploy/ci-models.txt:/ci-models.txt:ro

  fixture-site:
    image: nginx:1.29-alpine
    volumes:
      - ./backend/tests/fixtures/skeletons:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro
      - ./docker/e2e/fixture-site.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
    networks:
      default:
        # Docker's embedded DNS answers these names with this container, so no request reaches a publisher.

          - www.globenewswire.com
          - www.sec.gov
          - www.cnn.com
          - fortune.com
          - www.theguardian.com
          - www.bbc.com
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1/healthz"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 15
```

```python
"""Stack smoke: /api/health plus one /signal and one /analyze; prints status, labels and timings only."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import httpx

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PROBE = ROOT / "evals" / "data" / "source_probe.json"


def probe_url(source: str) -> str:
    articles = json.loads(PROBE.read_text())["sources"][source]["articles"]
    return next(a["fetch"]["url"] for a in articles if a["fetch"]["outcome"] == "ok")


def report(name: str, resp: httpx.Response) -> None:
    body: dict[str, Any] = resp.json()
    if resp.status_code != 200:
        err = body.get("error", body)
        print(f"{name}: HTTP {resp.status_code} code={err.get('code')}")
        return
    meta, timings, signal = body["meta"], body["timings"], body["signal"]
    inference = timings.get("inference") or {}
    print(
        f"{name}: HTTP 200 source={meta['source']} model={meta['model']} backend={meta['backend']} "
        f"sentiment={signal['sentiment']} abstained={signal['abstained']} policy={signal['policy']} "
        f"summary_chars={len(body.get('summary', ''))}"
    )
    print(
        f"  timings total={timings['total_ms']:.0f} fetch={timings['fetch_ms']:.0f} "
        f"extract={timings['extract_ms']:.0f} inference_wall={inference.get('wall_ms', 0):.0f} "
        f"ttft={inference.get('ttft_ms')} cache={timings['cache']}"
    )


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--source", default="bbc", help="probe source key whose first ok URL is used")
    parser.add_argument("--url", help="explicit article URL instead of a probe pick")
    parser.add_argument("--model", help="model for both calls; endpoint defaults when omitted")
    parser.add_argument("--only", choices=["signal", "analyze"])
    args = parser.parse_args()

    url = args.url or probe_url(args.source)
    with httpx.Client(base_url=args.base, timeout=300) as client:
        print("health:", client.get("/api/health").json())
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {"url": url, "no_cache": True}
        if args.model:
            payload["model"] = args.model
        for endpoint in ("signal", "analyze"):
            if args.only and args.only != endpoint:
                continue
            report(endpoint, client.post(f"/api/{endpoint}", json=payload))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
</details>

```python
"""Which skeleton fixtures the e2e models handle: status/error code and timings per endpoint, no text."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import time

import httpx

HOSTS = {
    "yahoo": "finance.yahoo.com",
    "cnbc": "www.cnbc.com",
    "fool": "www.fool.com",
    "prnewswire": "www.prnewswire.com",
    "globenewswire": "www.globenewswire.com",
    "sec": "www.sec.gov",
    "cnn": "www.cnn.com",
    "fortune": "fortune.com",
    "guardian": "www.theguardian.com",
    "bbc": "www.bbc.com",
}


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--base", default="http://localhost:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--sources", default=",".join(HOSTS))
    parser.add_argument("--endpoints", default="analyze,summary")
    parser.add_argument("--extractor", default="cascade")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with httpx.Client(base_url=args.base, timeout=300) as client:
        for source in args.sources.split(","):
            url = f"http://{HOSTS[source]}/vt-skeleton/article-1"
            for endpoint in args.endpoints.split(","):
                started = time.perf_counter()
                body = {"url": url, "no_cache": True, "extractor": args.extractor}
                resp = client.post(f"/api/{endpoint}", json=body)
                wall = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                data = resp.json()
                if resp.status_code == 200:
                    extra = f"summary_chars={len(data.get('summary', ''))} words={data['meta']['word_count']}"
                    if "signal" in data:
                        extra += f" sentiment={data['signal']['sentiment']}"
                else:
                    extra = f"code={data['error']['code']} msg={data['error']['message'][:90]}"
                print(f"{source:14} {endpoint:8} {resp.status_code} {wall:7.0f}ms {extra}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```
  { key: "bbc", name: "BBC Business" },
];

export function sourceName(key: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!key) return null;
  return SOURCES.find((s) => s.key === key)?.name ?? key;
```

```yaml
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - run: uv sync --all-packages --frozen
      - run: uv run python scripts/check.py --backend --full

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: API types match backend/openapi.json
        run: pnpm gen:api && git diff --exit-code -- src/lib/api-schema.d.ts
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm format:check
      - run: pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build

  # Full stack in containers: app image, CPU Ollama with the tiny CI models, fixture site, Playwright.
  e2e:
    needs: [backend, frontend]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      COMPOSE_FILE: compose.yaml:compose.e2e.yaml
      E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8000
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
          df -h /

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Build app image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/app.Dockerfile
          tags: veritrade-app:local
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=app
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=app

      - name: Restore Ollama models
        id: models
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ollama-models-${{ hashFiles('deploy/ci-models.txt') }}

      - name: Start the e2e stack
        run: |
          echo "OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR=$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models"
          OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 900 --no-build
          docker compose ps -a
          curl -fsS "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/health"

      # Saved right after the pull, so a failing test run still caches the models.
      - name: Save Ollama models
        if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR"
      - if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ${{ steps.models.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

      - name: Warm up both models
        run: |
          for model in qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0 tev1:0.8b-q8_0; do
            curl -fsS --max-time 600 -o /dev/null -w "$model %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" \
              -H 'content-type: application/json' \
              -d "{\"url\": \"http://www.cnn.com/vt-skeleton/article-1\", \"model\": \"$model\"}" \
              "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/signal"
          done

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - name: Install Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm exec playwright test

      - name: Collect compose logs
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color --timestamps > compose-logs.txt
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-failure
          path: |
            frontend/playwright-report/
            frontend/test-results/
            compose-logs.txt
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Tear down
        if: always()
        run: docker compose down --remove-orphans

```

```typescript
import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";

// Defaults match compose.e2e.yaml: the fixture site answers for publisher hostnames inside the stack.
const ARTICLE_URL = process.env.E2E_ARTICLE_URL ?? "http://www.cnn.com/vt-skeleton/article-1";
const DECISION_MODEL = process.env.E2E_DECISION_MODEL ?? "tev1:0.8b-q8_0";
const EXTRACTOR = process.env.E2E_EXTRACTOR ?? "trafilatura";

// Model-agnostic: any valid label passes, the point is the plumbing.
const SENTIMENT = /^(Bullish|Bearish|Neutral)$/;
const LABELS = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

async function open(page: Page, mode: "Split" | "Combined", streaming: boolean) {
  await page.goto("/");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
  // Pickers fill from /api/models; waiting here keeps selectOption from racing the fetch.
  await expect(page.getByLabel("Signal model")).toContainText("(default)");
  await page.getByRole("radio", { name: new RegExp(mode) }).check();
  const toggle = page.getByRole("checkbox", { name: /Streaming/ });
  if (streaming) await toggle.check();
  else await toggle.uncheck();
}

async function analyze(page: Page) {
  await page.getByLabel("Article URL").fill(ARTICLE_URL);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Analyze" }).click();
}

async function expectNoError(page: Page) {
  // Not getByRole("alert"): Next's route announcer also carries that role.
  await expect(page.getByTestId("error-banner")).toHaveCount(0);
}

test.describe("analyze page", () => {
  test("split mode streams a summary next to the signal, with timings", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Split", true);
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-text")).not.toBeEmpty();
    await expectNoError(page);

    const latency = page.getByTestId("latency");
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-signal")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-summary")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-signal-signal")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-summary-token")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByText("server total")).toHaveCount(2);
  });

  test("combined streaming delivers sentiment, summary and timings in one call", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Combined", true);
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-text")).not.toBeEmpty();
    await expectNoError(page);

    const latency = page.getByTestId("latency");
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-analyze")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-analyze-signal")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByText("server total")).toHaveCount(1);
  });

  test("decision model and extractor switch flow through the JSON endpoints", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Split", false);
    await page.getByLabel("Signal model").selectOption(DECISION_MODEL);
    await page.getByLabel("Extractor").selectOption(EXTRACTOR);
    await expect(page.getByLabel("Parser")).toBeDisabled();
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    const signal = page.getByRole("region", { name: "Signal" });
    await expect(signal).toContainText(DECISION_MODEL);
    await expect(signal).toContainText("probability");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("article-extraction")).toContainText(EXTRACTOR);
    await expectNoError(page);
  });
});

test("signal-only API call with the decision model returns a label and stage timings", async ({ request }) => {
  const resp = await request.post("/api/signal", { data: { url: ARTICLE_URL, model: DECISION_MODEL } });
  expect(resp.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await resp.json();

  expect(LABELS).toContain(body.signal.sentiment);
  expect(body.signal.policy).toBe("probability");
  expect(Object.keys(body.signal.probabilities).sort()).toEqual([...LABELS].sort());
  expect(body.meta).toMatchObject({ model: DECISION_MODEL, model_kind: "decision", endpoint: "signal" });
  expect(body.meta.source).toBe(new URL(ARTICLE_URL).hostname.split(".").at(-2));
  expect(body.timings.inference.wall_ms).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(body.timings.extract_ms).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
});
```

```typescript
// Runs against an already-running stack: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait`.
export default defineConfig({
```

```
test("signal-only API call with the decision model returns a label and stage timings", async ({
  request,
}) => {
  // no_cache: earlier tests and the CI warm-up may have cached this exact request.
  const resp = await request.post("/api/signal", {
    data: { url: ARTICLE_URL, model: DECISION_MODEL, no_cache: true },
  });
  expect(resp.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await resp.json();
  expect(body.meta.cached).toBe(false);

  expect(LABELS).toContain(body.signal.sentiment);
  expect(body.signal.policy).toBe("probability");
  expect(Object.keys(body.signal.probabilities).sort()).toEqual([...LABELS].sort());
  expect(body.meta).toMatchObject({ model: DECISION_MODEL, model_kind: "decision", endpoint: "signal" });
  // The fixture keeps the publisher hostname, so the source profile still resolves.
  expect(body.meta.source).toBeTruthy();
  expect(body.timings.inference.wall_ms).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(body.timings.extract_ms).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
});
```

```
commit 140ca9c6a40e178b9014baef849ff396dc597c81
Author: Kristiyan Dimitrov <kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Oct 18 19:18:06 2026 +0300

    fix: salvage length-cut generations and zero sampling penalties
    
    - A summary or analyze generation that hits num_predict is no longer a 502:
      the fields already produced are recovered with the streaming JSON scanner,
      the summary is cut back to its last complete sentence and the response
      carries `truncated: true` (shown as a note in the UI). analyze still needs
      its score. The doubled-budget retry is dropped for these endpoints.
    - Every chat call pins presence/frequency/repeat penalties to neutral: the
      qwen3.5 Modelfiles set presence_penalty 1.5, which skewed greedy outputs
      away from tokens in the few-shot answers.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

> # P4a final report: Docker, compose, e2e and CI
> 
> CI is green on all three jobs (backend, frontend, e2e): https://github.com/cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics/actions/runs/39145203026. The native, bundled and e2e stacks all ran here, and everything I started is torn down.
> 
> ## Files created or changed
> Commits 8dbdcc1, 7c7384e and 5c477fe, all pushed to main. I staged only my own paths, by name.
> - `docker/app.Dockerfile`, `docker/ollama-pull.sh`, `docker/e2e/fixture-site.conf` (new)
> - `compose.yaml`, `compose.e2e.yaml` (new), `deploy/bundled.env`, `.dockerignore`
> - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml` (new)
> - `frontend/e2e/analyze.spec.ts`, `frontend/playwright.config.ts`
> - Nothing outside my ownership, and no dependency or lockfile changes.
> 
> ## What works
> - **Image:**
>   - **Stages:** a pnpm static export, then a layer with the third-party Python packages, then a 1.8 MB layer with just the app wheel, then a python:3.13-slim-bookworm runtime.
>   - **Runtime:** runs as a non-root user with the `veritrade-healthcheck` HEALTHCHECK.
>   - **Size:** 437 MB unpacked, 94 MB compressed.
>   - **Benchmarks page:** builds even when `evals/results/benchmarks.json` doesn't exist yet; it falls back to the committed sample.
> - **Build times:** fully cold 29 s (fresh builder, base images pulled). A rebuild with no changes takes under 1 s, a frontend-only edit about 5 s, and the CI build with the GitHub Actions cache 36 s.
> - **Native path:** `docker compose up -d --wait` is healthy in about 5 s, and `/api/health` reports Ollama 0.40.6 with the `native-metal` label. Against a live BBC article:
>   - `/api/signal`: 200, neutral, 345 ms in total (inference 253 ms).
>   - `/api/analyze`: 200, bullish, 2.8 s in total.
>   - I used `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` rather than the defaults so the grid's loaded models weren't pushed out of memory.
> - **Bundled path:** `docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d --wait` took 36 s on first start, including a 1 GB model pull. Health reports `docker-cpu`, and `/api/analyze` on a live BBC article returned 200 (bullish) in 24.5 s.
> - **e2e stack:** `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait` takes about 31 s.
>   - An nginx fixture site answers for the 10 publisher hostnames inside the compose network, so nothing reaches a real publisher.
>   - The app runs in test mode with the SSRF allowlist set to exactly those hostnames; a request to 127.0.0.1 is still blocked.
> - **Playwright (6 tests):**
>   - **Coverage:** split streaming, combined streaming, the tev1 decision model with the trafilatura extractor over the JSON endpoints, a signal-only API call with tev1, the benchmarks page, and navigation.
>   - **Results:** 6/6 locally in 50 s on the first version of the tests, and 6/6 on CI in 46 s.
>   - **CI job:** the whole e2e job takes 3 min 31 s, and the cached models were reused.
> - **Live smoke:** dispatched once and 10/10 sources fetched: https://github.com/cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics/actions/runs/39145218933
> - **Model volume:** `veritrade_ollama-models` is kept so re-runs skip the download; it holds 1.7 GB.
> 
> ## Deviations and why
> - **Fixture hostnames:** Docker DNS aliases rather than a static IP plus `extra_hosts`, so no fixed subnet can clash with other Docker networks.
> - **Fixture URLs** use `http://` because the fixture site has no TLS.
> - **`VT_MODELS` on the host instead of `OLLAMA_MODELS`:** `OLLAMA_MODELS` is Ollama's own model-directory variable. A reviewer who has it set would have passed a path in as the model allowlist.
> - **No `--profile` needed for e2e:** the e2e overlay switches the Ollama services on itself.
> - **Ollama models mounted at `/root/.ollama/models`:** this keeps Ollama's root-only key file out of the CI cache. The pull step also skips models it already has, so cached runs work offline.
> - **`bundled.env` pulls only `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0`:** tev1 is a CI-only, unevaluated model, so reviewers shouldn't download it.
> - **Dropped the `# syntax=` line:** its Docker Hub lookup timed out once, and the built-in Dockerfile support handles everything the file uses.
> - **Disk cleanup on CI** now runs only below 25 GB free. The runner already had 104 GB free, and the cleanup was costing 173 s.
> 
> ## Open issues
> - **0.8b schema_violation errors:** `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` was returning 502s when it hit its output limit. Commit 140ca9c (the truncation salvage) addresses this and CI is green with it. I did not re-run the live Guardian analyze on the bundled stack after that fix.
> - **Other containers are running again:** `[redacted]-[redacted]-436-*` and `[redacted]-450-*` (postgres, redis, mailpit) were started outside this work at about 16:20. I didn't touch them; P5 should stop them again before its exclusive latency run.
> - **Host memory pressure:** about 24 GB of swap is in use. A second full local UI run timed out because of it, with the summary still streaming after 150 s. After the final test change I re-ran only the changed and quick tests locally (3/3 passed); the full suite passed on CI.
> - **Linux native path:** the host's Ollama must be started with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`. This is noted in the `compose.yaml` header.
> - **Fixture hostnames are listed in three places:** the nginx map, the compose aliases and the SSRF allowlist.
> - **One rule slip:** early on I ran an inline `uv run python -c "print(1)"`, which did nothing but breaks the no-inline-Python rule. I didn't repeat it.
> 
> ## Requests
> - P5's `select --write` should write `VT_PULL_MODELS`, `VT_MODELS` and `VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_*` into `deploy/bundled.env`.
> - The P5 README should include the native, bundled and e2e commands above; the e2e commands are also in the `compose.e2e.yaml` header.

```typescript
  expect(body.timings.extract_ms).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
});
```

### 🤖 Assistant: *The grid agent found a serving bug, and I…*

`15:10:04`

> The grid agent found a serving bug, and I approved the fix. I confirmed the cause with `ollama show`:
> 
> - **The bug:** the qwen3.5 models (0.8b/2b/4b) ship with `presence_penalty 1.5`, and that penalty still applies when we decode greedily.
> - **The effect:** the few-shot examples end with "neutral", so the penalty pushed answers away from neutral. On 60 dev tweets, 26 generated labels disagreed with the model's own most likely answer; with the penalty off, none did.
> - **Where it mattered:** it biased the generated scores and summaries. The confidence thresholds use probabilities computed before the penalty, so those were unaffected.
> 
> The fix sets all sampling penalties to zero on every Ollama chat call. The grid reruns the affected models, which adds about 15 minutes. I also asked the agent to fix a smaller bug in the fallback confidence code: it misreads qwen's combined " -" token. That fallback has never fired, in 1,200 label calls so far. Both findings are recorded in `01-decisions.md`.
> 
> Still running: the articles tooling, the eval grid, and Docker/e2e.

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 10 - Discover candidates for one source

You are the discovery agent for **one source** (its key is in the message that spawned you, for example `cnbc`).
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read titles only through the Read
tool on the private view file, never quote a headline or any article text in your messages or final report,
never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Goal

End with **at least 6 fetched articles per class** (bullish, bearish, neutral) for your source, published
between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-18, so that at least 5 per class survive the gold step. You judge the likely
class from the headline only; the real labels come later from independent labellers, so aim for clear cases.

A good candidate is one news story, press release or filing exhibit mainly about **one primary entity**: a
company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy. Skip live blogs, videos, galleries, opinion
roundups, newsletters, market wraps that list many stocks, "best stocks to buy" lists, quote pages, and law-firm
"class action" or "investor alert" releases (advertising, not issuer news).

What the classes mean (same rubric as the labellers, `30-label.md`): **bullish** = clear, material positive
economic impact on the primary entity (results or guidance above expectations, a major contract or approval, a
takeover at a premium); **bearish** = clear, material negative impact (results or guidance below expectations,
large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades, layoffs tied to weakness); **neutral** = no clear
material direction (scheduled announcements, routine appointments and dividends, conference-call notices,
explainers, balanced or minor news). Emotional wording is not a signal.

## Commands

All from the repository root. Output is ids, URLs, counts and paths only.

```bash
# 1. broad sweep with the source's feeds and deeper archives (sitemaps, archive pages, listings, EDGAR)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE

# 2. targeted sweeps: --query is a keyword search where the archive supports it (PR Newswire search,
#    EDGAR full-text search) and a headline/URL-slug filter everywhere else; repeat --query freely
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE --query "lowered guidance" --query "net loss"

# 3. extra listing pages on the source's own domain (Yahoo quote news pages, section pages)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source yahoo \
  --listing-url https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TICKER/news/

# 4. write a compact private view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) and Read it
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles candidates --source SOURCE --unfetched [--query WORD] [--limit 300]
#    -> evals/data/private/articles/views/SOURCE.tsv   (Read it with the Read tool; it is private)

# 5. fetch your picks through the serving fetcher; list ids one per line in a private file
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles fetch --source SOURCE --ids-file evals/data/private/articles/picks/SOURCE.txt

# progress for your source
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status --source SOURCE
```

Archive responses are cached for 6 hours, so repeating `discover` with new queries is cheap and polite.
`--pages N` deepens paged listings, search and EDGAR (default 3 to 40 depending on the archive).

## Query ideas

- Bearish: `lowered guidance`, `cuts forecast`, `profit warning`, `net loss`, `misses`, `downgrade`, `layoffs`,
  `recall`, `investigation`, `impairment`, `going concern`, `delisting`, `shares fall`, `plunge`, `default`.
- Bullish: `raises guidance`, `record revenue`, `beats`, `upgrade`, `to acquire`, `approval`, `contract`,
  `surges`, `dividend increase`, `buyback`.
- Neutral: `conference call`, `to present`, `appoints`, `annual meeting`, `declares quarterly dividend`,
  `launches`, `explainer`, `what to know`.

Source notes:

- **sec**: discovery uses EDGAR full-text search over 8-K filings and keeps the EX-99.1 exhibit. The view's
  `edgar_items` column helps: `2.02` is results of operations (earnings, either direction), `5.02` officer
  changes (usually neutral), `1.01` material agreements, `2.05`/`2.06` restructuring and impairments (often
  bearish), `8.01` other events. Search phrases such as `"third quarter"`, `net loss`, `record`, `lowered`.
- **prnewswire**, **globenewswire**: wires carry many non-US issuers and many law-firm ads; prefer issuer
  releases with numbers (results, guidance, deals). Bearish releases are rarer: search for losses, impairments,
  restructuring, going-concern and guidance cuts.
- **yahoo**, **bbc**, **cnn**, **guardian**: listings carry no or few dates; the publish date comes from the page
  at fetch time and out-of-window pages are dropped later, so prefer recent pages and check the fetch output.
- **fool**: much of the output is evergreen "should you buy" commentary; prefer news-driven articles about one
  company (earnings reactions, guidance, deals).

## Procedure

1. Run the broad sweep, then 2-4 targeted sweeps per class. Stop sweeping when the window holds plenty of
   plausible candidates per class (dozens), or after about 12 discover runs.
2. Write the view and Read it. Pick about **8 per class** (24 in total) by headline, preferring clear cases
   and a spread of companies. Put the ids, one per line, into
   `evals/data/private/articles/picks/<source>.txt` (create the folder if needed; only ids go in it).
3. Fetch them. For each printed line check: `ok` (not an error such as `source_blocked`, `paywalled`,
   `consent_required`, `upstream_http`), `words` of at least about 200, a `published` date inside the window, and
   `method` other than an `extract_error`. Replace failures with new picks and fetch again until you reach at
   least 6 good fetches per class.
4. Do not prepare packets, label or edit anything else; the main loop takes it from here.

## Final report (counts only, no headlines or article text)

- Fetched OK per intended class, and fetch errors by code.
- Which archive kinds and queries were productive (query strings are fine, they are yours).
- Any class that looks hard to fill for this source, and why in general terms.
````

````markdown
# 20 - Gold body, key facts and a provisional label

You turn fetched pages into reference ("gold") article bodies. The gold body is the yardstick for the
extraction benchmark (which parser and extractor recover the article best) and the text the labellers read.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read pages only with the Read tool
on the packet files you are given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/`, never quote article
text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Input

The message that spawned you lists gold packet paths, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/gold/<id>.md`.

A packet shows the page's visible text as numbered lines (`L0001 ...`), one per text block. Lines are
folded into marker rows that keep their numbers, for example `L0012-L0040 [29 lines hidden: short lines
(menus, buttons, tickers)]` or `L0001-L0140 [140 lines hidden: before the located article]`. Folding is only
for compactness: every line number stays valid. If the headline is not visible, the story looks cut off, or a
folded run might be part of the article (a short bulleted list), Read the full packet named in the header
(`<id>.full.md`), which shows every line.

## Decide: usable or not

Usable means one news story, press release or filing exhibit, in English, mainly about **one primary entity**
(a company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy), with at least 120 words of body text.
Otherwise set `usable: false` and one `reject_reason`:

| reject_reason | when |
|---|---|
| `not_article` | index or section page, quote page, data-only page, error, consent or login page |
| `live_blog` | rolling live coverage with timestamps |
| `paywalled_stub` | only a teaser; the rest is behind a wall |
| `roundup` | several unrelated items or companies with no primary entity (market wraps, newsletters, lists) |
| `video_only` | the story is a video with a caption |
| `too_short` | under 120 words of body text |
| `non_english` | not in English |
| `duplicate` | the same story as another packet in your batch (keep the better one) |
| `other` | anything else (say why in your final report, in general terms) |

## For usable pages

- `title_line`: the line holding the headline (normally the `h1` just above the story).
- `body_ranges`: inclusive `[start, end]` line ranges that together cover exactly the article body, in order and
  not overlapping. Include: the dateline lede, body paragraphs, in-body subheadings, bulleted or numbered lists
  that belong to the story, quotes. Exclude: the headline, standfirst or dek, editor key-points boxes, bylines,
  dates, image captions and credits, "read more" and related links, ads and their labels, newsletter and app
  promos, share buttons, author bios, comment prompts, financial tables, and press-release boilerplate after
  the story (About the company, forward-looking or safe-harbor statements, contacts, "SOURCE" lines, "View
  original content"). Split a range to skip a promo or a folded run of menu lines in the middle of a story.
  The title line must not fall inside a body range.
- `key_facts`: 3 to 5 statements, at most 25 words each, most market-moving first, in your own words. Copy
  numbers exactly as the body writes them ("$1.25 billion", "28%", "third quarter"), and only use numbers that
  appear in the body: no sums, differences or conversions. Never copy 10 or more consecutive words.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written ("Nvidia", "Brent crude", "UK economy").
- `ticker`: the ticker if the article states it or it is unambiguous, else `null`.
- `provisional_label`: your quick read with the rubric in `30-label.md` (bullish, bearish or neutral). It is
  only used to balance the selection; the real labels come from two independent labellers.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json` with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "usable": true,
  "reject_reason": null,
  "title_line": 41,
  "body_ranges": [[44, 61], [64, 70]],
  "key_facts": [
    "Fact in your own words with numbers copied exactly from the body.",
    "Second fact.",
    "Third fact."
  ],
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "provisional_label": "bearish"
}
```

For a rejected page: `{"id": "...", "usable": false, "reject_reason": "live_blog"}` (other fields may be
omitted).

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs of your batch, run:

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage gold
```

It prints one line per id: `PASS` (with your provisional label and the body word count, or `rejected:<reason>`)
or `FAIL` with codes. Fix every `FAIL` among your ids and run it again until they all pass.

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `schema:<field>:<type>` | field missing, misspelled, wrong type, or an unknown field |
| `missing:<field>` | usable outputs need `title_line`, `body_ranges`, `entity`, `provisional_label` |
| `range_inverted`, `range_out_of_bounds`, `ranges_overlap` | ranges must be `[start, end]`, start <= end, within the page, disjoint |
| `title_out_of_bounds`, `title_in_body` | the headline line must exist and sit outside the body ranges |
| `body_too_short` | under 120 words: widen the ranges if you cut too much, else reject as `too_short` |
| `key_facts_count`, `key_fact_too_long`, `key_fact_empty` | 3 to 5 facts, each 1 to 25 words |
| `key_fact_number_ungrounded` | a number in a fact does not appear in the body text; copy it exactly |
| `key_fact_verbatim` | a fact shares 10 consecutive words with the body; rephrase |
| `missing_packet_lines` | the packet was not prepared; tell the main loop |

## Final report (counts only)

Usable vs rejected (by reason), provisional labels (bullish / bearish / neutral), any ids that still fail
and their codes. No headlines, quotes or article text.

````
</details>

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# 40 - Adjudicate disagreements and ambiguous articles

You resolve the articles where the two labellers disagreed or at least one flagged the article as ambiguous.
The message that spawned you lists adjudication packets, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/adjudicate/<id>.md`.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read
tool on the packets you were given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/`, never quote
article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

A packet holds both labellers' outputs (label, score, entity, ticker, ambiguous flag, confidence, rationale)
followed by the headline and article body, the same text they read. Do not open other files.

## Rubric

Use exactly the rubric in `evals/opus_prompts/30-label.md`: the economic impact of the news on its primary
entity, not the tone; bullish or bearish only for a clear, material implication; mixed news follows the
dominant material driver, or neutral if balanced. Form your own reading from the article first, then weigh
the two rationales as arguments, not votes.

## Decide

- `keep`: the article has one defensible label under the rubric, and the disagreement came from a misreading,
  a materiality threshold, or a different primary entity that the article settles. Your label, score, entity
  and ticker become final.
- `replace`: the article stays genuinely ambiguous: balanced mixed news, no clear primary entity, materiality
  that depends on facts the article does not give, or a direction a careful analyst could reasonably dispute.
  Replaced articles leave the set and the main loop finds others. The set is only useful if its labels are
  defensible, so do not keep an article just to fill a quota.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/<id>.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "decision": "keep",
  "label": "neutral",
  "score": 0,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": null,
  "rationale": "Your own words, at most 50: why this label, and what settled the disagreement."
}
```

For `replace`, still give your best label and score (their sign must agree) and say in the rationale why the
article is too ambiguous to keep.

## Validate and fix

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage adjudicate
```

Fix every `FAIL`: `schema:<field>:<type>`, `score_label_mismatch`, `rationale_too_long`, `rationale_verbatim`
(rephrase), `not_requested` (the id is not in `adjudicate_ids.txt`; tell the main loop), `gold_missing`.
Do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Kept by final label, replaced, and for kept articles whether you sided with labeller A, labeller B or neither.
No headlines, quotes or article text.
````

🟢 **p3-articles-tooling** · *Rest of P3 articles report: deviations, open issues, requests*

> Rest of the P3 article-tooling report, from Deviations to the end.
> 
> ## Deviations and why
> - GlobeNewswire search is disallowed by robots.txt, so discovery uses its monthly sitemaps instead. Their URLs carry the issuer's org id instead of `/0/`, so discovery uses a relaxed pattern for this source.
> - CNBC's HTML site-map pages are rendered in the browser and return no article links, so discovery reads the newest `CNBCsitemapAll*.xml` instead.
> - Yahoo has no article sitemap, but it has a daily HTML archive at `/sitemap/YYYY_MM_DD/` (50 links per page plus a cursor link to the next page). Discovery follows the cursor (`--pages`, default 2 per day) and dates each undated link with its archive day; the page date at fetch time wins. The `topic/tech` page was dropped because it matched nothing.
> - Every archive request is checked against robots.txt, retried once after a timeout (read timeout raised to 45 s), and cached for 6 h, so agents can repeat `discover` with new queries without hitting publishers again.
> - EDGAR full-text search: phrase queries must be sent with spaces as `%20`, because `+` caused HTTP 500. With no query the search returns mostly 8-K cover documents, so up to 120 filing indexes are resolved to their EX-99.1, filings with items 2.02, 7.01, 8.01, 1.01, 2.05 or 2.06 first.
> - Added commands and flags beyond the spec:
>   - `articles candidates` writes a private TSV view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) for agents to Read.
>   - `ingest --agreement` prints the A/B agreement summary only for the main loop, so labellers never see the running agreement. `adjudicate_ids.txt` is still written on every label ingest.
> - Gold packets:
>   - `h1` lines are never folded and are listed in the packet header. On the Fool page the `h1` comes after the body in the page source, so the headline had been folded away.
>   - When the extracted title text does not match a line, the nearest `h1` above the body anchors the headline.
>   - Every packet has a `<id>.full.md` showing every line.
>   - Blocks over 250 words are split into chunks at sentence boundaries.
> - `reject_reason` is a fixed list of values (`not_article`, `live_blog`, `paywalled_stub`, `roundup`, `video_only`, `too_short`, `non_english`, `duplicate`, `other`) rather than free text, so it can be counted and printed safely.
> - The committed `score` is the adjudicator's score for adjudicated articles, otherwise the mean of the A and B scores, so it can be x.5. `entity` and `rationale` come from the adjudicator, otherwise from labeller A. `ticker` is the first non-null of adjudicator, A, B, gold.
> - Rebalancing is +-1 per source and class: each count stays within 2 to 4 and each class totals 30. A source can end with 8 to 10 articles, because I kept deviations from 3 to a minimum rather than forcing every source to exactly 9. Within a cell, agreed articles are picked before adjudicated ones, each group in a seeded order, and one seeded article per cell goes to dev, which makes dev exactly 30. The algorithm text is written into `stats.json`.
> - Before writing, `finalize` refuses any row whose committed text shares a 10-word run with the article body or contains its headline.
> 
> ## Open issues
> - Bearish will be the hardest class for the wires (PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire): they are flooded with law-firm "class action" ads, which the prompts exclude as not issuer news, and issuers seldom announce bad news. SEC also needs directional queries (losses, impairments, restructuring under items 2.05/2.06, lowered guidance).
> - Fool publishes a lot of evergreen "should you buy" commentary. Yahoo republishes partner copy, including Fool's, so the same story can appear from two sources; the gold `duplicate` reason only covers duplicates within one batch.
> - BBC and Guardian lean towards macro stories. I allowed one primary entity that is an asset, commodity, index or national economy, which helps fill those classes but is a judgement call. BBC has 825 undated candidates whose dates are only known after fetch.
> - Some SEC EX-99.1 exhibits are financial-statement tables or short. The dry-run exhibit came out at only 109 words from the extractor, with a packet ratio of 2.44 on an 18-line page.
> - PR Newswire is slow at times: its news sitemap had 3 timeouts on the first run. The retry and longer timeout came after that run; the search timeout disappeared with them, but I did not re-run the full news sitemap afterwards.
> - The test guard on the committed `articles.jsonl` skips until `finalize` has run.
> 
> ## Requests
> - Whoever owns `backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml`: widen the GlobeNewswire `article_pattern` to accept any numeric org id in place of `/0/` (`.../\d+/\d+/en/[^/]+\.html$`), so the registry matches the sitemap URLs.
> - No dependency or lockfile changes are needed.
