````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```
````

````markdown
# 10 - Discover candidates for one source

You are the discovery agent for **one source** (its key is in the message that spawned you, for example `cnbc`).
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read titles only through the Read
tool on the private view file, never quote a headline or any article text in your messages or final report,
never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Goal

End with **at least 6 fetched articles per class** (bullish, bearish, neutral) for your source, published
between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-18, so that at least 5 per class survive the gold step. You judge the likely
class from the headline only; the real labels come later from independent labellers, so aim for clear cases.

A good candidate is one news story, press release or filing exhibit mainly about **one primary entity**: a
company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy. Skip live blogs, videos, galleries, opinion
roundups, newsletters, market wraps that list many stocks, "best stocks to buy" lists, quote pages, and law-firm
"class action" or "investor alert" releases (advertising, not issuer news).

What the classes mean (same rubric as the labellers, `30-label.md`): **bullish** = clear, material positive
economic impact on the primary entity (results or guidance above expectations, a major contract or approval, a
takeover at a premium); **bearish** = clear, material negative impact (results or guidance below expectations,
large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades, layoffs tied to weakness); **neutral** = no clear
material direction (scheduled announcements, routine appointments and dividends, conference-call notices,
explainers, balanced or minor news). Emotional wording is not a signal.

## Commands

All from the repository root. Output is ids, URLs, counts and paths only.

```bash
# 1. broad sweep with the source's feeds and deeper archives (sitemaps, archive pages, listings, EDGAR)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE

# 2. targeted sweeps: --query is a keyword search where the archive supports it (PR Newswire search,
#    EDGAR full-text search) and a headline/URL-slug filter everywhere else; repeat --query freely
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE --query "lowered guidance" --query "net loss"

# 3. extra listing pages on the source's own domain (Yahoo quote news pages, section pages)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source yahoo \
  --listing-url https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TICKER/news/

# 4. write a compact private view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) and Read it
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles candidates --source SOURCE --unfetched [--query WORD] [--limit 300]
#    -> evals/data/private/articles/views/SOURCE.tsv   (Read it with the Read tool; it is private)

# 5. fetch your picks through the serving fetcher; list ids one per line in a private file
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles fetch --source SOURCE --ids-file evals/data/private/articles/picks/SOURCE.txt

# progress for your source
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status --source SOURCE
```

Archive responses are cached for 6 hours, so repeating `discover` with new queries is cheap and polite.
`--pages N` deepens paged listings, search and EDGAR (default 3 to 40 depending on the archive).

## Query ideas

- Bearish: `lowered guidance`, `cuts forecast`, `profit warning`, `net loss`, `misses`, `downgrade`, `layoffs`,
  `recall`, `investigation`, `impairment`, `going concern`, `delisting`, `shares fall`, `plunge`, `default`.
- Bullish: `raises guidance`, `record revenue`, `beats`, `upgrade`, `to acquire`, `approval`, `contract`,
  `surges`, `dividend increase`, `buyback`.
- Neutral: `conference call`, `to present`, `appoints`, `annual meeting`, `declares quarterly dividend`,
  `launches`, `explainer`, `what to know`.

Source notes:

- **sec**: discovery uses EDGAR full-text search over 8-K filings and keeps the EX-99.1 exhibit. The view's
  `edgar_items` column helps: `2.02` is results of operations (earnings, either direction), `5.02` officer
  changes (usually neutral), `1.01` material agreements, `2.05`/`2.06` restructuring and impairments (often
  bearish), `8.01` other events. Search phrases such as `"third quarter"`, `net loss`, `record`, `lowered`.
- **prnewswire**, **globenewswire**: wires carry many non-US issuers and many law-firm ads; prefer issuer
  releases with numbers (results, guidance, deals). Bearish releases are rarer: search for losses, impairments,
  restructuring, going-concern and guidance cuts.
- **yahoo**, **bbc**, **cnn**, **guardian**: listings carry no or few dates; the publish date comes from the page
  at fetch time and out-of-window pages are dropped later, so prefer recent pages and check the fetch output.
- **fool**: much of the output is evergreen "should you buy" commentary; prefer news-driven articles about one
  company (earnings reactions, guidance, deals).

## Procedure

1. Run the broad sweep, then 2-4 targeted sweeps per class. Stop sweeping when the window holds plenty of
   plausible candidates per class (dozens), or after about 12 discover runs.
2. Write the view and Read it. Pick about **8 per class** (24 in total) by headline, preferring clear cases
   and a spread of companies. Put the ids, one per line, into
   `evals/data/private/articles/picks/<source>.txt` (create the folder if needed; only ids go in it).
3. Fetch them. For each printed line check: `ok` (not an error such as `source_blocked`, `paywalled`,
   `consent_required`, `upstream_http`), `words` of at least about 200, a `published` date inside the window, and
   `method` other than an `extract_error`. Replace failures with new picks and fetch again until you reach at
   least 6 good fetches per class.
4. Do not prepare packets, label or edit anything else; the main loop takes it from here.

## Final report (counts only, no headlines or article text)

- Fetched OK per intended class, and fetch errors by code.
- Which archive kinds and queries were productive (query strings are fine, they are yours).
- Any class that looks hard to fill for this source, and why in general terms.
````

````markdown
# 20 - Gold body, key facts and a provisional label

You turn fetched pages into reference ("gold") article bodies. The gold body is the yardstick for the
extraction benchmark (which parser and extractor recover the article best) and the text the labellers read.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read pages only with the Read tool
on the packet files you are given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/`, never quote article
text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Input

The message that spawned you lists gold packet paths, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/gold/<id>.md`.

A packet shows the page's visible text as numbered lines (`L0001 ...`), one per text block. Lines are
folded into marker rows that keep their numbers, for example `L0012-L0040 [29 lines hidden: short lines
(menus, buttons, tickers)]` or `L0001-L0140 [140 lines hidden: before the located article]`. Folding is only
for compactness: every line number stays valid. If the headline is not visible, the story looks cut off, or a
folded run might be part of the article (a short bulleted list), Read the full packet named in the header
(`<id>.full.md`), which shows every line.

## Decide: usable or not

Usable means one news story, press release or filing exhibit, in English, mainly about **one primary entity**
(a company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy), with at least 120 words of body text.
Otherwise set `usable: false` and one `reject_reason`:

| reject_reason | when |
|---|---|
| `not_article` | index or section page, quote page, data-only page, error, consent or login page |
| `live_blog` | rolling live coverage with timestamps |
| `paywalled_stub` | only a teaser; the rest is behind a wall |
| `roundup` | several unrelated items or companies with no primary entity (market wraps, newsletters, lists) |
| `video_only` | the story is a video with a caption |
| `too_short` | under 120 words of body text |
| `non_english` | not in English |
| `duplicate` | the same story as another packet in your batch (keep the better one) |
| `other` | anything else (say why in your final report, in general terms) |

## For usable pages

- `title_line`: the line holding the headline (normally the `h1` just above the story).
- `body_ranges`: inclusive `[start, end]` line ranges that together cover exactly the article body, in order and
  not overlapping. Include: the dateline lede, body paragraphs, in-body subheadings, bulleted or numbered lists
  that belong to the story, quotes. Exclude: the headline, standfirst or dek, editor key-points boxes, bylines,
  dates, image captions and credits, "read more" and related links, ads and their labels, newsletter and app
  promos, share buttons, author bios, comment prompts, financial tables, and press-release boilerplate after
  the story (About the company, forward-looking or safe-harbor statements, contacts, "SOURCE" lines, "View
  original content"). Split a range to skip a promo or a folded run of menu lines in the middle of a story.
  The title line must not fall inside a body range.
- `key_facts`: 3 to 5 statements, at most 25 words each, most market-moving first, in your own words. Copy
  numbers exactly as the body writes them ("$1.25 billion", "28%", "third quarter"), and only use numbers that
  appear in the body: no sums, differences or conversions. Never copy 10 or more consecutive words.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written ("Nvidia", "Brent crude", "UK economy").
- `ticker`: the ticker if the article states it or it is unambiguous, else `null`.
- `provisional_label`: your quick read with the rubric in `30-label.md` (bullish, bearish or neutral). It is
  only used to balance the selection; the real labels come from two independent labellers.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json` with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "usable": true,
  "reject_reason": null,
  "title_line": 41,
  "body_ranges": [[44, 61], [64, 70]],
  "key_facts": [
    "Fact in your own words with numbers copied exactly from the body.",
    "Second fact.",
    "Third fact."
  ],
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "provisional_label": "bearish"
}
```

For a rejected page: `{"id": "...", "usable": false, "reject_reason": "live_blog"}` (other fields may be
omitted).

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs of your batch, run:

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage gold
```

It prints one line per id: `PASS` (with your provisional label and the body word count, or `rejected:<reason>`)
or `FAIL` with codes. Fix every `FAIL` among your ids and run it again until they all pass.

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `schema:<field>:<type>` | field missing, misspelled, wrong type, or an unknown field |
| `missing:<field>` | usable outputs need `title_line`, `body_ranges`, `entity`, `provisional_label` |
| `range_inverted`, `range_out_of_bounds`, `ranges_overlap` | ranges must be `[start, end]`, start <= end, within the page, disjoint |
| `title_out_of_bounds`, `title_in_body` | the headline line must exist and sit outside the body ranges |
| `body_too_short` | under 120 words: widen the ranges if you cut too much, else reject as `too_short` |
| `key_facts_count`, `key_fact_too_long`, `key_fact_empty` | 3 to 5 facts, each 1 to 25 words |
| `key_fact_number_ungrounded` | a number in a fact does not appear in the body text; copy it exactly |
| `key_fact_verbatim` | a fact shares 10 consecutive words with the body; rephrase |
| `missing_packet_lines` | the packet was not prepared; tell the main loop |

## Final report (counts only)

Usable vs rejected (by reason), provisional labels (bullish / bearish / neutral), any ids that still fail
and their codes. No headlines, quotes or article text.

````

<details>

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

```
84-
85:- From this IP, `finance.yahoo.com`, `yahoo.com/news`, `uk.finance.yahoo.com` and `de.yahoo.com` served content
86-  directly with no consent redirect. The pages carry `"gdpr":true` and a client-side CMP

90-  reject-all form in 857 ms and the jar received `A1`, `A1S`, `CFC`, `EuConsent`, `GUC`. Decoding the TCF v2
91-  string in `EuConsent` gives **0 of 24 purposes consented**, which confirms that reject-all was recorded and
92-  accept-all was never sent. A second pass with the same jar skips the form (about 120 ms, no POST).

94-  guard and retries the original URL once; if that lands on the wall again, `detect.classify` raises
95-  `consent_required` with a hint.

97-## Block, consent and paywall detection
98-
99-`detect.classify(status, headers, html, final_url)` is pure and string-based, so it runs on every fetch.
100-
101-| Signal | Raised as |
--
103:| Final URL on `consent.yahoo.com` / `guce.yahoo.com`, or a Yahoo consent form in the page | `consent_required` |
104-| HTTP 401, 403, 429 (retryable), 451 | `source_blocked`, naming the CDN edge from `server` / `cf-ray` |
105-| Cloudflare: `cf-mitigated: challenge`, "Just a moment...", `_cf_chl_opt`, `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/`, "Attention Required! \| Cloudflare" | `source_blocked` |
106-| DataDome `captcha-delivery.com` or `x-dd-b`; PerimeterX `px-captcha` or "Press & Hold"; Akamai "Access Denied" + "Reference #", `sec-if-cpt-container`, `errors.edgesuite.net`; Imperva `_Incapsula_Resource` | `source_blocked`, including when served with HTTP 200 |
107-| JSON-LD `isAccessibleForFree` false (bool or string) and both the JSON-LD `articleBody` and the visible `<p>` text under 200 words | `paywalled` |
108-
109-Design points the probe forced:
110-
111-- Cloudflare's passive `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/scripts/jsd/main.js` beacon sits on normal pages, so only
112-  the interactive `/h/` path counts. `x-datadome` alone is ignored because DataDome sets it on allowed responses.
113-- Markers are only searched in the first 64 KB: interstitials are a few KB, and it keeps 6 MB CNN pages cheap.
114-  Over all 42 captured pages `classify` takes at most 1.7 ms (CNN, 5.8 MB) and under 1 ms everywhere else
115-  (median of 5 runs).
--
119:  Yahoo Finance; WSJ, Barron's, FT and Bloomberg paywalls point to free sources.
120-
121-## What the extractors get
122-
123-Profile semantics (documented at the top of `sources.toml`): remove `drop` selectors, take `body` matches in
124-document order, ignore paragraphs under `min_words`, then cut at the first paragraph after the lede that starts
125-with a `stop_markers` prefix. All selectors use only tag, class, id, attribute and descendant parts; GlobeNewswire
126-also uses a selector list for `p, li`. All 30 primary pages pass the two-parser check.
127-
128-Findings that are not visible in the selectors:
129-
130-- **JSON-LD `articleBody` exists only on CNN** (3/3). Everywhere else the cascade has to fall through to the
131:  profile or density strategy. No source ships `__NEXT_DATA__`; Fool and Fortune use the Next.js flight stream
132:  and Yahoo SvelteKit, neither worth parsing for the body.
133-- **Text joining differs between parsers**: selectolax `text(separator=" ")` splits words at inline tags (drop
134-  caps become "R ogue", "Fla. ,"), while lxml `text_content()` glues text across `<br>` ("WangEmail"). Joining
135-  text nodes without a separator, with spaces only at `<br>` and block boundaries, gives the same text on both.
136-- **Press releases** end with an "About <issuer>" heading, forward-looking statements and contacts as plain
137-  paragraphs, so they are cut with stop markers, not selectors. The "About" check only applies after the lede.
138-- **SEC exhibits** arrive wrapped in the EDGAR SGML envelope, with no `h1`, JSON-LD or containers, and start with
139-  "Exhibit 99.1" and the issuer name. Some filer agents emit `div`/`span` text without `<p>`, which this profile
140-  cannot read; the cascade must fall back to density there. EX-99.1 is sometimes a financial statement (11.6k
141-  words in one sample), which `scope=lede` and the token cap absorb.
142:- **Yahoo** stories are mostly partner copy (Motley Fool, Insider Monkey, 24/7 Wall St, named in `providerId`)
143-  and partner promos survive inside the body; the second half of the text sits in a hidden "Story continues"
144-  block that must be kept.
145-- **CNBC** has editor-written Key Points (`div.RenderKeyPoints-list li`) outside the body, a ready-made lede.
146-- **CNN** pages are 5.7 MB, so DOM parsing is the slow step there; the JSON-LD strategy avoids it.
147-
148-## Caveats
149-
150-- One vantage point. Bot management depends on IP reputation: GitHub Actions runners use US datacenter IPs that
151:  Cloudflare and Akamai treat more strictly, and US visitors see different geo behaviour (no Yahoo consent at
152-  all, `www.cnn.com`, `bbc.com`). CI therefore runs on skeleton fixtures; the weekly live smoke is informational.
153-- Three articles per source on a Sunday: the wires were dominated by non-US issuers, and only 2 of the 25 newest
154-  8-K filing indexes had an EX-99.1 described as a press release.
155-- Blocking decisions drift over time and with request rate; the probe stayed at or under 1 request per second per
156-  domain. The Business Wire `/newsroom` challenge was seen while exploring and is not in the final JSON, because
```

```
"""Checks on agent outputs: schema, line ranges, grounded numbers, no verbatim runs, label agreement."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from itertools import pairwise
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import ValidationError

from veritrade.inference.types import SENTIMENTS, Sentiment
from veritrade_evals.articles import (
    KEY_FACT_MAX_WORDS,
    KEY_FACTS_MAX,
    KEY_FACTS_MIN,
    MIN_BODY_WORDS,
    RATIONALE_MAX_WORDS,
    SHINGLE_WORDS,
    AdjudicateOutput,
    ArticlePaths,
    GoldOutput,
    LabelOutput,
    Stage,
    read_fetched,
    schema_codes,
)

_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d+(?:[.,]\d+)*")
_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.split())


def number_set(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Numbers as canonical decimals: thousands commas dropped, 1.50 == 1.5."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for match in _NUMBER.finditer(text):
        raw = match.group(0).replace(",", "")
        try:
            out.add(format(Decimal(raw).normalize(), "f"))
        except InvalidOperation:
            out.add(raw)
    return out


def shingles(text: str, n: int = SHINGLE_WORDS) -> set[tuple[str, ...]]:
    tokens = _WORD.findall(text.lower())
    return {tuple(tokens[i : i + n]) for i in range(len(tokens) - n + 1)}


def shares_run(text: str, body_shingles: set[tuple[str, ...]], n: int = SHINGLE_WORDS) -> bool:
    return not shingles(text, n).isdisjoint(body_shingles)

        codes.append("title_in_body")
    return sorted(set(codes))


def _key_facts(facts: Sequence[str], body: str) -> list[str]:
    codes: set[str] = set()
    if not KEY_FACTS_MIN <= len(facts) <= KEY_FACTS_MAX:
        codes.add("key_facts_count")
    grounded = number_set(body)
    body_runs = shingles(body)
    for fact in facts:
        if not fact.strip():
            codes.add("key_fact_empty")
        if word_count(fact) > KEY_FACT_MAX_WORDS:
            codes.add("key_fact_too_long")
        if not number_set(fact) <= grounded:
            codes.add("key_fact_number_ungrounded")
        if shares_run(fact, body_runs):
            codes.add("key_fact_verbatim")
    return sorted(codes)
```

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```
````

````markdown
# 10 - Discover candidates for one source

You are the discovery agent for **one source** (its key is in the message that spawned you, for example `cnbc`).
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read titles only through the Read
tool on the private view file, never quote a headline or any article text in your messages or final report,
never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Goal

End with **at least 6 fetched articles per class** (bullish, bearish, neutral) for your source, published
between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-18, so that at least 5 per class survive the gold step. You judge the likely
class from the headline only; the real labels come later from independent labellers, so aim for clear cases.

A good candidate is one news story, press release or filing exhibit mainly about **one primary entity**: a
company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy. Skip live blogs, videos, galleries, opinion
roundups, newsletters, market wraps that list many stocks, "best stocks to buy" lists, quote pages, and law-firm
"class action" or "investor alert" releases (advertising, not issuer news).

What the classes mean (same rubric as the labellers, `30-label.md`): **bullish** = clear, material positive
economic impact on the primary entity (results or guidance above expectations, a major contract or approval, a
takeover at a premium); **bearish** = clear, material negative impact (results or guidance below expectations,
large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades, layoffs tied to weakness); **neutral** = no clear
material direction (scheduled announcements, routine appointments and dividends, conference-call notices,
explainers, balanced or minor news). Emotional wording is not a signal.

## Commands

All from the repository root. Output is ids, URLs, counts and paths only.

```bash
# 1. broad sweep with the source's feeds and deeper archives (sitemaps, archive pages, listings, EDGAR)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE

# 2. targeted sweeps: --query is a keyword search where the archive supports it (PR Newswire search,
#    EDGAR full-text search) and a headline/URL-slug filter everywhere else; repeat --query freely
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE --query "lowered guidance" --query "net loss"

# 3. extra listing pages on the source's own domain (Yahoo quote news pages, section pages)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source yahoo \
  --listing-url https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TICKER/news/

# 4. write a compact private view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) and Read it
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles candidates --source SOURCE --unfetched [--query WORD] [--limit 300]
#    -> evals/data/private/articles/views/SOURCE.tsv   (Read it with the Read tool; it is private)

# 5. fetch your picks through the serving fetcher; list ids one per line in a private file
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles fetch --source SOURCE --ids-file evals/data/private/articles/picks/SOURCE.txt

# progress for your source
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status --source SOURCE
```

Archive responses are cached for 6 hours, so repeating `discover` with new queries is cheap and polite.
`--pages N` deepens paged listings, search and EDGAR (default 3 to 40 depending on the archive).

## Query ideas

- Bearish: `lowered guidance`, `cuts forecast`, `profit warning`, `net loss`, `misses`, `downgrade`, `layoffs`,
  `recall`, `investigation`, `impairment`, `going concern`, `delisting`, `shares fall`, `plunge`, `default`.
- Bullish: `raises guidance`, `record revenue`, `beats`, `upgrade`, `to acquire`, `approval`, `contract`,
  `surges`, `dividend increase`, `buyback`.
- Neutral: `conference call`, `to present`, `appoints`, `annual meeting`, `declares quarterly dividend`,
  `launches`, `explainer`, `what to know`.

Source notes:

- **sec**: discovery uses EDGAR full-text search over 8-K filings and keeps the EX-99.1 exhibit. The view's
  `edgar_items` column helps: `2.02` is results of operations (earnings, either direction), `5.02` officer
  changes (usually neutral), `1.01` material agreements, `2.05`/`2.06` restructuring and impairments (often
  bearish), `8.01` other events. Search phrases such as `"third quarter"`, `net loss`, `record`, `lowered`.
- **prnewswire**, **globenewswire**: wires carry many non-US issuers and many law-firm ads; prefer issuer
  releases with numbers (results, guidance, deals). Bearish releases are rarer: search for losses, impairments,
  restructuring, going-concern and guidance cuts.
- **yahoo**, **bbc**, **cnn**, **guardian**: listings carry no or few dates; the publish date comes from the page
  at fetch time and out-of-window pages are dropped later, so prefer recent pages and check the fetch output.
- **fool**: much of the output is evergreen "should you buy" commentary; prefer news-driven articles about one
  company (earnings reactions, guidance, deals).

## Procedure

1. Run the broad sweep, then 2-4 targeted sweeps per class. Stop sweeping when the window holds plenty of
   plausible candidates per class (dozens), or after about 12 discover runs.
2. Write the view and Read it. Pick about **8 per class** (24 in total) by headline, preferring clear cases
   and a spread of companies. Put the ids, one per line, into
   `evals/data/private/articles/picks/<source>.txt` (create the folder if needed; only ids go in it).
3. Fetch them. For each printed line check: `ok` (not an error such as `source_blocked`, `paywalled`,
   `consent_required`, `upstream_http`), `words` of at least about 200, a `published` date inside the window, and
   `method` other than an `extract_error`. Replace failures with new picks and fetch again until you reach at
   least 6 good fetches per class.
4. Do not prepare packets, label or edit anything else; the main loop takes it from here.

## Final report (counts only, no headlines or article text)

- Fetched OK per intended class, and fetch errors by code.
- Which archive kinds and queries were productive (query strings are fine, they are yours).
- Any class that looks hard to fill for this source, and why in general terms.
````

````markdown
# 20 - Gold body, key facts and a provisional label

You turn fetched pages into reference ("gold") article bodies. The gold body is the yardstick for the
extraction benchmark (which parser and extractor recover the article best) and the text the labellers read.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read pages only with the Read tool
on the packet files you are given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/`, never quote article
text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Input

The message that spawned you lists gold packet paths, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/gold/<id>.md`.

A packet shows the page's visible text as numbered lines (`L0001 ...`), one per text block. Lines are
folded into marker rows that keep their numbers, for example `L0012-L0040 [29 lines hidden: short lines
(menus, buttons, tickers)]` or `L0001-L0140 [140 lines hidden: before the located article]`. Folding is only
for compactness: every line number stays valid. If the headline is not visible, the story looks cut off, or a
folded run might be part of the article (a short bulleted list), Read the full packet named in the header
(`<id>.full.md`), which shows every line.

## Decide: usable or not

Usable means one news story, press release or filing exhibit, in English, mainly about **one primary entity**
(a company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy), with at least 120 words of body text.
Otherwise set `usable: false` and one `reject_reason`:

| reject_reason | when |
|---|---|
| `not_article` | index or section page, quote page, data-only page, error, consent or login page |
| `live_blog` | rolling live coverage with timestamps |
| `paywalled_stub` | only a teaser; the rest is behind a wall |
| `roundup` | several unrelated items or companies with no primary entity (market wraps, newsletters, lists) |
| `video_only` | the story is a video with a caption |
| `too_short` | under 120 words of body text |
| `non_english` | not in English |
| `duplicate` | the same story as another packet in your batch (keep the better one) |
| `other` | anything else (say why in your final report, in general terms) |

## For usable pages

- `title_line`: the line holding the headline (normally the `h1` just above the story).
- `body_ranges`: inclusive `[start, end]` line ranges that together cover exactly the article body, in order and
  not overlapping. Include: the dateline lede, body paragraphs, in-body subheadings, bulleted or numbered lists
  that belong to the story, quotes. Exclude: the headline, standfirst or dek, editor key-points boxes, bylines,
  dates, image captions and credits, "read more" and related links, ads and their labels, newsletter and app
  promos, share buttons, author bios, comment prompts, financial tables, and press-release boilerplate after
  the story (About the company, forward-looking or safe-harbor statements, contacts, "SOURCE" lines, "View
  original content"). Split a range to skip a promo or a folded run of menu lines in the middle of a story.
  The title line must not fall inside a body range.
- `key_facts`: 3 to 5 statements, at most 25 words each, most market-moving first, in your own words. Copy
  numbers exactly as the body writes them ("$1.25 billion", "28%", "third quarter"), and only use numbers that
  appear in the body: no sums, differences or conversions. Never copy 10 or more consecutive words.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written ("Nvidia", "Brent crude", "UK economy").
- `ticker`: the ticker if the article states it or it is unambiguous, else `null`.
- `provisional_label`: your quick read with the rubric in `30-label.md` (bullish, bearish or neutral). It is
  only used to balance the selection; the real labels come from two independent labellers.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json` with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "usable": true,
  "reject_reason": null,
  "title_line": 41,
  "body_ranges": [[44, 61], [64, 70]],
  "key_facts": [
    "Fact in your own words with numbers copied exactly from the body.",
    "Second fact.",
    "Third fact."
  ],
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "provisional_label": "bearish"
}
```

For a rejected page: `{"id": "...", "usable": false, "reject_reason": "live_blog"}` (other fields may be
omitted).

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs of your batch, run:

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage gold
```

It prints one line per id: `PASS` (with your provisional label and the body word count, or `rejected:<reason>`)
or `FAIL` with codes. Fix every `FAIL` among your ids and run it again until they all pass.

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `schema:<field>:<type>` | field missing, misspelled, wrong type, or an unknown field |
| `missing:<field>` | usable outputs need `title_line`, `body_ranges`, `entity`, `provisional_label` |
| `range_inverted`, `range_out_of_bounds`, `ranges_overlap` | ranges must be `[start, end]`, start <= end, within the page, disjoint |
| `title_out_of_bounds`, `title_in_body` | the headline line must exist and sit outside the body ranges |
| `body_too_short` | under 120 words: widen the ranges if you cut too much, else reject as `too_short` |
| `key_facts_count`, `key_fact_too_long`, `key_fact_empty` | 3 to 5 facts, each 1 to 25 words |
| `key_fact_number_ungrounded` | a number in a fact does not appear in the body text; copy it exactly |
| `key_fact_verbatim` | a fact shares 10 consecutive words with the body; rephrase |
| `missing_packet_lines` | the packet was not prepared; tell the main loop |

## Final report (counts only)

Usable vs rejected (by reason), provisional labels (bullish / bearish / neutral), any ids that still fail
and their codes. No headlines, quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````
</details>

```
11:  `veritrade.fetch.headers` (UA, Accept, `Accept-Language: en-US`, client hints, `Sec-Fetch-*`,
12-  `Upgrade-Insecure-Requests`, `Priority`), `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` because `brotli` is installed.
13:  `sec.gov` gets the declared `SEC_USER_AGENT` and no Chrome hints. No cookies are pre-seeded, no TLS
14-  impersonation, headless browser, proxy or captcha solving (Q19).
15-- **Redirects**: followed by hand (max 5), exactly as the serving fetcher will; a hop to Yahoo's consent hosts is
16-  answered once with reject-all (`veritrade.fetch.consent`) and the original URL retried.
17:- **Politeness**: one request at a time per registrable domain with at least 1 s between them; EDGAR at 5 req/s
18-  (half its 10 req/s fair-access ceiling). Reported fetch times exclude these waits.
19-- **Discovery**: each source's `feeds` (RSS/Atom, non-English `dc:language` items skipped) or `sections`
20:  (HTML pages and sitemaps), filtered by `article_pattern`; the 3 newest matches are probed. EDGAR resolves the
21-  8-K Atom feed to filing indexes and then to the EX-99.1 exhibit, preferring index descriptions that say press
22-  release, earnings or results. When a source refuses its own hubs, links to it are harvested from the other
23-  sources' captured pages (AP).
```

```
_CIK_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\s*\(CIK \d+\)\s*$")


def edgar_fts_hits(payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[EdgarHit]:
    """Rows of an efts.sec.gov search-index response; `_id` is '<accession>:<file name>'."""
    hits: list[EdgarHit] = []
    rows = payload.get("hits", {}).get("hits", [])
    for row in rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []:
        source = row.get("_source", {})
        adsh, _, filename = str(row.get("_id", "")).partition(":")
        ciks = source.get("ciks") or []
        if not adsh or not filename or not ciks:
            continue
        names = source.get("display_names") or [""]
        hits.append(
            EdgarHit(
                adsh=str(source.get("adsh") or adsh),
                filename=filename,
                cik=str(ciks[0]),
                file_type=str(source.get("file_type") or ""),
                file_date=source.get("file_date"),
                items=tuple(str(i) for i in source.get("items") or ()),
                company=normalize_text(_CIK_SUFFIX.sub("", str(names[0]))),
                description=normalize_text(str(source.get("file_description") or "")),
            )
        )
    return hits

def load_sources() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    text = resources.files("veritrade").joinpath("data/sources.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    sources: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = tomllib.loads(text)["sources"]
    return sources


def primary_sources(sources: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    registry = sources if sources is not None else load_sources()
    keys = [k for k, cfg in registry.items() if cfg.get("status") == "primary"]
    return sorted(keys, key=lambda k: int(registry[k].get("rank", 99)))


def source_archives(key: str, cfg: Mapping[str, Any], listing_urls: Sequence[str] = ()) -> list[Archive]:
    archives = [Archive("feed", url) for url in cfg.get("feeds", [])]
    archives += [Archive("listing", url) for url in cfg.get("sections", [])]
    archives += ARCHIVES.get(key, ())
    archives += [Archive("listing", url) for url in listing_urls]
    return archives
```

> 
> HARD RULES (verbatim intent):
> - Article text, headlines and snippets only via the Read tool on private files.
> - Never quote them in messages, notes or the final report.
> - No WebFetch/WebSearch/browser.
> - Python only via `uv run`, never inline Python.
> - Do not edit any code or committed file; do not commit; never git stash.
> - Never run prepare/ingest for label or adjudicate stages, finalize, verify, or --agreement.
> - Never touch other sources.
> - Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell (README rule 2).
> - Write outputs only to evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json.
> - Key facts and rationales in own words; no run of 10 consecutive words shared with the article.
> - Provisional label is an honest quick read with the 30-label.md rubric (when in doubt, neutral); never shade it to fill a quota.
> 
> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
> - Classes:
>   - bullish: material positive impact on the primary entity.
>   - bearish: material negative impact.
>   - neutral: routine or balanced news, or no clear direction.
> - Gold JSON schema:
>   - Fields: id, usable, reject_reason, title_line, body_ranges [[start,end]...], key_facts (3–5, ≤25 words each, numbers copied exactly from the body), entity, ticker, provisional_label.
>   - A rejected page needs only `{"id","usable":false,"reject_reason"}`.
>   - Reject reasons: not_article, live_blog, paywalled_stub, roundup, video_only, too_short (<120 body words), non_english, duplicate, other.
> - Ingest FAIL codes:
>   - key_fact_verbatim (10 consecutive shared words), key_fact_number_ungrounded, body_too_short.
>   - schema, range_out_of_bounds, title_in_body, and similar.
> - SEC packets: EX-99.1 exhibits.
>   - Usually no h1; the title line is the headline row (~6–21).
>   - Exclude page-number rows like "1", "2", "-2-" and footnotes.
>   - Some have fused headline/body/table lines; I rejected those as "other".
> - PR Newswire packets:
>   - h1 at L0427.
>   - Dateline lede ~L0435–L0440.
>   - Exclude dek bullets, About, safe harbor, contacts and call logistics.
> - Discovery details:
>   - EDGAR full-text search (--query) for sec; the view shows company names plus edgar_items, not headlines.
>   - PRN search results are often undated and many are law-firm ads or outside the window.
>   - PRN category listings via --listing-url (bankruptcy-list, earnings-forecasts-projections-list, restructuring-recapitalization-list) helped.
>   - `candidates --query` filters on title/slug text only.
> 
> 3. Files and Code Sections:
> - Read: evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md, 10-discover.md, 20-gold.md, 30-label.md; .context/docs/design/02-source-probe.md.
> - Read for config: evals/src/veritrade_evals/discovery.py.
>   - The ARCHIVES dict for prnewswire holds the sitemap, a paged earnings-list (10 pages), a paged news-releases-list (5 pages) and search (3 pages).
>   - `--listing-url` is action=append and adds a single "listing" archive.

```python
    @property
    def usable(self) -> bool:
        return self.ok and self.output is not None and self.output.usable


def _ranges(output: GoldOutput, n_lines: int) -> list[str]:
    codes: list[str] = []
    ranges = sorted(output.body_ranges)
    for start, end in ranges:
        if start > end:
            codes.append("range_inverted")
        elif start < 1 or end > n_lines:
            codes.append("range_out_of_bounds")
    if any(later[0] <= earlier[1] for earlier, later in pairwise(ranges)):
        codes.append("ranges_overlap")
    title = output.title_line
    if title is not None and not 1 <= title <= n_lines:
        codes.append("title_out_of_bounds")
    elif title is not None and any(start <= title <= end for start, end in ranges):
        codes.append("title_in_body")
    return sorted(set(codes))


def _key_facts(facts: Sequence[str], body: str) -> list[str]:
    codes: set[str] = set()
    if not KEY_FACTS_MIN <= len(facts) <= KEY_FACTS_MAX:
        codes.add("key_facts_count")
    grounded = number_set(body)
    body_runs = shingles(body)
    for fact in facts:
        if not fact.strip():
            codes.add("key_fact_empty")
        if word_count(fact) > KEY_FACT_MAX_WORDS:
            codes.add("key_fact_too_long")
        if not number_set(fact) <= grounded:
            codes.add("key_fact_number_ungrounded")
        if shares_run(fact, body_runs):
            codes.add("key_fact_verbatim")
    return sorted(codes)
```

```python
"""Checks on agent outputs: schema, line ranges, grounded numbers, no verbatim runs, label agreement."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from itertools import pairwise
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import ValidationError

from veritrade.inference.types import SENTIMENTS, Sentiment
from veritrade_evals.articles import (
    KEY_FACT_MAX_WORDS,
    KEY_FACTS_MAX,
    KEY_FACTS_MIN,
    MIN_BODY_WORDS,
    RATIONALE_MAX_WORDS,
    SHINGLE_WORDS,
    AdjudicateOutput,
    ArticlePaths,
    GoldOutput,
    LabelOutput,
    Stage,
    read_fetched,
    schema_codes,
)

_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d+(?:[.,]\d+)*")
_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.split())


def number_set(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Numbers as canonical decimals: thousands commas dropped, 1.50 == 1.5."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for match in _NUMBER.finditer(text):
        raw = match.group(0).replace(",", "")
        try:
            out.add(format(Decimal(raw).normalize(), "f"))
        except InvalidOperation:
            out.add(raw)
    return out


```

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```
````

````markdown
# 10 - Discover candidates for one source

You are the discovery agent for **one source** (its key is in the message that spawned you, for example `cnbc`).
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read titles only through the Read
tool on the private view file, never quote a headline or any article text in your messages or final report,
never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Goal

End with **at least 6 fetched articles per class** (bullish, bearish, neutral) for your source, published
between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-18, so that at least 5 per class survive the gold step. You judge the likely
class from the headline only; the real labels come later from independent labellers, so aim for clear cases.

A good candidate is one news story, press release or filing exhibit mainly about **one primary entity**: a
company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy. Skip live blogs, videos, galleries, opinion
roundups, newsletters, market wraps that list many stocks, "best stocks to buy" lists, quote pages, and law-firm
"class action" or "investor alert" releases (advertising, not issuer news).

What the classes mean (same rubric as the labellers, `30-label.md`): **bullish** = clear, material positive
economic impact on the primary entity (results or guidance above expectations, a major contract or approval, a
takeover at a premium); **bearish** = clear, material negative impact (results or guidance below expectations,
large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades, layoffs tied to weakness); **neutral** = no clear
material direction (scheduled announcements, routine appointments and dividends, conference-call notices,
explainers, balanced or minor news). Emotional wording is not a signal.

## Commands

All from the repository root. Output is ids, URLs, counts and paths only.

```bash
# 1. broad sweep with the source's feeds and deeper archives (sitemaps, archive pages, listings, EDGAR)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE

# 2. targeted sweeps: --query is a keyword search where the archive supports it (PR Newswire search,
#    EDGAR full-text search) and a headline/URL-slug filter everywhere else; repeat --query freely
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source SOURCE --query "lowered guidance" --query "net loss"

# 3. extra listing pages on the source's own domain (Yahoo quote news pages, section pages)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles discover --source yahoo \
  --listing-url https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TICKER/news/

# 4. write a compact private view (id, date, how found, query, EDGAR items, headline or slug) and Read it
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles candidates --source SOURCE --unfetched [--query WORD] [--limit 300]
#    -> evals/data/private/articles/views/SOURCE.tsv   (Read it with the Read tool; it is private)

# 5. fetch your picks through the serving fetcher; list ids one per line in a private file
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles fetch --source SOURCE --ids-file evals/data/private/articles/picks/SOURCE.txt

# progress for your source
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status --source SOURCE
```

Archive responses are cached for 6 hours, so repeating `discover` with new queries is cheap and polite.
`--pages N` deepens paged listings, search and EDGAR (default 3 to 40 depending on the archive).

## Query ideas

- Bearish: `lowered guidance`, `cuts forecast`, `profit warning`, `net loss`, `misses`, `downgrade`, `layoffs`,
  `recall`, `investigation`, `impairment`, `going concern`, `delisting`, `shares fall`, `plunge`, `default`.
- Bullish: `raises guidance`, `record revenue`, `beats`, `upgrade`, `to acquire`, `approval`, `contract`,
  `surges`, `dividend increase`, `buyback`.
- Neutral: `conference call`, `to present`, `appoints`, `annual meeting`, `declares quarterly dividend`,
  `launches`, `explainer`, `what to know`.

Source notes:

- **sec**: discovery uses EDGAR full-text search over 8-K filings and keeps the EX-99.1 exhibit. The view's
  `edgar_items` column helps: `2.02` is results of operations (earnings, either direction), `5.02` officer
  changes (usually neutral), `1.01` material agreements, `2.05`/`2.06` restructuring and impairments (often
  bearish), `8.01` other events. Search phrases such as `"third quarter"`, `net loss`, `record`, `lowered`.
- **prnewswire**, **globenewswire**: wires carry many non-US issuers and many law-firm ads; prefer issuer
  releases with numbers (results, guidance, deals). Bearish releases are rarer: search for losses, impairments,
  restructuring, going-concern and guidance cuts.
- **yahoo**, **bbc**, **cnn**, **guardian**: listings carry no or few dates; the publish date comes from the page
  at fetch time and out-of-window pages are dropped later, so prefer recent pages and check the fetch output.
- **fool**: much of the output is evergreen "should you buy" commentary; prefer news-driven articles about one
  company (earnings reactions, guidance, deals).

## Procedure

1. Run the broad sweep, then 2-4 targeted sweeps per class. Stop sweeping when the window holds plenty of
   plausible candidates per class (dozens), or after about 12 discover runs.
2. Write the view and Read it. Pick about **8 per class** (24 in total) by headline, preferring clear cases
   and a spread of companies. Put the ids, one per line, into
   `evals/data/private/articles/picks/<source>.txt` (create the folder if needed; only ids go in it).
3. Fetch them. For each printed line check: `ok` (not an error such as `source_blocked`, `paywalled`,
   `consent_required`, `upstream_http`), `words` of at least about 200, a `published` date inside the window, and
   `method` other than an `extract_error`. Replace failures with new picks and fetch again until you reach at
   least 6 good fetches per class.
4. Do not prepare packets, label or edit anything else; the main loop takes it from here.

## Final report (counts only, no headlines or article text)

- Fetched OK per intended class, and fetch errors by code.
- Which archive kinds and queries were productive (query strings are fine, they are yours).
- Any class that looks hard to fill for this source, and why in general terms.
````

````markdown
# 20 - Gold body, key facts and a provisional label

You turn fetched pages into reference ("gold") article bodies. The gold body is the yardstick for the
extraction benchmark (which parser and extractor recover the article best) and the text the labellers read.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read pages only with the Read tool
on the packet files you are given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/`, never quote article
text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

## Input

The message that spawned you lists gold packet paths, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/gold/<id>.md`.

A packet shows the page's visible text as numbered lines (`L0001 ...`), one per text block. Lines are
folded into marker rows that keep their numbers, for example `L0012-L0040 [29 lines hidden: short lines
(menus, buttons, tickers)]` or `L0001-L0140 [140 lines hidden: before the located article]`. Folding is only
for compactness: every line number stays valid. If the headline is not visible, the story looks cut off, or a
folded run might be part of the article (a short bulleted list), Read the full packet named in the header
(`<id>.full.md`), which shows every line.

## Decide: usable or not

Usable means one news story, press release or filing exhibit, in English, mainly about **one primary entity**
(a company, or a single asset, commodity, index or national economy), with at least 120 words of body text.
Otherwise set `usable: false` and one `reject_reason`:

| reject_reason | when |
|---|---|
| `not_article` | index or section page, quote page, data-only page, error, consent or login page |
| `live_blog` | rolling live coverage with timestamps |
| `paywalled_stub` | only a teaser; the rest is behind a wall |
| `roundup` | several unrelated items or companies with no primary entity (market wraps, newsletters, lists) |
| `video_only` | the story is a video with a caption |
| `too_short` | under 120 words of body text |
| `non_english` | not in English |
| `duplicate` | the same story as another packet in your batch (keep the better one) |
| `other` | anything else (say why in your final report, in general terms) |

## For usable pages

- `title_line`: the line holding the headline (normally the `h1` just above the story).
- `body_ranges`: inclusive `[start, end]` line ranges that together cover exactly the article body, in order and
  not overlapping. Include: the dateline lede, body paragraphs, in-body subheadings, bulleted or numbered lists
  that belong to the story, quotes. Exclude: the headline, standfirst or dek, editor key-points boxes, bylines,
  dates, image captions and credits, "read more" and related links, ads and their labels, newsletter and app
  promos, share buttons, author bios, comment prompts, financial tables, and press-release boilerplate after
  the story (About the company, forward-looking or safe-harbor statements, contacts, "SOURCE" lines, "View
  original content"). Split a range to skip a promo or a folded run of menu lines in the middle of a story.
  The title line must not fall inside a body range.
- `key_facts`: 3 to 5 statements, at most 25 words each, most market-moving first, in your own words. Copy
  numbers exactly as the body writes them ("$1.25 billion", "28%", "third quarter"), and only use numbers that
  appear in the body: no sums, differences or conversions. Never copy 10 or more consecutive words.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written ("Nvidia", "Brent crude", "UK economy").
- `ticker`: the ticker if the article states it or it is unambiguous, else `null`.
- `provisional_label`: your quick read with the rubric in `30-label.md` (bullish, bearish or neutral). It is
  only used to balance the selection; the real labels come from two independent labellers.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/gold/<id>.json` with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "usable": true,
  "reject_reason": null,
  "title_line": 41,
  "body_ranges": [[44, 61], [64, 70]],
  "key_facts": [
    "Fact in your own words with numbers copied exactly from the body.",
    "Second fact.",
    "Third fact."
  ],
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "provisional_label": "bearish"
}
```

For a rejected page: `{"id": "...", "usable": false, "reject_reason": "live_blog"}` (other fields may be
omitted).

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs of your batch, run:

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage gold
```

It prints one line per id: `PASS` (with your provisional label and the body word count, or `rejected:<reason>`)
or `FAIL` with codes. Fix every `FAIL` among your ids and run it again until they all pass.

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `schema:<field>:<type>` | field missing, misspelled, wrong type, or an unknown field |
| `missing:<field>` | usable outputs need `title_line`, `body_ranges`, `entity`, `provisional_label` |
| `range_inverted`, `range_out_of_bounds`, `ranges_overlap` | ranges must be `[start, end]`, start <= end, within the page, disjoint |
| `title_out_of_bounds`, `title_in_body` | the headline line must exist and sit outside the body ranges |
| `body_too_short` | under 120 words: widen the ranges if you cut too much, else reject as `too_short` |
| `key_facts_count`, `key_fact_too_long`, `key_fact_empty` | 3 to 5 facts, each 1 to 25 words |
| `key_fact_number_ungrounded` | a number in a fact does not appear in the body text; copy it exactly |
| `key_fact_verbatim` | a fact shares 10 consecutive words with the body; rephrase |
| `missing_packet_lines` | the packet was not prepared; tell the main loop |

## Final report (counts only)

Usable vs rejected (by reason), provisional labels (bullish / bearish / neutral), any ids that still fail
and their codes. No headlines, quotes or article text.
````
