```
import type { components } from "./api-schema";

type Schemas = components["schemas"];

export type SignalRequest = Schemas["SignalRequest"];
export type SummaryRequest = Schemas["SummaryRequest"];
export type AnalyzeRequest = Schemas["AnalyzeRequest"];
export type SignalResponse = Schemas["SignalResponse"];
export type SummaryResponse = Schemas["SummaryResponse"];
export type AnalyzeResponse = Schemas["AnalyzeResponse"];
export type ModelsResponse = Schemas["ModelsResponse"];
export type HealthResponse = Schemas["HealthResponse"];
export type ModelInfo = Schemas["ModelInfo"];
export type ArticleMeta = Schemas["ArticleMeta"];
export type SignalResult = Schemas["SignalResult"];
export type Timings = Schemas["Timings"];
export type InferenceTimings = Schemas["InferenceTimings"];
export type CacheInfo = Schemas["CacheInfo"];
export type ErrorBody = Schemas["ErrorBody"];
export type ErrorCode = Schemas["ErrorCode"];

export type ParserName = SignalRequest["parser"];
export type ExtractorName = SignalRequest["extractor"];
export type Scope = SignalRequest["scope"];
export type Endpoint = ArticleMeta["endpoint"];
export type Sentiment = SignalResult["sentiment"];
export type PolicyName = SignalResult["policy"];

// The generated request types mark defaulted fields as required; callers only need the url.
type Body<T extends { url: string }> = Pick<T, "url"> & Partial<Omit<T, "url">>;
export type SignalBody = Body<SignalRequest>;
export type SummaryBody = Body<SummaryRequest>;
export type AnalyzeBody = Body<AnalyzeRequest>;

export const PARSERS: readonly ParserName[] = ["selectolax", "lxml", "bs4", "bs4-lxml"];
export const EXTRACTORS: readonly ExtractorName[] = [
  "cascade",
  "jsonld",
  "profile",
  "density",
  "trafilatura",
  "trafilatura-precision",
  "readability",
  "newspaper",
  "justext",
  "strip-tags",
];
export const SCOPES: readonly Scope[] = ["lede", "full"];

const SERVER_ERROR_CODES: Record<ErrorCode, true> = {
  invalid_url: true,
  blocked_destination: true,
  model_not_allowed: true,
  paywalled: true,
  consent_required: true,
  extraction_empty: true,
  unsupported_content: true,
  too_large: true,
  source_blocked: true,
  upstream_http: true,
  schema_violation: true,
  model_unavailable: true,
  llm_unreachable: true,
  upstream_timeout: true,
  inference_timeout: true,
};
export const ERROR_CODES = Object.keys(SERVER_ERROR_CODES) as ErrorCode[];

/** Failures detected in the browser rather than reported by the API envelope. */
export type ClientErrorCode = "network_error" | "invalid_request" | "http_error" | "bad_response";
export type ApiErrorCode = ErrorCode | ClientErrorCode;

export function isErrorCode(value: unknown): value is ErrorCode {
  return typeof value === "string" && Object.hasOwn(SERVER_ERROR_CODES, value);
}

export interface ApiErrorInit {
  code: ApiErrorCode;
  message: string;
  hint?: string | null;
import type { ApiError, ArticleMeta, SignalResult, Timings } from "./api";

export type Mode = "split" | "combined";
export type LaneId = "signal" | "summary" | "analyze";
export type LaneStatus = "pending" | "streaming" | "done" | "error" | "cancelled";

export interface Lane {
  id: LaneId;
  status: LaneStatus;
  meta: ArticleMeta | null;
  timings: Timings | null;
  error: ApiError | null;
  // Client clock: milliseconds since the run started, from performance.now().
  signalAtMs: number | null;
  firstTokenAtMs: number | null;
  endAtMs: number | null;
}

export interface RunState {
  runId: number;
  mode: Mode;
  streaming: boolean;
  running: boolean;
  lanes: Lane[];
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity: string | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on the combined stream. */
  serverSignalMs: number | null;
  summary: string;
}

interface Tagged {
  runId: number;
  lane: LaneId;
  atMs: number;
}

export type RunAction =
  | { type: "start"; runId: number; mode: Mode; streaming: boolean; lanes: LaneId[] }
  | ({ type: "meta"; meta: ArticleMeta } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "signal"; signal: SignalResult; entity: string | null; serverMs: number | null } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "delta"; text: string } & Tagged)
  | ({
      type: "done";
      meta: ArticleMeta;
      timings: Timings;
      summary?: string;
      signal?: SignalResult;
      entity?: string | null;
    } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "error"; error: ApiError } & Tagged)
  | { type: "cancel"; runId: number; atMs: number };

export const initialRunState: RunState = {
  runId: 0,
  mode: "split",
  streaming: true,
  running: false,
  lanes: [],
  signal: null,
  entity: null,
  serverSignalMs: null,
  summary: "",
};

function newLane(id: LaneId): Lane {
  return {
    id,
    status: "pending",
    meta: null,
    timings: null,
    error: null,
    signalAtMs: null,
    firstTokenAtMs: null,
    endAtMs: null,
  };
}

const isActive = (lane: Lane) => lane.status === "pending" || lane.status === "streaming";

function patchLane(state: RunState, id: LaneId, patch: (lane: Lane) => Partial<Lane>): RunState {
  const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) => (lane.id === id ? { ...lane, ...patch(lane) } : lane));
  return { ...state, lanes, running: lanes.some(isActive) };
}

export function runReducer(state: RunState, action: RunAction): RunState {
  if (action.type === "start") {
    return {
      ...initialRunState,
      runId: action.runId,
      mode: action.mode,
      streaming: action.streaming,
      running: true,
      lanes: action.lanes.map(newLane),
    };
  }
  // Late events from a superseded run must not leak into the current one.
  if (action.runId !== state.runId) return state;

  switch (action.type) {
    case "meta":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        meta: lane.meta ?? action.meta,
        status: lane.status === "pending" ? "streaming" : lane.status,
      }));
    case "signal":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({ signalAtMs: lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs })),
        signal: action.signal,
        entity: action.entity,
        serverSignalMs: action.serverMs,
      };
    case "delta":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
          firstTokenAtMs: lane.firstTokenAtMs ?? action.atMs,
          status: "streaming",
        })),
        summary: state.summary + action.text,
      };
    case "done": {
      const next = patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        status: "done",
        meta: action.meta,
        timings: action.timings,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
        signalAtMs: action.signal ? (lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs) : lane.signalAtMs,
      }));
      return {
        ...next,
        // The final payload is authoritative over the concatenated deltas.
        summary: action.summary ?? next.summary,
        signal: action.signal ?? next.signal,
        entity: action.entity !== undefined ? action.entity : next.entity,
      };
    }
    case "error":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, () => ({
        status: "error",
        error: action.error,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
      }));
    case "cancel": {
      const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) =>
        isActive(lane) ? { ...lane, status: "cancelled" as const, endAtMs: action.atMs } : lane,
      );
      return { ...state, lanes, running: false };
    }
  }
}

export function laneById(state: RunState, id: LaneId): Lane | undefined {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.id === id);
}

/** Article-level meta from whichever lane reported first. */
export function articleMeta(state: RunState): ArticleMeta | null {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.meta)?.meta ?? null;
}

/** One banner per distinct failure; split lanes often fail identically on a shared fetch. */
export function distinctErrors(state: RunState): { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] {
  const out: { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] = [];
  for (const lane of state.lanes) {
    if (!lane.error) continue;
    const same = out.find((e) => e.error.code === lane.error?.code && e.error.message === lane.error.message);
    if (same) same.lanes.push(lane.id);
    else out.push({ lanes: [lane.id], error: lane.error });
  }
  return out;
```
```
}

export function AnalyzeApp() {
  const models = useModels();
  const { state, start, cancel } = useAnalysis();

  const split = state.mode === "split";
  const signalLane = laneById(state, split ? "signal" : "analyze");
  const summaryLane = laneById(state, split ? "summary" : "analyze");
  const meta = articleMeta(state);
  const errors = distinctErrors(state);
  const showLatency = state.lanes.some(
    (l) => l.timings || l.signalAtMs !== null || l.firstTokenAtMs !== null,
  );

  return (
    <>
      <AnalyzeForm models={models} running={state.running} onSubmit={start} onCancel={cancel} />

      <p role="status" className="visually-hidden">
        {announcement(state)}
      </p>

      {models.status === "error" ? <ErrorBanner error={models.error} context="Model list" /> : null}
      {errors.map(({ lanes, error }) => (
        <ErrorBanner
          key={`${error.code}-${lanes.join("-")}`}
          error={error}
          context={lanes.map((id) => LANE_LABELS[id]).join(" and ")}
        />
      ))}

      {state.lanes.length ? (
        <div className={styles.results}>
          {meta ? <ArticleMetaLine meta={meta} /> : null}
          <div className={styles.cards}>
            {signalLane ? (
              <SignalCard
                status={signalLane.status}
                signal={state.signal}
                entity={state.entity}
                model={signalLane.meta?.model}
                timeToSignalMs={signalLane.signalAtMs}
                serverMs={state.serverSignalMs}
              />
            ) : null}
            {summaryLane ? (
              <SummaryPanel
                status={summaryLane.status}
                text={state.summary}
                model={summaryLane.meta?.model}
                streaming={state.streaming}
                firstTokenMs={summaryLane.firstTokenAtMs}
              />
            ) : null}
          </div>
          {showLatency ? <LatencyBar lanes={state.lanes.map(toLatencyLane)} /> : null}

        <p className={styles.empty}>

          keeps streaming; combined mode gets both from one generation.
        </p>
```

```typescript
import { useCallback, useEffect, useReducer, useRef, type Dispatch } from "react";

import {
  ApiError,
  isAbortError,
  postAnalyze,
  postSignal,
  postSummary,
  toApiError,
  type AnalyzeBody,
  type AnalyzeResponse,
  type ExtractorName,
  type ParserName,
  type Scope,
  type SignalBody,
  type SummaryBody,
  type SummaryResponse,
} from "@/lib/api";
import { initialRunState, runReducer, type LaneId, type Mode, type RunAction } from "@/lib/run-state";
import { streamAnalyze, streamSummary, type StreamEvent } from "@/lib/sse";

export interface RunParams {
  url: string;
  mode: Mode;
  streaming: boolean;
  parser: ParserName;
  extractor: ExtractorName;
  /** Signal scope in split mode; /analyze keeps its server default. */
  scope: Scope;
  /** Empty string lets the server pick the endpoint default. */
  signalModel: string;
  summaryModel: string;
  analyzeModel: string;
}

interface LaneContext {
  runId: number;
  dispatch: Dispatch<RunAction>;
  signal: AbortSignal;
  at: () => number;
}

const withModel = (model: string) => (model ? { model } : {});

async function guarded(ctx: LaneContext, lane: LaneId, work: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await work();
  } catch (err) {
    if (ctx.signal.aborted || isAbortError(err)) return;
    ctx.dispatch({ type: "error", runId: ctx.runId, lane, atMs: ctx.at(), error: toApiError(err) });
  }
}

function handleEvent(
  ctx: LaneContext,
  lane: LaneId,
  event: StreamEvent<SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse>,
): void {
  const tag = { runId: ctx.runId, lane, atMs: ctx.at() };
  switch (event.type) {
    case "meta":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "meta", ...tag, meta: event.data.meta });
      return;
    case "sentiment":
      ctx.dispatch({
        type: "signal",
        ...tag,
        signal: event.data.signal,
        entity: event.data.entity ?? null,
        serverMs: event.data.elapsed_ms,
      });
      return;
    case "summary_delta":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "delta", ...tag, text: event.data.text });
      return;
    case "done": {
      const result = event.data.result;
      const combined = "signal" in result ? result : null;
      ctx.dispatch({
        type: "done",
        ...tag,
        meta: result.meta,
        timings: result.timings,
        summary: result.summary,
        signal: combined?.signal,
        entity: combined ? (combined.entity ?? null) : undefined,
      });
      return;
    }
    case "error":
      ctx.dispatch({ type: "error", ...tag, error: ApiError.fromBody(event.data.error) });
      return;
  }
}

function runSignal(ctx: LaneContext, body: SignalBody) {
  return guarded(ctx, "signal", async () => {
    const res = await postSignal(body, ctx.signal);
    ctx.dispatch({
      type: "done",
      runId: ctx.runId,
      lane: "signal",
      atMs: ctx.at(),
      meta: res.meta,
      timings: res.timings,
      signal: res.signal,
    });
  });
}

function runSummary(ctx: LaneContext, body: SummaryBody, streaming: boolean) {
  return guarded(ctx, "summary", async () => {
    if (streaming) {
      for await (const event of streamSummary(body, { signal: ctx.signal }))
        handleEvent(ctx, "summary", event);
      return;
    }
    const res = await postSummary(body, ctx.signal);
    handleEvent(ctx, "summary", { type: "done", data: { result: res } });
  });
}

function runAnalyze(ctx: LaneContext, body: AnalyzeBody, streaming: boolean) {
  return guarded(ctx, "analyze", async () => {
    if (streaming) {
      for await (const event of streamAnalyze(body, { signal: ctx.signal }))
        handleEvent(ctx, "analyze", event);
      return;
    }
    const res = await postAnalyze(body, ctx.signal);
    handleEvent(ctx, "analyze", { type: "done", data: { result: res } });
  });
}

/** Owns one in-flight run; starting a new run aborts the previous one. */
export function useAnalysis() {
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(runReducer, initialRunState);
  const controllerRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null);
  const runIdRef = useRef(0);
  const startedAtRef = useRef(0);

  useEffect(() => () => controllerRef.current?.abort(), []);

  const start = useCallback((params: RunParams) => {
    controllerRef.current?.abort();
    const controller = new AbortController();
    controllerRef.current = controller;
    const runId = ++runIdRef.current;
    const t0 = performance.now();
    startedAtRef.current = t0;
    const ctx: LaneContext = { runId, dispatch, signal: controller.signal, at: () => performance.now() - t0 };
    const base = { url: params.url, parser: params.parser, extractor: params.extractor };

    if (params.mode === "split") {
      dispatch({
        type: "start",
        runId,
        mode: "split",
        streaming: params.streaming,
        lanes: ["signal", "summary"],
      });
      // Fired together on purpose: the backend single-flight shares one fetch between them.
      void runSignal(ctx, { ...base, scope: params.scope, ...withModel(params.signalModel) });
      void runSummary(ctx, { ...base, ...withModel(params.summaryModel) }, params.streaming);
    } else {
      dispatch({ type: "start", runId, mode: "combined", streaming: params.streaming, lanes: ["analyze"] });
      void runAnalyze(ctx, { ...base, ...withModel(params.analyzeModel) }, params.streaming);
    }
  }, []);

  const cancel = useCallback(() => {
    controllerRef.current?.abort();
    controllerRef.current = null;
    dispatch({ type: "cancel", runId: runIdRef.current, atMs: performance.now() - startedAtRef.current });
  }, []);

  return { state, start, cancel };
}
```

```
"""Single quality gate for local runs and CI: lint, types, tests, build and contract drift."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FRONTEND = ROOT / "frontend"


def backend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    backend_tests = "backend/tests" if full else "backend/tests/unit"
    tests = [backend_tests, "evals/tests", "scripts/tests"]
    steps = [
        ("ruff", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "."], ROOT),
        ("ruff-format", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", "."], ROOT),
        ("mypy", ["uv", "run", "mypy"], ROOT),
        ("openapi-drift", ["uv", "run", "python", "scripts/export_openapi.py", "--check"], ROOT),
        ("pytest", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q", *[t for t in tests if (ROOT / t).exists()]], ROOT),
    ]
    # The floor only means something once the API is wired and integration tests exist.
    if full and (ROOT / "backend" / "tests" / "integration").exists():
        steps[-1][1].extend(["--cov", "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered", "--cov-fail-under=75"])
    return steps


def frontend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    steps = [
        ("fe-lint", ["pnpm", "lint"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-format", ["pnpm", "format:check"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-typecheck", ["pnpm", "typecheck"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-test", ["pnpm", "test"], FRONTEND),
    ]
    if full:
        steps.append(("fe-build", ["pnpm", "build"], FRONTEND))
    return steps


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--fast", action="store_true", help="unit tests only, no build (default)")
    mode.add_argument("--full", action="store_true", help="integration tests, coverage floor, build")
    parser.add_argument("--backend", action="store_true", help="only backend + evals")
    parser.add_argument("--frontend", action="store_true", help="only frontend")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    run_be = not args.frontend or args.backend
    run_fe = not args.backend or args.frontend
    steps = (backend_steps(args.full) if run_be else []) + (frontend_steps(args.full) if run_fe else [])

    failed = []
    for name, cmd, cwd in steps:
        print(f"\n== {name}: {' '.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
        if subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd).returncode != 0:
            failed.append(name)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"\nFAILED: {', '.join(failed)}")
    print("\nall checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { SignalCard, leaning } from "@/components/SignalCard";
import type { SignalResult } from "@/lib/api";

const decision: SignalResult = {
  sentiment: "bearish",
  abstained: false,
  policy: "probability",
  confidence: 0.71,
  probabilities: { bullish: 0.09, bearish: 0.71, neutral: 0.2 },
};

describe("SignalCard", () => {
  it("renders the badge, confidence, probabilities, policy and timing", () => {
    render(<SignalCard status="done" signal={decision} model="nimble:9b-q4_K_M" timeToSignalMs={412.4} />);
    const badge = screen.getByTestId("signal-badge");
    expect(badge).toHaveTextContent("Bearish");
    expect(badge).toHaveAttribute("data-sentiment", "bearish");
    expect(screen.queryByText("Abstained")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("Confidence").nextSibling).toHaveTextContent("71.0%");
    expect(screen.getByText("probability")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("nimble:9b-q4_K_M")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("Time to signal").nextSibling).toHaveTextContent("412 ms");

    const probs = within(screen.getByRole("list", { name: "Class probabilities" })).getAllByRole("listitem");
    expect(probs.map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(["Bullish9.0%", "Bearish71.0%", "Neutral20.0%"]);
  });

  it("explains an abstained call as below the confidence threshold", () => {
    const abstained: SignalResult = {
      sentiment: "neutral",
      abstained: true,
      policy: "probability",
      confidence: 0.44,
      probabilities: { bullish: 0.44, bearish: 0.2, neutral: 0.36 },
    };
    render(<SignalCard status="done" signal={abstained} />);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveTextContent("Neutral");
    expect(screen.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveAttribute("data-abstained", "true");
    expect(screen.getByText("Abstained")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(/below confidence threshold/i)).toHaveTextContent("The model leaned Bullish.");
  });

  it("shows the ordinal score with its sign and the server timing", () => {
    const ordinal: SignalResult = { sentiment: "bullish", abstained: false, policy: "ordinal", score: 1 };
    render(
      <SignalCard status="streaming" signal={ordinal} entity="Acme" timeToSignalMs={800} serverMs={742} />,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText("Score").nextSibling).toHaveTextContent("+1 on -2..+2");
    expect(screen.getByText("Acme")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("Time to signal").nextSibling).toHaveTextContent("800 ms (server 742 ms)");
  });

  it("shows waiting, failed and cancelled states without a signal", () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<SignalCard status="pending" signal={null} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole("region", { name: "Signal" })).toHaveAttribute("aria-busy", "true");
    expect(screen.getByText(/waiting for the signal/i)).toBeInTheDocument();
    rerender(<SignalCard status="error" signal={null} />);
```

```
"""Write backend/openapi.json from the FastAPI app; --check fails on drift (CI contract gate)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from veritrade.api.app import create_app
from veritrade.config import Settings

TARGET = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "backend" / "openapi.json"


def render() -> str:
    app = create_app(Settings(static_dir=None))
    return json.dumps(app.openapi(), indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    rendered = render()
    if args.check:
        if not TARGET.exists() or TARGET.read_text() != rendered:
            sys.exit("backend/openapi.json is stale: run `uv run python scripts/export_openapi.py`")
        print("openapi.json up to date")
        return
    TARGET.write_text(rendered)
    print(f"wrote {TARGET}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
from __future__ import annotations

import json

import httpx

from veritrade.api.contracts import MetaEvent, SummaryDeltaEvent, SummaryDoneEvent, SummaryResponse

from .fakes import SUMMARY, FakeOllama, Page, sse_events


async def test_summary_json(api: httpx.AsyncClient, ollama: FakeOllama, page: Page) -> None:
    response = await api.post("/api/summary", json={"url": page.url})
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    body = SummaryResponse.model_validate(response.json())
    assert body.summary == SUMMARY
    assert (body.meta.endpoint, body.meta.scope, body.meta.model, body.meta.field_order) == (
        "summary",
        "full",
        "fake-label:1b",
        None,
    )
    assert body.timings.inference is not None
    assert body.timings.inference.ttft_ms is None
    assert body.timings.inference.eval_tokens == 40
    sent = json.loads(ollama.chat.calls.last.request.content)
    assert list(sent["format"]["properties"]) == ["summary"]
    assert page.body_markers[-1] in sent["messages"][-1]["content"]


async def test_summary_stream_event_order(api: httpx.AsyncClient, page: Page) -> None:
    response = await api.post("/api/summary/stream", json={"url": page.url})
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    assert response.headers["content-type"].startswith("text/event-stream")
    assert response.headers["cache-control"] == "no-cache"
    assert response.headers["x-accel-buffering"] == "no"
    events = sse_events(response.text)
    names = [name for name, _ in events]
    assert names[0] == "meta"
    assert names[-1] == "done"
    assert set(names[1:-1]) == {"summary_delta"}
    assert len(names) > 3, "the summary should arrive in several deltas"

    meta = MetaEvent.model_validate(events[0][1])
    assert (meta.meta.endpoint, meta.cache.fetch, meta.cache.result) == ("summary", "miss", "miss")
    text = "".join(SummaryDeltaEvent.model_validate(data).text for _, data in events[1:-1])
    done = SummaryDoneEvent.model_validate(events[-1][1]).result
    assert text == done.summary == SUMMARY
    assert done.meta == meta.meta
    inference = done.timings.inference
    assert inference is not None
    assert inference.ttft_ms is not None
    assert meta.fetch_ms <= inference.ttft_ms <= done.timings.total_ms
from __future__ import annotations

import json

import httpx
import pytest

from veritrade.api.contracts import AnalyzeDoneEvent, AnalyzeResponse, SentimentEvent, SummaryDeltaEvent

from .fakes import ENTITY, SUMMARY, FakeOllama, Page, sse_events


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("model", "field_order", "properties"),
    [
        ("fake-label:1b", "sentiment-first", ["score", "entity", "summary"]),
        ("fake-ordinal:1b", "summary-first", ["summary", "entity", "score"]),
    ],
)
async def test_analyze_json(
    api: httpx.AsyncClient,
    ollama: FakeOllama,
    page: Page,
    model: str,
    field_order: str,
    properties: list[str],
) -> None:
    ollama.score = 2
    response = await api.post("/api/analyze", json={"url": page.url, "model": model})
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    body = AnalyzeResponse.model_validate(response.json())
    assert (body.signal.sentiment, body.signal.score, body.signal.policy) == ("bullish", 2, "ordinal")
    assert (body.entity, body.summary) == (ENTITY, SUMMARY)
    assert (body.meta.endpoint, body.meta.scope, body.meta.field_order) == ("analyze", "full", field_order)
    sent = json.loads(ollama.chat.calls.last.request.content)
    assert list(sent["format"]["properties"]) == properties
    assert sent["options"]["num_predict"] == 200


async def test_sentiment_first_stream_sends_the_signal_before_any_text(
    api: httpx.AsyncClient, page: Page
) -> None:
    response = await api.post("/api/analyze/stream", json={"url": page.url, "model": "fake-label:1b"})
    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    events = sse_events(response.text)
    names = [name for name, _ in events]
    assert names[:2] == ["meta", "sentiment"]
    assert set(names[2:-1]) == {"summary_delta"}
    assert names[-1] == "done"

    sentiment = SentimentEvent.model_validate(events[1][1])
    done = AnalyzeDoneEvent.model_validate(events[-1][1]).result
    assert sentiment.signal == done.signal
    assert (sentiment.signal.sentiment, sentiment.signal.score) == ("bullish", 1)
    # The entity is generated after the score, so it only arrives with `done`.
    assert (sentiment.entity, done.entity) == (None, ENTITY)
    assert (
        "".join(SummaryDeltaEvent.model_validate(d).text for n, d in events if n == "summary_delta")
        == SUMMARY
    )
    assert done.timings.inference is not None
    assert done.timings.inference.ttft_ms is not None
    assert sentiment.elapsed_ms <= done.timings.inference.ttft_ms <= done.timings.total_ms


async def test_summary_first_stream_sends_the_signal_after_the_text(
    api: httpx.AsyncClient, page: Page
) -> None:
    response = await api.post("/api/analyze/stream", json={"url": page.url, "model": "fake-ordinal:1b"})
    events = sse_events(response.text)
    names = [name for name, _ in events]
    assert names[0] == "meta"
    assert names[-2:] == ["sentiment", "done"]
    assert set(names[1:-2]) == {"summary_delta"}

    sentiment = SentimentEvent.model_validate(events[-2][1])
    done = AnalyzeDoneEvent.model_validate(events[-1][1]).result
    assert sentiment.entity == ENTITY
    assert sentiment.signal == done.signal
    assert done.meta.field_order == "summary-first"
    assert done.timings.inference is not None
    assert done.timings.inference.ttft_ms is not None
    assert done.timings.inference.ttft_ms <= sentiment.elapsed_ms
```

```python
def _validate[T: BaseModel](out_type: type[T], content: str, model: str) -> T:
    try:
        return out_type.model_validate_json(content)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise SchemaViolation(
            f"{model} streamed output that does not match {out_type.__name__}", hint=str(exc)[:300]
        ) from exc


def cut_to_sentence(text: str) -> str:
    """The text up to its last complete sentence, or all of it when no sentence has ended."""
    match = _COMPLETE_SENTENCES.match(text)
    return (match.group(1) if match else text).strip()


def _salvage(spec: ModelSpec, endpoint: Endpoint, chat: ChatResult) -> tuple[int | None, str, str]:
    """Score, entity and sentence-cut summary decoded from JSON that num_predict cut off."""
    log.warning(
        "%s output from %s hit num_predict after %s eval tokens; salvaging the partial JSON",
        endpoint,
        spec.name,
        chat.timings.eval_tokens,
    )
    score: int | None = None
    entity = ""
    parts: list[str] = []
    for event in JsonFieldScanner().feed(chat.content):
        match event:
            case ScoreClosed(score=value):
                score = value
            case EntityClosed(entity=value):
                entity = value
            case SummaryText(delta=delta):
                parts.append(delta)
    summary = cut_to_sentence("".join(parts))
    if not summary:
        raise SchemaViolation(f"{spec.name} reached its output token limit before writing a summary")
    return score, entity, summary


def _salvage_summary(spec: ModelSpec, chat: ChatResult) -> SummaryResult:
    _, _, summary = _salvage(spec, "summary", chat)
    return SummaryResult(SummaryOut(summary=summary), chat, truncated=True)


def _salvage_analyze(
    spec: ModelSpec, out_type: type[AnalyzeSentimentFirst] | type[AnalyzeSummaryFirst], chat: ChatResult
) -> AnalyzeResult:
    """A cut generation still needs its score; summary-first output cut before it stays a violation."""
    score, entity, summary = _salvage(spec, "analyze", chat)
    if score is None:
        raise SchemaViolation(f"{spec.name} reached its output token limit before writing the score")
    out = out_type.model_validate({"score": score, "entity": entity, "summary": summary})
    return AnalyzeResult(out, score_verdict(spec, out.score), chat, truncated=True)


def _was_cut(chat: ChatResult, scanner: JsonFieldScanner) -> bool:
    return chat.done_reason == "length" and not scanner.done


async def summarize(client: OllamaClient, spec: ModelSpec, prompt: PromptSpec, text: str) -> SummaryResult:
    messages = prompt.messages(fit_input(text, spec.max_input_tokens), "default")
    try:
        out, chat = await client.chat_json(
            spec.name, messages, SummaryOut, options=chat_options(spec, "summary"), retry_cut=False
        )
    except OutputTruncated as cut:
        return _salvage_summary(spec, cut.chat)
    return SummaryResult(out, chat)
```

```python
"""Output cut at num_predict: salvaged, sentence-cut and flagged instead of retried or rejected."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from typing import Any

import httpx
import pytest
import respx

from veritrade.errors import SchemaViolation
from veritrade.inference.adapters import (
    AnalyzeResult,
    SummaryResult,
    analyze,
    analyze_stream,
    cut_to_sentence,
    summarize,
    summarize_stream,
)
from veritrade.inference.incremental import ScoreClosed, SummaryText
from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec
from veritrade.prompts import registry as prompts

from .conftest import chat_body, content_chunks, stream_response

ARTICLE = "Acme Corp cut its full-year guidance after demand slowed."


def _cut(content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return chat_body(content, done_reason="length", eval_count=160)


def _sent(route: respx.Route, index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    body: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(route.calls[index].request.content)
    return body


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "expected"),
    [
        ("Acme rose 5%. Shares fell 2% in ear", "Acme rose 5%."),
        ('Acme hailed "record demand." Shares', 'Acme hailed "record demand."'),
        ("Is it over? Not yet! Analysts", "Is it over? Not yet!"),
        ("Sales grew.\nRevenue rose 3.", "Sales grew."),
        ("Revenue rose 3.", "Revenue rose 3."),
        ("No sentence has ended yet", "No sentence has ended yet"),
        ("  ", ""),
    ],
)
def test_cut_to_sentence(text: str, expected: str) -> None:
    assert cut_to_sentence(text) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("content", "summary"),
    [
        ('{"summary": "Acme cut guidance. Shares sl', "Acme cut guidance."),
        ('{"summary": "Acme cut guidance. Analysts called it \\', "Acme cut guidance."),
        ('{"summary": "Acme cut guidance. Analysts saw \\u00', "Acme cut guidance."),
        ('{"summary": "Acme \\"slashed\\" guidance after dem', 'Acme "slashed" guidance after dem'),
    ],
    ids=["in-string", "in-escape", "in-unicode-escape", "no-complete-sentence"],
)
async def test_summary_cut_at_the_limit_is_salvaged_without_a_retry(
    client: OllamaClient,
    mock_ollama: respx.MockRouter,
    ordinal_spec: ModelSpec,
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    content: str,
    summary: str,
) -> None:
    route = mock_ollama.post("/api/chat").respond(json=_cut(content))
```

```
async def test_ollama_failures(
    api: httpx.AsyncClient,
    ollama: FakeOllama,
    page: Page,
    failure: httpx.Response | Exception,
    status: int,
    code: str,
) -> None:
    _chat_fails(failure)(ollama.router, ollama)
    for path in ("/api/signal", "/api/summary", "/api/analyze"):
        response = await api.post(path, json={"url": page.url})
        assert response.status_code == status, (path, response.text)
        assert ErrorResponse.model_validate(response.json()).error.code == code


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ["/api/summary/stream", "/api/analyze/stream"])
async def test_stream_failures_before_the_first_byte_are_json(
    api: httpx.AsyncClient, router: respx.MockRouter, path: str
) -> None:
    router.get(BLOCKED_URL).respond(403, html=CHALLENGE_HTML, headers={"cf-mitigated": "challenge"})
    response = await api.post(path, json={"url": BLOCKED_URL})
    assert response.status_code == 502
    assert response.headers["content-type"] == "application/json"
    assert ErrorResponse.model_validate(response.json()).error.code == "source_blocked"

    response = await api.post(path, json={"url": BLOCKED_URL, "model": "gpt-9"})
    assert (response.status_code, response.json()["error"]["code"]) == (400, "model_not_allowed")

    retry = SummaryResponse.model_validate((await api.post("/api/summary", json={"url": page.url})).json())
    assert retry.timings.cache.result == "miss"
```

```
import { HttpResponse } from "msw";

import type { StreamEventType } from "@/lib/sse";

export function sseFrame(event: StreamEventType, data: unknown): string {
  return `event: ${event}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(data)}\n\n`;
}

export const SSE_PING = ": ping\n\n";

/** Pull-based so a test can hold the stream open between chunks (e.g. awaiting a gate). */
export function sseStream(chunks: AsyncIterable<string> | Iterable<string>): ReadableStream<Uint8Array> {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const iterator =
    Symbol.asyncIterator in chunks ? chunks[Symbol.asyncIterator]() : toAsync(chunks[Symbol.iterator]());
  return new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    async pull(controller) {
      const { value, done } = await iterator.next();
      if (done) controller.close();
      else controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(value));
    },
    async cancel() {
      await iterator.return?.();
    },
  });
}

function toAsync(iterator: Iterator<string>): AsyncIterator<string> {
  return { next: async () => iterator.next() };
}

export function sseResponse(chunks: AsyncIterable<string> | Iterable<string>): HttpResponse<ReadableStream> {
  return new HttpResponse(sseStream(chunks), {
    headers: { "Content-Type": "text/event-stream", "Cache-Control": "no-cache" },
  });
}

export interface Gate {
  promise: Promise<void>;
  open: () => void;
}

export function gate(): Gate {
  let open: () => void = () => undefined;
  const promise = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    open = resolve;
  });
  return { promise, open };
}
```

```typescript
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { SummaryPanel } from "@/components/SummaryPanel";

const TEXT = "Acme Corp cut its full-year guidance.";

describe("SummaryPanel", () => {
  it("notes a summary the server cut at the model's output limit", () => {
    render(<SummaryPanel status="done" text={TEXT} truncated streaming model="qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0" />);

    expect(screen.getByTestId("summary-truncated")).toHaveTextContent(/output limit.*cut short/);
  });

  it("shows no note for a complete summary or when there is no text", () => {

    rerender(<SummaryPanel status="done" text="" truncated streaming />);
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("summary-truncated")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("The model returned an empty summary.")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

```python
"""Live /api/summary check against a running app: prints status, truncated flag and error code only."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import httpx

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PROBE = ROOT / "evals" / "data" / "source_probe.json"
ARTICLE = re.compile(r"^https://www\.theguardian\.com/.+/\d{4}/[a-z]{3}/\d{2}/")


def guardian_urls(node: Any, found: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        for key, value in node.items():
            if key == "url" and isinstance(value, str) and ARTICLE.match(value) and value not in found:
                found.append(value)
            else:
                guardian_urls(value, found)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            guardian_urls(item, found)
    return found


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base", default="http://127.0.0.1:8010")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0")
    parser.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", default="/api/summary")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    urls = guardian_urls(json.loads(PROBE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), [])[: args.count]
    with httpx.Client(base_url=args.base, timeout=180.0) as client:
        for url in urls:
            response = client.post(args.endpoint, json={"url": url, "model": args.model, "no_cache": True})
            body = response.json()
            inference = (body.get("timings") or {}).get("inference") or {}
            print(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "url": url,
                        "endpoint": args.endpoint,
                        "status": response.status_code,
                        "truncated": body.get("truncated"),
                        "error_code": (body.get("error") or {}).get("code"),
                        "eval_tokens": inference.get("eval_tokens"),
                    }
                )
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

> Summary and analyze outputs that hit the model's output token limit are now salvaged and flagged instead of failing with 502. The full gate (`uv run python scripts/check.py --full`) passes, and a live call on a cut article returned 200 with `truncated: true`.
> 
> **How it behaves**
> - A cut summary is trimmed back to its last complete sentence. A sentence only counts as complete if whitespace follows the full stop, so a cut like "3." inside "3.5" is never kept. If no sentence ended, the partial text is kept.
> - Analyze is salvaged only if the score was already produced. Summary-first output cut before the score, or any output with no summary text, is still a schema violation.
> - A cut output is not retried. Malformed JSON that ended normally still gets one retry on the same token budget. Signal calls keep their old doubled-budget retry.
> - Streams behave the same way: the `done` event carries the cut summary and the flag. Cached replays keep the flag.
> - One warning line is logged per cut generation, with endpoint, model and eval tokens.
> 
> **Files outside the list you gave me**
> - `backend/src/veritrade/inference/types.py`: `ChatResult` gained `done_reason`. The streaming path needs it, and the default keeps existing callers working.

### 🤖 Assistant: *The Docker/e2e agent hit a real serving bug…*

`15:35:35`

> The Docker/e2e agent hit a real serving bug, and a fix is underway.
> 
> **The problem:** when a model hits its output token limit, the JSON is cut off mid-string. The API then retried with double the token budget and, if that failed too, returned a 502.
> - `qwen3.5:0.8b` tends to copy the article and overrun the limit. On the CPU container, summaries failed on 6 of the 10 test pages, and one real Guardian article failed as well.
> - In those failures the score, entity and most of the summary had already been generated, so the 502 threw away a usable answer.
> - The retry also doubled the worst-case latency.
> 
> **The fix:** a new agent will keep what was generated: the score and entity, with the summary cut back to its last complete sentence. The response will say so with a `truncated: true` flag, and the UI will show a small note. It also drops the retry that doubled the token budget; malformed JSON that ended normally still gets one retry.
> 
> I didn't raise the token limit, because that raises worst-case latency for any model that rambles. The agent will add unit and integration tests and run one live check.
> 
> I told the Docker and grid agents which files the fix touches so they stay off them. Until it lands, e2e uses the CNN test page, which passes. Docker itself checks out: the native setup, the bundled setup and the e2e stack all work.
> 
> Still running: workflow A (finding and gold-annotating articles), the eval grid, Docker/e2e, and the truncation fix.

```
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ArticlePaths:
    private: Path = PRIVATE_ARTICLES_DIR
    committed: Path = ARTICLES_DIR

    def candidates(self, source: str) -> Path:
        return self.private / "candidates" / f"{source}.jsonl"
        return date.fromisoformat(self.published_at) if self.published_at else None


class FetchRecord(_Model):
    id: str
    source: str
    url: str
    final_url: str | None = None
    fetched_at: str
    status: int | None = None
    error: str | None = None
    html_sha256: str | None = None
    words: int = 0
    method: str | None = None
    published_at: str | None = None
    published_date: str | None = None
    published_from: Literal["page", "candidate"] | None = None
    paywalled: bool = False
    extract_error: str | None = None

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return self.error is None and self.html_sha256 is not None

    @property
    def published(self) -> date | None:
        return date.fromisoformat(self.published_date) if self.published_date else None


# --- agent outputs (documented in evals/opus_prompts) ---------------------------------------------------


class GoldOutput(_Model):
    id: str
    usable: bool
    reject_reason: RejectReason | None = None
    title_line: int | None = None
    body_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    key_facts: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    entity: str | None = None
    ticker: str | None = None
    provisional_label: Sentiment | None = None


class LabelOutput(_Model):
    id: str
    label: Sentiment
    score: int = Field(ge=-2, le=2)
    entity: str = Field(min_length=1)
    ticker: str | None = None
    rationale: str = Field(min_length=1)
    ambiguous: bool
    confidence: int = Field(ge=1, le=5)


class AdjudicateOutput(_Model):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def read_fetched(paths: ArticlePaths, article: str) -> FetchRecord | None:
    path = paths.fetched(article)
    return FetchRecord.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if path.exists() else None


def iter_fetched(paths: ArticlePaths, source: str | None = None) -> Iterator[FetchRecord]:
    folder = paths.private / "fetched"
    for path in sorted(folder.glob("art-*.json")) if folder.exists() else []:
        record = FetchRecord.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if source is None or record.source == source:
            yield record


def in_window(day: date | None, since: date = WINDOW_START, until: date = REFERENCE_DATE) -> bool:
    return day is not None and since <= day <= until
```

```python
"""Seeded pick of up to N usable, in-window gold articles per source x provisional label for labelling.

Prints counts only; ids go to private files: label_ids.txt plus two batches split evenly per cell.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import random
from collections import defaultdict

from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, GoldOutput, in_window, iter_fetched

LABELS = ("bullish", "bearish", "neutral")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--per-cell", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261018)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    paths = ArticlePaths()
    cells: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for record in iter_fetched(paths):
        out_path = paths.out("gold", record.id)
        if not (record.ok and in_window(record.published) and out_path.exists() and paths.gold(record.id).exists()):
            continue
        gold = GoldOutput.model_validate_json(out_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if gold.usable and gold.provisional_label:
            cells[(record.source, gold.provisional_label)].append(record.id)

    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    chosen: list[str] = []
    batches: tuple[list[str], list[str]] = ([], [])
    sources = sorted({source for source, _ in cells})
    print(f"{'source':14} " + " ".join(f"{label:>8}" for label in LABELS) + "   (picked/available)")
    for source in sources:
        row = []
        for label in LABELS:
            ids = sorted(cells.get((source, label), []))
            rng.shuffle(ids)
            picked = ids[: args.per_cell]
            chosen.extend(picked)
            for i, article in enumerate(picked):
                batches[i % 2].append(article)
            row.append(f"{len(picked)}/{len(ids)}")
        print(f"{source:14} " + " ".join(f"{cell:>8}" for cell in row))

    base = paths.private
    (base / "label_ids.txt").write_text("\n".join(chosen) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for n, batch in enumerate(batches, start=1):
        (base / f"label_batch_{n}.txt").write_text("\n".join(batch) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"total {len(chosen)}; batch sizes {len(batches[0])} / {len(batches[1])}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````
