````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
# 40 - Adjudicate disagreements and ambiguous articles

You resolve the articles where the two labellers disagreed or at least one flagged the article as ambiguous.
The message that spawned you lists adjudication packets, `evals/data/private/articles/packets/adjudicate/<id>.md`.
Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read
tool on the packets you were given, write only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/`, never quote
article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only through `uv run`.

A packet holds both labellers' outputs (label, score, entity, ticker, ambiguous flag, confidence, rationale)
followed by the headline and article body, the same text they read. Do not open other files.

## Rubric

Use exactly the rubric in `evals/opus_prompts/30-label.md`: the economic impact of the news on its primary
entity, not the tone; bullish or bearish only for a clear, material implication; mixed news follows the
dominant material driver, or neutral if balanced. Form your own reading from the article first, then weigh
the two rationales as arguments, not votes.

## Decide

- `keep`: the article has one defensible label under the rubric, and the disagreement came from a misreading,
  a materiality threshold, or a different primary entity that the article settles. Your label, score, entity
  and ticker become final.
- `replace`: the article stays genuinely ambiguous: balanced mixed news, no clear primary entity, materiality
  that depends on facts the article does not give, or a direction a careful analyst could reasonably dispute.
  Replaced articles leave the set and the main loop finds others. The set is only useful if its labels are
  defensible, so do not keep an article just to fill a quota.

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/adjudicate/<id>.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "decision": "keep",
  "label": "neutral",
  "score": 0,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": null,
  "rationale": "Your own words, at most 50: why this label, and what settled the disagreement."
}
```

For `replace`, still give your best label and score (their sign must agree) and say in the rationale why the
article is too ambiguous to keep.

## Validate and fix

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage adjudicate
```

Fix every `FAIL`: `schema:<field>:<type>`, `score_label_mismatch`, `rationale_too_long`, `rationale_verbatim`
(rephrase), `not_requested` (the id is not in `adjudicate_ids.txt`; tell the main loop), `gold_missing`.
Do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Kept by final label, replaced, and for kept articles whether you sided with labeller A, labeller B or neither.
No headlines, quotes or article text.

````
</details>

```python
"""Reserve pick for a refill round: usable, in-window gold not yet labelled, for given source:label cells.

Prints counts only; ids go to evals/data/private/articles/refill_ids.txt.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, GoldOutput, in_window, iter_fetched


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("cells", nargs="+", help="source:label, e.g. bbc:bearish")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    wanted = {tuple(cell.split(":", 1)) for cell in args.cells}

    paths = ArticlePaths()
    labelled = set((paths.private / "label_ids.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split())
    picked: list[str] = []
    for record in iter_fetched(paths):
        out_path = paths.out("gold", record.id)
        if record.id in labelled or not (record.ok and in_window(record.published) and out_path.exists()):
            continue
        if not paths.gold(record.id).exists():
            continue
        gold = GoldOutput.model_validate_json(out_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if gold.usable and (record.source, gold.provisional_label) in wanted:
            picked.append(record.id)
            print(f"{record.source}:{gold.provisional_label}")

    (paths.private / "refill_ids.txt").write_text("\n".join(picked) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"total {len(picked)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

````markdown
# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify` and `ingest --agreement`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```

````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

````markdown
An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.

1. Article text, headlines, snippets and raw HTML live only under `evals/data/private/` (gitignored).
2. Read article text only with the Read tool, and only from the private files your prompt names (packets, and
   for discovery the candidates view). Do not grep, cat or print article files in a shell.
3. Write your outputs only to `evals/data/private/articles/out/<stage>/<id>.json`.
4. Never quote article text, headlines or snippets in messages, final reports, file names or committed files.
   Refer to articles by id (`art-` + 12 hex characters) and to sources by key. Key facts and rationales are
   written in your own words; the CLI rejects any that share a run of 10 consecutive words with the article.
5. Never use WebFetch, WebSearch or a browser on publisher pages. All fetching goes through the CLI, which uses
   the serving fetcher (SSRF guard, consent handling), honours robots.txt and waits at least 1 s between
   requests to one domain (EDGAR: 5 requests per second with a declared contact user agent).
6. Python only through `uv run ...` from the repository root; no inline Python.

## Private layout (`evals/data/private/articles/`)

| Path | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates/<source>.jsonl` | `discover` | id, url, title, published date, how it was found |
| `views/<source>.tsv` | `candidates` | compact id / date / title-or-slug view for an agent to Read |
| `html/<id>.html`, `fetched/<id>.json` | `fetch` | raw page; status, words, extraction method, publish date |
| `packets/gold/<id>.md`, `<id>.full.md`, `<id>.lines.json` | `prepare --stage gold` | numbered page lines |
| `packets/label/<id>.md`, `packets/adjudicate/<id>.md` | `prepare` | headline + gold body (+ both labels) |
| `out/{gold,label_a,label_b,adjudicate}/<id>.json` | agents | outputs, schemas in the stage prompts |
| `gold/<id>.txt` | `ingest --stage gold` | the validated gold body |
| `adjudicate_ids.txt` | `ingest --stage label_*` | ids where the labellers disagree or one is unsure |
| `cache/`, `discovery_log.jsonl` | `discover` | archive responses (6 h), per-run archive counts |

## Main-loop runbook

```bash
# 1. discovery agents (one per source, 10-discover.md), then check the counts
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles status

# 2. gold
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage gold
#    spawn gold agents over batches of packet paths (20-gold.md); they run `ingest --stage gold` themselves

# 3. labels (the two labellers never see each other's outputs or the provisional label)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage label
#    spawn labeller A and labeller B over the same packet list (30-label.md)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_b --agreement   # writes adjudicate_ids.txt

# 4. adjudication
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles prepare --stage adjudicate
#    spawn the adjudicator (40-adjudicate.md)

# 5. refill short cells, then
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles finalize
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles verify
```
````

````markdown
# 30 - Label an article (labeller A or labeller B)

You are one of two independent labellers. The message that spawned you says whether you are **labeller A**
(write to `out/label_a/`) or **labeller B** (write to `out/label_b/`), and lists label packet paths,
`evals/data/private/articles/packets/label/<id>.md`. Read `evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md` first; its rules
bind you. In short: read articles only with the Read tool on the packets you were given, write only to your own
output folder, never quote article text or headlines in messages or your final report, and run Python only
through `uv run`.

## Independence

Your label must be your own reading of the article. Do not open anything under
`evals/data/private/articles/out/` except your own outputs, nor gold, adjudication or full packets, candidates,
fetch records or HTML. Do not look up the company, its share price or later events; judge the article as of its
publication. A packet holds an id, the headline and the article body (long articles are cut at a paragraph
boundary after about 1,200 words; a note says how much is not shown).

## Rubric (the same one the service's prompts use)

Judge the **economic impact of the news on its primary entity** (the company or asset the article is mainly
about), not the emotional tone of the writing.

- **bullish**: a clear, material positive implication for the entity's value, for example results or guidance
  above expectations, a major contract or approval, a takeover offer at a premium.
- **bearish**: a clear, material negative implication, for example results or guidance below expectations,
  large losses, investigations, recalls, defaults, downgrades.
- **neutral**: no clear material direction: routine or scheduled announcements, commentary without new facts,
  minor news.

Mixed news follows the dominant material driver; if positives and negatives are balanced, choose neutral.
Dramatic or emotional wording is not a signal, and neither is the outlet's general mood about the market.
Only call bullish or bearish when the implication is both clear and material; when in doubt, neutral.

## Fields

- `label`: `bullish`, `bearish` or `neutral`.
- `score`: an integer from -2 to 2 whose sign matches the label (0 if and only if neutral).
  2 = major, unambiguous positive news; 1 = clear but moderate positive implication; 0 = no clear material
  direction (routine, minor or balanced news); -1 = clear but moderate negative implication; -2 = major,
  unambiguous negative news.
- `entity`: the primary entity as commonly written. `ticker`: the ticker if stated or unambiguous, else `null`.
- `rationale`: at most 50 words, your own words, naming the driver of your call. No quotes; never 10 or more
  consecutive words from the article.
- `ambiguous`: `true` when a careful analyst could reasonably pick a different class: genuinely mixed news,
  unclear materiality, no clear primary entity, or a story whose direction depends on facts it does not give.
  Ambiguous articles go to an adjudicator, so flag honestly rather than forcing a call.
- `confidence`: 1 (guess) to 5 (certain).

## Output

Write `evals/data/private/articles/out/label_a/<id>.json` (labeller A) or `.../out/label_b/<id>.json`
(labeller B):

```json
{
  "id": "art-0123456789ab",
  "label": "bearish",
  "score": -1,
  "entity": "Example Corp",
  "ticker": "EXMP",
  "rationale": "Your own words: the driver and why it is material.",
  "ambiguous": false,
  "confidence": 4
}
```

## Validate and fix

After writing all outputs, run the ingest for your stage (`label_a` or `label_b`):

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles ingest --stage label_a
```

Fix every `FAIL` among your ids: `schema:<field>:<type>` (missing or wrong field), `score_label_mismatch`
(the score's sign must match the label, 0 only for neutral), `rationale_too_long` (over 50 words),
`rationale_verbatim` (10 consecutive words shared with the article; rephrase), `gold_missing` (tell the main
loop). Do not pass `--agreement` and do not run `articles status`.

## Final report (counts only)

Labels by class, how many you flagged ambiguous, mean confidence, any ids that still fail. No headlines,
quotes or article text.

````

> ## Deviations and why
> - **Network aliases instead of a static IP plus extra_hosts:** no fixed subnet that could clash with other Docker networks.
> - **Fixture URLs use http://** because the fixture site has no TLS.
> - **Host-side VT_MODELS instead of OLLAMA_MODELS:** OLLAMA_MODELS is Ollama's own model-directory variable, so a reviewer who has it set would have injected a path as the allowlist.
> - **`profiles: !reset []` in compose.e2e.yaml:** the e2e command does not need `--profile`.
> - **Ollama models mounted at /root/.ollama/models:** the CI cache then excludes Ollama's root-only key. The pull script skips models already in the store, so cached runs work offline.
> - **bundled.env pulls only qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0:** tev1 is CI-only and unevaluated.
> - **Removed the `# syntax=` line:** the Docker Hub lookup timed out once, and the built-in frontend supports the mounts.
> - **Disk cleanup only runs below 25 GB free:** the runner already had 104 GB free, and the cleanup cost 173 s.

```markdown
# Signal grid on dev300

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.grid analyze` from the local prediction cache; no dataset text is stored here.

- Data: dev300, 300 Twitter Financial News train tweets, 100 per class; every rate is weighted back to the train prior (bullish 20.2%, bearish 15.1%, neutral 64.7%). Confusion and error counts are raw.
- Selection: F0.5 macro over bullish/bearish; operating point = best F0.5 with bullish<->bearish inversions <= 2% of directional calls; below the threshold the call abstains to neutral.
- Policies: decision models threshold native class probabilities (min_p); generative /signal thresholds first-token label probabilities (label schema) or the |score| of an ordinal -2..2 schema (t in {1, 2}); /analyze is streamed sentiment-first and always uses |score|.
- Decoding: Ollama options temperature=0, seed=0, presence_penalty=0, frequency_penalty=0, repeat_penalty=1 on every generative call (greedy; overrides the penalties some Modelfiles ship).
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000) at the chosen threshold; the threshold choice itself is not resampled, so these are optimistic.
- Latency: per-call wall ms during the grid run (Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal, warm, client concurrency 1); /analyze is time to the score with the stream stopped there. Indicative only: the latency suite runs separately.

## Not served yet: directional-mass threshold

The serving policies abstain only when the winning class is unsure, so a model that keeps most of its mass on neutral is never pushed into a call. This informational policy calls bullish or bearish whenever that class's probability clears tau, even when neutral is the argmax. It is tuned on the same 300 tweets as everything else here (gap: paired bootstrap against the serving best config).
```

```
"""Single entry point from HTML to Article; parse and extract time are measured separately."""

from __future__ import annotations

import html as html_lib
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from veritrade.errors import ExtractionEmpty
from veritrade.extract import cascade, density, jsonld, profiles, third_party
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, head_title, normalize, parse, scan_json_ld
from veritrade.extract.profiles import source_for_url
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS, Article, ExtractorName, ParserName

__all__ = ["MIN_WORDS", "extract", "source_for_url"]

MIN_WORDS = 40

OWN: dict[ExtractorName, Callable[[Dom, str, str | None], list[str]]] = {
    "jsonld": jsonld.extract,
    "profile": profiles.extract,
    "density": density.extract,
}
_PUBLISHED_META = re.compile(
    r"""<meta\b[^>]*?(?:property|name|itemprop)\s*=\s*["']"""
    r"""(?:article:published_time|datePublished|pubdate|publishdate)["'][^>]*>""",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_CONTENT_ATTR = re.compile(r"""\bcontent\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.IGNORECASE)


def _published_meta(html: str) -> str | None:
    if (meta := _PUBLISHED_META.search(html)) and (content := _CONTENT_ATTR.search(meta.group(0))):
        return normalize(html_lib.unescape(content.group(1) or content.group(2) or "")) or None
    return None


def _dom_title(dom: Dom, source: str | None) -> str:
    profile = profiles.profile_for(source)
    if profile is not None and profile.title:
        for node in dom.select(profile.title):
            if text := node.text():
                return text
    return dom.title()


def extract(
    html: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax",
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade",
) -> Article:
    """Raises ExtractionEmpty when fewer than MIN_WORDS words come out."""
    source = source_for_url(url)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    dom: Dom | None = None
    if extractor in PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS:
        dom = parse(html, parser)
        if extractor == "cascade":
            method, paragraphs = cascade.run(dom, url, source)
        else:
            method, paragraphs = extractor, OWN[extractor](dom, url, source)
        objects = dom.json_ld()
    else:
        method, paragraphs = extractor, third_party.extract(extractor, html, url)
        objects = scan_json_ld(html)
    words = sum(len(p.split()) for p in paragraphs)
    if words < MIN_WORDS:
        raise ExtractionEmpty(
            f"The {extractor} extractor found {words} words on {urlsplit(url).hostname or url}; "
            f"at least {MIN_WORDS} are needed",
            hint="Try another extractor (for example trafilatura), or check that the URL is a single "
            "article rather than a section or video page.",
        )
    title = jsonld.headline(objects) or (_dom_title(dom, source) if dom is not None else head_title(html))
    published_at = jsonld.date_published(objects) or _published_meta(html)
    total_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    parse_ms = dom.parse_ms if dom is not None else 0.0
    return Article(
        url=url,
        title=title,
        paragraphs=tuple(paragraphs),
        published_at=published_at,
        source=source,
        method=method,
        parser=parser if dom is not None else None,
        extractor=extractor,
        parse_ms=parse_ms,
        extract_ms=total_ms - parse_ms,
        paywalled=jsonld.is_paywalled(objects),
    )
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal, get_args

ParserName = Literal["selectolax", "lxml", "bs4", "bs4-lxml"]
ExtractorName = Literal[
    "cascade",
    "jsonld",
    "profile",
    "density",
    "trafilatura",
    "trafilatura-precision",
    "readability",
    "newspaper",
    "justext",
    "strip-tags",
]
Scope = Literal["lede", "full"]

PARSERS: tuple[ParserName, ...] = get_args(ParserName)
EXTRACTORS: tuple[ExtractorName, ...] = get_args(ExtractorName)
# Own strategies run on every parser backend; third-party extractors bring their own parser.
PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS: frozenset[ExtractorName] = frozenset({"cascade", "jsonld", "profile", "density"})


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Article:
    url: str
    title: str
    paragraphs: tuple[str, ...]
    published_at: str | None
    source: str | None
    method: str
    parser: ParserName | None
    extractor: ExtractorName
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    paywalled: bool = False

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return "\n\n".join(self.paragraphs)

    @property
    def word_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(len(p.split()) for p in self.paragraphs)
"""What the model reads: the headline plus the lede or the whole body, cut to a token budget."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Sequence

from veritrade.extract.dom import split_sentences
from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for
from veritrade.extract.types import Article, Scope

CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
LEDE_PARAGRAPHS = 2
LEDE_MIN_TOKENS = 60  # a dateline-only first paragraph is topped up with the next one
LEDE_MAX_TOKENS = 200
_SEP = "\n\n"


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return math.ceil(len(text) / CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def lede_paragraphs(article: Article) -> list[str]:
    profile = profile_for(article.source)
    count = profile.lede_paragraphs if profile else LEDE_PARAGRAPHS
    out = list(article.paragraphs[:count])
    for paragraph in article.paragraphs[count:]:
        if estimate_tokens(_SEP.join(out)) >= LEDE_MIN_TOKENS:
            break
        out.append(paragraph)
    return out


def _cut(paragraph: str, room: int, *, mid_sentence: bool) -> str:
    kept = ""
    for sentence in split_sentences(paragraph):
        candidate = f"{kept} {sentence}" if kept else sentence
        if len(candidate) > room:
            break
        kept = candidate
    if kept or not mid_sentence:
        return kept
    head = paragraph[: room + 1]
    return head[:room] if " " not in head else head.rsplit(" ", 1)[0]


def fit(paragraphs: Sequence[str], budget_chars: int) -> list[str]:
    """Whole paragraphs, then whole sentences; words are cut only when not even one sentence fits."""
    out: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for paragraph in paragraphs:
        sep = len(_SEP) if out else 0
        if used + sep + len(paragraph) <= budget_chars:
            out.append(paragraph)
            used += sep + len(paragraph)
            continue
        if partial := _cut(paragraph, budget_chars - used - sep, mid_sentence=not out):
            out.append(partial)
        break
    return out


def build_input(article: Article, scope: Scope, max_tokens: int) -> str:
    """'TITLE: ...' then a blank line and the body; the estimate (chars / 4) never exceeds max_tokens."""
    if max_tokens <= 0:
        raise ValueError("max_tokens must be positive")
    budget = max_tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN
    head = f"TITLE: {article.title}" if article.title else ""
    if len(head) > budget:
        return _SEP.join(fit([head], budget))
    room = budget - len(head) - (len(_SEP) if head else 0)
    if scope == "lede":
        body = fit(lede_paragraphs(article), min(room, LEDE_MAX_TOKENS * CHARS_PER_TOKEN))
    else:
        body = fit(article.paragraphs, room)
    return _SEP.join([head, *body] if head else body)
"""Off-the-shelf extractors behind one signature; each is imported on first use and brings its own parser."""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from collections.abc import Callable

from veritrade.extract.dom import normalize, parse, strip_xml_declaration
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName


def _lines(text: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return [line for raw in (text or "").splitlines() if (line := normalize(raw))]


def _trafilatura(html: str, url: str, *, precision: bool) -> list[str]:
    import trafilatura

    text = trafilatura.extract(
        html,
        url=url,
        favor_precision=precision,
        include_comments=False,
        include_tables=False,
        deduplicate=False,
        with_metadata=False,
        output_format="txt",
    )
    return _lines(text)


def _readability(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    from readability import Document

    fragment = Document(strip_xml_declaration(html), url=url).summary(html_partial=True)
    return [block.text for block in parse(fragment, "lxml").iter_blocks()]


def _newspaper(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        # Import-time notice about the optional NLP extra, which plain text extraction never uses.
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        from newspaper import Article

    # Parse the given HTML only: no download, no image probing, no on-disk URL memo.
    article = Article(
        url, language="en", fetch_images=False, follow_meta_refresh=False, memorize_articles=False
    )
    article.download(input_html=html)
    article.parse()
    return _lines(article.text)


def _justext(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    import justext

    found = justext.justext(html.encode("utf-8"), justext.get_stoplist("English"), encoding="utf-8")
    return [text for p in found if not p.is_boilerplate and (text := normalize(p.text))]


def _strip_tags(html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    """Baseline: every visible text run on the page, scripts and styles removed."""
    return [block.text for block in parse(html, "selectolax").iter_blocks()]


ADAPTERS: dict[ExtractorName, Callable[[str, str], list[str]]] = {
    "trafilatura": lambda html, url: _trafilatura(html, url, precision=False),
    "trafilatura-precision": lambda html, url: _trafilatura(html, url, precision=True),
    "readability": _readability,
    "newspaper": _newspaper,
    "justext": _justext,
    "strip-tags": _strip_tags,
}


def extract(name: ExtractorName, html: str, url: str) -> list[str]:
    return ADAPTERS[name](html, url)
"""Cheapest trustworthy strategy first: JSON-LD, then the source profile, then text density."""

from __future__ import annotations

from veritrade.extract import density, jsonld, profiles
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom

JSONLD_MIN_CHARS = 400
PROFILE_MIN_WORDS = 80


def _words(paragraphs: list[str]) -> int:
    return sum(len(p.split()) for p in paragraphs)


def run(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """(winning method, paragraphs); a JSON-LD hit returns before the DOM is ever built."""
    tried: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    body = jsonld.extract(dom, url, source_key)
    if sum(len(p) for p in body) >= JSONLD_MIN_CHARS:
        return "jsonld", body
    tried.append(("jsonld", body))
    if profiles.profile_for(source_key) is not None:
        body = profiles.extract(dom, url, source_key)
        if _words(body) >= PROFILE_MIN_WORDS:
            return "profile", body
        tried.append(("profile", body))
    tried.append(("density", density.extract(dom, url, source_key)))
    # A short release beats an empty density pass; ties go to the more specific method.
    return max(tried, key=lambda item: _words(item[1]))


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return run(dom, url, source_key)[1]
"""HTML to Article. Entry points: `registry.extract`, `registry.source_for_url`, `scope.build_input`.

Kept import-free so `extract.types`, which the API contract imports, does not pull in the parsers.
"""
```

````
## Build-time findings that adjusted the plan

Measured during P1/P2, recorded here so the deviations are traceable. Inputs for the Ollama probe were synthetic
(`evals/results/ollama_probe.json`, native Metal, warm, n=5).

- **Sources** (`02-source-probe.md`): AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
  their CDN (Cloudflare / Akamai), so all four backups were promoted. Final 10: Yahoo Finance, CNBC, Motley Fool,
  PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune, Guardian Business, BBC Business.
- **R7 sanity gate passed**: each endpoint has at least one candidate inside its budget, so no budget moved.
  - `/signal`: `qwen3.5:0.8b` answers in 190 ms at ~510 prompt tokens. The 9B decision models take 1.3-1.5 s
    at the same size, so they are reported against the budget rather than the budget relaxed for them.
  - `/summary`: `qwen3.5:2b` shows first text at 0.93 s and finishes at 2.2 s on ~1.6k-token articles;
    `qwen3.5:4b` misses the 1.5 s TTFT budget at that size (2.4 s).
  - `/analyze`: `ministral-3:3b` reaches the score at 1.47 s and finishes at 3.5 s on ~1.75k tokens; the 4B
    qwen models miss TTFT at full-article size.
- **Logprobs**: Ollama 0.40.6 also returns logprobs on streamed chunks (undocumented). The knob comparison stays
  on non-streaming `/signal`; `/analyze` keeps the ordinal knob. Logprob-weighted streaming confidence goes to
  the backlog.
- **Field order**: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` ignores schema property order (always entity, score, summary) and
  ignores `think:false` when a schema is set, so the field-order dimension runs on `qwen3.5:4b` and
  `ministral-3:3b` only.
- **Fetch cap** raised from 5 MB to 10 MB: CNN article pages are 5.7-6.6 MB decompressed.
- **Sampling penalties zeroed**: the qwen3.5 Modelfiles ship `presence_penalty 1.5`, which still applies under
  greedy decoding. Few-shot answers end in `neutral` / `0`, so the penalty pushed generated labels away from
  neutral (26 of 60 dev tweets disagreed with the logprob argmax; 0 of 60 with the penalty off). Every chat call
  now pins `presence_penalty 0`, `frequency_penalty 0`, `repeat_penalty 1`; `num_predict` still bounds runaway
  output.
# 02 - Source probe

Question (Q18, Q19): which of the 14 candidate publishers can a plain Python client fetch, with no evasion,
and what do the extractors need to know about each one? The answer is measured, not assumed:
`scripts/probe_sources.py` fetched every candidate live on 2026-10-18 and its output decided
`backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml`.

## Method

- **Client**: `httpx 0.28.1` `AsyncClient`, HTTP/2, the Chrome 155 desktop header set from
  `veritrade.fetch.headers` (UA, Accept, `Accept-Language: en-US`, client hints, `Sec-Fetch-*`,
  `Upgrade-Insecure-Requests`, `Priority`), `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` because `brotli` is installed.
  `sec.gov` gets the declared `SEC_USER_AGENT` and no Chrome hints. No cookies are pre-seeded, no TLS
  impersonation, headless browser, proxy or captcha solving (Q19).
- **Redirects**: followed by hand (max 5), exactly as the serving fetcher will; a hop to Yahoo's consent hosts is
  answered once with reject-all (`veritrade.fetch.consent`) and the original URL retried.
- **Politeness**: one request at a time per registrable domain with at least 1 s between them; EDGAR at 5 req/s
  (half its 10 req/s fair-access ceiling). Reported fetch times exclude these waits.
- **Discovery**: each source's `feeds` (RSS/Atom, non-English `dc:language` items skipped) or `sections`
  (HTML pages and sitemaps), filtered by `article_pattern`; the 3 newest matches are probed. EDGAR resolves the
  8-K Atom feed to filing indexes and then to the EX-99.1 exhibit, preferring index descriptions that say press
  release, earnings or results. When a source refuses its own hubs, links to it are harvested from the other
  sources' captured pages (AP).
- **Per article** (all in `evals/data/source_probe.json`, metadata only): status, final URL, redirects, bytes,
  network ms, `detect.classify` outcome and time, JSON-LD types / `articleBody` words / `isAccessibleForFree` /
  `hasPart` selectors, framework JSON markers, ranked body-container candidates with paragraph and word counts
  under both parsers, noise blocks inside the best container (selectors only) and press-release boilerplate
  labels (label and position only). Raw HTML goes to `evals/data/private/probe/<source>/<n>.html` (gitignored).
- **Profile check**: every `[sources.<key>.profile]` is applied with selectolax (Lexbor) and lxml `cssselect`;
  it passes when both parsers keep the same paragraphs in the same order (non-whitespace characters within 1%)
  and the body has at least 120 words. `--reanalyze` reruns all analysis on the saved HTML without network,
  which is how the profiles were tuned.

## Results

Vantage: residential ISP in Bulgaria (EU), macOS, Sunday 2026-10-18. Fetch ms is network time per article
(median, max of 3); size is the median HTML size.

| Source | Discovery used | OK | Fetch ms | Size | JSON-LD NewsArticle / articleBody | `isAccessibleForFree` | Blocks, consent | Profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yahoo Finance | `/topic/stock-market-news/` page (RSS now 404) | 3/3 | 477 (575) | 682 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none; no consent redirect | 3/3 |
| CNBC | RSS `id/100003114` | 3/3 | 161 (221) | 838 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| Motley Fool | RSS `foolwatch` | 3/3 | 202 (235) | 372 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| PR Newswire | RSS financial services | 3/3 | 34 (43) | 219 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| GlobeNewswire | RSS public companies | 3/3 | 552 (662) | 74 KB | 3 / 0 | true | none | 3/3 |
| SEC 8-K EX-99.1 | Atom, 25 indexes, 2 releases + 1 statement | 3/3 | 135 (538) | 19 KB | 0 / 0 | absent | none (declared UA) | 3/3 |
| CNN Business | `edition.cnn.com/business` page (no RSS) | 3/3 | 35 (50) | 5.7 MB | 3 / 3 | false, full text served | none; www redirects to edition for EU | 3/3 |

Every response came over HTTP/2 and no article URL redirected. One PR Newswire release took 6.8 s on a cache
miss during an earlier run, close to the 8 s fetch deadline.

## Decision

Final 10 (`status = "primary"`, `rank` in `sources.toml`), plan order with backups swapped in for the
rejected sources:

1. Yahoo Finance
2. CNBC
3. The Motley Fool
4. PR Newswire
5. GlobeNewswire
6. SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1
7. CNN Business
8. Fortune (replaces AP News)
9. The Guardian Business (replaces Investing.com)
10. BBC Business (replaces Benzinga)

The mix is 7 news outlets, 2 press-release wires and 1 regulatory filing source. **No backups remain**: the
fourth backup, Business Wire, is blocked too. If a primary degrades, rerun the probe with `--only` on the
candidates and promote from there.

Rejected (`status = "rejected"`, `reason` in `sources.toml`): AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga, Business Wire,
all refused at the CDN (Cloudflare or Akamai) before any content is served. These outlets are syndicated
widely, so `detect.py` answers a block with a hint that points at the syndicated copy (usually Yahoo Finance).

## Yahoo EU consent

- From this IP, `finance.yahoo.com`, `yahoo.com/news`, `uk.finance.yahoo.com` and `de.yahoo.com` served content
  directly with no consent redirect. The pages carry `"gdpr":true` and a client-side CMP
  (`consent.cmp.oath.com`), so in October 2026 the server-side wall no longer stands in front of articles.
- The server-side flow still exists at `guce.yahoo.com/consent` -> `consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent`, so the
  probe exercises it on every run (`yahoo_consent_check` in the JSON): `consent.reject_all` posted the
  reject-all form in 857 ms and the jar received `A1`, `A1S`, `CFC`, `EuConsent`, `GUC`. Decoding the TCF v2
  string in `EuConsent` gives **0 of 24 purposes consented**, which confirms that reject-all was recorded and
  accept-all was never sent. A second pass with the same jar skips the form (about 120 ms, no POST).
- Serving contract: when a redirect lands on a consent host, the fetcher calls `reject_all` with its SSRF
  guard and retries the original URL once; if that lands on the wall again, `detect.classify` raises
  `consent_required` with a hint.

## Block, consent and paywall detection

`detect.classify(status, headers, html, final_url)` is pure and string-based, so it runs on every fetch.

| Signal | Raised as |
|---|---|
| Final URL on `consent.yahoo.com` / `guce.yahoo.com`, or a Yahoo consent form in the page | `consent_required` |
| HTTP 401, 403, 429 (retryable), 451 | `source_blocked`, naming the CDN edge from `server` / `cf-ray` |
| Cloudflare: `cf-mitigated: challenge`, "Just a moment...", `_cf_chl_opt`, `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/`, "Attention Required! \| Cloudflare" | `source_blocked` |
| DataDome `captcha-delivery.com` or `x-dd-b`; PerimeterX `px-captcha` or "Press & Hold"; Akamai "Access Denied" + "Reference #", `sec-if-cpt-container`, `errors.edgesuite.net`; Imperva `_Incapsula_Resource` | `source_blocked`, including when served with HTTP 200 |
| JSON-LD `isAccessibleForFree` false (bool or string) and both the JSON-LD `articleBody` and the visible `<p>` text under 200 words | `paywalled` |

Design points the probe forced:

- Cloudflare's passive `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/scripts/jsd/main.js` beacon sits on normal pages, so only
  the interactive `/h/` path counts. `x-datadome` alone is ignored because DataDome sets it on allowed responses.
- Markers are only searched in the first 64 KB: interstitials are a few KB, and it keeps 6 MB CNN pages cheap.
  Over all 42 captured pages `classify` takes at most 1.7 ms (CNN, 5.8 MB) and under 1 ms everywhere else
  (median of 5 runs).
- CNN and Fortune declare `isAccessibleForFree: false` yet serve the whole article (their walls are
  client-side), which is why a not-free flag alone is never treated as a paywall.
- Hints are keyed by host suffix: Reuters, AP, Business Wire and Benzinga blocks point to the syndicated copy on
  Yahoo Finance; WSJ, Barron's, FT and Bloomberg paywalls point to free sources.

## What the extractors get

Profile semantics (documented at the top of `sources.toml`): remove `drop` selectors, take `body` matches in
document order, ignore paragraphs under `min_words`, then cut at the first paragraph after the lede that starts
with a `stop_markers` prefix. All selectors use only tag, class, id, attribute and descendant parts; GlobeNewswire
also uses a selector list for `p, li`. All 30 primary pages pass the two-parser check.

Findings that are not visible in the selectors:

- **JSON-LD `articleBody` exists only on CNN** (3/3). Everywhere else the cascade has to fall through to the
  profile or density strategy. No source ships `__NEXT_DATA__`; Fool and Fortune use the Next.js flight stream
  and Yahoo SvelteKit, neither worth parsing for the body.
- **Text joining differs between parsers**: selectolax `text(separator=" ")` splits words at inline tags (drop
  caps become "R ogue", "Fla. ,"), while lxml `text_content()` glues text across `<br>` ("WangEmail"). Joining
  text nodes without a separator, with spaces only at `<br>` and block boundaries, gives the same text on both.
- **Press releases** end with an "About <issuer>" heading, forward-looking statements and contacts as plain
  paragraphs, so they are cut with stop markers, not selectors. The "About" check only applies after the lede.
- **SEC exhibits** arrive wrapped in the EDGAR SGML envelope, with no `h1`, JSON-LD or containers, and start with
  "Exhibit 99.1" and the issuer name. Some filer agents emit `div`/`span` text without `<p>`, which this profile
  cannot read; the cascade must fall back to density there. EX-99.1 is sometimes a financial statement (11.6k
  words in one sample), which `scope=lede` and the token cap absorb.
- **Yahoo** stories are mostly partner copy (Motley Fool, Insider Monkey, 24/7 Wall St, named in `providerId`)
  and partner promos survive inside the body; the second half of the text sits in a hidden "Story continues"
  block that must be kept.
- **CNBC** has editor-written Key Points (`div.RenderKeyPoints-list li`) outside the body, a ready-made lede.
- **CNN** pages are 5.7 MB, so DOM parsing is the slow step there; the JSON-LD strategy avoids it.

## Caveats

- One vantage point. Bot management depends on IP reputation: GitHub Actions runners use US datacenter IPs that
  Cloudflare and Akamai treat more strictly, and US visitors see different geo behaviour (no Yahoo consent at
  all, `www.cnn.com`, `bbc.com`). CI therefore runs on skeleton fixtures; the weekly live smoke is informational.
- Three articles per source on a Sunday: the wires were dominated by non-US issuers, and only 2 of the 25 newest
  8-K filing indexes had an EX-99.1 described as a press release.
- Blocking decisions drift over time and with request rate; the probe stayed at or under 1 request per second per
  domain. The Business Wire `/newsroom` challenge was seen while exploring and is not in the final JSON, because
  discovery uses its MRSS feed.
- AP's article URLs were harvested from other publishers' pages because its own hubs and sitemaps are blocked.
- A Chrome TLS fingerprint might get past Cloudflare for AP, Benzinga and Investing.com. That is evasion, which
  Q19 rules out.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --vantage "EU (Bulgaria) residential ISP"   # live, about 2 minutes
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --only cnbc,bbc                               # re-probe some sources
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --reanalyze                                   # re-score saved HTML offline
```
````
