```
"""Per-source profiles from sources.toml and the paragraph rules every own strategy applies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import tomllib
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from functools import cache
from importlib import resources
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom, Node

# Unambiguous press-release tails; they end the body on any page, on top of a profile's own markers.
GENERIC_STOPS = (
    "Forward-Looking Statement",
    "Forward Looking Statement",
    "Cautionary Statement",
    "Safe Harbor",
    "Media Contact",
    "Investor Contact",
    "Investors Contact",
    "Investor Relations Contact",
    "Contact:",
    "Contacts:",
    "Contact Information",
)
# Whole-line UI leftovers that sit between body paragraphs.
BOILERPLATE_LINES = frozenset(
    {
        "advertisement", "continue reading", "read more", "read next", "recommended stories",
        "related articles", "related content", "related stories", "scroll to continue", "share this article",
        "show less", "show more", "sign up", "skip advertisement", "story continues", "subscribe",
        "view comments",
    }
)  # fmt: skip
_BOILERPLATE_TRAIL = " .:»›>…"
# "About Acme" ends a release, "About 40% of" does not: name-style markers need a capital or a short line.
_HEADING_WORDS = 8
# A short line with an e-mail address is a contact line; dropped, not a stop, since "Send tips to ..."
# promos also sit mid-article.
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+")
CONTACT_MAX_WORDS = 15


class Fate(StrEnum):
    KEEP = "keep"
    EMPTY = "empty"
    NESTED = "nested"
    SHORT = "short"
    BOILERPLATE = "boilerplate"
    CONTACT = "contact"
    STOP = "stop"
    AFTER_STOP = "after_stop"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Verdict:
    fate: Fate
    phrase: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Profile:
    source: str
    body: str
    drop: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    title: str | None = None
    lede_paragraphs: int = 2
    min_words: int = 1
    stop_markers: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    paywall: str | None = None

    @property
    def stops(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return self.stop_markers + tuple(m for m in GENERIC_STOPS if m not in self.stop_markers)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Source:
    key: str
    name: str
    domains: tuple[str, ...]
    status: str
    kind: str
    profile: Profile | None


def _profile(key: str, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Profile:
    return Profile(
        source=key,
        body=str(raw["body"]),
        drop=tuple(str(s) for s in raw.get("drop", ())),
        title=raw.get("title"),
        lede_paragraphs=int(raw.get("lede_paragraphs", 2)),
        min_words=int(raw.get("min_words", 1)),
        stop_markers=tuple(str(s) for s in raw.get("stop_markers", ())),
        paywall=raw.get("paywall"),
    )


@cache
def sources() -> dict[str, Source]:
    text = resources.files("veritrade").joinpath("data/sources.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    out: dict[str, Source] = {}
    for key, raw in tomllib.loads(text).get("sources", {}).items():
        profile = raw.get("profile")
        out[key] = Source(
            key=key,
            name=str(raw.get("name", key)),
            domains=tuple(str(d).lower() for d in raw.get("domains", ())),
            status=str(raw.get("status", "")),
            kind=str(raw.get("kind", "")),
            profile=_profile(key, profile) if isinstance(profile, dict) else None,
        )
    return out


@cache
def _domain_index() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {domain: key for key, source in sources().items() for domain in source.domains}


def source_for_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """Source key for the URL's host or its closest listed parent domain (uk.finance.yahoo.com -> yahoo)."""
    host = (urlsplit(url).hostname or "").rstrip(".").lower()
    index = _domain_index()
    while host:
        if (key := index.get(host)) is not None:
            return key
        _, _, host = host.partition(".")
    return None


def profile_for(source_key: str | None) -> Profile | None:
    source = sources().get(source_key) if source_key else None
    return source.profile if source else None


# --- paragraph rules --------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def stop_marker(text: str, markers: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
    lowered = text.lower()
    for marker in markers:
        if not lowered.startswith(marker.lower()):
            continue
        rest = text[len(marker) :]
        if marker.endswith(" ") and rest and not rest[0].isupper() and len(text.split()) > _HEADING_WORDS:
            continue
        return marker
    return None


def boilerplate_line(text: str) -> str | None:
    line = text.lower().rstrip(_BOILERPLATE_TRAIL)
    return line if line in BOILERPLATE_LINES else None


def contact_line(text: str) -> bool:
    return len(text.split()) <= CONTACT_MAX_WORDS and _EMAIL.search(text) is not None
```
```

# Source registry shared by the fetcher, extractors, probe, Opus discovery and live smoke.
# Decided by scripts/probe_sources.py (evidence: evals/data/source_probe.json, .context/docs/design/02-source-probe.md).
#
# status            primary (served + evaluated, `rank` = preference order) | backup | rejected (`reason`)
# feeds             RSS/Atom URLs, tried in order; items with a non-English <dc:language> are skipped
# sections          HTML pages or sitemaps scanned for links when there is no usable feed
# article_pattern   regex on the normalized URL (https, no query or fragment) that marks an article
# exclude_pattern   regex that drops live blogs, video and galleries
# discovery         "edgar-8k-ex99": feed entries are filing indexes resolved to their EX-99.1 exhibit
#
# [sources.<key>.profile] (selectors are tag/class/id/attribute + descendant only, so selectolax and lxml
# cssselect agree; the probe checks both on every captured page)
# body              selector of the body paragraphs, in document order
# drop              selectors removed before `body` is applied (captions, widgets, promos, tables)
# title             selector of the headline element
# lede_paragraphs   paragraphs that form the lede (default 2); stop markers never cut inside the lede
# min_words         paragraphs shorter than this are ignored (default 1)
# stop_markers      case-insensitive paragraph prefixes; the body ends at the first match after the lede
#                   (press-release About / forward-looking / contacts, partner promo pitches)
```

```
"""Skeleton fixtures: real publisher DOM, synthetic text (written by scripts/capture_skeletons.py)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

SKELETONS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "fixtures" / "skeletons"
BODY_MARKER = re.compile(r"VTB-\d+")
OTHER_MARKER = re.compile(r"VTX-\d+")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Skeleton:
    source: str
    html: str
    expected: dict[str, Any]

    @property
    def url(self) -> str:
        return str(self.expected["fixture_url"])

    @property
    def body_markers(self) -> list[str]:
        return list(self.expected["body_markers"])

    def recall(self, text: str) -> float:
        found = set(BODY_MARKER.findall(text))
        return len(found & set(self.body_markers)) / len(self.body_markers)


@cache
def skeletons() -> tuple[Skeleton, ...]:
    out = []
    for expected_path in sorted(SKELETONS.glob("*/*.expected.json")):
        expected = json.loads(expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        html = expected_path.with_name(f"{expected['slug']}.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        out.append(Skeleton(expected["source"], html, expected))
    return tuple(out)


@cache
def vocabulary() -> dict[str, Any]:
    data: dict[str, Any] = json.loads((SKELETONS / "vocabulary.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return data
"""Every extractor on every skeleton: body-marker recall and leakage of non-body text."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from veritrade.extract import third_party
from veritrade.extract.registry import extract
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSERS, ExtractorName, ParserName

from ._skeletons import BODY_MARKER, OTHER_MARKER, Skeleton, skeletons

SKELETONS = skeletons()
OWN_EXACT: tuple[ExtractorName, ...] = ("jsonld", "profile", "cascade")
THIRD_PARTY: tuple[ExtractorName, ...] = (
    "trafilatura",
    "trafilatura-precision",
    "readability",
    "newspaper",
    "justext",
    "strip-tags",
)


def _ids(skeleton: Skeleton) -> str:
    return skeleton.source


def test_every_primary_source_has_a_skeleton() -> None:
    assert len(SKELETONS) >= 10
    assert all(s.body_markers for s in SKELETONS)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("parser", PARSERS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("extractor", OWN_EXACT)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_own_strategy_recovers_the_body_without_leakage(
    skeleton: Skeleton, extractor: ExtractorName, parser: ParserName
) -> None:
    if extractor == "jsonld" and not skeleton.expected["jsonld_body"]:
        pytest.skip("page has no JSON-LD articleBody")
    article = extract(skeleton.html, skeleton.url, parser=parser, extractor=extractor)

    assert article.source == skeleton.source
    assert skeleton.recall(article.text) >= 0.9
    assert OTHER_MARKER.findall(article.text) == []
    if title_marker := skeleton.expected["title_marker"]:
        assert title_marker in article.title


@pytest.mark.parametrize("parser", PARSERS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_density_finds_most_of_the_body(skeleton: Skeleton, parser: ParserName) -> None:
    """A leaked line holds only non-body text; an inline chip inside a body paragraph does not count."""
    article = extract(skeleton.html, skeleton.url, parser=parser, extractor="density")

    leaked = [p for p in article.paragraphs if OTHER_MARKER.search(p) and not BODY_MARKER.search(p)]
    assert skeleton.recall(article.text) >= 0.8
    assert len(leaked) <= 0.1 * len(article.paragraphs)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_cascade_takes_jsonld_only_when_the_page_has_a_body(skeleton: Skeleton) -> None:
    article = extract(skeleton.html, skeleton.url, extractor="cascade")

    assert article.method == ("jsonld" if skeleton.expected["jsonld_body"] else "profile")
    # A JSON-LD hit never builds a DOM.
    assert (article.parse_ms == 0.0) is (article.method == "jsonld")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("extractor", THIRD_PARTY)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_third_party_smoke(skeleton: Skeleton, extractor: ExtractorName) -> None:
    paragraphs = third_party.extract(extractor, skeleton.html, skeleton.url)

    assert paragraphs
    assert all(isinstance(p, str) and p for p in paragraphs)
from __future__ import annotations

import socket
from typing import Any

import pytest

from veritrade.extract import third_party
from veritrade.extract.types import EXTRACTORS, PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS

from ._skeletons import skeletons


def test_every_non_own_extractor_has_an_adapter() -> None:
    assert set(third_party.ADAPTERS) == set(EXTRACTORS) - PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS


def test_adapters_never_touch_the_network(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def refuse(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        raise AssertionError("an extractor tried to open a connection")

    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "connect", refuse)
    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, "create_connection", refuse)
    skeleton = next(s for s in skeletons() if s.source == "fool")

    for name in third_party.ADAPTERS:
        assert third_party.extract(name, skeleton.html, skeleton.url)


def test_strip_tags_returns_every_visible_run() -> None:
    page = "<html><head><title>T</title><style>p{}</style></head><body><p>One <b>two</b></p><div>three</div>"

    assert third_party.extract("strip-tags", page, "https://example.com/") == ["One two", "three"]
```

```
Text is rebuilt from a fixed vocabulary; body paragraphs carry VTB-<k> markers and all other text VTX-<k>.
"""
```

```python
"""Structure only: profile body nodes in order with tag, attribute hints, word count, gold coverage and fate.

Never prints article words; a node's prefix is reported only as a category from a fixed list.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
import sys
import warnings

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser, LexborNode

from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for, source_for_url, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

CATEGORIES = (
    "about", "forward", "safe harbor", "cautionary", "contact", "media", "investor", "source", "view original",
    "attachment", "photo", "logo", "video", "disclaimer", "disclosure", "important", "related", "read more",
    "see also", "more from", "the motley fool", "motley fool", "should you", "before you", "where to invest",
    "10 stocks", "this article", "originally published", "first appeared", "disclosure:", "learn more",
    "for more information", "click here", "follow", "subscribe", "sign up", "to read", "story continues",
    "recommended", "trending", "*", "(", "-", "#", "note", "editor", "sponsored", "advertisement",
    "copyright", "©", "all rights", "website", "web site", "www", "http", "email", "phone", "tel",
    "investors:", "press:", "media:", "for further", "further information", "notes to editors",
)  # fmt: skip


def category(text: str) -> str:
    low = text.strip().lower()
    hits = [c for c in CATEGORIES if low.startswith(c)]
    return max(hits, key=len) if hits else "-"


def ancestors(node: LexborNode, stop: int = 4) -> str:
    out = []
    current = node.parent
    while current is not None and len(out) < stop and current.tag not in ("body", "html"):
        attrs = current.attributes
        bits = [current.tag or "?"]
        if attrs.get("id"):
            bits.append(f"#{attrs['id']}")
        if attrs.get("data-testid"):
            bits.append(f"[testid={attrs['data-testid']}]")
        cls = [c for c in (attrs.get("class") or "").split() if not re.match(r"yf-", c)]
        bits += [f".{c}" for c in cls[:2]]
        out.append("".join(bits))
        current = current.parent
    return " < ".join(out)


def own(node: LexborNode) -> str:
    attrs = node.attributes
    cls = [c for c in (attrs.get("class") or "").split() if not re.match(r"yf-", c)]
    bold = node.css_first("strong, b") is not None
    return f"{node.tag}{''.join('.' + c for c in cls[:2])}{' [bold]' if bold else ''}"


def main(article_ids: list[str], source: str | None) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if (source and ex.source != source) or (article_ids and ex.id not in article_ids):
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        assert profile is not None
        tree = LexborHTMLParser(ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in tree.css(css):
                node.decompose()
        nodes = tree.css(profile.body)
        texts = [" ".join(n.text(deep=True, separator=" ").split()) for n in nodes]
        fates = triage(texts, profile)
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        print(f"== {ex.id} {ex.source} nodes={len(nodes)}")
        for i, (node, text, fate) in enumerate(zip(nodes, texts, fates, strict=True)):
            toks = word_tokens(text)
            leaked = unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) if toks else 0
            status = "GOLD" if toks and leaked <= len(toks) / 2 else ("leak" if toks else "empty")
            print(
                f"  {i:3d} {status:5s} {fate.fate.value:11s} w={len(toks):4d} cat={category(text):18s} "
                f"{own(node)} < {ancestors(node)}"
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    src = next((a.split("=", 1)[1] for a in args if a.startswith("source=")), None)
    main([a for a in args if a.startswith("art-")], src)
```

```python
"""Counts only: how often each candidate stop marker opens a gold paragraph vs a leaked kept one, per source.

Only the candidate strings below (ours) and counts are printed, never article words.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
import warnings
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser

from veritrade.extract.profiles import Fate, profile_for, source_for_url, stop_marker, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

CANDIDATES = (
    "About ", "Forward-looking", "Forward looking", "Forward-Looking Information", "Cautionary", "Caution ",
    "Note Regarding", "Special Note", "Disclaimer", "Disclosure", "Non-GAAP", "Use of Non-GAAP",
    "Reconciliation", "Conference Call", "Webcast", "Earnings Call", "Investor Day", "Upcoming", "Events",
    "Highlights", "Financial Highlights", "Outlook", "Guidance", "Dividend", "Additional Information",
    "Important Information", "Where to Find", "Participants in", "No Offer", "Notice", "Legal",
    "Methodology", "Survey Methodology", "Inquiries", "Enquiries", "For further information",
    "For more information", "Further information", "Information", "Contact", "Press contact",
    "Company contact", "Media", "Investor", "Investors", "Resources", "Connect with", "Follow",
    "Social", "Join", "Learn more", "Links", "Attachment", "Image", "Photo", "Video", "Download", "Logo",
    "Notes to editors", "Note to editors", "Editor", "Background", "Source:", "SOURCE ", "Neither ",
    "This news release", "This press release", "This announcement", "The information", "Statements in",
    "Certain statements", "Except for", "All statements", "To learn more", "Visit", "For additional",
    "Website", "www.", "http", "###", "-30-", "* * *", "*", "Read more", "READ NEXT", "Read next",
    "Related", "While we acknowledge", "This article", "Originally published", "The post ",
    "The views and opinions", "Should you invest", "Before you buy", "Stock Advisor", "The Motley Fool",
    "Don't miss", "Where to invest", "Want ", "Click here", "Sign up", "Subscribe", "Read the latest",
    "Yahoo Finance", "Story continues", "Most Read", "Up Next", "See also", "Also read", "More from",
    "Suggested", "Sponsored", "Featured", "Disclaimer:", "Editor's note", "(Reporting by", "Reporting by",
    "Editing by", "Image source", "Image:", "Photo:", "Recommended", "Trending", "Get ", "Is it time",
    "Thinking about", "Ever feel", "Consider when", "Now, it", "Here's", "Learn More",
)  # fmt: skip
DASHES = str.maketrans({"‐": "-", "‑": "-", "‒": "-", "–": "-", "−": "-"})


def main(sources: list[str]) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    table: dict[str, dict[str, Counter[str]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(Counter))
    dash_codes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    unmatched: dict[str, Counter[str]] = defaultdict(Counter)
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source not in sources:
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        assert profile is not None
        tree = LexborHTMLParser(ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in tree.css(css):
                node.decompose()
        nodes = tree.css(profile.body)
        texts = [" ".join(n.text(deep=True, separator=" ").split()) for n in nodes]
        fates = triage(texts, profile)
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        for node, text, fate in zip(nodes, texts, fates, strict=True):
            toks = word_tokens(text)
            if not toks:
                continue
            in_gold = unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) <= len(toks) / 2
            kept = fate.fate is Fate.KEEP
            bucket = "gold" if in_gold else ("leak_kept" if kept else "leak_dropped")
            low = text.lower()
            if low.startswith("forward") and len(low) > 7:
                dash_codes[f"U+{ord(text[7]):04X}"] += 1
            hit = stop_marker(text.translate(DASHES), CANDIDATES)
            table[ex.source][hit or "(none)"][bucket] += 1
            if bucket == "leak_kept" and hit is None:
                bold = node.css_first("strong, b") is not None
                unmatched[ex.source][f"bold={bold} words={'<=8' if len(toks) <= 8 else '>8'}"] += 1
    for source in sorted(table):
        print(f"== {source}")
        for cand, counts in sorted(table[source].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]["leak_kept"]):
            if counts["leak_kept"] or counts["gold"]:
                print(f"  {cand!r:32s} gold={counts['gold']:3d} leak_kept={counts['leak_kept']:3d} "
                      f"leak_dropped={counts['leak_dropped']:3d}")
        print("  unmatched leaked kept:", dict(unmatched[source]))
    print("char after 'forward':", dict(dash_codes))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1].split(","))

```

```python
"""Structure only: per profile body node, child tags, bold/italic/link char share and preceding sibling tags."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
import warnings

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser, LexborNode

from veritrade.extract.profiles import Fate, profile_for, source_for_url, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")


def chars(node: LexborNode, css: str) -> int:
    return sum(len(n.text(deep=True).strip()) for n in node.css(css))


def shape(node: LexborNode) -> str:
    kids = [c.tag for c in node.iter() if c.tag and c.tag != "-text"]
    total = max(1, len(node.text(deep=True).strip()))
    bold = chars(node, "strong, b") / total
    ital = chars(node, "em, i") / total
    link = chars(node, "a") / total
    prev = node.prev
    while prev is not None and prev.tag == "-text":
        prev = prev.prev
    prev_tag = prev.tag if prev is not None else "^"
    return f"kids={'/'.join(kids[:4]) or '-'} bold={bold:.2f} ital={ital:.2f} link={link:.2f} prev={prev_tag}"


def main(source: str) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source != source:
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        assert profile is not None
        tree = LexborHTMLParser(ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in tree.css(css):
                node.decompose()
        nodes = tree.css(profile.body)
        texts = [" ".join(n.text(deep=True, separator=" ").split()) for n in nodes]
        fates = triage(texts, profile)
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        print(f"== {ex.id}")
        for i, (node, text, fate) in enumerate(zip(nodes, texts, fates, strict=True)):
            toks = word_tokens(text)
            if not toks or fate.fate is not Fate.KEEP:
                continue
            status = "GOLD" if unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) <= len(toks) / 2 else "leak"
            print(f"  {i:3d} {status} w={len(toks):4d} {shape(node)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])

```
</details>

```python
"""Metadata only: the syndication partner (providerId / provider name fields) of each Yahoo article."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import Counter

from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles

FIELDS = re.compile(r'"(providerId|providerName|provider_name|publisher)"\s*:\s*"([^"]{1,60})"')


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source != "yahoo":
            continue
        html = ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        found = Counter(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in FIELDS.findall(html))
        print(ex.id, dict(found.most_common(4)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
```
class Node(Protocol):
    @property
    def tag(self) -> str: ...

    def text(self) -> str: ...

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None: ...


class Container:
    """A non-inline element on the path of a text block; density scores these."""

    __slots__ = ("_hint", "_hint_of", "depth", "native", "tag")

    def __init__(self, tag: str, native: Any, depth: int, hint_of: Callable[[Any], str]) -> None:
        self.tag = tag
        self.native = native
        self.depth = depth
        self._hint_of = hint_of
        self._hint: str | None = None

    @property
    def hint(self) -> str:
        """Class and id as written, computed only for the containers density inspects."""
        if self._hint is None:
            self._hint = self._hint_of(self.native)
        return self._hint


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Block:
    text: str
    link_chars: int
    tag: str
    path: tuple[Container, ...]  # nearest container first

    @property
    def link_density(self) -> float:
        return self.link_chars / len(self.text) if self.text else 0.0


class Dom(Protocol):
    @property
    def parser(self) -> ParserName: ...

    @property
    def parse_ms(self) -> float: ...

    def select(self, css: str) -> list[Node]: ...

    def remove(self, css: str) -> int: ...

    def iter_blocks(self) -> Iterator[Block]: ...

    def json_ld(self) -> list[Any]: ...

    def title(self) -> str: ...


class _Node[E]:
    __slots__ = ("_dom", "native")

    def __init__(self, dom: _TreeDom[E], native: E) -> None:
        self._dom = dom
        self.native = native

    @property
    def tag(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._tag(self.native)

    def text(self) -> str:
        return self._dom._text(self.native)

    def attr(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        return self._dom._attr(self.native, name)


class _TreeDom[E](ABC):
    """Shared walkers; a backend only supplies parse, select, drop and child iteration."""

    name: ParserName

    def __init__(self, html: str) -> None:
        self._html = html
    def _hint(self, el: E) -> str:
        return f"{self._attr(el, 'class') or ''} {self._attr(el, 'id') or ''}"

    def _text(self, el: E) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        # Explicit stacks, not recursion: unclosed tags in old filings can nest thousands deep.
        stack: list[tuple[Iterator[E | str], bool]] = [(self._content(el), False)]
        while stack:
            children, block = stack[-1]
            item = next(children, None)
            if item is None:
                stack.pop()
                if block:
                    parts.append(" ")
            elif isinstance(item, str):
                parts.append(item)
            elif (tag := self._tag(item)) not in SKIP_TAGS:
                block = tag not in INLINE_TAGS
                if block:
                    parts.append(" ")
                stack.append((self._content(item), block))
        return normalize("".join(parts))

    def _blocks(self, root: E) -> list[Block]:
        """Split visible text at every non-inline boundary; each run remembers its container path."""
        out: list[Block] = []
        buffer: list[str] = []
        link_chars = 0
        containers: list[Container] = [Container(self._tag(root), root, 0, self._hint)]

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal link_chars
            if buffer:
                if text := normalize("".join(buffer)):
                    path = tuple(reversed(containers))
                    out.append(Block(text, min(link_chars, len(text)), containers[-1].tag, path))
                buffer.clear()
            link_chars = 0

        # (children, closes a container, inside a link)
        stack: list[tuple[Iterator[E | str], bool, bool]] = [(self._content(root), False, False)]
        while stack:
            children, block, in_link = stack[-1]
            item = next(children, None)
            if item is None:
                stack.pop()
                if block:
                    flush()
                    containers.pop()
            elif isinstance(item, str):
                buffer.append(item)
                if in_link:
                    link_chars += len(item.strip())
            elif (tag := self._tag(item)) in SKIP_TAGS:
                continue
            elif tag in INLINE_TAGS:
                stack.append((self._content(item), False, in_link or tag == "a"))
            elif tag == "br":
                buffer.append(" ")
            else:
                flush()
                containers.append(Container(tag, item, len(containers), self._hint))
                stack.append((self._content(item), True, in_link))
        flush()
        return out


# --- selectolax (Lexbor) --------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```python
"""Counts only: Yahoo gold vs leaked link shares, and partner-template prefixes (our strings) per bucket."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import warnings
from collections import Counter

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser, LexborNode

from veritrade.extract.profiles import Fate, profile_for, source_for_url, stop_marker, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

CANDIDATES = (
    "Join Paid", "Top 5", "Top 6", "Top 9", "Top 10", "Unless you", "Market Beating", "High-Quality",
    "High Quality", "Stocks We Like", "StockStory", "Your portfolio", "We think", "Is now the time",
    "Is now a good time", "Is now a great time", "Should you buy", "Sign up", "Help us", "Want to",
    "Our list", "Access our", "Find out", "Read our", "Get started", "We see", "Unlock", "While", "Today",
    "More Top Reads", "By ", "Oilprice", "This article by", "This article", "Have feedback", "Valuation is",
    "Simply Wall St", "For updates and corrections", "Read also", "Read Also", "Also See", "Also Read",
    "Related", "Disclaimer", "Disclosure", "Editor", "Story continues", "Final Judgment", "Final judgement",
    "In the meantime", "The author", "Meanwhile", "If you", "To learn more", "Before you", "Here's",
    "Check out", "See how", "Click here", "Looking for", "Interested in",
)  # fmt: skip


def link_share(node: LexborNode) -> float:
    total = max(1, len(node.text(deep=True).strip()))
    return sum(len(a.text(deep=True).strip()) for a in node.css("a")) / total


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    shares: Counter[str] = Counter()
    hits: dict[str, Counter[str]] = {}
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source != "yahoo":
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        assert profile is not None
        tree = LexborHTMLParser(ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in tree.css(css):
                node.decompose()
        nodes = tree.css(profile.body)
        texts = [" ".join(n.text(deep=True, separator=" ").split()) for n in nodes]
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        for node, text, fate in zip(nodes, texts, triage(texts, profile), strict=True):
            toks = word_tokens(text)
            if not toks or fate.fate is not Fate.KEEP:
                continue
            status = "gold" if unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) <= len(toks) / 2 else "leak"
            share = link_share(node)
            band = "0" if share == 0 else "<0.3" if share < 0.3 else "<0.5" if share < 0.5 else ">=0.5"
            shares[f"{status} link{band}"] += 1
            if (hit := stop_marker(text, CANDIDATES)) is not None:
                hits.setdefault(hit, Counter())[status] += 1
    print("link share bands:", dict(sorted(shares.items())))
    for cand, counts in sorted(hits.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]["leak"]):
        print(f"  {cand!r:32s} gold={counts['gold']} leak={counts['leak']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```
def plan_body(annotated: str, profile: Profile) -> Plan:
    """Replay the profile strategy on the annotated page so the skeleton matches what it keeps."""
    dom = parse(annotated, "lxml")
    nodes = profiles.select_body(dom, profile)
    texts = [node.text() for node in nodes]
    keep: set[str] = set()
    special: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for node, verdict in zip(nodes, profiles.triage(texts, profile), strict=True):
        key = node.attr(KEY_ATTR) or ""
        if verdict.fate is Fate.KEEP:
            keep.add(key)
        elif verdict.fate is Fate.STOP and verdict.phrase:
            special[key] = ("stop", verdict.phrase)
        elif verdict.fate is Fate.BOILERPLATE and verdict.phrase:
            special[key] = ("boilerplate", verdict.phrase.capitalize())
        elif verdict.fate is Fate.CONTACT:
            special[key] = ("contact", CONTACT_EMAIL)
    fresh = parse(annotated, "lxml")
    dropped = {node.attr(KEY_ATTR) or "" for css in profile.drop for node in fresh.select(css)}
    titles = fresh.select(profile.title) if profile.title else []
    return Plan(keep, special, dropped, titles[0].attr(KEY_ATTR) if titles else None)


@dataclass
class Walker:
    synth: Synth
    plan: Plan
    body_seen: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    title_marker: str | None = None

    def run(self, root: Any) -> None:
        self._walk(root, kept=None, dropped=False, special=None, in_title=False)
def capture(key: str, pick: int, probe: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    profile = profiles.profile_for(key)
    source = profiles.sources()[key]
    if profile is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"{key}: no [sources.{key}.profile] in sources.toml")
    articles = {a["n"]: a for a in probe["sources"][key]["articles"]}
    url = articles[pick]["fetch"]["final_url"]
    html = (PROBE_DIR / key / f"{pick}.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

    root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(strip_xml_declaration(html))
    strip_comments(root)
    for index, el in enumerate(e for e in root.iter() if isinstance(e.tag, str)):
        el.set(KEY_ATTR, str(index))
    annotated = lxml.html.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
    plan = plan_body(annotated, profile)

    synth = Synth(random.Random(f"veritrade-skeleton-{key}"))
    walker = Walker(synth, plan)
    walker.run(root)

    slug = f"article-{pick}"
    fixture_url = f"https://{source.domains[0]}/vt-skeleton/{slug}"
    skeleton = lxml.html.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
    paragraphs = profiles.extract(parse(skeleton, "lxml"), fixture_url, key)
    # The title as the registry reads it; pages without a profile title fall back to <title>.
    titled = parse(skeleton, "lxml").select(profile.title) if profile.title else []
    head_title = root.find(".//title")
    title = titled[0].text() if titled else ""
    if not title and head_title is not None:
        title = normalize(head_title.text or "")
        found = re.search(r"VTX-\d+", title)
        walker.title_marker = found.group(0) if found else None
    if head_title is not None and title:
        head_title.text = title
    selectors = (profile.body, *profile.drop, profile.title or "", profile.paywall or "")
    keep_ids = {m.group(1) for css in selectors for m in re.finditer(r"#([\w-]+)", css)}
    keep_attrs = {m.group(1).lower() for css in selectors for m in _SELECTOR_ATTR.finditer(css)}
    scrub_attributes(root, synth, keep_ids, keep_attrs)
    had_body = rewrite_jsonld(root, synth, title, paragraphs)
    for meta in root.iter("meta"):
        if meta.get("content") == "{title}":
            meta.set("content", title or synth.words(3))

    out = OUT_DIR / key
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Punctuation-only text nodes survive verbatim; the repo style bans the em-dash character outright.
    document = lxml.html.tostring(root, encoding="unicode", doctype="<!DOCTYPE html>").replace(EM_DASH, "-")
    (out / f"{slug}.html").write_text(document + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    expected = {
        "source": key,
        "slug": slug,
        "captured_at": probe.get("generated_at"),
        "url_sha256": hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).hexdigest(),
        "fixture_url": fixture_url,
        "title_marker": walker.title_marker,
        "body_markers": [f"VTB-{k}" for k in range(1, synth.vtb + 1)],
        "jsonld_body": had_body,
        "stop_marker": next((phrase for mode, phrase in plan.special.values() if mode == "stop"), None),
        "bytes": len(document.encode()),
    }
    (out / f"{slug}.expected.json").write_text(json.dumps(expected, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return expected


def write_vocabulary() -> None:
    phrases = sorted(
        {m for s in profiles.sources().values() if s.profile for m in s.profile.stop_markers}
"""Skeletons must not carry publisher text: every string is built from the fixed synthetic vocabulary."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any

import lxml.html
import pytest

from ._skeletons import Skeleton, skeletons, vocabulary

SKELETONS = skeletons()
VOCAB = vocabulary()
WORDS = frozenset(VOCAB["words"])
PHRASES = sorted((p.strip() for p in VOCAB["phrases"]), key=len, reverse=True)
INVALID_URL = VOCAB["url"]
JSONLD_KEEP = frozenset(VOCAB["jsonld_keep_keys"])
MARKER = re.compile(r"VT[BX]-\d+")
TOKEN = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+|\d+")
ISO_DATE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[T ][\d:.+\-Z]*)?$")
TEXT_ATTRS = ("alt", "title", "aria-label", "placeholder", "aria-description")
TEXT_METAS = frozenset({"description", "og:title", "og:description", "twitter:title", "twitter:description"})


def synthetic(text: str) -> bool:
    """Only vocabulary words and markers, optionally after one stop/boilerplate phrase at the start."""
    rest = text.strip()
    for phrase in PHRASES:
        if rest.lower().startswith(phrase.lower()):
            rest = rest[len(phrase) :]
            break
    rest = MARKER.sub(" ", rest).replace(VOCAB["contact_email"], " ")
    return all(token.lower() in WORDS for token in TOKEN.findall(rest))


def _ids(skeleton: Skeleton) -> str:
    return skeleton.source


def _strings(value: Any, key: str = "") -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(key, string) pairs; structural keys such as @context are skipped with everything under them."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for k, v in value.items():
            if k not in JSONLD_KEEP:
                yield from _strings(v, k)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            yield from _strings(item, key)
    elif isinstance(value, str):
        yield key, value


def test_vocabulary_is_small_and_plain() -> None:
    assert 40 <= len(WORDS) <= 150
    assert all(re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", w) for w in WORDS)


def test_detector_rejects_real_prose() -> None:
    assert synthetic("VTB-3 The company said the plan was shared with the board.")
    assert synthetic("About VTX-9 the group")
    assert not synthetic("Shares of Acme jumped 12% after earnings beat estimates.")
    assert not synthetic("VTB-3 the company said revenue")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_text_nodes_are_synthetic(skeleton: Skeleton) -> None:
    root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(skeleton.html)
    offenders = []
    for el in root.iter():
        if not isinstance(el.tag, str):
            offenders.append("comment or processing instruction")
            continue
        if el.tag in ("script", "style"):
            ld = el.tag == "script" and "ld+json" in (el.get("type") or "")
            if el.text and el.text.strip() and not ld:
                offenders.append(f"non-empty <{el.tag}>")
        elif el.text and not synthetic(el.text):
            offenders.append(f"<{el.tag}> text")
        if el.tail and not synthetic(el.tail):
            offenders.append(f"<{el.tag}> tail")
    assert offenders == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_jsonld_strings_are_synthetic(skeleton: Skeleton) -> None:
    root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(skeleton.html)
    offenders = []
    for script in root.iter("script"):
        if "ld+json" not in (script.get("type") or ""):
            continue
        for key, value in _strings(json.loads(script.text or "null")):
            structural = key.startswith("@") and key != "@id"
            if structural or value == INVALID_URL or ISO_DATE.match(value) or synthetic(value):
                continue
            offenders.append(key)
    assert offenders == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("skeleton", SKELETONS, ids=_ids)
def test_attributes_carry_no_publisher_text_or_links(skeleton: Skeleton) -> None:
    root = lxml.html.document_fromstring(skeleton.html)
    offenders = []
    for el in root.iter():
        if not isinstance(el.tag, str):
            continue
        for name in TEXT_ATTRS:
            if (value := el.get(name)) and not synthetic(value):
                offenders.append(f"<{el.tag} {name}>")
        for name in ("href", "src"):
            if (value := el.get(name)) and value != INVALID_URL:
                offenders.append(f"<{el.tag} {name}>")
        key = (el.get("property") or el.get("name") or "").lower()
        content = el.get("content") or ""
        if el.tag == "meta" and key in TEXT_METAS and content != INVALID_URL and not synthetic(content):
            offenders.append(f"<meta {key}>")
    assert offenders == []
```

```python
"""Structure only: tags and container paths of page blocks that are in the gold body but not in the cascade output."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
import warnings
from collections import Counter

from veritrade.extract import registry
from veritrade.extract.dom import parse
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")


def main(sources: list[str]) -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source not in sources:
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        html = ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        out = word_tokens(registry.extract(html, url, extractor="cascade").text)
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        missing: Counter[str] = Counter()
        for block in parse(html, "selectolax").iter_blocks():
            toks = word_tokens(block.text)
            if len(toks) < 3:
                continue
            in_gold = unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) <= len(toks) / 2
            in_out = unsupported_tokens(toks, out) <= len(toks) / 2 if out else False
            if in_gold and not in_out:
                path = " < ".join(f"{c.tag}{('.' + c.hint.split()[0]) if c.hint.split() else ''}" for c in block.path[:4])
                missing[f"{block.tag} | {path}"] += len(toks)
        if missing:
            print(f"== {ex.id} {ex.source}")
            for label, words in missing.most_common(6):
                print(f"  {words:5d} tokens  {label}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1].split(","))
```

```diff
+    def _link_density(self, el: E) -> float:
+        """Share of visible characters inside links, counted like Block.link_chars."""
+        total = links = 0
+        stack: list[tuple[Iterator[E | str], bool]] = [(self._content(el), False)]
```

```python
def select_body(dom: Dom, profile: Profile) -> list[Node]:
    """Body candidates in document order after the profile's drop selectors ran."""
    for css in profile.drop:
        dom.remove(css)
    return dom.select(profile.body)


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    profile = profile_for(source_key)
    if profile is None:
        return []
    return refine([node.text() for node in select_body(dom, profile)], profile)
```

```python
"""Numbers only: per-source and overall F1, recall, leakage and failures for rows of a measure JSONL."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import quality_scores


def main(path: Path, rows: list[str]) -> None:
    records = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        rec = json.loads(line)
        records[(rec["row"], rec["id"])] = rec
    for row in rows:
        by_source: dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]] = defaultdict(list)
        for (name, _), rec in records.items():
            if name == row:
                by_source[str(rec["source"])].append(rec)
        allrecs = [r for recs in by_source.values() for r in recs]

        def line(recs: list[dict[str, object]]) -> str:
            scores = [quality_scores(r) for r in recs]
            ok = [r for r in recs if r.get("error") is None]
            leak = [int(r["tokens_leaked"]) / int(r["tokens_extracted"]) for r in ok if r["tokens_extracted"]]  # type: ignore[call-overload]
            return (
                f"n={len(recs):2d} F1={statistics.fmean(s[2] for s in scores):.3f} "
                f"R={statistics.fmean(s[1] for s in scores):.3f} "
                f"leak={statistics.fmean(leak) if leak else 0:.3f} fail={len(recs) - len(ok)}"
            )

        print(f"== {row}: {line(allrecs)}")
        for source in sorted(by_source):
            print(f"  {source:14s} {line(by_source[source])}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2:])

```
</details>

```python
"""Booleans only: which stop markers match body paragraphs that start with 'forward', and their fate."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import warnings

from selectolax.lexbor import LexborHTMLParser

from veritrade.extract.profiles import profile_for, source_for_url, stop_marker, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
MARKERS = ("Forward-Looking Statement", "Forward-Looking Information", "Forward-looking", "Forward looking")


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        if ex.source not in ("globenewswire", "prnewswire"):
            continue
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        assert profile is not None
        tree = LexborHTMLParser(ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in tree.css(css):
                node.decompose()
        texts = [" ".join(n.text(deep=True, separator=" ").split()) for n in tree.css(profile.body)]
        for i, (text, verdict) in enumerate(zip(texts, triage(texts, profile), strict=True)):
            if not text.lower().startswith("forward"):
                continue
            words = text.split()
            shape = [len(w) for w in words[:3]]
            matches = {m: stop_marker(text, (m,)) is not None for m in MARKERS}
            print(f"{ex.id} node={i} fate={verdict.fate.value} first-word-lengths={shape} {matches}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```python
"""Counts only: which new stop markers fire and which paragraphs the new drops and link cap remove (gold or not)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import warnings
from collections import Counter

from veritrade.extract.dom import parse
from veritrade.extract.profiles import Fate, profile_for, source_for_url, triage
from veritrade_evals.articles import ArticlePaths, load_articles, read_fetched
from veritrade_evals.extraction_bench import unsupported_tokens, word_tokens

logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
NEW_STOPS = {
    "Forward-looking", "For further information", "Conference Call", "Non-GAAP", "More Top Reads From",
    "This article by Simply Wall St", "For updates and corrections", "Forward-Looking Information",
    "Forward Looking Information",
}
NEW_DROPS = {"p.prntac", "p#gnw_attachments_section-header", "ul#gnw_attachments_section-items"}


def in_gold(text: str, gold: list[str]) -> bool:
    toks = word_tokens(text)
    return bool(toks) and unsupported_tokens(toks, gold) <= len(toks) / 2


def main() -> None:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    stops: Counter[str] = Counter()
    removed: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for ex in load_articles("all", paths=paths):
        fetched = read_fetched(paths, ex.id)
        url = fetched.final_url if fetched and fetched.final_url else ex.url
        profile = profile_for(source_for_url(url))
        if profile is None:
            continue
        html = ex.html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        gold = word_tokens(ex.gold_text)
        dom = parse(html, "selectolax")
        for css in profile.drop:
            for node in dom.select(css):
                if css in NEW_DROPS and node.text():
                    removed[f"{ex.source} drop {css} {'GOLD' if in_gold(node.text(), gold) else 'leak'}"] += 1
            dom.remove(css)
        nodes = dom.select(profile.body)
        if profile.max_link_density is not None:
            for node in nodes:
                if node.link_density() > profile.max_link_density and node.text():
                    removed[f"{ex.source} link-cap {'GOLD' if in_gold(node.text(), gold) else 'leak'}"] += 1
            nodes = [n for n in nodes if n.link_density() <= profile.max_link_density]
        texts = [n.text() for n in nodes]
        verdicts = triage(texts, profile)
        for i, verdict in enumerate(verdicts):
            if verdict.fate is Fate.STOP and verdict.phrase in NEW_STOPS:
                after = texts[i:]
                gold_after = sum(in_gold(t, gold) for t in after)
                stops[f"{ex.source} stop {verdict.phrase!r} gold-paragraphs-cut={gold_after}"] += 1
    for line, n in sorted({**stops, **removed}.items()):
        print(f"{n:3d}  {line}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
</details>

```python
"""Add synthetic structural elements to three skeletons so the new profile rules run on real publisher DOM.

Text is fixture vocabulary plus VTB/VTX markers only; links point at example.invalid. Idempotent: refuses to
run twice. Rewrites vocabulary.json with the capture script's own writer so its phrases follow the profiles.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SKELETONS = ROOT / "backend/tests/fixtures/skeletons"
YAHOO_P = '<p class="text text-block paragraph text-left neo-font-paragraph-xl-reg  yf-18d6y07">'
LINK = '<a href="https://example.invalid/" data-ylk="vt" target="_blank">'


def insert_after_paragraph(html: str, marker: str, addition: str) -> str:
    start = html.index(f">{marker} ")
    end = html.index("</p>", start) + len("</p>")
    return html[:end] + addition + html[end:]


def edit(source: str, change: callable, new_vtb: list[str] | None = None, stop: str | None = None) -> None:  # type: ignore[valid-type]
    html_path = SKELETONS / source / "article-1.html"
    expected_path = SKELETONS / source / "article-1.expected.json"
    html = html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "VTX-90" in html:
        raise SystemExit(f"{source}: already extended")
    html = change(html)  # type: ignore[operator]
    html_path.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
    expected = json.loads(expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    expected["body_markers"] += new_vtb or []
    if stop is not None:
        expected["stop_marker"] = stop
    expected["bytes"] = len(html.encode())
    expected_path.write_text(json.dumps(expected, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def yahoo(html: str) -> str:
    promo = f"{YAHOO_P}{LINK}VTX-901 report on the new plan for the region</a></p>"
    tail = (
        f"{YAHOO_P}More Top Reads From VTX-902</p>"
        f'<ul><li>{YAHOO_P}{LINK}<strong>VTX-903 the board review</strong></a></p></li></ul>'
        f"{YAHOO_P}VTX-904 a plan for the week with the board and the staff</p>"
    )
    return insert_after_paragraph(insert_after_paragraph(html, "VTB-6", promo), "VTB-8", tail)


def prnewswire(html: str) -> str:
    dek = '<p class="prntac">VTX-901 the new plan for the region</p>'
    html = html.replace("<p><span><i>VTB-1 ", f"{dek}<p><span><i>VTB-1 ", 1)
    bullets = (
        "<ul><li>VTB-15 the board noted a new plan for the region and the staff</li>"
        "<li>VTB-16 the team will review the program with the public later this year</li></ul>"
    )
    return insert_after_paragraph(html, "VTB-13", bullets)


def globenewswire(html: str) -> str:
    tail = (
        '<p id="gnw_attachments_section-header">VTX-901 report</p>'
        '<ul id="gnw_attachments_section-items"><li>VTX-902 the plan for the region</li></ul>'
        "<p>Forward-looking VTX-903 this report has a plan that the board will review later</p>"
    )
    return insert_after_paragraph(html, "VTB-22", tail)


def main() -> None:
    edit("yahoo", yahoo)
    edit("prnewswire", prnewswire, new_vtb=["VTB-15", "VTB-16"])
    edit("globenewswire", globenewswire, stop="Forward-looking")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("capture_skeletons", ROOT / "scripts/capture_skeletons.py")
    assert spec and spec.loader
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    module.write_vocabulary()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```python
"""Rewrite the skeleton vocabulary.json with scripts/capture_skeletons.py's own writer (no capture)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def main() -> None:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("capture_skeletons", ROOT / "scripts/capture_skeletons.py")
    assert spec and spec.loader
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[spec.name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    module.write_vocabulary()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
from veritrade.extract.dom import head_title, normalize, parse, scan_json_ld, split_sentences
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSERS, ParserName

PAGE = """<!doctype html><html><head><title>Plain title | Site</title>
<meta property="og:title" content="Social &amp; title">
<script type="application/ld+json">{"@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "LD headline"}</script>
<script type="application/ld+json"><!-- {"@type": "Organization", "name": "Org"} --></script>
<script type="application/ld+json">{not json</script>
</head><body>
<div id="main" class="story body">
  <p><span class="dropcap">R</span>ogue traders<br>were <b>caught</b>&nbsp;today\u200b.</p>
  <ul><li>First <a href="/x">point</a></li></ul>
  <p>Second<!-- hidden --> paragraph<script>var x = 1;</script> here.</p>
  <div class="ad"><div class="ad"><p>nested ad copy</p></div></div>
</div>
<p class="tail">Outside text</p>
</body></html>"""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("parser", PARSERS)
def test_text_joins_inline_runs_and_separates_breaks(parser: ParserName) -> None:
def test_blocks_carry_link_density_and_container_path(parser: ParserName) -> None:
    dom = parse(PAGE, parser)
    blocks = {b.text: b for b in dom.iter_blocks()}

    item = blocks["First point"]
    assert item.tag == "li"
    assert item.link_chars == len("point")
    assert 0.4 < item.link_density < 0.5
    assert [c.tag for c in item.path[:3]] == ["li", "ul", "div"]
    assert item.path[2].hint.strip() == "story body main"
    assert blocks["Rogue traders were caught today."].link_density == 0.0
    assert "var x = 1;" not in " ".join(blocks)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("parser", PARSERS)
def test_title_prefers_og_title(parser: ParserName) -> None:
def test_inner_matches_of_a_selector_list_are_not_duplicated() -> None:
    texts = ["Outer item with an inner paragraph and more", "inner paragraph", "and more", "Next one."]

    assert fates(texts, Profile(source="x", body="p")) == ["keep", "nested", "nested", "keep"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("parser", PARSERS)
def test_profile_strategy_applies_drops_and_stops(parser: ParserName) -> None:
    page = """<html><body><h1>Headline here</h1><div id="article-body">
      <p>Shares of Acme <span class="ticker-mention">( ACME -1.2% )</span> rose after the update today.</p>
      <p>Second paragraph of the story has words.</p>
      <div class="image"><p>Caption text for an image.</p></div>
      <p>Third paragraph of the story has words.</p>
      <p>Before you buy stock in Acme, consider this pitch.</p>
      <p>Pitch body that must not appear.</p>
    </div></body></html>"""
    paragraphs = profiles.extract(parse(page, parser), "https://www.fool.com/investing/x/", "fool")

    assert paragraphs == [
        "Shares of Acme rose after the update today.",
        "Second paragraph of the story has words.",
        "Third paragraph of the story has words.",
    ]


def test_profile_strategy_is_empty_for_unknown_sources() -> None:
    assert profiles.extract(parse("<p>text</p>"), "https://example.com/", None) == []
```

````
# 03 - Extraction

Question (Q10, R4): which parser and extractor recover a financial news body best and fastest, and does the
choice change what the `/signal` model decides? The answer is measured on the 90-article evaluation set with
the same `extract` function the API calls, not assumed from library benchmarks. Numbers come from
`evals/results/extraction/matrix.json` (summary tables in `evals/results/extraction/summary.md`).

## Setup

- **Articles**: the 90 committed articles, 10 sources with 9 each (Yahoo 10, BBC 8), fetched on
  2026-10-18. The stored HTML and the gold bodies stay in `evals/data/private/`; only ids, sources
  and numbers are committed. All splits are used: nothing in the extraction layer is tuned on them. The
  extraction code and source profiles were committed (M2) before the set existed (M3), and none of the 90 URLs
  is among the probe pages the profiles were tuned on (`02-source-probe.md`).
- **Gold body**: Opus chose line ranges from the page's visible-text lines (`evals/opus_prompts/20-gold.md`).
  The lines are the selectolax block walk (the `strip-tags` output), with very long blocks split into
  sentence chunks. The gold excludes the headline, dek, key-points boxes, captions, promos, financial tables and
  press-release boilerplate (About, forward-looking statements, contacts).
- **Rows (22)**: 4 parsers (`selectolax`, `lxml`, `bs4`, `bs4-lxml`) x 4 own strategies (`cascade`, `jsonld`,
  `profile`, `density`), plus 6 extractors that bring their own parser: `trafilatura` (default and
  `favor_precision`), `readability-lxml`, `newspaper4k`, `jusText` and the `strip-tags` baseline. Every row
  calls `veritrade.extract.registry.extract(html, final_url, parser=..., extractor=...)`. An extraction under
  40 words raises `ExtractionEmpty`, as in the API.

## Metrics

- **Tokens**: maximal runs of Python `\w` characters in the lowercased text; an extraction's text is its
  paragraphs joined by blank lines.
- **Precision, recall, F1**: bag of words with multiplicity. With `c(t)` the count of token `t`,
  `common = sum over t of min(c_extracted(t), c_gold(t))`, `P = common / |extracted|`,
  `R = common / |gold|`, `F1 = 2PR / (P + R)`. Each is a macro mean over the 90 articles, and a failed
  extraction scores 0 on all three. 95% CIs are percentile bootstraps over articles (B = 1000, same resamples
  for every row).
- **Leakage**: the share of extracted tokens that lie in no 5-token window also present, in order, in the
  gold token sequence. It is a mean over successful extractions, since a failure sends nothing. Bag-of-words
  `1 - P` is reported too. The two differ on purpose: `1 - P` credits a promo or caption that reuses the
  story's names and common words, and it penalises body text repeated twice. Order-aware coverage asks
  whether the text is part of the story. On this set the two agree within about 1 point per row, except
  `readability` (34.4% against 30.7%), where order-aware coverage flags more of the output.
- **Failure rate**: `ExtractionEmpty` or any exception, recorded by type name.
- **Time**: wall ms around one `extract` call, covering parse, strategy, JSON-LD scan and title. Each
  (row, article) gets one untimed warm-up, which is the output that gets scored, then 5 timed calls. The
  article's time is the median of the 5, and p50 / p95 are taken over the 90 articles, failures included. Rows
  are interleaved per article, so machine-load drift hits every row alike.
- **Tokens to the LLM**: `chars / 4`, the service's estimate, of `build_input(article, "full", uncapped)`
  (`TITLE:` line plus body), at p50. Served inputs are further capped at the model's `max_input_tokens`
  (2000 to 6000). The lede size is `build_input(article, "lede", 2000)`.
- **Install MB**: decimal MB of the files in each distribution's RECORD, summed over the row's dependency
  closure minus the backend core. The core is the closure of the backend's requirements with every parser and
  extractor package removed, so it is what a row adds to the app. Own strategies add nothing beyond their
  parser.
- **Downstream signal**: the `/signal` decision model `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` with its grid-best config `v4`
  (plain instructions, bare criteria) and the probability policy at the grid's operating point,
  `p >= 0.8` (abstentions become neutral, as served). The input is the serving lede,
  `build_input(article, "lede", 2000)`, built from each row's paragraphs. The title is held at the gold
  headline so that only the body varies. The reference is the same lede built from the gold body.
  Agreement is the share of the 90 articles whose verdict matches the gold-lede verdict, and a failed
  extraction counts as a miss. Calls go through the grid runner's `call_once` at concurrency 1. The
  prediction cache keys each record by (row, article) and reuses an answer when the input hash repeats.
  There were 2,070 records (1,980 rows x articles plus 90 gold ledes). The 362 failed extractions need no
  call, and the remaining 1,708 collapse to 380 distinct ledes, so the model answered 380 times.

## Results

### Quality: the parser does not matter

For every own strategy the four parsers give the same scores (F1 spread 0.0000). The shared block walker joins
text identically on every backend (`02-source-probe.md`), so the parser is purely a speed and footprint
choice. Own strategies below use `selectolax`.

| extractor | F1 [95% CI] | P | R | leakage | fail | tokens full (p50) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cascade` (served) | 0.929 [0.900, 0.957] | 0.909 | 0.975 | 9.0% | 0.0% | 769 |
| `density` | 0.932 [0.906, 0.957] | 0.910 | 0.977 | 8.8% | 0.0% | 720 |
| `profile` | 0.897 [0.855, 0.939] | 0.879 | 0.941 | 9.0% | 3.3% | 770 |
| `jsonld` | 0.100 [0.044, 0.167] | 0.100 | 0.100 | 0.0% | 90.0% | 917 |
| `trafilatura-precision` | 0.802 [0.738, 0.863] | 0.771 | 0.888 | 13.9% | 10.0% | 726 |
| `newspaper` | 0.800 [0.750, 0.853] | 0.776 | 0.911 | 21.3% | 2.2% | 742 |
| `trafilatura` | 0.797 [0.733, 0.858] | 0.762 | 0.889 | 15.0% | 10.0% | 739 |
| `justext` | 0.759 [0.714, 0.805] | 0.733 | 0.879 | 26.6% | 1.1% | 806 |
| `readability` | 0.644 [0.567, 0.716] | 0.623 | 0.781 | 34.4% | 10.0% | 822 |
| `strip-tags` | 0.512 [0.479, 0.545] | 0.360 | 1.000 | 63.0% | 0.0% | 2,116 |

The gold body itself is 438 tokens (p50); its `full` input is 690 tokens and its lede 128 tokens.

### Speed and footprint

p50 / p95 ms per article; install MB is what the parser adds to the app core.

| parser (parse p50 ms) | install MB | `cascade` | `density` | `profile` | `jsonld` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selectolax` (0.8) | 7.5 | 1.6 / 3.3 | 2.1 / 14.0 | 1.5 / 12.2 | 0.3 / 2.5 |
| `lxml` (1.9) | 20.0 | 2.5 / 6.8 | 3.5 / 27.8 | 3.0 / 27.5 | 0.3 / 2.6 |
| `bs4` (13.2) | 0.6 | 15.0 / 63.1 | 19.5 / 70.4 | 16.7 / 69.4 | 0.3 / 2.5 |
| `bs4-lxml` (8.2) | 20.5 | 11.2 / 48.8 | 14.6 / 57.4 | 12.6 / 56.2 | 0.3 / 2.6 |

| extractor | p50 ms | p95 ms | install MB | failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trafilatura-precision` | 19.3 | 70.4 | 60.8 | 9 (all SEC) |
| `trafilatura` | 15.6 | 70.3 | 60.8 | 9 (all SEC) |
| `newspaper` | 80.8 | 191 | 37.1 | 2 (1 SEC, 1 Yahoo) |
| `justext` | 12.1 | 52.4 | 22.4 | 1 (BBC) |
| `readability` | 24.8 | 150 | 23.4 | 9 (all Motley Fool) |
| `strip-tags` | 2.9 | 15.0 | 7.5 | none |

`bs4` is small because `beautifulsoup4` and `soupsieve` are pure Python, and it is the slowest parser for the
same reason. The `jsonld` rows never build a tree, so all four cost 0.3 ms. They fail on 81 of 90 pages,
because only CNN ships an `articleBody`.

### Per source

F1 by source. The `cascade` column also names the strategy that won.

### Downstream signal

On the 90 gold ledes, `clef-flash` calls 35 bullish, 28 bearish and 27 neutral (abstentions included). Each
row's verdicts are compared with those. Own strategies are shown on `selectolax`; the other parsers give
the same ledes.

| extractor | agree [95% CI] | agree, extracted pages only | lede identical to gold | bull/bear flips | directional lost | directional added | no verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cascade` (served) | 96.7% [92.2%, 100%] | 96.7% | 50.0% | 0 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| `density` | 96.7% [93.3%, 100%] | 96.7% | 64.4% | 0 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| `newspaper` | 95.6% [91.1%, 98.9%] | 97.7% | 56.7% | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| `profile` | 94.4% [90.0%, 98.9%] | 97.7% | 58.9% | 0 | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| `justext` | 93.3% [87.8%, 97.8%] | 94.4% | 21.1% | 0 | 4 | 1 | 1 |
| `trafilatura-precision` | 90.0% [83.3%, 95.6%] | 100% | 60.0% | 0 | 0 | 0 | 9 |
| `trafilatura` | 87.8% [81.1%, 94.4%] | 97.5% | 57.8% | 0 | 2 | 0 | 9 |
| `readability` | 85.6% [77.8%, 92.2%] | 95.1% | 40.0% | 0 | 3 | 1 | 9 |
| `strip-tags` | 83.3% [74.4%, 91.1%] | 83.3% | 0.0% | 0 | 14 | 1 | 0 |
| `jsonld` | 10.0% [4.4%, 16.7%] | 100% | 1.1% | 0 | 0 | 0 | 81 |

Column notes:

- "Directional lost" means a bullish or bearish gold verdict became neutral.
- "Added" is the reverse.
- "No verdict" is a failed extraction, which counts as a miss.

The cascade's 3 disagreements:

- 2 are SEC exhibits near the 0.8 threshold.
  - In one, the gold lede is bearish at 0.92 and the cascade lede leans bearish at 0.75, below the threshold,
    so it is served as neutral.
  - In the other, the gold lede leans bearish at 0.79, just under the threshold (served neutral), while the
    cascade lede reads bullish at 0.88. That is the one case in which the top class itself changes. The
    cascade fell back to `density` on that exhibit, and 21 of the 40 tokens in its lede are header lines
    that the gold leaves out.
- 1 is a PR Newswire release where the model abstains on the cascade lede (top probability 0.57). That
  lede holds only gold text, but it splits the opening into different paragraphs, so the cut lands elsewhere.

## Findings

1. **The parser is a speed and footprint choice, not a quality one.** All four give identical bodies.
   `selectolax` is the fastest (parse p50 0.8 ms against 1.9 for `lxml` and 13.2 for `bs4`) and adds 7.5 MB.
2. **`cascade` and `density` are tied on quality, and `cascade` is faster at the tail.** F1 is 0.929 for
   `cascade` against 0.932 for `density`; the paired gap is +0.003 [-0.007, +0.016], which is noise.
   `density` does better on Yahoo and PR Newswire and worse on Motley Fool and Fortune. The cascade's p95 is
   3.3 ms against 14.0, because a JSON-LD hit (CNN, 5.7 MB pages) returns before any tree is built.
3. **The cascade's fallback earns its place on SEC.** The SEC profile fails on the 3 exhibits whose filer
   agent emits no `<p>` (profile alone: F1 0.59, 3 failures). The cascade falls through to `density` and
   reaches 0.91 with no failure.
4. **Where the served cascade still leaks, it leaks at the end of the story.** Leakage is 31% on
   GlobeNewswire, 24% on Yahoo and 22% on PR Newswire, and under 7% elsewhere. In counts, 1,676 of the
   GlobeNewswire, 1,265 of the PR Newswire and 1,082 of the Yahoo leaked tokens sit after the last gold
   paragraph: release boilerplate and attachment lists that the stop markers miss, and the trailing
   partner-promo and list blocks on Yahoo. This costs the `full` scope (`/summary`, `/analyze`) tokens, not
   the lede.
5. **Every third-party extractor trails the own strategies here, and each has a source it breaks on.**
   - `trafilatura` returns nothing for all 9 SEC exhibits, because it rejects the EDGAR SGML envelope
     around the HTML. On the pages where it succeeds its F1 is 0.89, close to the own strategies.
   - `readability` picks the same 21-word block on every Motley Fool page, before our adapter touches the
     output, and the wrong block on Fortune (F1 0.08).
   - `newspaper4k` is the slowest (p50 81 ms) and not deterministic: on one Yahoo page it returned two
     different bodies across repeated calls in one process.
   - `jusText` keeps boilerplate (27% leakage).
6. **Extraction quality barely moves the lede signal until the extraction is wrong.**
   - Every extractor that finds the story agrees with the gold-lede verdict on 94 to 100% of the pages it
     extracts, even though its lede is byte-identical to the gold lede on only 21 to 64% of the 90 pages.
   - What costs agreement is failing outright (`trafilatura` on SEC, `readability` on Motley Fool) or
     putting page chrome in the lede. `strip-tags` loses 14 of 63 directional calls, because navigation
     text pushes the story out of the 200-token lede and the model abstains.
   - No row turns a served bullish verdict into a bearish one or back: bad extraction makes the model
     abstain, it does not make it invert.
7. **Tokens**: competent extractors send 720 to 822 tokens of `full` input (p50), against 2,116 for
   `strip-tags`. Ledes are 119 to 129 tokens for every extractor that finds the story.

## What we serve and why

The default stays **`selectolax` + `cascade`** (already the `registry.extract` default):

- **Quality**: best or tied F1 (0.929 [0.900, 0.957]), zero failures on the 90 pages, and 96.7% [92.2%, 100%]
  agreement with the gold-lede verdict, with no inversion.
- **Speed**: the lowest tail of any row that finds bodies, p50 1.6 ms and p95 3.3 ms. That is noise
  against the 500 ms `/signal` budget.
- **Footprint and provenance**: 7.5 MB, no third-party extractor needed at runtime, and the winning method
  (`jsonld`, `profile` or `density`) is reported in every response's meta.

`density` is not promoted despite its nominal lead: the gap is inside the noise, its p95 is four times
higher, and the cascade already falls back to it where profiles fail. The other 21 rows stay selectable from
the UI and the API (Q10) so the comparison can be repeated on any URL. If a source-agnostic default were ever
needed, `trafilatura-precision` would be the candidate once the SEC envelope is unwrapped (Requests). It
costs 60.8 MB and about 12 times the cascade's p50.

## Requests

These are for the extraction owner; the bench does not change backend code.

1. **Unwrap the EDGAR envelope for third-party extractors.** Synthetic repro
   (`.temp/P4/extraction/repro_sec_envelope.py`): wrap a 4-paragraph `<html>` page in
   `<DOCUMENT><TYPE>EX-99.1 ... <TEXT> ... </TEXT></DOCUMENT>`. `registry.extract(..., extractor="trafilatura")`
   then raises `ExtractionEmpty`, and so does `trafilatura-precision`. Both return 164 words for the inner
   `<html>` alone, while `readability`, `justext` and `cascade` handle both. Passing the inner `<html>...</html>`
   (or the `<TEXT>` body) to the third-party adapters would fix all 9 SEC failures.
2. **Tighten the tails of three profiles.** These selectors are counted only on the profile's body matches,
   with no text read.
   - GlobeNewswire: leaked `p` after the story inside `div#main-body-container`, and the attachment blocks
     `p#gnw_attachments_section-header` and `ul#gnw_attachments_section-items` (droppable by selector).
   - PR Newswire: trailing `p` in `div.col-lg-10` that no stop marker catches.
   - Yahoo: trailing `p.text-block` inside `div.read-more-wrapper` (partner promos) and a trailing
     `ul.yf-1jsc1up` list. The hashed class is fragile.
   - A `--reanalyze` pass of the probe on these pages would show which stop markers to add.

## Caveats

- **The gold leans toward the own strategies, and toward the cascade in particular.**
  - Opus picked from the same selectolax block lines that the own strategies walk, so their text matches the
    gold token for token. Third-party extractors join text their own way and lose a little even on the right
    blocks.
  - The gold packets folded the page outside the span the served cascade found. Opus could open the full
    page, but the default view was anchored on the cascade.
  - So the gap between own and third-party extractors is an upper bound. The ranking among third-party
    extractors, and the failures listed above, do not depend on it.
- **One annotator, small n.** Opus made one gold body per page and no human checked them. There are 9 pages
  per source, so per-source numbers rest on 9 pages, and one signal disagreement moves agreement by 1.1 points.
- **Timings come from a shared workstation.** It is an Apple M4 Pro with 14 cores and 48 GB. During the
  run, the mean 1-minute load average was 24.6 (max 43.7) and Ollama had a model resident in 85 of 90
  per-article samples, because other evals were running. Medians of 5 and per-article interleaving keep the
  comparison fair, but absolute milliseconds are pessimistic. This is not the latency suite.
- **The signal check is narrow.** It uses one decision model at one operating point, and agreement is with
  that model's own verdict on the gold lede, not with the labels: the test split's labels stay reserved for
  the one-shot holdout. It covers the lede only, so tail leakage (finding 4) is not exercised.
- **The title is held fixed in the signal check.** The served title, from the JSON-LD headline, `og:title` or
  `<title>`, equals the gold headline in 87% of articles for own strategies and 96% for `trafilatura`.
- **Install sizes are macOS arm64 wheels.** Linux wheels differ, and runtime `__pycache__` is not counted.
- **Versions**: `selectolax` 1.0.1, `lxml` 6.1.3, `beautifulsoup4` 4.15.0, `trafilatura` 2.3.1,
  `readability-lxml` 0.8.4.1, `newspaper4k` 0.9.6, `justext` 3.0.2, and Ollama 0.40.6.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench list      # the 22 rows
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench measure   # timing + quality, CPU only, resumable (~5 min)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench signal    # lede verdicts via native Ollama, concurrency 1
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report    # evals/results/extraction/{matrix.json,summary.md}
```

`measure` and `signal` need the private article files (`articles verify` passes). `signal` reads the operating
point from `evals/results/grid/signal__clef-flash_9b-q8_0.json`, so re-run it after the grid's best config
changes.
````

```
# Extraction matrix

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report` from local measurements; no article text is stored here.

- Data: the 90 committed articles (all splits, none tuned on) from 10 sources; stored HTML through the serving `veritrade.extract.registry.extract`; third-party extractors bring their own parser (parser column `(built-in)`).
- Quality: macro means over articles against the Opus gold body. Tokens are lowercased `\w+` runs; P/R/F1 are bag-of-words with multiplicity; a failed extraction scores 0. Leakage is the share of extracted tokens outside every 5-token window that also occurs in the gold body (successful extractions only). 95% CIs: bootstrap over articles (B=1000).
- Time: wall ms of one `extract` call (parse + extract), median of 5 runs per article after a warm-up, then p50/p95 over articles, failures included.
- Tokens: chars / 4 of the uncapped `full` input (title + body) at p50; lede = the `/signal` lede input at the decision model's budget.
- Install: decimal MB of the RECORD files a row adds to the backend core (its closure without any parser or extractor); own strategies add 0 beyond their parser.
- Signal: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` v4 (grid best), served sentiment at p >= 0.8; agreement = share of articles whose verdict on the row's lede equals the verdict on the gold lede, title held at the gold headline; a failed extraction is a miss.
- Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Python 3.13.12; Ollama had a model resident in 85/90 per-article samples (another eval was running), mean 1-min load average 24.6.
```
