```
# 01 - Design decisions

Every decision below was settled with Kris in a `/grill-me` interview (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-18) before any code
was written. Background facts came from read-only research agents (local machine, Ollama library, Docker/CI, news
sources, datasets, transcript format) and were re-verified against primary sources where they were surprising
(the Ollama decision-model API). The full conversation is in `.context/transcript/`.

Guiding principle (Kris, R2): **this is a PoC - balance the level of rigor per aspect**, no exhaustive sweeps.

## Round 1

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Where does the Ollama server run? | Native Ollama on the host is the documented default on macOS; a `bundled` compose profile runs `ollama/ollama` (CPU) for Linux/CI; `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` switches; benchmarks are labelled `native-metal` / `docker-cpu` | Docker Desktop cannot pass Apple's GPU into Linux containers (~0.2x prompt-eval, ~0.4x generation vs native); reviewers on Macs will have Ollama anyway |
| Q2 | What does "precision" mean, how is a winner picked? | Positives are directional calls (bullish/bearish); neutral is the safe default. Selection metric F0.5 macro over {bullish, bearish}; bullish<->bearish inversions capped at 2%; winner = best F0.5 inside the latency budget, else the Pareto knee | A wrong call costs a trade, a missed call costs little; F0.5 cannot be gamed by "always neutral" |
| Q3 | Sentiment output contract | 3-class `sentiment` + `abstained`; compare two precision knobs for generative models (label-token logprob threshold vs ordinal -2..+2 \|score\| threshold) and keep the better one; decision models threshold their native class probabilities | Ollama emits logprobs, but only for non-streaming calls; the ordinal knob also works when streaming |
| Q4 | What does the quick signal read? | `scope=lede` (headline + opening paragraphs) by default, `scope=full` available; both evaluated for accuracy and speed | Lede matches headline-level datasets and decision-model context limits; prompt length drives latency |
| Q5 | Article-level gold set | 90 real articles (10 sources x 3 classes x 3), labelled by Opus subagents, no human check | Public datasets are sentences/headlines; real requests are full articles |
| Q6 | Public datasets and splits | Dev: stratified 300 from Twitter Financial News train. Holdout: full Twitter validation + Financial PhraseBank AllAgree (downloaded at eval time, never committed, CC BY-NC-SA) + FinEntity single-label paragraphs | Twitter FNS already uses Bearish/Bullish/Neutral and has official splits; FPB is the cleanest cross-domain check |
| Q7 | Prompt tuning method | Automated grid per model, then one manual error-analysis pass, freeze, run holdout once. Optional backlog starts with a DSPy-style optimizer loop | Reproducible and explainable within a PoC budget |
| Q8 | API surface | `/api/signal`, `/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`, `/api/models`, `/api/health`; model allowlist; per-URL fetch cache with single-flight; result cache; timing breakdown in every response; SSE **and** JSON variants for `/summary` and `/analyze` | Streaming improves perceived latency; both variants make the comparison measurable |
| Q9 | How the UI is served | Reopened in round 2 (R1) | - |
| Q10 | Extraction | Full parser x extractor comparison matrix, switchable from the UI, results published | Extraction quality and speed both feed end-to-end latency |
| Q11 | Fixtures and publisher rights | Skeleton fixtures (real DOM structure, synthetic text) + scheduled live smoke; article texts never committed (URL + hash + labels only) | Respect each publisher's content rights in a public repo |
| Q12 | CI | Everything on GitHub Actions, including e2e with a real tiny model | Free for public repos |
| Q13 | Transcript | Redacted raw JSONL + rendered Markdown/HTML + `meta.json` under `.context/transcript/`, stripped of anything not suitable for a public repo | The brief asks for the AI log; Kris wants reviewers to read it |
| Q14 | Git workflow | Milestone commits straight to `main`, no feature branches; repo-local author Kristiyan Dimitrov; public repo `cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics` | Solo PoC |
| Q15 | Tooling | Python 3.13 uv workspace (`backend`, `evals`), ruff + mypy; Node 24 + pnpm, Next.js 16 strict TS, ESLint + Prettier, Vitest + RTL + MSW, Playwright | Conventional, fast |
| Q16 | Native Ollama install | `brew install ollama` + `brew services` | Metal acceleration for evals and the native path |
| Q17 | Model roster | See R2 and the follow-ups | - |
| Q18 | Top-10 sources | Yahoo Finance, CNBC, AP News, Investing.com, Motley Fool, Benzinga, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business; backups Fortune, Business Wire, Guardian, BBC; the live probe decides | Reviewer likelihood x accessibility; the brief names earnings reports, EDGAR is their primary source |
| Q19 | Fetch identity | Standard browser header set, no evasion (no captcha solving, proxies or TLS impersonation); typed `source_blocked` / `paywalled` / `consent_required` errors with hints; `SEC_USER_AGENT` for EDGAR | Neither end of the spectrum |
| Q20 | Yahoo EU consent wall | Submit "reject all" and cache the cookie; fall back to `consent_required` | Gets the article without granting tracking consent on anyone's behalf |

## Round 2

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | UI serving topology | FastAPI serves the static Next.js export from the same origin (multi-stage Docker build); dev uses `pnpm dev` + CORS for localhost | No proxy hop on the latency path, no nginx, no Node at runtime; the brief requires a Python backend anyway |
| R2 | Decision models | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` + `nimble:9b-q4_K_M`, with `qwen3.5:0.8b` as the generative baseline | PoC balance; clef-flash by request, nimble best published accuracy among the rest |
| R3 | Streaming `/analyze` | Typed SSE events `meta` -> `sentiment` -> `summary_delta*` -> `done`; JSON field order (sentiment-first vs summary-first) is an eval dimension | Sentiment arrives after a handful of output tokens when it is generated first |
| R4 | Extraction matrix + reference | 4 parsers x 4 own strategies + trafilatura (default, precision), readability-lxml, newspaper4k, justext, strip-tags; reference bodies produced by Opus, kept local (gitignored) | Comparable quality metric without publishing article text |
| R5 | Article-set procedure | Opus discovery via RSS/sections (last ~60 days, fetchable by our fetcher); two independent Opus labellers + adjudicator, ambiguous articles replaced; agreement reported; split 30 dev / 60 test | Stand-in for a human check |
| R6 | Summary evaluation | Deterministic checks (numbers grounded in source, entity named, length) + key-fact coverage via a local embedding model + Opus-as-judge on finalists | Cheap reproducible signal plus a strong judge where it matters |
| R7 | Latency budgets (native, warm, excl. fetch) | `/signal` lede p50 <= 500 ms; `/summary` and `/analyze` TTFT <= 1.5 s, complete p50 <= 4 s; unrealistic budgets are surfaced, not silently moved | Concrete selection gate |
| R8 | Bundled models | Per-endpoint winners if they total <= ~10 GB, else the best finalist that fits; all other Docker containers stopped during setup | Docker Desktop VM has 15.6 GiB |
| R9 | Transcript scope | Only this build session (main + subagents + workflows) | No other relevant sessions |
| R10 | Docs layout | `.context/docs/design/NN-*.md`, backlog in `90-optional-backlog.md`, eval reports in `evals/results/` | Book-order reading |

## Follow-ups

- Generative roster trimmed: summary {`qwen3.5:2b`, `qwen3.5:4b`}; combined {`qwen3.5:4b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`,
  `ministral-3:3b`}; `qwen3.5:9b` only as a holdout quality ceiling; Gemma 4 dropped (open think+format bug).
- Lean prompt grid: 2 rubric styles x few-shot {0, 4} x field order where relevant (<= 8 configs per model).
- Stopped Docker containers stay stopped; the restart command is handed back at the end.
- `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` is used only in CI to exercise the real decision-model path in containers; it is not evaluated.

## Build-time findings that adjusted the plan

Measured during P1/P2, recorded here so the deviations are traceable. Inputs for the Ollama probe were synthetic
(`evals/results/ollama_probe.json`, native Metal, warm, n=5).

- **Sources** (`02-source-probe.md`): AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
  their CDN (Cloudflare / Akamai), so all four backups were promoted. Final 10: Yahoo Finance, CNBC, Motley Fool,
  PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune, Guardian Business, BBC Business.
- **R7 sanity gate passed**: each endpoint has at least one candidate inside its budget, so no budget moved.
  - `/signal`: `qwen3.5:0.8b` answers in 190 ms at ~510 prompt tokens. The 9B decision models take 1.3-1.5 s
    at the same size, so they are reported against the budget rather than the budget relaxed for them.
  - `/summary`: `qwen3.5:2b` shows first text at 0.93 s and finishes at 2.2 s on ~1.6k-token articles;
    `qwen3.5:4b` misses the 1.5 s TTFT budget at that size (2.4 s).
  - `/analyze`: `ministral-3:3b` reaches the score at 1.47 s and finishes at 3.5 s on ~1.75k tokens; the 4B
    qwen models miss TTFT at full-article size.
- **Logprobs**: Ollama 0.40.6 also returns logprobs on streamed chunks (undocumented). The knob comparison stays
  on non-streaming `/signal`; `/analyze` keeps the ordinal knob. Logprob-weighted streaming confidence goes to
  the backlog.
- **Field order**: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` ignores schema property order (always entity, score, summary) and
  ignores `think:false` when a schema is set, so the field-order dimension runs on `qwen3.5:4b` and
  `ministral-3:3b` only.
- **Fetch cap** raised from 5 MB to 10 MB: CNN article pages are 5.7-6.6 MB decompressed.
- **Sampling penalties zeroed**: the qwen3.5 Modelfiles ship `presence_penalty 1.5`, which still applies under
  greedy decoding. Few-shot answers end in `neutral` / `0`, so the penalty pushed generated labels away from
  neutral (26 of 60 dev tweets disagreed with the logprob argmax; 0 of 60 with the penalty off). Every chat call
  now pins `presence_penalty 0`, `frequency_penalty 0`, `repeat_penalty 1`; `num_predict` still bounds runaway
  output.
- **Length-cut generations are salvaged**: a summary or analyze output that hits `num_predict` returns its fields
  with the summary cut to the last full sentence and `truncated: true`, instead of a 502 after a doubled-budget
  retry.
- **Summary length is enforced in serving** (R6 follow-up): no candidate reached the 0.8 deterministic pass rate
  on the dev articles, mostly on the 60-word cap. Rather than relax the gate, the service caps every summary at
  3 sentences / 60 words at a sentence boundary, and the frozen prompts ask for 2-3 sentences of at most 50 words
  that name the primary entity first.
- **Key-fact coverage threshold 0.60** (R6): a hand spot-check of 45 key facts on 10 dev articles agreed best
  at a cosine of 0.60 (33/45); 0.75 marked no false "covered" but missed 20 stated facts. 0.60 is primary and
  0.75 is reported as a conservative bound; the Opus judge remains the selection signal.
```

```
# Signal grid on dev300

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.grid analyze` from the local prediction cache; no dataset text is stored here.

- Data: dev300, 300 Twitter Financial News train tweets, 100 per class; every rate is weighted back to the train prior (bullish 20.2%, bearish 15.1%, neutral 64.7%). Confusion and error counts are raw.
- Selection: F0.5 macro over bullish/bearish; operating point = best F0.5 with bullish<->bearish inversions <= 2% of directional calls; below the threshold the call abstains to neutral.
- Policies: decision models threshold native class probabilities (min_p); generative /signal thresholds first-token label probabilities (label schema) or the |score| of an ordinal -2..2 schema (t in {1, 2}); both probability policies are also swept with the served `directional_tau` rule (min_p 0, see below); /analyze is streamed sentiment-first and always uses |score|.
- Decoding: Ollama options temperature=0, seed=0, presence_penalty=0, frequency_penalty=0, repeat_penalty=1 on every generative call (greedy; overrides the penalties some Modelfiles ship).
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000) at the chosen threshold; the threshold choice itself is not resampled, so these are optimistic.
- Latency: per-call wall ms during the grid run (Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal, warm, client concurrency 1); /analyze is time to the score with the stream stopped there. Indicative only: the latency suite runs separately.

## Knob comparison: logprob threshold vs ordinal threshold

### `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0`

| knob | config | reads | threshold | F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull | P bear | inversion | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| logprob | v2-label | label tokens | none | 0.512 [0.408, 0.602] | 1.000 | 0.837 | 0.0% | 100.0% |
| ordinal | v4-ordinal | score value | \|s\| >= 1 | 0.453 [0.350, 0.549] | 0.726 | 1.000 | 1.4% | 100.0% |

Paired bootstrap, logprob minus ordinal: F0.5 gap +0.059 [-0.068, +0.187]; no significant difference at n=300 (95% CI of the gap spans 0).

## directional_tau vs the plain rule

The plain rule calls the argmax class and abstains below min_p, so a model that keeps most of its mass on neutral is never pushed into a call. The served `directional_tau` rule (min_p 0) calls the likelier directional class when neutral leads and that class holds p >= tau; a leading directional class is always called, and below tau the row is a served neutral, not an abstention. Both rules are tuned on these 300 tweets; the gap is a paired bootstrap.

| model | rule | config | threshold | F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull | P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | tau - plain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Notes from the error-analysis read

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no dataset text. These are
tweets, not articles: the thresholds and latencies here are a starting point for the article dev set, not a
substitute for it.

**A decoding fix came out of this grid.** The qwen3.5 Modelfiles ship `presence_penalty 1.5`, and the client
only pinned temperature and seed, so "greedy" qwen3.5 output was pushed away from any token in the recent
context. With four shots whose last answer is neutral (or score 0), the generated qwen3.5:0.8b label disagreed
with its own first-token argmax on 84/300 (v2) and 62/300 (v4) tweets, and v2-ordinal emitted -2 for 104/300.
`FIXED_OPTIONS` now neutralises the penalties; every number on this page comes from the greedy re-run. The
label-logprob cells were identical before and after (logprobs are reported before the penalty is applied), and
seven cells re-run to replace contended timings reproduced their predictions exactly, so the cache and decoding
are deterministic.

**Decision models lead on precision.** clef-flash v4 (plain question, bare labels) reaches F0.5 0.874 at
min_p 0.80 with no inversions, answering 73% of tweets and calling 33% directional against a 35% directional
prior. nimble over-calls: with no threshold it calls 65-74% of tweets directional, and it only becomes precise
at min_p 0.97-0.98, where it answers about a quarter of the tweets (F0.5 0.843 for v1). The served
`directional_tau` rule runs at min_p 0, so for these peaked models it only removes their abstention: it loses
to the plain rule by 0.046 (clef-flash) and 0.303 (nimble) F0.5, both significant, and is not served for them.

**qwen3.5:0.8b is neutral-leaning, which caps the served label policy.** Its first-token argmax is neutral on
most directional tweets (0.3-7% signal rate across label configs), so a min_p threshold can only remove calls:
the plain rule (v2-label, no abstention) misses 162 of 200 directional tweets at F0.5 0.512. The served
`directional_tau` rule calls the likelier directional class when neutral leads and that class reaches tau;
at tau 0.28 it gives F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] with precision 0.91 / 0.92 and no inversions (+0.218
[+0.141, +0.307] paired). It is the largest single lever found here, it is now the model's best config, and it
is frozen (min_p 0, directional_tau 0.28).

**Knob verdict for qwen3.5:0.8b.** As served (argmax + min_p on label tokens vs |score| >= t on the ordinal
schema), the best label config beats the best ordinal config by +0.059 F0.5 [-0.068, +0.187]: not significant
at n=300. With the `directional_tau` rule the logprob knob wins clearly. The ordinal schema cannot borrow that
rule: this tokenizer fuses the space and the minus sign (" -") while the bare-space alternative keeps about a
quarter of the mass, so the sign is unobservable for negative scores. `score_sign_probabilities` used to read
those as bearish 1.0 (and miss the " -" mass behind positive scores). It now returns None for every negative
score in these cells (48, 32, 17 and 8 of 300), and serving falls back to the ordinal policy there.

**Prompt dimensions.**
- Rubric A (definitions) beats rubric B (impact questions) for every generative model. B's "is the change
  clear and material" framing makes the small models answer neutral: qwen3.5:0.8b v3-label calls 0.3% of
  tweets directional, and ministral drops from 0.660 to 0.440.
- Four synthetic shots help qwen3.5:0.8b on the label schema (0.365 to 0.512) but hurt every /analyze model:
  qwen3.5:4b 0.752 to 0.655, ministral 0.660 to 0.494, and qwen3-instruct v2 breaks the inversion cap. Shots
  also roughly double qwen3.5:4b's time to score.
- For the decision models the spread across prompts is small (clef 0.83-0.87, nimble 0.81-0.84). Bare labels
  with the short question are also the fastest variant (clef 468 vs 710 ms, nimble 751 vs 975 ms).

**Where the calls go wrong.**
- Inversions are nearly absent: one bullish tweet called bearish across all six best configs.
- Wrong calls are mostly gold-neutral tweets called directional (1-8 per model). Relative to its size, the
  earnings and guidance bucket holds the most of them (13 across the six models in 46 tweets, against 14 in
  128 for the catch-all bucket), which fits mixed results (a beat alongside a cut outlook) being the hard case.
- The real loss is recall: 34 (clef-flash) to 162 (qwen3.5:0.8b) directional tweets missed.
- The biggest miss bucket for every generative model is the price-move tweet: 33-44 of 57 directional ones
  missed, against 10 for clef-flash. The rubrics ask for economic impact, not tone, and the small models read
  a reported share-price move as not material, while the dataset labels such moves as directional. Whether to
  close that gap is a product question: on articles the impact reading is the intended behaviour.
- Analyst actions (upgrades, price targets) are handled well by the larger models (qwen3.5:4b catches 21 of
  22, clef-flash 19 of 22, with no wrong calls).
- 20 directional tweets get no correct call from any model; they are the first place to look for label noise
  or genuinely ambiguous items.

**Follow-ups after the grid (analyze).** Two cells per model, each paired against v1 on the same tweets
and never eligible as the best config.
- v5 = v1 with the summary rule tightened after the summary eval (2 to 3 sentences, at most 50 words, entity
  first). Only the summary line changes, yet the score moves: ministral +0.025 [+0.002, +0.052], qwen3-instruct
  -0.011 [-0.047, +0.023], qwen3.5:4b -0.021 [-0.054, +0.007]. On the article dev set qwen3.5:4b loses more
  (0.800 vs 0.880, gap -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]: two more bullish articles missed), so the freeze keeps v1 for
  qwen3.5:4b /analyze and serves v5 to ministral and qwen3-instruct.
- `v1-summary-first` (the field-order check) is never better: ministral -0.017 [-0.088, +0.059], qwen3.5:4b
  -0.061 [-0.122, +0.003], and its time to the score is 1.0-1.5 s against 0.15-0.6 s, because the whole
  summary decodes first. Every /analyze model stays sentiment-first.

**The one manual revision.** Few-shot is dropped for /analyze (every frozen /analyze prompt is zero-shot).
The price-move / analyst-action sentence was not added: on the article dev set the /analyze models miss 0-1
of the 5 directional price-move headlines and no headline falls in the analyst-action bucket, so the tweet
misses do not carry over (see `evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md`). qwen3.5:0.8b keeps its four shots: they
help the label schema (0.365 to 0.512 plain).

**Timing provenance.** Wall times are per call at client concurrency 1, warm. Concurrent load on the shared
machine (mostly the Docker Desktop VM saturating the CPU) inflated some tails, so clef-flash v2 and nimble v2/v3
were re-run at 19:28-19:47 and all eight qwen3.5:0.8b cells at 20:11-20:25, each with identical predictions.
The tables show the re-run timings. The qwen3.5:0.8b re-run still shared the machine (load about 30): on a
quiet machine earlier the same calls measured p50 155-200 ms with p95 near 210-300 ms, against 209-276 ms and
up to 1.06 s here. nimble v3's tail is also somewhat elevated. The analyze follow-ups (v5, summary-first)
ran later at concurrency 1 on an Ollama shared with two other eval runs, so their timings are indicative only.
```

```
## Notes

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no article text. With 10
articles per class, read these as a check that the dev300 operating points transfer, not as a ranking.

**Every served rule holds.** No served rule clearly fails (no inversion CI above the 2% cap, no coverage
collapse), so every dev300 threshold is frozen as tuned and nothing was re-picked on the articles.

**/signal.**
- clef-flash v4 at p >= 0.80 scores F0.5 0.848 on the lede and 0.907 on the full body, close to its dev300
  0.874. It makes one inversion in 20 calls on the lede and none on the full body.
- nimble v1 at p >= 0.97 answers far more articles than tweets (coverage 60-67% against 26% on dev300) at
  F0.5 0.88-0.90: articles state their news more plainly than tweets, so the peaked model is sure more often.
- qwen3.5:0.8b with `directional_tau` 0.28 scores 0.685 on the lede against 0.595 for the plain rule (a tie
  at n=30); on the full body the tau rule wins clearly (+0.229 [+0.022, +0.560]). It still misses about half
  the directional articles, so it remains the fast, low-recall option.
- Lede vs full is a tie for all three models; the lede (the /signal default) is two to three times faster.

**/analyze.**
- Articles are easier than tweets for every generative model: qwen3.5:4b v1 0.880, qwen3-instruct 0.798 and
  ministral 0.741, against 0.75 / 0.66 / 0.66 on dev300.
- The tightened summary rule (v5) changes no ministral call, costs qwen3-instruct one (a tie), and costs
  qwen3.5:4b two bullish and one bearish article plus one false alarm (-0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). It therefore
  keeps v1 for /analyze; its /summary endpoint still gets the tightened summary prompt.
- Summary-first is a tie on the articles (qwen3.5:4b -0.013, ministral +0.058) and never wins on dev300,
  while its time to the score is two to three times longer. Every model stays sentiment-first.
- The wrong calls are mostly neutral articles called directional (3-5 of the 10 per model, mostly bullish).
  Price-move headlines are not the problem they were on tweets (0-1 of the 5 directional ones missed per
  model), so the price-move / analyst-action rubric sentence was not added.
```

```
# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

## /signal finalists

Served = the dev300 best rule for the model. P / R are precision / recall; inversions are raw bullish<->bearish calls over directional calls.

| model | config | rule | threshold (dev300) | scope | served | F0.5 [95% CI] | bull P / R | bear P / R | inversions | coverage | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | p50 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | v4 | probability | p >= 0.8 | lede | yes | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 0.83 / 1.00 | 0.88 / 0.70 | 1/20 | 77% | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 718 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | v4 | probability+tau | tau 0.48 | lede |  | 0.814 [0.688, 0.924] | 0.71 / 1.00 | 0.89 / 0.80 | 1/23 | 100% | 0.770 [0.705, 0.854] | 718 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | v4 | probability | p >= 0.8 | full | yes | 0.907 [0.820, 0.989] | 0.83 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.80 | 0/20 | 77% | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 1911 |

## Notes

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no article text. With 10
articles per class, read these as a check that the dev300 operating points transfer, not as a ranking.

**Every served rule holds.** No served rule clearly fails (no inversion CI above the 2% cap, no coverage
collapse), so every dev300 threshold is frozen as tuned and nothing was re-picked on the articles.

**/signal.**
- clef-flash v4 at p >= 0.80 scores F0.5 0.848 on the lede and 0.907 on the full body, close to its dev300
  0.874. It makes one inversion in 20 calls on the lede and none on the full body.
- nimble v1 at p >= 0.97 answers far more articles than tweets (coverage 60-67% against 26% on dev300) at
  F0.5 0.88-0.90: articles state their news more plainly than tweets, so the peaked model is sure more often.
- qwen3.5:0.8b with `directional_tau` 0.28 scores 0.685 on the lede against 0.595 for the plain rule (a tie
  at n=30); on the full body the tau rule wins clearly (+0.229 [+0.022, +0.560]). It still misses about half
  the directional articles, so it remains the fast, low-recall option.
- Lede vs full is a tie for all three models; the lede (the /signal default) is two to three times faster.
```

```
# Summary evaluation

Decision R6: deterministic checks, key-fact coverage by a local embedding model, and Claude Opus as a
blind judge. Summaries come from the serving adapters (`/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`) with the default
`selectolax` + `cascade` extraction and `full` scope, run on the stored HTML of the Opus article set.
Written by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval report`; no article or summary text is committed.
Every check scores the served summary: serving caps it at 3 sentences and 60 words
(`cap_summary` in `veritrade.inference.adapters`), and `score` applies the same cap to cached generations.

Coverage threshold spot check:

- 10 summaries, 45 key facts, 29 of them stated in the summary by hand label (read in the private files)
- at 0.60: 33 of 45 flags right, 5 wrongly covered, 7 wrongly not covered
- at 0.75: 25 of 45 flags right, 0 wrongly covered, 20 wrongly not covered
- Hand labels from reading the summaries as generated before the serving cap; the flags shown in the review file used 0.75.

## Definitions

- **Pass**: <= 60 words, <= 3 sentences (serving sentence splitter), every number
  grounded, entity named, not truncated. Rates are over all articles; a candidate that produced no summary
  fails every check. Length holds by construction for served summaries; **Capped** is the share the cap
  had to shorten (whole leading sentences kept; an overlong first sentence ends in an ellipsis).
- **Numbers**: every number in the summary appears in the gold title or body. Thousands separators, `%`,
  currency symbols and units are ignored and 1.50 equals 1.5; number words up to twenty in the article
  ground their digits; Q1-Q4 / H1-H2 match the same token, `third quarter` / `first half`, `September
  quarter` or `July to September` (calendar quarters); `FY27` matches 2027; `80K` matches 80,000 (K/M/B
  abbreviations); a clock time on the hour (`5:00 p.m.`) matches the bare hour (`5PM`). Derived figures
  (a percentage change the model computed) count as unsupported: the prompt asks for verbatim numbers.
- **Entity**: the gold entity appears (case-insensitive, whole words); or its short name, without legal
  suffixes (Inc, Corp, Ltd, plc, Holdings, Group, ...) and trailing descriptors (Entertainment,
  Technologies, Industries, ...), as a phrase or as all its words anywhere (`UK ... economy`); or its first
  word when the name has several words and that word has 4+ letters and is not generic (American, United,
  Bank, ...); or the gold ticker (case-sensitive, also without an exchange suffix such as `.HK`).
- **Truncated**: the output hit `num_predict` and the serving path cut it to its last full sentence.
- **Key facts**: each of the 3-5 Opus key facts and each summary sentence is embedded with
  `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact is covered when its best cosine is >= 0.60, the threshold
  that agreed best with hand labels in the spot check. Mean share per article. **Key facts (strict)** uses
  0.75, where every flagged fact was really stated: a conservative lower bound.
- **Faithful / Cover**: Opus judge scores 1-5 (`evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md`), candidates anonymised and
  shuffled per article. **Halluc.**: share of judged summaries with at least one unsupported claim.
  **Leads**: share the judge found leading with the market-moving fact.
```

```
# Extraction matrix

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report` from local measurements; no article text is stored here.

- Data: the 90 committed articles (all splits, none tuned on) from 10 sources; stored HTML through the serving `veritrade.extract.registry.extract`; third-party extractors bring their own parser (parser column `(built-in)`).
- Quality: macro means over articles against the Opus gold body. Tokens are lowercased `\w+` runs; P/R/F1 are bag-of-words with multiplicity; a failed extraction scores 0. Leakage is the share of extracted tokens outside every 5-token window that also occurs in the gold body (successful extractions only). 95% CIs: bootstrap over articles (B=1000).
- Time: wall ms of one `extract` call (parse + extract), median of 5 runs per article after a warm-up, then p50/p95 over articles, failures included.
- Tokens: chars / 4 of the uncapped `full` input (title + body) at p50; lede = the `/signal` lede input at the decision model's budget.
- Install: decimal MB of the RECORD files a row adds to the backend core (its closure without any parser or extractor); own strategies add 0 beyond their parser.
- Signal: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` v4 (grid best), served sentiment at p >= 0.8; agreement = share of articles whose verdict on the row's lede equals the verdict on the gold lede, title held at the gold headline; a failed extraction is a miss.
- Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Python 3.13.12; Ollama had a model resident in 85/90 per-article samples (another eval was running), mean 1-min load average 24.6.
```

```
"""`uv run python -m veritrade_evals <command>`: dataset, split and evaluation commands."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any, Protocol

from veritrade_evals import articles_cli, extraction_bench, finalists, freeze, grid, summary_eval
from veritrade_evals.datasets import (
    SPECS,
    DatasetError,
    Example,
    class_counts,
    fetch_all,
    finentity_single,
    fpb_allagree,
    twitter_fns,
)
from veritrade_evals.splits import SPLIT_NAMES, SplitError, load_split, make_splits, read_split_file


class Command(Protocol):
    """A module that registers one subcommand and dispatches its parsed arguments."""

    def add_parser(self, subparsers: Any) -> argparse.ArgumentParser: ...
    def run(self, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int: ...


COMMANDS: tuple[Command, ...] = (grid, finalists, freeze, extraction_bench, summary_eval)
PLANNED = {
    "signal": "signal accuracy run over a split",
    "latency": "latency suite",
    "select": "pick per-endpoint winners",
    "holdout": "one-shot holdout run",
    "report": "benchmarks.json and results README",
    "opus": "Opus subagent prompts and judgements",
}


def _balance(examples: Sequence[Example]) -> str:
    counts = class_counts(examples)
    return " ".join(f"{k}={v} ({v / len(examples):.1%})" for k, v in counts.items())


def cmd_datasets_fetch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    lock = fetch_all(update=args.update)
    for name, entry in lock.items():
        print(f"{name}: {SPECS[name].repo_id}@{entry.revision[:12]} ({entry.license})")
    loaded = {
        "tfns train": twitter_fns("train"),
        "tfns validation": twitter_fns("validation"),
        "fpb allagree": fpb_allagree(),
        "finentity single": finentity_single(),
    }
    for label, examples in loaded.items():
        print(f"  {label}: n={len(examples)} {_balance(examples)}")
    return 0


def cmd_splits_make(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    for name, path in make_splits().items():
        payload = read_split_file(name)
        print(f"{name}: n={payload['n']} {payload['class_counts']} -> {path.name}")
        if "class_weights" in payload:
            print(f"  train_prior={payload['train_prior']} weights={payload['class_weights']}")
            print(f"  excluded={payload['excluded']}")
    return 0


def cmd_splits_verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    failed = 0
    for name in SPLIT_NAMES:
        try:
            split = load_split(name)
        except (SplitError, DatasetError) as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        print(f"ok {name}: n={len(split.examples)} {_balance(split.examples)}")
    return 1 if failed else 0


def cmd_planned(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    print(f"`{args.command}` is not implemented yet ({PLANNED[args.command]})", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="veritrade_evals", description=__doc__)
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    datasets = commands.add_parser("datasets", help="public dataset downloads").add_subparsers(
        dest="action", required=True
    )
    fetch = datasets.add_parser(
        "fetch", help="download pinned revisions and record them in datasets.lock.json"
    )
    fetch.add_argument(
        "--update", action="store_true", help="re-resolve refs instead of reusing locked commits"
    )
    fetch.set_defaults(func=cmd_datasets_fetch)

    splits = commands.add_parser("splits", help="committed split files").add_subparsers(
        dest="action", required=True
    )
    splits.add_parser("make", help="write evals/data/splits/*.json").set_defaults(func=cmd_splits_make)
    splits.add_parser("verify", help="re-read datasets and check split hashes").set_defaults(
        func=cmd_splits_verify
    )

    articles_cli.register(commands)
    for module in COMMANDS:
        module.add_parser(commands).set_defaults(func=module.run)

    for name, help_text in PLANNED.items():
        planned = commands.add_parser(name, help=f"{help_text} (not implemented yet)")
        planned.set_defaults(func=cmd_planned)
    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = build_parser()
    args, extra = parser.parse_known_args(argv)
    # Planned commands accept anything so scripts written against them fail with the clear message below.
    if extra and args.func is not cmd_planned:
        parser.error(f"unrecognized arguments: {' '.join(extra)}")
    code: int = args.func(args)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```
"""Eval runner: drives the serving adapters over examples and caches raw outputs for offline thresholds."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import hashlib
import sys
import time
from collections import deque
from collections.abc import Callable, Coroutine, Mapping, Sequence
from contextlib import aclosing
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol, TextIO, get_args

from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

from veritrade.errors import LlmUnreachable, ModelUnavailable, SchemaViolation, VtError
from veritrade.inference.adapters import (
    TOP_LOGPROBS,
    AnalyzeResult,
    analyze_stream,
    chat_options,
    classify_signal,
)
from veritrade.inference.confidence import score_sign_probabilities
from veritrade.inference.incremental import ScoreClosed
from veritrade.inference.ollama import FIXED_OPTIONS, OllamaClient
from veritrade.inference.schemas import ANALYZE_MODELS, LabelOut, OrdinalOut, ollama_format
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, DecisionResult, Endpoint, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptSpec
from veritrade_evals.paths import PREDS_DIR
from veritrade_evals.predcache import PredCache, PredError, canonical_json

# Part of every cache key: bump when the runner changes what it records for an unchanged config.
RUNNER_VERSION = "1"
# Signal cells record score_sign_probabilities output (fallback and sign_probs): bump when it changes.
SCORE_SIGN_VERSION = 2
DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 4
# Rendering the prompt with its own placeholder hashes everything the model sees except the input.
TEXT_SENTINEL = "{text}"
# Synthetic input that loads the model and warms the prompt cache before any timed call.
WARMUP_TEXT = "Ostrava Logistics appoints a new chief financial officer effective January 1."

Variant = Literal["decision", "label", "ordinal", "sentiment-first", "summary-first"]
VARIANTS: tuple[Variant, ...] = get_args(Variant)
VARIANT_ENDPOINT: dict[Variant, Endpoint] = {
    "decision": "signal",
    "label": "signal",
    "ordinal": "signal",
    "sentiment-first": "analyze",
    "summary-first": "analyze",
}
ANALYZE_VARIANTS: tuple[Variant, ...] = ("sentiment-first", "summary-first")
Pred = dict[str, Any]
Timing = dict[str, float]


class RunAborted(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Item(Protocol):
    """One scored input: a dataset example or an extracted article."""

    @property
    def id(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def text(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def label(self) -> str: ...


def serving_spec(base: ModelSpec, variant: Variant) -> ModelSpec:
    """The allowlisted spec switched to the variant under test; thresholds are applied offline."""
    if (variant == "decision") != (base.kind == "decision"):
        raise ValueError(f"{base.name} is a {base.kind} model and cannot run the {variant} variant")
    update: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if variant == "label":
        update = {
            "signal_schema": "label",
            "policy": "label-logprob",
            "min_p": 0.5 if base.min_p is None else base.min_p,
        }
    elif variant == "ordinal":
        update = {"signal_schema": "ordinal", "policy": "ordinal", "directional_tau": None}
    elif variant in ANALYZE_VARIANTS:
        update = {"field_order": variant}
    return ModelSpec.model_validate({**base.model_dump(), **update})


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RunSpec:
    """One grid cell: a model asked for one output variant under one prompt version."""

    name: str
    spec: ModelSpec
    prompt: PromptSpec
    variant: Variant
    dims: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def model(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.name

    @property
    def endpoint(self) -> Endpoint:
        return VARIANT_ENDPOINT[self.variant]

    def run_config(self, split: str, inputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """`inputs` identifies derived inputs (scope, extractor, content hash) so they re-key the cache."""
        config: dict[str, Any] = {
            "runner": RUNNER_VERSION,
            "split": split,
            "endpoint": self.endpoint,
            "variant": self.variant,
            "prompt_version": self.prompt.version,
            "max_input_tokens": self.spec.max_input_tokens,
        }
        if self.variant != "decision":
            # Exactly what the client sends, so a change to the fixed decoding options re-keys the cache.
            config["options"] = {**chat_options(self.spec, self.endpoint), **FIXED_OPTIONS}
        if self.variant in ("label", "ordinal"):
            config["top_logprobs"] = TOP_LOGPROBS
            config["score_sign"] = SCORE_SIGN_VERSION
        if self.variant in ANALYZE_VARIANTS:
            config["stop_after_score"] = True
        if inputs:
            config["inputs"] = dict(inputs)
        return config

    def prompt_sha(self) -> str:
        payload: dict[str, Any]
        if self.variant == "decision":
            payload = {
                "state": self.prompt.state(TEXT_SENTINEL),
                "instructions": self.prompt.instructions,
                "criteria": self.prompt.criteria,
            }
        else:
            payload = {
                "messages": self.prompt.messages(TEXT_SENTINEL, self.variant),
                "format": ollama_format(_out_type(self.variant)),
            }
            if self.variant == "label":
                payload["fallback"] = {
                    "messages": self.prompt.messages(TEXT_SENTINEL, "ordinal"),
                    "format": ollama_format(OrdinalOut),
                }
        return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    def cache(
        self, split: str, model_digest: str, root: Path = PREDS_DIR, inputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> PredCache:
        return PredCache(
            self.model,
            self.run_config(split, inputs),
            model_digest=model_digest,
            prompt_sha=self.prompt_sha(),
            root=root,
        )


def _out_type(variant: Variant) -> type[BaseModel]:
    if variant == "label":
        return LabelOut
    if variant == "ordinal":
        return OrdinalOut
    if variant in ("sentiment-first", "summary-first"):
        return ANALYZE_MODELS[variant]
    raise ValueError(f"{variant} has no chat output type")


# --- one call --------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _chat_timing(chat: ChatResult) -> Timing:
    timing: Timing = {"wall_ms": chat.wall_ms}
    timing.update({k: float(v) for k, v in asdict(chat.timings).items() if v is not None})
    return timing


def _parsed_label(content: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        return LabelOut.model_validate_json(content).label
    except ValidationError:
        return None


def _label_pred(verdict: Verdict, chat: ChatResult) -> Pred:
    """Records which branch of the serving fallback chain produced the probabilities, if any did."""
    if verdict.policy == "ordinal":
        fallback = "ordinal"
    elif verdict.score is not None:
        fallback = "score-sign"
    else:
        fallback = "none"
    return {
        "kind": "label",
        "label": _parsed_label(chat.content) if fallback == "none" else None,
        "probs": dict(verdict.probabilities) if verdict.probabilities is not None else None,
        "fallback": fallback,
        "score": verdict.score,
    }


async def _score_first(client: OllamaClient, run: RunSpec, text: str) -> tuple[Pred, Timing]:
    """Stops at the score: later tokens cannot change it, and closing the stream frees Ollama early."""
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    stream = analyze_stream(client, run.spec, run.prompt, text)
    async with aclosing(stream):
        async for item in stream:
            if isinstance(item, ScoreClosed):
                return {"kind": "analyze", "score": item.score}, {
                    "wall_ms": (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
                }
            if isinstance(item, AnalyzeResult):
                # A generation cut at its token limit is salvaged without a ScoreClosed event.
                return {
                    "kind": "analyze",
                    "score": item.output.score,
                    "truncated": item.truncated,
                }, _chat_timing(item.chat)
    raise SchemaViolation(f"{run.model} finished the stream without a score")


async def call_once(client: OllamaClient, run: RunSpec, text: str) -> tuple[Pred, Timing]:
    """One example through the serving adapters; returns raw outputs, never the input."""
    if run.variant in ANALYZE_VARIANTS:
        return await _score_first(client, run, text)
    verdict, raw = await classify_signal(client, run.spec, run.prompt, text)
    if isinstance(raw, DecisionResult):
        timing: Timing = {"wall_ms": raw.wall_ms}
        if raw.input_tokens is not None:
            timing["prompt_tokens"] = float(raw.input_tokens)
        pred: Pred = {
            "kind": "decision",
            "choice": raw.choice,
            "probs": dict(verdict.probabilities or {}),
            "model_confidence": raw.confidence,
        }
        return pred, timing
    if run.variant == "label":
        return _label_pred(verdict, raw), _chat_timing(raw)
    pred = {
        "kind": "ordinal",
        "score": verdict.score,
        "sign_probs": score_sign_probabilities(raw.content, raw.logprobs),
    }
    return pred, _chat_timing(raw)


# --- model residency -------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def model_digest(client: OllamaClient, model: str) -> str:
    for entry in await client.tags():
        if model in (entry.get("name"), entry.get("model")) and isinstance(entry.get("digest"), str):
            return str(entry["digest"])
    raise ModelUnavailable(f"{model} is not installed in Ollama", hint=f"Pull it with `ollama pull {model}`.")


async def make_resident(
    client: OllamaClient, run: RunSpec, *, shared: bool = False, log: TextIO = sys.stderr
) -> None:
    """Unload every other model, then warm this one so the first timed call is not a cold load. On an
    Ollama shared with other runs, only warm up: their models stay loaded."""
    for entry in [] if shared else await client.ps():
        name = str(entry.get("name") or entry.get("model") or "")
        if name and name != run.model:
            try:
                await client.unload(name)
            except VtError as exc:
                print(f"warning: could not unload {name}: {exc.message}", file=log)
    await call_once(client, run, WARMUP_TEXT)


# --- cell run --------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RunStats:
    key: str
    path: Path
    total: int
    cached: int
    called: int
    errors: int


class Progress:
    """Counts only: neither inputs nor outputs reach the console."""

    def __init__(self, label: str, total: int, cached: int, *, every_s: float, out: TextIO) -> None:
        self.label, self.total, self.cached = label, total, cached
        self.every_s, self.out = every_s, out
        self.called = self.errors = 0
        self._t0 = self._last = time.monotonic()

    def tick(self, *, error: bool) -> None:
        self.called += 1
        self.errors += error
        now = time.monotonic()
        if now - self._last >= self.every_s:
            self._last = now
            self.emit()

    def emit(self, final: bool = False) -> None:
        rate = self.called / max(time.monotonic() - self._t0, 1e-9)
        status = "done" if final else "running"
        print(
            f"[{self.label}] {status} {self.cached + self.called}/{self.total} "
            f"(cached {self.cached}, new {self.called}, errors {self.errors}, {rate:.1f}/s)",
            file=self.out,
            flush=True,
        )


def _pred_error(exc: VtError) -> PredError:
    # Greedy seeded decoding repeats a schema failure, so it is final; transport failures retry on resume.
    retryable = not isinstance(exc, SchemaViolation) and (exc.retryable or isinstance(exc, ModelUnavailable))
    return PredError(exc.code.value, exc.message[:300], retryable)


async def _pool(workers: int, job: Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, None]]) -> None:
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(job()) for _ in range(workers)]
    try:
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    finally:
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)


async def run_cell(
    client: OllamaClient,
    run: RunSpec,
    examples: Sequence[Item],
    *,
    split: str,
    model_digest: str,
    concurrency: int = DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY,
    root: Path = PREDS_DIR,
    inputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    progress_every_s: float = 30.0,
    log: TextIO = sys.stderr,
) -> RunStats:
    """Run every example not yet in the cache; an unreachable Ollama aborts, other failures are recorded."""
    if concurrency < 1:
        raise ValueError("concurrency must be >= 1")
    with run.cache(split, model_digest, root, inputs) as cache:
        done = cache.done_ids()
        todo = deque(e for e in examples if e.id not in done)
        cached = len(examples) - len(todo)
        progress = Progress(
            f"{run.endpoint} {run.model} {run.name}", len(examples), cached, every_s=progress_every_s, out=log
        )

        async def worker() -> None:
            while todo:
                example = todo.popleft()
                t0 = time.perf_counter()
                try:
                    pred, timing = await call_once(client, run, example.text)
                except LlmUnreachable as exc:
                    raise RunAborted(f"{run.model} {run.name}: {exc.message}") from exc
                except VtError as exc:
                    wall = {"wall_ms": (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000}
                    cache.append(example.id, example.label, error=_pred_error(exc), t=wall)
                    progress.tick(error=True)
                else:
                    cache.append(example.id, example.label, pred=pred, t=timing)
                    progress.tick(error=False)

        if todo:
            await _pool(min(concurrency, len(todo)), worker)
        progress.emit(final=True)
        return RunStats(cache.key, cache.path, len(examples), cached, progress.called, progress.errors)
"""Resumable JSONL prediction cache, one file per (run config, model digest, prompt, harness) hash."""

from __future__ import annotations

import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from types import TracebackType
from typing import IO, Any, Self

from veritrade_evals.paths import PREDS_DIR

# Bump when harness changes alter predictions for an unchanged config, so old caches stop matching.
HARNESS_VERSION = "1"
RESERVED_KEYS = frozenset({"id", "gold", "error", "t"})
# Publisher and dataset licences: a record may describe a prediction, never carry its input.
FORBIDDEN_KEYS = frozenset({"text", "input", "input_text", "prompt", "messages", "article"})


class PredCacheError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def canonical_json(obj: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)


def run_hash(
    run_config: Mapping[str, Any], model_digest: str, prompt_sha: str, harness_version: str = HARNESS_VERSION
) -> str:
    payload = {
        "config": run_config,
        "model_digest": model_digest,
        "prompt_sha": prompt_sha,
        "harness_version": harness_version,
    }
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def model_slug(model: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", model)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PredError:
    code: str
    message: str
    retryable: bool


def _terminal(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    error = record.get("error")
    return error is None or not error.get("retryable", False)


class PredCache:
    """Single writer per file (flock); every append is flushed so a killed run resumes from the last line."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str,
        run_config: Mapping[str, Any],
        *,
        model_digest: str,
        prompt_sha: str,
        root: Path = PREDS_DIR,
        harness_version: str = HARNESS_VERSION,
    ) -> None:
        self.key = run_hash(run_config, model_digest, prompt_sha, harness_version)
        self.sidecar = {
            "key": self.key,
            "model": model,
            "model_digest": model_digest,
            "prompt_sha": prompt_sha,
            "harness_version": harness_version,
            "run_config": json.loads(canonical_json(run_config)),
        }
        directory = root / model_slug(model)
        self.path = directory / f"{self.key}.jsonl"
        self.config_path = directory / f"{self.key}.config.json"
        self._fh: IO[str] | None = None

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        return self.open()

    def __exit__(
        self, exc_type: type[BaseException] | None, exc: BaseException | None, tb: TracebackType | None
    ) -> None:
        self.close()

    def open(self) -> Self:
        if self._fh is not None:
            return self
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._write_or_check_sidecar()
        fh = self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fh.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError as exc:
            fh.close()
            raise PredCacheError(f"{self.path} is already open for writing by another process") from exc
        self._drop_partial_tail()
        self._fh = fh
        return self

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._fh is not None:
            self._fh.close()
            self._fh = None

    def append(
        self,
        example_id: str,
        gold: str,
        *,
        pred: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        error: PredError | None = None,
        t: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if self._fh is None:
            raise PredCacheError("cache is not open; use `with PredCache(...) as cache`")
        fields = dict(pred or {})
        clash = fields.keys() & (RESERVED_KEYS | FORBIDDEN_KEYS)
        if clash:
            raise ValueError(f"prediction fields may not use {sorted(clash)}")
        record = {
            "id": example_id,
            "gold": gold,
            **fields,
            "error": asdict(error) if error else None,
            "t": dict(t or {}),
        }
        self._fh.write(canonical_json(record) + "\n")
        self._fh.flush()
        return record

    def iter_records(self) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
        if not self.path.exists():
            return
        with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                if line.endswith("\n"):
                    yield json.loads(line)

    def records(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Per id: the last terminal record, else the last (retryable) failure."""
        latest: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for record in self.iter_records():
            current = latest.get(record["id"])
            if current is None or _terminal(record) or not _terminal(current):
                latest[record["id"]] = record
        return latest

    def done_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        """Ids to skip on resume: answered or failed for good; retryable errors run again."""
        return {rid for rid, record in self.records().items() if _terminal(record)}

    def _write_or_check_sidecar(self) -> None:
        if self.config_path.exists():
            existing = json.loads(self.config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            existing.pop("created_at", None)
            if existing != self.sidecar:
                raise PredCacheError(f"{self.config_path} describes a different run for key {self.key}")
            return
        payload = {**self.sidecar, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
        tmp = self.config_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        tmp.replace(self.config_path)

    def _drop_partial_tail(self) -> None:
        # A crash mid-write leaves a line without "\n"; cut it so the next append starts a clean line.
        data = self.path.read_bytes()
        if data and not data.endswith(b"\n"):
            os.truncate(self.path, data.rfind(b"\n") + 1)
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
EVALS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "evals"
DATA_DIR = EVALS_DIR / "data"
SPLITS_DIR = DATA_DIR / "splits"
DATASETS_LOCK = DATA_DIR / "datasets.lock.json"
RESULTS_DIR = EVALS_DIR / "results"
# Committed article set: URLs, hashes, labels and model-written facts only.
ARTICLES_DIR = DATA_DIR / "articles"
OPUS_PROMPTS_DIR = EVALS_DIR / "opus_prompts"

# Gitignored: dataset files, publisher HTML and prediction caches never leave the machine.
PRIVATE_DIR = DATA_DIR / "private"
HF_CACHE_DIR = PRIVATE_DIR / "hf"
PREDS_DIR = PRIVATE_DIR / "preds"
PRIVATE_ARTICLES_DIR = PRIVATE_DIR / "articles"
```

```
"""Signal metrics: bullish/bearish calls are the positives; neutral and abstain are the safe default."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from numpy.typing import NDArray

from veritrade.inference.types import SENTIMENTS, Sentiment

DIRECTIONAL: tuple[Sentiment, Sentiment] = ("bullish", "bearish")
CONFUSION_COLUMNS = ("bullish", "bearish", "neutral", "abstain")
BETA = 0.5
INVERSION_CAP = 0.02
HEADLINE = ("f05_macro", "inversion_rate", "coverage", "signal_rate", "accuracy")
BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 20261018

FloatArray = NDArray[np.float64]
IndexArray = NDArray[np.intp]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ClassScores:
    precision: float
    recall: float
    f05: float
    calls: float
    support: float


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SignalMetrics:
    """Rates are prevalence-weighted when weights are given; `confusion` is raw counts (gold x columns)."""

    n: int
    per_class: dict[str, ClassScores]
    f05_macro: float
    inversion_rate: float
    coverage: float
    signal_rate: float
    accuracy: float
    selective_accuracy: float
    confusion: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


def _div(num: float, den: float) -> float:
    # Zero calls or zero support score 0 (not NaN): "always neutral" cannot look good and JSON stays strict.
    return float(num / den) if den > 0 else 0.0


def fbeta(precision: float, recall: float, beta: float = BETA) -> float:
    b2 = beta * beta
    den = b2 * precision + recall
    return (1 + b2) * precision * recall / den if den > 0 else 0.0


def _labels(values: Sequence[str], what: str) -> NDArray[np.str_]:
    arr = np.asarray(list(values), dtype=np.str_)
    unknown = set(arr.tolist()) - set(SENTIMENTS)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown {what} labels: {sorted(unknown)}")
    return arr


def _weights(weights: Sequence[float] | None, n: int) -> FloatArray:
    if weights is None:
        return np.ones(n, dtype=np.float64)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)
    if w.shape != (n,) or (w < 0).any() or w.sum() <= 0:
        raise ValueError("weights must be one non-negative value per example with a positive sum")
    return w


def signal_metrics(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    pred: Sequence[Sentiment],
    abstained: Sequence[bool],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> SignalMetrics:
    g, p = _labels(gold, "gold"), _labels(pred, "pred")
    a = np.asarray(abstained, dtype=bool)
    n = len(g)
    if n == 0 or p.shape != (n,) or a.shape != (n,):
        raise ValueError("gold, pred and abstained must be non-empty and the same length")
    w = _weights(weights, n)
    total = float(w.sum())
    answered = ~a
    call = np.where(answered & np.isin(p, DIRECTIONAL), p, "")
    directional = call != ""

    per_class: dict[str, ClassScores] = {}
    for c in DIRECTIONAL:
        tp = float(w[(call == c) & (g == c)].sum())
        calls = float(w[call == c].sum())
        support = float(w[g == c].sum())
        precision, recall = _div(tp, calls), _div(tp, support)
        per_class[c] = ClassScores(precision, recall, fbeta(precision, recall), calls, support)

    inverted = directional & np.isin(g, DIRECTIONAL) & (call != g)
    served = np.where(a, "neutral", p)
    confusion = tuple(
        (*(int(((g == gl) & answered & (p == pl)).sum()) for pl in SENTIMENTS), int(((g == gl) & a).sum()))
        for gl in SENTIMENTS
    )
    return SignalMetrics(
        n=n,
        per_class=per_class,
        f05_macro=float(np.mean([per_class[c].f05 for c in DIRECTIONAL])),
        inversion_rate=_div(float(w[inverted].sum()), float(w[directional].sum())),
        coverage=float(w[answered].sum()) / total,
        signal_rate=float(w[directional].sum()) / total,
        accuracy=float(w[served == g].sum()) / total,
        selective_accuracy=_div(float(w[answered & (p == g)].sum()), float(w[answered].sum())),
        confusion=confusion,
    )


def example_weights(gold: Sequence[Sentiment], class_weights: Mapping[str, float]) -> list[float]:
    return [class_weights[label] for label in gold]


# --- risk-coverage and operating point -------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SweepPoint:
    threshold: float
    metrics: SignalMetrics

    @property
    def f05_macro(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.f05_macro

    @property
    def inversion_rate(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.inversion_rate

    @property
    def coverage(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.coverage

    @property
    def risk(self) -> float:
        return 1.0 - self.metrics.selective_accuracy


def candidate_thresholds(confidences: Sequence[float]) -> list[float]:
    """0 (never abstain) plus each distinct finite confidence: the only points where calls change."""
    finite = {float(c) for c in confidences if math.isfinite(c)}
    return sorted(finite | {0.0})


def risk_coverage_sweep(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    labels: Sequence[Sentiment],
    confidences: Sequence[float],
    thresholds: Sequence[float],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> list[SweepPoint]:
    """Abstain whenever confidence < threshold; a NaN confidence never clears any threshold."""
    conf = np.asarray(confidences, dtype=np.float64)
    points = []
    for t in sorted(set(thresholds)):
        abstained = ~(conf >= t)
        points.append(SweepPoint(float(t), signal_metrics(gold, labels, abstained.tolist(), weights)))
    return points


def select_operating_point(
    points: Sequence[SweepPoint], inversion_cap: float = INVERSION_CAP
) -> SweepPoint | None:
    """Best F0.5 among points under the inversion cap; ties go to higher coverage, then lower threshold."""
    eligible = [p for p in points if p.inversion_rate <= inversion_cap + 1e-12]
    if not eligible:
        return None
    return max(eligible, key=lambda p: (round(p.f05_macro, 12), round(p.coverage, 12), -p.threshold))


# --- bootstrap -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ConfidenceInterval:
    point: float
    low: float
    high: float
    level: float
    n_boot: int


def stratified_indices(gold: NDArray[np.str_], rng: np.random.Generator) -> IndexArray:
    """Resample with replacement inside each gold class so every replicate keeps the class sizes."""
    parts = [
        rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(gold == label), size=int((gold == label).sum()))
        for label in np.unique(gold)
    ]
    return np.concatenate(parts).astype(np.intp)


def bootstrap_cis(
    metrics_fn: Callable[[IndexArray], Mapping[str, float]],
    gold: Sequence[str],
    *,
    n_boot: int = 1000,
    seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
    level: float = 0.95,
) -> dict[str, ConfidenceInterval]:
    """Percentile CIs for several metrics from one shared set of stratified resamples."""
    g = np.asarray(list(gold), dtype=np.str_)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    point = metrics_fn(np.arange(len(g), dtype=np.intp))
    samples: dict[str, list[float]] = {k: [] for k in point}
    for _ in range(n_boot):
        values = metrics_fn(stratified_indices(g, rng))
        for k in samples:
            samples[k].append(values[k])
    tail = (1 - level) / 2
    out: dict[str, ConfidenceInterval] = {}
    for k, vals in samples.items():
        low, high = np.quantile(np.asarray(vals), [tail, 1 - tail])
        out[k] = ConfidenceInterval(float(point[k]), float(low), float(high), level, n_boot)
    return out


def bootstrap_ci(
    metric_fn: Callable[[IndexArray], float],
    gold: Sequence[str],
    *,
    n_boot: int = 1000,
    seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
    level: float = 0.95,
) -> ConfidenceInterval:
    return bootstrap_cis(lambda idx: {"m": metric_fn(idx)}, gold, n_boot=n_boot, seed=seed, level=level)["m"]


def headline_cis(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    pred: Sequence[Sentiment],
    abstained: Sequence[bool],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    *,
    n_boot: int = 1000,
    seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
) -> dict[str, ConfidenceInterval]:
    g = np.asarray(list(gold), dtype=np.str_)
    p = np.asarray(list(pred), dtype=np.str_)
    a = np.asarray(abstained, dtype=bool)
    w = None if weights is None else np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)

    def fn(idx: IndexArray) -> dict[str, float]:
        m = signal_metrics(
            g[idx].tolist(), p[idx].tolist(), a[idx].tolist(), None if w is None else w[idx].tolist()
        )
        return {k: float(getattr(m, k)) for k in HEADLINE}

    return bootstrap_cis(fn, g.tolist(), n_boot=n_boot, seed=seed)


# --- quality vs latency ----------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Candidate:
    name: str
    f05: float
    latency_ms: float


def pareto_front(candidates: Sequence[Candidate]) -> list[Candidate]:
    """Non-dominated candidates (F0.5 up, latency down), fastest first."""
    front: list[Candidate] = []
    best = -math.inf
    for c in sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: (c.latency_ms, -c.f05, c.name)):
        if c.f05 > best:
            front.append(c)
            best = c.f05
    return front


def _minmax(values: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
    span = float(values.max() - values.min())
    return (values - values.min()) / span if span > 0 else np.zeros_like(values)


def knee(candidates: Sequence[Candidate]) -> Candidate:
    """Front point farthest above the fastest-to-best chord on min-max axes; ties prefer higher F0.5."""
    front = pareto_front(candidates)
    if not front:
        raise ValueError("knee of an empty candidate set")
    if len(front) <= 2:
        return max(front, key=lambda c: (c.f05, -c.latency_ms))
    lat = _minmax(np.array([c.latency_ms for c in front], dtype=np.float64))
    q = _minmax(np.array([c.f05 for c in front], dtype=np.float64))
    dx, dy = lat[-1] - lat[0], q[-1] - q[0]
    # Signed so only points bulging toward the fast-and-accurate corner count as a knee.
    dist = (dx * (q - q[0]) - dy * (lat - lat[0])) / math.hypot(dx, dy)
    return max(zip(front, dist.tolist(), strict=True), key=lambda cd: (round(cd[1], 12), cd[0].f05))[0]
```
