````markdown
# 04 - Evaluation

How the models, prompts and thresholds behind `/signal`, `/summary` and `/analyze` were chosen, and how well
they do. The reasons behind each choice are in [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md). The fetch and extraction
path that every eval runs through is in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) and
[`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md). Every number here links to the committed result file it comes from.

Rigor is balanced per aspect, as for the rest of this PoC (R2). The signal metric, the splits and the one-time
holdout are strict. The prompt grid is deliberately lean. The article labels and the summary judgements come
from Claude Opus subagents with no human check.

```
dev300 grid (prompt x policy x threshold per model) -> one error-analysis pass -> articles dev check
(transfer only, never re-tuned) -> freeze -> summary eval -> latency suite -> select -> holdout, run once
```

## 1. Objective and metrics

A wrong directional call costs a trade, and a missed one costs little (Q2). So the positive class is a
directional call, and neutral or an abstention is the safe default. Definitions follow
[`metrics.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/metrics.py):

- **Directional call**: an answered row (not abstained) that predicts bullish or bearish. An abstention is
  served as neutral with `abstained: true`.
- **Precision / recall** per class c in {bullish, bearish}: correct c calls / c calls, and correct c calls /
  gold c rows. A class with no calls scores 0, not NaN, so "always neutral" scores F0.5 0.
- **F0.5 macro** (the selection metric): the mean of the two per-class F-beta scores at beta = 0.5, which
  weights precision above recall. Neutral is not a positive class.
- **Inversion rate**: bullish<->bearish flips (a directional call on a gold-directional row, with the opposite
  label) over all directional calls. The cap is **2%**.
- **Coverage**: the share of rows answered (not abstained). **Signal rate**: the share of rows with a
  directional call. **Accuracy**: the served label (abstention -> neutral) equals gold.
- **Operating point**: thresholds are swept over 0 and every distinct confidence value, which are the only
  points where calls change. The chosen point has the **max F0.5 among points with inversion <= 2%**; ties go
  to higher coverage, then a lower threshold. A config with no point under the cap is "cap missed" and cannot
  be selected.
- **Prevalence weights** (dev300 only): each row is weighted by train prior / sample prior for its class, so
  rates on the balanced sample estimate the real tweet mix. Confusion and error counts stay raw. The articles
  and the holdout sets are unweighted.
- **CIs**: a 95% percentile bootstrap (B = 1,000, seed 20261018) that resamples within each gold class, on the
  headline metrics only (F0.5 macro, inversion, coverage, signal rate, accuracy). Gaps between two configs on
  the same rows use a paired bootstrap. The threshold is not re-chosen per resample, so a CI at a tuned
  operating point is optimistic.

## 2. Datasets and splits

| split | source | role | n | bullish / bearish / neutral | weighting |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `dev300` | Twitter Financial News Sentiment (FNS), train | tuning: prompt grid, thresholds | 300 | 100 / 100 / 100 | train prior 20.2% / 15.1% / 64.7% |
| articles dev | Opus-labelled articles (section 3) | transfer check, error analysis, summary eval | 30 | 10 / 10 / 10 | none |
| articles test | Opus-labelled articles | holdout | 60 | 20 / 20 / 20 | none |
| `tfns_val` | Twitter FNS, validation | holdout, in-domain tweets | 2,388 | 475 / 347 / 1,566 | none (natural prior) |
| `fpb_allagree` | Financial PhraseBank, Sentences_AllAgree | holdout, cross-domain sentences | 2,259 | 570 / 303 / 1,386 | none |
| `finentity_single` | FinEntity, rows with one distinct label | holdout, cross-domain paragraphs | 851 | 181 / 180 / 490 | none |

Sources: the split headers in [`evals/data/splits/`](../../../evals/data/splits/) and
[`stats.json`](../../../evals/data/articles/stats.json).

- **dev300** is drawn from Twitter FNS train after dropping 69 rows whose normalised text also appears in
  validation, 70 duplicates and 4 rows with conflicting labels. Then 100 rows per class are drawn with seed
  20261018. Class weights are 0.605 (bullish), 0.453 (bearish) and 1.942 (neutral).
- **Label mapping**: Twitter FNS already uses Bearish / Bullish / Neutral. FPB and FinEntity positive /
  negative / neutral map to bullish / bearish / neutral. In FPB, exact duplicates are collapsed and sentences
  seen with two labels are dropped. FinEntity keeps rows with at least one entity annotation and exactly one
  distinct label.
- **Committed**: each split file holds the ids, the sha1 of the normalised text (NFKC, casefold, URLs and
  whitespace runs dropped), the labels, the selection rule and the dataset revision.
  [`datasets.lock.json`](../../../evals/data/datasets.lock.json) pins each dataset commit, each file's sha256
  and its licence. A split fails to load on a revision mismatch, a missing id, text-hash drift or label drift.
- **Never committed**: dataset text (FPB is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0). It is downloaded at eval time into the
  gitignored `evals/data/private/`, together with article HTML, gold bodies, headlines, predictions, generated
  summaries and judge packets.

## 3. The Opus-labelled article set

Public datasets hold sentences and headlines, but the service reads whole articles (Q5, R5). The set has 90
real articles from the 10 sources in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md): 3 classes x 3 articles per
source, published 2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18. One seeded article per (source, class) cell goes to dev, giving
**30 dev / 60 test**. Two quota adjustments keep the 30/30/30 class balance: Yahoo has 4 bearish articles and
BBC has 2. Every Opus step ran as a Claude Code subagent pinned to Claude Opus 5.5, so no API key or paid
service was used. The prompts and the runbook are in [`evals/opus_prompts/`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md).

1. **Discover** (one agent per source): candidates from RSS and section pages, fetched through the serving
   fetcher by the deterministic `articles` CLI. Agents never fetch anything themselves.
2. **Gold**: Opus picks the article body as line ranges of the page, writes 3-5 key facts in its own words
   and gives a provisional label.
3. **Label A / label B**: two independent agents apply the service's rubric. The rubric judges the economic
   impact on the primary entity, not the tone; neutral is the answer when in doubt. Neither agent sees the
   other's output or the provisional label.
4. **Adjudicate**: one agent reviews every article where the labels differ or either labeller flagged it as
   ambiguous. It either keeps the article (its label becomes final) or replaces it as genuinely ambiguous.
5. **Refill and finalize**: short cells go through steps 1-4 again. `finalize` picks per cell (agreed
   articles first), and `verify` re-checks the set. The CLI rejects any key fact or rationale that shares 10
   consecutive words with the article.

| pool statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| articles with a usable gold body | 298 |
| labelled by both labellers | 157 |
| labels agree | 151 (raw agreement 96.2%) |
| Cohen's kappa (A vs B) | 0.943 |
| sent to adjudication (6 disagreements, 43 agreed but flagged ambiguous) | 49 (31.2%) |
| replaced by the adjudicator | 24 of 49 (49.0%) |
| adjudicated articles kept in the final 90 | 5 |

In the final 90, A and B agree on every label (kappa 1.0). That is by construction, because agreed articles
are picked first, so the pool agreement above is the meaningful figure. The committed
[`articles.jsonl`](../../../evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl) holds the ids, URLs, sources, dates, both labels,
the adjudication, the entity and ticker, and the rationales and key facts in Opus's words. It holds no article
text.

**Caveats.** The labels come from Opus only, with no human check. Replacing ambiguous articles makes the set
cleaner than real traffic. With 10 articles per class on dev, a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero.

## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` and `/summary`; the combined one
serves `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells in [`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json).
Every cell ran on native Metal under Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0). Sampling penalties were
pinned to neutral values (see the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic
  shots, giving v1-v4. For `qwen3.5:0.8b` each of these runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: a rubric or a plain one-line question x described or bare criteria, giving v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, each paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the
  field-order check, run on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): the argmax of the native class probabilities. The model abstains when
  that probability is below `min_p`.
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): the probability of the first label token, renormalised over the
  tokens the grammar accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still
  yields the likelier directional class when that class holds p >= tau. Below tau the row is served as a
  confident neutral, not an abstention. When labels collide on the first token, the adapter re-asks with the
  ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streaming and the fallback): a score from -2 to 2, called directional only when
  \|score\| >= t. Ollama returns logprobs only on non-streamed calls, and the score is read mid-stream, so
  this is the only policy that works on streams (Q3).

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default: the headline plus the opening paragraphs, at
most 200 tokens. Both `lede` and `full` are scored on articles. `/analyze` always reads `full` and puts the
sentiment field first, so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error-analysis pass.** After the grid, one hand-written read of the counts went into
[`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md). The resulting changes and their effects are in
section 5. Then the configs were frozen by `veritrade_evals freeze` into [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json)
and [`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml).

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze`
takes v5 unless its paired gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles; that rejected v5 for
`qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first would be chosen only if it won on dev300 and did
not lose on the articles, which never happened.

## 5. Accuracy on dev

All rows are frozen configs. Articles use the dev300 threshold unchanged, with the serving extraction
(`selectolax` + `cascade`). Sources: [`grid/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md) and
[`articles_dev/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md).

**`/signal`** (dev300 weighted; articles lede = the served default):

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | articles lede F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. | articles full F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.914 / 0.918 | 0.0% | 100.0% | 15.4% | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 1/14 | 0.635 [0.329, 0.817] | 0/10 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.867 / 0.905 | 0.0% | 72.9% | 33.2% | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 1/20 | 0.907 [0.820, 0.989] | 0/20 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.948 / 0.891 | 0.0% | 26.3% | 24.2% | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 0/17 | 0.880 [0.761, 0.976] | 0/19 |

**`/analyze`** (full scope, sentiment-first, \|s\| >= 1, coverage 100% for all):

| model | config | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | signal rate | articles F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | v1 | 0.752 [0.664, 0.834] | 0.877 / 0.821 | 0.0% | 21.4% | 0.880 [0.791, 0.989] | 0/22 |
| `ministral-3:3b` | v5 | 0.685 [0.589, 0.772] | 0.837 / 0.768 | 1.0% | 20.0% | 0.741 [0.611, 0.858] | 0/19 |
| `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | v5 | 0.647 [0.553, 0.741] | 0.702 / 0.752 | 0.0% | 23.1% | 0.779 [0.646, 0.879] | 1/22 |

No served rule clearly fails on the articles. Clearly failing means the whole inversion CI is above 2%, or the
whole coverage CI is below half the dev300 coverage. So every dev300 threshold stands.

What the error analysis found ([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md),
[`error_patterns.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/error_patterns.json)):

- **Inversions are nearly absent.** One tweet is inverted across the six best configs. The wrong calls are
  mostly gold-neutral tweets called directional (1-8 per model). The real loss is recall: 34 (`clef-flash`) to
  162 (`qwen3.5:0.8b`) directional tweets are missed, mostly price-move tweets that the impact rubric reads as
  immaterial.
- **`directional_tau` is the largest single lever.** `qwen3.5:0.8b` puts most of its mass on neutral, and the
  tau rule lifts its F0.5 by +0.218 [+0.141, +0.307] (paired). The same rule loses for the peaked decision
  models (-0.046 and -0.303), so they keep the plain rule.
- **Other changes.** Rubric A beats rubric B for every generative model. Shots help only `qwen3.5:0.8b`, so
  every frozen `/analyze` prompt is zero-shot. Summary-first never wins and delays the score 2-3x. The
  price-move rubric sentence was not added, because articles do not show the tweet miss (0-1 of 5 directional
  price-move headlines missed).
- **Knob comparison.** Without tau, the logprob knob beats the ordinal knob on `qwen3.5:0.8b` by +0.059
  [-0.068, +0.187], which is not significant. With tau the logprob knob wins clearly. The ordinal schema
  cannot use tau, because this tokenizer fuses `" -"` and so hides the sign of negative scores.

## 6. Summary evaluation

Decision R6, run by `veritrade_evals.summary_eval`. Summaries come from the serving adapters on the stored HTML
of the 30 dev articles, with full scope and the frozen prompts. Serving caps every summary at **3 sentences / 60
words** at a sentence boundary, and the checks score the capped text.

- **Deterministic checks** (pass rate gate >= 0.8): length, sentence count, every number grounded in the gold
  article (format-tolerant; a derived figure counts as unsupported), the gold entity named, and no truncation.
- **Key-fact coverage**: each Opus key fact and each summary sentence is embedded with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`.
  A fact counts as covered at a best cosine of **>= 0.60** (primary), and 0.75 is the strict bound. In a
  hand-labelled spot check of 45 facts on 10 summaries
  ([`spotcheck.dev.json`](../../../evals/results/summary/spotcheck.dev.json)), 0.60 matched 33 of 45 flags
  with 5 false "covered". 0.55 matched 34 with 6 false, a near tie. 0.75 had no false "covered" but missed 20
  stated facts. See the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`.
- **Opus judges**, blind: per article, the candidate summaries are anonymised as `S1..Sn` and shuffled
  ([`50-judge.md`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md)). Each summary gets faithfulness 1-5, coverage
  1-5, a list of hallucinations, and whether it leads with the market-moving fact. The **material error
  rate** is the share of summaries at faithfulness <= 3.

Results on the dev articles, n = 30 per row ([`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)).
Length and sentence count pass 100% by construction. CIs are bootstrapped within each article's sentiment
label.

| endpoint | model | pass | numbers | entity | key facts 0.60 / 0.75 | faithful [95% CI] | cover | halluc. flag | material [95% CI] | leads |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| summary | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 97% | 93% | 52% / 24% | 3.97 [3.67, 4.23] | 4.30 | 67% | 30% [17%, 47%] | 90% |
| summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 97% | 47% / 23% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 97% | 57% / 29% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 90% | 90% | 100% | 56% / 25% | 4.73 [4.53, 4.93] | 4.43 | 20% | 7% [0%, 17%] | 83% |
| analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | 77% | 80% | 97% | 45% / 19% | 3.77 [3.37, 4.20] | 4.27 | 63% | 40% [23%, 57%] | 80% |

**Hallucination flag vs material error.** The flag rate counts any summary with at least one entry in the
judge's hallucination list. That includes minor slips that still allow faithfulness 4: a loosely worded or
small unsupported detail that "a trader would shrug off". The material error rate counts only faithfulness
<= 3: a wrong key number, an unsupported claim that matters, a misattribution, or worse. So `qwen3.5:4b` on
`/summary` is flagged on half the articles but has a material error on 10% [0%, 20%] of them. The material
rate is the one to read as risk. The deterministic number check agrees in direction: 1-3 unsupported numbers
across 30 summaries for the qwen models, and 8 for `ministral`.

## 7. Selection

The rules are in [`selection/selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md). A candidate must
first pass the accuracy filters: dev300 inversion <= 2%, articles dev not clearly over the cap, and the summary
pass rate >= 0.8. It must then meet the native warm latency budgets from R7 (measured in `05-latency.md`).
Among the survivors, `/signal` and `/analyze` rank on dev300 F0.5, then articles dev F0.5. `/summary` ranks on
judge faithfulness, then judge coverage. Budgets are reported, never moved. When nothing meets a budget, the
Pareto knee is used and the reason is stated.

| endpoint | winner | deciding numbers | others |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (v2-label, tau 0.28) | the only candidate inside the 500 ms lede budget: p50 178 ms, dev300 F0.5 0.730 | `clef-flash` 0.874 at 659 ms; `nimble` 0.843 at 1,061 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v2) | faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97, paired +0.43 [0.07, 0.77]; TTFT p50 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | `qwen3.5:2b` faster (484 / 1,272 ms), more material errors (30%) |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v1) | dev300 F0.5 0.752; TTFT p50 1,292 ms (limit 1,500), complete 2,584 ms | `ministral` 0.685, `qwen3-instruct` 0.647 |

The bundled models are `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` + `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, 4.34 GB in total against the 10 GB cap (R8).

**The `/signal` trade-off.** `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874) but misses the 500 ms lede
budget (p50 659 ms). Its 10.58 GB model file alone also exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap. `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (0.843,
1,061 ms) misses the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms, with high precision
(0.91 / 0.92) but low recall: it misses about half the directional articles on dev. The budget was not moved
to fit the 9B models. Both stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on
native Ollama, for users who prefer precision and recall over speed.

On `/analyze`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` has the best summary faithfulness (4.73 vs 4.47). The paired gap of
0.27 [-0.07, 0.60] is not significant, and the endpoint ranks on signal F0.5 first, where it is last.

## 8. Holdout

**Protocol.** `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}`
([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)).

- It runs the frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, with no re-tuning, on natural class priors
  (unweighted). A prompt that has drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` is the holdout F0.5 minus the
  dev F0.5 of the same rule: the articles dev set at the same scope for articles, dev300 for the tweet and
  cross-domain sets.
- Cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`, and the three
  `/analyze` finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`. The two winners also run on `fpb_allagree`
  and `finentity_single`. The `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling runs on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. That
  makes 22 cells. Summaries from the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles then go to the
  blind Opus judges.
- **Run once.** [`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) is a guard keyed by the
  sha256 of `frozen.json`. It records the selection sha256, the git sha, and the start and completion times.
  An interrupted run resumes from its caches. A completed config refuses a second run unless
  `--force --reason` is passed, and that is logged in the guard and must be disclosed. The run also refuses a
  provisional selection, one made before the latency suite, unless `--allow-provisional` is passed. This
  selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` re-scores the cached predictions only and never calls a model. The tables below come from
  `evals/results/holdout/holdout.md`, which that command writes.

## 9. Threats to validity

- **One labeller family.** The article labels, the gold bodies, the key facts and the summary judges are all
  Claude Opus. The labellers were independent and the judges blind, but a shared bias would not show, and no
  human checked any label.
- **Small n.** With 30 dev and 60 test articles, the CIs span 0.2-0.5 F0.5. Article results check that the
  rules transfer; they do not rank the models.
- **Tuned on tweets.** Thresholds and prompts were tuned on 300 tweets and only checked on articles. The CIs
  at a tuned threshold do not include the threshold choice. `directional_tau` adds one more tuned parameter.
- **Class mix.** The article sets are balanced, while real traffic is likely neutral-heavy (64.7% of Twitter
  FNS train). So per-call precision in production is likely below the article-set figure. dev300 corrects for
  this with weights; the articles do not.
- **A cleaner set than reality.** It covers 10 fetchable sources only, a 60-day window, and 24 ambiguous
  articles replaced. For three sources the extraction profiles were tuned with this set in view (see the
  caveats in `03-extraction.md`).
- **Contamination.** The public datasets may be in the models' pretraining data. The articles are recent,
  which limits that overlap but does not rule it out.
- **Precision first, by design.** The selected `/signal` model misses about half the directional articles. A
  missed call is cheap under Q2, but users will see many neutrals.
- **Latency context.** Grid and articles timings ran on a shared machine and are indicative only. The selection
  uses the dedicated native-metal suite; the Docker CPU picture is in `05-latency.md`.
- **Keyword buckets** in the error analysis are a first-match heuristic, meant for orientation only.
````

```diff
+1,061 ms) misses the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms. Its dev300
+precision is high (0.91 / 0.92) but its recall is low: it misses about half the directional articles on dev.
+The budget was not moved to fit the 9B models. Both stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with
+the `model` parameter on native Ollama, for callers who can trade latency for accuracy.
```

````markdown
# 04 - Evaluation

How the models, prompts and thresholds behind `/signal`, `/summary` and `/analyze` were chosen, and how well
they do. The reasons behind each choice are in [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md). The fetch and extraction
path that every eval runs through is in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) and
[`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md). Every number here links to the committed result file it comes from.

Rigor is balanced per aspect, as for the rest of this PoC (R2). The signal metric, the splits and the one-time
holdout are strict. The prompt grid is deliberately lean. The article labels and the summary judgements come
from Claude Opus subagents with no human check.

```
dev300 grid (prompt x policy x threshold per model) -> one error-analysis pass -> articles dev check
(transfer only, never re-tuned) -> freeze -> summary eval on the frozen prompts -> latency suite -> select
-> holdout, run once
```

## 1. Objective and metrics

A wrong directional call costs a trade, and a missed one costs little (Q2). So the positive class is a
directional call, and neutral or an abstention is the safe default. Definitions follow
[`metrics.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/metrics.py):

- **Directional call**: an answered row (not abstained) that predicts bullish or bearish. An abstention is
  served as neutral with `abstained: true`.
- **Precision / recall** per class c in {bullish, bearish}: correct c calls / c calls, and correct c calls /
  gold c rows. A class with no calls scores 0, not NaN, so "always neutral" scores F0.5 0.
- **F0.5 macro** (the selection metric): the mean of the two per-class F-beta scores at beta = 0.5, which
  weights precision above recall. Neutral is not a positive class.
- **Inversion rate**: bullish<->bearish flips (a directional call on a gold-directional row, with the opposite
  label) over all directional calls. The cap is **2%**.
- **Coverage**: the share of rows answered (not abstained). **Signal rate**: the share of rows with a
  directional call. **Accuracy**: the served label (abstention -> neutral) equals gold.
- **Operating point**: thresholds are swept over 0 and every distinct confidence value, which are the only
  points where calls change. The chosen point has the **max F0.5 among points with inversion <= 2%**; ties go
  to higher coverage, then a lower threshold. A config with no point under the cap is "cap missed" and cannot
  be selected.
- **Prevalence weights** (dev300 only): each row is weighted by train prior / sample prior for its class, so
  rates on the balanced sample estimate the real tweet mix. Confusion and error counts stay raw. The articles
  and the holdout sets are unweighted.
- **CIs**: a 95% percentile bootstrap (B = 1,000, seed 20261018) that resamples within each gold class, on the
  headline metrics only (F0.5 macro, inversion, coverage, signal rate, accuracy). Gaps between two configs on
  the same rows use a paired bootstrap. The threshold is not re-chosen per resample, so a CI at a tuned
  operating point is optimistic.

## 2. Datasets and splits

| split | source | role | n | bullish / bearish / neutral | weighting |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `dev300` | Twitter Financial News Sentiment (FNS), train | tuning: prompt grid, thresholds | 300 | 100 / 100 / 100 | train prior 20.2% / 15.1% / 64.7% |
| articles dev | Opus-labelled articles (section 3) | transfer check, error analysis, summary eval | 30 | 10 / 10 / 10 | none |
| articles test | Opus-labelled articles | holdout | 60 | 20 / 20 / 20 | none |
| `tfns_val` | Twitter FNS, validation | holdout, in-domain tweets | 2,388 | 475 / 347 / 1,566 | none (natural prior) |
| `fpb_allagree` | Financial PhraseBank, Sentences_AllAgree | holdout, cross-domain sentences | 2,259 | 570 / 303 / 1,386 | none |
| `finentity_single` | FinEntity, rows with one distinct label | holdout, cross-domain paragraphs | 851 | 181 / 180 / 490 | none |

Sources: the split headers in [`evals/data/splits/`](../../../evals/data/splits/) and
[`stats.json`](../../../evals/data/articles/stats.json).

- **dev300** is drawn from Twitter FNS train after dropping 69 rows whose normalised text also appears in
  validation, 70 duplicates and 4 rows with conflicting labels. Then 100 rows per class are drawn with seed
  20261018. Class weights are 0.605 (bullish), 0.453 (bearish) and 1.942 (neutral).
- **Label mapping**: Twitter FNS already uses Bearish / Bullish / Neutral. FPB and FinEntity positive /
  negative / neutral map to bullish / bearish / neutral. In FPB, exact duplicates are collapsed and sentences
  seen with two labels are dropped. FinEntity keeps rows with at least one entity annotation and exactly one
  distinct label.
- **Committed**: each split file holds the ids, the sha1 of the normalised text (NFKC, casefold, URLs and
  whitespace runs dropped), the labels, the selection rule and the dataset revision.
  [`datasets.lock.json`](../../../evals/data/datasets.lock.json) pins each dataset commit, each file's sha256
  and its licence. A split fails to load on a revision mismatch, a missing id, text-hash drift or label drift.
- **Never committed**: dataset text (FPB is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0). It is downloaded at eval time into the
  gitignored `evals/data/private/`, together with article HTML, gold bodies, headlines, predictions, generated
  summaries and judge packets.

## 3. The Opus-labelled article set

Public datasets hold sentences and headlines, but the service reads whole articles (Q5, R5). The set has 90
real articles from the 10 sources in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md): 3 classes x 3 articles per
source, published 2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18. One seeded article per (source, class) cell goes to dev, giving
**30 dev / 60 test**. Two quota adjustments keep the 30/30/30 class balance: Yahoo has 4 bearish articles and
BBC has 2. Every Opus step ran as a Claude Code subagent pinned to Claude Opus 5.5, so no API key or paid
service was used. The prompts and the runbook are in [`evals/opus_prompts/`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md).

1. **Discover** (one agent per source): candidates from RSS and section pages, fetched through the serving
   fetcher by the deterministic `articles` CLI. Agents never fetch anything themselves.
2. **Gold**: Opus picks the article body as line ranges of the page, writes 3-5 key facts in its own words
   and gives a provisional label.
3. **Label A / label B**: two independent agents apply the service's rubric. The rubric judges the economic
   impact on the primary entity, not the tone; neutral is the answer when in doubt. Neither agent sees the
   other's output or the provisional label.
4. **Adjudicate**: one agent reviews every article where the labels differ or either labeller flagged it as
   ambiguous. It either keeps the article (its label becomes final) or replaces it as genuinely ambiguous.
5. **Refill and finalize**: short cells go through steps 1-4 again. `finalize` picks per cell (agreed
   articles first), and `verify` re-checks the set.

| pool statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| articles with a usable gold body | 298 |
| labelled by both labellers | 157 |
| labels agree | 151 (raw agreement 96.2%) |
| Cohen's kappa (A vs B) | 0.943 |
| sent to adjudication (6 disagreements, 43 agreed but flagged ambiguous) | 49 (31.2%) |
| replaced by the adjudicator | 24 of 49 (49.0%) |
| adjudicated articles kept in the final 90 | 5 |

In the final 90, A and B agree on every label (kappa 1.0). That is by construction, because agreed articles
are picked first, so the pool agreement above is the meaningful figure. The committed
[`articles.jsonl`](../../../evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl) holds the ids, URLs, sources, dates, both labels,
the adjudication, the entity and ticker, and the rationales and key facts in Opus's words. It holds no article
text: the CLI rejects any key fact or rationale that shares 10 consecutive words with the article.

**Caveats.** The labels come from Opus only, with no human check. Replacing ambiguous articles makes the set
cleaner than real traffic. With 10 articles per class on dev, a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero.

## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` and `/summary`; the combined one
serves `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells in [`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json).
Every cell ran on native Metal under Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0). Sampling penalties were
pinned to neutral values (see the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic
  shots, giving v1-v4. For `qwen3.5:0.8b` each of these runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: a rubric or a plain one-line question x described or bare criteria, giving v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, each paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the
  field-order check, run on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): the argmax of the native class probabilities. The model abstains when
  that probability is below `min_p`.
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): the probability of the first label token, renormalised over the
  tokens the grammar accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still
  yields the likelier directional class when that class holds p >= tau. Below tau the row is served as a
  confident neutral, not an abstention. When labels collide on the first token, the adapter re-asks with the
  ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streaming and the fallback): a score from -2 to 2, called directional only when
  \|score\| >= t. The score is read mid-stream as soon as it closes and needs no logprobs, so streams and
  `/analyze` use this policy (Q3). Logprob-weighted streaming confidence is on the backlog.

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default: the headline plus the opening paragraphs, with
the body capped at 200 tokens. Both `lede` and `full` are scored on articles. `/analyze` always reads `full` and puts the
sentiment field first, so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error-analysis pass.** After the grid, one hand-written read of the counts went into
[`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md). The resulting changes and their effects are in
section 5. Then the configs were frozen by `veritrade_evals freeze` into [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json)
and [`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml).

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze`
takes v5 unless the whole paired 95% CI of its gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles. That
rejected v5 for `qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first would be chosen only if it won on dev300 and did
not lose on the articles, which never happened.

## 5. Accuracy on dev

All rows are frozen configs. Articles use the dev300 threshold unchanged, with the serving extraction
(`selectolax` + `cascade`). Sources: [`grid/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md) and
[`articles_dev/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md).

**`/signal`** (dev300 weighted; articles lede = the served default):

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | articles lede F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. | articles full F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.914 / 0.918 | 0.0% | 100.0% | 15.4% | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 1/14 | 0.635 [0.329, 0.817] | 0/10 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.867 / 0.905 | 0.0% | 72.9% | 33.2% | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 1/20 | 0.907 [0.820, 0.989] | 0/20 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.948 / 0.891 | 0.0% | 26.3% | 24.2% | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 0/17 | 0.880 [0.761, 0.976] | 0/19 |

**`/analyze`** (full scope, sentiment-first, \|s\| >= 1, coverage 100% for all):

| model | config | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | signal rate | articles F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | v1 | 0.752 [0.664, 0.834] | 0.877 / 0.821 | 0.0% | 21.4% | 0.880 [0.791, 0.989] | 0/22 |
| `ministral-3:3b` | v5 | 0.685 [0.589, 0.772] | 0.837 / 0.768 | 1.0% | 20.0% | 0.741 [0.611, 0.858] | 0/19 |
| `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | v5 | 0.647 [0.553, 0.741] | 0.702 / 0.752 | 0.0% | 23.1% | 0.779 [0.646, 0.879] | 1/22 |

No served rule clearly fails on the articles. Clearly failing means the whole inversion CI is above 2%, or the
whole coverage CI is below half the dev300 coverage. So every dev300 threshold stands.

What the error analysis found ([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md),
[`error_patterns.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/error_patterns.json)):

- **Inversions are nearly absent.** Across the six best configs only one tweet is inverted, by `ministral`.
  The wrong calls are mostly gold-neutral tweets called directional (1-8 per model). The real loss is recall:
  34 (`clef-flash`) to 162 (`qwen3.5:0.8b`) directional tweets are missed. For every generative model the
  largest miss bucket is price-move tweets, which the impact rubric reads as immaterial.
- **`directional_tau` is the largest single lever.** `qwen3.5:0.8b` puts most of its mass on neutral, and the
  tau rule lifts its F0.5 by +0.218 [+0.141, +0.307] (paired). The same rule loses for the peaked decision
  models (-0.046 and -0.303), so they keep the plain rule.
- **Other changes.** Rubric A beats rubric B for every generative model. Shots help `qwen3.5:0.8b` on the
  label schema but hurt every `/analyze` model, so every frozen `/analyze` prompt is zero-shot. Summary-first
  never wins and delays the score (2-3x on articles). The price-move rubric sentence was not added, because
  articles do not show the tweet miss (0-1 of 5 directional price-move headlines missed).
- **Knob comparison.** Without tau, the logprob knob beats the ordinal knob on `qwen3.5:0.8b` by +0.059
  [-0.068, +0.187], which is not significant. With tau the logprob knob wins clearly. The ordinal schema
  cannot use tau, because this tokenizer fuses `" -"` and so hides the sign of negative scores.

## 6. Summary evaluation

Decision R6, run by `veritrade_evals.summary_eval`. Summaries come from the serving adapters on the stored HTML
of the 30 dev articles, with full scope and the frozen prompts. Serving caps every summary at **3 sentences / 60
words** at a sentence boundary, and the checks score the capped text.

- **Deterministic checks** (pass rate gate >= 0.8): length, sentence count, every number grounded in the gold
  article (format-tolerant; a derived figure counts as unsupported), the gold entity named, and no truncation.
- **Key-fact coverage**: each Opus key fact and each summary sentence is embedded with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`.
  A fact counts as covered at a best cosine of **>= 0.60** (primary), and 0.75 is the strict bound. In a
  hand-labelled spot check of 45 facts on 10 summaries
  ([`spotcheck.dev.json`](../../../evals/results/summary/spotcheck.dev.json)), 0.60 matched 33 of 45 flags
  with 5 false "covered". 0.55 matched 34 with 6 false, a near tie. 0.75 had no false "covered" but missed 20
  stated facts. See the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`.
- **Opus judges**, blind: per article, the candidate summaries are anonymised as `S1..Sn` and shuffled
  ([`50-judge.md`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md)). Each summary gets faithfulness 1-5, coverage
  1-5, a list of hallucinations, and whether it leads with the market-moving fact. The **material error
  rate** is the share of summaries at faithfulness <= 3.

Results on the dev articles, n = 30 per row ([`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)).
Length and sentence count pass 100% by construction. CIs are bootstrapped within each article's sentiment
label.

| endpoint | model | pass | numbers | entity | key facts 0.60 / 0.75 | faithful [95% CI] | cover | halluc. flag | material [95% CI] | leads |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| summary | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 97% | 93% | 52% / 24% | 3.97 [3.67, 4.23] | 4.30 | 67% | 30% [17%, 47%] | 90% |
| summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 97% | 47% / 23% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 97% | 57% / 29% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 90% | 90% | 100% | 56% / 25% | 4.73 [4.53, 4.93] | 4.43 | 20% | 7% [0%, 17%] | 83% |
| analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | 77% | 80% | 97% | 45% / 19% | 3.77 [3.37, 4.20] | 4.27 | 63% | 40% [23%, 57%] | 80% |

**Hallucination flag vs material error.** The flag rate counts any summary with at least one entry in the
judge's hallucination list. That includes minor slips that still allow faithfulness 4: a loosely worded or
small unsupported detail that "a trader would shrug off". The material error rate counts only faithfulness
<= 3: a wrong key number, an unsupported claim that matters, a misattribution, or worse. So `qwen3.5:4b` on
`/summary` is flagged on half the articles but has a material error on 10% [0%, 20%] of them. The material
rate is the one to read as risk. The deterministic number check agrees in direction: 1-3 unsupported numbers
across 30 summaries for the qwen models, and 8 for `ministral`.

## 7. Selection

The rules are in [`selection/selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md). A candidate must
first pass the accuracy filters: dev300 inversion <= 2%, articles dev not clearly over the cap, and the summary
pass rate >= 0.8. It must then meet the native warm latency budgets from R7 (measured in `05-latency.md`).
Among the survivors, `/signal` and `/analyze` rank on dev300 F0.5, then articles dev F0.5. `/summary` ranks on
judge faithfulness, then judge coverage. Budgets are reported, never moved. When nothing meets a budget, the
Pareto knee is used and the reason is stated.

| endpoint | winner | deciding numbers | others |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (v2-label, tau 0.28) | the only candidate inside the 500 ms lede budget: p50 178 ms, dev300 F0.5 0.730 | `clef-flash` 0.874 at 659 ms; `nimble` 0.843 at 1,061 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v2) | faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97, paired +0.43 [0.07, 0.77]; TTFT p50 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | `qwen3.5:2b` faster (484 / 1,272 ms), more material errors (30%) |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v1) | dev300 F0.5 0.752; TTFT p50 1,292 ms (limit 1,500), complete 2,584 ms | `ministral` 0.685, `qwen3-instruct` 0.647 |

The bundled models are `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` + `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, 4.34 GB in total against the 10 GB cap (R8).

**The `/signal` trade-off.** `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874) but misses the 500 ms lede
budget (p50 659 ms). Its 10.58 GB model file alone also exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap. `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (0.843,
1,061 ms) misses the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms. Its dev300
precision is high (0.91 / 0.92) but its recall is low: it misses about half the directional articles on dev.
The budget was not moved to fit the 9B models. Both stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with
the `model` parameter on native Ollama, for callers who can trade latency for accuracy.

On `/analyze`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` has the best summary faithfulness (4.73 vs 4.47). The paired gap of
0.27 [-0.07, 0.60] is not significant, and the endpoint ranks on signal F0.5 first, where it is last.

## 8. Holdout

**Protocol.** `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}`
([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)).

- It runs the frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, with no re-tuning, on natural class priors
  (unweighted). A prompt that has drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` is the holdout F0.5 minus the
  dev F0.5 of the same rule: the articles dev set at the same scope for articles, dev300 for the tweet and
  cross-domain sets.
- Cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`, and the three
  `/analyze` finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`. The two winners also run on `fpb_allagree`
  and `finentity_single`. The `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling runs on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. That
  makes 22 cells. Summaries from the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles then go to the
  blind Opus judges.
- **Run once.** [`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) is a guard keyed by the
  sha256 of `frozen.json`. It records the selection sha256, the git sha, and the start and completion times.
  An interrupted run resumes from its caches. A completed config refuses a second run unless
  `--force --reason` is passed, and that is logged in the guard and must be disclosed. The run also refuses a
  provisional selection, one made before the latency suite, unless `--allow-provisional` is passed. This
  selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` re-scores the cached predictions only and never calls a model. The tables below come from
  `evals/results/holdout/holdout.md`, which that command writes.

## 9. Threats to validity

- **One labeller family.** The article labels, the gold bodies, the key facts and the summary judges are all
  Claude Opus. The labellers were independent and the judges blind, but a shared bias would not show, and no
  human checked any label.
- **Small n.** With 30 dev and 60 test articles, the CIs span 0.2-0.5 F0.5. Article results check that the
  rules transfer; they do not rank the models.
- **Tuned on tweets.** Thresholds and prompts were tuned on 300 tweets and only checked on articles. The CIs
  at a tuned threshold do not include the threshold choice. `directional_tau` adds one more tuned parameter.
- **Class mix.** The article sets are balanced, while real traffic is likely neutral-heavy (64.7% of Twitter
  FNS train). So per-call precision in production is likely below the article-set figure. dev300 corrects for
  this with weights; the articles do not.
- **A cleaner set than reality.** It covers 10 fetchable sources only, a 60-day window, and 24 ambiguous
  articles replaced. For three sources the extraction profiles were tuned with this set in view (see the
  caveats in `03-extraction.md`).
- **Contamination.** The public datasets may be in the models' pretraining data. The articles are recent,
  which limits that overlap but does not rule it out.
- **Precision first, by design.** The selected `/signal` model misses about half the directional articles. A
  missed call is cheap under Q2, but users will see many neutrals.
- **Latency context.** Grid and articles timings ran on a shared machine and are indicative only. The selection
  uses the dedicated native-metal suite; the Docker CPU picture is in `05-latency.md`.
- **Keyword buckets** in the error analysis are a first-match heuristic, meant for orientation only.
````

````markdown
# 04 - Evaluation

How the models, prompts and thresholds behind `/signal`, `/summary` and `/analyze` were chosen, and how well they
do. The reasons behind each choice are in [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md); the fetch and extraction path every
eval runs through is in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) and [`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md).
Every number links to the committed result file it comes from. Rigor is balanced per aspect, as for the rest of this
PoC (R2): the signal metric, the splits and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean;
the article labels and summary judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check.

```
dev300 grid (prompt x policy x threshold per model) -> one error-analysis pass -> articles dev check (transfer only,
never re-tuned) -> freeze -> summary eval on the frozen prompts -> latency suite -> select -> holdout, run once
```

## 1. Objective and metrics

A wrong directional call costs a trade, a missed one costs little (Q2). So the positives are directional calls, and
neutral or an abstention is the safe default. Definitions follow
[`metrics.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/metrics.py):

- **Directional call**: an answered (not abstained) bullish or bearish prediction. An abstention is served as neutral
  with `abstained: true`. **Coverage** is the share of rows answered, **signal rate** the share with a directional
  call, **accuracy** the share whose served label (abstention -> neutral) equals gold.
- **Precision / recall** per class c in {bullish, bearish}: correct c calls / c calls and correct c calls / gold c
  rows. A class with no calls scores 0, not NaN, so "always neutral" scores F0.5 0.
- **F0.5 macro** (the selection metric): the mean of the two per-class F-beta scores at beta = 0.5, which weights
  precision above recall. Neutral is not a positive class.
- **Inversion rate**: bullish<->bearish flips (a directional call on a gold-directional row with the opposite label)
  over all directional calls. The cap is **2%**.
- **Operating point**: thresholds are swept over 0 and every distinct confidence value (the only points where calls
  change); the chosen point is the **max F0.5 among points with inversion <= 2%**, ties to higher coverage, then a
  lower threshold. A config with no point under the cap is "cap missed" and cannot be selected.
- **Prevalence weights** (dev300 only): each row is weighted by train prior / sample prior of its class, so rates on
  the balanced sample estimate the real tweet mix; confusion and error counts stay raw. Articles and holdout sets are
  unweighted.
- **CIs**: 95% percentile bootstrap (B = 1,000, seed 20261018), resampled within each gold class, on the headline
  metrics only (F0.5 macro, inversion, coverage, signal rate, accuracy). Gaps between two configs on the same rows use
  a paired bootstrap. The threshold is not re-chosen per resample, so a CI at a tuned operating point is optimistic.

## 2. Datasets and splits

| split | source | role | n | bullish / bearish / neutral | weighting |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `dev300` | Twitter Financial News Sentiment (FNS), train | tuning: prompt grid, thresholds | 300 | 100 / 100 / 100 | train prior 20.2% / 15.1% / 64.7% |
| articles dev | Opus-labelled articles (section 3) | transfer check, error analysis, summary eval | 30 | 10 / 10 / 10 | none |
| articles test | Opus-labelled articles | holdout | 60 | 20 / 20 / 20 | none |
| `tfns_val` | Twitter FNS, validation | holdout, in-domain tweets | 2,388 | 475 / 347 / 1,566 | none (natural prior) |
| `fpb_allagree` | Financial PhraseBank, Sentences_AllAgree | holdout, cross-domain sentences | 2,259 | 570 / 303 / 1,386 | none |
| `finentity_single` | FinEntity, rows with one distinct label | holdout, cross-domain paragraphs | 851 | 181 / 180 / 490 | none |

Sources: the split headers in [`evals/data/splits/`](../../../evals/data/splits/) and
[`stats.json`](../../../evals/data/articles/stats.json).

- **dev300** comes from Twitter FNS train after dropping 69 rows whose normalised text is also in validation, 70
  duplicates and 4 rows with conflicting labels; then 100 per class with seed 20261018. Class weights are 0.605
  (bullish), 0.453 (bearish) and 1.942 (neutral). FPB and FinEntity positive / negative / neutral map to bullish /
  bearish / neutral; FPB collapses exact duplicates and drops sentences seen with two labels; FinEntity keeps rows
  with at least one entity annotation and exactly one distinct label.
- **Committed**: per split, the ids, the sha1 of the normalised text (NFKC, casefold, URLs and whitespace runs
  dropped), the labels, the selection rule and the dataset revision;
  [`datasets.lock.json`](../../../evals/data/datasets.lock.json) pins each dataset commit, file sha256 and licence. A
  split fails to load on a revision mismatch, a missing id, text-hash drift or label drift.
- **Never committed**: dataset text (FPB is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), downloaded at eval time into the gitignored
  `evals/data/private/`, along with article HTML, gold bodies, headlines, predictions, summaries and judge packets.

## 3. The Opus-labelled article set

Public datasets hold sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles (Q5, R5). The set has 90 real articles
from the 10 sources in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md), 3 classes x 3 per source, published 2026-08-19 to
2026-10-18. One seeded article per (source, class) cell goes to dev: **30 dev / 60 test**. Two quota adjustments keep
the 30/30/30 balance (Yahoo 4 bearish, BBC 2). Every Opus step ran as a Claude Code subagent pinned to Claude Opus
5.5, so no API key or paid service was used. Prompts and runbook:
[`evals/opus_prompts/`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md).

1. **Discover** (one agent per source): candidates from RSS and section pages, fetched by the deterministic
   `articles` CLI through the serving fetcher; agents never fetch anything themselves.
2. **Gold**: Opus picks the body as line ranges of the page, writes 3-5 key facts in its own words, and gives a
   provisional label.
3. **Label A / label B**: two independent agents apply the service's rubric (economic impact on the primary entity,
   not tone; neutral when in doubt), never seeing each other's output or the provisional label.
4. **Adjudicate**: one agent reviews every article where the labels differ or either labeller flagged ambiguity, and
   either keeps it (its label is final) or replaces it as genuinely ambiguous.
5. **Refill and finalize**: short cells repeat steps 1-4; `finalize` picks per cell, agreed articles first; `verify`
   re-checks the set.

| pool statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| articles with a usable gold body | 298 |
| labelled by both labellers | 157 |
| labels agree | 151 (raw agreement 96.2%) |
| Cohen's kappa (A vs B) | 0.943 |
| sent to adjudication (6 disagreements, 43 agreed but flagged ambiguous) | 49 (31.2%) |
| replaced by the adjudicator | 24 of 49 (49.0%) |
| adjudicated articles kept in the final 90 | 5 |

In the final 90, A and B agree on every label (kappa 1.0), by construction since agreed articles are picked first, so
the pool agreement is the meaningful figure. The committed [`articles.jsonl`](../../../evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl)
holds ids, URLs, sources, dates, both labels, the adjudication, entity and ticker, and rationales and key facts in
Opus's words; the CLI rejects any that share 10 consecutive words with the article, so no article text is committed.
**Caveats**: Opus-only labels with no human check; replacing ambiguous articles makes the set cleaner than real
traffic; with 10 articles per class on dev, a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero.

## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` + `/summary`; the combined one `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells ([`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json)), all on
native Metal, Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0, sampling penalties neutralised; see the build-time
findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic shots =
  v1-v4; for `qwen3.5:0.8b` each runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: rubric or plain one-line question x described or bare criteria = v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the field-order
  check, on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): argmax of the native class probabilities; abstain when it is below `min_p`.
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): first label-token probabilities, renormalised over the tokens the grammar
  accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still yields the likelier
  directional class when that class holds p >= tau; below tau the row is a served neutral, not an abstention. On a
  first-token label collision the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streams, fallback): a score from -2 to 2, directional only when \|score\| >= t. It is read
  mid-stream as soon as it closes and needs no logprobs (Q3); logprob-weighted streaming confidence is on the backlog.

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default (headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200
tokens); `lede` and `full` are both scored on articles. `/analyze` reads `full` and emits the sentiment field first,
so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error analysis and freeze.** One hand-written read of the grid counts
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)) drove the changes listed in section 5. `veritrade_evals
freeze` then wrote [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json) and
[`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml):

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze` takes v5
unless the whole paired 95% CI of its gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles, which rejected v5 for
`qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first needed a dev300 win without an articles loss; it never
got one.

## 5. Accuracy on dev

Frozen configs only. Articles use the dev300 threshold unchanged and the serving extraction (`selectolax` +
`cascade`). Sources: [`grid/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md),
[`articles_dev/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md).

**`/signal`** (dev300 weighted; articles lede is the served default):

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | articles lede F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. | articles full F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.914 / 0.918 | 0.0% | 100.0% | 15.4% | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 1/14 | 0.635 [0.329, 0.817] | 0/10 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.867 / 0.905 | 0.0% | 72.9% | 33.2% | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 1/20 | 0.907 [0.820, 0.989] | 0/20 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.948 / 0.891 | 0.0% | 26.3% | 24.2% | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 0/17 | 0.880 [0.761, 0.976] | 0/19 |

**`/analyze`** (full scope, sentiment-first, \|s\| >= 1, coverage 100% for all):

| model | config | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | signal rate | articles F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | v1 | 0.752 [0.664, 0.834] | 0.877 / 0.821 | 0.0% | 21.4% | 0.880 [0.791, 0.989] | 0/22 |
| `ministral-3:3b` | v5 | 0.685 [0.589, 0.772] | 0.837 / 0.768 | 1.0% | 20.0% | 0.741 [0.611, 0.858] | 0/19 |
| `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | v5 | 0.647 [0.553, 0.741] | 0.702 / 0.752 | 0.0% | 23.1% | 0.779 [0.646, 0.879] | 1/22 |

No served rule clearly fails on the articles (whole inversion CI above 2%, or whole coverage CI below half the dev300
coverage), so every dev300 threshold stands. What the error analysis found
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md),
[`error_patterns.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/error_patterns.json)):

- **Inversions are nearly absent**: across the six best configs one tweet is inverted, by `ministral`. Wrong calls
  are mostly gold-neutral tweets called directional (1-8 per model). The real loss is recall: 34 (`clef-flash`) to
  162 (`qwen3.5:0.8b`) directional tweets missed; for every generative model the largest miss bucket is price-move
  tweets, which the impact rubric reads as immaterial.
- **`directional_tau` is the largest single lever**: `qwen3.5:0.8b` parks most of its mass on neutral, and the tau
  rule lifts its F0.5 by +0.218 [+0.141, +0.307] (paired). It loses for the peaked decision models (-0.046 and
  -0.303), so they keep the plain rule.
- **Other changes**: rubric A beats B for every generative model; shots help `qwen3.5:0.8b` on the label schema but
  hurt every `/analyze` model, so all frozen `/analyze` prompts are zero-shot; summary-first never wins and delays
  the score (2-3x on articles). The price-move rubric sentence was not added: articles do not show the tweet miss
  (0-1 of 5 directional price-move headlines missed).
- **Knob comparison**: without tau, the logprob knob beats the ordinal one on `qwen3.5:0.8b` by +0.059 [-0.068,
  +0.187], not significant; with tau it wins clearly. The ordinal schema cannot use tau, because this tokenizer fuses
  `" -"` and hides the sign of negative scores.

## 6. Summary evaluation

Decision R6, run by `veritrade_evals.summary_eval` on the stored HTML of the 30 dev articles through the serving
adapters (full scope, frozen prompts). Serving caps every summary at **3 sentences / 60 words** at a sentence
boundary, and the checks score the capped text.

- **Deterministic checks** (pass-rate gate >= 0.8): length, sentence count, every number grounded in the gold article
  (format-tolerant; a derived figure counts as unsupported), gold entity named, not truncated.
- **Key-fact coverage**: each Opus key fact and each summary sentence is embedded with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact
  is covered at a best cosine **>= 0.60** (primary), with 0.75 as the strict bound. In the hand-labelled spot check
  of 45 facts on 10 summaries ([`spotcheck.dev.json`](../../../evals/results/summary/spotcheck.dev.json)), 0.60
  matched 33 of 45 flags with 5 false "covered" and 0.55 matched 34 with 6, a near tie; 0.75 had no false "covered"
  but missed 20 stated facts (see the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`).
- **Opus judges**, blind: per article the candidate summaries are anonymised as `S1..Sn` and shuffled
  ([`50-judge.md`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md)); each gets faithfulness 1-5, coverage 1-5, a list of
  hallucinations, and whether it leads with the market-moving fact. **Material error rate** = share at
  faithfulness <= 3.

Dev articles, n = 30 per row ([`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)); length and sentence
count pass 100% by construction; CIs resample articles within their sentiment label.

| endpoint | model | pass | numbers | entity | key facts 0.60 / 0.75 | faithful [95% CI] | cover | halluc. flag | material [95% CI] | leads |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| summary | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 97% | 93% | 52% / 24% | 3.97 [3.67, 4.23] | 4.30 | 67% | 30% [17%, 47%] | 90% |
| summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 97% | 47% / 23% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 97% | 57% / 29% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 90% | 90% | 100% | 56% / 25% | 4.73 [4.53, 4.93] | 4.43 | 20% | 7% [0%, 17%] | 83% |
| analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | 77% | 80% | 97% | 45% / 19% | 3.77 [3.37, 4.20] | 4.27 | 63% | 40% [23%, 57%] | 80% |

**Hallucination flag vs material error.** The flag rate counts any summary with at least one entry in the judge's
hallucination list, including minor slips that still allow faithfulness 4 (a loosely worded or small unsupported
detail "a trader would shrug off"). The material error rate counts only faithfulness <= 3: a wrong key number, an
unsupported claim that matters, a misattribution, or worse. So `qwen3.5:4b` on `/summary` is flagged on half the
articles but has a material error on 10% [0%, 20%]; the material rate is the one to read as risk. The deterministic
number check agrees in direction: 1-3 unsupported numbers across 30 summaries for the qwen models, 8 for `ministral`.

## 7. Selection

Rules: [`selection/selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md). Accuracy filters come first (dev300
inversion <= 2%, articles dev not clearly over the cap, summary pass rate >= 0.8), then the native warm latency
budgets of R7 (measured in `05-latency.md`). Survivors rank on dev300 F0.5 then articles dev F0.5 (`/signal`,
`/analyze`) or on judge faithfulness then coverage (`/summary`). Budgets are reported, never moved; when nothing meets
one, the Pareto knee is used with the reason stated.

| endpoint | winner | deciding numbers | others |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (v2-label, tau 0.28) | only candidate inside the 500 ms lede budget: p50 178 ms, dev300 F0.5 0.730 | `clef-flash` 0.874 at 659 ms; `nimble` 0.843 at 1,061 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v2) | faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97, paired +0.43 [0.07, 0.77]; TTFT p50 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | `qwen3.5:2b` faster (484 / 1,272 ms), more material errors (30%) |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v1) | dev300 F0.5 0.752; TTFT p50 1,292 ms (limit 1,500), complete 2,584 ms | `ministral` 0.685, `qwen3-instruct` 0.647 |

Bundled models (R8): `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` + `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, 4.34 GB against the 10 GB cap.

**The `/signal` trade-off.** `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874) but misses the 500 ms lede budget
(p50 659 ms), and its 10.58 GB file alone exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap. `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (0.843, 1,061 ms) misses
the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms: high dev300 precision (0.91 / 0.92), low
recall (it misses about half the directional articles on dev). The budget was not moved to fit the 9B models; both
stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native Ollama.

On `/analyze`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` has the best summary faithfulness (4.73 vs 4.47, paired gap 0.27 [-0.07,
0.60], not significant), but the endpoint ranks on signal F0.5 first, where it is last.

## 8. Holdout

**Protocol**: `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}`
([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)).

- Frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, no re-tuning, natural class priors (unweighted); a prompt that
  drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` = holdout F0.5 minus the dev F0.5 of the same rule (articles dev at
  the same scope for articles; dev300 for the tweet and cross-domain sets).
- 22 cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`; the three `/analyze`
  finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`; the two winners also on `fpb_allagree` and
  `finentity_single`; the `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. Then summaries from
  the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles go to the blind Opus judges.
- **Run once**: [`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) is a guard keyed by the sha256 of
  `frozen.json`, recording the selection sha256, git sha, and start and completion times. An interrupted run resumes
  from its caches; a completed config refuses a second run unless `--force --reason` is passed, which is logged in
  the guard and must be disclosed. It also refuses a provisional selection (one made before the latency suite)
  without `--allow-provisional`; this selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` only re-scores the cached predictions and never calls a model; the tables below come from the
  `evals/results/holdout/holdout.md` it writes.

## 9. Threats to validity

- **One labeller family**: article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judges are all Claude Opus. Labellers
  were independent and judges blind, but a shared bias would not show, and no human checked any label.
- **Small n**: with 30 dev and 60 test articles, CIs span 0.2-0.5 F0.5; article results check that rules transfer,
  they do not rank models.
- **Tuned on tweets**: thresholds and prompts were tuned on 300 tweets and only checked on articles; CIs at a tuned
  threshold exclude the threshold choice, and `directional_tau` is one more tuned parameter.
- **Class mix**: the article sets are balanced while real traffic is likely neutral-heavy (64.7% in Twitter FNS
  train), so per-call precision in production is likely below the article figure. dev300 reweights; articles do not.
- **Cleaner than reality**: 10 fetchable sources, a 60-day window, 24 ambiguous articles replaced; for three sources
  the extraction profiles were tuned with this set in view (caveats in `03-extraction.md`).
- **Contamination**: the public datasets may be in the models' pretraining data; the articles are recent, which
  limits but does not rule out overlap.
- **Precision first, by design**: the selected `/signal` model misses about half the directional articles; a miss is
  cheap under Q2, but users will see many neutrals.
- **Latency context**: grid and articles timings ran on a shared machine and are indicative only; selection uses the
  dedicated native-metal suite, and the Docker CPU picture is in `05-latency.md`.
- **Keyword buckets** in the error analysis are a first-match heuristic, for orientation only.
````

````markdown
# 04 - Evaluation

How the models, prompts and thresholds behind `/signal`, `/summary` and `/analyze` were chosen, and how well they
do. The reasons behind each choice are in [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md); the fetch and extraction path every
eval runs through is in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) and [`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md).
Every number links to the committed result file it comes from. Rigor is balanced per aspect, as for the rest of this
PoC (R2): the signal metric, the splits and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean;
the article labels and summary judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check.

```
dev300 grid (prompt x policy x threshold per model) -> one error-analysis pass -> articles dev check (transfer only,
never re-tuned) -> freeze -> summary eval on the frozen prompts -> latency suite -> select -> holdout, run once
```

## 1. Objective and metrics

A wrong directional call costs a trade, a missed one costs little (Q2). So the positives are directional calls, and
neutral or an abstention is the safe default. Definitions follow
[`metrics.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/metrics.py):

- **Directional call**: an answered (not abstained) bullish or bearish prediction. An abstention is served as neutral
  with `abstained: true`. **Coverage** is the share of rows answered, **signal rate** the share with a directional
  call, **accuracy** the share whose served label (abstention -> neutral) equals gold.
- **Precision / recall** per class c in {bullish, bearish}: correct c calls / c calls and correct c calls / gold c
  rows. A class with no calls scores 0, not NaN, so "always neutral" scores F0.5 0.
- **F0.5 macro** (the selection metric): the mean of the two per-class F-beta scores at beta = 0.5, which weights
  precision above recall. Neutral is not a positive class.
- **Inversion rate**: bullish<->bearish flips (a directional call on a gold-directional row with the opposite label)
  over all directional calls. The cap is **2%**.
- **Operating point**: thresholds are swept over 0 and every distinct confidence value (the only points where calls
  change); the chosen point is the **max F0.5 among points with inversion <= 2%**, ties to higher coverage, then a
  lower threshold. A config with no point under the cap is "cap missed" and cannot be selected.
- **Prevalence weights** (dev300 only): each row is weighted by train prior / sample prior of its class, so rates on
  the balanced sample estimate the real tweet mix; confusion and error counts stay raw. Articles and holdout sets are
  unweighted.
- **CIs**: 95% percentile bootstrap (B = 1,000, seed 20261018), resampled within each gold class, on the headline
  metrics only (F0.5 macro, inversion, coverage, signal rate, accuracy). Gaps between two configs on the same rows use
  a paired bootstrap. The threshold is not re-chosen per resample, so a CI at a tuned operating point is optimistic.

## 2. Datasets and splits

| split | source | role | n | bullish / bearish / neutral | weighting |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `dev300` | Twitter Financial News Sentiment (FNS), train | tuning: prompt grid, thresholds | 300 | 100 / 100 / 100 | train prior 20.2% / 15.1% / 64.7% |
| articles dev | Opus-labelled articles (section 3) | transfer check, error analysis, summary eval | 30 | 10 / 10 / 10 | none |
| articles test | Opus-labelled articles | holdout | 60 | 20 / 20 / 20 | none |
| `tfns_val` | Twitter FNS, validation | holdout, in-domain tweets | 2,388 | 475 / 347 / 1,566 | none (natural prior) |
| `fpb_allagree` | Financial PhraseBank, Sentences_AllAgree | holdout, cross-domain sentences | 2,259 | 570 / 303 / 1,386 | none |
| `finentity_single` | FinEntity, rows with one distinct label | holdout, cross-domain paragraphs | 851 | 181 / 180 / 490 | none |

Sources: the split headers in [`evals/data/splits/`](../../../evals/data/splits/) and
[`stats.json`](../../../evals/data/articles/stats.json).

- **dev300** comes from Twitter FNS train after dropping 69 rows whose normalised text is also in validation, 70
  duplicates and 4 rows with conflicting labels; then 100 per class with seed 20261018. Class weights are 0.605
  (bullish), 0.453 (bearish) and 1.942 (neutral). FPB and FinEntity positive / negative / neutral map to bullish /
  bearish / neutral; FPB collapses exact duplicates and drops sentences seen with two labels; FinEntity keeps rows
  with at least one entity annotation and exactly one distinct label.
- **Committed**: per split, the ids, the sha1 of the normalised text (NFKC, casefold, URLs and whitespace runs
  dropped), the labels, the selection rule and the dataset revision;
````

```python
"""Report relative markdown links in the given files whose targets do not exist."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)#\s]+)(?:#[^)]*)?\)")

missing = 0
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    doc = Path(name).resolve()
    for target in LINK.findall(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        if "://" in target:
            continue
        path = (doc.parent / target).resolve()
        status = "ok" if path.exists() else "MISSING"
        missing += status == "MISSING"
        print(f"{status:7s} {target}")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)

```
