````markdown
# VeriTrade Analytics prescreen - implementation plan

## Context

VeriTrade's prescreen (`.context/prescreen-brief-kristiyan-dimitrov.md`) asks for a Python API that takes a public
financial-news URL, fetches and extracts the article, and returns an LLM summary + Bullish/Bearish/Neutral sentiment
with low latency, plus a basic frontend, a README (design, latency trade-offs, run/test, AI tools) and the committed AI
conversation log. Kris handpicked the approach from `.context/openai-research.md` in a `/grill-me` interview (Q1-Q20,
R1-R10, 3 follow-ups); every decision below is settled. Guiding principle: this is a PoC, balance rigor per aspect.
Deliverable: public repo `cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics`, everything pushed, transcript + meta under `.context/`.

Greenfield repo: only `.context/` exists, so there is nothing to reuse; evals import the serving code so what is
measured is what is served.

## Settled decisions (copied verbatim into `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`)

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Stack | FastAPI + uv (Python 3.13 workspace: `backend`, `evals`); Next.js 16 static export served BY FastAPI (one origin, zero proxy hops, no nginx/Node at runtime); dev = `pnpm dev` + CORS localhost |
| Ollama | Native brew Ollama 0.40.4 (Metal) is the Mac default; compose profile `bundled` (ollama/ollama:0.40.5 + pull init) for Linux/CI; `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` switch; results labelled `native-metal` / `docker-cpu` |
| Split group | `/api/signal`: decision models `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (`/v1/systemone`, native probabilities) + generative baseline `qwen3.5:0.8b`; `/api/summary`: `qwen3.5:2b`, `qwen3.5:4b` |
| Combined group | `/api/analyze`: `qwen3.5:4b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`, `ministral-3:3b`; `qwen3.5:9b` holdout-only quality ceiling |
| Objective | F0.5 macro over {bullish, bearish}; bullish<->bearish inversion cap 2%; winner = best F0.5 within latency budget, else Pareto knee (stated) |
| Confidence | Compare label-token logprob threshold vs ordinal -2..+2 \|score\| threshold for generative models; decision models threshold `probabilities`; API returns `sentiment` + `abstained` (+ confidence/score) |
| Scope | `/signal` `scope=lede` (default) vs `full`, both evaluated |
| Streaming | Both SSE and JSON variants for `/summary` and `/analyze`; SSE events `meta` -> `sentiment` -> `summary_delta*` -> `done` (sentiment exactly once before `done`; position follows frozen field order) |
| Budgets (native, warm, excl. fetch) | `/signal` lede p50 <= 500 ms; `/summary` + `/analyze` TTFT <= 1.5 s, complete p50 <= 4 s; surfaced to Kris (not moved) if unrealistic after baseline |
| Data | Dev: stratified 300 Twitter FNS train; holdout: full Twitter validation + FPB AllAgree (zip, never committed) + FinEntity single-label; 90 Opus-labelled articles (10 sources x 3 classes x 3; 30 dev / 60 test), double label + adjudicator, no human check |
| Prompts | Lean grid per model (2 rubrics x few-shot {0,4} x field order where relevant, <= 8 configs), one error-analysis pass, freeze, holdout once |
| Summaries | <= 3 sentences / 60 words, lead with market-moving fact; eval = deterministic checks + embedding key-fact coverage + Opus-as-judge on finalists |
| Extraction | Matrix: parsers {selectolax, lxml, bs4+html.parser, bs4+lxml} x own {jsonld, profile, density, cascade} + trafilatura {default, precision}, readability-lxml, newspaper4k, justext, strip-tags; Opus gold bodies (gitignored); switchable from UI |
| Sources | Yahoo Finance, CNBC, AP News, Investing.com, Motley Fool, Benzinga, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business; backups Fortune, Business Wire, Guardian, BBC; `probe_sources.py` decides |
| Fetching | Browser header set, no evasion; typed `source_blocked` / `paywalled` / `consent_required` with hints; Yahoo consent = reject-all + cookie cache, fallback `consent_required`; `SEC_USER_AGENT` env |
| Tests/CI | Unit + integration BE/FE, Playwright e2e on compose, all on GitHub Actions; skeleton fixtures (real DOM, synthetic text) + weekly non-blocking live smoke |
| Repo | Milestone commits straight to `main` (no branches); repo-local `Kristiyan Dimitrov <kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com>`; MIT; `.context/` committed; transcript = session `0024648c-...` only, redacted |
| Ops | Stop all other running Docker containers during setup (names recorded); leave them stopped; final message gives the exact `docker start ...` |

## Architecture

```
pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version(3.13)   # uv workspace root; ruff, mypy, pytest config
backend/src/veritrade/
  config.py errors.py timing.py models_registry.py
  data/{models.toml, sources.toml}              # single serving config + source registry
  fetch/{client,ssrf,headers,consent,detect,cache}.py
  extract/{dom,jsonld,profiles,density,cascade,third_party,registry,scope}.py
  prompts/{registry.py, data/<endpoint>/<model>.toml}
  inference/{schemas,ollama,decision,adapters,confidence,incremental}.py
  services/{article,signal,summary,analyze}.py
  api/{app,routes,contracts,sse}.py  healthcheck.py
backend/tests/{unit,integration,live}/  backend/tests/fixtures/{skeletons/<source>/,ollama/}
evals/src/veritrade_evals/{__main__,datasets,splits,runner,metrics,extraction_bench,latency,opus,select,report}.py
evals/{opus_prompts/, data/{splits,articles,judgements}/, results/}   evals/data/private/ (gitignored)
frontend/{src/app/{page,benchmarks/page}.tsx, src/lib/{api,sse}.ts, src/components/, tests/, e2e/}
docker/app.Dockerfile  docker/ollama-pull.sh  compose.yaml  compose.e2e.yaml  env/{bundled.env,ci-models.txt}
scripts/{check,dev_setup,probe_sources,capture_skeletons,export_openapi,export_transcript}.py
.github/workflows/{ci.yml,live-smoke.yml}
.context/{brief, research, docs/design/{00-overview,01-decisions,02-source-probe,03-extraction,04-evals,05-latency,90-optional-backlog}.md, transcript/}
```

Backend essentials:
- **fetch/**: one `httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, follow_redirects=False)`; manual redirect loop (max 5) with
  `ssrf.check_target` on every hop (http/https, ports 80/443, all resolved IPs `is_global`); streamed body cap 5 MB,
  HTML content-type gate, 3 s connect / 8 s deadline. `headers.py` Chrome set, `sec.gov` uses `SEC_USER_AGENT`
  (default: public commit contact), EDGAR <= 10 req/s. `consent.py` Yahoo reject-all POST + retry once.
  `detect.classify` maps 401/403/429 + challenge markers (Cloudflare, DataDome, PerimeterX, Akamai) to
  `SourceBlocked`, JSON-LD `isAccessibleForFree:false` to `Paywalled`. `cache.SingleFlightCache` (LRU+TTL,
  in-flight task sharing; typed errors 60 s negative TTL).
- **extract/**: `Dom` protocol over 4 parser backends; own strategies run on `Dom` (16 cells); third-party
  extractors lazy-imported (parser N/A); `registry.extract(html, url, parser, extractor) -> Article`;
  `scope.build_input` lede (~200 tokens) / full, capped by model `max_input_tokens`. Press-release boilerplate
  (forward-looking statements, About, contacts) dropped by profiles.
- **prompts/**: TOML per (endpoint, model) with versions `v1..vN`, `active=`; `prompt_version` includes content
  sha so caches invalidate. Article text fenced as untrusted data.
- **inference/**: `ollama.OllamaClient` (httpx) is the ONLY Ollama path for app and evals: `chat`/`chat_stream`
  (`think:false`, JSON-schema `format`, `temperature:0`, `seed`, `num_ctx`/`num_predict` from `models.toml`,
  `logprobs:true, top_logprobs:20` on non-streaming label calls), `systemone` (criteria order neutral, bullish,
  bearish; client-side timing), `embed`, `ps`, `unload`, `show`, `version`. `confidence.py` policies:
  `ProbabilityPolicy`, `LabelLogprobPolicy` (first-token probs of the 3 labels; score-sign fallback if tokens
  collide), `OrdinalPolicy`; streaming and `/analyze` always use ordinal. `incremental.JsonFieldScanner` emits
  `ScoreClosed` / `SummaryText` from chunk deltas (escape-safe).
- **config**: `models.toml` holds allowlist, per-endpoint defaults, `num_ctx`, `num_predict`, scope default, ordinal
  `t` (always) and `tau` (when knob L wins); `freeze` writes it. Container env: `VT_MODELS`, `VT_PULL_MODELS`
  (host-side compose var `OLLAMA_MODELS` maps to these; never passed raw into the ollama container),
  `VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL`, `VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS` (refused unless `VT_ENV=test`).
- **API** (`/api`): `POST /signal`, `/summary`, `/summary/stream`, `/analyze`, `/analyze/stream`; `GET /models`
  (allowlist x installed tags x defaults), `GET /health` (Ollama reachable, version >= 0.40.4, backend label).
  Requests carry `url, model?, parser, extractor, scope, no_cache`. Responses carry `meta` (model, prompt_version,
  parser, extractor, scope, cached) and `timings` (fetch, consent, parse, extract, inference wall/ttft/load/
  prompt_eval/eval, cache hit/miss/joined). One error table in `contracts.py`: 400 invalid_url /
  blocked_destination / model_not_allowed; 422 paywalled / consent_required / extraction_empty /
  unsupported_content; 502 source_blocked / upstream_http; 503 model_unavailable / llm_unreachable; 504 timeouts.
  Fetch/extract errors return before a stream opens; mid-stream failures emit `error`. Static export mounted at `/`
  after the routers.
- **Frontend**: Next 16 App Router, strict TS, CSS modules, `output:'export'`. Analyze page: URL, mode
  split|combined, streaming toggle, model/parser/extractor/scope pickers from `/api/models`, SignalCard (abstained
  state), streaming SummaryPanel, ErrorBanner (code + hint), LatencyBar (two lanes in split mode). Split mode fires
  `/signal` + `/summary/stream` concurrently (backend single-flight shares the fetch). `lib/sse.ts` = fetch +
  `TextDecoderStream` frame parser + AbortController. Benchmarks page renders `benchmarks.json` (prebuild copies
  `evals/results/benchmarks.json`, falls back to committed `benchmarks.sample.json`). Types generated from
  `backend/openapi.json` (drift-checked).
- **Docker**: `app.Dockerfile` stages node:24-slim (pnpm build) -> uv python3.13 (`uv sync --frozen --no-dev
  --no-editable --package veritrade-backend`) -> python:3.13-slim runtime, non-root, `veritrade-healthcheck`
  console script, `uvicorn veritrade.api.app:create_app --factory`. `compose.yaml`: `app` (8000, default
  `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434`, `extra_hosts` host-gateway); profile `bundled`: `ollama`
  (named volume, no host port, healthcheck `ollama list`) + `ollama-pull` (`service_completed_successfully`,
  `required:false`), enabled via `--profile bundled --env-file env/bundled.env`. `compose.e2e.yaml`: nginx
  `fixture-site` serving skeletons as `fixtures.local`, test env, model dir bind mount for CI cache.

## Evaluation (`uv run python -m veritrade_evals <cmd>`)

- **Datasets**: Twitter FNS parquet via `hf_hub_download` at pinned revision; FPB zip ->
  `Sentences_AllAgree.txt` (iso-8859-1, `rsplit("@",1)`); FinEntity single-label rows. Committed: revisions lock,
  split ids + text hashes; never dataset text. dev300 balanced 100/100/100 (seed 20261018) with prevalence weights
  applied to metrics and tau selection (flagged in docs).
- **Runner**: async, bounded concurrency (4 for accuracy, 1 for latency), resumable JSONL prediction cache keyed by
  sha(config, model digest, rendered prompt, harness version), one model resident at a time via
  `OllamaClient.ps/unload`. Sentiment-first runs stop after the score closes (later tokens cannot change it).
- **Grid** (lean): decision models: instructions {plain, rubric} x criteria descriptions {none, one-line};
  `qwen3.5:0.8b` signal: rubric {A, B} x k {0, 4} x schema {label, ordinal} (gives both knobs); combined models:
  rubric x k (4) sentiment-first, then best config summary-first (field-order check, only if the M3 probe confirms
  Ollama honours schema property order); scope lede vs full on articles_dev for signal finalists. Few-shot shots
  are synthetic (no dataset leakage). Error pass writes `.temp/eval/error-analysis/*.md`, one revision, then
  `freeze` writes `active=` versions + thresholds into `models.toml`.
- **Metrics**: weighted per-class P/R, F0.5 macro, inversion rate, coverage/signal rate, 3x4 confusion, risk-coverage
  sweep, operating point = max F0.5 under 2% inversion; bootstrap CIs (B=1000) on headline metrics only.
  Holdout-once guard (`evals/results/holdout_runs.json`).
- **Opus pipeline** (Claude Code subagents, every spawn `model: "opus"`, prompts in `evals/opus_prompts/`):
  1. discover per source (RSS/sections, last 60 days, oversample 5/class, keep only URLs our fetcher retrieves;
     HTML saved to `evals/data/private/html/`);
  2. gold body + 3-5 key facts in one pass (gold to `private/gold/`, validated as >= 95% substrings of page text);
  3. labellers A and B in parallel, isolated, see only gold body; 4. adjudicator on disagreement/ambiguity,
     replacements re-run 2-4; 5. finalize 3/3/3 per source (+-1, 30/30/30 overall), seeded 30/60 split,
     agreement + Cohen's kappa; 6. judge finalist summaries anonymised (faithfulness 1-5, coverage 1-5,
     hallucination flags, leads-with-market-moving-fact).
  Committed: `evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl` (url, fetched_at, sha256, label, score, entity, ticker,
  rationale, key_facts, split, agreement), `evals/data/judgements/`. Never committed: HTML, gold bodies.
- **Summary eval**: numeric faithfulness, entity named, length; key-fact coverage via `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`
  (cosine >= 0.75, spot-checked); Opus judge on dev for selection, winner judged on test.
- **Extraction matrix**: 22 combos over 90 local HTML: p50/p95 ms (median of 5), token P/R/F1 vs gold, leakage,
  tokens-to-LLM, failure rate, downstream signal agreement (lede of each extraction vs gold), install MB.
- **Latency**: preflight asserts no running containers + records Ollama env/version/backend; `no_cache=true`;
  cold n=3, warm n=30 over articles_dev; p50/p95, TTFT from request receipt, time-to-signal per field order,
  per-stage timings via in-process app with local fetcher; one `docker-cpu` pass through the bundled app (winners,
  n=10).
- **Select**: filter inversion <= 2% + budgets, max F0.5 (summary: judge faithfulness then coverage, gated on
  deterministic pass >= 0.8), else Pareto knee; `select --write` updates `models.toml` defaults and
  `env/bundled.env` pull list (winners if <= ~10 GB, else best finalist that fits; clef-flash alone never fits).
  Order: freeze -> latency -> select -> holdout once -> report.
- **Report**: `evals/results/benchmarks.json` (canonical), `evals/results/README.md`, README tables between markers.
- **Compute**: ~36 GB of pulls; ~3-4 h machine time on the M4 Pro (resumable, background) + Opus wall time.

## Testing and CI

- **BE unit**: extractors on skeletons (own strategies x 4 parsers: body-marker recall >= 0.9 and zero leakage for
  jsonld/profile/cascade; density recall >= 0.8, leakage <= 10%; third-party smoke), skeleton purity, SSRF (all
  address classes, rebinding via injected resolver, per-hop redirects, caps), detect/consent (respx), prompt goldens,
  confidence policies, stream scanner split at every byte offset (both field orders), schemas + openapi drift,
  every allowlisted model resolves prompt + thresholds.
- **BE integration**: ASGI app + respx (publishers and Ollama, hand-written NDJSON chunk fixtures with delays):
  signal (decision + generative), summary/analyze JSON + SSE event order, single-flight (2 requests, 1 upstream
  hit), result cache, error status table, Ollama down, health, models. Coverage floor 75%.
- **FE**: Vitest + RTL (sse parser chunking, components incl. abstained/errors); MSW 3 integration (sentiment
  renders before summary completes, timings, model list, benchmarks page); prettier/eslint/tsc.
- **E2E** (Playwright, compose stack on CI): analyze happy path, signal-only with `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` (CI-only,
  unevaluated plumbing model, documented), extractor switch, `/benchmarks/`. Models `qwen3.5:0.8b` +
  `tev1:0.8b-q8_0`; model-agnostic assertions.
- **CI** (`ci.yml`, push/PR): `backend` (uv cache, `scripts/check.py --backend --full`, transcript scan-only
  guard), `frontend` (pnpm cache, gen:api check, lint, typecheck, vitest, build), `e2e` (needs both; free disk,
  buildx gha cache, ollama model cache, compose up, wait pull, health, warm-up, playwright, upload logs on failure).
  `live-smoke.yml` weekly + dispatch, informational only.

## Transcript export (`scripts/export_transcript.py`, the very last step)

Collect session `0024648c-2a0d-4dde-9495-8d22e0c9ccaa` main JSONL + `subagents/**` + workflow scripts/journals
(exclude `tool-results/`, other sessions) -> staging in `.temp/transcript/`. Allowlist record types (user,
assistant, system informational, mode, permission-mode, titles) and attachments (plan_mode, ultra_effort_enter,
model, date, skill_mention); drop everything else (api-request*, instructions, session context, credential_org,
hooks, listings). Strip thinking signatures and system reminder blocks. Replace tool_result text and Write/Edit
inputs touching `evals/data/private/**` or dataset text with `[omitted: sha256]`. Redact home path, emails other
than the public commit email and `noreply@anthropic.com`, secret patterns, and a gitignored denylist (work
domain, other org/project/container names). Render with `uvx claude-code-log@1.7.0` (HTML + MD). `meta.json`:
Claude Code 2.1.301, `claude-opus-5-5`, effort xhigh, adaptive thinking, ultracode, plan mode, skills, workflows,
subagents (type/model), deduped token usage, date range, redaction counts. Gate: zero hits for `~`, private
emails, denylist, secret regexes, dropped record markers, and 12-word shingles from gold bodies/FPB; only then move
to `.context/transcript/{raw,rendered,meta.json,README.md}` (README notes the export/push turns themselves are
not included, and carries Kris's note to the reviewers).

## Execution phases (Workflows; every agent `model: 'opus'`; main loop commits after each gate)

| Phase | Work | Gate -> commit to main |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Main loop: record + `docker stop` running containers; `brew install ollama`, `brew services start`, `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS`; background model pulls; `git init`, repo-local identity, `.gitignore`, MIT, `gh repo create cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics --public`, SSH-alias remote; workspace + all deps declared and locked; contracts (`contracts.py`, protocols, `openapi.json`), `models.toml`/`sources.toml` skeletons; `ci.yml` backend + frontend jobs; design docs 00/01 | `check.py --fast`, CI green, M0 push |
| P1 | Probe agent: `probe_sources.py` over 14 sources -> `02-source-probe.md`, final 10 + profile hints | 10 usable sources, M1 |
| P2 | 5 parallel file-disjoint agents: fetch/, extract/ + skeleton capture, inference/ + scanner, frontend (MSW against contract), evals loaders/metrics | `check.py --fast`; M3-style probe on real Ollama (logprobs in stream? schema order honoured? systemone shape?) + baseline dev300 + latency probe; **R7 sanity gate: if budgets look unrealistic, stop and ask Kris** -> M2 |
| P3 | (a) api/services/caches/SSE + integration tests; (b) Opus article sub-workflow: discover -> gold + key facts -> labellers A/B -> adjudicate -> finalize | `check.py --full`; one analyze per source on native Ollama; M3 |
| P4 | (a) Docker, compose, e2e, Playwright (iterate on main); (b) accuracy grid, knobs, scope, field order, error pass, freeze, extraction matrix (background); (c) summary eval + Opus judge on finalists | CI incl. e2e green (`gh run watch`), M4 |
| P5 | Exclusive (no builds/agents): re-stop containers, latency suite, select --write, holdout once, docker-cpu pass, report, design docs 03-05 + 90, README | budgets reported, M5 |
| P6 | Verification checklist, fresh-clone smoke, transcript export + gate | M6 push; final message with `docker start ...` command |

Ad-hoc scripts live in `.temp/<slug>/` and run via `uv run python`; no inline Python; terse WHY-only comments; no
em-dashes; no git stash.

## Verification

1. `uv run python scripts/check.py --full` passes (ruff, format, mypy, BE unit + integration, evals tests, FE lint/
   typecheck/prettier/vitest/build, openapi + type drift).
2. Native path: `brew services list` shows ollama; `docker compose up -d`; `/api/health` reports `native-metal`;
   one `/api/analyze` (JSON + stream) succeeds per source; blocked/paywalled cases return typed errors.
3. Bundled path: `docker compose --profile bundled --env-file env/bundled.env up -d` healthy; one analyze succeeds.
4. UI: split and combined modes, streaming toggle, model/parser/extractor/scope switches, Benchmarks page.
5. Latency report vs R7 budgets printed and committed; holdout run recorded once.
6. GitHub Actions `ci.yml` green on HEAD incl. e2e; `live-smoke.yml` dispatched once and noted.
7. `git ls-files` contains nothing from `evals/data/private/`; skeleton purity test passes; every commit authored by
   Kristiyan Dimitrov with the Co-Authored-By trailer.
8. Fresh clone into `.temp/fresh-clone/` builds and serves one analyze without private data.
9. Transcript gate passes with zero hits; rendered HTML skimmed; README links resolve.

## Risks

- Label-token logprobs may be ambiguous or masked by grammar -> score-sign fallback or ordinal only (probe decides).
- Ollama may ignore schema property order -> field-order dimension dropped, documented.
- 9B decision models may miss the 500 ms lede budget -> Pareto knee, stated.
- 30/60 article sets give wide CIs; Opus-only labels may inflate agreement; thresholds from tweets may not transfer.
- Publisher DOMs, Yahoo consent forms and blocking change; runner IPs get blocked differently than Kris's IP.
- Docker Desktop restart can revive stopped containers -> re-stop before P5.
- Brew Ollama 0.40.4 vs container 0.40.5 version drift -> versions recorded with every benchmark.
````

```
# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

## /signal finalists

Served = the dev300 best rule for the model. P / R are precision / recall; inversions are raw bullish<->bearish calls over directional calls.

| model | config | rule | threshold (dev300) | scope | served | F0.5 [95% CI] | bull P / R | bear P / R | inversions | coverage | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | p50 ms |
```

```
# Signal grid on dev300

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.grid analyze` from the local prediction cache; no dataset text is stored here.

- Data: dev300, 300 Twitter Financial News train tweets, 100 per class; every rate is weighted back to the train prior (bullish 20.2%, bearish 15.1%, neutral 64.7%). Confusion and error counts are raw.
- Selection: F0.5 macro over bullish/bearish; operating point = best F0.5 with bullish<->bearish inversions <= 2% of directional calls; below the threshold the call abstains to neutral.
- Policies: decision models threshold native class probabilities (min_p); generative /signal thresholds first-token label probabilities (label schema) or the |score| of an ordinal -2..2 schema (t in {1, 2}); both probability policies are also swept with the served `directional_tau` rule (min_p 0, see below); /analyze is streamed sentiment-first and always uses |score|.
- Decoding: Ollama options temperature=0, seed=0, presence_penalty=0, frequency_penalty=0, repeat_penalty=1 on every generative call (greedy; overrides the penalties some Modelfiles ship).
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000) at the chosen threshold; the threshold choice itself is not resampled, so these are optimistic.
- Latency: per-call wall ms during the grid run (Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal, warm, client concurrency 1); /analyze is time to the score with the stream stopped there. Indicative only: the latency suite runs separately.
```

```
def container_reload(container: str, wait_s: float = UNLOAD_WAIT_S) -> Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]:
    """The bundled Ollama has no host port, so models are stopped inside its container."""

    async def reload(model: str) -> None:
        if _cmd(["docker", "exec", container, "ollama", "stop", model]) is None:
            raise LatencyError(f"could not stop {model} in container {container}")
        deadline = time.monotonic() + wait_s
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            listed = _cmd(["docker", "exec", container, "ollama", "ps"])
            if listed is not None and model not in listed:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        raise LatencyError(f"{model} is still resident in {container} {wait_s:.0f} s after `ollama stop`")

    return reload
```

```
# Real-Time Financial News Analysis Service

## Overview
VeriTrade Analytics is a fintech firm providing high-speed market intelligence to day traders and quantitative analysts. Our analysts currently waste precious minutes manually reading breaking news articles, press releases, and earnings reports to gauge market sentiment. In a world where milliseconds matter, this manual process introduces critical delays, leading to missed opportunities. To solve this, VeriTrade needs a tool that can ingest a news article and provide an instant, AI-powered summary and sentiment analysis.

Your task is to build a prototype for this internal tool. You will create a web service that accepts a URL to a public financial news article. The service should then fetch the article's content, use a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate a concise summary and a sentiment analysis (e.g., Bullish, Bearish, Neutral), and return this information via an API. The core business constraint is speed; the system must be designed for low latency to be useful for traders making time-sensitive decisions. You will also build a simple frontend interface to interact with this service.

A successful submission will demonstrate thoughtful system design focused on performance, effective use of an LLM for a specific task, and clear communication of your design trade-offs. The frontend UI does not need to be visually polished; a functional interface that clearly presents the workflow and results is sufficient.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository or a single public GitHub gist URL containing your complete solution.
- A backend service written in Python that exposes an API to analyze a given news article URL.
- A basic frontend web application (e.g., React, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JS) that consumes the backend API and displays the results.
- A `README.md` file explaining your design decisions, trade-offs (especially regarding latency optimization), instructions on how to run the application and any tests, and a brief note on which AI tools you used.
- The conversation log from any AI assistants used during development (e.g., VS Code Copilot Chat export, Claude conversation history) committed to the repository.

## Suggested tools / libraries
- Backend Framework: FastAPI, Flask
- LLM Integration: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, Groq, or a local model via Ollama
- Web Scraping: BeautifulSoup, requests
- Frontend Framework: React + Vite, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- API Client: `fetch` API, Axios
- Containerization: Docker (optional)

## On AI assistants & follow-up
- We expect and encourage the use of AI assistants. Your goal is to deliver a great solution, not to memorize APIs.
- Please commit the conversation log from your AI assistant (e.g., Copilot Chat export, Claude history) to your repository and briefly describe its role in your README.
- Be prepared to walk through your code and justify your design decisions, especially regarding performance and architectural trade-offs, in the follow-up interview.
- The focus is on your design judgment, problem decomposition, and verification, not on writing every line of code from scratch.

## How to submit
Reply to this email with **one** public GitHub repository or gist URL containing your solution.

# Opus prompts: the 90-article evaluation set

Public sentiment datasets are sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles. This folder holds the
prompts for the Claude Opus subagents that build a set of 90 real articles: 10 primary sources x 3 classes
(bullish, bearish, neutral) x 3 articles, split 30 dev / 60 test. There is no human check: two independent
labellers and an adjudicator stand in for one (decisions Q5 and R5 in `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`).

The agents never fetch anything themselves. They drive the deterministic CLI
`uv run python -m veritrade_evals articles <command>` (code in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/articles*.py` and
`discovery.py`), read private packet files, and write JSON outputs that the CLI validates.

## Pipeline

| Step | Who (every spawn `model: "opus"`) | Prompt | Commands | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 discover | one agent per source | `10-discover.md` | `discover`, `candidates`, `fetch` | candidates, raw HTML, fetch records |
| 2 gold | agents over batches of gold packets | `20-gold.md` | `prepare --stage gold`, `ingest --stage gold` | gold body, key facts, provisional label |
| 3 label | labeller A and labeller B, separate agents | `30-label.md` | `prepare --stage label`, `ingest --stage label_a` / `label_b` | labels, agreement, `adjudicate_ids.txt` |
| 4 adjudicate | one agent | `40-adjudicate.md` | `prepare --stage adjudicate`, `ingest --stage adjudicate` | keep or replace |
| 5 refill | main loop | - | `status`, then steps 1-4 for the cells that are short | every cell has enough eligible articles |
| 6 finalize | main loop | - | `finalize`, `verify` | committed `evals/data/articles/{articles.jsonl,stats.json}` |
| 7 judge summaries | judge agents over batches of judge packets | `50-judge.md` | `summary_eval judge-prepare`, `judge-check`, `judge-ingest` | blind 1-5 faithfulness and coverage per candidate summary |

Step 7 uses `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval <command>` and runs after `generate` and `score`
have produced the candidate summaries (decision R6). Judges see each article with its candidate summaries
under shuffled labels `S1..Sn`; the label-to-model map stays in a private file only `judge-ingest` reads.

Only the main loop runs `prepare`, `finalize`, `verify`, `ingest --agreement`, `judge-prepare` and
`judge-ingest`. Discovery and gold agents may
run `status`; labellers and the adjudicator do not, so their judgements stay independent.

An article is **eligible** when its gold output is usable, it was published within 60 days before 2026-10-18
(2026-08-19 to 2026-10-18), both labellers produced valid outputs, and either they agree with neither flagging
`ambiguous`, or the adjudicator decided `keep` (its label is then final). `finalize` picks 3/3/3 per source; a
source that cannot fill a class may give up one article there (minimum 2) while other sources take a 4th, so
the set is still 30/30/30. The exact algorithm is printed into `stats.json`.

## Rules for every agent (publisher rights and the public transcript)

This build session's transcript is published, and the repository is public.
```

```
def plan_cells(rules: Sequence[Rule], ceiling: Rule, winners: Mapping[str, str]) -> list[HCell]:
    """Finalists on the test articles and tweets; winners and the ceiling on the cross-domain sets."""
    cells: list[HCell] = []
    for rule in rules:
        scopes: tuple[Scope, ...] = ("lede", "full") if rule.endpoint == "signal" else ("full",)
        cells += [HCell(rule, ARTICLES, s) for s in scopes]
        cells.append(HCell(rule, TWEETS))
        if winners.get(rule.endpoint) == rule.model:
            cells += [HCell(rule, split) for split in CROSS]
    cells += [HCell(ceiling, ARTICLES, "full"), *(HCell(ceiling, split) for split in CROSS)]
    order = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(c.model for c in cells))}
    return sorted(cells, key=lambda c: order[c.model])


def summary_pairs(winners: Mapping[str, str]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    return [(e, winners[e]) for e in ("summary", "analyze") if winners.get(e)]


def per_call_ms(cell: HCell) -> float | None:
    """Measured p50 per call of the same rule: the articles dev run for articles, else the dev300 grid."""
    rule = cell.rule
    if cell.split == ARTICLES:
        rows = (read_json(ARTICLES_JSON) or {}).get("rows", [])
        key = f"{rule.model}/{rule.run.name}/{cell.scope}"
        value = next(((r.get("latency") or {}).get("wall_ms_p50") for r in rows if r["key"] == key), None)
    else:
        report = read_json(GRID_DIR / f"{rule.endpoint}__{model_slug(rule.model)}.json") or {}
        entry: dict[str, Any] = next(
            (c for c in report.get("configs", []) if c.get("name") == rule.run.name), {}
        )
        value = (entry.get("latency") or {}).get("wall_ms_p50")
    return float(value) if isinstance(value, int | float) else None
```

```
"""Cheapest trustworthy strategy first: JSON-LD, then the source profile, then text density."""

from __future__ import annotations

from veritrade.extract import density, jsonld, profiles
from veritrade.extract.dom import Dom

JSONLD_MIN_CHARS = 400
PROFILE_MIN_WORDS = 80


def _words(paragraphs: list[str]) -> int:
    return sum(len(p.split()) for p in paragraphs)


def run(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """(winning method, paragraphs); a JSON-LD hit returns before the DOM is ever built."""
    tried: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    body = jsonld.extract(dom, url, source_key)
    if sum(len(p) for p in body) >= JSONLD_MIN_CHARS:
        return "jsonld", body
    tried.append(("jsonld", body))
    if profiles.profile_for(source_key) is not None:
        body = profiles.extract(dom, url, source_key)
        if _words(body) >= PROFILE_MIN_WORDS:
            return "profile", body
        tried.append(("profile", body))
    tried.append(("density", density.extract(dom, url, source_key)))
    # A short release beats an empty density pass; ties go to the more specific method.
    return max(tried, key=lambda item: _words(item[1]))


def extract(dom: Dom, url: str, source_key: str | None) -> list[str]:
    return run(dom, url, source_key)[1]
```

```markdown
# 90 - Optional backlog

What we would do with more time. This is a PoC and rigor was balanced per aspect (R2 in
[01-decisions.md](01-decisions.md)), so each item below marks a place where we stopped on purpose. Every item gives
the reason and the expected payoff; items are ranked by impact within their group, highest first. Items that an
earlier doc or a results file already names as future work link back to it.

## Accuracy

1. **A DSPy-style prompt optimiser instead of the hand grid** (Q7). The grid tried at most 8 configs per model with
   synthetic shots. An optimiser over instructions, shot selection and the decision rule, scored on dev300 F0.5
   under the 2% inversion cap, searches far wider. The largest lever found by hand was a decision rule
   (`directional_tau`, +0.218 F0.5 for `qwen3.5:0.8b`, [grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)).
2. **Distil the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier.** Label a large unlabelled stream of headlines and ledes
   with `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.874), then fine-tune `qwen3.5:0.8b` or a small classifier head on its
   calls. Payoff: part of the 0.874 vs 0.730 gap at the 178 ms tier, without a 10.58 GB model
   ([selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
3. **Logprob-weighted confidence for streamed `/analyze`.** Streams already carry logprobs (undocumented, see
   [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)), so the ordinal
   `|score| >= 1` rule could become a tunable probability threshold like `/signal`'s. It needs a sign-safe score
   encoding: the qwen3.5 tokenizer fuses the space and minus sign, which hid negative scores in the 0.8b grid.
4. **Serve the number-grounding check.** The summary eval already checks every number against the source; running
   it on each served summary and flagging sentences with unsupported numbers costs well under a millisecond of CPU.
   The `/summary` winner still has minor slips in 50% and material errors in 10% of dev summaries
   ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)), and numbers are the slips a trader acts on.
5. **A rubric for mixed results.** Earnings and guidance tweets hold the most wrong calls for their size (13 in 46,
   against 14 in 128 for the catch-all bucket), which fits a beat alongside a cut outlook. An aspect-level output
   (results vs outlook) or an explicit mixed rule targets the content type the brief names.
6. **Decide price moves before tuning for them.** The rubrics ask for economic impact, so the generative models miss
   33-44 of 57 directional price-move tweets, yet only 0-1 of 5 such article headlines
   ([articles dev notes](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/notes.md)). Whether a reported move is directional is a
   product call; the rubric sentence the error pass left out is ready if the answer is yes.
7. **Revisit dropped candidates when their bugs close**: Gemma 4 (think + format bug) and `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`
   ignoring schema property order and `think:false` under a schema. Low effort, more combined-endpoint candidates.

## Latency and serving

1. **Analyse on publish, not on request.** The 10 sources already have `feeds` / `sections` in
   [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), and the evals' discovery code reads them.
   Polling them and analysing new articles ahead of time turns a request into a cache hit; the cost is inference on
   articles nobody opens.
2. **Progressive `/signal`.** Return the 0.8b verdict at 178 ms, then replace it when a 9B decision model answers
   (clef-flash lede p50 659 ms, [latency.md](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). On the article dev set the
   default catches 10 of 20 directional articles and clef-flash 17 of 20, with 1 inversion each.
3. **A GPU compose profile.** A `gpu` profile with a device reservation would give Linux hosts with a CUDA GPU the
   bundled path at native-like speed. CPU-only Docker measured roughly 5-15x slower than Metal on the build machine
   (indicative, [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)).
4. **Split-mode concurrency on one Ollama.** The latency suite runs at client concurrency 1, yet split mode fires
   `/signal` and `/summary/stream` at once against two resident models on one GPU. Measure that pair, then tune
   `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` and `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` (3 native, 2 bundled). Payoff: the split-mode TTFT a user
   actually sees.
5. **A batching server for throughput.** Beyond a handful of analysts, a server with continuous batching (vLLM, or
   llama.cpp server with parallel slots) serves many concurrent streams per GPU. Cost: a second serving stack and
   model format beside Ollama.
6. **CPU threads for the bundled Ollama.** `OLLAMA_CPUS` in [`compose.yaml`](../../../compose.yaml) sets a CPU
   quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota below the visible cores can slow inference
   rather than cap it. Pin a `cpuset` or set `num_thread` to match. Payoff: predictable CPU latency in CI and on
   shared hosts.
7. **Trim the remaining story tails.** The cascade still leaks 13-15% of tokens on Yahoo, PR Newswire and
   GlobeNewswire, mostly after the story ([03](03-extraction.md)). That costs prompt-eval time and summary focus on
   the `full` scope, not the lede.
8. **Start `/signal` on a partial body.** The lede sits early in the HTML, so parsing a streamed prefix could start
   inference before the download ends. The payoff is bounded by transfer time, so mostly on large pages (CNN
   5.7 MB).

## Data and evaluation

1. **A human-checked article set and a larger test set.** The 90 articles are labelled by Opus only (two labellers
   and an adjudicator). With 10 per class on dev a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most article
   comparisons are ties ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). A few hundred
   human-checked articles would separate finalists that tie today.
2. **Extraction beyond the top 10.** Any public URL is accepted, but the matrix covers only profiled sources; other
   publishers fall through to JSON-LD and `density`, unmeasured. A set of other publishers would show whether
   `trafilatura-precision`, the source-agnostic candidate in [03](03-extraction.md), should back the cascade there.
3. **Entity-level and multi-entity sentiment data.** Labels are for the article's primary entity, and the public
   sets are sentence- or headline-level (FinEntity only in its single-label rows). Entity-level data would measure
   the question an analyst asks ("bullish for whom?") and back entity-targeted requests.
4. **Fresh pages for the three tuned profiles.** GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire and Yahoo were tightened on the pages
   they are scored on, so the honest cascade F1 is 0.929 and 0.959 is in-sample ([03](03-extraction.md)).
5. **Resample the threshold choice.** Grid CIs hold the operating point fixed, so they are optimistic
   ([grid summary](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md)). A nested bootstrap or a separate threshold split would
   give honest CIs on the precision knobs.
6. **A sharper key-fact metric.** Embedding coverage agrees with hand labels on 33 of 45 facts at cosine 0.60. A
   per-fact entailment check would track the Opus judge more closely and could gate summary prompts in CI.
7. **Latency on a dedicated host and under load.** Grid and extraction timings came from a shared workstation, and
   contention invalidated a docker-cpu pass. A dedicated runner plus a 1 / 4 / 16 client sweep would give p95s fit
   for capacity planning.
8. **A label-noise pass.** 20 directional dev300 tweets get no correct call from any model
   ([grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)); review them before reading that recall loss as model error.
9. **A second vantage point for the source probe.** One EU residential IP chose the final 10, and datacenter IPs
   meet stricter bot management ([02](02-source-probe.md)). Probe from where the service would run.

## Product and API

1. **Entity-targeted requests.** Accept a ticker or entity and answer for it, and return per-entity calls for
   multi-entity articles (a supplier's warning is bearish for its customer too). Depends on data item 3.
2. **Licensed feeds for the blocked sources.** AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain
   client at their CDN, and evasion is ruled out (Q19). Licensed APIs or feeds would add four widely read sources.
3. **A per-request precision knob.** Thresholds are frozen per model; an override of `min_p` / `directional_tau`
   within the dev300 operating curve would let a desk trade recall for precision without a redeploy.
4. **Non-HTML content.** PDF exhibits and attachments return `unsupported_content`, yet earnings decks and some
   filings arrive that way.
5. **Non-English news.** Discovery skips non-English items and every prompt is English; EU and Asian sources need
   multilingual prompts and their own labelled set.

## Operations

1. **Auth and inbound rate limiting.** The API has no authentication and no per-client limit; the only limiter is
   outbound, for EDGAR ([`client.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/fetch/client.py)). API keys or SSO plus per-key
   quotas come before it leaves localhost. The SSRF guard is already in place.
2. **Source DOM drift monitoring beyond the weekly live smoke.** [`live-smoke.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml)
   runs weekly and never gates. Profiles depend on selectors, and Guardian, BBC and Yahoo hash class names. A
   daily canary over fresh feed items that alerts when the cascade falls back from `profile` to `density`, body
   word counts drop, or `source_blocked` rises would catch silent degradation. No backup sources remain.
3. **Observability.** Every response already carries per-stage timings. Exported as traces and histograms
   (OpenTelemetry) with alerts on the R7 budgets, they make the latency report a live one.
4. **A shared cache (Redis) with distributed single-flight.** Fetch and result caches are in-process, so each
   replica fetches the same breaking story and a restart empties them. A shared store with a short lock keeps one
   fetch per URL across replicas.
5. **Quality monitoring.** Shadow-score a sample of served `/signal` calls with a 9B decision model and judge a
   sample of summaries offline; alert when agreement drops. It catches model, prompt or publisher drift that
   latency metrics miss.
6. **Pin models by digest and gate upgrades.** Eval manifests record model digests. Serving only digests that
   passed `freeze` and the holdout keeps served behaviour equal to measured behaviour across `ollama pull` and
   Ollama upgrades.

```

````markdown
# 00 - Overview

VeriTrade analysts lose minutes reading breaking news to gauge sentiment. This PoC takes a public financial-news
URL and returns a short summary plus a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal, optimised for latency and for
**precision of directional calls** (a wrong call costs a trade; a missed call costs little).

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

Two architectures are compared head to head:

- **Split**: a decision model answers `/signal` fast while a summariser streams `/summary` in parallel.
- **Combined**: one haiku-grade model produces score + summary in a single call (`/analyze`).

## Sources

Any public URL is accepted. The source profiles and the evaluation cover the final 10, chosen by a live probe
([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md), [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml)):
Yahoo Finance, CNBC, The Motley Fool, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune,
The Guardian Business and BBC Business. AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
their CDN and are rejected rather than evaded.

## Outcome

Picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal` serves
`qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
bundled profile pulls 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models call more precisely (`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` F0.5 0.874) but
miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades precision and recall for speed, and the 9B
models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Evidence: [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).
<!-- PENDING:holdout one sentence: whether the one-shot holdout on the test splits confirms the three defaults, with the headline F0.5 per endpoint and a link to evals/results/holdout/ -->

## Reading order

| Doc | Content |
|---|---|
| [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md) | Every settled design decision and why, build-time findings, selection outcome |
| [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) | Which publishers a plain Python client can fetch, and the final top 10 |
| [`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md) | Parser x extractor matrix results |
| [`04-evals.md`](04-evals.md) | Datasets, prompt grid, precision knobs, Opus-labelled articles, results |
| [`05-latency.md`](05-latency.md) | Latency budgets vs measurements, native vs container |
| [`90-optional-backlog.md`](90-optional-backlog.md) | What we would do with more time |

````

```python
"""Report relative markdown links in the given files whose target path does not exist."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)\s]+)\)")

for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    doc = Path(name).resolve()
    for n, line in enumerate(doc.read_text().splitlines(), start=1):
        for target in LINK.findall(line):
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "#")):
                continue
            path = (doc.parent / target.split("#", 1)[0]).resolve()
            status = "ok" if path.exists() else "MISSING"
            print(f"{status}\t{doc.name}:{n}\t{target}")

```

```markdown
# 90 - Optional backlog

What we would do with more time. This is a PoC and rigor was balanced per aspect (R2 in
[01-decisions.md](01-decisions.md)), so each item below marks a place where we stopped on purpose. Every item gives
the reason and the expected payoff; items are ranked by impact within their group, highest first. Items that an
earlier doc or a results file already names as future work link back to it.

## Accuracy

1. **A DSPy-style prompt optimiser instead of the hand grid** (Q7). The lean grid tried up to 8 configs per model
   with synthetic shots. An optimiser over instructions, shot selection and the decision rule, scored on dev300 F0.5
   under the 2% inversion cap, searches far wider. The largest lever found by hand was a decision rule
   (`directional_tau`, +0.218 F0.5 for `qwen3.5:0.8b`, [grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)).
2. **Distil the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier.** Label a large unlabelled stream of headlines and ledes
   with `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.874), then fine-tune `qwen3.5:0.8b` or a small classifier head on its
   calls. Payoff: part of the 0.874 vs 0.730 gap at the 178 ms tier, without a 10.58 GB model
   ([selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
3. **Logprob-weighted confidence for streamed `/analyze`.** Streams already carry logprobs (undocumented, see
   [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)), so the ordinal
   `|score| >= 1` rule could become a tunable probability threshold like `/signal`'s. It needs a sign-safe score
   encoding: the qwen3.5 tokenizer fuses the space and minus sign, which hid negative scores in the 0.8b grid.
4. **Serve the number-grounding check.** The summary eval already checks every number against the source; running
   it on each served summary and flagging sentences with unsupported numbers needs no model call. The `/summary` winner still has minor slips in 50% and material errors in 10% of dev summaries
   ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)), and numbers are the slips a trader acts on.
5. **A rubric for mixed results.** Earnings and guidance tweets hold the most wrong calls for their size (13 in 46,
   against 14 in 128 for the catch-all bucket), which fits a beat alongside a cut outlook. An aspect-level output
   (results vs outlook) or an explicit mixed rule targets the content type the brief names.
6. **Decide price moves before tuning for them.** The rubrics ask for economic impact, so the generative models miss
   33-44 of 57 directional price-move tweets, while the `/analyze` models miss only 0-1 of the 5 directional
   price-move headlines in the article dev set ([articles dev notes](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/notes.md)). Whether a reported move is directional is a
   product call; the rubric sentence the error pass left out is ready if the answer is yes.
7. **Revisit dropped candidates when their bugs close**: Gemma 4 (think + format bug) and `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`
   ignoring schema property order and `think:false` under a schema. Low effort, more combined-endpoint candidates.

## Latency and serving

1. **Analyse on publish, not on request.** The 10 sources already have `feeds` / `sections` in
   [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), and the evals' discovery code reads them.
   Polling them and analysing new articles ahead of time turns a request into a cache hit; the cost is inference on
   articles nobody opens.
2. **Progressive `/signal`.** Return the 0.8b verdict at 178 ms, then replace it when a 9B decision model answers
   (clef-flash lede p50 659 ms, [latency.md](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). On the article dev set the
   default catches 10 of 20 directional articles and clef-flash 17 of 20, with 1 inversion each
   ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)).
3. **A GPU compose profile.** A `gpu` profile with a device reservation would give Linux hosts with a CUDA GPU the
   bundled path at native-like speed. CPU-only Docker measured roughly 5-15x slower than Metal on the build machine
   (indicative, [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)).
4. **Split-mode concurrency on one Ollama.** The latency suite runs at client concurrency 1, yet split mode fires
   `/signal` and `/summary/stream` at once against two resident models on one GPU. Measure that pair, then tune
   `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` and `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` (3 native, 2 bundled). Payoff: the split-mode TTFT a user
   actually sees.
5. **A batching server for throughput.** Beyond a handful of analysts, a server with continuous batching (vLLM, or
   llama.cpp server with parallel slots) serves many concurrent streams per GPU. Cost: a second serving stack and
   model format beside Ollama.
6. **CPU threads for the bundled Ollama.** `OLLAMA_CPUS` in [`compose.yaml`](../../../compose.yaml) sets a CPU
   quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota below the visible cores can slow inference
   rather than cap it. Pin a `cpuset` or set `num_thread` to match. Payoff: predictable CPU latency in CI and on
   shared hosts.
7. **Trim the remaining story tails.** The cascade still leaks 13-15% of tokens on Yahoo, PR Newswire and
   GlobeNewswire, mostly after the story ([03](03-extraction.md)). That costs prompt-eval time and summary focus on
   the `full` scope, not the lede.
8. **Start `/signal` on a partial body.** The lede sits early in the HTML, so parsing a streamed prefix could start
   inference before the download ends. The payoff is bounded by transfer time, so mostly on large pages (CNN
   5.7 MB).

## Data and evaluation

1. **A human-checked article set and a larger test set.** The 90 articles are labelled by Opus only (two labellers
   and an adjudicator). With 10 per class on dev a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most article
   comparisons are ties ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). A few hundred
   human-checked articles would separate finalists that tie today.
2. **Extraction beyond the top 10.** Any public URL is accepted, but the matrix covers only profiled sources; other
   publishers fall through to JSON-LD and `density`, unmeasured. A set of other publishers would show whether
   `trafilatura-precision`, the source-agnostic candidate in [03](03-extraction.md), should back the cascade there.
3. **Entity-level and multi-entity sentiment data.** Labels are for the article's primary entity, and the public
   sets are sentence- or headline-level (FinEntity only in its single-label rows). Entity-level data would measure
   the question an analyst asks ("bullish for whom?") and back entity-targeted requests.
4. **Fresh pages for the three tuned profiles.** GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire and Yahoo were tightened on the pages
   they are scored on, so the honest cascade F1 is 0.929 and 0.959 is in-sample ([03](03-extraction.md)).
5. **Resample the threshold choice.** Grid CIs hold the operating point fixed, so they are optimistic
   ([grid summary](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md)). A nested bootstrap or a separate threshold split would
   give honest CIs on the precision knobs.
6. **A sharper key-fact metric.** Embedding coverage agrees with hand labels on 33 of 45 facts at cosine 0.60. A
   per-fact entailment check would track the Opus judge more closely and could gate summary prompts in CI.
7. **Latency on a dedicated host and under load.** Grid and extraction timings came from a shared workstation, and
   contention invalidated a docker-cpu pass. A dedicated runner plus a 1 / 4 / 16 client sweep would give p95s fit
   for capacity planning.
8. **A label-noise pass.** 20 directional dev300 tweets get no correct call from any model
   ([grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)); review them before reading that recall loss as model error.
9. **A second vantage point for the source probe.** One EU residential IP chose the final 10, and datacenter IPs
   meet stricter bot management ([02](02-source-probe.md)). Probe from where the service would run.

## Product and API

1. **Entity-targeted requests.** Accept a ticker or entity and answer for it, and return per-entity calls for
   multi-entity articles, where one story can be bullish for one company and bearish for another. Depends on data
   item 3.
2. **Licensed feeds for the blocked sources.** AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain
   client at their CDN, and evasion is ruled out (Q19). Licensed APIs or feeds would add four widely read sources.
3. **A per-request precision knob.** Thresholds are frozen per model; an override of `min_p` / `directional_tau`
   within the dev300 operating curve would let a desk trade recall for precision without a redeploy.
4. **Non-HTML content.** PDF exhibits and attachments return `unsupported_content`, yet earnings decks and some
   filings arrive that way.
5. **Non-English news.** Discovery skips non-English items and every prompt is English; EU and Asian sources need
   multilingual prompts and their own labelled set.

## Operations

1. **Auth and inbound rate limiting.** The API has no authentication and no per-client limit; the only limiter is
   outbound, for EDGAR ([`client.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/fetch/client.py)). API keys or SSO plus per-key
   quotas come before it leaves localhost. The SSRF guard is already in place.
2. **Source DOM drift monitoring beyond the weekly live smoke.** [`live-smoke.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml)
   runs weekly and never gates. Profiles depend on selectors, and Guardian, BBC and Yahoo hash class names. A
   daily canary over fresh feed items that alerts when the cascade falls back from `profile` to `density`, body
   word counts drop, or `source_blocked` rises would catch silent degradation. No backup sources remain.
3. **Observability.** Every response already carries per-stage timings. Exported as traces and histograms
   (OpenTelemetry) with alerts on the R7 budgets, they make the latency report a live one.
4. **A shared cache (Redis) with distributed single-flight.** Fetch and result caches are in-process, so each
   replica fetches the same breaking story and a restart empties them. A shared store with a short lock keeps one
   fetch per URL across replicas.
5. **Quality monitoring.** Shadow-score a sample of served `/signal` calls with a 9B decision model and judge a
   sample of summaries offline; alert when agreement drops. It catches model, prompt or publisher drift that
   latency metrics miss.
6. **Pin models by digest and gate upgrades.** Eval manifests record model digests. Serving only digests that
   passed `freeze` and the holdout keeps served behaviour equal to measured behaviour across `ollama pull` and
   Ollama upgrades.

```

```markdown
  0.75 is reported as a conservative bound; the Opus judge remains the selection signal.
- **Docker-cpu pass 1 was biased by Ollama's prompt cache**: the pass ran the bundled app over HTTP (n=10 warm per
  cell), and each JSON cell re-sent prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles, so its prompt eval
  read 118-171 ms. `container_reload` in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/latency.py` now stops the model inside the
  bundled container (`docker exec ... ollama stop`) before every warm phase, mirroring the native suite's unload.
- **Docker-cpu pass 2 was invalidated by host contention**: unrelated workloads on the same Mac pushed the load
  average to 50-64 (6.89 at the native preflight, [`preflight.json`](../../../evals/results/latency/preflight.json)),
  `qwen3.5:0.8b` decode went from about 31 ms to about 2.8 s per token, and 4 `/analyze` requests timed out. The
  bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp with 14 threads on a 14-vCPU Docker VM over a 14-core host, and its spin-barrier
  threads stall whenever the host takes cores. The samples of both passes were discarded and are not committed.
  - Pass 1's valid streaming rows, indicative only (native-metal p50 from
    [`latency.md`](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md) in brackets): `/signal` 0.8b lede p50 2,657 ms (178);
    `/summary` 4B SSE TTFT 8,768 ms (1,128), complete 14,405 ms (2,199); `/analyze` 4B SSE time to signal
    8,644 ms (1,098), TTFT 9,147 ms (1,292), complete 12,106 ms (2,584). CPU-only Docker is roughly 5-15x slower
    than Metal on this machine, which is why native Ollama is the macOS default (Q1) and the bundled profile is for
    Linux and CI.
<!-- PENDING:docker-cpu one line: date and load average of the quiet-host re-run and its per-endpoint docker-cpu p50 / TTFT against native, linking evals/results/latency/latency.md -->
- **`OLLAMA_CPUS` is a quota, not a thread count**: compose's `cpus:` caps CPU time but does not lower llama.cpp's
  thread count, so a quota below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower, not just capped. A `cpuset`
  or `num_thread` is the fix ([90-optional-backlog.md](90-optional-backlog.md)).

## Selection outcome

`uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` applied the Q2 / R6 / R7 rules to the committed results, and
`select --write` set `[defaults]` in [`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) and the pull
list in [`deploy/bundled.env`](../../../deploy/bundled.env). Rules and per-candidate verdicts are in
[`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md); latency is native-metal, warm, excluding fetch
([`latency.md`](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). Every endpoint had an accuracy-eligible candidate inside
its budget, so no Pareto knee was needed.

| Endpoint | Winner, frozen config | Rule that picked it | Accuracy (dev) | Latency p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0`, v2-label, label logprobs with `directional_tau` 0.28, lede | Best dev300 F0.5 among candidates with dev300 inversions <= 2%, an articles-dev inversion CI reaching 2%, and lede p50 <= 500 ms | dev300 F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795]; articles 0.685 | 178 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, prompt v2 | Deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 and both stream budgets, then Opus judge faithfulness | Faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97 for `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, paired gap 0.43 [0.07, 0.77] ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)) | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, v1, ordinal \|s\| >= 1, sentiment-first | As `/signal`, with TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s | dev300 F0.5 0.752 [0.664, 0.834]; articles 0.880 | Signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms |

- **Bundle (R8)**: the winners alone, `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` and `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, are 4.34 GB of model files
  against the 10 GB cap, because one 4B file serves both `/summary` and `/analyze`; no fallback combination was
  needed.
- **The `/signal` trade-off**: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874 [0.811, 0.937]) but misses the
  500 ms lede budget (p50 659 ms), and its 10.58 GB file alone exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap; `nimble:9b-q4_K_M`
  (0.843, 1,061 ms) misses too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms. On the article dev set it
  catches 10 of 20 directional articles against 17 for clef-flash, with one inversion each
  ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). The budget was reported, never moved (R7). Both
  9B decision models stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native
  Ollama.
- **The winner's articles-dev inversion**: that one inversion is 1 of 14 directional calls (7.1%). The rule passes
  it because at n=30 the 95% CI reaches down to 0%; the point estimate alone would fail the 2% cap, so the holdout
  is the real check.
- **Provisional defaults replaced**: the budget-feasible defaults set after the P2 probe (`/summary`
  `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `/analyze` `ministral-3:3b`, see `defaults_untouched` in
  [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json)) gave way to `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` on both. The probe's
  synthetic inputs were about 1.6k tokens, where the 4B model missed TTFT; the served cascade sends about 718 tokens
  of `full` input at p50 ([03](03-extraction.md)), and there it meets both budgets.
- **Split vs combined**: split mode delivers the signal at 178 ms; the combined `/analyze` stream delivers it at
  1,098 ms, about six times later, but scores higher on the article dev set (0.880 [0.791, 0.989] vs
  0.685 [0.473, 0.833], overlapping CIs at n=30) and is close on dev300 (0.752 vs 0.730).

**Holdout check.** The frozen configs run once on the test splits (`articles_test`, `tfns_val`, `fpb_allagree`,
`finentity_single`), with `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` as a holdout-only quality ceiling, and Opus judges the winners'
summaries on the test articles. Nothing is re-tuned on these numbers; results go to `evals/results/holdout/` and
[04-evals.md](04-evals.md#8-holdout).
```

<details>
<summary><code>~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/.context/docs/design/00-overview.md</code></summary>

```markdown
Two architectures are compared head to head:

- **Split**: a fast signal model (a decision model or a tiny LLM) answers `/signal` while a summariser streams
  `/summary` in parallel.
- **Combined**: one haiku-grade model produces score + summary in a single call (`/analyze`).

## Sources

Any public URL is accepted. The source profiles and the evaluation cover the final 10, chosen by a live probe
([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md), [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml)):
Yahoo Finance, CNBC, The Motley Fool, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune,
The Guardian Business and BBC Business. AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
their CDN and are rejected rather than evaded.

## Outcome

Picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal` serves
`qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
bundled profile pulls just those two models, 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models call more precisely (`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` F0.5 0.874) but
miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades precision and recall for speed, and the 9B
models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Evidence: [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).
<!-- PENDING:holdout one sentence: whether the one-shot holdout on the test splits confirms the three defaults, with the headline F0.5 per endpoint and a link to evals/results/holdout/ -->

| Doc | Content |
|---|---|
| [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md) | Every settled design decision and why, build-time findings, selection outcome |
| [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) | Which publishers a plain Python client can fetch, and the final top 10 |
| [`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md) | Parser x extractor matrix results |
| [`04-evals.md`](04-evals.md) | Datasets, prompt grid, precision knobs, Opus-labelled articles, results |
| [`05-latency.md`](05-latency.md) | Latency budgets vs measurements, native vs container |
| [`90-optional-backlog.md`](90-optional-backlog.md) | What we would do with more time |
```

```
# VeriTrade Analytics - real-time financial news analysis (PoC)

Paste a public financial-news URL, get a concise summary and a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal, fast.

> Work in progress. Design decisions: [`.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md).
> The full README (run instructions, latency trade-offs, eval results, AI tooling) lands with the final milestone.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `backend/` | FastAPI service (`veritrade` package): fetch, extract, inference, API |
| `evals/` | Evaluation and benchmarking harness (`veritrade_evals` package) |
| `frontend/` | Next.js 16 static export, served by FastAPI |
| `scripts/` | Setup, quality gate, probes, exports |
| `.context/` | Brief, research, design docs, AI conversation transcript |
```

```markdown
# Real-Time Financial News Analysis Service

## Overview
VeriTrade Analytics is a fintech firm providing high-speed market intelligence to day traders and quantitative analysts. Our analysts currently waste precious minutes manually reading breaking news articles, press releases, and earnings reports to gauge market sentiment. In a world where milliseconds matter, this manual process introduces critical delays, leading to missed opportunities. To solve this, VeriTrade needs a tool that can ingest a news article and provide an instant, AI-powered summary and sentiment analysis.

Your task is to build a prototype for this internal tool. You will create a web service that accepts a URL to a public financial news article. The service should then fetch the article's content, use a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate a concise summary and a sentiment analysis (e.g., Bullish, Bearish, Neutral), and return this information via an API. The core business constraint is speed; the system must be designed for low latency to be useful for traders making time-sensitive decisions. You will also build a simple frontend interface to interact with this service.

A successful submission will demonstrate thoughtful system design focused on performance, effective use of an LLM for a specific task, and clear communication of your design trade-offs. The frontend UI does not need to be visually polished; a functional interface that clearly presents the workflow and results is sufficient.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository or a single public GitHub gist URL containing your complete solution.
- A backend service written in Python that exposes an API to analyze a given news article URL.
- A basic frontend web application (e.g., React, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JS) that consumes the backend API and displays the results.
- A `README.md` file explaining your design decisions, trade-offs (especially regarding latency optimization), instructions on how to run the application and any tests, and a brief note on which AI tools you used.
- The conversation log from any AI assistants used during development (e.g., VS Code Copilot Chat export, Claude conversation history) committed to the repository.

## Suggested tools / libraries
- Backend Framework: FastAPI, Flask
- LLM Integration: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, Groq, or a local model via Ollama
- Web Scraping: BeautifulSoup, requests
- Frontend Framework: React + Vite, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- API Client: `fetch` API, Axios
- Containerization: Docker (optional)

## On AI assistants & follow-up
```

````markdown
# 00 - Overview

VeriTrade analysts lose minutes reading breaking news to gauge sentiment. This PoC takes a public financial-news
URL and returns a short summary plus a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal, optimised for latency and for
**precision of directional calls** (a wrong call costs a trade; a missed call costs little).

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

Two architectures are compared head to head:

- **Split**: a fast signal model (a decision model or a tiny LLM) answers `/signal` while a summariser streams
  `/summary` in parallel.
- **Combined**: one haiku-grade model produces score + summary in a single call (`/analyze`).

## Sources

Any public URL is accepted. The source profiles and the evaluation cover the final 10, chosen by a live probe
([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md), [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml)):
Yahoo Finance, CNBC, The Motley Fool, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune,
The Guardian Business and BBC Business. AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
their CDN and are rejected rather than evaded.

## Outcome

The defaults were picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal`
serves `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
bundled profile pulls just those two models, 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models call more precisely
(`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` F0.5 0.874) but miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades precision
and recall for speed, and the 9B models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Details:
[01 selection outcome](01-decisions.md#selection-outcome), [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).
<!-- PENDING:holdout one sentence: whether the one-shot holdout on the test splits confirms the three defaults, with the headline F0.5 per endpoint and a link to evals/results/holdout/ -->

| [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) | Which publishers a plain Python client can fetch, and the final top 10 |

| [`05-latency.md`](05-latency.md) | Latency budgets vs measurements, native vs container |
| [`90-optional-backlog.md`](90-optional-backlog.md) | What we would do with more time |
````
