### Downstream signal

On the 90 gold ledes, `clef-flash` calls 35 bullish, 28 bearish and 27 neutral (abstentions included). Each
row's verdicts are compared with those. Own strategies are shown on `selectolax`; the other parsers give
the same ledes.

| extractor | agree [95% CI] | agree, extracted pages only | lede identical to gold | bull/bear flips | directional lost | directional added | no verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trafilatura-precision` | 98.9% [96.7%, 100%] | 98.9% | 60.0% | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `cascade` (served) | 97.8% [94.4%, 100%] | 97.8% | 51.1% | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `density` | 96.7% [93.3%, 100%] | 96.7% | 64.4% | 0 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| `trafilatura` | 96.7% [93.3%, 100%] | 96.7% | 57.8% | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `profile` | 95.6% [91.1%, 98.9%] | 98.9% | 60.0% | 0 | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| `newspaper` | 95.6% [91.1%, 98.9%] | 97.7% | 56.7% | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| `justext` | 93.3% [87.8%, 97.8%] | 94.4% | 21.1% | 0 | 4 | 1 | 1 |
| `readability` | 85.6% [77.8%, 92.2%] | 95.1% | 40.0% | 0 | 3 | 1 | 9 |
| `strip-tags` | 83.3% [74.4%, 91.1%] | 83.3% | 0.0% | 0 | 14 | 1 | 0 |
| `jsonld` | 10.0% [4.4%, 16.7%] | 100% | 1.1% | 0 | 0 | 0 | 81 |

Column notes:

- "Directional lost" means a bullish or bearish gold verdict became neutral.
- "Added" is the reverse.
- "No verdict" is a failed extraction, which counts as a miss.

The cascade's 2 disagreements are both SEC exhibits near the 0.8 threshold:

- In one, the gold lede is bearish at 0.92 and the cascade lede leans bearish at 0.75, below the threshold,
  so it is served as neutral.
- In the other, the gold lede leans bearish at 0.79, just under the threshold (served neutral), while the
  cascade lede reads bullish at 0.88. That is the one case in which the top class itself changes. The
  cascade fell back to `density` on that exhibit, and 21 of the 40 tokens in its lede are header lines that
  the gold leaves out.

The first run's third disagreement was a PR Newswire release on which the model abstained. It is gone: after
the PR Newswire profile change, that release's cascade lede is one the model had already scored, and the
verdict agrees.

## Findings

1. **The parser is a speed and footprint choice, not a quality one.** All four give identical bodies.
   `selectolax` is the fastest (parse p50 0.6 ms against 1.3 for `lxml` and 11.4 for `bs4`) and adds 7.5 MB.
2. **`cascade` and `density` are tied on quality, and `cascade` is faster at the tail.**
   - F1 is 0.959 for `cascade` against 0.953 for `density`. The paired gap, `density` minus `cascade`, is
     -0.006 [-0.013, +0.001], which is inside the noise.
   - `density` leaks less on Yahoo (10.3% against 14.9%) and does worse on Motley Fool and Fortune.
   - The cascade's p95 is 2.4 ms against 11.6, because a JSON-LD hit (CNN, 5.7 MB pages) returns before any
     tree is built.
3. **The cascade's fallback earns its place on SEC.** The SEC profile fails on the 3 exhibits whose filer
   agent emits no `<p>` (profile alone: F1 0.59, 3 failures). The cascade falls through to `density` and
   reaches 0.91 with no failure.
4. **What the served cascade still leaks, it mostly leaks at the end of the story, on the same three
   sources.**
   - Leakage is 14.9% on Yahoo, 13.3% on PR Newswire and 13.1% on GlobeNewswire (first run: 24.1%, 22.3%,
     31.2%), and at most 6.6% elsewhere.
   - Counting a paragraph as leaked when most of its tokens are, 597 of the Yahoo, 469 of the GlobeNewswire
     and 249 of the PR Newswire leaked tokens sit after the last gold paragraph.
   - What is left:
     - Yahoo partner tails with no stable opening phrase (StockStory's closing pair).
     - One PR Newswire release (66% leaked) whose "About" heading falls inside the protected lede.
     - One short GlobeNewswire release that still leaks half its tokens.
   - This costs the `full` scope (`/summary`, `/analyze`) tokens, not the lede.
5. **Every third-party extractor trails the own strategies here, and each has a source it breaks on.**
   - `trafilatura` now extracts all 9 SEC exhibits (the EDGAR envelope is unwrapped, see below). It returns
     the whole exhibit, though: SEC F1 0.62 with 52% leakage. 5,644 of the 8,169 leaked tokens come after
     the last gold paragraph, and 98% sit in prose paragraphs, not tables. Its weak sources are the three
     wires (GlobeNewswire 0.62, PR Newswire 0.55, SEC 0.62).
   - `readability` picks the same 21-word block on every Motley Fool page, before our adapter touches the
     output, and the wrong block on Fortune (F1 0.08).
   - `newspaper4k` is the slowest (p50 72 ms) and not deterministic: on one Yahoo page it returned two
     different bodies across repeated calls in one process.
   - `jusText` keeps boilerplate (27% leakage).
6. **Extraction quality barely moves the lede signal until the extraction is wrong.**
   - Every extractor that finds the story agrees with the gold-lede verdict on 94 to 99% of the pages it
     extracts, even though its lede is byte-identical to the gold lede on only 21 to 64% of the 90 pages.
   - What costs agreement is failing outright (`readability` on Motley Fool, `jsonld` off CNN) or putting
     page chrome in the lede. `strip-tags` loses 14 of 63 directional calls, because navigation text pushes
     the story out of the 200-token lede and the model abstains.
   - With SEC now extracted, `trafilatura-precision` agrees on 98.9% (first run 90.0%, all 9 misses were SEC
     failures). Most of its SEC leakage comes after the story, past the lede, and its one miss is an SEC
     exhibit.
   - No row turns a served bullish verdict into a bearish one or back: bad extraction makes the model
     abstain, it does not make it invert.
7. **Tokens**: competent extractors send 704 to 822 tokens of `full` input (p50), against 2,116 for
   `strip-tags`. Ledes are 119 to 128 tokens for every extractor that finds the story.

## What we serve and why

The default stays **`selectolax` + `cascade`** (already the `registry.extract` default):

- **Quality**: best or tied F1 (0.959 [0.942, 0.973]), zero failures on the 90 pages, and 97.8% [94.4%, 100%]
  agreement with the gold-lede verdict, with no inversion.
- **Speed**: the lowest tail of any row that finds bodies, p50 1.2 ms and p95 2.4 ms. That is noise
  against the 500 ms `/signal` budget.
- **Footprint and provenance**: 7.5 MB, no third-party extractor needed at runtime, and the winning method
  (`jsonld`, `profile` or `density`) is reported in every response's meta.

`density` is not promoted: it trails by a gap inside the noise, its p95 is about five times higher, and the
cascade already falls back to it where profiles fail. The other 21 rows stay selectable from the UI and the
API (Q10) so the comparison can be repeated on any URL. If a source-agnostic default were ever needed,
`trafilatura-precision` is now the candidate. It has no failures and the best signal agreement (98.9%), but it
leaks 17.7% (51 to 59% on the three wire sources), costs 60.8 MB and takes about 14 times the cascade's p50.

## Changes after the first measurement

The first run filed two requests for the extraction code. Both were applied, and then the set was
re-measured: a fresh `measure`, `signal` for the 9 ledes that were new, and `report`. The four parsers still
agree on every own strategy, and the skeleton tests cover the new rules on all four.

1. **EDGAR envelope** (`veritrade.extract.third_party.unwrap_edgar`).
   - Third-party adapters now get the `<TEXT>` body of an EDGAR SGML document; any other page passes
     unchanged.
   - It is unit-tested with the synthetic envelope from the first run's repro
     (`backend/tests/unit/extract/test_third_party.py`).
   - The own strategies already read the envelope and are unaffected. The other third-party rows see the
     inner page too, and their SEC F1 moves by 0.01 at most.
2. **Profile tails** (`[sources.*.profile]` in `backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml`, plus one engine
   option).
   - **`max_link_density`** (new; set on Yahoo to 0.5).
     - A body paragraph whose link text exceeds that share of its visible characters is dropped before
       triage, without ending the body.
     - It removes Yahoo's related-story promos and partner link lists without the hashed `yf-*` classes. On
       this set it dropped 18 leaked paragraphs and no gold paragraph.
     - `Node.link_density` counts characters the way the block walker does, so all parsers agree.
   - **Yahoo**: stop markers for partner sign-offs ("More Top Reads From", "This article by Simply Wall St",
     "For updates and corrections").
     - A drop for the trailing list in the read-more block was tried and rejected. It added 0.013 F1 on
       Yahoo, but it needs either the hashed class or a bare `ul` drop that would also remove story lists.
   - **PR Newswire**:
     - The body selector adds `li`, because bulleted highlights are story text: recall went from 0.903 to
       0.966.
     - `p.prntac` is dropped (centred deks and logo lines).
     - New stop markers: "Forward-looking", "For further information" and "Conference Call".
   - **GlobeNewswire**: drops the attachment block (`#gnw_attachments_section-header`,
     `#gnw_attachments_section-items`) and adds the same three stop markers.
   - **All sources**: `GENERIC_STOPS` gains "Forward-Looking Information".
   - **Fixtures**: the Yahoo, PR Newswire and GlobeNewswire skeleton fixtures gained synthetic structural
     elements, so these rules run on real publisher DOM in the four-parser skeleton tests:
     - a link-only promo and a partner tail (Yahoo)
     - a dek and a bullet list (PR Newswire)
     - an attachment block (GlobeNewswire)

   The fixture vocabulary was regenerated by the capture script's own writer.

| scope (`selectolax/cascade`) | F1 first run | F1 now | leakage first run | leakage now | recall first run / now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all 90 articles | 0.929 [0.900, 0.957] | 0.959 [0.942, 0.973] | 9.0% | 5.3% | 0.975 / 0.981 |
| GlobeNewswire | 0.780 | 0.918 | 31.2% | 13.1% | 1.000 / 1.000 |
| PR Newswire | 0.814 | 0.910 | 22.3% | 13.3% | 0.903 / 0.966 |
| Yahoo Finance | 0.848 | 0.904 | 24.1% | 14.9% | 0.996 / 0.995 |
| the other 7 sources | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

| row | SEC failures | SEC F1 | overall F1 | signal agreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trafilatura` | 9 -> 0 | 0.00 -> 0.62 | 0.797 -> 0.859 | 87.8% -> 96.7% |
| `trafilatura-precision` | 9 -> 0 | 0.00 -> 0.62 | 0.802 -> 0.864 | 90.0% -> 98.9% |

`density` rose too, from 0.932 to 0.953, because it cuts its block run at the same profile stop markers and
triage. `profile` rose from 0.897 to 0.927.

## Caveats

- **Three profiles were tuned on this set.**
  - The GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire and Yahoo changes were made after the first measurement. They were
    chosen from counts taken on these same 90 articles: selector matches, stop-marker candidates and
    per-paragraph link shares, with no text printed. The same pages were then used to check them.
  - So the gains on those three sources are in-sample. For an unseen page, the first-run scores (F1 0.780,
    0.814, 0.848) are the honest estimate, and the new ones (0.918, 0.910, 0.904) are optimistic. The same
    holds for the overall cascade F1: 0.929 is the honest figure and 0.959 the optimistic one.
  - The rules are generic in form: a link-share cap, attachment-block ids and release stop phrases. Still,
    "Conference Call" and "For further information" would cut a release whose story continues after a call
    notice or a contact line. Stop markers never cut the lede.
  - No other source's profile changed. The EDGAR unwrap fixes a bug rather than tuning a score.
- **The gold leans toward the own strategies, and toward the cascade in particular.**
  - Opus picked from the same selectolax block lines that the own strategies walk, so their text matches the
    gold token for token. Third-party extractors join text their own way and lose a little even on the right
    blocks.
  - The gold packets folded the page outside the span the served cascade found. Opus could open the full
    page, but the default view was anchored on the cascade.
  - So the gap between own and third-party extractors is an upper bound. The ranking among third-party
    extractors, and the failures listed above, do not depend on it.
- **One annotator, small n.** Opus made one gold body per page and no human checked them. There are 9 pages
  per source, so per-source numbers rest on 9 pages, and one signal disagreement moves agreement by 1.1 points.
- **Timings come from a shared workstation.**
  - The machine is an Apple M4 Pro with 14 cores and 48 GB.
  - During the second run, the mean 1-minute load average was 6.1 (max 7.3), and Ollama had a model
    resident in all 90 per-article samples. During the first run, the load average was 24.6 (max 43.7).
  - Medians of 5 and per-article interleaving keep rows comparable within one run. Compare rows within a
    run, not across runs.
  - Absolute milliseconds are pessimistic. This is not the latency suite.
- **The signal check is narrow.** It uses one decision model at one operating point, and agreement is with
  that model's own verdict on the gold lede, not with the labels: the test split's labels stay reserved for
  the one-shot holdout. It covers the lede only, so tail leakage (finding 4) is not exercised.
- **The title is held fixed in the signal check.** The served title, from the JSON-LD headline, `og:title` or
  `<title>`, equals the gold headline in 85 to 90% of the extracted articles, depending on the row (87% for
  the cascade and for `trafilatura`).
- **Install sizes are macOS arm64 wheels.** Linux wheels differ, and runtime `__pycache__` is not counted.
- **Versions**: `selectolax` 1.0.1, `lxml` 6.1.3, `beautifulsoup4` 4.15.0, `trafilatura` 2.3.1,
  `readability-lxml` 0.8.4.1, `newspaper4k` 0.9.6, `justext` 3.0.2, and Ollama 0.40.6.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench list              # the 22 rows
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench measure --fresh   # timing + quality, CPU only (~5 min)
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench signal            # lede verdicts via native Ollama, concurrency 1
uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report            # evals/results/extraction/{matrix.json,summary.md}
```

`measure` and `signal` need the private article files (`articles verify` passes). `measure` resumes when run
without `--fresh`. `signal` calls the model only for ledes it has not seen. It reads the operating point from
`evals/results/grid/signal__clef-flash_9b-q8_0.json`, so re-run it after the grid's best config changes.

# 02 - Source probe

Question (Q18, Q19): which of the 14 candidate publishers can a plain Python client fetch, with no evasion,
and what do the extractors need to know about each one? The answer is measured, not assumed:
`scripts/probe_sources.py` fetched every candidate live on 2026-10-18 and its output decided
`backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml`.

## Method

- **Client**: `httpx 0.28.1` `AsyncClient`, HTTP/2, the Chrome 155 desktop header set from
  `veritrade.fetch.headers` (UA, Accept, `Accept-Language: en-US`, client hints, `Sec-Fetch-*`,
  `Upgrade-Insecure-Requests`, `Priority`), `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` because `brotli` is installed.
  `sec.gov` gets the declared `SEC_USER_AGENT` and no Chrome hints. No cookies are pre-seeded, no TLS
  impersonation, headless browser, proxy or captcha solving (Q19).
- **Redirects**: followed by hand (max 5), exactly as the serving fetcher will; a hop to Yahoo's consent hosts is
  answered once with reject-all (`veritrade.fetch.consent`) and the original URL retried.
- **Politeness**: one request at a time per registrable domain with at least 1 s between them; EDGAR at 5 req/s
  (half its 10 req/s fair-access ceiling). Reported fetch times exclude these waits.
- **Discovery**: each source's `feeds` (RSS/Atom, non-English `dc:language` items skipped) or `sections`
  (HTML pages and sitemaps), filtered by `article_pattern`; the 3 newest matches are probed. EDGAR resolves the
  8-K Atom feed to filing indexes and then to the EX-99.1 exhibit, preferring index descriptions that say press
  release, earnings or results. When a source refuses its own hubs, links to it are harvested from the other
  sources' captured pages (AP).
- **Per article** (all in `evals/data/source_probe.json`, metadata only): status, final URL, redirects, bytes,
  network ms, `detect.classify` outcome and time, JSON-LD types / `articleBody` words / `isAccessibleForFree` /
  `hasPart` selectors, framework JSON markers, ranked body-container candidates with paragraph and word counts
  under both parsers, noise blocks inside the best container (selectors only) and press-release boilerplate
  labels (label and position only). Raw HTML goes to `evals/data/private/probe/<source>/<n>.html` (gitignored).
- **Profile check**: every `[sources.<key>.profile]` is applied with selectolax (Lexbor) and lxml `cssselect`;
  it passes when both parsers keep the same paragraphs in the same order (non-whitespace characters within 1%)
  and the body has at least 120 words. `--reanalyze` reruns all analysis on the saved HTML without network,
  which is how the profiles were tuned.

## Results

Vantage: residential ISP in Bulgaria (EU), macOS, Sunday 2026-10-18. Fetch ms is network time per article
(median, max of 3); size is the median HTML size.

| Source | Discovery used | OK | Fetch ms | Size | JSON-LD NewsArticle / articleBody | `isAccessibleForFree` | Blocks, consent | Profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yahoo Finance | `/topic/stock-market-news/` page (RSS now 404) | 3/3 | 477 (575) | 682 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none; no consent redirect | 3/3 |
| CNBC | RSS `id/100003114` | 3/3 | 161 (221) | 838 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| Motley Fool | RSS `foolwatch` | 3/3 | 202 (235) | 372 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| PR Newswire | RSS financial services | 3/3 | 34 (43) | 219 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| GlobeNewswire | RSS public companies | 3/3 | 552 (662) | 74 KB | 3 / 0 | true | none | 3/3 |
| SEC 8-K EX-99.1 | Atom, 25 indexes, 2 releases + 1 statement | 3/3 | 135 (538) | 19 KB | 0 / 0 | absent | none (declared UA) | 3/3 |
| CNN Business | `edition.cnn.com/business` page (no RSS) | 3/3 | 35 (50) | 5.7 MB | 3 / 3 | false, full text served | none; www redirects to edition for EU | 3/3 |
| Fortune | RSS | 3/3 | 367 (495) | 431 KB | 3 / 0 | "False", full text served | none | 3/3 |
| Guardian Business | RSS `uk/business` | 3/3 | 116 (169) | 412 KB | 3 / 0 | true | none | 3/3 |
| BBC Business | RSS | 3/3 | 26 (62) | 394 KB | 3 / 0 | absent | none | 3/3 |
| AP News | hub + news sitemap both 403; 3 links harvested | 0/3 | - | - | - | - | Cloudflare managed challenge (403, `cf-mitigated: challenge`) on every path | - |
| Investing.com | RSS works | 0/3 | - | - | - | - | Cloudflare 403 with a 3-byte body on every HTML page | - |
| Benzinga | Google News sitemap works | 0/3 | - | - | - | - | Cloudflare "Sorry, you have been blocked" 403 on every HTML page | - |
| Business Wire | MRSS feed works | 0/3 | - | - | - | - | Akamai 403 "Page Unavailable" on releases; `/newsroom` serves an Akamai interactive challenge with HTTP 200 | - |

Every response came over HTTP/2 and no article URL redirected. One PR Newswire release took 6.8 s on a cache
miss during an earlier run, close to the 8 s fetch deadline.

## Decision

Final 10 (`status = "primary"`, `rank` in `sources.toml`), plan order with backups swapped in for the
rejected sources:

1. Yahoo Finance
2. CNBC
3. The Motley Fool
4. PR Newswire
5. GlobeNewswire
6. SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1
7. CNN Business
8. Fortune (replaces AP News)
9. The Guardian Business (replaces Investing.com)
10. BBC Business (replaces Benzinga)

The mix is 7 news outlets, 2 press-release wires and 1 regulatory filing source. **No backups remain**: the
fourth backup, Business Wire, is blocked too. If a primary degrades, rerun the probe with `--only` on the
candidates and promote from there.

Rejected (`status = "rejected"`, `reason` in `sources.toml`): AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga, Business Wire,
all refused at the CDN (Cloudflare or Akamai) before any content is served. These outlets are syndicated
widely, so `detect.py` answers a block with a hint that points at the syndicated copy (usually Yahoo Finance).

## Yahoo EU consent

- From this IP, `finance.yahoo.com`, `yahoo.com/news`, `uk.finance.yahoo.com` and `de.yahoo.com` served content
  directly with no consent redirect. The pages carry `"gdpr":true` and a client-side CMP
  (`consent.cmp.oath.com`), so in October 2026 the server-side wall no longer stands in front of articles.
- The server-side flow still exists at `guce.yahoo.com/consent` -> `consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent`, so the
  probe exercises it on every run (`yahoo_consent_check` in the JSON): `consent.reject_all` posted the
  reject-all form in 857 ms and the jar received `A1`, `A1S`, `CFC`, `EuConsent`, `GUC`. Decoding the TCF v2
  string in `EuConsent` gives **0 of 24 purposes consented**, which confirms that reject-all was recorded and
  accept-all was never sent. A second pass with the same jar skips the form (about 120 ms, no POST).
- Serving contract: when a redirect lands on a consent host, the fetcher calls `reject_all` with its SSRF
  guard and retries the original URL once; if that lands on the wall again, `detect.classify` raises
  `consent_required` with a hint.

## Block, consent and paywall detection

`detect.classify(status, headers, html, final_url)` is pure and string-based, so it runs on every fetch.

| Signal | Raised as |
|---|---|
| Final URL on `consent.yahoo.com` / `guce.yahoo.com`, or a Yahoo consent form in the page | `consent_required` |
| HTTP 401, 403, 429 (retryable), 451 | `source_blocked`, naming the CDN edge from `server` / `cf-ray` |
| Cloudflare: `cf-mitigated: challenge`, "Just a moment...", `_cf_chl_opt`, `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/`, "Attention Required! \| Cloudflare" | `source_blocked` |
| DataDome `captcha-delivery.com` or `x-dd-b`; PerimeterX `px-captcha` or "Press & Hold"; Akamai "Access Denied" + "Reference #", `sec-if-cpt-container`, `errors.edgesuite.net`; Imperva `_Incapsula_Resource` | `source_blocked`, including when served with HTTP 200 |
| JSON-LD `isAccessibleForFree` false (bool or string) and both the JSON-LD `articleBody` and the visible `<p>` text under 200 words | `paywalled` |

Design points the probe forced:

- Cloudflare's passive `/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/scripts/jsd/main.js` beacon sits on normal pages, so only
  the interactive `/h/` path counts. `x-datadome` alone is ignored because DataDome sets it on allowed responses.
- Markers are only searched in the first 64 KB: interstitials are a few KB, and it keeps 6 MB CNN pages cheap.
  Over all 42 captured pages `classify` takes at most 1.7 ms (CNN, 5.8 MB) and under 1 ms everywhere else
  (median of 5 runs).
- CNN and Fortune declare `isAccessibleForFree: false` yet serve the whole article (their walls are
  client-side), which is why a not-free flag alone is never treated as a paywall.
- Hints are keyed by host suffix: Reuters, AP, Business Wire and Benzinga blocks point to the syndicated copy on
  Yahoo Finance; WSJ, Barron's, FT and Bloomberg paywalls point to free sources.

## What the extractors get

Profile semantics (documented at the top of `sources.toml`): remove `drop` selectors, take `body` matches in
document order, ignore paragraphs under `min_words`, then cut at the first paragraph after the lede that starts
with a `stop_markers` prefix. All selectors use only tag, class, id, attribute and descendant parts; GlobeNewswire
also uses a selector list for `p, li`. All 30 primary pages pass the two-parser check.

Findings that are not visible in the selectors:

- **JSON-LD `articleBody` exists only on CNN** (3/3). Everywhere else the cascade has to fall through to the
  profile or density strategy. No source ships `__NEXT_DATA__`; Fool and Fortune use the Next.js flight stream
  and Yahoo SvelteKit, neither worth parsing for the body.
- **Text joining differs between parsers**: selectolax `text(separator=" ")` splits words at inline tags (drop
  caps become "R ogue", "Fla. ,"), while lxml `text_content()` glues text across `<br>` ("WangEmail"). Joining
  text nodes without a separator, with spaces only at `<br>` and block boundaries, gives the same text on both.
- **Press releases** end with an "About <issuer>" heading, forward-looking statements and contacts as plain
  paragraphs, so they are cut with stop markers, not selectors. The "About" check only applies after the lede.
- **SEC exhibits** arrive wrapped in the EDGAR SGML envelope, with no `h1`, JSON-LD or containers, and start with
  "Exhibit 99.1" and the issuer name. Some filer agents emit `div`/`span` text without `<p>`, which this profile
  cannot read; the cascade must fall back to density there. EX-99.1 is sometimes a financial statement (11.6k
  words in one sample), which `scope=lede` and the token cap absorb.
- **Yahoo** stories are mostly partner copy (Motley Fool, Insider Monkey, 24/7 Wall St, named in `providerId`)
  and partner promos survive inside the body; the second half of the text sits in a hidden "Story continues"
  block that must be kept.
- **CNBC** has editor-written Key Points (`div.RenderKeyPoints-list li`) outside the body, a ready-made lede.
- **CNN** pages are 5.7 MB, so DOM parsing is the slow step there; the JSON-LD strategy avoids it.

## Caveats

- One vantage point. Bot management depends on IP reputation: GitHub Actions runners use US datacenter IPs that
  Cloudflare and Akamai treat more strictly, and US visitors see different geo behaviour (no Yahoo consent at
  all, `www.cnn.com`, `bbc.com`). CI therefore runs on skeleton fixtures; the weekly live smoke is informational.
- Three articles per source on a Sunday: the wires were dominated by non-US issuers, and only 2 of the 25 newest
  8-K filing indexes had an EX-99.1 described as a press release.
- Blocking decisions drift over time and with request rate; the probe stayed at or under 1 request per second per
  domain. The Business Wire `/newsroom` challenge was seen while exploring and is not in the final JSON, because
  discovery uses its MRSS feed.
- AP's article URLs were harvested from other publishers' pages because its own hubs and sitemaps are blocked.
- A Chrome TLS fingerprint might get past Cloudflare for AP, Benzinga and Investing.com. That is evasion, which
  Q19 rules out.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --vantage "EU (Bulgaria) residential ISP"   # live, about 2 minutes
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --only cnbc,bbc                               # re-probe some sources
uv run python scripts/probe_sources.py --reanalyze                                   # re-score saved HTML offline
```

# Model selection

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` from committed results; numbers only.

## Rules

- **signal**: Candidates: the frozen /signal configs at the default lede scope. Filters: dev300 inversion rate <= 2% at the frozen operating point (n=300); the articles dev set must not fail the cap, meaning the 95% CI of its inversion rate reaches down to 2% (the freeze's clear-failure rule: at n=30 one inversion is about 5% of the calls); warm native p50 excluding fetch <= 500 ms at lede. Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro (primary, n=300), then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **analyze**: Candidates: the frozen /analyze configs (full scope, ordinal |score| >= t, sentiment-first). Filters: the same inversion rules as /signal; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s (warm, native, excluding fetch). Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro, then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **summary**: Candidates: the frozen /summary models. Filter: deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 on the dev articles; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s. Rank: Opus judge faithfulness, then judge coverage, then key-fact coverage (key-fact coverage leads while the judge is pending).
- **winner**: The best-ranked candidate inside every filter. When no accuracy-eligible candidate meets its latency budget, the Pareto knee (metrics.knee) of quality against budget utilisation (the worst measured metric divided by its limit) among the measured candidates, with the reason stated.
- **bundle**: R8: the per-endpoint winners when their model files total <= 10 GB (decimal), else the combination of accuracy-eligible candidates that fits with the fewest rank steps away from the winners (ties: signal, then summary, then analyze keeps its better pick; then the smaller total).

# Default: the app uses native Ollama on the host (Metal on macOS; on Linux start it with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0).
#   docker compose up -d
# Bundled: CPU Ollama in a container, models pulled on first start (Linux, CI, no native install).
#   docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
# Either way the UI and API answer on http://localhost:8000 (VT_PORT changes the host port).
name: veritrade

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/app.Dockerfile
    image: veritrade-app:local
    ports:
      - "${VT_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL:-native-metal}
      # Empty values keep the models.toml allowlist and defaults.
      VT_MODELS: ${VT_MODELS:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE:-}
      # Passed through only when set on the host; otherwise the app's public contact default applies.
      SEC_USER_AGENT:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      ollama-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
        required: false

  ollama:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    # Unlimited by default; OLLAMA_CPUS=4 mimics a GitHub runner and spares a busy host.
    cpus: ${OLLAMA_CPUS:-0}
    volumes:
      # OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR swaps the named volume for a host directory (CI caches it between runs).
      - ${OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR:-ollama-models}:/root/.ollama/models
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: 30m
      OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: "2"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
      OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: q8_0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 30

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      OLLAMA_HOST: http://ollama:11434
      VT_PULL_MODELS: ${VT_PULL_MODELS:-qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0}
    volumes:
      - ./docker/ollama-pull.sh:/ollama-pull.sh:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/ollama-pull.sh"]
    restart: "no"

volumes:
  ollama-models:

ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.13-slim-bookworm
ARG UV_IMAGE=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.10.9

FROM ${UV_IMAGE} AS uv

# Static Next.js export: FastAPI serves it from the same origin, so no Node runs in production.
FROM node:24-slim AS frontend
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /src/frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --store-dir /pnpm/store
COPY frontend/ ./
# The context holds evals/results/benchmarks.json only once evals publish it; until then the sample is used.
RUN --mount=type=bind,source=evals,target=/src/evals pnpm build

# Third-party dependencies only, so backend edits do not invalidate this layer.
FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS deps
COPY --from=uv /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/
COPY evals/pyproject.toml evals/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-workspace --package veritrade-backend

FROM deps AS wheel
COPY backend/src backend/src
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv build --wheel --package veritrade-backend --out-dir /dist

FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS runtime
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/.venv /app/.venv
# A small layer of its own: only the app wheel changes between backend edits.
RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=from=wheel,source=/dist,target=/dist \
    uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python --no-deps --compile-bytecode --no-cache /dist/*.whl
COPY --from=frontend /src/frontend/out /app/static
ENV PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    VT_ENV=prod \
    VT_STATIC_DIR=/app/static
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=5s --start-period=30s --retries=5 CMD ["veritrade-healthcheck"]
CMD ["uvicorn", "veritrade.api.app:create_app", "--factory", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
#!/bin/sh
# One-shot init for the bundled profile: pulls VT_PULL_MODELS (comma-separated) plus the lines of
# VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE into the ollama service's model store, skipping models it already holds.
set -eu

models=$(printf '%s\n' "${VT_PULL_MODELS:-}" | tr ',' '\n')
if [ -n "${VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE:-}" ]; then
  models="${models}
$(sed 's/#.*//' "${VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE}")"
fi

count=0
for model in $(printf '%s\n' "${models}" | tr -d ' \r' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u); do
  # A model already in the store needs no registry round-trip, so cached re-runs work offline.
  if ollama show "${model}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "present ${model}"
  else
    echo "pulling ${model}"
    ollama pull "${model}"
  fi
  count=$((count + 1))
done

if [ "${count}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no models requested: set VT_PULL_MODELS or VT_PULL_MODELS_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "models ready (${count})"
"""Local machine setup: free Docker resources, install native Ollama, pull model sets."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
STOPPED_FILE = ROOT / ".temp" / "setup" / "stopped-containers.txt"
MODEL_SETS = {
    "eval": ROOT / "deploy" / "models-eval.txt",
    "ci": ROOT / "deploy" / "ci-models.txt",
}
OLLAMA_URL = "http://localhost:11434"
# brew services only reads launchd env, so these must go through launchctl.
LAUNCHD_ENV = {"OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS": "3", "OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE": "30m"}


def run(cmd: list[str], check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    print("$", " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=check, text=True, capture_output=True)


def stop_containers() -> None:
    names = run(["docker", "ps", "--format", "{{.Names}}"]).stdout.split()
    if not names:
        print("no running containers")
        return
    STOPPED_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    with STOPPED_FILE.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"# {stamp}\n" + "\n".join(names) + "\n")
    run(["docker", "stop", *names])
    print(f"stopped {len(names)} containers; restart with:\n  docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def restart_hint() -> None:
    if not STOPPED_FILE.exists():
        print("nothing recorded")
        return
    lines = STOPPED_FILE.read_text().splitlines()
    names = sorted({ln.strip() for ln in lines if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")})
    print(f"docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def ollama_version() -> str | None:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_URL}/api/version", timeout=2) as resp:
            return str(json.load(resp)["version"])
    except OSError:
        return None


def native() -> None:
    if shutil.which("ollama") is None:
        run(["brew", "install", "ollama"])
    for key, value in LAUNCHD_ENV.items():
        run(["launchctl", "setenv", key, value])
    run(["brew", "services", "restart", "ollama"])
    for _ in range(60):
        version = ollama_version()
        if version:
            print(f"ollama {version} up at {OLLAMA_URL}")
            return
        time.sleep(1)
    sys.exit("ollama did not come up within 60 s; check /opt/homebrew/var/log/ollama.log")


def pull(model_set: str) -> None:
    models = [
        ln.strip()
        for ln in MODEL_SETS[model_set].read_text().splitlines()
        if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")
    ]
    failed = []
    for model in models:
        result = subprocess.run(["ollama", "pull", model], text=True, capture_output=True)
        status = "ok" if result.returncode == 0 else f"FAILED: {result.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
        print(f"{model}: {status}", flush=True)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            failed.append(model)
    print(run(["ollama", "list"]).stdout)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"failed pulls: {', '.join(failed)}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("stop-containers")
    sub.add_parser("restart-hint")
    sub.add_parser("native")
    pull_p = sub.add_parser("pull")
    pull_p.add_argument("--set", choices=sorted(MODEL_SETS), default="eval")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    match args.cmd:
        case "stop-containers":
            stop_containers()
        case "restart-hint":
            restart_hint()
        case "native":
            native()
        case "pull":
            pull(args.set)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""Single quality gate for local runs and CI: lint, types, tests, build and contract drift."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FRONTEND = ROOT / "frontend"


def backend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    backend_tests = "backend/tests" if full else "backend/tests/unit"
    tests = [backend_tests, "evals/tests", "scripts/tests"]
    steps = [
        ("ruff", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "."], ROOT),
        ("ruff-format", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", "."], ROOT),
        ("mypy", ["uv", "run", "mypy"], ROOT),
        ("openapi-drift", ["uv", "run", "python", "scripts/export_openapi.py", "--check"], ROOT),
        ("pytest", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q", *[t for t in tests if (ROOT / t).exists()]], ROOT),
    ]
    # The floor only means something once the API is wired and integration tests exist.
    if full and (ROOT / "backend" / "tests" / "integration").exists():
        steps[-1][1].extend(["--cov", "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered", "--cov-fail-under=75"])
    return steps


def frontend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    steps = [
        ("fe-lint", ["pnpm", "lint"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-format", ["pnpm", "format:check"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-typecheck", ["pnpm", "typecheck"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-test", ["pnpm", "test"], FRONTEND),
    ]
    if full:
        steps.append(("fe-build", ["pnpm", "build"], FRONTEND))
    return steps


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--fast", action="store_true", help="unit tests only, no build (default)")
    mode.add_argument("--full", action="store_true", help="integration tests, coverage floor, build")
    parser.add_argument("--backend", action="store_true", help="only backend + evals")
    parser.add_argument("--frontend", action="store_true", help="only frontend")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    run_be = not args.frontend or args.backend
    run_fe = not args.backend or args.frontend
    steps = (backend_steps(args.full) if run_be else []) + (frontend_steps(args.full) if run_fe else [])

    failed = []
    for name, cmd, cwd in steps:
        print(f"\n== {name}: {' '.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
        if subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd).returncode != 0:
            failed.append(name)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"\nFAILED: {', '.join(failed)}")
    print("\nall checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - run: uv sync --all-packages --frozen
      - run: uv run python scripts/check.py --backend --full

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: API types match backend/openapi.json
        run: pnpm gen:api && git diff --exit-code -- src/lib/api-schema.d.ts
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm format:check
      - run: pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build

  # Full stack in containers: app image, CPU Ollama with the tiny CI models, fixture site, Playwright.
  e2e:
    needs: [backend, frontend]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      COMPOSE_FILE: compose.yaml:compose.e2e.yaml
      E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8000
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # The stack needs ~10 GB (Ollama image, models, app image, browser); deleting preinstalled SDKs
      # costs ~3 minutes, so it only runs when the runner image is short on space.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          avail_gb=$(df --output=avail -BG / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
          if [ "$avail_gb" -lt 25 ]; then
            sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
          fi
          df -h /

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Build app image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/app.Dockerfile
          tags: veritrade-app:local
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=app
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=app

      - name: Restore Ollama models
        id: models
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ollama-models-${{ hashFiles('deploy/ci-models.txt') }}

      - name: Start the e2e stack
        run: |
          echo "OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR=$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models"
          OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 900 --no-build
          docker compose ps -a
          df -h /
          curl -fsS "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/health"

      # Saved right after the pull, so a failing test run still caches the models.
      - name: Save Ollama models
        if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR"
      - if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ${{ steps.models.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

      # Loads both models; a different article than the tests use keeps their requests uncached.
      - name: Warm up both models
        run: |
          for model in qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0 tev1:0.8b-q8_0; do
            curl -fsS --max-time 600 -o /dev/null -w "$model %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" \
              -H 'content-type: application/json' \
              -d "{\"url\": \"http://www.bbc.com/vt-skeleton/article-1\", \"model\": \"$model\"}" \
              "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/signal"
          done

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - name: Install Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm exec playwright test

      - name: Collect compose logs
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color --timestamps > compose-logs.txt
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-failure
          path: |
            frontend/playwright-report/
            frontend/test-results/
            compose-logs.txt
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Tear down
        if: always()
        run: docker compose down --remove-orphans
name: live-smoke

        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - run: uv sync --all-packages --frozen
      - run: uv run pytest -m live backend/tests/live -rA

```
"""Public API contract: request/response bodies, SSE event payloads and the error envelope."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from veritrade.errors import ErrorCode
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName, ParserName, Scope
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint, FieldOrder, ModelKind, PolicyName, Sentiment


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


# --- requests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _ArticleRequest(_Strict):
    url: AnyHttpUrl
    model: str | None = Field(None, description="Allowlisted Ollama tag; endpoint default when omitted.")
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax"
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade"
    no_cache: bool = Field(False, description="Bypass fetch and result caches (used by latency benchmarks).")


class SignalRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = Field("lede", description="lede = headline + opening paragraphs; full = whole article.")


class SummaryRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    pass


class AnalyzeRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = "full"


# --- shared response parts ------------------------------------------------------------------


class CacheInfo(_Strict):
    fetch: Literal["hit", "miss", "joined", "bypass"]
    result: Literal["hit", "miss", "bypass"]


class InferenceTimings(_Strict):
    wall_ms: float
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    load_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_eval_ms: float | None = None
    eval_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    eval_tokens: int | None = None


class Timings(_Strict):
    total_ms: float
    fetch_ms: float
    consent_ms: float | None = None
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    inference: InferenceTimings | None = None
    cache: CacheInfo


class ArticleMeta(_Strict):
    url: str
    final_url: str
    title: str
    source: str | None = Field(None, description="Key from sources.toml when the domain is a known source.")
    published_at: str | None = None
    endpoint: Endpoint
    model: str
    model_kind: ModelKind
    prompt_version: str
    parser: ParserName
    extractor: ExtractorName
    extraction_method: str = Field(description="Strategy that produced the body (cascade resolves to one).")
    scope: Scope
    input_chars: int
    word_count: int
    field_order: FieldOrder | None = None
    cached: bool
    backend: str = Field(description="Inference backend label, e.g. native-metal or docker-cpu.")


class SignalResult(_Strict):
    sentiment: Sentiment
    abstained: bool = Field(description="True when the call fell below the frozen confidence threshold.")
    policy: PolicyName
    confidence: float | None = None
    score: int | None = Field(None, ge=-2, le=2)
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float] | None = None


# --- responses ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SignalResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    timings: Timings


class SummaryResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class AnalyzeResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class ErrorBody(_Strict):
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str
    hint: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    upstream_status: int | None = None


class ErrorResponse(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


class ModelInfo(_Strict):
    name: str
    kind: ModelKind
    endpoints: list[Endpoint]
    installed: bool
    size_bytes: int | None = None
    evaluated: bool = Field(True, description="False for plumbing-only models (e.g. the CI decision model).")


class ModelsResponse(_Strict):
    models: list[ModelInfo]
    defaults: dict[Endpoint, str]
    parsers: list[ParserName]
    extractors: list[ExtractorName]
    scopes: list[Scope]


class HealthResponse(_Strict):
    status: Literal["ok", "degraded"]
    ollama_reachable: bool
    ollama_version: str | None = None
    backend: str
    version: str


# --- SSE event payloads (event name -> data model) ------------------------------------------
# /summary/stream: meta -> summary_delta* -> done
# /analyze/stream: meta -> sentiment (exactly once, position follows field order) + summary_delta* -> done
# Any failure after the stream opens emits a single `error` event and closes.


class MetaEvent(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    fetch_ms: float
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    cache: CacheInfo


class SentimentEvent(_Strict):
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    elapsed_ms: float = Field(description="Milliseconds since the request was received.")


class SummaryDeltaEvent(_Strict):
    text: str


class SummaryDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: SummaryResponse


class AnalyzeDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: AnalyzeResponse


class ErrorEvent(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


SSE_EVENT_NAMES = ("meta", "sentiment", "summary_delta", "done", "error")

```
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack, asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exception_handlers import request_validation_exception_handler
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from veritrade import __version__
from veritrade.api.contracts import ErrorResponse
from veritrade.api.routes import router
from veritrade.api.sse import error_body
from veritrade.config import Settings, get_settings
from veritrade.errors import InvalidUrl, VtError
from veritrade.fetch import Fetcher, HttpFetcher
from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.models_registry import Registry
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime

URL_HINT = "Send the full article address, starting with http:// or https://."


def error_response(exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
    body = ErrorResponse(error=error_body(exc))
    return JSONResponse(status_code=exc.http_status, content=body.model_dump(mode="json"))


def create_app(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    *,
    fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
    ollama: OllamaClient | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Injected clients stay owned by the caller; the lifespan closes only what it builds."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            page_fetcher = fetcher
            if page_fetcher is None:
                page_fetcher = HttpFetcher(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(page_fetcher.aclose)
            llm = ollama
            if llm is None:
                llm = OllamaClient.from_settings(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(llm.aclose)
            app.state.runtime = Runtime.build(settings, fetcher=page_fetcher, ollama=llm, registry=registry)
            yield

    app = FastAPI(title="VeriTrade Analytics", version=__version__, lifespan=lifespan)
    app.state.settings = settings

    @app.exception_handler(VtError)
    async def _vt_error(_: Request, exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
        return error_response(exc)

    @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
    async def _invalid_request(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> Response:
        # A malformed article URL gets the documented invalid_url code; other shape errors keep FastAPI's 422.
        errors = exc.errors()
        if errors and all(tuple(error["loc"][:2]) == ("body", "url") for error in errors):
            return error_response(InvalidUrl(f"url: {errors[0]['msg']}", hint=URL_HINT))
        return await request_validation_exception_handler(request, exc)

    if settings.cors_origin_list:
        app.add_middleware(
            CORSMiddleware,
            allow_origins=settings.cors_origin_list,
            allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
            allow_headers=["*"],
        )
    app.include_router(router)
    # Mounted last so /api routes win; html=True serves the static export's index.html files.
    if settings.static_dir and settings.static_dir.is_dir():
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=settings.static_dir, html=True), name="static")
    return app
"""HTTP routes: thin adapters from request bodies to services.

Stream routes take their events from a dependency, so every failure before the first byte (bad URL, model,
fetch, extraction) still reaches the client as a JSON error with its own HTTP status.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, AsyncIterator
from contextlib import aclosing
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request
from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse, ServerSentEvent

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeRequest,
    AnalyzeResponse,
    ErrorResponse,
    HealthResponse,
    ModelsResponse,
    SignalRequest,
    SignalResponse,
    SummaryRequest,
    SummaryResponse,
)
from veritrade.api.sse import event_stream
from veritrade.services.analyze import open_analyze_stream, run_analyze
from veritrade.services.pipeline import StreamPayload
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.services.signal import run_signal
from veritrade.services.summary import open_summary_stream, run_summary
from veritrade.services.system import check_health, list_models
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer

_ERROR_STATUSES = (400, 422, 502, 503, 504)
ERROR_RESPONSES: dict[int | str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    status: {"model": ErrorResponse} for status in _ERROR_STATUSES
}
# A `model` entry would inherit the route's text/event-stream media type; stream errors are sent as JSON.
STREAM_ERROR_RESPONSES: dict[int | str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    status: {
        "description": "Error raised before the stream opens",
        "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}}},
    }
    for status in _ERROR_STATUSES
}

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api")


async def request_clock() -> StageTimer:
    return StageTimer()


async def get_runtime(request: Request) -> Runtime:
    runtime: Runtime = request.app.state.runtime
    return runtime


# Declared first in every route so the clock starts before any other dependency or validation runs.
Clock = Annotated[StageTimer, Depends(request_clock)]
RuntimeDep = Annotated[Runtime, Depends(get_runtime)]
Events = AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]


async def summary_events(clock: Clock, runtime: RuntimeDep, body: SummaryRequest) -> Events:
    return await open_summary_stream(runtime, body, clock)


async def analyze_events(clock: Clock, runtime: RuntimeDep, body: AnalyzeRequest) -> Events:
    return await open_analyze_stream(runtime, body, clock)


@router.post("/signal", response_model=SignalResponse, responses=ERROR_RESPONSES)
async def signal(clock: Clock, runtime: RuntimeDep, body: SignalRequest) -> SignalResponse:
    return await run_signal(runtime, body, clock)


@router.post("/summary", response_model=SummaryResponse, responses=ERROR_RESPONSES)
async def summary(clock: Clock, runtime: RuntimeDep, body: SummaryRequest) -> SummaryResponse:
    return await run_summary(runtime, body, clock)


@router.post("/summary/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse, responses=STREAM_ERROR_RESPONSES)
async def summary_stream(
    events: Annotated[Events, Depends(summary_events)],
) -> AsyncIterator[ServerSentEvent]:
    async with aclosing(event_stream(events)) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            yield event


@router.post("/analyze", response_model=AnalyzeResponse, responses=ERROR_RESPONSES)
async def analyze(clock: Clock, runtime: RuntimeDep, body: AnalyzeRequest) -> AnalyzeResponse:
    return await run_analyze(runtime, body, clock)


@router.post("/analyze/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse, responses=STREAM_ERROR_RESPONSES)
async def analyze_stream(
    events: Annotated[Events, Depends(analyze_events)],
) -> AsyncIterator[ServerSentEvent]:
    async with aclosing(event_stream(events)) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            yield event


@router.get("/models", response_model=ModelsResponse)
async def models(runtime: RuntimeDep) -> ModelsResponse:
    return await list_models(runtime)


@router.get("/health", response_model=HealthResponse)
async def health(runtime: RuntimeDep) -> HealthResponse:
    return await check_health(runtime)
from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


def _csv(value: str) -> list[str]:
    return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="VT_", extra="ignore")

    env: Literal["dev", "test", "prod"] = "dev"

    ollama_base_url: str = Field(
        "http://localhost:11434",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "OLLAMA_BASE_URL"),
    )
    ollama_backend_label: str = "native-metal"
    ollama_keep_alive: str = "30m"
    inference_timeout_s: float = 90.0
    # Comma-separated restriction of the models.toml allowlist; empty keeps the full allowlist.
    models: str = ""
    default_model_signal: str | None = None
    default_model_summary: str | None = None
    default_model_analyze: str | None = None

    sec_user_agent: str = Field(
        "VeriTrade Analytics PoC kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_SEC_USER_AGENT", "SEC_USER_AGENT"),
    )
    fetch_connect_timeout_s: float = 3.0
    fetch_deadline_s: float = 8.0
    fetch_max_bytes: int = 10_000_000
    fetch_max_redirects: int = 5
    fetch_cache_ttl_s: float = 600.0
    fetch_error_ttl_s: float = 60.0
    # Pages are up to fetch_max_bytes each, so the fetch cache is bounded by size as well as count.
    fetch_cache_max_bytes: int = 200_000_000
    result_cache_ttl_s: float = 3600.0
    cache_max_entries: int = 512
    models_cache_ttl_s: float = 10.0
    # /health and /models answer even when Ollama hangs, so the container healthcheck stays meaningful.
    ollama_probe_timeout_s: float = 2.0

    cors_origins: str = ""
    static_dir: Path | None = None
    # Lets e2e reach the fixture container; refused outside VT_ENV=test so prod keeps the full SSRF guard.
    ssrf_test_allow_hosts: str = ""

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _guard_test_only_settings(self) -> Settings:
        if self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts and self.env != "test":
            raise ValueError("VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS is only allowed when VT_ENV=test")
        return self

    @property
    def model_restriction(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.models)

    @property
    def cors_origin_list(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.cors_origins)

    @property
    def ssrf_allow_hosts(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        return frozenset(host.lower() for host in _csv(self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts))


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import StrEnum
from typing import ClassVar


class ErrorCode(StrEnum):
    INVALID_URL = "invalid_url"
    BLOCKED_DESTINATION = "blocked_destination"
    MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED = "model_not_allowed"
    PAYWALLED = "paywalled"
    CONSENT_REQUIRED = "consent_required"
    EXTRACTION_EMPTY = "extraction_empty"
    UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT = "unsupported_content"
    TOO_LARGE = "too_large"
    SOURCE_BLOCKED = "source_blocked"
    UPSTREAM_HTTP = "upstream_http"
    SCHEMA_VIOLATION = "schema_violation"
    MODEL_UNAVAILABLE = "model_unavailable"
    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
    UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT = "upstream_timeout"
    INFERENCE_TIMEOUT = "inference_timeout"


ERROR_STATUS: dict[ErrorCode, int] = {
    ErrorCode.INVALID_URL: 400,
    ErrorCode.BLOCKED_DESTINATION: 400,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED: 400,
    ErrorCode.PAYWALLED: 422,
    ErrorCode.CONSENT_REQUIRED: 422,
    ErrorCode.EXTRACTION_EMPTY: 422,
    ErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT: 422,
    ErrorCode.TOO_LARGE: 422,
    ErrorCode.SOURCE_BLOCKED: 502,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_HTTP: 502,
    ErrorCode.SCHEMA_VIOLATION: 502,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT: 504,
    ErrorCode.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT: 504,
}


class VtError(Exception):
    code: ClassVar[ErrorCode]
    retryable_default: ClassVar[bool] = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        hint: str | None = None,
        retryable: bool | None = None,
        upstream_status: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.hint = hint
        self.retryable = self.retryable_default if retryable is None else retryable
        self.upstream_status = upstream_status

    @property
    def http_status(self) -> int:
        return ERROR_STATUS[self.code]


class InvalidUrl(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.INVALID_URL


class BlockedDestination(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.BLOCKED_DESTINATION


class ModelNotAllowed(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED


class Paywalled(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.PAYWALLED


class ConsentRequired(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.CONSENT_REQUIRED


class ExtractionEmpty(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.EXTRACTION_EMPTY


class UnsupportedContent(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT


class TooLarge(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.TOO_LARGE


class SourceBlocked(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.SOURCE_BLOCKED


class UpstreamHttp(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_HTTP
    retryable_default = True


class SchemaViolation(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.SCHEMA_VIOLATION
    retryable_default = True


class ModelUnavailable(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE


class LlmUnreachable(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE
    retryable_default = True


class UpstreamTimeout(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT
    retryable_default = True


class InferenceTimeout(VtError):
    code = ErrorCode.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT
    retryable_default = True
"""Server-sent event framing: service payloads become named events, late failures one `error` event."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Mapping
from contextlib import aclosing

from fastapi.sse import ServerSentEvent
from pydantic import BaseModel

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeDoneEvent,
    ErrorBody,
    ErrorEvent,
    MetaEvent,
    SentimentEvent,
    SummaryDeltaEvent,
    SummaryDoneEvent,
)
from veritrade.errors import VtError
from veritrade.services.pipeline import StreamPayload

EVENT_NAMES: Mapping[type[BaseModel], str] = {
    MetaEvent: "meta",
    SentimentEvent: "sentiment",
    SummaryDeltaEvent: "summary_delta",
    SummaryDoneEvent: "done",
    AnalyzeDoneEvent: "done",
    ErrorEvent: "error",
}


def error_body(exc: VtError) -> ErrorBody:
    return ErrorBody(
        code=exc.code,
        message=exc.message,
        hint=exc.hint,
        retryable=exc.retryable,
        upstream_status=exc.upstream_status,
    )


async def event_stream(events: AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]) -> AsyncGenerator[ServerSentEvent]:
    """Closing the payload generator on any exit is what stops the upstream Ollama stream on disconnect."""
    async with aclosing(events):
        try:
            async for payload in events:
                yield ServerSentEvent(event=EVENT_NAMES[type(payload)], data=payload)
        except VtError as exc:
            yield ServerSentEvent(event="error", data=ErrorEvent(error=error_body(exc)))

````
# Frontend

Next.js 16 (App Router, strict TypeScript, CSS modules) built as a **static export**. In production FastAPI
serves `out/` from the same origin as `/api`, so no Node process runs and the browser talks to the API with no
proxy hop.

## Pages

- `/` (Analyze): URL input, Split vs Combined mode, streaming on/off, model, parser, extractor and scope pickers
  filled from `GET /api/models`. Split mode fires `/api/signal` and `/api/summary/stream` together so the
  signal card renders as soon as it lands; Combined mode calls `/api/analyze` (or `/api/analyze/stream`). The
  latency bar puts the server stage timings of each request on one client time axis (`performance.now()`
  from submit), with time-to-signal and time-to-first-token marks. Resubmitting aborts the in-flight run.
- `/benchmarks/`: renders `src/data/benchmarks.json`, which `scripts/copy-benchmarks.mjs` copies from
  `evals/results/benchmarks.json`, falling back to the committed `benchmarks.sample.json` (shown with a
  "sample data" banner).

## Layout

| Path                                 | Role                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/lib/api.ts`                     | Typed fetch helpers over the generated `api-schema.d.ts`; error envelope to `ApiError`                                |
| `src/lib/sse.ts`                     | POST + `TextDecoderStream` SSE parser yielding typed `meta` / `sentiment` / `summary_delta` / `done` / `error` events |
| `src/lib/run-state.ts`, `src/hooks/` | Run reducer (per-lane status and client timing marks) and the hooks that drive it                                     |
| `src/components/`                    | `AnalyzeForm`, `SignalCard`, `SummaryPanel`, `ArticleMetaLine`, `LatencyBar`, `ErrorBanner`, benchmark tables         |
| `src/mocks/`                         | MSW handlers and synthetic fixtures, shared by tests and any mocked dev run                                           |
| `tests/unit`, `tests/integration`    | Vitest + Testing Library; integration tests run the real components against MSW                                       |
| `e2e/`                               | Playwright specs for the docker compose stack                                                                         |

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # http://localhost:3000; set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=http://localhost:8000 for a local API
pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm typecheck
pnpm test           # unit + MSW integration tests, no backend needed
pnpm build          # static export to out/
pnpm gen:api        # regenerate src/lib/api-schema.d.ts from backend/openapi.json
E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 E2E_ARTICLE_URL=... pnpm e2e   # against a running stack
```

`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` is inlined at build time; leave it unset for the production build so requests stay
same-origin. In development the backend must allow the dev origin through `VT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
import type { NextConfig } from "next";

// Static export: FastAPI serves `out/` from the same origin as /api, so no Node server runs in production.
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  output: "export",
  trailingSlash: true,
  images: { unoptimized: true },
};

export default nextConfig;
import type { components } from "./api-schema";

type Schemas = components["schemas"];

export type SignalRequest = Schemas["SignalRequest"];
export type SummaryRequest = Schemas["SummaryRequest"];
export type AnalyzeRequest = Schemas["AnalyzeRequest"];
export type SignalResponse = Schemas["SignalResponse"];
export type SummaryResponse = Schemas["SummaryResponse"];
export type AnalyzeResponse = Schemas["AnalyzeResponse"];
export type ModelsResponse = Schemas["ModelsResponse"];
export type HealthResponse = Schemas["HealthResponse"];
export type ModelInfo = Schemas["ModelInfo"];
export type ArticleMeta = Schemas["ArticleMeta"];
export type SignalResult = Schemas["SignalResult"];
export type Timings = Schemas["Timings"];
export type InferenceTimings = Schemas["InferenceTimings"];
export type CacheInfo = Schemas["CacheInfo"];
export type ErrorBody = Schemas["ErrorBody"];
export type ErrorCode = Schemas["ErrorCode"];

export type ParserName = SignalRequest["parser"];
export type ExtractorName = SignalRequest["extractor"];
export type Scope = SignalRequest["scope"];
export type Endpoint = ArticleMeta["endpoint"];
export type Sentiment = SignalResult["sentiment"];
export type PolicyName = SignalResult["policy"];

// The generated request types mark defaulted fields as required; callers only need the url.
type Body<T extends { url: string }> = Pick<T, "url"> & Partial<Omit<T, "url">>;
export type SignalBody = Body<SignalRequest>;
export type SummaryBody = Body<SummaryRequest>;
export type AnalyzeBody = Body<AnalyzeRequest>;

export const PARSERS: readonly ParserName[] = ["selectolax", "lxml", "bs4", "bs4-lxml"];
export const EXTRACTORS: readonly ExtractorName[] = [
  "cascade",
  "jsonld",
  "profile",
  "density",
  "trafilatura",
  "trafilatura-precision",
  "readability",
  "newspaper",
  "justext",
  "strip-tags",
];
export const SCOPES: readonly Scope[] = ["lede", "full"];

const SERVER_ERROR_CODES: Record<ErrorCode, true> = {
  invalid_url: true,
  blocked_destination: true,
  model_not_allowed: true,
  paywalled: true,
  consent_required: true,
  extraction_empty: true,
  unsupported_content: true,
  too_large: true,
  source_blocked: true,
  upstream_http: true,
  schema_violation: true,
  model_unavailable: true,
  llm_unreachable: true,
  upstream_timeout: true,
  inference_timeout: true,
};
export const ERROR_CODES = Object.keys(SERVER_ERROR_CODES) as ErrorCode[];

/** Failures detected in the browser rather than reported by the API envelope. */
export type ClientErrorCode = "network_error" | "invalid_request" | "http_error" | "bad_response";
export type ApiErrorCode = ErrorCode | ClientErrorCode;

export function isErrorCode(value: unknown): value is ErrorCode {
  return typeof value === "string" && Object.hasOwn(SERVER_ERROR_CODES, value);
}

export interface ApiErrorInit {
  code: ApiErrorCode;
  message: string;
  hint?: string | null;
  status?: number | null;
  retryable?: boolean;
  upstreamStatus?: number | null;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly code: ApiErrorCode;
  readonly hint: string | null;
  readonly status: number | null;
  readonly retryable: boolean;
  readonly upstreamStatus: number | null;

  constructor(init: ApiErrorInit) {
    super(init.message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.code = init.code;
    this.hint = init.hint ?? null;
    this.status = init.status ?? null;
    this.retryable = init.retryable ?? false;
    this.upstreamStatus = init.upstreamStatus ?? null;
  }

  static fromBody(body: ErrorBody, status: number | null = null): ApiError {
    return new ApiError({
      code: body.code,
      message: body.message,
      hint: body.hint,
      status,
      retryable: body.retryable,
      upstreamStatus: body.upstream_status,
    });
  }
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function asErrorBody(value: unknown): ErrorBody | null {
  if (!isRecord(value) || !isErrorCode(value.code) || typeof value.message !== "string") return null;
  return {
    code: value.code,
    message: value.message,
    hint: typeof value.hint === "string" ? value.hint : null,
    retryable: value.retryable === true,
    upstream_status: typeof value.upstream_status === "number" ? value.upstream_status : null,
  };
}

/** Maps any error payload (our envelope, FastAPI validation detail, or junk) to an ApiError. */
export function errorFromPayload(status: number, payload: unknown): ApiError {
  const envelope = isRecord(payload) ? asErrorBody(payload.error) : null;
  if (envelope) return ApiError.fromBody(envelope, status);

  // FastAPI request validation runs before our handlers and answers {"detail": [...]}.
  if (isRecord(payload) && Array.isArray(payload.detail)) {
    const first: unknown = payload.detail[0];
    const msg = isRecord(first) && typeof first.msg === "string" ? first.msg : "Request validation failed.";
    const loc = isRecord(first) && Array.isArray(first.loc) ? first.loc.slice(1).join(".") : "";
    return new ApiError({
      code: "invalid_request",
      message: loc ? `${loc}: ${msg}` : msg,
      status,
    });
  }

  return new ApiError({
    code: "http_error",
    message: `The API answered with HTTP ${status}.`,
    status,
    retryable: status >= 500,
  });
}

export async function readError(res: Response): Promise<ApiError> {
  let text = "";
  try {
    text = await res.text();
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
  }
  let payload: unknown = null;
  try {
    payload = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
  } catch {
    payload = null;
  }
  return errorFromPayload(res.status, payload);
}

export function isAbortError(err: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof err === "object" && err !== null && (err as { name?: unknown }).name === "AbortError";
}

export function toApiError(err: unknown): ApiError {
  if (err instanceof ApiError) return err;
  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
  return new ApiError({ code: "bad_response", message });
}

/** Empty base means same origin, which is how FastAPI serves the static export in production. */
export function apiUrl(path: string): string {
  const base = (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE ?? "").replace(/\/+$/, "");
  if (base) return `${base}${path}`;
  return typeof window === "undefined" ? path : new URL(path, window.location.origin).toString();
}

/** fetch() that turns network failures and non-2xx answers into ApiError; aborts pass through. */
export async function apiFetch(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> {
  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(apiUrl(path), init);
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
    throw new ApiError({
      code: "network_error",
      message: "Could not reach the API.",
      retryable: true,
    });
  }
  if (!res.ok) throw await readError(res);
  return res;
}

async function readJson<T>(res: Response): Promise<T> {
  try {
    return (await res.json()) as T;
  } catch (err) {
    if (isAbortError(err)) throw err;
    throw new ApiError({
      code: "bad_response",
      message: "The API returned invalid JSON.",
      status: res.status,
    });
  }
}

export function jsonPost(body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal, accept = "application/json"): RequestInit {
  return {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: accept },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
    signal,
  };
}

async function postJson<T>(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
  return readJson<T>(await apiFetch(path, jsonPost(body, signal)));
}

export async function getHealth(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<HealthResponse> {
  return readJson<HealthResponse>(await apiFetch("/api/health", { signal }));
}

export async function getModels(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ModelsResponse> {
  return readJson<ModelsResponse>(await apiFetch("/api/models", { signal }));
}

export function postSignal(body: SignalBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SignalResponse> {
  return postJson<SignalResponse>("/api/signal", body, signal);
}

export function postSummary(body: SummaryBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SummaryResponse> {
  return postJson<SummaryResponse>("/api/summary", body, signal);
}

export function postAnalyze(body: AnalyzeBody, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<AnalyzeResponse> {
  return postJson<AnalyzeResponse>("/api/analyze", body, signal);
}

// Copies the canonical eval results into the app; falls back to the committed sample before evals exist.
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const canonical = resolve(here, "../../evals/results/benchmarks.json");
const sample = resolve(here, "../src/data/benchmarks.sample.json");
const target = resolve(here, "../src/data/benchmarks.json");

function isVersion1(path) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8")).version === 1;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

let source = sample;
if (existsSync(canonical)) {
  if (isVersion1(canonical)) source = canonical;
  else console.warn(`benchmarks: ${canonical} is not a version 1 file; using the sample`);
}

mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
copyFileSync(source, target);
console.log(`benchmarks: ${source} -> ${target}`);
