import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";

// Source key -> hostname the fixture site answers for inside the stack (compose.e2e.yaml).
const FIXTURE_HOSTS: Record<string, string> = {
  yahoo: "finance.yahoo.com",
  cnbc: "www.cnbc.com",
  fool: "www.fool.com",
  prnewswire: "www.prnewswire.com",
  globenewswire: "www.globenewswire.com",
  sec: "www.sec.gov",
  cnn: "www.cnn.com",
  fortune: "fortune.com",
  guardian: "www.theguardian.com",
  bbc: "www.bbc.com",
};
const fixtureUrl = (host: string) => `http://${host}/vt-skeleton/article-1`;

const ARTICLE_URL = process.env.E2E_ARTICLE_URL ?? fixtureUrl(FIXTURE_HOSTS.cnbc);
const DECISION_MODEL = process.env.E2E_DECISION_MODEL ?? "tev1:0.8b-q8_0";
const EXTRACTOR = process.env.E2E_EXTRACTOR ?? "trafilatura";

// Model-agnostic: any valid label passes, the point is the plumbing.
const SENTIMENT = /^(Bullish|Bearish|Neutral)$/;
const LABELS = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

async function open(page: Page, mode: "Split" | "Combined", streaming: boolean) {
  await page.goto("/");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
  // Pickers fill from /api/models; waiting here keeps selectOption from racing the fetch.
  await expect(page.getByLabel("Signal model")).toContainText("(default)");
  await page.getByRole("radio", { name: new RegExp(mode) }).check();
  const toggle = page.getByRole("checkbox", { name: /Streaming/ });
  if (streaming) await toggle.check();
  else await toggle.uncheck();
}

async function analyze(page: Page) {
  await page.getByLabel("Article URL").fill(ARTICLE_URL);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Analyze" }).click();
}

async function expectNoError(page: Page) {
  // Not getByRole("alert"): Next's route announcer also carries that role.
  await expect(page.getByTestId("error-banner")).toHaveCount(0);
}

test.describe("analyze page", () => {
  test("split mode streams a summary next to the signal, with timings", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Split", true);
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-text")).not.toBeEmpty();
    await expectNoError(page);

    const latency = page.getByTestId("latency");
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-signal")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-summary")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-signal-signal")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-summary-token")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByText("server total")).toHaveCount(2);
  });

  test("combined streaming delivers sentiment, summary and timings in one call", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Combined", true);
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-text")).not.toBeEmpty();
    await expectNoError(page);

    const latency = page.getByTestId("latency");
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("lane-analyze")).toBeVisible();
    await expect(latency.getByTestId("mark-analyze-signal")).toBeAttached();
    await expect(latency.getByText("server total")).toHaveCount(1);
  });

  test("decision model and extractor switch flow through the JSON endpoints", async ({ page }) => {
    await open(page, "Split", false);
    await page.getByLabel("Signal model").selectOption(DECISION_MODEL);
    await page.getByLabel("Extractor").selectOption(EXTRACTOR);
    await expect(page.getByLabel("Parser")).toBeDisabled();
    await analyze(page);

    await expect(page.getByTestId("signal-badge")).toHaveText(SENTIMENT);
    const signal = page.getByRole("region", { name: "Signal", exact: true });
    await expect(signal).toContainText(DECISION_MODEL);
    await expect(signal).toContainText("probability");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveText("Complete");
    await expect(page.getByTestId("article-extraction")).toContainText(EXTRACTOR);
    await expectNoError(page);
  });
});

test.describe("signal-only API with the decision model", () => {
  for (const [source, host] of Object.entries(FIXTURE_HOSTS)) {
    test(`${source}: label, source profile and stage timings`, async ({ request }) => {
      // no_cache: earlier tests and the CI warm-up may have cached this exact request.
      const resp = await request.post("/api/signal", {
        data: { url: fixtureUrl(host), model: DECISION_MODEL, no_cache: true },
      });
      expect(resp.status()).toBe(200);
      const body = await resp.json();

      expect(LABELS).toContain(body.signal.sentiment);
      expect(body.signal.policy).toBe("probability");
      expect(Object.keys(body.signal.probabilities).sort()).toEqual([...LABELS].sort());
      expect(body.meta).toMatchObject({
        source,
        model: DECISION_MODEL,
        model_kind: "decision",
        endpoint: "signal",
        cached: false,
      });
      expect(body.timings.inference.wall_ms).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    });
  }
});

"use client";

import { useId, useState, type SubmitEvent } from "react";

import type { ModelsState } from "@/hooks/useModels";
import type { RunParams } from "@/hooks/useAnalysis";
import {
  EXTRACTORS,
  PARSERS,
  SCOPES,
  type Endpoint,
  type ExtractorName,
  type ModelInfo,
  type ParserName,
  type Scope,
} from "@/lib/api";
import type { Mode } from "@/lib/run-state";
import { SOURCES } from "@/lib/sources";

import styles from "./AnalyzeForm.module.css";

// Third-party extractors bring their own HTML parser, so the parser picker does not apply.
const PARSER_AWARE: ReadonlySet<ExtractorName> = new Set(["cascade", "jsonld", "profile", "density"]);

export function isHttpUrl(value: string): boolean {
  try {
    const url = new URL(value);
    return url.protocol === "http:" || url.protocol === "https:";
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function modelLabel(model: ModelInfo, isDefault: boolean): string {
  const notes = [
    isDefault ? "default" : null,
    model.installed ? null : "not installed",
    model.evaluated ? null : "CI plumbing, unevaluated",
  ].filter(Boolean);
  return notes.length ? `${model.name} (${notes.join(", ")})` : model.name;
}

interface ModelSelectProps {
  label: string;
  endpoint: Endpoint;
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  models: ModelsState;
}

function ModelSelect({ label, endpoint, value, onChange, models }: ModelSelectProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const ready = models.status === "ready" ? models.data : null;
  const fallback = ready?.defaults[endpoint];
  const options = ready ? ready.models.filter((m) => m.endpoints.includes(endpoint)) : [];
  return (
    <div className={styles.field}>
      <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>
      <select id={id} value={value} onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)}>
        <option value="">{fallback ? `Server default (${fallback})` : "Server default"}</option>
        {options.map((m) => (
          <option key={m.name} value={m.name} disabled={!m.installed}>
            {modelLabel(m, m.name === fallback)}
          </option>
        ))}
      </select>
    </div>
  );
}

interface AnalyzeFormProps {
  models: ModelsState;
  running: boolean;
  onSubmit: (params: RunParams) => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
}

export function AnalyzeForm({ models, running, onSubmit, onCancel }: AnalyzeFormProps) {
  const [url, setUrl] = useState("");
  const [urlError, setUrlError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<Mode>("split");
  const [streaming, setStreaming] = useState(true);
  const [signalModel, setSignalModel] = useState("");
  const [summaryModel, setSummaryModel] = useState("");
  const [analyzeModel, setAnalyzeModel] = useState("");
  const [parser, setParser] = useState<ParserName>("selectolax");
  const [extractor, setExtractor] = useState<ExtractorName>("cascade");
  const [scope, setScope] = useState<Scope>("lede");

  const ids = { url: useId(), urlHelp: useId(), parser: useId(), extractor: useId(), scope: useId() };
  const ready = models.status === "ready" ? models.data : null;
  const parsers = ready?.parsers.length ? ready.parsers : PARSERS;
  const extractors = ready?.extractors.length ? ready.extractors : EXTRACTORS;
  const scopes = ready?.scopes.length ? ready.scopes : SCOPES;
  const parserApplies = PARSER_AWARE.has(extractor);

  function handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    const trimmed = url.trim();
    if (!isHttpUrl(trimmed)) {
      setUrlError("Enter a full http(s) URL, for example https://www.cnbc.com/2026/...");
      return;
    }
    setUrlError(null);
    onSubmit({
      url: trimmed,
      mode,
      streaming,
      parser,
      extractor,
      scope,
      signalModel,
      summaryModel,
      analyzeModel,
    });
  }

  const examples = SOURCES.filter((s) => s.exampleUrl);

  return (
    <form className={styles.form} onSubmit={handleSubmit} noValidate aria-label="Analyze an article">
      <div className={styles.urlRow}>
        <div className={styles.urlField}>
          <label htmlFor={ids.url}>Article URL</label>
          <input
            id={ids.url}
            name="url"
            type="url"
            inputMode="url"
            autoComplete="off"
            spellCheck={false}
            placeholder="https://..."
            value={url}
            onChange={(e) => setUrl(e.target.value)}
            aria-invalid={urlError ? true : undefined}
            aria-describedby={ids.urlHelp}
            required
          />
        </div>
        <div className={styles.actions}>
          <button type="submit" className={styles.primary}>
            {running ? "Restart" : "Analyze"}
          </button>
          {running ? (
            <button type="button" className={styles.secondary} onClick={onCancel}>
              Cancel
            </button>
          ) : null}
        </div>
      </div>
      <p id={ids.urlHelp} className={urlError ? styles.error : styles.help}>
        {urlError ?? "A public news article, press release or SEC 8-K exhibit."}
      </p>

      <div className={styles.sources}>
        <span className={styles.sourcesLabel}>Tested sources:</span>
        <ul className={styles.chips}>
          {SOURCES.map((s) => (
            <li key={s.key} className={styles.chip}>
              {s.name}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
        {examples.length ? (
          <div className={styles.examples}>
            {examples.map((s) => (
              <button
                key={s.key}
                type="button"
                className={styles.secondary}
                onClick={() => setUrl(s.exampleUrl ?? "")}
              >
                Example: {s.name}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.groups}>
        <fieldset className={styles.group}>
          <legend>Mode</legend>
          <label className={styles.choice}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              name="mode"
              value="split"
              checked={mode === "split"}
              onChange={() => setMode("split")}
            />
            <span>
              Split
              <small>/api/signal and /api/summary fire together; the signal lands first.</small>
            </span>
          </label>
          <label className={styles.choice}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              name="mode"
              value="combined"

export interface SourceInfo {

  exampleUrl?: string;

  { key: "prnewswire", name: "PR Newswire" },

  { key: "sec", name: "SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1" },
  { key: "cnn", name: "CNN Business" },
  { key: "fortune", name: "Fortune" },
  { key: "guardian", name: "The Guardian Business" },
  { key: "bbc", name: "BBC Business" },
];

export function sourceName(key: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!key) return null;
  return SOURCES.find((s) => s.key === key)?.name ?? key;
}

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tomllib
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

import veritrade
from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.fetch.client import HttpFetcher

pytestmark = pytest.mark.live

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PROBE = REPO / "evals" / "data" / "source_probe.json"
SOURCES = Path(veritrade.__file__).parent / "data" / "sources.toml"


def primary_urls() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """First article per primary source that the probe fetched successfully."""
    sources: dict[str, Any] = tomllib.loads(SOURCES.read_text())["sources"]
    probed: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(PROBE.read_text())["sources"]
    picks = []
    for key, source in sorted(sources.items(), key=lambda item: item[1].get("rank", 99)):
        if source["status"] != "primary":
            continue
        ok = [
            a["fetch"]["url"]
            for a in probed.get(key, {}).get("articles", [])
            if a["fetch"]["outcome"] == "ok"
        ]
        if ok:
            picks.append((key, ok[0]))
    return picks

# Summary evaluation

Decision R6: deterministic checks, key-fact coverage by a local embedding model, and Claude Opus as a
blind judge. Summaries come from the serving adapters (`/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`) with the default
`selectolax` + `cascade` extraction and `full` scope, run on the stored HTML of the Opus article set.
Written by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval report`; no article or summary text is committed.
Every check scores the served summary: serving caps it at 3 sentences and 60 words
(`cap_summary` in `veritrade.inference.adapters`), and `score` applies the same cap to cached generations.

- **Halluc.** (`hallucinationRate`): share of summaries with any unsupported detail, minor slips included.

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import urllib.request


def main() -> None:
    port = os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/health", timeout=3) as resp:
            sys.exit(0 if resp.status == 200 else 1)
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":

# VeriTrade Analytics prescreen - implementation plan

## Context

VeriTrade's prescreen (`.context/prescreen-brief-kristiyan-dimitrov.md`) asks for a Python API that takes a public
financial-news URL, fetches and extracts the article, and returns an LLM summary + Bullish/Bearish/Neutral sentiment
with low latency, plus a basic frontend, a README (design, latency trade-offs, run/test, AI tools) and the committed AI
conversation log. Kris handpicked the approach from `.context/openai-research.md` in a `/grill-me` interview (Q1-Q20,
R1-R10, 3 follow-ups); every decision below is settled. Guiding principle: this is a PoC, balance rigor per aspect.
Deliverable: public repo `cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics`, everything pushed, transcript + meta under `.context/`.

Greenfield repo: only `.context/` exists, so there is nothing to reuse; evals import the serving code so what is
measured is what is served.

## Settled decisions (copied verbatim into `.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md`)

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Stack | FastAPI + uv (Python 3.13 workspace: `backend`, `evals`); Next.js 16 static export served BY FastAPI (one origin, zero proxy hops, no nginx/Node at runtime); dev = `pnpm dev` + CORS localhost |
| Ollama | Native brew Ollama 0.40.4 (Metal) is the Mac default; compose profile `bundled` (ollama/ollama:0.40.5 + pull init) for Linux/CI; `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` switch; results labelled `native-metal` / `docker-cpu` |
| Split group | `/api/signal`: decision models `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (`/v1/systemone`, native probabilities) + generative baseline `qwen3.5:0.8b`; `/api/summary`: `qwen3.5:2b`, `qwen3.5:4b` |
| Combined group | `/api/analyze`: `qwen3.5:4b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`, `ministral-3:3b`; `qwen3.5:9b` holdout-only quality ceiling |
| Objective | F0.5 macro over {bullish, bearish}; bullish<->bearish inversion cap 2%; winner = best F0.5 within latency budget, else Pareto knee (stated) |
| Confidence | Compare label-token logprob threshold vs ordinal -2..+2 \|score\| threshold for generative models; decision models threshold `probabilities`; API returns `sentiment` + `abstained` (+ confidence/score) |
| Scope | `/signal` `scope=lede` (default) vs `full`, both evaluated |
| Streaming | Both SSE and JSON variants for `/summary` and `/analyze`; SSE events `meta` -> `sentiment` -> `summary_delta*` -> `done` (sentiment exactly once before `done`; position follows frozen field order) |
| Budgets (native, warm, excl. fetch) | `/signal` lede p50 <= 500 ms; `/summary` + `/analyze` TTFT <= 1.5 s, complete p50 <= 4 s; surfaced to Kris (not moved) if unrealistic after baseline |
| Data | Dev: stratified 300 Twitter FNS train; holdout: full Twitter validation + FPB AllAgree (zip, never committed) + FinEntity single-label; 90 Opus-labelled articles (10 sources x 3 classes x 3; 30 dev / 60 test), double label + adjudicator, no human check |
| Prompts | Lean grid per model (2 rubrics x few-shot {0,4} x field order where relevant, <= 8 configs), one error-analysis pass, freeze, holdout once |
| Summaries | <= 3 sentences / 60 words, lead with market-moving fact; eval = deterministic checks + embedding key-fact coverage + Opus-as-judge on finalists |
| Extraction | Matrix: parsers {selectolax, lxml, bs4+html.parser, bs4+lxml} x own {jsonld, profile, density, cascade} + trafilatura {default, precision}, readability-lxml, newspaper4k, justext, strip-tags; Opus gold bodies (gitignored); switchable from UI |
| Sources | Yahoo Finance, CNBC, AP News, Investing.com, Motley Fool, Benzinga, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business; backups Fortune, Business Wire, Guardian, BBC; `probe_sources.py` decides |
| Fetching | Browser header set, no evasion; typed `source_blocked` / `paywalled` / `consent_required` with hints; Yahoo consent = reject-all + cookie cache, fallback `consent_required`; `SEC_USER_AGENT` env |
| Tests/CI | Unit + integration BE/FE, Playwright e2e on compose, all on GitHub Actions; skeleton fixtures (real DOM, synthetic text) + weekly non-blocking live smoke |
| Repo | Milestone commits straight to `main` (no branches); repo-local `Kristiyan Dimitrov <kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com>`; MIT; `.context/` committed; transcript = session `0024648c-...` only, redacted |
| Ops | Stop all other running Docker containers during setup (names recorded); leave them stopped; final message gives the exact `docker start ...` |

```
The goal is to develop a low-latency financial-news analysis service that accepts a publicly accessible article URL and returns a concise factual summary and a financial sentiment classification.

Three architectures were considered:

1. **Single generative LLM:** One lightweight model produces the summary and financial sentiment as structured JSON.
2. **Hybrid decision model + LLM:** Clef-Flash or Jev performs sentiment classification while a separate generative LLM summarizes the article.
3. **Dedicated financial classifier + LLM:** A specialized model such as FinBERT handles sentiment while a generative model produces summaries.

### Recommended approach

**Start with a single locally hosted Qwen3.5 9B model through Ollama**, using structured JSON output and Pydantic validation.

Benchmark Qwen3.5 4B as a faster alternative and compare the results against a Clef-Flash-based hybrid architecture.

Introduce a dedicated classifier only if evaluation demonstrates a meaningful improvement in accuracy, reliability, latency, or throughput.

**Guiding principle:** Select the simplest architecture that satisfies measured performance requirements rather than assuming a more complex architecture is inherently superior.

---

## 2. Project Requirements

### Functional requirements

- Accept a public financial-news article URL via an API.
- Retrieve and extract the article's main text.
- Generate a concise, factual summary.
- Classify financial sentiment as Bullish, Bearish, or Neutral.
- Return structured JSON suitable for programmatic consumption.
- Provide a minimal web frontend.

# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

const POLICY_NOTES: Record<PolicyName, string> = {
  probability: "threshold on the decision model's class probability",
  "label-logprob": "threshold on the label token probability",
  ordinal: "threshold on |score| of the -2..+2 scale",
};

const ORDER: readonly Sentiment[] = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

/** Direction the model leaned before the threshold turned it into an abstention. */
export function leaning(signal: SignalResult): Sentiment {
  if (signal.probabilities) {
    let best: Sentiment = signal.sentiment;
    for (const s of ORDER) {
      if ((signal.probabilities[s] ?? 0) > (signal.probabilities[best] ?? 0)) best = s;
    }
    return best;
  }
  if (typeof signal.score === "number" && signal.score !== 0) return signal.score > 0 ? "bullish" : "bearish";
  return signal.sentiment;
}

function formatScore(score: number): string {
  return score > 0 ? `+${score}` : String(score);
}

interface SignalCardProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity?: string | null;
  model?: string | null;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the signal arriving. */
  timeToSignalMs?: number | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on a combined stream. */
  serverMs?: number | null;
}

export function SignalCard({ status, signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: SignalCardProps) {
  const busy = !signal && (status === "pending" || status === "streaming");
  return (
    <section className={styles.card} aria-labelledby="signal-heading" aria-busy={busy}>
      <h2 id="signal-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Signal
      </h2>
      {signal ? (
        <SignalBody
          signal={signal}
          entity={entity}
          model={model}
          timeToSignalMs={timeToSignalMs}
          serverMs={serverMs}
        />
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.placeholder}>
          {busy
            ? "Waiting for the signal..."
            : status === "cancelled"
              ? "Cancelled."
              : "No signal: the request failed."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

type SignalBodyProps = Omit<SignalCardProps, "status" | "signal"> & { signal: SignalResult };

function SignalBody({ signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: SignalBodyProps) {
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <span
          className={styles.badge}
          data-sentiment={signal.sentiment}
          data-abstained={signal.abstained || undefined}
          data-testid="signal-badge"
        >
          {capitalize(signal.sentiment)}
        </span>
        {signal.abstained ? <span className={styles.abstainTag}>Abstained</span> : null}
        {entity ? <span className={styles.entity}>{entity}</span> : null}
      </div>
      {signal.abstained ? (
        <p className={styles.abstainNote}>
          Below confidence threshold: the call is not confident enough to trade on, so treat it as no
          directional signal.
          {lean !== signal.sentiment ? ` The model leaned ${capitalize(lean)}.` : null}
        </p>

def _status_error(status: int, text: str, model: str | None) -> VtError:
    name = model or "?"
    if status == 404 or "not found" in text.lower():
        return ModelUnavailable(
            f"Model {name} is not available in Ollama: {text}",
            hint=f"Pull it with `ollama pull {name}` or pick an installed model.",
            upstream_status=status,
        )
    return ModelUnavailable(
        f"Ollama rejected the request for {name} ({status}): {text}", upstream_status=status
    )

def _looks_like_html(body: bytes) -> bool:
    head = body[:SNIFF_BYTES].lstrip().lower()

def _unsupported(host: str, media: str) -> UnsupportedContent:
    return UnsupportedContent(
        f"{host} returned {media}, not an HTML article",
        hint="Only HTML article pages are supported; link the article page rather than a PDF, image or feed.",
    )


def _too_large(host: str, limit: int) -> TooLarge:
    return TooLarge(
        f"{host} sent more than {limit / 1_000_000:g} MB",
        hint="Article pages are far smaller; the URL probably points at a file download.",
    )


def _status_hint(status: int) -> str:
    if status in (404, 410):
        return "The page does not exist; check the URL or whether the article was taken down."

"""Report relative markdown links in the given files whose targets do not exist."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)#\s]+)(?:#[^)]*)?\)")

missing = 0
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    doc = Path(name).resolve()
    for target in LINK.findall(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        if "://" in target:
            continue
        path = (doc.parent / target).resolve()
        status = "ok" if path.exists() else "MISSING"
        missing += status == "MISSING"
        print(f"{status:7s} {target}")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)
"""Hygiene checks for a design doc: dashes, home paths, emails, emojis, broken relative links, PENDING lines."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

doc = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
lines = text.splitlines()
print("lines", len(lines))

for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
    if "—" in line or "–" in line:
        print(f"dash at {i}")
    if "~" in line or "/private/" in line:
        print(f"home path at {i}")
    if re.search(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+", line):
        print(f"email-like at {i}: {line.strip()[:80]}")
    if re.search(r"[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF☀-➿]", line):
        print(f"emoji at {i}")
    if "PENDING" in line:
        ok = re.fullmatch(r"<!-- PENDING:(holdout|docker-cpu) [^\n]+ -->", line)
        print(f"pending at {i}: {'ok' if ok else 'MALFORMED'}")

for target in re.findall(r"\]\(([^)#]+)\)", text):
    if target.startswith("http"):
        continue
    resolved = (doc.parent / target).resolve()
    if not resolved.exists():
        print(f"missing link target: {target}")

# VeriTrade Analytics - real-time financial news analysis (PoC)

Paste a public financial-news URL and get a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal in about 0.2 s and a 2-3 sentence
summary that starts streaming in about 1.1 s (native Metal, warm models, fetch excluded). A FastAPI service fetches
and extracts the article and runs open-weight models locally through Ollama, tuned for **precision of directional
calls**, with every model, prompt and threshold chosen by a committed evaluation.

> **This is a proof of concept, and rigor is balanced per aspect.** The signal metric, the data splits, the latency
> budgets and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean; article labels and summary
> judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check. The limits are listed
> [at the end](#limitations-and-next-steps).

| The brief asks for | Where |
|---|---|
| Design decisions | [Design decisions](#design-decisions), [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md) |
| Latency trade-offs | [Latency trade-offs](#latency-trade-offs), [`05-latency.md`](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md) |
| How to run | [Quickstart](#quickstart), [Using it](#using-it) |
| How to test | [Testing](#testing) |
| AI tools and the conversation log | [AI tools used](#ai-tools-used), [`.context/transcript/`](.context/transcript/) |

The design docs read in order from [`00-overview.md`](.context/docs/design/00-overview.md); each number below links
to the committed result it comes from.

## Results at a glance

Per-endpoint defaults, picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md). Latency is
native Metal on an Apple M4 Pro, warm, client concurrency 1, excluding fetch
([`latency.md`](evals/results/latency/latency.md)). The budgets were set before anything was measured.

| Endpoint | Default model | Quality on dev | Warm p50 latency | Budget (p50) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/signal` (lede) | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | dev300 F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795], 0.0% inversions | 178 ms (p95 195) | <= 500 ms: met |
| `/api/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | Opus judge faithfulness 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] of 5, material errors 10% [0%, 20%] | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | TTFT <= 1,500 ms, complete <= 4,000 ms: met |
| `/api/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | dev300 F0.5 0.752 [0.664, 0.834], 0.0% inversions; faithfulness 4.47 | signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms | as `/summary`: met |

- Two model files serve all three endpoints: 4.34 GB against the 10 GB bundle cap.
- Extraction (`selectolax` + `cascade`): body F1 0.959 [0.942, 0.973] on 90 articles, of which 0.929 is the honest
  out-of-sample figure; p50 1.2 ms ([`03-extraction.md`](.context/docs/design/03-extraction.md)).
- Live fetch, outside the budgets: median of the per-source medians 148 ms, slowest source 552 ms.
- The more precise 9B decision models miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget; see [the `/signal` trade-off](#the-signal-trade-off).

These are dev numbers. The frozen configs then run once on unseen test splits
([`04-evals.md`](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#8-holdout)).

## Quickstart

Requirements: Docker with Compose v2. The macOS default also needs Homebrew; local development needs
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 24 with pnpm (via corepack).

### 1. macOS (default): native Ollama plus the app container

Docker Desktop cannot pass the Apple GPU into a Linux container, so Ollama runs on the host with Metal.

```bash
brew install ollama && brew services start ollama
ollama pull qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0 && ollama pull qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M   # the two defaults, 4.34 GB
docker compose up -d                                              # builds the app image on the first run
open http://localhost:8000
```

- `uv run python scripts/dev_setup.py native` does the install and also sets `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m` and
  `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=3` for the brew service; the full measured service env is in
  [`preflight.json`](evals/results/latency/preflight.json).
- Every other allowlisted model works per request once pulled. `uv run python scripts/dev_setup.py pull --set eval`
  pulls the whole eval roster in [`deploy/models-eval.txt`](deploy/models-eval.txt), about 36 GB.
- On Linux with a native Ollama, start it with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` so the container reaches it through
  `host.docker.internal`.

### 2. Bundled CPU Ollama (Linux, CI, no native install)

```bash
docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
```

An `ollama/ollama` container pulls the two defaults into a named volume on the first start (the list in
[`deploy/bundled.env`](deploy/bundled.env) is written by `veritrade_evals select --write`), and the app waits for the
pull. CPU-only inference was roughly 5-15x slower than Metal on the build machine (indicative, see
[native vs docker-cpu](#native-vs-docker-cpu)), so this is a portability path, not a latency path. Leave
`OLLAMA_CPUS` unset: it is a CPU quota, not a thread count, and a quota below the visible cores can slow llama.cpp
down rather than just cap it.

### 3. Local development without Docker

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
VT_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000 uv run uvicorn veritrade.api.app:create_app --factory --port 8000 --reload
cd frontend && pnpm install && NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=http://localhost:8000 pnpm dev   # second shell, port 3000
```

To serve the built UI from FastAPI instead, run `pnpm build` in `frontend/` and start uvicorn with
`VT_STATIC_DIR=frontend/out`.

### Where it answers, and how to stop

- **UI**: http://localhost:8000 (Analyze) and http://localhost:8000/benchmarks/ (the eval tables from
  `evals/results/benchmarks.json`, written by `veritrade_evals report`; a labelled sample shows when it is absent).
- **API**: `http://localhost:8000/api/...`, interactive docs at `/docs`, contract in
  [`backend/openapi.json`](backend/openapi.json). Health: `curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/health`.
- **Stop**: `docker compose down`; for the bundled stack `docker compose --profile bundled --env-file
  deploy/bundled.env down` (add `-v` to delete the pulled models); `brew services stop ollama` for native Ollama.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `VT_PORT` | `8000` | Host port of the app container |
| `VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | `http://host.docker.internal:11434` in compose, `http://localhost:11434` locally | Where Ollama answers |
| `VT_MODELS` | empty: the whole allowlist in [`models.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) | Comma-separated restriction of the allowlist |
| `VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL`, `_SUMMARY`, `_ANALYZE` | empty: `[defaults]` in `models.toml` | Per-endpoint default model |
| `VT_CORS_ORIGINS` | empty | Origins allowed to call the API (for `pnpm dev`) |
| `SEC_USER_AGENT` | a public contact | Declared user agent for SEC EDGAR's fair-access policy; set your own |

All settings: [`config.py`](backend/src/veritrade/config.py) and [`compose.yaml`](compose.yaml).

## Using it

### The UI

- Paste a URL (any public HTML article; the 10 tested sources are listed under the input) and press **Analyze**.
  Resubmitting or **Cancel** aborts the run in flight.
- **Mode**: *Split* (default) fires `/api/signal` and `/api/summary` together, so the signal card renders first;
  *Combined* makes one `/api/analyze` call that returns sentiment, entity and summary.
- **Streaming** (on by default) uses the SSE endpoints; off uses the JSON ones.
- **Pickers**, filled from `GET /api/models`: a model per endpoint (the default is marked, models not pulled are
  disabled), the extractor (10), the parser (4; disabled for third-party extractors that bring their own) and, in
  split mode, the signal scope (`lede` or `full`).
- **Results**: the signal card (label, an abstention with the direction the model leaned, policy, confidence), the
  summary panel (streamed text, a note when it was cut at the output limit), the article line (source, extraction
  method) and a latency bar that puts each request's server stage timings on one client time axis, with
  time-to-signal and first-token marks.

### The API

| Method and path | Request body | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/signal` | `url`, `model`, `parser`, `extractor`, `scope` (default `lede`), `no_cache` | `meta`, `signal`, `timings` |
| `POST /api/summary` | `url`, `model`, `parser`, `extractor`, `no_cache` (scope is always `full`) | `meta`, `summary`, `truncated`, `timings` |
| `POST /api/summary/stream` | as `/api/summary` | SSE: `meta -> summary_delta* -> done` |
| `POST /api/analyze` | as `/api/signal`, `scope` default `full` | `meta`, `signal`, `entity`, `summary`, `truncated`, `timings` |
| `POST /api/analyze/stream` | as `/api/analyze` | SSE: `meta -> sentiment -> summary_delta* -> done` |
| `GET /api/models` | - | Allowlist (kind, endpoints, installed, size), per-endpoint defaults, parsers, extractors, scopes |
| `GET /api/health` | - | `ok` / `degraded`, Ollama reachability and version, backend label (`native-metal` / `docker-cpu`) |

- Only `url` is required. `model` must be on the allowlist. `parser` defaults to `selectolax` (also `lxml`, `bs4`,
  `bs4-lxml`); `extractor` to `cascade` (also `jsonld`, `profile`, `density`, `trafilatura`,
  `trafilatura-precision`, `readability`, `newspaper`, `justext`, `strip-tags`). `no_cache: true` bypasses both
  caches.
- `signal` holds `sentiment`, `abstained`, `policy` and, by policy, `confidence`, `score` (-2..2) or `probabilities`.
  `timings` splits the request into fetch, consent, parse, extract and inference (wall, TTFT, load, prompt eval,
  eval, token counts) and says whether each cache hit; `meta` names the source, model, prompt version and
  extraction method.

```bash
URL='https://...'   # any public article URL
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/signal -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
curl -sN http://localhost:8000/api/analyze/stream -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
```

**SSE order.** `meta` (article meta, fetch / parse / extract timings) arrives once extraction is done; on
`/analyze/stream` the `sentiment` event follows exactly once, as soon as the score closes (the served field order is
sentiment-first); then `summary_delta` text chunks; then `done` with the full JSON response. A failure before the
stream opens is a JSON error with its HTTP status; after that it is one `error` event, and a closed connection stops
the upstream generation.

**Errors** share one envelope, `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "retryable", "upstream_status"}}`
([`errors.py`](backend/src/veritrade/errors.py), [`contracts.py`](backend/src/veritrade/api/contracts.py)):

| HTTP | Codes | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_url`, `blocked_destination`, `model_not_allowed` | Malformed URL; SSRF guard (private or reserved address, a port other than 80/443); model not on the allowlist |
| 422 | `paywalled`, `consent_required`, `extraction_empty`, `unsupported_content`, `too_large` | Fetched, but no usable article: paywall, consent wall, under 40 words, not HTML (PDF, feed), over 10 MB |
| 502 | `source_blocked`, `upstream_http`, `schema_violation` | Publisher refused (CDN bot wall, 401/403/429/451, with a hint to a syndicated copy); other upstream HTTP error; malformed model output |
| 503 | `model_unavailable`, `llm_unreachable` | Model not pulled (the hint gives the `ollama pull` command); Ollama down |
| 504 | `upstream_timeout`, `inference_timeout` | Fetch deadline (8 s); inference timeout (90 s) |

## Architecture

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

The browser loads the static UI from FastAPI and calls `/api` on the same origin. A request is checked against the
model allowlist, then one pooled HTTP/2 client fetches the page behind an SSRF guard that vets every resolved
address and redirect hop; a string-based classifier turns CDN bot walls, consent walls and paywalls into typed
errors, and a single-flight cache lets split mode's two requests share one download. Extraction runs the parser x
extractor registry (default `selectolax` + `cascade`: JSON-LD `articleBody`, then the per-source profile in
[`sources.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), then a text-density fallback), cuts the `lede` or `full`
input and caps its tokens. Inference sends the model's frozen prompt to Ollama with a JSON schema, greedy decoding
and `think: false` (decision models answer through `/v1/systemone` with class probabilities), and the model's
confidence policy turns the answer into a label or an abstention. Every response carries per-stage timings, and
finished results are cached for an hour. Code: `backend/src/veritrade/{api,fetch,extract,inference,services}`.

## Design decisions

Every decision was settled in an interview before any code was written; the full table with the question each one
answers is in [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md).

- **Open-weight models on a local Ollama** ([Q1](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md#round-1)). Everything runs and
  reproduces from this repo with no API key or paid service, on hardware that was measured. Native Metal is the
  macOS default because Docker Desktop cannot reach the Apple GPU; a `bundled` CPU profile covers Linux and CI.
- **Precision first** (Q2). A wrong directional call costs a trade and a missed one costs little, so bullish and
  bearish calls are the positives: selection runs on F0.5 macro over those two classes with bullish<->bearish
  inversions capped at 2%, and "always neutral" scores 0 ([04 section 1](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#1-objective-and-metrics)).
- **Abstain rather than guess** (Q3). Decision models threshold their native class probabilities; the generative
  `/signal` thresholds label-token probabilities with a `directional_tau` rule; `/analyze` and streams use an
  ordinal -2..+2 score with `|score| >= 1`, which works mid-stream. Every response says whether it `abstained`.
- **Split and combined, both served** (Q8). Split runs a fast signal model next to a summariser; combined asks one
  model for score, entity and summary. The UI switches between them, and both were measured
  ([05](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md#split-against-combined)).
- **The quick signal reads the lede** (Q4). Headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200 tokens: `/signal`
  answers in about 7 tokens, so the prompt length is the latency.
- **Stream, sentiment first** (R3). SSE and JSON variants of `/summary` and `/analyze`; the schema puts the score
  before the summary and an incremental scanner emits it the moment it closes.
- **One origin** ([R1](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md#round-2)). FastAPI serves the static Next.js export: no
  proxy hop on the latency path and no Node at runtime.
- **Extraction measured, not assumed** (Q10, R4). 22 parser x extractor rows on 90 real articles; the served
  `selectolax` + `cascade` is best or tied on quality and fastest at the tail, and every row stays selectable
  ([03](.context/docs/design/03-extraction.md)).
- **Fetch like a browser, never evade** (Q18-Q20). A standard browser header set, Yahoo's EU consent answered with
  reject-all, and typed `source_blocked` / `paywalled` / `consent_required` errors with hints. The four publishers
  that refuse a plain client at their CDN were replaced, not evaded ([02](.context/docs/design/02-source-probe.md)).
- **Budgets before measurements** (R7). `/signal` lede p50 <= 500 ms, `/summary` and `/analyze` TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s
  and complete p50 <= 4 s; a miss is reported, never moved.
- **Select by rules in code, test once** (Q6, Q7, R5-R8). A lean prompt grid on dev300, one error-analysis pass,
  freeze, `select` applies the rules and writes the defaults, and the holdout runs once behind a guard keyed by the
  frozen config's hash ([04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md)).
- **Publisher rights in a public repo** (Q11). Tests use skeleton fixtures (real DOM structure, synthetic text);
  article and dataset text is never committed, only ids, URLs, hashes, labels and numbers.

## Latency trade-offs

Full analysis: [`05-latency.md`](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md). Native suite: 528 samples, 0 errors; cold n=3
and warm n=30 per cell on the 30 dev articles, served from memory so the network stays out.

| Endpoint (default) | Budget, p50 | Measured p50 | Measured p95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` lede, `qwen3.5:0.8b` | <= 500 ms | 178 ms | 195 ms |
| `/summary` SSE, `qwen3.5:4b` | TTFT <= 1,500 ms, complete <= 4,000 ms | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | complete 4,232 ms |
| `/analyze` SSE, `qwen3.5:4b` | TTFT <= 1,500 ms, complete <= 4,000 ms | signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms | complete 4,627 ms |

The budgets bind the p50 and every default meets them. The tails do not: the slowest requests are the longest
articles, at about 2,550-2,800 prompt tokens against 825-1,074 at p50.

- **Split or combined.** Split delivers the signal at 178 ms while the summary streams (first text 1,128 ms); the
  combined `/analyze` stream delivers it at 1,098 ms, about six times later, from one model and one prompt instead
  of two resident models (1.02 + 3.32 GB) and two prefills. Combined scores higher on the article dev set (0.880 vs
  0.685, overlapping CIs at n=30) and is close on dev300 (0.752 vs 0.730). Split's two requests running at once on
  one GPU were not measured, so its summary times are a lower bound. The UI defaults to split.
- **Streaming.** SSE does not change the total (-2.9% to +1.1% against JSON at p50) but shows text at 38-54% of it.
  With sentiment first, the streamed score lands 194-249 ms before the first summary text and 1.1-1.5 s before a
  JSON client would see it.
- **Lede scope.** The 0.8B answers in 178 / 195 ms (p50 / p95) on the lede against 231 / 532 ms on the full
  article; the 9B tails grow 4-5x at full scope. Lede keeps `/signal` predictable as well as fast.
- **Where the time goes.** `/signal` is prefill: 75% of the 0.8B's inference is prompt eval for a 7-token answer.
  The 4B summariser prefills at about 800 tokens/s, so prompt eval is 1,029 of its 1,128 ms TTFT. Parse and
  extract take 1.2-1.6 and 1.6-2.5 ms, under 2% of the fastest `/signal`; the extractor matters through tokens
  instead (704-822 `full` tokens for competent extractors, 2,116 for `strip-tags`).
- **Caches and the network.** Fetch is outside the budgets: median of the per-source medians 148 ms, slowest 552 ms
  (GlobeNewswire), so a lede signal lands roughly 0.33 s after submit on a typical source. One pooled HTTP/2
  client keeps connections alive for 60 s; the single-flight fetch cache (10 min, 512 entries, 200 MB; errors 60 s)
  lets split mode download a page once; the result cache answers repeats for an hour; Yahoo's consent cookie is
  reused (857 ms once, then about 120 ms).
- **Cold start.** A model load adds 0.7-1.3 s for the generative models; every call sends `keep_alive` 30m, so only
  the first request after a start or 30 idle minutes pays it.

### The `/signal` trade-off

| Model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | Articles dev F0.5 | Lede p50 / p95 | File | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.685 | 178 / 195 ms | 1.02 GB | served default |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.848 | 659 / 807 ms | 10.58 GB | misses 500 ms; alone over the 10 GB bundle cap |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.895 | 1,061 / 1,182 ms | 5.63 GB | misses 500 ms |

`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 but misses the 500 ms lede budget, and its file alone exceeds the
10 GB bundle cap; `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` misses too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` is precise when it calls (dev300
precision 0.91 / 0.92) but cautious: on the article dev set it catches 10 of 20 directional articles against 17 for
clef-flash, with one inversion each. The budget was reported, never moved. Both 9B decision models stay on the
allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native Ollama, trading about 0.5-0.9 s for
precision.

### Native vs docker-cpu

The bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp on CPU. Two docker-cpu passes were discarded, and neither is committed: pass 1's
JSON rows were biased by Ollama's prompt cache (prompt eval 118-171 ms, because each JSON cell re-sent prompts its
SSE twin had just evaluated), fixed by a reload hook (`container_reload` in
[`latency.py`](evals/src/veritrade_evals/latency.py)) that stops the model inside the container before every warm
phase; pass 2 was invalidated by unrelated workloads on the same Mac (load average 50-64 against 6.9 at the native
preflight), under which llama.cpp's 14 spin-barrier threads on a 14-vCPU VM stalled and 4 `/analyze` requests timed
out. Pass 1's unaffected streaming rows, indicative only (n=10, not committed):

| Endpoint | Transport | docker-cpu p50 | x native |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` 0.8B lede | JSON | 2,657 ms | 14.9x |
| `/summary` 4B | SSE | TTFT 8,768 ms, complete 14,405 ms | 7.8x / 6.6x |
| `/analyze` 4B | SSE | signal 8,644 ms, TTFT 9,147 ms, complete 12,106 ms | 7.9x / 7.1x / 4.7x |

CPU-only Docker is roughly 5-15x slower than Metal on this machine and would miss every budget, which is why native
Ollama is the macOS default and the bundled profile is for Linux and CI. The quiet-host re-run uses the same
protocol, reload hook included, and its rows go to the `docker-cpu` section of
[`latency.md`](evals/results/latency/latency.md).

## Evaluation

Full method and results: [`04-evals.md`](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md). The harness imports the serving code, so
what is measured is what is served.

- **Metric**: F0.5 macro over bullish and bearish (precision weighted above recall), a 2% inversion cap, and an
  operating point at the best F0.5 under the cap; 95% stratified bootstrap CIs (B = 1,000) on headline metrics.
- **Tweets**: `dev300` (100 per class from Twitter Financial News train, reweighted to the train prior of 20.2 /
  15.1 / 64.7%) for tuning; Twitter FNS validation (2,388), Financial PhraseBank AllAgree (2,259) and FinEntity
  single-label paragraphs (851) held out. Only ids, text hashes and labels are committed
  ([`splits/`](evals/data/splits/)).
- **Articles**: 90 recent articles from the 10 sources, 3 per class per source, split 30 dev / 60 test, labelled by
  two independent Opus labellers plus an adjudicator. In the 157 double-labelled pool articles the labellers agree
  on 96.2% (kappa 0.943); 24 ambiguous articles were replaced ([`stats.json`](evals/data/articles/stats.json)).
- **Prompt grid**: 33 cells on dev300 (rubric x shots x schema), one error-analysis pass, then a freeze into
  [`frozen.json`](evals/results/frozen.json) and `models.toml`. The largest lever was a decision rule, not a prompt:
  `directional_tau` lifts the 0.8B by +0.218 [+0.141, +0.307] F0.5 ([grid notes](evals/results/grid/notes.md)).
- **`/analyze` candidates** on dev300: `qwen3.5:4b` 0.752, `ministral-3:3b` 0.685, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` 0.647
  ([grid summary](evals/results/grid/summary.md)); all three meet the latency budgets.
- **Summaries**: deterministic checks (length, every number grounded in the source, entity named), key-fact
  coverage with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b` at cosine 0.60, and blind Opus judges (faithfulness, coverage,
  hallucinations, lead) on the 30 dev articles ([`summary.md`](evals/results/summary/summary.md)).
- **Extraction**: 22 parser x extractor rows on the 90 articles against Opus gold bodies, including how often each
  row's lede changes a `/signal` verdict ([`summary.md`](evals/results/extraction/summary.md)).

Summary quality of the served pair on the dev articles (n = 30):

| Endpoint, model | Checks pass | Numbers grounded | Key facts (0.60) | Opus faithfulness [95% CI] | Coverage | Hallucination flag | Material errors [95% CI] |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|---|
| `/summary`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 47% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] |
| `/analyze`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 57% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] |

The hallucination flag counts any unsupported detail, minor slips included; a material error is faithfulness <= 3
(a wrong key number, an unsupported claim that matters). The `/summary` runner-up, `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, is faster
(TTFT 484 ms) but scores 3.97 with 30% material errors, so the 4B serves both summary endpoints.

**Holdout.** The frozen configs run once on the test splits (`articles_test`, `tfns_val`, `fpb_allagree`,
`finentity_single`), with `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` as an untuned quality ceiling, and Opus judges the winners' summaries
on the 60 test articles. Nothing is re-tuned on these numbers
([protocol](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#8-holdout)).

## Testing

| Layer | Where | What it guards |
|---|---|---|
| Backend unit | `backend/tests/unit` | Extractors on skeleton fixtures under all four parsers, the SSRF guard (address classes, DNS rebinding, ports), block / consent / paywall detection, prompts, confidence policies, the stream scanner split at every byte offset, the Ollama client, the API contract |
| Backend integration | `backend/tests/integration` | The ASGI app against fake publishers (skeleton pages) and a scripted Ollama: every endpoint in JSON and SSE, event order, single-flight and result caches, the error table, failures mid-stream, client disconnects |
| Evals and scripts | `evals/tests/unit`, `scripts/tests` | Metrics, splits, grid, freeze, selection, the holdout guard, latency aggregation, the report, transcript redaction |
| Frontend | `frontend/tests` | Vitest + Testing Library: SSE parser, components, and MSW integration (signal before the summary completes, JSON fallback, errors, abort on resubmit, benchmarks page) |
| End to end | `frontend/e2e` | Playwright on the compose stack: bundled CPU Ollama with the CI models, an nginx fixture site answering for the 10 publisher hostnames, split and combined streaming, a decision model with a switched extractor, a signal check per source profile, the benchmarks page |
| Live smoke | `backend/tests/live` | One real article per source; informational, never gates |

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
uv run python scripts/check.py --fast    # ruff, format, mypy, OpenAPI drift, backend unit + evals + scripts tests, frontend lint/format/typecheck/test
uv run python scripts/check.py --full    # adds backend integration tests with a 75% coverage floor, and the frontend build
cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test   # frontend alone
uv run pytest -m live backend/tests/live -rA                              # live publishers, opt-in
```

End to end, as CI runs it (the stack pulls `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` and `tev1:0.8b-q8_0`, a CI-only decision model used
to exercise the decision-model path, never evaluated; CPU inference is slow, so test timeouts are 300 s):

```bash
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait
cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm exec playwright install chromium && pnpm exec playwright test
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml down
```

**CI** ([`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml), on push to `main` and pull requests): `backend` runs
`scripts/check.py --backend --full`; `frontend` checks the generated API types against `backend/openapi.json`, then
lint, format, typecheck, tests and the build; `e2e` builds the app image, restores the cached Ollama models, starts
the compose stack, warms both models and runs Playwright, uploading the report and compose logs on failure.
[`live-smoke.yml`](.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml) fetches the real publishers weekly and never gates a merge,
because publishers change markup and block datacenter IPs.

## AI tools used

- **Claude Code CLI** (2.1.30x) with **Claude Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`) as the main loop, high reasoning effort
  and plan mode.
- **`/grill-me` skill**: Claude interviewed Kris and every design decision was settled before any code (rounds
  Q1-Q20, R1-R10 and follow-ups, recorded in [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md)). The input
  was [`.context/openai-research.md`](.context/openai-research.md), a research and architecture proposal Kris
  provided, from which the approach was handpicked.
- **Workflow tool** (multi-agent orchestration, "ultracode") and **Claude Code subagents**, every one pinned to Opus
  5.5, each owning a disjoint set of files.
- **Opus subagents as eval labour** where judgment was needed: article discovery, gold bodies and key facts, two
  independent labellers, an adjudicator and blind summary judges (prompts in
  [`evals/opus_prompts/`](evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md)). No API key or paid service was used anywhere.
- **Serving** uses only open-weight local models through Ollama; no LLM API is called at runtime.

Division of work: Kris set the direction and settled every decision in the interview; Claude Code planned, wrote the
code, tests, eval harness and these docs, and ran the evaluations. The full, redacted conversation (main loop,
subagents and workflows) is in [`.context/transcript/`](.context/transcript/): rendered HTML and Markdown, the raw
JSONL, and `meta.json` with the harness, model, effort, subagents and token usage.

## Limitations and next steps

- **Labels and judges are one model family.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
  from Claude Opus with no human check, and with 30 dev / 60 test articles the CIs span 0.2-0.5 F0.5.
- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles; users will see many
  neutrals. The 9B decision models catch more but miss the latency budget.
- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets and only checked on articles; real traffic
  is likely neutral-heavy while the article sets are balanced, so served precision is likely below the article
  figures ([threats to validity](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has a minor unsupported detail in 50% of dev summaries and a
  material error in 10% [0%, 20%]; numbers are not yet re-checked against the source at serve time.
- **Latency is one machine at concurrency 1.** Tails exceed the budgets, split mode's concurrent pair and multi-user
  load were not measured, and the docker-cpu figures are indicative.
- **Coverage of the web.** 10 profiled English-language sources; other publishers fall back to JSON-LD and density,
  unmeasured; four CDN-blocked publishers are out; PDFs return `unsupported_content`.
- **Not production-hardened.** No authentication or inbound rate limiting, and the caches are in-process (per
  replica, emptied on restart); the SSRF guard is in place.

Next, from [`90-optional-backlog.md`](.context/docs/design/90-optional-backlog.md): a DSPy-style prompt optimiser in
place of the hand grid; distilling the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier; a progressive `/signal` that
returns the 0.8B verdict and upgrades it when a 9B model answers; analysing articles on publish instead of on
request; serving the number-grounding check; and a GPU compose profile for Linux hosts.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `backend/` | FastAPI service (`veritrade` package): fetch, extract, inference, API; serving config in `src/veritrade/data/` |
| `evals/` | Evaluation and benchmarking harness (`veritrade_evals` package), committed splits and results, Opus prompts |
| `frontend/` | Next.js 16 static export, served by FastAPI |
| `scripts/` | Setup, quality gate, probes, exports |
| `docker/`, `deploy/`, `compose.yaml`, `compose.e2e.yaml` | App image, bundled Ollama pull, e2e fixture site, model lists |
| `.github/workflows/` | CI and the weekly live smoke |
| `.context/` | Brief, research, design docs, AI conversation transcript |

````python
"""Check every relative link and #anchor in a markdown file against GitHub-style heading slugs."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)\s]*)\)")
FENCE = re.compile(r"^```")


def slugs(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    out: set[str] = set()
    in_code = False
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if FENCE.match(line):
            in_code = not in_code
            continue
        if in_code or not line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        text = line.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
        text = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text)
        out.add(text.replace(" ", "-"))
    return out


doc = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
bad = 0
for target in LINK.findall(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
    if "://" in target or not target:
        continue
    file_part, _, anchor = target.partition("#")
    path = (doc.parent / file_part).resolve() if file_part else doc
    if not path.exists():
        print(f"MISSING FILE {target}")
        bad += 1
        continue
    if anchor and path.suffix == ".md" and anchor not in slugs(path):
        print(f"MISSING ANCHOR {target}")
        bad += 1
print("bad links:", bad)

````
</details>

````markdown
# VeriTrade Analytics - real-time financial news analysis (PoC)

Paste a public financial-news URL and get a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal in about 0.2 s and a 2-3 sentence
summary that starts streaming in about 1.1 s (native Metal, warm models, fetch excluded). A FastAPI service fetches
and extracts the article and runs open-weight models locally through Ollama, tuned for **precision of directional
calls**, with every model, prompt and threshold chosen by a committed evaluation.

> **This is a proof of concept, and rigor is balanced per aspect.** The signal metric, the data splits, the latency
> budgets and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean; article labels and summary
> judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check. The limits are listed
> [at the end](#limitations-and-next-steps).

| `/api/signal` (lede) | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | dev300 F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795], 0.0% inversions | 178 ms (p95 195) | <= 500 ms: met |
| `/api/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | Opus judge faithfulness 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] of 5, material errors 10% [0%, 20%] | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | TTFT <= 1,500 ms, complete <= 4,000 ms: met |
| `/api/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | dev300 F0.5 0.752 [0.664, 0.834], 0.0% inversions; faithfulness 4.47 | signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms | as `/summary`: met |
