# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

## Notes

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no article text. With 10
articles per class, read these as a check that the dev300 operating points transfer, not as a ranking.

**Every served rule holds.** No served rule clearly fails (no inversion CI above the 2% cap, no coverage
collapse), so every dev300 threshold is frozen as tuned and nothing was re-picked on the articles.

**/signal.**
- clef-flash v4 at p >= 0.80 scores F0.5 0.848 on the lede and 0.907 on the full body, close to its dev300
  0.874. It makes one inversion in 20 calls on the lede and none on the full body.
- nimble v1 at p >= 0.97 answers far more articles than tweets (coverage 60-67% against 26% on dev300) at
  F0.5 0.88-0.90: articles state their news more plainly than tweets, so the peaked model is sure more often.
- qwen3.5:0.8b with `directional_tau` 0.28 scores 0.685 on the lede against 0.595 for the plain rule (a tie
  at n=30); on the full body the tau rule wins clearly (+0.229 [+0.022, +0.560]). It still misses about half
  the directional articles, so it remains the fast, low-recall option.
- Lede vs full is a tie for all three models; the lede (the /signal default) is two to three times faster.

**/analyze.**
- Articles are easier than tweets for every generative model: qwen3.5:4b v1 0.880, qwen3-instruct 0.798 and
  ministral 0.741, against 0.75 / 0.66 / 0.66 on dev300.
- The tightened summary rule (v5) changes no ministral call, costs qwen3-instruct one (a tie), and costs
  qwen3.5:4b two bullish and one bearish article plus one false alarm (-0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). It therefore
  keeps v1 for /analyze; its /summary endpoint still gets the tightened summary prompt.
- Summary-first is a tie on the articles (qwen3.5:4b -0.013, ministral +0.058) and never wins on dev300,
  while its time to the score is two to three times longer. Every model stays sentiment-first.
- The wrong calls are mostly neutral articles called directional (3-5 of the 10 per model, mostly bullish).
  Price-move headlines are not the problem they were on tweets (0-1 of the 5 directional ones missed per
  model), so the price-move / analyst-action rubric sentence was not added.
----

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no article text. With 10
articles per class, read these as a check that the dev300 operating points transfer, not as a ranking.

**Every served rule holds.** No served rule clearly fails (no inversion CI above the 2% cap, no coverage
collapse), so every dev300 threshold is frozen as tuned and nothing was re-picked on the articles.

# Summary evaluation

Decision R6: deterministic checks, key-fact coverage by a local embedding model, and Claude Opus as a
blind judge. Summaries come from the serving adapters (`/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`) with the default
`selectolax` + `cascade` extraction and `full` scope, run on the stored HTML of the Opus article set.
Written by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval report`; no article or summary text is committed.
Every check scores the served summary: serving caps it at 3 sentences and 60 words
(`cap_summary` in `veritrade.inference.adapters`), and `score` applies the same cap to cached generations.

- **Halluc.** (`hallucinationRate`): share of summaries with any unsupported detail, minor slips included.
- **Material** (`materialErrorRate`): share at faithfulness <= 3: a material error.

## dev split (n=30 articles)

| Endpoint | Model | Pass | <=60 words | <=3 sent. | Numbers | Entity | Truncated | Capped | Errors | Median words | Key facts | Key facts (strict) | Faithful | Cover | Halluc. | Material | Leads |

| summary | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 100% | 100% | 97% | 93% | 3% | 37% | 0% | 49.0 | 52% | 24% | 3.97 | 4.30 | 67% | 30% | 90% |
| summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 100% | 100% | 93% | 97% | 0% | 3% | 0% | 40.0 | 47% | 23% | 4.40 | 4.57 | 50% | 10% | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 100% | 100% | 97% | 97% | 0% | 33% | 0% | 48.0 | 57% | 29% | 4.47 | 4.63 | 40% | 10% | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 90% | 100% | 100% | 90% | 100% | 0% | 7% | 0% | 40.5 | 56% | 25% | 4.73 | 4.43 | 20% | 7% | 83% |
| analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | 77% | 100% | 100% | 80% | 97% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 37.0 | 45% | 19% | 3.77 | 4.27 | 63% | 40% | 80% |

Unsupported numbers (distinct per summary, summed) and how many of them the model input had:

- summary `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`: 1 unsupported, 1 present in the extracted input but not in the gold article
- summary `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: 2 unsupported, 0 present in the extracted input but not in the gold article
- analyze `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: 1 unsupported, 0 present in the extracted input but not in the gold article
- analyze `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`: 3 unsupported, 0 present in the extracted input but not in the gold article
- analyze `ministral-3:3b`: 8 unsupported, 1 present in the extracted input but not in the gold article

Key-fact coverage at other thresholds (main threshold 0.60):

- summary `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`: 0.65: 46%, 0.70: 33%, 0.80: 17%
- summary `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: 0.65: 39%, 0.70: 32%, 0.80: 16%
- analyze `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: 0.65: 48%, 0.70: 40%, 0.80: 23%
- analyze `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`: 0.65: 48%, 0.70: 32%, 0.80: 17%
- analyze `ministral-3:3b`: 0.65: 36%, 0.70: 26%, 0.80: 14%

Quality order (deterministic pass rate >= 0.8, then judge faithfulness, then judge
coverage; latency budgets are applied later by `select`):

- /summary: `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`
- /analyze: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`

Judge means with 95% bootstrap CIs (articles resampled within their sentiment label):

- summary `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`: faithfulness 3.97 [3.67, 4.23], coverage 4.30 [4.03, 4.57], hallucination rate 67% [53%, 80%], material error rate 30% [17%, 47%] (n=30)
- summary `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: faithfulness 4.40 [4.17, 4.60], coverage 4.57 [4.40, 4.73], hallucination rate 50% [33%, 67%], material error rate 10% [0%, 20%] (n=30)
- analyze `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: faithfulness 4.47 [4.20, 4.70], coverage 4.63 [4.47, 4.80], hallucination rate 40% [27%, 57%], material error rate 10% [0%, 20%] (n=30)
- analyze `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`: faithfulness 4.73 [4.53, 4.93], coverage 4.43 [4.17, 4.67], hallucination rate 20% [7%, 33%], material error rate 7% [0%, 17%] (n=30)
- analyze `ministral-3:3b`: faithfulness 3.77 [3.37, 4.20], coverage 4.27 [3.97, 4.60], hallucination rate 63% [47%, 80%], material error rate 40% [23%, 57%] (n=30)

Leader minus runner-up, paired by article:

- /analyze: `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` vs `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`: faithfulness 0.27 [-0.07, 0.60], coverage -0.20 [-0.53, 0.10]

Coverage threshold spot check:

- 10 summaries, 45 key facts, 29 of them stated in the summary by hand label (read in the private files)
- at 0.60: 33 of 45 flags right, 5 wrongly covered, 7 wrongly not covered
- at 0.75: 25 of 45 flags right, 0 wrongly covered, 20 wrongly not covered
- Hand labels from reading the summaries as generated before the serving cap; the flags shown in the review file used 0.75.

## Definitions

- **Pass**: <= 60 words, <= 3 sentences (serving sentence splitter), every number
  grounded, entity named, not truncated. Rates are over all articles; a candidate that produced no summary
  fails every check. Length holds by construction for served summaries; **Capped** is the share the cap
  had to shorten (whole leading sentences kept; an overlong first sentence ends in an ellipsis).
- **Numbers**: every number in the summary appears in the gold title or body. Thousands separators, `%`,
  currency symbols and units are ignored and 1.50 equals 1.5; number words up to twenty in the article
  ground their digits; Q1-Q4 / H1-H2 match the same token, `third quarter` / `first half`, `September
  quarter` or `July to September` (calendar quarters); `FY27` matches 2027; `80K` matches 80,000 (K/M/B
  abbreviations); a clock time on the hour (`5:00 p.m.`) matches the bare hour (`5PM`). Derived figures
  (a percentage change the model computed) count as unsupported: the prompt asks for verbatim numbers.
- **Entity**: the gold entity appears (case-insensitive, whole words); or its short name, without legal
  suffixes (Inc, Corp, Ltd, plc, Holdings, Group, ...) and trailing descriptors (Entertainment,
  Technologies, Industries, ...), as a phrase or as all its words anywhere (`UK ... economy`); or its first
  word when the name has several words and that word has 4+ letters and is not generic (American, United,
  Bank, ...); or the gold ticker (case-sensitive, also without an exchange suffix such as `.HK`).
- **Truncated**: the output hit `num_predict` and the serving path cut it to its last full sentence.
- **Key facts**: each of the 3-5 Opus key facts and each summary sentence is embedded with
  `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact is covered when its best cosine is >= 0.60, the threshold
  that agreed best with hand labels in the spot check. Mean share per article. **Key facts (strict)** uses
  0.75, where every flagged fact was really stated: a conservative lower bound.
- **Faithful / Cover**: Opus judge scores 1-5 (`evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md`), candidates anonymised and
  shuffled per article. **Halluc.** and **Material** are defined at the top: a minor slip such as a
  loosely worded detail counts towards the first only. **Leads**: share the judge found leading with the
  market-moving fact.

# Serving config: allowlist, per-endpoint defaults, decoding options and frozen thresholds.
# `veritrade_evals freeze` writes the per-model thresholds and prompt versions from the eval results
# (evals/results/frozen.json); `select --write` owns [defaults]. Models it has not frozen keep provisional values.
#
# kind        generative (/api/chat) | decision (/v1/systemone)
# endpoints   endpoints the model may serve
# signal_schema   generative signal output: "label" (one of 3 labels) | "ordinal" (score -2..2)
# policy      probability | label-logprob | ordinal  (streaming and /analyze always use ordinal)
# min_p       decision/label-logprob threshold on the winning class probability; 0 never abstains
# directional_tau   optional, probability policies only: when neutral wins the argmax and the likelier
#             directional class has p >= tau, call that class; otherwise argmax + min_p applies
# ordinal_t   directional call only when |score| >= ordinal_t (always set: streaming fallback)
# field_order /analyze JSON order: sentiment-first (streams the score early) | summary-first
# prompt      frozen prompt version per endpoint, e.g. { signal = "v4" }; an endpoint left out serves
#             the prompt file's `active` version

```
# Extraction matrix

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report` from local measurements; no article text is stored here.

- Data: the 90 committed articles (all splits) from 10 sources; stored HTML through the serving `veritrade.extract.registry.extract`; third-party extractors bring their own parser (parser column `(built-in)`).
- Quality: macro means over articles against the Opus gold body. Tokens are lowercased `\w+` runs; P/R/F1 are bag-of-words with multiplicity; a failed extraction scores 0. Leakage is the share of extracted tokens outside every 5-token window that also occurs in the gold body (successful extractions only). 95% CIs: bootstrap over articles (B=1000).
- Time: wall ms of one `extract` call (parse + extract), median of 5 runs per article after a warm-up, then p50/p95 over articles, failures included.
- Tokens: chars / 4 of the uncapped `full` input (title + body) at p50; lede = the `/signal` lede input at the decision model's budget.
- Install: decimal MB of the RECORD files a row adds to the backend core (its closure without any parser or extractor); own strategies add 0 beyond their parser.
- Signal: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` v4 (grid best), served sentiment at p >= 0.8; agreement = share of articles whose verdict on the row's lede equals the verdict on the gold lede, title held at the gold headline; a failed extraction is a miss.
- Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Python 3.13.12; Ollama had a model resident in 90/90 per-article samples (another eval was running), mean 1-min load average 6.1.

"""Print every latency.json cell's cold and warm metrics in one line each, for doc fact-checking."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())


def g(d, *keys):
    for k in keys:
        if d is None:
            return None
        d = d.get(k)
    return d


for c in data["cells"]:
    for phase in ("cold", "warm"):
        p = c.get(phase) or {}
        st = p.get("stagesP50Ms") or {}
        tk = p.get("tokensP50") or {}
        print(
            c["key"],
            phase,
            "n",
            p.get("n"),
            "err",
            p.get("errors"),
            "tot",
            g(p, "totalMs", "p50"),
            g(p, "totalMs", "p95"),
            "ttft",
            g(p, "ttftMs", "p50"),
            g(p, "ttftMs", "p95"),
            "sig",
            g(p, "signalMs", "p50"),
            g(p, "signalMs", "p95"),
            "client",
            g(p, "clientMs", "p50"),
            "stages",
            {k: st.get(k) for k in ("parse", "extract", "wall", "load", "prompt_eval", "eval")},
            "tok",
            tk,
            "trunc",
            p.get("truncated"),
            "orderviol",
            p.get("orderViolations"),
        )
for k in data:
    if k not in ("cells", "environment", "preflight"):
        print("TOP", k, json.dumps(data[k])[:600])

"""Derive fact-check figures from the raw latency JSONL: tails, token quantiles, truncation, event order, client vs server."""

import json
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path


def q(xs, p):
    xs = sorted(xs)
    if not xs:
        return None
    k = (len(xs) - 1) * p
    f = int(k)
    c = min(f + 1, len(xs) - 1)
    return xs[f] + (xs[c] - xs[f]) * (k - f)


rows = [json.loads(line) for line in Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
print("rows", len(rows), "errors", sum(1 for r in rows if not r.get("ok")))
cells = defaultdict(list)
for r in rows:
    cells[(r["cell"], r["phase"])].append(r)
print("cells", len({r["cell"] for r in rows}))
streamed = [r for r in rows if r.get("streaming")]
print("streamed samples", len(streamed), "order_ok values", {str(r.get("order_ok")) for r in streamed})
print("order_ok false", sum(1 for r in streamed if r.get("order_ok") is False))
maxdiff = 0.0
for r in rows:
    if r.get("client_ms") is not None and r.get("total_ms") is not None:
        maxdiff = max(maxdiff, r["client_ms"] - r["total_ms"])
print("max client-total ms", round(maxdiff, 2))
for (cell, phase), rs in sorted(cells.items()):
    pt = [r["prompt_tokens"] for r in rs if r.get("prompt_tokens") is not None]
    et = [r["eval_tokens"] for r in rs if r.get("eval_tokens") is not None]
    tot = [r["total_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("total_ms") is not None]
    ttft = [r["ttft_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("ttft_ms") is not None]
    sig = [r["signal_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("signal_ms") is not None]
    load = [r["load_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("load_ms") is not None]
    trunc = sum(1 for r in rs if r.get("truncated"))
    parse = [r["parse_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("parse_ms") is not None]
    extract = [r["extract_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("extract_ms") is not None]
    wall = [r["wall_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("wall_ms") is not None]
    outside = [t - w for t, w in zip(tot, wall)] if len(tot) == len(wall) else []
    slow = []
    if tot and pt and len(tot) == len(pt):
        pairs = sorted(zip(tot, pt))
        n10 = max(1, round(len(pairs) * 0.1))
        slow = [p for _, p in pairs[-n10:]]
    print(
        cell,
        phase,
        "n",
        len(rs),
        "pt p50",
        q(pt, 0.5),
        "pt p90",
        q(pt, 0.9),
        "slowest10% pt",
        slow,
        "et p50",
        q(et, 0.5),
        "tot p50/p95",
        q(tot, 0.5) and round(q(tot, 0.5), 1),
        q(tot, 0.95) and round(q(tot, 0.95), 1),
        "ttft p50/p95",
        q(ttft, 0.5) and round(q(ttft, 0.5), 1),
        q(ttft, 0.95) and round(q(ttft, 0.95), 1),
        "sig p50",
        q(sig, 0.5) and round(q(sig, 0.5), 1),
        "load p50",
        q(load, 0.5) and round(q(load, 0.5), 1),
        "parse p50",
        q(parse, 0.5) and round(q(parse, 0.5), 2),
        "extract p50",
        q(extract, 0.5) and round(q(extract, 0.5), 2),
        "outside min/max",
        outside and (round(min(outside), 1), round(max(outside), 1)),
        "outside p50",
        outside and round(statistics.median(outside), 1),
        "trunc",
        trunc,
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


def _csv(value: str) -> list[str]:
    return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="VT_", extra="ignore")

    env: Literal["dev", "test", "prod"] = "dev"

    ollama_base_url: str = Field(
        "http://localhost:11434",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "OLLAMA_BASE_URL"),
    )
    ollama_backend_label: str = "native-metal"
    ollama_keep_alive: str = "30m"
    inference_timeout_s: float = 90.0
    # Comma-separated restriction of the models.toml allowlist; empty keeps the full allowlist.
    models: str = ""
    default_model_signal: str | None = None
    default_model_summary: str | None = None
    default_model_analyze: str | None = None

    sec_user_agent: str = Field(
        "VeriTrade Analytics PoC kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_SEC_USER_AGENT", "SEC_USER_AGENT"),
    )
    fetch_connect_timeout_s: float = 3.0
    fetch_deadline_s: float = 8.0
    fetch_max_bytes: int = 10_000_000
    fetch_max_redirects: int = 5
    fetch_cache_ttl_s: float = 600.0
    fetch_error_ttl_s: float = 60.0
    # Pages are up to fetch_max_bytes each, so the fetch cache is bounded by size as well as count.
    fetch_cache_max_bytes: int = 200_000_000
    result_cache_ttl_s: float = 3600.0
    cache_max_entries: int = 512
    models_cache_ttl_s: float = 10.0
    # /health and /models answer even when Ollama hangs, so the container healthcheck stays meaningful.
    ollama_probe_timeout_s: float = 2.0

    cors_origins: str = ""
    static_dir: Path | None = None
    # Lets e2e reach the fixture container; refused outside VT_ENV=test so prod keeps the full SSRF guard.
    ssrf_test_allow_hosts: str = ""

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _guard_test_only_settings(self) -> Settings:
        if self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts and self.env != "test":
            raise ValueError("VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS is only allowed when VT_ENV=test")
        return self

    @property
    def model_restriction(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.models)

    @property
    def cors_origin_list(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.cors_origins)

    @property
    def ssrf_allow_hosts(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        return frozenset(host.lower() for host in _csv(self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts))


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

"""Result cache: finished responses keyed by everything that can change them."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from collections.abc import Callable, Hashable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from veritrade.api.contracts import AnalyzeResponse, SignalResponse, SummaryResponse
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName, ParserName, Scope
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint

CachedResponse = SignalResponse | SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ResultKey:
    endpoint: Endpoint
    url: str
    model: str
    prompt_version: str
    parser: ParserName
    extractor: ExtractorName
    scope: Scope


class TtlCache[K: Hashable, V]:
    """LRU with a fixed time to live; no single-flight, since a stream cannot be shared mid-generation."""

    def __init__(
        self, *, max_entries: int, ttl_s: float, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    ) -> None:
        if max_entries < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_entries must be at least 1")
        self._max_entries = max_entries
        self._ttl_s = ttl_s
        self._clock = clock
        self._entries: OrderedDict[K, tuple[float, V]] = OrderedDict()

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._entries)

    def get(self, key: K) -> V | None:
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry is None:
            return None
        expires_at, value = entry
        if expires_at <= self._clock():
            del self._entries[key]
            return None
        self._entries.move_to_end(key)
        return value

    def put(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
        if self._ttl_s <= 0:
            return
        self._entries[key] = (self._clock() + self._ttl_s, value)
        self._entries.move_to_end(key)
        while len(self._entries) > self._max_entries:
            self._entries.popitem(last=False)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self._entries.clear()

"""Public API contract: request/response bodies, SSE event payloads and the error envelope."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from veritrade.errors import ErrorCode
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName, ParserName, Scope
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint, FieldOrder, ModelKind, PolicyName, Sentiment


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


# --- requests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _ArticleRequest(_Strict):
    url: AnyHttpUrl
    model: str | None = Field(None, description="Allowlisted Ollama tag; endpoint default when omitted.")
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax"
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade"
    no_cache: bool = Field(False, description="Bypass fetch and result caches (used by latency benchmarks).")


class SignalRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = Field("lede", description="lede = headline + opening paragraphs; full = whole article.")


class SummaryRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    pass


class AnalyzeRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = "full"


# --- shared response parts ------------------------------------------------------------------


class CacheInfo(_Strict):
    fetch: Literal["hit", "miss", "joined", "bypass"]
    result: Literal["hit", "miss", "bypass"]


class InferenceTimings(_Strict):
    wall_ms: float
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    load_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_eval_ms: float | None = None
    eval_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    eval_tokens: int | None = None


class Timings(_Strict):
    total_ms: float
    fetch_ms: float
    consent_ms: float | None = None
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    inference: InferenceTimings | None = None
    cache: CacheInfo


class ArticleMeta(_Strict):
    url: str
    final_url: str
    title: str
    source: str | None = Field(None, description="Key from sources.toml when the domain is a known source.")
    published_at: str | None = None
    endpoint: Endpoint
    model: str
    model_kind: ModelKind
    prompt_version: str
    parser: ParserName
    extractor: ExtractorName
    extraction_method: str = Field(description="Strategy that produced the body (cascade resolves to one).")
    scope: Scope
    input_chars: int
    word_count: int
    field_order: FieldOrder | None = None
    cached: bool
    backend: str = Field(description="Inference backend label, e.g. native-metal or docker-cpu.")


class SignalResult(_Strict):
    sentiment: Sentiment
    abstained: bool = Field(description="True when the call fell below the frozen confidence threshold.")
    policy: PolicyName
    confidence: float | None = None
    score: int | None = Field(None, ge=-2, le=2)
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float] | None = None


# --- responses ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SignalResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    timings: Timings


class SummaryResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class AnalyzeResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class ErrorBody(_Strict):
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str
    hint: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    upstream_status: int | None = None


class ErrorResponse(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


class ModelInfo(_Strict):
    name: str
    kind: ModelKind
    endpoints: list[Endpoint]
    installed: bool
    size_bytes: int | None = None
    evaluated: bool = Field(True, description="False for plumbing-only models (e.g. the CI decision model).")


class ModelsResponse(_Strict):
    models: list[ModelInfo]
    defaults: dict[Endpoint, str]
    parsers: list[ParserName]
    extractors: list[ExtractorName]
    scopes: list[Scope]


class HealthResponse(_Strict):
    status: Literal["ok", "degraded"]
    ollama_reachable: bool
    ollama_version: str | None = None
    backend: str
    version: str


# --- SSE event payloads (event name -> data model) ------------------------------------------
# /summary/stream: meta -> summary_delta* -> done
# /analyze/stream: meta -> sentiment (exactly once, position follows field order) + summary_delta* -> done
# Any failure after the stream opens emits a single `error` event and closes.


class MetaEvent(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    fetch_ms: float
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    cache: CacheInfo


class SentimentEvent(_Strict):
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    elapsed_ms: float = Field(description="Milliseconds since the request was received.")


class SummaryDeltaEvent(_Strict):
    text: str


class SummaryDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: SummaryResponse


class AnalyzeDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: AnalyzeResponse


class ErrorEvent(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


SSE_EVENT_NAMES = ("meta", "sentiment", "summary_delta", "done", "error")

from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.models_registry import Registry
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime

URL_HINT = "Send the full article address, starting with http:// or https://."


def error_response(exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
    body = ErrorResponse(error=error_body(exc))
    return JSONResponse(status_code=exc.http_status, content=body.model_dump(mode="json"))


def create_app(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    *,
    fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
    ollama: OllamaClient | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Injected clients stay owned by the caller; the lifespan closes only what it builds."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            page_fetcher = fetcher
            if page_fetcher is None:
                page_fetcher = HttpFetcher(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(page_fetcher.aclose)
            llm = ollama
            if llm is None:
                llm = OllamaClient.from_settings(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(llm.aclose)
            app.state.runtime = Runtime.build(settings, fetcher=page_fetcher, ollama=llm, registry=registry)
            yield

    app = FastAPI(title="VeriTrade Analytics", version=__version__, lifespan=lifespan)
    app.state.settings = settings

    @app.exception_handler(VtError)
    async def _vt_error(_: Request, exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
        return error_response(exc)

    @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
    async def _invalid_request(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> Response:
        # A malformed article URL gets the documented invalid_url code; other shape errors keep FastAPI's 422.
        errors = exc.errors()
        if errors and all(tuple(error["loc"][:2]) == ("body", "url") for error in errors):
            return error_response(InvalidUrl(f"url: {errors[0]['msg']}", hint=URL_HINT))
        return await request_validation_exception_handler(request, exc)

    if settings.cors_origin_list:
        app.add_middleware(
            CORSMiddleware,
            allow_origins=settings.cors_origin_list,
            allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
            allow_headers=["*"],
        )
    app.include_router(router)
    # Mounted last so /api routes win; html=True serves the static export's index.html files.
    if settings.static_dir and settings.static_dir.is_dir():
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=settings.static_dir, html=True), name="static")
    return app

```
"""Confidence policies: raw model output -> Verdict, abstaining to neutral below the frozen threshold."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from veritrade.inference.schemas import LabelOut, OrdinalOut, score_sentiment
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, Endpoint, PolicyName, Sentiment, TokenLogprob, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec

# Ties resolve to the safe class first; also the criteria order sent to decision models.
TIE_ORDER: tuple[Sentiment, ...] = ("neutral", "bullish", "bearish")
# Share of first-token mass allowed on tokens that could start several classes before we give up.
AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX = 0.05

_VALUE_START = {
    "label": re.compile(r'"label"\s*:\s*"'),
    "score": re.compile(r'"score"\s*:\s*'),
}
_SCORE_HEAD = re.compile(r"^(?:-|-[12](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?|[012](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?)$")
_SCORE_KEY = re.compile(r'"score"\s*:')


def winner(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Sentiment:
    best = TIE_ORDER[0]
    for sentiment in TIE_ORDER[1:]:
        if probabilities.get(sentiment, 0.0) > probabilities.get(best, 0.0):
            best = sentiment
    return best


def normalise(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> dict[Sentiment, float]:
    total = sum(max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) for s in TIE_ORDER)
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("probabilities sum to zero")
    return {s: max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def _threshold(
    name: PolicyName,
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float],
    min_p: float,
    score: int | None = None,
    tau: float | None = None,
) -> Verdict:
    top = winner(probabilities)
    if tau is not None and top == "neutral":
        side: Sentiment = "bullish" if probabilities["bullish"] >= probabilities["bearish"] else "bearish"
        if probabilities[side] >= tau:
            return Verdict(
                sentiment=side,
                abstained=False,
                policy=name,
                confidence=probabilities[side],
                score=score,
                probabilities=probabilities,
            )
    confidence = probabilities[top]
    abstained = confidence < min_p
    return Verdict(
        sentiment="neutral" if abstained else top,
        abstained=abstained,
        policy=name,
        confidence=confidence,
        score=score,
        probabilities=probabilities,
    )


def label_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Labels a token's text could start; empty means the grammar would reject it."""
    return {s for s in TIE_ORDER if s.startswith(rest) or rest.startswith(s + '"')}


def sign_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Class implied by a token that starts an enum score (-2..2); empty when the grammar rejects it."""
    if not rest:
        return set(TIE_ORDER)
    if not _SCORE_HEAD.match(rest):
        return set()
    return {"bearish" if rest[0] == "-" else "neutral" if rest[0] == "0" else "bullish"}


def first_value_token(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob], key: str
) -> tuple[str, dict[str, float]] | None:
    """The generated token that starts the value of `key` (minus any text before the value) and its
    alternatives as {text after the same prefix: probability}; None if tokens do not tile the content."""
    match = _VALUE_START[key].search(content)
    if match is None:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end > offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset]
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            return tok.token[len(prefix) :], candidates
        pos = end
    return None


def _first_token_distribution(
    content: str,
    logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None,
    key: str,
    classes: Callable[[str], set[Sentiment]],
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    found = first_value_token(content, logprobs or (), key)
    if found is None:
        return None
    chosen, candidates = found
    if len(classes(chosen)) != 1:
        return None
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    ambiguous = 0.0
    for rest, p in candidates.items():
        # A token ending exactly where the value starts (e.g. a bare space) says nothing about the class.
        if not rest:
            continue
        hit = classes(rest)
        if len(hit) == 1:
            mass[next(iter(hit))] += p
        elif hit:
            ambiguous += p
    total = sum(mass.values())
    if total <= 0 or ambiguous > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + ambiguous):
        return None
    return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def label_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """First label-token probabilities renormalised over tokens the grammar accepts (Ollama reports
    pre-mask logprobs, so "positive" is dropped). None when the generated first token is shared by
    two labels or ambiguous tokens carry real mass."""
    return _first_token_distribution(content, logprobs, "label", label_classes)


def score_sign_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """Class probabilities of the score's sign ("-" bearish, "0" neutral, "1"/"2" bullish) from the tokens
    after the colon, whitespace-insensitive because tokenizers fuse " -". A generated bare space defers to
    the next token; a bare space that was not generated hides its sign and counts as ambiguous."""
    match = _SCORE_KEY.search(content)
    if match is None or not logprobs:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    hidden = 0.0
    path = 1.0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end >= offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset] if pos < offset else ""
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            chosen = tok.token[len(prefix) :]
            for rest, p in candidates.items():
                if rest == chosen:
                    continue
                if not rest.strip():
                    hidden += path * p
                elif hit := sign_classes(rest.lstrip()):
                    mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * p
            if chosen.strip():
                hit = sign_classes(chosen.lstrip())
                if len(hit) != 1:
                    return None
                mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * candidates[chosen]
                total = sum(mass.values())
                if total <= 0 or hidden > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + hidden):
                    return None
                return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}
            path *= candidates[chosen]
        pos = end
    return None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProbabilityPolicy:
    """Argmax unless its probability is below min_p (then neutral, abstained). With directional_tau, a
    neutral argmax still yields the likelier directional class when that class reaches tau: models that
    park most of their mass on neutral are otherwise never pushed into a call."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "probability"

    def decide(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, tau=self.directional_tau)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LabelLogprobPolicy:
    """The probability rule (min_p, directional_tau) on first-token label probabilities. On a label
    collision `decide` returns None and the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema; when its sign is
    unreadable too, the chain ends at the ordinal policy."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "label-logprob"

    def decide(self, out: LabelOut | OrdinalOut, chat: ChatResult) -> Verdict | None:
        if isinstance(out, LabelOut):
            probabilities = label_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
            return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities)
        probabilities = score_sign_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
        return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities, score=out.score)

    def threshold(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float], score: int | None = None) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(
            self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, score=score, tau=self.directional_tau
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrdinalPolicy:
    """Directional only when |score| >= t; a zero score is a confident neutral, not an abstention."""

    t: int
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "ordinal"

    def decide(self, score: int) -> Verdict:
        raw = score_sentiment(score)
        abstained = raw != "neutral" and abs(score) < self.t
        return Verdict(
            sentiment="neutral" if abstained else raw, abstained=abstained, policy=self.name, score=score
        )


Policy = ProbabilityPolicy | LabelLogprobPolicy | OrdinalPolicy


def _min_p(spec: ModelSpec) -> float:
    if spec.min_p is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{spec.name}: policy {spec.policy} needs min_p")
    return spec.min_p


def policy_for(spec: ModelSpec, streaming: bool = False, *, endpoint: Endpoint = "signal") -> Policy:
    """Streams and /analyze always threshold the ordinal score: it is read mid-JSON as soon as it
    closes, with no dependency on logprobs or on where the score sits in the output."""
    if spec.kind == "decision":
        return ProbabilityPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
    if streaming or endpoint == "analyze" or spec.policy == "ordinal":
        return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t)
    return LabelLogprobPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)

# Default: the app uses native Ollama on the host (Metal on macOS; on Linux start it with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0).
#   docker compose up -d
# Bundled: CPU Ollama in a container, models pulled on first start (Linux, CI, no native install).
#   docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
# Either way the UI and API answer on http://localhost:8000 (VT_PORT changes the host port).
name: veritrade

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/app.Dockerfile
    image: veritrade-app:local
    ports:
      - "${VT_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL:-native-metal}
      # Empty values keep the models.toml allowlist and defaults.
      VT_MODELS: ${VT_MODELS:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE:-}
      # Passed through only when set on the host; otherwise the app's public contact default applies.
      SEC_USER_AGENT:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      ollama-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
        required: false

  ollama:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    # Unlimited by default; OLLAMA_CPUS=4 mimics a GitHub runner and spares a busy host.
    cpus: ${OLLAMA_CPUS:-0}
    volumes:
      # OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR swaps the named volume for a host directory (CI caches it between runs).
      - ${OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR:-ollama-models}:/root/.ollama/models
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: 30m
      OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: "2"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
      OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: q8_0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 30

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      OLLAMA_HOST: http://ollama:11434
      VT_PULL_MODELS: ${VT_PULL_MODELS:-qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0}
    volumes:
      - ./docker/ollama-pull.sh:/ollama-pull.sh:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/ollama-pull.sh"]
    restart: "no"

volumes:
  ollama-models:

        www.sec.gov,www.cnn.com,fortune.com,www.theguardian.com,www.bbc.com
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://ollama:11434
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: docker-cpu

      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
    depends_on:
      fixture-site:
        condition: service_healthy

  ollama:

    environment:

  fixture-site:

    networks:

          - www.fool.com
          - www.prnewswire.com
          - www.globenewswire.com
          - www.sec.gov
          - www.cnn.com
          - fortune.com
          - www.theguardian.com
          - www.bbc.com
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1/healthz"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 15

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
STOPPED_FILE = ROOT / ".temp" / "setup" / "stopped-containers.txt"
MODEL_SETS = {
    "eval": ROOT / "deploy" / "models-eval.txt",
    "ci": ROOT / "deploy" / "ci-models.txt",
}
OLLAMA_URL = "http://localhost:11434"
# brew services only reads launchd env, so these must go through launchctl.
LAUNCHD_ENV = {"OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS": "3", "OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE": "30m"}


def run(cmd: list[str], check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    print("$", " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=check, text=True, capture_output=True)


def stop_containers() -> None:
    names = run(["docker", "ps", "--format", "{{.Names}}"]).stdout.split()
    if not names:
        print("no running containers")
        return
    STOPPED_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    with STOPPED_FILE.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"# {stamp}\n" + "\n".join(names) + "\n")
    run(["docker", "stop", *names])
    print(f"stopped {len(names)} containers; restart with:\n  docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def restart_hint() -> None:
    if not STOPPED_FILE.exists():
        print("nothing recorded")
        return
    lines = STOPPED_FILE.read_text().splitlines()
    names = sorted({ln.strip() for ln in lines if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")})
    print(f"docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def ollama_version() -> str | None:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_URL}/api/version", timeout=2) as resp:
            return str(json.load(resp)["version"])
    except OSError:
        return None


def native() -> None:
    if shutil.which("ollama") is None:
        run(["brew", "install", "ollama"])
    for key, value in LAUNCHD_ENV.items():
        run(["launchctl", "setenv", key, value])
    run(["brew", "services", "restart", "ollama"])
    for _ in range(60):
        version = ollama_version()
        if version:
            print(f"ollama {version} up at {OLLAMA_URL}")
            return
        time.sleep(1)
    sys.exit("ollama did not come up within 60 s; check /opt/homebrew/var/log/ollama.log")


def pull(model_set: str) -> None:
    models = [
        ln.strip()
        for ln in MODEL_SETS[model_set].read_text().splitlines()
        if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")
    ]
    failed = []
    for model in models:
        result = subprocess.run(["ollama", "pull", model], text=True, capture_output=True)
        status = "ok" if result.returncode == 0 else f"FAILED: {result.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
        print(f"{model}: {status}", flush=True)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            failed.append(model)
    print(run(["ollama", "list"]).stdout)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"failed pulls: {', '.join(failed)}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("stop-containers")
    sub.add_parser("restart-hint")
    sub.add_parser("native")
    pull_p = sub.add_parser("pull")
```

```
def _num(value: Any) -> float | None:
    return float(value) if isinstance(value, int | float) else None


def parse_reply(cell: Cell, status: int, text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Server-side timings of one response; streams also yield TTFT, time to signal and event order."""
    if status != 200:
        return {"ok": False, "error": _error_code(text) or f"http_{status}"}
    signal_ms: float | None = None
    order_ok: bool | None = None
    deltas: int | None = None
    try:
        if cell.streaming:
            events = sse_events(text)
            names = [name for name, _ in events]
            if "error" in names:
                payload = events[names.index("error")][1]
                return {"ok": False, "error": str(payload.get("error", {}).get("code") or "stream_error")}
            if names.count("done") != 1:
                return {"ok": False, "error": "no_done_event"}
            result = events[names.index("done")][1]["result"]
            deltas = names.count("summary_delta")
            if cell.endpoint == "analyze":
                order_ok = names.count("sentiment") == 1 and names.index("sentiment") < names.index("done")
                if "sentiment" in names:
                    signal_ms = _num(events[names.index("sentiment")][1].get("elapsed_ms"))
            else:
                order_ok = "sentiment" not in names
            order_ok = order_ok and names[0] == "meta" and names[-1] == "done"
        else:
            result = json.loads(text)
        timings = result["timings"]
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, IndexError):
        return {"ok": False, "error": "unparsable_response"}
    inference = timings.get("inference") or {}
    total = _num(timings.get("total_ms"))
    if not cell.streaming and cell.endpoint != "summary":
        signal_ms = total
    return {
        "ok": True,
        "error": None,
        "total_ms": total,
        "fetch_ms": _num(timings.get("fetch_ms")),
        "consent_ms": _num(timings.get("consent_ms")),
        "parse_ms": _num(timings.get("parse_ms")),
        "extract_ms": _num(timings.get("extract_ms")),
        "wall_ms": _num(inference.get("wall_ms")),
        "ttft_ms": _num(inference.get("ttft_ms")),
        "signal_ms": signal_ms,
        "load_ms": _num(inference.get("load_ms")),
        "prompt_eval_ms": _num(inference.get("prompt_eval_ms")),
        "eval_ms": _num(inference.get("eval_ms")),
        "prompt_tokens": inference.get("prompt_tokens"),
        "eval_tokens": inference.get("eval_tokens"),
        "input_chars": (result.get("meta") or {}).get("input_chars"),
        "truncated": result.get("truncated"),
        "deltas": deltas,
        "order_ok": order_ok,
    }


def make_sample(cell: Cell, **values: Any) -> Sample:
    base = {
        "cell": cell.key,
        "endpoint": cell.endpoint,
        "model": cell.model,
        "scope": cell.scope,
        "streaming": cell.streaming,
        "at": _now(),
    }
    merged = {**base, **values}
    return {k: merged.get(k) for k in SAMPLE_FIELDS}


async def post(http: httpx.AsyncClient, cell: Cell, url: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], int, float]:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        response = await http.post(cell.path, json=cell.body(url))
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"client_{type(exc).__name__}"}, 0, (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
    client_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
    return parse_reply(cell, response.status_code, response.text), response.status_code, client_ms


async def measure(
    http: httpx.AsyncClient, cell: Cell, article: ArticleExample, *, phase: Phase, session: str, backend: str
) -> Sample:
    parsed, status, client_ms = await post(http, cell, article.url)
    return make_sample(
        cell,
        session=session,
        backend=backend,
        phase=phase,
        article=article.id,
        status=status,
        client_ms=client_ms,
        **parsed,
    )


# --- raw store -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class RawStore:
    """Append-only JSONL per session; a recorded (cell, phase, article) is never measured again."""


def percentile(values: Sequence[float], q: float) -> float | None:
    return round(float(np.percentile(np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64), q)), 1) if values else None


def _excl(sample: Sample, key: str) -> float | None:
    value = sample.get(key)
    if not isinstance(value, int | float):
        return None
    return float(value) - float(sample.get("fetch_ms") or 0.0) - float(sample.get("consent_ms") or 0.0)


def _dist(values: Iterable[float | None]) -> dict[str, float | None] | None:
    vals = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    return {"p50": percentile(vals, 50), "p95": percentile(vals, 95)} if vals else None


def aggregate(samples: Sequence[Sample]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Totals, TTFT and time to signal exclude fetch and consent (the R7 definition); stages are p50s."""
    ok = [s for s in samples if s.get("ok")]
    return {
        "n": len(ok),
        "errors": len(samples) - len(ok),
        "errorCodes": dict(Counter(str(s.get("error")) for s in samples if not s.get("ok"))),
        "totalMs": _dist(_excl(s, "total_ms") for s in ok),
        "totalInclFetchMs": _dist(_num(s.get("total_ms")) for s in ok),
        "ttftMs": _dist(_excl(s, "ttft_ms") for s in ok),
        "signalMs": _dist(_excl(s, "signal_ms") for s in ok),
        "clientMs": _dist(_num(s.get("client_ms")) for s in ok),
        "stagesP50Ms": {
            k.removesuffix("_ms"): percentile([float(s[k]) for s in ok if _num(s.get(k)) is not None], 50)
            for k in STAGES
        },
        "tokensP50": {
            k: percentile([float(s[f"{k}_tokens"]) for s in ok if _num(s.get(f"{k}_tokens")) is not None], 50)
            for k in ("prompt", "eval")
        },
        "truncated": sum(bool(s.get("truncated")) for s in ok),
        "orderViolations": sum(s.get("order_ok") is False for s in ok),
    }

async def _stream(prepared: Prepared) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    job = prepared.job
    yield prepared.meta_event()
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    events = summarize_stream(job.runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    async with aclosing(events):
        async for event in events:
            match event:
                case SummaryText(delta=delta):
                    if ttft_ms is None:
                        ttft_ms = job.clock.elapsed_ms()
                    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=delta)
                case SummaryResult():
                    response = _response(prepared, event, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)
                    job.remember(response)
                    yield SummaryDoneEvent(result=response)


async def _replay(hit: SummaryResponse) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    yield cached_meta_event(hit)
    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=hit.summary)
    yield SummaryDoneEvent(result=hit)


async def open_analyze_stream(
    runtime: Runtime, request: AnalyzeRequest, clock: StageTimer
) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    """Runs every step that can fail before the stream opens; the returned events only do inference."""
    job = _job(runtime, request, clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(AnalyzeResponse)) is not None:
        return _replay(hit, clock)
    return _stream(await job.prepare())


async def _stream(prepared: Prepared) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    """Events follow generation order, so the frozen field order decides where `sentiment` lands."""
    job = prepared.job
    yield prepared.meta_event()
    entity: str | None = None
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    events = analyze_stream(job.runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    async with aclosing(events):
        async for event in events:
            match event:
                case ScoreClosed(score=score):
                    yield SentimentEvent(
                        signal=signal_result(score_verdict(job.spec, score)),
                        entity=entity,
                        elapsed_ms=job.clock.elapsed_ms(),
                    )
                case EntityClosed(entity=name):
                    entity = name.strip() or None
                case SummaryText(delta=delta):
                    if ttft_ms is None:
                        ttft_ms = job.clock.elapsed_ms()
                    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=delta)
                case AnalyzeResult():
                    response = _response(prepared, event, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)
                    job.remember(response)
                    yield AnalyzeDoneEvent(result=response)


async def _replay(hit: AnalyzeResponse, clock: StageTimer) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    yield cached_meta_event(hit)
    yield SentimentEvent(signal=hit.signal, entity=hit.entity, elapsed_ms=clock.elapsed_ms())
    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=hit.summary)
    yield AnalyzeDoneEvent(result=hit)

"""Server-sent event framing: service payloads become named events, late failures one `error` event."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Mapping
from contextlib import aclosing

from fastapi.sse import ServerSentEvent
from pydantic import BaseModel

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeDoneEvent,
    ErrorBody,
    ErrorEvent,
    MetaEvent,
    SentimentEvent,
    SummaryDeltaEvent,
    SummaryDoneEvent,
)
from veritrade.errors import VtError
from veritrade.services.pipeline import StreamPayload

EVENT_NAMES: Mapping[type[BaseModel], str] = {
    MetaEvent: "meta",
    SentimentEvent: "sentiment",
    SummaryDeltaEvent: "summary_delta",
    SummaryDoneEvent: "done",
    AnalyzeDoneEvent: "done",
    ErrorEvent: "error",
}


def error_body(exc: VtError) -> ErrorBody:
    return ErrorBody(
        code=exc.code,
        message=exc.message,
        hint=exc.hint,
        retryable=exc.retryable,
        upstream_status=exc.upstream_status,
    )


async def event_stream(events: AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]) -> AsyncGenerator[ServerSentEvent]:
    """Closing the payload generator on any exit is what stops the upstream Ollama stream on disconnect."""
    async with aclosing(events):
        try:
            async for payload in events:
                yield ServerSentEvent(event=EVENT_NAMES[type(payload)], data=payload)
        except VtError as exc:
            yield ServerSentEvent(event="error", data=ErrorEvent(error=error_body(exc)))

```python
"""Print the structure of ollama_probe.json minus the logprob token dumps, to check the 01 build-time figures."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())


def walk(node, path, depth):
    if depth > 6:
        return
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        for k, v in node.items():
            if k in ("top", "tokens", "grammar_valid_candidates", "content"):
                continue
            if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                walk(v, f"{path}.{k}", depth + 1)
            else:
                print(f"{path}.{k} = {v}")
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for i, v in enumerate(node[:12]):
            walk(v, f"{path}[{i}]", depth + 1)


for key in data:
    if key == "a_logprobs":
        print("a_logprobs: skipped")
        continue
    walk(data[key], key, 0) if isinstance(data[key], (dict, list)) else print(key, "=", data[key])

 - **Key-fact coverage threshold 0.60** (R6): a hand spot-check of 45 key facts on 10 dev articles agreed best

+- **Docker-cpu pass 1 was biased by Ollama's prompt cache**: the pass ran the bundled app over HTTP (n=10 warm per
+  cell), and each JSON cell re-sent prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles, so its prompt eval
+  read 118-171 ms. `container_reload` in `evals/src/veritrade_evals/latency.py` now stops the model inside the
+  bundled container (`docker exec ... ollama stop`) before every warm phase, mirroring the native suite's unload.
+- **Docker-cpu pass 2 was invalidated by host contention**: unrelated workloads on the same Mac pushed the load
+  average to 50-64 (6.89 at the native preflight, [`preflight.json`](../../../evals/results/latency/preflight.json)),
+  `qwen3.5:0.8b` decode went from about 31 ms to about 2.8 s per token, and 4 `/analyze` requests timed out. The
+  bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp with 14 threads on a 14-vCPU Docker VM over a 14-core host, and its spin-barrier
+  threads stall whenever the host takes cores. The samples of both passes were discarded and are not committed.
+  - Pass 1's valid streaming rows, indicative only (native-metal p50 from
+    [`latency.md`](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md) in brackets): `/signal` 0.8b lede p50 2,657 ms (178);
+    `/summary` 4B SSE TTFT 8,768 ms (1,128), complete 14,405 ms (2,199); `/analyze` 4B SSE time to signal
+    8,644 ms (1,098), TTFT 9,147 ms (1,292), complete 12,106 ms (2,584). CPU-only Docker is roughly 5-15x slower
+    than Metal on this machine, which is why native Ollama is the macOS default (Q1) and the bundled profile is for
+    Linux and CI.
+<!-- PENDING:docker-cpu one line: date and load average of the quiet-host re-run and its per-endpoint docker-cpu p50 / TTFT against native, linking evals/results/latency/latency.md -->
+- **`OLLAMA_CPUS` is a quota, not a thread count**: compose's `cpus:` caps CPU time but does not lower llama.cpp's
+  thread count, so a quota below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower, not just capped. A `cpuset`
+  or `num_thread` is the fix ([90-optional-backlog.md](90-optional-backlog.md)).
+
+## Selection outcome
+
+`uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` applied the Q2 / R6 / R7 rules to the committed results, and
+`select --write` set `[defaults]` in [`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) and the pull
+list in [`deploy/bundled.env`](../../../deploy/bundled.env). Rules and per-candidate verdicts are in
+[`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md); latency is native-metal, warm, excluding fetch
+([`latency.md`](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). Every endpoint had an accuracy-eligible candidate inside
+its budget, so no Pareto knee was needed.
+
+| Endpoint | Winner, frozen config | Rule that picked it | Accuracy (dev) | Latency p50 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0`, v2-label, label logprobs with `directional_tau` 0.28, lede | Best dev300 F0.5 among candidates with dev300 inversions <= 2%, an articles-dev inversion CI reaching 2%, and lede p50 <= 500 ms | dev300 F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795]; articles 0.685 | 178 ms |
+| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, prompt v2 | Deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 and both stream budgets, then Opus judge faithfulness | Faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97 for `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, paired gap 0.43 [0.07, 0.77] ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)) | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms |
+| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, v1, ordinal \|s\| >= 1, sentiment-first | As `/signal`, with TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s | dev300 F0.5 0.752 [0.664, 0.834]; articles 0.880 | Signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms |
+
+- **Bundle (R8)**: the winners alone, `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` and `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, are 4.34 GB of model files
+  against the 10 GB cap, because one 4B file serves both `/summary` and `/analyze`; no fallback combination was
+  needed.
+- **The `/signal` trade-off**: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874 [0.811, 0.937]) but misses the
+  500 ms lede budget (p50 659 ms), and its 10.58 GB file alone exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap; `nimble:9b-q4_K_M`
+  (0.843, 1,061 ms) misses too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms. On the article dev set it
+  catches 10 of 20 directional articles against 17 for clef-flash, with one inversion each
+  ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). The budget was reported, never moved (R7). Both
+  9B decision models stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native
+  Ollama.
+- **The winner's articles-dev inversion**: that one inversion is 1 of 14 directional calls (7.1%). The rule passes
+  it because at n=30 the 95% CI reaches down to 0%; the point estimate alone would fail the 2% cap, so the holdout
+  is the real check.
+- **Provisional defaults replaced**: the budget-feasible defaults set after the P2 probe (`/summary`
+  `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `/analyze` `ministral-3:3b`, see `defaults_untouched` in
+  [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json)) gave way to `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` on both. The probe's
+  synthetic inputs were about 1.6k tokens, where the 4B model missed TTFT; the served cascade sends about 718 tokens
+  of `full` input at p50 ([03](03-extraction.md)), and there it meets both budgets.
+- **Split vs combined**: split mode delivers the signal at 178 ms; the combined `/analyze` stream delivers it at
+  1,098 ms, about six times later, but scores higher on the article dev set (0.880 [0.791, 0.989] vs
+  0.685 [0.473, 0.833], overlapping CIs at n=30) and is close on dev300 (0.752 vs 0.730).
+
+**Holdout check.** The frozen configs run once on the test splits (`articles_test`, `tfns_val`, `fpb_allagree`,
+`finentity_single`), with `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` as a holdout-only quality ceiling, and Opus judges the winners'
+summaries on the test articles. Nothing is re-tuned on these numbers; results go to `evals/results/holdout/` and
+[04-evals.md](04-evals.md#8-holdout).

async def run_suite(
    http: httpx.AsyncClient,
    cells: Sequence[Cell],
    articles: Sequence[ArticleExample],
    store: RawStore,
    *,
    session: str,
    backend: str,
    cold_n: int,
    ollama: OllamaClient | None,
    shared: bool,
    warmup_url: str = WARMUP_URL,
    reload: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]] | None = None,
    log: TextIO = sys.stderr,
) -> int:
    """Cold samples (model unloaded first), then a reload through one warm-up on an unmeasured page and the
    warm samples, cell by cell; returns the number of new samples. An unreachable Ollama aborts the run.
    `reload` unloads a model when the Ollama API is out of reach (the bundled container)."""
    cold = list(articles[:cold_n]) if ollama is not None else []
    added = 0
    for model, group in by_model(cells):
        if ollama is not None and not shared:
            await unload_others(ollama, model, log)
        for cell in group:
            new: list[Sample] = []
            for article in cold:
                if store.has(cell, "cold", article.id):
                    continue
                assert ollama is not None
                await unload(ollama, model)
                new.append(await measure(http, cell, article, phase="cold", session=session, backend=backend))
                store.append(new[-1])
            todo = [a for a in articles if not store.has(cell, "warm", a.id)]
            if todo:
                # A reload empties the prompt cache, so no warm sample reuses a prompt an earlier cell sent.
                if ollama is not None:
                    await unload(ollama, model)
                elif reload is not None:
                    await reload(model)
                warmed, _, _ = await post(http, cell, warmup_url)
                if not warmed["ok"]:
                    print(f"[{cell.key}] warm-up failed: {warmed['error']}", file=log, flush=True)
            for article in todo:
                new.append(await measure(http, cell, article, phase="warm", session=session, backend=backend))
                store.append(new[-1])
                if new[-1]["error"] == "llm_unreachable":
                    raise LatencyError(f"{cell.key}: Ollama is unreachable; fix it and re-run to resume")
            added += len(new)
            errors = Counter(str(s["error"]) for s in new if not s["ok"])
            warm = [s for s in new if s["phase"] == "warm"]
            print(
                f"[{cell.key}] new {len(new)} (cold {len(new) - len(warm)}, warm {len(warm)}), "
                f"warm p50 {_p50(warm, 'total_ms')}, errors {dict(errors) or 0}",
                file=log,
                flush=True,
            )
    return added

# --- docker-cpu ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def bundled_defaults(path: Path = BUNDLED_ENV) -> dict[Endpoint, str]:
    keys: dict[str, Endpoint] = {
        "VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL": "signal",
        "VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY": "summary",
        "VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE": "analyze",
    }
    out: dict[Endpoint, str] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
        if sep and key.strip() in keys and value.strip():
            out[keys[key.strip()]] = value.strip()
    return out


def container_reload(container: str, wait_s: float = UNLOAD_WAIT_S) -> Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]:
    """The bundled Ollama has no host port, so models are stopped inside its container."""

    async def reload(model: str) -> None:
        if _cmd(["docker", "exec", container, "ollama", "stop", model]) is None:
            raise LatencyError(f"could not stop {model} in container {container}")
        deadline = time.monotonic() + wait_s
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            listed = _cmd(["docker", "exec", container, "ollama", "ps"])
            if listed is not None and model not in listed:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        raise LatencyError(f"{model} is still resident in {container} {wait_s:.0f} s after `ollama stop`")

    return reload


def docker_cells(models: Sequence[str] | None, defaults: Mapping[Endpoint, str]) -> list[Cell]:
    """The bundled default per endpoint (signal at lede), or every matrix cell of the given models."""
    if models:
        return select_cells(matrix(), models, None)
    cells: list[Cell] = []
    for endpoint, model in defaults.items():
        if endpoint == "signal":
            cells.append(Cell("signal", model, "lede", False))
        else:
            cells += [Cell(endpoint, model, "full", True), Cell(endpoint, model, "full", False)]
    return cells


async def run_docker(
    base_url: str,
    cells: Sequence[Cell],
    articles: Sequence[ArticleExample],
    *,
    warmup: ArticleExample,
    session: str,
    reload: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]] | None,
    log: TextIO,
) -> int:
    """The bundled app fetches live, so its warm-up is a dev article outside the measured slice."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=base_url, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT_S) as http:
        health = (await http.get("/api/health")).json()
        print(f"health: backend {health.get('backend')}, Ollama {health.get('ollama_version')}", file=log)
        if health.get("backend") != DOCKER_BACKEND:
            raise LatencyError(
                f"{base_url} reports backend {health.get('backend')!r}, not {DOCKER_BACKEND!r}"
            )
        store = RawStore(raw_path(f"{DOCKER_BACKEND}-{session}"))
        return await run_suite(
            http,
            cells,
            articles,
            store,
            session=session,
            backend=DOCKER_BACKEND,
            cold_n=0,
            ollama=None,
            shared=True,
            warmup_url=warmup.url,
            reload=reload,
            log=log,
        )


# --- CLI -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _dev_articles(limit: int) -> tuple[list[ArticleExample], ArticlePaths]:
    paths = ArticlePaths()
    print(f"clean={report['clean']} missing={len(report['missing'])} partial={len(report['partial'])}")
    return 0


def cmd_docker(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    pf = read_json(PREFLIGHT_JSON)
    session = args.session or (pf["session"] if pf else new_session())
    every, _ = _dev_articles(0)
    if not 0 < args.n < len(every):
        raise LatencyError(f"--n must be between 1 and {len(every) - 1} (one dev article warms up)")
    articles, warmup = every[: args.n], every[args.n]
    cells = docker_cells(args.model, bundled_defaults())
    print(f"{DOCKER_BACKEND} session {session}: {len(cells)} cells x {len(articles)} warm", file=sys.stderr)
    added = asyncio.run(
        run_docker(
            args.base_url,
            cells,
            articles,
            warmup=warmup,
            session=session,
            reload=container_reload(args.ollama_container),
            log=sys.stderr,
        )
    )
    write_report()
    print(f"{added} new samples; wrote {_rel(LATENCY_JSON)}")
    return 0

async def run_native(
    cells: Sequence[Cell],
    articles: Sequence[ArticleExample],
    pages: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str]],
    *,
    session: str,
    settings: Settings,
    cold_n: int,
    shared: bool,
    raw_dir: Path = RAW_DIR,
    log: TextIO = sys.stderr,
) -> int:
    store = RawStore(raw_path(session, raw_dir))
    ollama = OllamaClient.from_settings(settings)
    app = create_app(settings, fetcher=LocalFetcher(pages), ollama=ollama)
    async with ollama, app.router.lifespan_context(app):
        installed = {str(e.get("name")) for e in await ollama.tags()}
        missing = sorted({c.model for c in cells} - installed)
        if missing:
            print(f"skipping models that are not installed: {', '.join(missing)}", file=log)
        runnable = [c for c in cells if c.model not in missing]
        transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=app)
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(
            transport=transport, base_url="http://latency.local", timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT_S
        ) as http:
            return await run_suite(
                http,
                runnable,
                articles,
                store,
                session=session,
                backend=settings.ollama_backend_label,
                cold_n=cold_n,
                ollama=ollama,
                shared=shared,
                log=log,
            )

```
def signal_metrics(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    pred: Sequence[Sentiment],
    abstained: Sequence[bool],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> SignalMetrics:
    g, p = _labels(gold, "gold"), _labels(pred, "pred")
    a = np.asarray(abstained, dtype=bool)
    n = len(g)
    if n == 0 or p.shape != (n,) or a.shape != (n,):
        raise ValueError("gold, pred and abstained must be non-empty and the same length")
    w = _weights(weights, n)
    total = float(w.sum())
    answered = ~a
    call = np.where(answered & np.isin(p, DIRECTIONAL), p, "")
    directional = call != ""

    per_class: dict[str, ClassScores] = {}
    for c in DIRECTIONAL:
        tp = float(w[(call == c) & (g == c)].sum())
        calls = float(w[call == c].sum())
        support = float(w[g == c].sum())
        precision, recall = _div(tp, calls), _div(tp, support)
        per_class[c] = ClassScores(precision, recall, fbeta(precision, recall), calls, support)

    inverted = directional & np.isin(g, DIRECTIONAL) & (call != g)
    served = np.where(a, "neutral", p)
    confusion = tuple(
        (*(int(((g == gl) & answered & (p == pl)).sum()) for pl in SENTIMENTS), int(((g == gl) & a).sum()))
        for gl in SENTIMENTS
    )
    return SignalMetrics(
        n=n,
        per_class=per_class,
        f05_macro=float(np.mean([per_class[c].f05 for c in DIRECTIONAL])),
        inversion_rate=_div(float(w[inverted].sum()), float(w[directional].sum())),
        coverage=float(w[answered].sum()) / total,
        signal_rate=float(w[directional].sum()) / total,
        accuracy=float(w[served == g].sum()) / total,
        selective_accuracy=_div(float(w[answered & (p == g)].sum()), float(w[answered].sum())),
        confusion=confusion,
    )


def example_weights(gold: Sequence[Sentiment], class_weights: Mapping[str, float]) -> list[float]:
    return [class_weights[label] for label in gold]


# --- risk-coverage and operating point -------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SweepPoint:
    threshold: float
    metrics: SignalMetrics

    @property
    def f05_macro(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.f05_macro

    @property
    def inversion_rate(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.inversion_rate

    @property
    def coverage(self) -> float:
        return self.metrics.coverage

    @property
    def risk(self) -> float:
        return 1.0 - self.metrics.selective_accuracy


def candidate_thresholds(confidences: Sequence[float]) -> list[float]:
    """0 (never abstain) plus each distinct finite confidence: the only points where calls change."""
    finite = {float(c) for c in confidences if math.isfinite(c)}
    return sorted(finite | {0.0})


def risk_coverage_sweep(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    labels: Sequence[Sentiment],
    confidences: Sequence[float],
    thresholds: Sequence[float],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> list[SweepPoint]:
    """Abstain whenever confidence < threshold; a NaN confidence never clears any threshold."""
    conf = np.asarray(confidences, dtype=np.float64)
    points = []
    for t in sorted(set(thresholds)):
        abstained = ~(conf >= t)
        points.append(SweepPoint(float(t), signal_metrics(gold, labels, abstained.tolist(), weights)))
    return points


def select_operating_point(
    points: Sequence[SweepPoint], inversion_cap: float = INVERSION_CAP
) -> SweepPoint | None:
    """Best F0.5 among points under the inversion cap; ties go to higher coverage, then lower threshold."""
    eligible = [p for p in points if p.inversion_rate <= inversion_cap + 1e-12]
    if not eligible:
        return None
    return max(eligible, key=lambda p: (round(p.f05_macro, 12), round(p.coverage, 12), -p.threshold))

    low: float
    high: float
    level: float
    n_boot: int

def headline_cis(
    gold: Sequence[Sentiment],
    pred: Sequence[Sentiment],
    abstained: Sequence[bool],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    *,
    n_boot: int = 1000,
    seed: int = BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
) -> dict[str, ConfidenceInterval]:
    g = np.asarray(list(gold), dtype=np.str_)
    p = np.asarray(list(pred), dtype=np.str_)
    a = np.asarray(abstained, dtype=bool)
    w = None if weights is None else np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)

    def fn(idx: IndexArray) -> dict[str, float]:
        m = signal_metrics(
            g[idx].tolist(), p[idx].tolist(), a[idx].tolist(), None if w is None else w[idx].tolist()
        )
        return {k: float(getattr(m, k)) for k in HEADLINE}

    return bootstrap_cis(fn, g.tolist(), n_boot=n_boot, seed=seed)
