| /analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,219 | 3,974 | - | 2,219 | 3,516 | 2 | 2 | 2,213 | 713 | 1,350 | met (complete p50 2,219/4,000) |
| /analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | full | SSE | 30 | 2,234 | 4,979 | 1,201 | 1,118 | 3,479 | 2 | 2 | 2,229 | 862 | 1,236 | met (complete p50 2,234/4,000, TTFT p50 1,201/1,500) |
| /analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,243 | 4,969 | - | 2,243 | 3,403 | 2 | 2 | 2,237 | 868 | 1,242 | met (complete p50 2,243/4,000) |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | full | SSE | 30 | 2,584 | 4,627 | 1,292 | 1,098 | 3,570 | 1 | 2 | 2,578 | 992 | 1,539 | met (complete p50 2,584/4,000, TTFT p50 1,292/1,500) |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,580 | 4,582 | - | 2,580 | 3,544 | 2 | 2 | 2,575 | 992 | 1,504 | met (complete p50 2,580/4,000) |

### What meets and what misses

- **Every generative candidate meets its budgets at p50.** The R7 sanity gate in 01 predicted a TTFT miss for
  `qwen3.5:4b` (2.4 s on ~1.6k-token synthetic inputs); real dev articles after the cascade are shorter (an
  825-token `/summary` prompt at p50), so its TTFT lands at 1,128 ms.
- **Both 9B decision models miss the `/signal` budget** (659 and 1,061 ms; see the trade-off section below).
- **The tails are outside the budgets, which bind only the p50.** Streamed TTFT p95 is 1,108 ms for the 2B and
  2,469 to 2,995 ms for the 3-4B models; complete p95 passes 4 s for `/summary` 4B (4,232) and for `/analyze` on
  both 4B models (4,627 and 4,979). The tail is the long articles: in the raw samples, the slowest 10% of
  full-scope requests carry about 2,550 to 2,800 prompt tokens against 825 to 1,074 at p50, and write longer.
- In each `qwen3.5:2b` cell, 1 of 30 warm summaries hit `num_predict` and was served cut at a sentence with
  `truncated: true` (01); no other cell truncated. All 165 streamed samples, cold and warm, kept the event
  order (`meta` first, `done` last, one `sentiment` before `done` on `/analyze`).

### Where the time goes

Warm p50s from `latency.json`; per-token rates are ratios of p50s, so approximate.

| endpoint | model | prompt tokens | prompt eval ms | output tokens | eval ms | prompt eval share | decode ms/token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal lede | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 530 | 126 | 7 | 43 | 75% | 6.1 |
| /summary SSE | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 825 | 423 | 92 | 827 | 34% | 9.0 |
| /summary SSE | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 825 | 1,029 | 68 | 1,075 | 49% | 15.8 |
| /analyze SSE | `ministral-3:3b` | 979 | 713 | 92 | 1,361 | 34% | 14.8 |
| /analyze SSE | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 970 | 862 | 88 | 1,236 | 41% | 14.0 |
| /analyze SSE | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 963 | 992 | 96 | 1,539 | 39% | 16.0 |

- `/signal` is a prefill problem: 7 output tokens (label schema, `num_predict` 16), so prompt length decides
  the time. That is why the quick signal reads the lede (01, Q4).
- The summarisers differ. The 2B spends two thirds decoding; the 4B prefills at about 800 tokens/s against
  about 1,950 for the 2B, so prompt eval is half its time and almost all of its TTFT (1,029 of 1,128 ms).
  Shorter inputs move TTFT; shorter outputs move completion. Warm load is under 1 ms, and everything outside
  inference (parse, extract, input, response) is 3 to 6 ms.

### Streaming, JSON and field order

Same model, same articles: the transport does not change the total (SSE minus JSON is -2.9% to +1.1% at p50),
but SSE shows text at 38 to 54% of it (`/summary` 4B: 1,128 of 2,199 ms). The UI defaults to streaming.

**Sentiment-first field order** (R3) is what makes the streamed signal useful in `/analyze`. The incremental
scanner emits the `sentiment` event as soon as the score closes: 194 to 249 ms before the first summary text,
and 1.1 to 1.5 s before a JSON client would see it (signal 802 / 1,098 ms streamed against 2,219 / 2,580 ms JSON
for `ministral-3:3b` / `qwen3.5:4b`). `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` ignores schema property order and writes the
entity first (01), so its signal leads the summary by only 83 ms.

### Lede against full scope

| model | lede p50 / p95 | full p50 / p95 | prompt tokens lede / full |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 178 / 195 | 231 / 532 | 530 / 1,074 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 659 / 807 | 1,893 / 4,007 | 286 / 831 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 1,061 / 1,182 | 2,321 / 5,242 | 448 / 1,003 |

Full scope costs the 0.8B little at the median but widens every tail: its p95 crosses 500 ms, and the 9B tails
grow 4 to 5 times. Lede keeps `/signal` predictable as well as fast.

### Cold start, parse and extract

- **Cold**: the model load adds 0.7 to 1.3 s over warm for the generative models (load p50 785 to 1,328 ms),
  0.9 to 1.2 s for `nimble` and 5.4 to 6.2 s for `clef-flash` (a 10.58 GB file); n=3, so indicative. A cold 4B
  misses TTFT (2,132 ms for `/summary`). Every call sends `keep_alive` 30m, so only the first request after a
  start or 30 idle minutes pays it.
- **Parse and extract**: 1.2 to 1.6 ms and 1.6 to 2.5 ms at p50 in every cell, under 2% of even the fastest
  `/signal`, so the parser is not a latency lever (03: every parser yields the same body; `selectolax` is
  chosen for speed and footprint). The extractor matters through tokens instead: competent extractors send
  704 to 822 `full` tokens against 2,116 for `strip-tags` (03), and prompt eval scales with that.

## Network

The suite excludes fetch on purpose. Live cost from the source probe ([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md),
EU residential ISP, 2026-10-18): median of the per-source medians 148 ms, slowest 552 ms.

| source | fetch ms (median) | source | fetch ms (median) |
|---|---|---|---|
| bbc | 26 | globenewswire | 552 |
| cnbc | 161 | guardian | 116 |
| cnn | 35 | prnewswire | 34 |
| fool | 202 | sec | 135 |
| fortune | 367 | yahoo | 477 |

As a rough sum of medians (not measured end to end), a lede signal lands about 0.33 s after submit on a
typical source and about 0.73 s on the slowest; on 4 of the 10 sources the fetch takes longer than the signal.
What the service does about it:

- **One pooled HTTP/2 client** (`veritrade.fetch.client`): keep-alive connections (60 s) let a second article
  from the same publisher skip TCP and TLS setup. Deadline 8 s, connect 3 s.
- **Single-flight fetch cache** (`veritrade.fetch.cache`): split mode fires `/signal` and `/summary` at once,
  and the second request joins the first one's in-flight download (`timings.cache.fetch` is `"joined"`), so
  the page is fetched once. Pages live 10 minutes (512 entries, 200 MB); typed fetch errors live 60 s, so a
  refusing publisher is not hit per request.
- **Result cache** (`veritrade.services.cache`): finished responses keyed by (endpoint, url, model, prompt
  version, parser, extractor, scope) for 1 hour; a hit returns with zero stage timings and `meta.cached`.
- **Consent cookie**: the Yahoo reject-all form costs 857 ms once; the shared cookie jar skips it afterwards
  (about 120 ms, 02).

## Split against combined

The UI offers both, split by default. Defaults first, then the other combined candidates; each row measured
alone at concurrency 1.

| arrangement | signal | first summary text | summary complete | resident model files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| split: `/signal` 0.8B lede + `/summary` `qwen3.5:4b` SSE | 178 | 1,128 | 2,199 | 2 (1.02 + 3.32 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b` SSE (default) | 1,098 | 1,292 | 2,584 | 1 (3.32 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `ministral-3:3b` SSE | 802 | 1,051 | 2,242 | 1 (2.95 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` SSE | 1,118 | 1,201 | 2,234 | 1 (2.50 GB) |

- **Split** gives the fastest signal, about 0.2 s, while the summary streams, at the cost of two prompts, two
  resident models and two prefills of the same article.
- **Combined** yields the signal at about 0.8 to 1.1 s and the summary by about 2.2 to 2.6 s, from one model
  and one prompt. Its signal is not worse: `qwen3.5:4b` scores dev300 F0.5 0.752 against 0.730 for the 0.8B,
  and 0.880 against 0.685 on the 30 dev articles (wide CIs, [selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
- **Not measured**: split mode's two requests running at once on one GPU; the split row joins two isolated
  measurements, so its summary times are a lower bound for real use.

## /signal: accuracy against latency

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | articles dev F0.5 [95% CI] | lede p50 / p95 ms | cold p50 ms | file GB | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 178 / 195 | 992 | 1.02 | served default |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 659 / 807 | 6,064 | 10.58 | misses 500 ms; alone over the 10 GB bundle cap (R8) |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 1,061 / 1,182 | 2,219 | 5.63 | misses 500 ms |

The 9B decision models are 0.11 to 0.14 F0.5 better on dev300 and neither fits the budget, so the 0.8B wins as
the only candidate inside it. The budget was reported, not moved to admit them. Both stay on the allowlist: on
native Ollama a request picks one with the `model` parameter and trades about 0.5 to 0.9 s for precision.
Whether the gap holds on unseen data is a holdout question ([04-evals.md](04-evals.md)).

<!-- PENDING:holdout articles_test and tfns_val F0.5 of the three /signal candidates at lede scope, to show whether the 9B accuracy lead holds on unseen data -->

## docker-cpu

Docker Desktop cannot pass Apple's GPU into a Linux container (01, Q1), so the bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp on
CPU. `latency docker-cpu` measures the bundled defaults over HTTP (`/signal` 0.8B lede JSON; `/summary` and
`/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b`, SSE and JSON), warm n=10 per cell; the app fetches live, so fetch and consent are
subtracted, and it warms up on an 11th dev article.

Two earlier passes were discarded, and neither is committed:

1. **Pass 1 found a prompt-cache bias.** The bundled Ollama has no host port, so the native unload was not
   available, and each JSON cell re-sent the prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles;
   those rows showed prompt eval of 118 to 171 ms. Fix: a reload hook (`container_reload` in `latency.py`) runs
   `docker exec ... ollama stop <model>` before every warm phase and waits until `ollama ps` drops it,
   mirroring the native unload.
2. **Pass 2 was invalidated by host contention.** Unrelated workloads on the same Mac pushed the load average
   to 50-64 (6.9 at the native preflight). `qwen3.5:0.8b` decode went from about 31 ms/token to about
   2.8 s/token and 4 `/analyze` requests timed out. Root cause: the bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp with 14
   threads on a 14-vCPU Docker VM over a 14-core host, and its spin-barrier threads stall whenever the host
   takes cores, so CPU inference collapses instead of slowing in proportion.

Indicative only (pass-1 rows the cache bias did not touch, n=10, not committed):

| endpoint | model | transport | complete p50 | TTFT p50 | to signal p50 | x native (complete / TTFT / signal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` lede | JSON | 2,657 | - | - | 14.9x |
| /summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 14,405 | 8,768 | - | 6.6x / 7.8x |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 12,106 | 9,147 | 8,644 | 4.7x / 7.1x / 7.9x |

In pass 1, CPU-only Docker was roughly 5 to 15 times slower than Metal on this machine and would miss every
budget. That is why native Ollama is the macOS default and the bundled profile is for Linux and CI: a portability path, not
a latency path. `OLLAMA_CPUS` in `compose.yaml` sets a `cpus:` quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread
count, so a quota below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower rather than just capped; a cpuset
or `num_thread` is the fix (backlog). The re-run repeats pass 1's protocol, reload hook included, on a quiet
host, and its rows go in the `docker-cpu` section of `latency.md`.

<!-- PENDING:docker-cpu warm n=10 table from the quiet-host re-run (signal 0.8b lede JSON; summary and analyze qwen3.5:4b SSE and JSON): complete p50/p95, TTFT p50, time to signal p50, ratio to native, preflight load average -->

## Levers

Used:
- **Input and model size**: lede scope for `/signal` (half the tokens of full, p95 195 ms instead of 532); a
  cascade that sends about 720 `full` tokens where `strip-tags` sends about 2,100 (03); the smallest `/signal`
  model that clears the accuracy filters, answering in 7 tokens.
- **Perceived latency**: SSE, sentiment-first field order and an incremental JSON scanner.
- **Warm models**: `keep_alive` 30m on every call; `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` 3 native (2 bundled) keeps both
  split-mode models resident; flash attention and a q8_0 KV cache in the Ollama env.
- **Bounded generation**: `think: false`, greedy decoding, per-endpoint `num_predict`, and the served summary
  cap of 3 sentences / 60 words (01).
- **Network and hops**: pooled HTTP/2, single-flight fetch cache, result cache, consent cookie reuse; the UI is
  served by the same FastAPI process (R1), and the fast parsers extract inline, without a thread hand-off.

Left: the latency items in [90-optional-backlog.md](90-optional-backlog.md) (progressive `/signal`, split-mode
concurrency, a GPU compose profile, CPU threads for the bundled Ollama, latency under load), plus:
- Preload the default models at app start, so the first request does not pay 0.7 to 1.3 s of load.
- Trim the 4B prompts: prompt eval is half of `/summary` and nearly all of its TTFT.
- Start the fetch when a URL is pasted, before submit, to hide part of the network cost.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency preflight   # records the machine; fails while Docker containers run
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency run         # native suite, resumable; writes latency.{json,md}
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency docker-cpu --base-url http://localhost:8000   # bundled stack up first
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency report      # re-aggregates the raw samples
```

The native run needs the private article HTML (`articles verify` passes) and an otherwise idle machine.

# 90 - Optional backlog

What we would do with more time. This is a PoC and rigor was balanced per aspect (R2 in
[01-decisions.md](01-decisions.md)), so each item below marks a place where we stopped on purpose. Every item gives
the reason and the expected payoff; items are ranked by impact within their group, highest first. Items that an
earlier doc or a results file already names as future work link back to it.

## Accuracy

1. **A DSPy-style prompt optimiser instead of the hand grid** (Q7). The lean grid tried up to 8 configs per model
   with synthetic shots. An optimiser over instructions, shot selection and the decision rule, scored on dev300 F0.5
   under the 2% inversion cap, searches far wider. The largest lever found by hand was a decision rule
   (`directional_tau`, +0.218 F0.5 for `qwen3.5:0.8b`, [grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)).
2. **Distil the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier.** Label a large unlabelled stream of headlines and ledes
   with `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.874), then fine-tune `qwen3.5:0.8b` or a small classifier head on its
   calls. Payoff: part of the 0.874 vs 0.730 gap at the 178 ms tier, without a 10.58 GB model
   ([selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
3. **Logprob-weighted confidence for streamed `/analyze`.** Streams already carry logprobs (undocumented, see
   [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)), so the ordinal
   `|score| >= 1` rule could become a tunable probability threshold like `/signal`'s. It needs a sign-safe score
   encoding: the qwen3.5 tokenizer fuses the space and minus sign, which hid the sign of negative scores in the
   0.8b grid.
4. **Serve the number-grounding check.** The summary eval already checks every number against the source; running
   it on each served summary and flagging sentences with unsupported numbers needs no model call. The `/summary`
   winner still has minor slips in 50% and material errors in 10% of dev summaries
   ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)), and numbers are the slips a trader acts on.
5. **A rubric for mixed results.** Earnings and guidance tweets hold the most wrong calls for their size (13 in 46,
   against 14 in 128 for the catch-all bucket), which fits a beat alongside a cut outlook. An aspect-level output
   (results vs outlook) or an explicit mixed rule targets the content type the brief names.
6. **Decide price moves before tuning for them.** The rubrics ask for economic impact, so the generative models miss
   33-44 of 57 directional price-move tweets, while the `/analyze` models miss only 0-1 of the 5 directional
   price-move headlines in the article dev set ([articles dev notes](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/notes.md)).
   Whether a reported move is directional is a product call; the rubric sentence the error pass left out is ready
   if the answer is yes.
7. **Revisit dropped candidates when their bugs close.** Gemma 4 (think + format bug) and `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`
   ignoring schema property order and `think:false` under a schema. Low effort, more combined-endpoint candidates.

## Latency and serving

1. **Analyse on publish, not on request.** The 10 sources already have `feeds` / `sections` in
   [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), and the evals' discovery code reads them.
   Polling them and analysing new articles ahead of time turns a request into a cache hit; the cost is inference on
   articles nobody opens.
2. **Progressive `/signal`.** Return the 0.8b verdict at 178 ms, then replace it when a 9B decision model answers
   (clef-flash lede p50 659 ms, [latency.md](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). On the article dev set the
   default catches 10 of 20 directional articles and clef-flash 17 of 20, with 1 inversion each
   ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)).
3. **A GPU compose profile.** A `gpu` profile with a device reservation would give Linux hosts with a CUDA GPU the
   bundled path at native-like speed. CPU-only Docker measured roughly 5-15x slower than Metal on the build machine
   (indicative, [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)).
4. **Split-mode concurrency on one Ollama.** The latency suite runs at client concurrency 1, yet split mode fires
   `/signal` and `/summary/stream` at once against two resident models on one GPU. Measure that pair, then tune
   `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` and `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` (3 native, 2 bundled). Payoff: the split-mode TTFT a user
   actually sees.
5. **A batching server for throughput.** Beyond a handful of analysts, a server with continuous batching (vLLM, or
   llama.cpp server with parallel slots) serves many concurrent streams per GPU. Cost: a second serving stack and
   model format beside Ollama.
6. **CPU threads for the bundled Ollama.** `OLLAMA_CPUS` in [`compose.yaml`](../../../compose.yaml) sets a CPU
   quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota below the visible cores can slow inference
   rather than cap it. Pin a `cpuset` or set `num_thread` to match. Payoff: predictable CPU latency in CI and on
   shared hosts.
7. **Trim the remaining story tails.** The cascade still leaks 13-15% of tokens on Yahoo, PR Newswire and
   GlobeNewswire, mostly after the story ([03](03-extraction.md)). That costs prompt-eval time and summary focus on
   the `full` scope, not the lede.
8. **Start `/signal` on a partial body.** The lede sits early in the HTML, so parsing a streamed prefix could start
   inference before the download ends. The payoff is bounded by transfer time, so mostly on large pages (CNN
   5.7 MB).

## Data and evaluation

1. **A human-checked article set and a larger test set.** The 90 articles are labelled by Opus only (two labellers
   and an adjudicator). With 10 per class on dev a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most article
   comparisons are ties ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). A few hundred
   human-checked articles would separate finalists that tie today.
2. **Extraction beyond the top 10.** Any public URL is accepted, but the matrix covers only profiled sources; other
   publishers fall through to JSON-LD and `density`, unmeasured. A set of other publishers would show whether
   `trafilatura-precision`, the source-agnostic candidate in [03](03-extraction.md), should back the cascade there.
3. **Entity-level and multi-entity sentiment data.** Labels are for the article's primary entity, and the public
   sets are sentence- or headline-level (FinEntity only in its single-label rows). Entity-level data would measure
   the question an analyst asks ("bullish for whom?") and back entity-targeted requests.
4. **Fresh pages for the three tuned profiles.** GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire and Yahoo were tightened on the pages
   they are scored on, so the honest cascade F1 is 0.929 and 0.959 is in-sample ([03](03-extraction.md)).
5. **Resample the threshold choice.** Grid CIs hold the operating point fixed, so they are optimistic
   ([grid summary](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md)). A nested bootstrap or a separate threshold split would
   give honest CIs on the precision knobs.
6. **A sharper key-fact metric.** Embedding coverage agrees with hand labels on 33 of 45 facts at cosine 0.60. A
   per-fact entailment check would track the Opus judge more closely and could gate summary prompts in CI.
7. **Latency on a dedicated host and under load.** Grid and extraction timings came from a shared workstation, and
   contention invalidated a docker-cpu pass. A dedicated runner plus a 1 / 4 / 16 client sweep would give p95s fit
   for capacity planning.
8. **A label-noise pass.** 20 directional dev300 tweets get no correct call from any model
   ([grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)); review them before reading that recall loss as model error.
9. **A second vantage point for the source probe.** One EU residential IP chose the final 10, and datacenter IPs
   meet stricter bot management ([02](02-source-probe.md)). Probe from where the service would run.

## Product and API

1. **Entity-targeted requests.** Accept a ticker or entity and answer for it, and return per-entity calls for
   multi-entity articles, where one story can be bullish for one company and bearish for another. Depends on data
   item 3.
2. **Licensed feeds for the blocked sources.** AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain
   client at their CDN, and evasion is ruled out (Q19). Licensed APIs or feeds would add four widely read sources.
3. **A per-request precision knob.** Thresholds are frozen per model; an override of `min_p` / `directional_tau`
   within the dev300 operating curve would let a desk trade recall for precision without a redeploy.
4. **Non-HTML content.** PDF exhibits and attachments return `unsupported_content`, yet earnings decks and some
   filings arrive that way.
5. **Non-English news.** Discovery skips non-English items and every prompt is English; EU and Asian sources need
   multilingual prompts and their own labelled set.

## Operations

1. **Auth and inbound rate limiting.** The API has no authentication and no per-client limit; the only limiter is
   outbound, for EDGAR ([`client.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/fetch/client.py)). API keys or SSO plus per-key
   quotas come before it leaves localhost. The SSRF guard is already in place.
2. **Source DOM drift monitoring beyond the weekly live smoke.**
   [`live-smoke.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml) runs weekly and never gates. Profiles depend on selectors, and Guardian, BBC and Yahoo hash class names. A
   daily canary over fresh feed items that alerts when the cascade falls back from `profile` to `density`, body
   word counts drop, or `source_blocked` rises would catch silent degradation. No backup sources remain.
3. **Observability.** Every response already carries per-stage timings. Exported as traces and histograms
   (OpenTelemetry) with alerts on the R7 budgets, they make the latency report a live one.
4. **A shared cache (Redis) with distributed single-flight.** Fetch and result caches are in-process, so each
   replica fetches the same breaking story and a restart empties them. A shared store with a short lock keeps one
   fetch per URL across replicas.
5. **Quality monitoring.** Shadow-score a sample of served `/signal` calls with a 9B decision model and judge a
   sample of summaries offline; alert when agreement drops. It catches model, prompt or publisher drift that
   latency metrics miss.
6. **Pin models by digest and gate upgrades.** Eval manifests record model digests. Serving only digests that
   passed `freeze` and the holdout keeps served behaviour equal to measured behaviour across `ollama pull` and
   Ollama upgrades.

```

+
+The defaults were picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal`
+serves `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
+`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
+bundled profile pulls just those two models, 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models call more precisely
+(`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` F0.5 0.874) but miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades precision
+and recall for speed, and the 9B models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Details:
+[01 selection outcome](01-decisions.md#selection-outcome), [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).
+<!-- PENDING:holdout one sentence: whether the one-shot holdout on the test splits confirms the three defaults, with the headline F0.5 per endpoint and a link to evals/results/holdout/ -->

````python
"""Check relative links, anchors and backticked repo paths in the reviewed docs."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FILES = [
    "README.md",
    ".context/docs/design/00-overview.md",
    ".context/docs/design/01-decisions.md",
    ".context/docs/design/04-evals.md",
    ".context/docs/design/05-latency.md",
    ".context/docs/design/90-optional-backlog.md",
]
LINK = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)\)")
TICK = re.compile(r"`([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.\-/]*)`")


def slug(heading: str) -> str:
    s = heading.strip().lower()
    s = re.sub(r"[`*_]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", s)
    return s.replace(" ", "-")


def anchors(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    out: set[str] = set()
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    in_code = False
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        if line.startswith("```"):
            in_code = not in_code
            continue
        if in_code:
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#+)\s+(.*)$", line)
        if m:
            base = slug(m.group(2))
            n = counts.get(base, 0)
            out.add(base if n == 0 else f"{base}-{n}")
            counts[base] = n + 1
    return out


def main() -> int:
    bad = 0
    for rel in FILES:
        doc = ROOT / rel
        text = doc.read_text()
        for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
            for target in LINK.findall(line):
                if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "mailto:")):
                    continue
                path_part, _, frag = target.partition("#")
                dest = (doc.parent / path_part).resolve() if path_part else doc
                if ".context/transcript" in str(dest):
                    continue
                if not dest.exists():
                    print(f"MISSING {rel}:{i} -> {target}")
                    bad += 1
                    continue
                if frag and dest.suffix == ".md" and frag not in anchors(dest):
                    print(f"ANCHOR {rel}:{i} -> {target}")
                    bad += 1
            for p in TICK.findall(line):
                if p.startswith(("http", "/api", "/v1")) or p.count("/") == 0:
                    continue
                cand = [ROOT / p, doc.parent / p, ROOT / "backend" / p, ROOT / "backend/src/veritrade" / p]
                if not any(c.exists() for c in cand):
                    print(f"PATH? {rel}:{i} -> `{p}`")
    print(f"done, {bad} broken links")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

````
</details>

# Default: the app uses native Ollama on the host (Metal on macOS; on Linux start it with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0).
#   docker compose up -d
# Bundled: CPU Ollama in a container, models pulled on first start (Linux, CI, no native install).
#   docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
# Either way the UI and API answer on http://localhost:8000 (VT_PORT changes the host port).
name: veritrade

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/app.Dockerfile
    image: veritrade-app:local
    ports:
      - "${VT_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL:-native-metal}
      # Empty values keep the models.toml allowlist and defaults.
      VT_MODELS: ${VT_MODELS:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE:-}
      # Passed through only when set on the host; otherwise the app's public contact default applies.
      SEC_USER_AGENT:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      ollama-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
        required: false

  ollama:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    # Unlimited by default; OLLAMA_CPUS=4 mimics a GitHub runner and spares a busy host.
    cpus: ${OLLAMA_CPUS:-0}
    volumes:
      # OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR swaps the named volume for a host directory (CI caches it between runs).
      - ${OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR:-ollama-models}:/root/.ollama/models
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: 30m
      OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: "2"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
      OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: q8_0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 30

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      OLLAMA_HOST: http://ollama:11434
      VT_PULL_MODELS: ${VT_PULL_MODELS:-qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0}
    volumes:
      - ./docker/ollama-pull.sh:/ollama-pull.sh:ro
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/ollama-pull.sh"]
    restart: "no"

volumes:
  ollama-models:

# e2e stack: bundled CPU Ollama with the CI models, a fixture site posing as the publishers, app in test mode.
#   docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait
#   (cd frontend && pnpm exec playwright test)
#   docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml down
# Article URLs look like http://www.cnbc.com/vt-skeleton/article-1 and never leave the compose network.
services:
  app:
    environment:
      VT_ENV: test
      # Lifts the private-address block for exactly the fixture hostnames (refused outside VT_ENV=test).
      VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS: >-
        finance.yahoo.com,www.cnbc.com,www.fool.com,www.prnewswire.com,www.globenewswire.com,
        www.sec.gov,www.cnn.com,fortune.com,www.theguardian.com,www.bbc.com
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://ollama:11434
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: docker-cpu
      # The models listed in deploy/ci-models.txt.
      VT_MODELS: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0,tev1:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0
    depends_on:
      fixture-site:
        condition: service_healthy

  ollama:
    profiles: !reset []

    environment:

      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 15

```
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - run: uv sync --all-packages --frozen
      - run: uv run python scripts/check.py --backend --full

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: API types match backend/openapi.json
        run: pnpm gen:api && git diff --exit-code -- src/lib/api-schema.d.ts
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm format:check
      - run: pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build

  # Full stack in containers: app image, CPU Ollama with the tiny CI models, fixture site, Playwright.
  e2e:
    needs: [backend, frontend]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      COMPOSE_FILE: compose.yaml:compose.e2e.yaml
      E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8000
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # The stack needs ~10 GB (Ollama image, models, app image, browser); deleting preinstalled SDKs
      # costs ~3 minutes, so it only runs when the runner image is short on space.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          avail_gb=$(df --output=avail -BG / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
          if [ "$avail_gb" -lt 25 ]; then
            sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
          fi
          df -h /

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Build app image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/app.Dockerfile
          tags: veritrade-app:local
          load: true
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=app
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=app

      - name: Restore Ollama models
        id: models
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ollama-models-${{ hashFiles('deploy/ci-models.txt') }}

      - name: Start the e2e stack
        run: |
          echo "OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR=$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models"
          OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/ollama-models" docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 900 --no-build
          docker compose ps -a
          df -h /
          curl -fsS "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/health"

      # Saved right after the pull, so a failing test run still caches the models.
      - name: Save Ollama models
        if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR"
      - if: steps.models.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ollama-models
          key: ${{ steps.models.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

      # Loads both models; a different article than the tests use keeps their requests uncached.
      - name: Warm up both models
        run: |
          for model in qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0 tev1:0.8b-q8_0; do
            curl -fsS --max-time 600 -o /dev/null -w "$model %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" \
              -H 'content-type: application/json' \
              -d "{\"url\": \"http://www.bbc.com/vt-skeleton/article-1\", \"model\": \"$model\"}" \
              "$E2E_BASE_URL/api/signal"
          done

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          package_json_file: frontend/package.json
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: frontend/.nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - name: Install Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Playwright
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm exec playwright test

      - name: Collect compose logs
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color --timestamps > compose-logs.txt
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-failure
          path: |
            frontend/playwright-report/
            frontend/test-results/
            compose-logs.txt
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Tear down
        if: always()
        run: docker compose down --remove-orphans

```
"""Single quality gate for local runs and CI: lint, types, tests, build and contract drift."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FRONTEND = ROOT / "frontend"


def backend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    backend_tests = "backend/tests" if full else "backend/tests/unit"
    tests = [backend_tests, "evals/tests", "scripts/tests"]
    steps = [
        ("ruff", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "."], ROOT),
        ("ruff-format", ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", "."], ROOT),
        ("mypy", ["uv", "run", "mypy"], ROOT),
        ("openapi-drift", ["uv", "run", "python", "scripts/export_openapi.py", "--check"], ROOT),
        ("pytest", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q", *[t for t in tests if (ROOT / t).exists()]], ROOT),
    ]
    # The floor only means something once the API is wired and integration tests exist.
    if full and (ROOT / "backend" / "tests" / "integration").exists():
        steps[-1][1].extend(["--cov", "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered", "--cov-fail-under=75"])
    return steps


def frontend_steps(full: bool) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], Path]]:
    steps = [
        ("fe-lint", ["pnpm", "lint"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-format", ["pnpm", "format:check"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-typecheck", ["pnpm", "typecheck"], FRONTEND),
        ("fe-test", ["pnpm", "test"], FRONTEND),
    ]
    if full:
        steps.append(("fe-build", ["pnpm", "build"], FRONTEND))
    return steps


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--fast", action="store_true", help="unit tests only, no build (default)")
    mode.add_argument("--full", action="store_true", help="integration tests, coverage floor, build")
    parser.add_argument("--backend", action="store_true", help="only backend + evals")
    parser.add_argument("--frontend", action="store_true", help="only frontend")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    run_be = not args.frontend or args.backend
    run_fe = not args.backend or args.frontend
    steps = (backend_steps(args.full) if run_be else []) + (frontend_steps(args.full) if run_fe else [])

    failed = []
    for name, cmd, cwd in steps:
        print(f"\n== {name}: {' '.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
        if subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd).returncode != 0:
            failed.append(name)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"\nFAILED: {', '.join(failed)}")
    print("\nall checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Local machine setup: free Docker resources, install native Ollama, pull model sets."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
STOPPED_FILE = ROOT / ".temp" / "setup" / "stopped-containers.txt"
MODEL_SETS = {
    "eval": ROOT / "deploy" / "models-eval.txt",
    "ci": ROOT / "deploy" / "ci-models.txt",
}
OLLAMA_URL = "http://localhost:11434"
# brew services only reads launchd env, so these must go through launchctl.
LAUNCHD_ENV = {"OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS": "3", "OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE": "30m"}


def run(cmd: list[str], check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    print("$", " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, check=check, text=True, capture_output=True)


def stop_containers() -> None:
    names = run(["docker", "ps", "--format", "{{.Names}}"]).stdout.split()
    if not names:
        print("no running containers")
        return
    STOPPED_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    with STOPPED_FILE.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"# {stamp}\n" + "\n".join(names) + "\n")
    run(["docker", "stop", *names])
    print(f"stopped {len(names)} containers; restart with:\n  docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def restart_hint() -> None:
    if not STOPPED_FILE.exists():
        print("nothing recorded")
        return
    lines = STOPPED_FILE.read_text().splitlines()
    names = sorted({ln.strip() for ln in lines if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")})
    print(f"docker start {' '.join(names)}")


def ollama_version() -> str | None:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_URL}/api/version", timeout=2) as resp:
            return str(json.load(resp)["version"])
    except OSError:
        return None


def native() -> None:
    if shutil.which("ollama") is None:
        run(["brew", "install", "ollama"])
    for key, value in LAUNCHD_ENV.items():
        run(["launchctl", "setenv", key, value])
    run(["brew", "services", "restart", "ollama"])
    for _ in range(60):
        version = ollama_version()
        if version:
            print(f"ollama {version} up at {OLLAMA_URL}")
            return
        time.sleep(1)
    sys.exit("ollama did not come up within 60 s; check /opt/homebrew/var/log/ollama.log")


def pull(model_set: str) -> None:
    models = [
        ln.strip()
        for ln in MODEL_SETS[model_set].read_text().splitlines()
        if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith("#")
    ]
    failed = []
    for model in models:
        result = subprocess.run(["ollama", "pull", model], text=True, capture_output=True)
        status = "ok" if result.returncode == 0 else f"FAILED: {result.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
        print(f"{model}: {status}", flush=True)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            failed.append(model)
    print(run(["ollama", "list"]).stdout)
    if failed:
        sys.exit(f"failed pulls: {', '.join(failed)}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("stop-containers")
    sub.add_parser("restart-hint")
    sub.add_parser("native")
    pull_p = sub.add_parser("pull")
    pull_p.add_argument("--set", choices=sorted(MODEL_SETS), default="eval")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    match args.cmd:
        case "stop-containers":
            stop_containers()
        case "restart-hint":
            restart_hint()
        case "native":
            native()
        case "pull":
            pull(args.set)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";

const CI = Boolean(process.env.CI);

// Runs against an already-running stack: `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait`.
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  // One Ollama instance: parallel inference would only measure contention.
  fullyParallel: false,
  workers: 1,
  forbidOnly: CI,
  retries: CI ? 1 : 0,
  // CPU-only inference on a 4-vCPU runner is slow; assertions wait on results, not on fixed sleeps.
  timeout: 300_000,
  expect: { timeout: 150_000 },
  reporter: CI
    ? [["github"], ["list"], ["html", { open: "never" }]]
    : [["list"], ["html", { open: "never" }]],

    trace: "retain-on-failure",
    screenshot: "only-on-failure",
  },

});

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


def _csv(value: str) -> list[str]:
    return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="VT_", extra="ignore")

    env: Literal["dev", "test", "prod"] = "dev"

    ollama_base_url: str = Field(
        "http://localhost:11434",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "OLLAMA_BASE_URL"),
    )
    ollama_backend_label: str = "native-metal"
    ollama_keep_alive: str = "30m"
    inference_timeout_s: float = 90.0
    # Comma-separated restriction of the models.toml allowlist; empty keeps the full allowlist.
    models: str = ""
    default_model_signal: str | None = None
    default_model_summary: str | None = None
    default_model_analyze: str | None = None

    sec_user_agent: str = Field(
        "VeriTrade Analytics PoC kris.dimitrov92@gmail.com",
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("VT_SEC_USER_AGENT", "SEC_USER_AGENT"),
    )
    fetch_connect_timeout_s: float = 3.0
    fetch_deadline_s: float = 8.0
    fetch_max_bytes: int = 10_000_000
    fetch_max_redirects: int = 5
    fetch_cache_ttl_s: float = 600.0
    fetch_error_ttl_s: float = 60.0
    # Pages are up to fetch_max_bytes each, so the fetch cache is bounded by size as well as count.
    fetch_cache_max_bytes: int = 200_000_000
    result_cache_ttl_s: float = 3600.0
    cache_max_entries: int = 512
    models_cache_ttl_s: float = 10.0
    # /health and /models answer even when Ollama hangs, so the container healthcheck stays meaningful.
    ollama_probe_timeout_s: float = 2.0

    cors_origins: str = ""
    static_dir: Path | None = None
    # Lets e2e reach the fixture container; refused outside VT_ENV=test so prod keeps the full SSRF guard.
    ssrf_test_allow_hosts: str = ""

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _guard_test_only_settings(self) -> Settings:
        if self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts and self.env != "test":
            raise ValueError("VT_SSRF_TEST_ALLOW_HOSTS is only allowed when VT_ENV=test")
        return self

    @property
    def model_restriction(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.models)

    @property
    def cors_origin_list(self) -> list[str]:
        return _csv(self.cors_origins)

    @property
    def ssrf_allow_hosts(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        return frozenset(host.lower() for host in _csv(self.ssrf_test_allow_hosts))


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

def error_response(exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
    body = ErrorResponse(error=error_body(exc))
    return JSONResponse(status_code=exc.http_status, content=body.model_dump(mode="json"))


def create_app(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    *,
    fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
    ollama: OllamaClient | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Injected clients stay owned by the caller; the lifespan closes only what it builds."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            page_fetcher = fetcher
            if page_fetcher is None:
                page_fetcher = HttpFetcher(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(page_fetcher.aclose)
            llm = ollama
            if llm is None:
                llm = OllamaClient.from_settings(settings)
                stack.push_async_callback(llm.aclose)
            app.state.runtime = Runtime.build(settings, fetcher=page_fetcher, ollama=llm, registry=registry)
            yield

    app = FastAPI(title="VeriTrade Analytics", version=__version__, lifespan=lifespan)
    app.state.settings = settings

    @app.exception_handler(VtError)
    async def _vt_error(_: Request, exc: VtError) -> JSONResponse:
        return error_response(exc)

    @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
    async def _invalid_request(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> Response:
        # A malformed article URL gets the documented invalid_url code; other shape errors keep FastAPI's 422.
        errors = exc.errors()
        if errors and all(tuple(error["loc"][:2]) == ("body", "url") for error in errors):
            return error_response(InvalidUrl(f"url: {errors[0]['msg']}", hint=URL_HINT))
        return await request_validation_exception_handler(request, exc)

    if settings.cors_origin_list:
        app.add_middleware(
            CORSMiddleware,
            allow_origins=settings.cors_origin_list,
            allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
            allow_headers=["*"],
        )
    app.include_router(router)
    # Mounted last so /api routes win; html=True serves the static export's index.html files.
    if settings.static_dir and settings.static_dir.is_dir():
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=settings.static_dir, html=True), name="static")
    return app

ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.13-slim-bookworm
ARG UV_IMAGE=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.10.9

FROM ${UV_IMAGE} AS uv

# Static Next.js export: FastAPI serves it from the same origin, so no Node runs in production.
FROM node:24-slim AS frontend
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /src/frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \
    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --store-dir /pnpm/store
COPY frontend/ ./
# The context holds evals/results/benchmarks.json only once evals publish it; until then the sample is used.
RUN --mount=type=bind,source=evals,target=/src/evals pnpm build

# Third-party dependencies only, so backend edits do not invalidate this layer.
FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS deps
COPY --from=uv /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/
COPY evals/pyproject.toml evals/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-workspace --package veritrade-backend

FROM deps AS wheel
COPY backend/src backend/src
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv build --wheel --package veritrade-backend --out-dir /dist

FROM ${PYTHON_IMAGE} AS runtime
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/.venv /app/.venv
# A small layer of its own: only the app wheel changes between backend edits.
RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=from=wheel,source=/dist,target=/dist \
    uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python --no-deps --compile-bytecode --no-cache /dist/*.whl
COPY --from=frontend /src/frontend/out /app/static
ENV PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    VT_ENV=prod \
    VT_STATIC_DIR=/app/static
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=5s --start-period=30s --retries=5 CMD ["veritrade-healthcheck"]
CMD ["uvicorn", "veritrade.api.app:create_app", "--factory", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

// Copies the canonical eval results into the app; falls back to the committed sample before evals exist.
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const canonical = resolve(here, "../../evals/results/benchmarks.json");
const sample = resolve(here, "../src/data/benchmarks.sample.json");
const target = resolve(here, "../src/data/benchmarks.json");

function isVersion1(path) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8")).version === 1;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

let source = sample;
if (existsSync(canonical)) {
  if (isVersion1(canonical)) source = canonical;
  else console.warn(`benchmarks: ${canonical} is not a version 1 file; using the sample`);
}

mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
copyFileSync(source, target);
console.log(`benchmarks: ${source} -> ${target}`);

# Latency suite

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency report`; ids and numbers only, no article text.

- Session `20261018T200825Z`; machine Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Ollama 0.40.6 (`native-metal`), service env `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=30m`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=3`.
- Load average at preflight [6.89, 5.35, 4.11]; memory {'freePct': 70, 'swapUsedMb': 23199.94, 'swapTotalMb': 25600.0}.
- native: in-process app (create_app) with a local fetcher serving the stored HTML of the 30 dev articles; no_cache=true; client concurrency 1; parser selectolax, extractor cascade
- cold: n=3 per cell on the first dev articles, the model unloaded before each request
- warm: n=30 per cell, one per dev article, after one unrecorded warm-up request
- docker: warm n=10 over HTTP against the bundled app; it fetches live, so fetch and consent time are subtracted from every metric
- clock: server-side from request receipt; totals, TTFT and time to signal exclude fetch and consent; TTFT = first summary_delta, time to signal = the sentiment event (JSON: total)
- Budgets (R7, native, warm, excl. fetch): /signal lede p50 <= 500 ms; /summary and /analyze TTFT p50 <= 1,500 ms and complete p50 <= 4,000 ms. A missed budget is reported, never moved.

```
# Model selection

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` from committed results; numbers only.

## Rules

- **signal**: Candidates: the frozen /signal configs at the default lede scope. Filters: dev300 inversion rate <= 2% at the frozen operating point (n=300); the articles dev set must not fail the cap, meaning the 95% CI of its inversion rate reaches down to 2% (the freeze's clear-failure rule: at n=30 one inversion is about 5% of the calls); warm native p50 excluding fetch <= 500 ms at lede. Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro (primary, n=300), then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **analyze**: Candidates: the frozen /analyze configs (full scope, ordinal |score| >= t, sentiment-first). Filters: the same inversion rules as /signal; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s (warm, native, excluding fetch). Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro, then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **summary**: Candidates: the frozen /summary models. Filter: deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 on the dev articles; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s. Rank: Opus judge faithfulness, then judge coverage, then key-fact coverage (key-fact coverage leads while the judge is pending).
- **winner**: The best-ranked candidate inside every filter. When no accuracy-eligible candidate meets its latency budget, the Pareto knee (metrics.knee) of quality against budget utilisation (the worst measured metric divided by its limit) among the measured candidates, with the reason stated.
- **bundle**: R8: the per-endpoint winners when their model files total <= 10 GB (decimal), else the combination of accuracy-eligible candidates that fits with the fewest rank steps away from the winners (ties: signal, then summary, then analyze keeps its better pick; then the smaller total).

## /signal: `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (inside-budget)

Best dev300 F0.5 0.730 among the candidates inside every filter; p50 excl. fetch 178 ms (limit 500).

# Summary evaluation

Decision R6: deterministic checks, key-fact coverage by a local embedding model, and Claude Opus as a
blind judge. Summaries come from the serving adapters (`/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`) with the default
`selectolax` + `cascade` extraction and `full` scope, run on the stored HTML of the Opus article set.
Written by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval report`; no article or summary text is committed.
Every check scores the served summary: serving caps it at 3 sentences and 60 words
(`cap_summary` in `veritrade.inference.adapters`), and `score` applies the same cap to cached generations.

- **Halluc.** (`hallucinationRate`): share of summaries with any unsupported detail, minor slips included.
- **Material** (`materialErrorRate`): share at faithfulness <= 3: a material error.

Coverage threshold spot check:

- 10 summaries, 45 key facts, 29 of them stated in the summary by hand label (read in the private files)
- at 0.60: 33 of 45 flags right, 5 wrongly covered, 7 wrongly not covered
- at 0.75: 25 of 45 flags right, 0 wrongly covered, 20 wrongly not covered
- Hand labels from reading the summaries as generated before the serving cap; the flags shown in the review file used 0.75.

## Definitions

- **Pass**: <= 60 words, <= 3 sentences (serving sentence splitter), every number
  grounded, entity named, not truncated. Rates are over all articles; a candidate that produced no summary
  fails every check. Length holds by construction for served summaries; **Capped** is the share the cap
  had to shorten (whole leading sentences kept; an overlong first sentence ends in an ellipsis).
- **Numbers**: every number in the summary appears in the gold title or body. Thousands separators, `%`,
  currency symbols and units are ignored and 1.50 equals 1.5; number words up to twenty in the article
  ground their digits; Q1-Q4 / H1-H2 match the same token, `third quarter` / `first half`, `September
  quarter` or `July to September` (calendar quarters); `FY27` matches 2027; `80K` matches 80,000 (K/M/B
  abbreviations); a clock time on the hour (`5:00 p.m.`) matches the bare hour (`5PM`). Derived figures
  (a percentage change the model computed) count as unsupported: the prompt asks for verbatim numbers.
- **Entity**: the gold entity appears (case-insensitive, whole words); or its short name, without legal
  suffixes (Inc, Corp, Ltd, plc, Holdings, Group, ...) and trailing descriptors (Entertainment,
  Technologies, Industries, ...), as a phrase or as all its words anywhere (`UK ... economy`); or its first
  word when the name has several words and that word has 4+ letters and is not generic (American, United,
  Bank, ...); or the gold ticker (case-sensitive, also without an exchange suffix such as `.HK`).
- **Truncated**: the output hit `num_predict` and the serving path cut it to its last full sentence.
- **Key facts**: each of the 3-5 Opus key facts and each summary sentence is embedded with
  `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact is covered when its best cosine is >= 0.60, the threshold
  that agreed best with hand labels in the spot check. Mean share per article. **Key facts (strict)** uses
  0.75, where every flagged fact was really stated: a conservative lower bound.
- **Faithful / Cover**: Opus judge scores 1-5 (`evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md`), candidates anonymised and
  shuffled per article. **Halluc.** and **Material** are defined at the top: a minor slip such as a
  loosely worded detail counts towards the first only. **Leads**: share the judge found leading with the
  market-moving fact.

# Extraction matrix

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report` from local measurements; no article text is stored here.

- Data: the 90 committed articles (all splits) from 10 sources; stored HTML through the serving `veritrade.extract.registry.extract`; third-party extractors bring their own parser (parser column `(built-in)`).
- Quality: macro means over articles against the Opus gold body. Tokens are lowercased `\w+` runs; P/R/F1 are bag-of-words with multiplicity; a failed extraction scores 0. Leakage is the share of extracted tokens outside every 5-token window that also occurs in the gold body (successful extractions only). 95% CIs: bootstrap over articles (B=1000).
- Time: wall ms of one `extract` call (parse + extract), median of 5 runs per article after a warm-up, then p50/p95 over articles, failures included.
- Tokens: chars / 4 of the uncapped `full` input (title + body) at p50; lede = the `/signal` lede input at the decision model's budget.
- Install: decimal MB of the RECORD files a row adds to the backend core (its closure without any parser or extractor); own strategies add 0 beyond their parser.
- Signal: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` v4 (grid best), served sentiment at p >= 0.8; agreement = share of articles whose verdict on the row's lede equals the verdict on the gold lede, title held at the gold headline; a failed extraction is a miss.
- Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Python 3.13.12; Ollama had a model resident in 90/90 per-article samples (another eval was running), mean 1-min load average 6.1.

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import StrEnum
from typing import ClassVar


class ErrorCode(StrEnum):
    INVALID_URL = "invalid_url"
    BLOCKED_DESTINATION = "blocked_destination"
    MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED = "model_not_allowed"
    PAYWALLED = "paywalled"
    CONSENT_REQUIRED = "consent_required"
    EXTRACTION_EMPTY = "extraction_empty"
    UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT = "unsupported_content"
    TOO_LARGE = "too_large"
    SOURCE_BLOCKED = "source_blocked"
    UPSTREAM_HTTP = "upstream_http"
    SCHEMA_VIOLATION = "schema_violation"
    MODEL_UNAVAILABLE = "model_unavailable"
    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
    UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT = "upstream_timeout"
    INFERENCE_TIMEOUT = "inference_timeout"


ERROR_STATUS: dict[ErrorCode, int] = {
    ErrorCode.INVALID_URL: 400,
    ErrorCode.BLOCKED_DESTINATION: 400,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED: 400,
    ErrorCode.PAYWALLED: 422,
    ErrorCode.CONSENT_REQUIRED: 422,
    ErrorCode.EXTRACTION_EMPTY: 422,
    ErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT: 422,
    ErrorCode.TOO_LARGE: 422,
    ErrorCode.SOURCE_BLOCKED: 502,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_HTTP: 502,
    ErrorCode.SCHEMA_VIOLATION: 502,
    ErrorCode.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 503,
    ErrorCode.UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT: 504,
    ErrorCode.INFERENCE_TIMEOUT: 504,
}


class VtError(Exception):
    code: ClassVar[ErrorCode]
    retryable_default: ClassVar[bool] = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        hint: str | None = None,
        retryable: bool | None = None,
        upstream_status: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.hint = hint
        self.retryable = self.retryable_default if retryable is None else retryable
        self.upstream_status = upstream_status

    @property
    def http_status(self) -> int:
        return ERROR_STATUS[self.code]

# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

**/signal.**
- clef-flash v4 at p >= 0.80 scores F0.5 0.848 on the lede and 0.907 on the full body, close to its dev300
  0.874. It makes one inversion in 20 calls on the lede and none on the full body.
- nimble v1 at p >= 0.97 answers far more articles than tweets (coverage 60-67% against 26% on dev300) at
  F0.5 0.88-0.90: articles state their news more plainly than tweets, so the peaked model is sure more often.
- qwen3.5:0.8b with `directional_tau` 0.28 scores 0.685 on the lede against 0.595 for the plain rule (a tie
  at n=30); on the full body the tau rule wins clearly (+0.229 [+0.022, +0.560]). It still misses about half
  the directional articles, so it remains the fast, low-recall option.
- Lede vs full is a tie for all three models; the lede (the /signal default) is two to three times faster.

**/analyze.**
- Articles are easier than tweets for every generative model: qwen3.5:4b v1 0.880, qwen3-instruct 0.798 and
  ministral 0.741, against 0.75 / 0.66 / 0.66 on dev300.
- The tightened summary rule (v5) changes no ministral call, costs qwen3-instruct one (a tie), and costs
  qwen3.5:4b two bullish and one bearish article plus one false alarm (-0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). It therefore
  keeps v1 for /analyze; its /summary endpoint still gets the tightened summary prompt.
- Summary-first is a tie on the articles (qwen3.5:4b -0.013, ministral +0.058) and never wins on dev300,
  while its time to the score is two to three times longer. Every model stays sentiment-first.
- The wrong calls are mostly neutral articles called directional (3-5 of the 10 per model, mostly bullish).
  Price-move headlines are not the problem they were on tweets (0-1 of the 5 directional ones missed per
  model), so the price-move / analyst-action rubric sentence was not added.

###### 💻 Bash: *Read Yahoo consent section and extraction speed note*

```
## Yahoo EU consent

- From this IP, `finance.yahoo.com`, `yahoo.com/news`, `uk.finance.yahoo.com` and `de.yahoo.com` served content
  directly with no consent redirect. The pages carry `"gdpr":true` and a client-side CMP
  (`consent.cmp.oath.com`), so in October 2026 the server-side wall no longer stands in front of articles.
- The server-side flow still exists at `guce.yahoo.com/consent` -> `consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent`, so the
  probe exercises it on every run (`yahoo_consent_check` in the JSON): `consent.reject_all` posted the
  reject-all form in 857 ms and the jar received `A1`, `A1S`, `CFC`, `EuConsent`, `GUC`. Decoding the TCF v2
  string in `EuConsent` gives **0 of 24 purposes consented**, which confirms that reject-all was recorded and
  accept-all was never sent. A second pass with the same jar skips the form (about 120 ms, no POST).
- Serving contract: when a redirect lands on a consent host, the fetcher calls `reject_all` with its SSRF
  guard and retries the original URL once; if that lands on the wall again, `detect.classify` raises
  `consent_required` with a hint.

## Block, consent and paywall detection

`detect.classify(status, headers, html, final_url)` is pure and string-based, so it runs on every fetch.

The default stays **`selectolax` + `cascade`** (already the `registry.extract` default):

- **Quality**: best or tied F1 (0.959 [0.942, 0.973]), zero failures on the 90 pages, and 97.8% [94.4%, 100%]
  agreement with the gold-lede verdict, with no inversion.
- **Speed**: the lowest tail of any row that finds bodies, p50 1.2 ms and p95 2.4 ms. That is noise
  against the 500 ms `/signal` budget.
- **Footprint and provenance**: 7.5 MB, no third-party extractor needed at runtime, and the winning method
  (`jsonld`, `profile` or `density`) is reported in every response's meta.
```

"""Print a compact per-cell view of evals/results/latency/latency.json (numbers only)."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

path = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "evals/results/latency/latency.json")
report = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def p(d, k="p50"):
    return "-" if not d else d.get(k)


for c in report["cells"]:
    w, co = c["warm"], c["cold"]
    print(
        c["key"],
        "| warm n", w["n"], "err", w["errors"], w["errorCodes"],
        "| total p50/p95", p(w["totalMs"]), p(w["totalMs"], "p95"),
        "| ttft p50/p95", p(w["ttftMs"]), p(w["ttftMs"], "p95"),
        "| signal p50/p95", p(w["signalMs"]), p(w["signalMs"], "p95"),
        "| client p50", p(w["clientMs"]),
        "| stages", w["stagesP50Ms"],
        "| tokens", w["tokensP50"],
        "| trunc", w["truncated"], "orderViol", w["orderViolations"],
    )
    print(
        "    cold n", co["n"], "err", co["errors"],
        "| total p50/p95", p(co["totalMs"]), p(co["totalMs"], "p95"),
        "| ttft p50", p(co["ttftMs"]), "| signal p50", p(co["signalMs"]),
        "| stages", co["stagesP50Ms"], "| tokens", co["tokensP50"],
    )

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrdinalPolicy:
    """Directional only when |score| >= t; a zero score is a confident neutral, not an abstention."""

    t: int
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "ordinal"

    def decide(self, score: int) -> Verdict:
        raw = score_sentiment(score)
        abstained = raw != "neutral" and abs(score) < self.t
        return Verdict(
            sentiment="neutral" if abstained else raw, abstained=abstained, policy=self.name, score=score
        )

```
# Real-Time Financial News Analysis Service

## Overview
VeriTrade Analytics is a fintech firm providing high-speed market intelligence to day traders and quantitative analysts. Our analysts currently waste precious minutes manually reading breaking news articles, press releases, and earnings reports to gauge market sentiment. In a world where milliseconds matter, this manual process introduces critical delays, leading to missed opportunities. To solve this, VeriTrade needs a tool that can ingest a news article and provide an instant, AI-powered summary and sentiment analysis.

Your task is to build a prototype for this internal tool. You will create a web service that accepts a URL to a public financial news article. The service should then fetch the article's content, use a Large Language Model (LLM) to generate a concise summary and a sentiment analysis (e.g., Bullish, Bearish, Neutral), and return this information via an API. The core business constraint is speed; the system must be designed for low latency to be useful for traders making time-sensitive decisions. You will also build a simple frontend interface to interact with this service.

A successful submission will demonstrate thoughtful system design focused on performance, effective use of an LLM for a specific task, and clear communication of your design trade-offs. The frontend UI does not need to be visually polished; a functional interface that clearly presents the workflow and results is sufficient.

## Deliverables
- A public GitHub repository or a single public GitHub gist URL containing your complete solution.
- A backend service written in Python that exposes an API to analyze a given news article URL.
- A basic frontend web application (e.g., React, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JS) that consumes the backend API and displays the results.
- A `README.md` file explaining your design decisions, trade-offs (especially regarding latency optimization), instructions on how to run the application and any tests, and a brief note on which AI tools you used.
- The conversation log from any AI assistants used during development (e.g., VS Code Copilot Chat export, Claude conversation history) committed to the repository.

## Suggested tools / libraries
- Backend Framework: FastAPI, Flask
- LLM Integration: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, Groq, or a local model via Ollama
- Web Scraping: BeautifulSoup, requests
- Frontend Framework: React + Vite, Next.js, or plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- API Client: `fetch` API, Axios
- Containerization: Docker (optional)

## On AI assistants & follow-up
- We expect and encourage the use of AI assistants. Your goal is to deliver a great solution, not to memorize APIs.
- Please commit the conversation log from your AI assistant (e.g., Copilot Chat export, Claude history) to your repository and briefly describe its role in your README.
- Be prepared to walk through your code and justify your design decisions, especially regarding performance and architectural trade-offs, in the follow-up interview.
- The focus is on your design judgment, problem decomposition, and verification, not on writing every line of code from scratch.

## How to submit
Reply to this email with **one** public GitHub repository or gist URL containing your solution.

<!-- AI-EVALUATOR:PRESCREEN-META {"language":"Python","dueDays":10,"timeBudgetHours":8} -->
```

````markdown
# VeriTrade Analytics - real-time financial news analysis (PoC)

Paste a public financial-news URL and get a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal in about 0.2 s and a 2-3 sentence
summary that starts streaming in about 1.1 s (native Metal, warm models, fetch excluded). A FastAPI service fetches
and extracts the article and runs open-weight models locally through Ollama, tuned for **precision of directional
calls**, with every model, prompt and threshold chosen by a committed evaluation.

> **This is a proof of concept, and rigor is balanced per aspect.** The signal metric, the data splits, the latency
> budgets and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean; article labels and summary
> judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check. The limits are listed
> [at the end](#limitations-and-next-steps).

|---|---|
| Design decisions | [Design decisions](#design-decisions), [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md) |
| Latency trade-offs | [Latency trade-offs](#latency-trade-offs), [`05-latency.md`](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md) |
| How to run | [Quickstart](#quickstart), [Using it](#using-it) |
| How to test | [Testing](#testing) |

Per-endpoint defaults, picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md). Latency is
native Metal on an Apple M4 Pro, warm, concurrency 1, excluding fetch ([`latency.md`](evals/results/latency/latency.md)).

| Endpoint | Default model | Quality on dev | Warm p50 latency | Budget (p50) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/signal` (lede) | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | dev300 F0.5 0.730 [0.651, 0.795], 0.0% inversions | 178 ms (p95 195) | <= 500 ms: met |
| `/api/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | Opus judge faithfulness 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] of 5, material errors 10% [0%, 20%] | TTFT 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | TTFT <= 1,500 ms, complete <= 4,000 ms: met |
| `/api/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | dev300 F0.5 0.752 [0.664, 0.834], 0.0% inversions; faithfulness 4.47 | signal 1,098 ms, TTFT 1,292 ms, complete 2,584 ms | as `/summary`: met |

- Two model files serve all three endpoints: 4.34 GB against the 10 GB bundle cap.
