````markdown
## Testing

| Layer | Where | What it guards |
|---|---|---|
| Backend unit | `backend/tests/unit` | Extractors on skeleton fixtures under all four parsers, the SSRF guard (address classes, DNS rebinding, ports), block / consent / paywall detection, prompts, confidence policies, the stream scanner split at every byte offset, the Ollama client, the API contract |
| Backend integration | `backend/tests/integration` | The ASGI app against fake publishers (skeleton pages) and a scripted Ollama: every endpoint in JSON and SSE, event order, single-flight and result caches, the error table, failures mid-stream, client disconnects |
| Evals and scripts | `evals/tests/unit`, `scripts/tests` | Metrics, splits, grid, freeze, selection, the holdout guard, latency aggregation, the report, transcript redaction |
| Frontend | `frontend/tests` | Vitest + Testing Library: SSE parser, components, and MSW integration (signal before the summary completes, JSON fallback, errors, abort on resubmit, benchmarks page) |
| End to end | `frontend/e2e` | Playwright on the compose stack: bundled CPU Ollama with the CI models, an nginx fixture site answering for the 10 publisher hostnames, split and combined streaming, a decision model with a switched extractor, a signal check per source profile, the benchmarks page |
| Live smoke | `backend/tests/live` | One real article per source; informational, never gates |

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
(cd frontend && pnpm install)            # frontend deps for check.py
uv run python scripts/check.py --fast    # ruff, format, mypy, OpenAPI drift, backend unit + evals + scripts tests, frontend lint/format/typecheck/test
uv run python scripts/check.py --full    # adds backend integration tests with a 75% coverage floor, and the frontend build
uv run pytest -m live backend/tests/live -rA   # live publishers, opt-in
```

End to end on the CI stack, which pulls `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` and `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` (a CI-only decision model that
exercises the decision-model path and is never evaluated); CPU inference is slow, so test timeouts are 300 s.

```bash
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml up -d --wait
(cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm exec playwright install chromium && pnpm exec playwright test)
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.e2e.yaml down
```

**CI** ([`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml), on push to `main` and pull requests): `backend` runs
`scripts/check.py --backend --full`; `frontend` checks the generated API types against `backend/openapi.json`, then
lint, format, typecheck, tests and the build; `e2e` builds the image, restores the cached Ollama models, starts the
stack, warms both models and runs Playwright, uploading logs on failure. [`live-smoke.yml`](.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml)
fetches the real publishers weekly and never gates, because publishers change markup and block datacenter IPs.

## AI tools used

- **Claude Code CLI** (2.1.301) with **Claude Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`) as the main loop, `xhigh` reasoning
  effort with adaptive thinking, and plan mode.
- **`/grill-me` skill**: Claude interviewed Kris until every decision was settled, before any code (Q1-Q20, R1-R10
  and follow-ups in [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md)). The approach was handpicked from
  [`.context/openai-research.md`](.context/openai-research.md), a research and architecture proposal Kris provided.
- **Workflow tool** (multi-agent orchestration, "ultracode") and **Claude Code subagents**, every one pinned to Opus
  5.5, each owning a disjoint set of files. Opus subagents also produced the eval data that needs judgment: article
  discovery, gold bodies and key facts, two independent labellers, an adjudicator and blind summary judges (prompts
  in [`evals/opus_prompts/`](evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md)).
- **No API keys or paid services** anywhere. Serving uses only open-weight local models through Ollama.

Kris set the direction and settled every decision; Claude Code planned, wrote the code, tests, eval harness and docs,
and ran the evaluations. The full, redacted conversation (main loop, subagents, workflows) is in
[`.context/transcript/`](.context/transcript/): rendered HTML and Markdown, raw JSONL, and `meta.json` with the
harness, model, effort, subagents and token usage.

## Limitations and next steps

- **One model family labels and judges.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
  from Claude Opus with no human check, and with 30 dev articles the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5.
- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles, so users will see many
  neutrals; the 9B decision models catch more but miss the latency budget.
- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** On the 30 dev articles the `/signal` default inverts 1 of its 14
  directional calls (7.1% against the 2% cap); selection passes it only because the 95% CI at n=30 reaches 0%, so
  the holdout is the real check ([`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets and checked on balanced article sets; real
  traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely lower ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev
  summaries and a material error in 10% [0%, 20%]; numbers are not re-checked against the source at serve time.
- **Latency is one machine at concurrency 1.** Tails exceed the budgets, split mode's concurrent pair and multi-user
  load were not measured, and the docker-cpu figures are indicative.
- **Coverage and hardening.** 10 profiled English sources (others fall back to JSON-LD and density, unmeasured),
  no PDFs; no authentication or inbound rate limiting, and the caches are in-process (per replica).

Next, from [`90-optional-backlog.md`](.context/docs/design/90-optional-backlog.md): a DSPy-style prompt optimiser;
distilling the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier; a progressive `/signal` that upgrades the 0.8B verdict
when a 9B model answers; analysing articles on publish; serving the number-grounding check; a GPU compose profile.

| `evals/` | Evaluation and benchmarking harness (`veritrade_evals` package), committed splits and results, Opus prompts |
| `frontend/` | Next.js 16 static export, served by FastAPI |
````

````markdown
# 04 - Evaluation

How the models, prompts and thresholds behind `/signal`, `/summary` and `/analyze` were chosen, and how well they
do. The reasons behind each choice are in [`01-decisions.md`](01-decisions.md); the fetch and extraction path every
eval runs through is in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md) and [`03-extraction.md`](03-extraction.md).
Every number links to the committed result file it comes from. Rigor is balanced per aspect, as for the rest of this
PoC (R2): the signal metric, the splits and the one-time holdout are strict; the prompt grid is deliberately lean;
the article labels and summary judgements come from Claude Opus subagents with no human check.

```
dev300 grid (prompt x policy x threshold per model) -> one error-analysis pass -> articles dev check (transfer only,
never re-tuned) -> freeze -> summary eval on the frozen prompts -> latency suite -> select -> holdout, run once
```

## 1. Objective and metrics

A wrong directional call costs a trade, a missed one costs little (Q2). So the positives are directional calls, and
neutral or an abstention is the safe default. Definitions follow
[`metrics.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/metrics.py):

- **Directional call**: an answered (not abstained) bullish or bearish prediction. An abstention is served as neutral
  with `abstained: true`. **Coverage** is the share of rows answered, **signal rate** the share with a directional
  call, **accuracy** the share whose served label (abstention -> neutral) equals gold.
- **Precision / recall** per class c in {bullish, bearish}: correct c calls / c calls and correct c calls / gold c
  rows. A class with no calls scores 0, not NaN, so "always neutral" scores F0.5 0.
- **F0.5 macro** (the selection metric): the mean of the two per-class F-beta scores at beta = 0.5, which weights
  precision above recall. Neutral is not a positive class.
- **Inversion rate**: bullish<->bearish flips (a directional call on a gold-directional row with the opposite label)
  over all directional calls. The cap is **2%**.
- **Operating point**: thresholds are swept over 0 and every distinct confidence value (the only points where calls
  change); the chosen point is the **max F0.5 among points with inversion <= 2%**, ties to higher coverage, then a
  lower threshold. A config with no point under the cap is "cap missed" and cannot be selected.
- **Prevalence weights** (dev300 only): each row weighs train prior / sample prior of its class, so rates estimate
  the real tweet mix; confusion and error counts stay raw. Articles and holdout sets are unweighted.
- **CIs**: 95% percentile bootstrap (B = 1,000, seed 20261018), resampled within each gold class, on the headline
  metrics only (F0.5 macro, inversion, coverage, signal rate, accuracy). Gaps between two configs on the same rows use
  a paired bootstrap. The threshold is not re-chosen per resample, so a CI at a tuned operating point is optimistic.

## 2. Datasets and splits

From the split headers in [`evals/data/splits/`](../../../evals/data/splits/) and [`stats.json`](../../../evals/data/articles/stats.json):

| split | source | role | n | bullish / bearish / neutral | weighting |
|---|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `dev300` | Twitter Financial News Sentiment (FNS), train | tuning: prompt grid, thresholds | 300 | 100 / 100 / 100 | train prior 20.2% / 15.1% / 64.7% |
| articles dev | Opus-labelled articles (section 3) | transfer check, error analysis, summary eval | 30 | 10 / 10 / 10 | none |
| articles test | Opus-labelled articles | holdout | 60 | 20 / 20 / 20 | none |
| `tfns_val` | Twitter FNS, validation | holdout, in-domain tweets | 2,388 | 475 / 347 / 1,566 | none (natural prior) |
| `fpb_allagree` | Financial PhraseBank, Sentences_AllAgree | holdout, cross-domain sentences | 2,259 | 570 / 303 / 1,386 | none |
| `finentity_single` | FinEntity, rows with one distinct label | holdout, cross-domain paragraphs | 851 | 181 / 180 / 490 | none |

- **dev300** comes from Twitter FNS train after dropping 69 rows whose normalised text is also in validation, 70
  duplicates and 4 rows with conflicting labels; then 100 per class with seed 20261018. Class weights are 0.605
  (bullish), 0.453 (bearish) and 1.942 (neutral). FPB and FinEntity positive / negative / neutral map to bullish /
  bearish / neutral; FPB collapses exact duplicates and drops sentences seen with two labels; FinEntity keeps rows
  with at least one entity annotation and exactly one distinct label.
- **Committed**: per split, the ids, the sha1 of the normalised text (NFKC, casefold, URLs and whitespace runs
  dropped), the labels, the selection rule and the dataset revision;
  [`datasets.lock.json`](../../../evals/data/datasets.lock.json) pins each dataset commit, file sha256 and licence. A
  split fails to load on a revision mismatch, a missing id, text-hash drift or label drift.
- **Never committed**: dataset text (FPB is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), downloaded at eval time into the gitignored
  `evals/data/private/`, along with article HTML, gold bodies, headlines, predictions, summaries and judge packets.

## 3. The Opus-labelled article set

Public datasets hold sentences and headlines; the service reads whole articles (Q5, R5). The set has 90 real articles
from the 10 sources in [`02-source-probe.md`](02-source-probe.md), 3 classes x 3 per source, published 2026-08-19 to
2026-10-18. One seeded article per (source, class) cell goes to dev: **30 dev / 60 test**. Two quota adjustments keep
the 30/30/30 balance (Yahoo 4 bearish, BBC 2 bearish). Every Opus step ran as a Claude Code subagent pinned to Claude Opus
5.5, so no API key or paid service was used. Prompts and runbook: [`evals/opus_prompts/`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/00-README.md).

1. **Discover** (one agent per source): candidates from RSS and section pages, fetched by the deterministic
   `articles` CLI through the serving fetcher; agents never fetch anything themselves.
2. **Gold**: Opus picks the body as line ranges of the page, writes 3-5 key facts in its own words, and gives a
   provisional label.
3. **Label A / label B**: two independent agents apply the service's rubric (economic impact on the primary entity,
   not tone; neutral when in doubt), never seeing each other's output or the provisional label.
4. **Adjudicate**: one agent reviews every article where the labels differ or either labeller flagged ambiguity, and
   either keeps it (its label is final) or replaces it as genuinely ambiguous.
5. **Refill and finalize**: short cells repeat steps 1-4; `finalize` picks per cell, agreed articles first; `verify`
   re-checks the set.

| pool statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| articles with a usable gold body | 298 |
| labelled by both labellers | 157 |
| labels agree | 151 (raw agreement 96.2%) |
| Cohen's kappa (A vs B) | 0.943 |
| sent to adjudication (6 disagreements, 43 agreed but flagged ambiguous) | 49 (31.2%) |
| replaced by the adjudicator | 24 of 49 (49.0%) |
| adjudicated articles kept in the final 90 | 5 |

In the final 90, A and B agree on every label (kappa 1.0), by construction since agreed articles are picked first, so
the pool agreement is the meaningful figure. The committed [`articles.jsonl`](../../../evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl)
holds ids, URLs, sources, dates, both labels, the adjudication, entity and ticker, and rationales and key facts in
Opus's words; the CLI rejects any that share 10 consecutive words with the article, so no article text is committed.
**Caveats**: Opus-only labels with no human check; replacing ambiguous articles makes the set cleaner than real
traffic; with 10 articles per class on dev, a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero.

## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` + `/summary`; the combined one `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells ([`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json)), all on
native Metal, Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0, sampling penalties neutralised; see the build-time
findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic shots =
  v1-v4; for `qwen3.5:0.8b` each runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: rubric or plain one-line question x described or bare criteria = v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the field-order
  check, on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): argmax of the native class probabilities; abstain when it is below `min_p`.
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): first label-token probabilities, renormalised over the tokens the grammar
  accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still yields the likelier
  directional class when that class holds p >= tau; below tau the row is a served neutral, not an abstention. On a
  first-token label collision the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streams, fallback): a score from -2 to 2, directional only when \|score\| >= t. It is read
  mid-stream as soon as it closes and needs no logprobs (Q3); logprob-weighted streaming confidence is on the backlog.

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default (headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200
tokens); `lede` and `full` are both scored on articles. `/analyze` reads `full` and emits the sentiment field first,
so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error analysis and freeze.** One hand-written read of the grid counts
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)) drove the changes listed in section 5. The `freeze`
command then wrote [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json) and
[`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml):

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze` takes v5
unless the whole paired 95% CI of its gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles, which rejected v5 for
`qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first needed a dev300 win without an articles loss; it never
got one.

## 5. Accuracy on dev

Frozen configs only. Articles use the dev300 threshold unchanged and the serving extraction (`selectolax` +
`cascade`). Sources: [`grid/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md),
[`articles_dev/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md).

**`/signal`** (dev300 weighted; articles lede is the served default):

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | articles lede F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. | articles full F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.914 / 0.918 | 0.0% | 100.0% | 15.4% | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 1/14 | 0.635 [0.329, 0.817] | 0/10 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.867 / 0.905 | 0.0% | 72.9% | 33.2% | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 1/20 | 0.907 [0.820, 0.989] | 0/20 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.948 / 0.891 | 0.0% | 26.3% | 24.2% | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 0/17 | 0.880 [0.761, 0.976] | 0/19 |

**`/analyze`** (full scope, sentiment-first, \|s\| >= 1, coverage 100% for all):

| model | config | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | P bull / P bear | inversion | signal rate | articles F0.5 [95% CI] | inv. |
|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | v1 | 0.752 [0.664, 0.834] | 0.877 / 0.821 | 0.0% | 21.4% | 0.880 [0.791, 0.989] | 0/22 |
| `ministral-3:3b` | v5 | 0.685 [0.589, 0.772] | 0.837 / 0.768 | 1.0% | 20.0% | 0.741 [0.611, 0.858] | 0/19 |
| `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | v5 | 0.647 [0.553, 0.741] | 0.702 / 0.752 | 0.0% | 23.1% | 0.779 [0.646, 0.879] | 1/22 |

No served rule clearly fails on the articles (whole inversion CI above 2%, or whole coverage CI below half the dev300
coverage), so every dev300 threshold stands. What the error analysis found
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md),
[`error_patterns.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/error_patterns.json)):

- **Inversions are nearly absent**: across the six best configs one tweet is inverted, by `ministral`. Wrong calls
  are mostly gold-neutral tweets called directional (2-8 per model). The real loss is recall: 34 (`clef-flash`) to
  118 (`qwen3.5:0.8b`) directional tweets missed; after the catch-all bucket, the largest miss bucket for every
  generative model is price-move tweets (33-38 of 57 directional ones missed, against 10 for `clef-flash`), which
  the impact rubric reads as immaterial.
- **`directional_tau` is the largest single lever**: `qwen3.5:0.8b` parks most of its mass on neutral, and the tau
  rule lifts its F0.5 by +0.218 [+0.141, +0.307] (paired). It loses for the peaked decision models (-0.046 and
  -0.303), so they keep the plain rule.
- **Other changes**: rubric A beats B for every generative model; shots help `qwen3.5:0.8b` on the label schema but
  hurt every `/analyze` model, so all frozen `/analyze` prompts are zero-shot; summary-first never wins and delays
  the score (2-3x on articles). The price-move rubric sentence was not added: articles do not show the tweet miss
  (0-1 of 5 directional price-move headlines missed).
- **Knob comparison**: without tau, the logprob knob beats the ordinal one on `qwen3.5:0.8b` by +0.059 [-0.068,
  +0.187], not significant; with tau it wins clearly. The ordinal schema cannot use tau, because this tokenizer fuses
  `" -"` and hides the sign of negative scores.

## 6. Summary evaluation

Decision R6, run by `veritrade_evals.summary_eval` on the stored HTML of the 30 dev articles through the serving
adapters (full scope, frozen prompts). Serving caps every summary at **3 sentences / 60 words** at a sentence
boundary, and the checks score the capped text.

- **Deterministic checks** (pass-rate gate >= 0.8): length, sentence count, every number grounded in the gold article
  (format-tolerant; a derived figure counts as unsupported), gold entity named, not truncated.
- **Key-fact coverage**: each Opus key fact and each summary sentence is embedded with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact
  is covered at a best cosine **>= 0.60** (primary), with 0.75 as the strict bound. In the hand-labelled spot check
  of 45 facts on 10 summaries ([`spotcheck.dev.json`](../../../evals/results/summary/spotcheck.dev.json)), 0.60
  matched 33 of 45 flags with 5 false "covered" and 0.55 matched 34 with 6, a near tie; 0.75 had no false "covered"
  but missed 20 stated facts (see the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`).
- **Opus judges**, blind: per article the candidate summaries are anonymised as `S1..Sn` and shuffled
  ([`50-judge.md`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md)); each gets faithfulness 1-5, coverage 1-5, a list of
  hallucinations, and whether it leads with the market-moving fact. **Material error rate** = share at
  faithfulness <= 3.

Dev articles, n = 30 per row ([`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)); length and sentence
count pass 100% by construction; CIs resample articles within their sentiment label.

**Hallucination flag vs material error.** The flag rate counts any summary with at least one entry in the judge's
hallucination list, including minor slips that still allow faithfulness 4 (a loosely worded or small unsupported
detail "a trader would shrug off"). The material error rate counts only faithfulness <= 3: a wrong key number, an
unsupported claim that matters, a misattribution, or worse. So `qwen3.5:4b` on `/summary` is flagged on half the
articles but has a material error on 10% [0%, 20%]; the material rate is the one to read as risk. The deterministic
number check agrees in direction: 1-3 unsupported numbers across 30 summaries for the qwen models, 8 for `ministral`.

## 7. Selection

Rules: [`selection/selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md). Accuracy filters come first (dev300
inversion <= 2%, articles dev not clearly over the cap, summary pass rate >= 0.8), then the native warm latency
budgets of R7 (measured in `05-latency.md`). Survivors rank on dev300 F0.5 then articles dev F0.5 (`/signal`,
`/analyze`) or on judge faithfulness then coverage (`/summary`). Budgets are reported, never moved; when nothing meets
one, the Pareto knee is used with the reason stated.

| endpoint | winner | deciding numbers | others |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (v2-label, tau 0.28) | only candidate inside the 500 ms lede budget: p50 178 ms, dev300 F0.5 0.730 | `clef-flash` 0.874 at 659 ms; `nimble` 0.843 at 1,061 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v2) | faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97, paired +0.43 [0.07, 0.77]; TTFT p50 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | `qwen3.5:2b` faster (484 / 1,272 ms), more material errors (30%) |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v1) | dev300 F0.5 0.752; TTFT p50 1,292 ms (limit 1,500), complete 2,584 ms | `ministral` 0.685; `qwen3-instruct` 0.647, though its summary faithfulness is best (4.73 vs 4.47, paired gap 0.27 [-0.07, 0.60], not significant) |

Bundled models (R8): `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` + `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, 4.34 GB against the 10 GB cap.

**The `/signal` trade-off.** `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874) but misses the 500 ms lede budget
(p50 659 ms), and its 10.58 GB file alone exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap. `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (0.843, 1,061 ms) misses
the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms: high dev300 precision (0.91 / 0.92), low
recall (it misses about half the directional articles on dev). The budget was not moved to fit the 9B models; both
stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native Ollama.

## 8. Holdout

Protocol of `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}` ([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)):

- Frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, no re-tuning, natural class priors (unweighted); a prompt that
  drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` = holdout F0.5 minus the dev F0.5 of the same rule (articles dev at
  the same scope for articles; dev300 for the tweet and cross-domain sets).
- 22 cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`; the three `/analyze`
  finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`; the two winners also on `fpb_allagree` and
  `finentity_single`; the `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. Then summaries from
  the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles go to the blind Opus judges.
- **Run once**: `evals/results/holdout_runs.json` is a guard keyed by the sha256 of
  `frozen.json`, recording the selection sha256, git sha, and start and completion times. An interrupted run resumes
  from its caches; a completed config refuses a second run unless `--force --reason` is passed, which is logged in
  the guard and must be disclosed. It also refuses a provisional selection (one made before the latency suite)
  without `--allow-provisional`; this selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` only re-scores the cached predictions and never calls a model; the tables below come from the
  `evals/results/holdout/holdout.md` it writes.

## 9. Threats to validity

- **One labeller family**: article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judges are all Claude Opus. Labellers
  were independent and judges blind, but a shared bias would not show, and no human checked any label.
- **Small n**: with 30 dev articles, the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5 (60 test articles in the
  holdout); article results check that rules transfer,
  they do not rank models.
- **Tuned on tweets**: thresholds and prompts were tuned on 300 tweets and only checked on articles; CIs at a tuned
  threshold exclude the threshold choice, and `directional_tau` is one more tuned parameter.
- **Class mix**: the article sets are balanced while real traffic is likely neutral-heavy (64.7% in Twitter FNS
  train), so per-call precision in production is likely below the article figure. dev300 reweights; articles do not.
- **Cleaner than reality**: 10 fetchable sources, a 60-day window, 24 ambiguous articles replaced; for three sources
  the extraction profiles were tuned with this set in view (caveats in `03-extraction.md`).
- **Contamination**: the public datasets may be in the models' pretraining data; the articles are recent, which
  limits but does not rule out overlap.
- **Precision first, by design**: the selected `/signal` model misses about half the directional articles; a miss is
  cheap under Q2, but users will see many neutrals.
- **Indicative parts**: grid and articles timings ran on a shared machine (selection uses the dedicated native-metal
  suite; Docker CPU is in `05-latency.md`), and the error-analysis keyword buckets are a first-match heuristic.
````

````markdown
# 00 - Overview

VeriTrade analysts lose minutes reading breaking news to gauge sentiment. This PoC takes a public financial-news
URL and returns a short summary plus a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal, optimised for latency and for
**precision of directional calls** (a wrong call costs a trade; a missed call costs little).

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

Two architectures are compared head to head:

- **Split**: a fast signal model (a decision model or a tiny LLM) answers `/signal` while a summariser streams
  `/summary` in parallel.
- **Combined**: one haiku-grade model produces score + summary in a single call (`/analyze`).

## Sources

Any public URL is accepted. The source profiles and the evaluation cover the final 10, chosen by a live probe
([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md), [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml)):
Yahoo Finance, CNBC, The Motley Fool, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune,
The Guardian Business and BBC Business. AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
their CDN and are rejected rather than evaded.

## Outcome

The defaults were picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal`
serves `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
bundled profile pulls just those two models, 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models score higher
(`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` dev300 F0.5 0.874, mostly through recall: its bullish / bearish precision is 0.867 / 0.905
against 0.914 / 0.918 for the 0.8B) but miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades recall
for speed, and the 9B models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Details:
[01 selection outcome](01-decisions.md#selection-outcome), [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).
````

````markdown
- **Single-flight fetch cache** (`veritrade.fetch.cache`): split mode fires `/signal` and `/summary` at once,
  and the second request joins the first one's in-flight download (`timings.cache.fetch` is `"joined"`), so

## docker-cpu

Docker Desktop cannot pass Apple's GPU into a Linux container (01, Q1), so the bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp on
CPU. `latency docker-cpu` measures the bundled defaults over HTTP (`/signal` 0.8B lede JSON; `/summary` and
`/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b`, SSE and JSON), warm n=10 per cell; the app fetches live, so fetch and consent are
subtracted, and it warms up on an 11th dev article.

Two earlier passes were discarded, and neither is committed:

1. **Pass 1 found a prompt-cache bias.** The bundled Ollama has no host port, so the native unload was not
   available, and each JSON cell re-sent the prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles;
   those rows showed prompt eval of 118 to 171 ms. Fix: a reload hook (`container_reload` in `latency.py`) runs
   `docker exec ... ollama stop <model>` before every warm phase and waits until `ollama ps` drops it,
   mirroring the native unload.
2. **Pass 2 was invalidated by host contention.** Unrelated workloads on the same Mac pushed the load average
   to 50-64 (6.9 at the native preflight). `qwen3.5:0.8b` decode went from about 31 ms/token to about
   2.8 s/token and 4 `/analyze` requests timed out. Root cause: the bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp with 14
   threads on a 14-vCPU Docker VM over a 14-core host, and its spin-barrier threads stall whenever the host
   takes cores, so CPU inference collapses instead of slowing in proportion.

Indicative only (pass-1 rows the cache bias did not touch, n=10, not committed):

| endpoint | model | transport | complete p50 | TTFT p50 | to signal p50 | x native (complete / TTFT / signal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` lede | JSON | 2,657 | - | - | 14.9x |
| /summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 14,405 | 8,768 | - | 6.6x / 7.8x |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 12,106 | 9,147 | 8,644 | 4.7x / 7.1x / 7.9x |

In pass 1, CPU-only Docker was roughly 5 to 15 times slower than Metal on this machine and would miss every
budget. That is why native Ollama is the macOS default and the bundled profile is for Linux and CI: a portability path, not
a latency path. `OLLAMA_CPUS` in `compose.yaml` sets a `cpus:` quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread
count, so a quota below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower rather than just capped; a cpuset
or `num_thread` is the fix (backlog). The re-run repeats pass 1's protocol, reload hook included, on a quiet
host, and its rows go in the `docker-cpu` section of `latency.md`.

<!-- PENDING:docker-cpu warm n=10 table from the quiet-host re-run (signal 0.8b lede JSON; summary and analyze qwen3.5:4b SSE and JSON): complete p50/p95, TTFT p50, time to signal p50, ratio to native, preflight load average -->

## Levers

Used:
- **Input and model size**: lede scope for `/signal` (half the tokens of full, p95 195 ms instead of 532); a
  cascade that sends about 720 `full` tokens where `strip-tags` sends about 2,100 (03); the smallest `/signal`
  model that clears the accuracy filters, answering in 7 tokens.
- **Perceived latency**: SSE, sentiment-first field order and an incremental JSON scanner.
- **Warm models**: `keep_alive` 30m on every call; `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` 3 native (2 bundled) keeps both
  split-mode models resident; flash attention and a q8_0 KV cache in the Ollama env.
- **Bounded generation**: `think: false`, greedy decoding, per-endpoint `num_predict`, and the served summary
  cap of 3 sentences / 60 words (01).
- **Network and hops**: pooled HTTP/2, single-flight fetch cache, result cache, consent cookie reuse; the UI is
  served by the same FastAPI process (R1), and the fast parsers extract inline, without a thread hand-off.

Left: the latency items in [90-optional-backlog.md](90-optional-backlog.md) (progressive `/signal`, split-mode
concurrency, a GPU compose profile, CPU threads for the bundled Ollama, latency under load), plus:
- Preload the default models at app start, so the first request does not pay 0.7 to 1.3 s of load.
- Trim the 4B prompts: prompt eval is half of `/summary` and nearly all of its TTFT.
- Start the fetch when a URL is pasted, before submit, to hide part of the network cost.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency preflight   # records the machine; fails while Docker containers run
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency run         # native suite, resumable; writes latency.{json,md}
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency docker-cpu --base-url http://localhost:8000   # bundled stack up first
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency report      # re-aggregates the raw samples
```

The native run needs the private article HTML (`articles verify` passes) and an otherwise idle machine.
````

"""Hygiene checks for a design doc: dashes, home paths, emails, emojis, broken relative links, PENDING lines."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

doc = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
lines = text.splitlines()
print("lines", len(lines))

for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
    if "—" in line or "–" in line:
        print(f"dash at {i}")
    if "~" in line or "/private/" in line:
        print(f"home path at {i}")
    if re.search(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+", line):
        print(f"email-like at {i}: {line.strip()[:80]}")
    if re.search(r"[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF☀-➿]", line):
        print(f"emoji at {i}")
    if "PENDING" in line:
        ok = re.fullmatch(r"<!-- PENDING:(holdout|docker-cpu) [^\n]+ -->", line)
        print(f"pending at {i}: {'ok' if ok else 'MALFORMED'}")

for target in re.findall(r"\]\(([^)#]+)\)", text):
    if target.startswith("http"):
        continue
    resolved = (doc.parent / target).resolve()
    if not resolved.exists():
        print(f"missing link target: {target}")
"""Report relative markdown links in the given files whose targets do not exist."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)#\s]+)(?:#[^)]*)?\)")

missing = 0
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    doc = Path(name).resolve()
    for target in LINK.findall(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        if "://" in target:
            continue
        path = (doc.parent / target).resolve()
        status = "ok" if path.exists() else "MISSING"
        missing += status == "MISSING"
        print(f"{status:7s} {target}")
sys.exit(1 if missing else 0)
"""Check every relative link and #anchor in a markdown file against GitHub-style heading slugs."""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(([^)\s]*)\)")
FENCE = re.compile(r"^```")


def slugs(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    out: set[str] = set()
    in_code = False
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if FENCE.match(line):
            in_code = not in_code
            continue
        if in_code or not line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        text = line.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
        text = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text)
        out.add(text.replace(" ", "-"))
    return out


doc = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
bad = 0
for target in LINK.findall(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
    if "://" in target or not target:
        continue
    file_part, _, anchor = target.partition("#")
    path = (doc.parent / file_part).resolve() if file_part else doc
    if not path.exists():
        print(f"MISSING FILE {target}")
        bad += 1
        continue
    if anchor and path.suffix == ".md" and anchor not in slugs(path):
        print(f"MISSING ANCHOR {target}")
        bad += 1
print("bad links:", bad)

```python
"""Print raw counts behind each holdout rate: directional calls, inversions, abstentions, CIs, dev reference."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
print("top keys:", list(data))

for row in data["rows"]:
    m = row["metrics"]
    conf = m["confusion"]
    cols, golds, counts = conf["columns_pred"], conf["rows_gold"], conf["counts"]
    c = {g: dict(zip(cols, r)) for g, r in zip(golds, counts)}
    calls = sum(c[g]["bullish"] + c[g]["bearish"] for g in golds)
    inv = c["bullish"]["bearish"] + c["bearish"]["bullish"]
    abst = sum(c[g]["abstain"] for g in golds)
    ci = row["cis"]
    print(
        f"{row['key']}: n={row['n']} f05={m['f05_macro']} "
        f"[{ci['f05_macro']['low']}, {ci['f05_macro']['high']}] "
        f"inv={inv}/{calls} ({m['inversion_rate']}) inv_ci=[{ci['inversion_rate']['low']}, {ci['inversion_rate']['high']}] "
        f"abstain={abst} cov={m['coverage']} cov_ci=[{ci['coverage']['low']}, {ci['coverage']['high']}] "
        f"correct_bull={c['bullish']['bullish']}/{c['bullish']['bullish'] + c['bullish']['bearish'] + c['bullish']['neutral'] + c['bullish']['abstain']} "
        f"correct_bear={c['bearish']['bearish']} "
        f"dev={row.get('dev')} gap={row.get('gap')} ref={row.get('reference')} errors={row['counts']['errors']}"
    )

for key in data:
    if key in ("rows", "guard"):
        continue
    val = data[key]
    if isinstance(val, (dict, list)):
        print(key, "->", json.dumps(val)[:3000])
```

```
# Model selection

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` from committed results; numbers only.

## Rules

- **signal**: Candidates: the frozen /signal configs at the default lede scope. Filters: dev300 inversion rate <= 2% at the frozen operating point (n=300); the articles dev set must not fail the cap, meaning the 95% CI of its inversion rate reaches down to 2% (the freeze's clear-failure rule: at n=30 one inversion is about 5% of the calls); warm native p50 excluding fetch <= 500 ms at lede. Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro (primary, n=300), then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **analyze**: Candidates: the frozen /analyze configs (full scope, ordinal |score| >= t, sentiment-first). Filters: the same inversion rules as /signal; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s (warm, native, excluding fetch). Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro, then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **summary**: Candidates: the frozen /summary models. Filter: deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 on the dev articles; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s. Rank: Opus judge faithfulness, then judge coverage, then key-fact coverage (key-fact coverage leads while the judge is pending).
- **winner**: The best-ranked candidate inside every filter. When no accuracy-eligible candidate meets its latency budget, the Pareto knee (metrics.knee) of quality against budget utilisation (the worst measured metric divided by its limit) among the measured candidates, with the reason stated.
- **bundle**: R8: the per-endpoint winners when their model files total <= 10 GB (decimal), else the combination of accuracy-eligible candidates that fits with the fewest rank steps away from the winners (ties: signal, then summary, then analyze keeps its better pick; then the smaller total).

# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.
```

```
## Quickstart

Requirements: Docker with Compose 2.20 or later (the `docker compose` plugin), Homebrew for the macOS default, and
----
  `evals/data/private/`, which publisher rights keep out of the repo, so for those a clone can only read the
  committed results.

Summary quality of the served pair on the dev (n = 30) and test (n = 60) articles:

| Articles | Endpoint, model | Checks pass | Numbers grounded | Key facts (0.60) | Opus faithfulness [95% CI] | Coverage | Hallucination flag | Material errors [95% CI] |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|---|
| dev | `/summary`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 47% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] |
| dev | `/analyze`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 57% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] |
| test | `/summary`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 58% | 4.37 [4.17, 4.57] | 4.50 | 42% | 17% [7%, 27%] |
| test | `/analyze`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 92% | 95% | 63% | 4.17 [3.97, 4.37] | 4.63 | 52% | 25% [15%, 35%] |

The hallucination flag counts any unsupported detail, minor slips included; a material error is faithfulness <= 3
(a wrong key number, an unsupported claim that matters). The `/summary` runner-up, `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, is faster
(TTFT 484 ms) but scores 3.97 on dev with 30% material errors, so the 4B serves both summary endpoints. On the
unseen test articles `/summary` holds its faithfulness, while `/analyze` summaries degrade (15 of 60 with a material
error) and the served 60-word cap shortened 25% of them.

**Holdout.** The frozen configs ran once, on 2026-10-19, with `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` as an untuned quality ceiling, and
six blind Opus judges scored the winners' test summaries (above). Ollama hung mid-run and was restarted; the run
resumed from its caches, as the guard records, and every cell finished with 0 errors. Nothing was re-tuned and the
defaults stay as frozen ([`holdout.md`](evals/results/holdout/holdout.md),
[protocol](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#8-holdout)). F0.5 [95% CI], inversion rate and gap to dev (articles
dev, else dev300); coverage is 100% in every cell:

| Test set (n) | `/signal` `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (lede) | `/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Articles (60) | 0.801 [0.668, 0.886], 3.3%, +0.117 | 0.871 [0.804, 0.940], 0.0%, -0.009 | 0.814 [0.759, 0.880], 2.0% |
| `tfns_val` tweets (2,388) | 0.648 [0.612, 0.679], 0.5%, -0.082 | 0.662 [0.631, 0.690], 0.8%, -0.090 | - |
| `fpb_allagree` sentences (2,259) | 0.700 [0.669, 0.728], 1.0%, -0.030 | 0.940 [0.928, 0.952], 0.1%, +0.188 | 0.932 [0.919, 0.945], 0.2% |
| `finentity_single` paragraphs (851) | 0.711 [0.672, 0.749], 0.0%, -0.019 | 0.760 [0.727, 0.794], 1.7%, +0.008 | 0.692 [0.661, 0.723], 1.2% |

`/analyze` generalises best; its FPB jump only means AllAgree sentences are unambiguous by construction (that gap
compares domains). The untuned 9B beats the 4B nowhere: no sign the 4B leaves quality on the table at this prompt,
and a floor for the 9B, not its best. Tweets run 0.03-0.09 below dev300 for every model, the winner's curse of
tuning on 300 dev tweets.

## Testing

| Layer | Where | What it guards |
|---|---|---|
----

- **One model family labels and judges.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
  from Claude Opus with no human check; the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5 on 30 dev articles and
  0.14-0.25 on 60 test articles.
- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles and 26 of 40 test ones
  (bearish recall 0.40 on both), so users will see many neutrals; the 9B decision models catch more but miss the
  latency budget.
- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** The `/signal` default inverts 1 of its 14 directional calls on the
  dev articles (7.1% against the 2% cap) and 1 of 30 on the test articles (3.3%, 95% CI 0% to 10.3%). Selection let
  it through because the dev CI at n=30 reaches 0%; the holdout does not clear that doubt, though on 2,388 tweets it
  inverts 2 of 386 calls (0.5%) ([`holdout.md`](evals/results/holdout/holdout.md)).
- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets, and every model scores 0.03-0.09 F0.5 lower on
  the 2,388 held-out ones; real traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely below the balanced
  article figures ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev and
  42% of test summaries, and a material error in 10% [0%, 20%] and 17% [7%, 27%]; `/analyze` summaries degrade on
  unseen articles, to 25% [15%, 35%] material errors (10% on dev). Numbers are not re-checked at serve time.
- **Latency is one machine at concurrency 1.** Tails exceed the budgets, split mode's concurrent pair and multi-user
  load were not measured, and the docker-cpu figures are indicative.
- **Coverage and hardening.** 10 profiled English sources (others fall back to JSON-LD and density, unmeasured),
  no PDFs; no authentication or inbound rate limiting, and the caches are in-process (per replica).

Next, from [`90-optional-backlog.md`](.context/docs/design/90-optional-backlog.md): a DSPy-style prompt optimiser;
distilling the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier; a progressive `/signal` that upgrades the 0.8B verdict
when a 9B model answers; analysing articles on publish; serving the number-grounding check; a GPU compose profile.
```

```diff
 ## Limitations and next steps
 
 - **One model family labels and judges.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
-  from Claude Opus with no human check, and with 30 dev articles the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5.
-- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles, so users will see many
-  neutrals; the 9B decision models catch more but miss the latency budget.
-- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** On the 30 dev articles the `/signal` default inverts 1 of its 14
-  directional calls (7.1% against the 2% cap); selection passes it only because the 95% CI at n=30 reaches 0%, so
-  the holdout is the real check ([`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
-- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets and checked on balanced article sets; real
-  traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely lower ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
-- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev
-  summaries and a material error in 10% [0%, 20%]; numbers are not re-checked against the source at serve time.
```

```diff
+  articles (7.1% against the 2% cap) and 1 of 30 on test (3.3%, 95% CI 0% to 10.3%); selection let it through as the
+  dev CI at n=30 reaches 0%, and the holdout does not clear that doubt ([`holdout.md`](evals/results/holdout/holdout.md)).
```

```python
"""List numbers on added diff lines that appear in none of the source files, for manual review."""

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SOURCES = [
    "evals/results/holdout/holdout.md",
    "evals/results/holdout/holdout.json",
    "evals/results/summary/summary.md",
    "evals/results/selection/selection.md",
    "evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md",
    "evals/results/holdout_runs.json",
]
NUM = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?%?")

corpus = " ".join(Path(s).read_text(encoding="utf-8") for s in SOURCES)
for doc in sys.argv[1:]:
    corpus += " " + subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"HEAD:{doc}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
known = set(NUM.findall(corpus)) | {n.rstrip("%") for n in NUM.findall(corpus)}

for doc in sys.argv[1:]:
    diff = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "-U0", "--", doc], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("+") or line.startswith("+++"):
            continue
        for tok in NUM.findall(line):
            bare = tok.lstrip("+-").rstrip("%")
            if tok in known or bare in known or tok.lstrip("+-") in known:
                continue
            print(f"{doc}: {tok!r} in: {line[:110]}")

```
```
## 8. Holdout

Protocol of `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}` ([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)):

- Frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, no re-tuning, natural class priors (unweighted); a prompt that
  drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` = holdout F0.5 minus the dev F0.5 of the same rule (articles dev at
  the same scope for articles; dev300 for the tweet and cross-domain sets).
- 22 cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`; the three `/analyze`
  finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`; the two winners also on `fpb_allagree` and
  `finentity_single`; the `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. Then summaries from
  the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles go to the blind Opus judges.
- **Run once**: [`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) is a guard keyed by the sha256 of
  `frozen.json`, recording the selection sha256, git sha, and start and completion times. An interrupted run resumes
  from its caches; a completed config refuses a second run unless `--force --reason` is passed, which is logged in
  the guard and must be disclosed. It also refuses a provisional selection (one made before the latency suite)
  without `--allow-provisional`; this selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` only re-scores the cached predictions and never calls a model; the tables below come from the
  [`holdout.md`](../../../evals/results/holdout/holdout.md) it writes, and the summary rows from the test split of
  [`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md).

**The run.** It ran once, on 2026-10-19 from 05:57 to 10:03 UTC, over all 22 cells
([`manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout/manifest.json)). Mid-run the native Ollama server hung: every
`/api/chat` call timed out after 90 s, which hit 21 rows of one cell (`/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b` on `fpb_allagree`).
The run was stopped, Ollama restarted with the same service environment, and the run resumed from its caches; the
timeouts are retryable errors, so the resume re-ran those 21 rows and their answers replaced the errors. Every cell
finished with 0 errors, and the guard records the one resume and no `--force`. Six blind Opus judges then scored
the 60 test summaries per endpoint (10 articles each, labels anonymised); their output was validated, de-blinded and
ingested. Nothing was re-tuned on these numbers, and the selected defaults stay as frozen.

### Holdout results

The frozen rules mostly hold. On the test articles no rule loses more than 0.043 F0.5 against its articles dev
figure (gaps -0.043 to +0.129), and no coverage CI falls below half its dev300 coverage. The 2% inversion cap holds
on every tweet and cross-domain set (0.0-1.7%) but not on the articles as a point estimate: the `/signal` default
inverts 1 of 30 calls (3.3%), `clef-flash` lede 1 of 44 (2.3%) and `ministral` 2 of 45 (4.4%). Each of those CIs
reaches 0%, so none clearly fails by the freeze rule, but the `/signal` default's doubt from dev (1 of 14) is not
cleared. On 2,388 tweets every model lands 0.03-0.09 F0.5 below dev300.

----
  (0.752 vs 0.730).

**Holdout check.** The frozen configs ran once, on 2026-10-19, on the test splits (`articles_test`, `tfns_val`,
`fpb_allagree`, `finentity_single`), with `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` as a holdout-only quality ceiling, and six blind Opus
judges scored the winners' summaries on the 60 test articles. Mid-run the native Ollama server hung (21 timed-out
rows in one cell); it was restarted with the same service environment and the run resumed from its caches, which
[`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) records, and every cell finished with 0 errors.
Nothing was re-tuned on these numbers and the defaults stay as frozen. Full tables:
[04-evals.md](04-evals.md#holdout-results), [`holdout.md`](../../../evals/results/holdout/holdout.md).

| Default | Test articles F0.5 [95% CI], inversions | Articles dev | `tfns_val` F0.5 [95% CI], inversions | dev300 | `fpb_allagree` / `finentity_single` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0`, lede | 0.801 [0.668, 0.886], 1/30 (3.3%) | 0.685, 1/14 | 0.648 [0.612, 0.679], 2/386 (0.5%) | 0.730, 0.0% | 0.700 / 0.711 |
| `/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, full | 0.871 [0.804, 0.940], 0/42 | 0.880, 0/22 | 0.662 [0.631, 0.690], 4/527 (0.8%) | 0.752, 0.0% | 0.940 / 0.760 |
| `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M`, untuned ceiling | 0.814 [0.759, 0.880], 1/51 (2.0%) | - | - | - | 0.932 / 0.692 |

| Summaries, test (dev) | Opus faithfulness [95% CI] | Coverage | Material errors [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/summary` `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 4.37 [4.17, 4.57] (4.40) | 4.50 (4.57) | 17% [7%, 27%] (10%) |
| `/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 4.17 [3.97, 4.37] (4.47) | 4.63 (4.63) | 25% [15%, 35%] (10%) |

- **`/signal`**: F0.5 is higher than on dev, but the inversion point estimate is above the 2% cap again and bearish
  recall is 0.40 on both sets. Selection let it through because the articles-dev CI at n=30 reached 0%; the test
  result does not clear that doubt. On tweets and the cross-domain sets it stays under the cap (0.0-1.0%).
- **`/analyze`** generalises best of the served defaults: 0.871 against 0.880, no inversions. Its FPB 0.940 is far
  above dev300 because AllAgree sentences are unambiguous by construction; that gap compares domains and is not an
  improvement. On FinEntity it scores 0.760 against the 0.8B's 0.711.
- **Tweets**: every model, finalists included, lands 0.03-0.09 F0.5 below dev300, the expected optimism of picking
  prompts and thresholds on 300 dev tweets; each endpoint's dev300 leader still leads. The 9B decision models keep
  their accuracy lead (test articles 0.859 lede for both, 0.896 full for `nimble`; tweets 0.783 / 0.755 against
  0.648) and still miss the latency budget, so the `/signal` trade-off above stands.
- **The 9B ceiling** beats the 4B nowhere (0.814 vs 0.871 on articles, 0.692 vs 0.760 on FinEntity, a tie on FPB):
  no evidence the 4B leaves quality on the table at this prompt. It is untuned, so this is a floor for the 9B.
- **Summaries**: `/summary` holds on unseen articles; `/analyze` summaries degrade (faithfulness 4.17, 15 of 60 with
  a material error), and the served length cap shortened 25% of them
  ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)).
```

```markdown
# Summary evaluation

Decision R6: deterministic checks, key-fact coverage by a local embedding model, and Claude Opus as a
blind judge. Summaries come from the serving adapters (`/api/summary`, `/api/analyze`) with the default
`selectolax` + `cascade` extraction and `full` scope, run on the stored HTML of the Opus article set.
Written by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.summary_eval report`; no article or summary text is committed.
Every check scores the served summary: serving caps it at 3 sentences and 60 words
(`cap_summary` in `veritrade.inference.adapters`), and `score` applies the same cap to cached generations.

- **Halluc.** (`hallucinationRate`): share of summaries with any unsupported detail, minor slips included.
- **Material** (`materialErrorRate`): share at faithfulness <= 3: a material error.

## Definitions

- **Pass**: <= 60 words, <= 3 sentences (serving sentence splitter), every number
  grounded, entity named, not truncated. Rates are over all articles; a candidate that produced no summary
  fails every check. Length holds by construction for served summaries; **Capped** is the share the cap
  had to shorten (whole leading sentences kept; an overlong first sentence ends in an ellipsis).
- **Numbers**: every number in the summary appears in the gold title or body. Thousands separators, `%`,
  currency symbols and units are ignored and 1.50 equals 1.5; number words up to twenty in the article
  ground their digits; Q1-Q4 / H1-H2 match the same token, `third quarter` / `first half`, `September
  quarter` or `July to September` (calendar quarters); `FY27` matches 2027; `80K` matches 80,000 (K/M/B
  abbreviations); a clock time on the hour (`5:00 p.m.`) matches the bare hour (`5PM`). Derived figures
  (a percentage change the model computed) count as unsupported: the prompt asks for verbatim numbers.
- **Entity**: the gold entity appears (case-insensitive, whole words); or its short name, without legal
  suffixes (Inc, Corp, Ltd, plc, Holdings, Group, ...) and trailing descriptors (Entertainment,
  Technologies, Industries, ...), as a phrase or as all its words anywhere (`UK ... economy`); or its first
  word when the name has several words and that word has 4+ letters and is not generic (American, United,
  Bank, ...); or the gold ticker (case-sensitive, also without an exchange suffix such as `.HK`).
- **Truncated**: the output hit `num_predict` and the serving path cut it to its last full sentence.
- **Key facts**: each of the 3-5 Opus key facts and each summary sentence is embedded with
  `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact is covered when its best cosine is >= 0.60, the threshold
  that agreed best with hand labels in the spot check. Mean share per article. **Key facts (strict)** uses
  0.75, where every flagged fact was really stated: a conservative lower bound.
- **Faithful / Cover**: Opus judge scores 1-5 (`evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md`), candidates anonymised and
  shuffled per article. **Halluc.** and **Material** are defined at the top: a minor slip such as a
  loosely worded detail counts towards the first only. **Leads**: share the judge found leading with the
  market-moving fact.
```

```diff
 ## Limitations and next steps
 
 - **One model family labels and judges.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
-  from Claude Opus with no human check, and with 30 dev articles the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5.
-- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles, so users will see many
-  neutrals; the 9B decision models catch more but miss the latency budget.
-- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** On the 30 dev articles the `/signal` default inverts 1 of its 14
-  directional calls (7.1% against the 2% cap); selection passes it only because the 95% CI at n=30 reaches 0%, so
-  the holdout is the real check ([`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
-- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets and checked on balanced article sets; real
-  traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely lower ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
-- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev
-  summaries and a material error in 10% [0%, 20%]; numbers are not re-checked against the source at serve time.
+  from Claude Opus with no human check; served-rule CIs span 0.2-0.5 F0.5 on 30 dev and 0.14-0.25 on 60 test articles.

+- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** The `/signal` default inverts 1 of 14 directional calls on dev
+  articles (7.1% against the 2% cap) and 1 of 30 on test (3.3%, 95% CI 0% to 10.3%); selection let it through as the
+  dev CI at n=30 reaches 0%, and the holdout does not clear that doubt ([`holdout.md`](evals/results/holdout/holdout.md)).
+- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets, and every model scores 0.03-0.09 F0.5 lower on
+  the 2,388 held-out ones; real traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely below the balanced
+  article figures ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
+- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev and

+  unseen articles, to 25% [15%, 35%] material errors (10% on dev). Numbers are not re-checked at serve time.
 - **Latency is one machine at concurrency 1.** Tails exceed the budgets, split mode's concurrent pair and multi-user
   load were not measured, and the docker-cpu figures are indicative.
```

```markdown
# Model selection

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` from committed results; numbers only.

## Rules

- **signal**: Candidates: the frozen /signal configs at the default lede scope. Filters: dev300 inversion rate <= 2% at the frozen operating point (n=300); the articles dev set must not fail the cap, meaning the 95% CI of its inversion rate reaches down to 2% (the freeze's clear-failure rule: at n=30 one inversion is about 5% of the calls); warm native p50 excluding fetch <= 500 ms at lede. Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro (primary, n=300), then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **analyze**: Candidates: the frozen /analyze configs (full scope, ordinal |score| >= t, sentiment-first). Filters: the same inversion rules as /signal; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s (warm, native, excluding fetch). Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro, then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **summary**: Candidates: the frozen /summary models. Filter: deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 on the dev articles; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s. Rank: Opus judge faithfulness, then judge coverage, then key-fact coverage (key-fact coverage leads while the judge is pending).
- **winner**: The best-ranked candidate inside every filter. When no accuracy-eligible candidate meets its latency budget, the Pareto knee (metrics.knee) of quality against budget utilisation (the worst measured metric divided by its limit) among the measured candidates, with the reason stated.
- **bundle**: R8: the per-endpoint winners when their model files total <= 10 GB (decimal), else the combination of accuracy-eligible candidates that fits with the fewest rank steps away from the winners (ties: signal, then summary, then analyze keeps its better pick; then the smaller total).

## /signal: `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (inside-budget)
```

```markdown
# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.

## Notes

Hand-written after reading the tables above; counts and my own descriptions only, no article text. With 10
articles per class, read these as a check that the dev300 operating points transfer, not as a ranking.

**Every served rule holds.** No served rule clearly fails (no inversion CI above the 2% cap, no coverage
collapse), so every dev300 threshold is frozen as tuned and nothing was re-picked on the articles.

**/signal.**
- clef-flash v4 at p >= 0.80 scores F0.5 0.848 on the lede and 0.907 on the full body, close to its dev300
  0.874. It makes one inversion in 20 calls on the lede and none on the full body.
- nimble v1 at p >= 0.97 answers far more articles than tweets (coverage 60-67% against 26% on dev300) at
  F0.5 0.88-0.90: articles state their news more plainly than tweets, so the peaked model is sure more often.
- qwen3.5:0.8b with `directional_tau` 0.28 scores 0.685 on the lede against 0.595 for the plain rule (a tie
  at n=30); on the full body the tau rule wins clearly (+0.229 [+0.022, +0.560]). It still misses about half
  the directional articles, so it remains the fast, low-recall option.
- Lede vs full is a tie for all three models; the lede (the /signal default) is two to three times faster.

**/analyze.**
- Articles are easier than tweets for every generative model: qwen3.5:4b v1 0.880, qwen3-instruct 0.798 and
  ministral 0.741, against 0.75 / 0.66 / 0.66 on dev300.
- The tightened summary rule (v5) changes no ministral call, costs qwen3-instruct one (a tie), and costs
  qwen3.5:4b two bullish and one bearish article plus one false alarm (-0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). It therefore
  keeps v1 for /analyze; its /summary endpoint still gets the tightened summary prompt.
- Summary-first is a tie on the articles (qwen3.5:4b -0.013, ministral +0.058) and never wins on dev300,
  while its time to the score is two to three times longer. Every model stays sentiment-first.
- The wrong calls are mostly neutral articles called directional (3-5 of the 10 per model, mostly bullish).
  Price-move headlines are not the problem they were on tweets (0-1 of the 5 directional ones missed per
  model), so the price-move / analyst-action rubric sentence was not added.
```

```
# Signal grid on dev300

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.grid analyze` from the local prediction cache; no dataset text is stored here.

- Data: dev300, 300 Twitter Financial News train tweets, 100 per class; every rate is weighted back to the train prior (bullish 20.2%, bearish 15.1%, neutral 64.7%). Confusion and error counts are raw.
- Selection: F0.5 macro over bullish/bearish; operating point = best F0.5 with bullish<->bearish inversions <= 2% of directional calls; below the threshold the call abstains to neutral.
- Policies: decision models threshold native class probabilities (min_p); generative /signal thresholds first-token label probabilities (label schema) or the |score| of an ordinal -2..2 schema (t in {1, 2}); both probability policies are also swept with the served `directional_tau` rule (min_p 0, see below); /analyze is streamed sentiment-first and always uses |score|.
- Decoding: Ollama options temperature=0, seed=0, presence_penalty=0, frequency_penalty=0, repeat_penalty=1 on every generative call (greedy; overrides the penalties some Modelfiles ship).
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000) at the chosen threshold; the threshold choice itself is not resampled, so these are optimistic.
- Latency: per-call wall ms during the grid run (Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal, warm, client concurrency 1); /analyze is time to the score with the stream stopped there. Indicative only: the latency suite runs separately.

## Best config per model

| endpoint | model | config | policy | threshold | F0.5 macro [95% CI] | P bull | P bear | inversion | coverage | signal rate | p50 ms | p95 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | v2-label | label-logprob+tau | tau 0.28 | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.914 | 0.918 | 0.0% | 100.0% | 15.4% | 209 | 322 |
| /signal | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | v4 | probability | p >= 0.8 | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.867 | 0.905 | 0.0% | 72.9% | 33.2% | 468 | 564 |
```

```markdown
## 6. Summary evaluation

Decision R6, run by `veritrade_evals.summary_eval` on the stored HTML of the 30 dev articles through the serving
adapters (full scope, frozen prompts). Serving caps every summary at **3 sentences / 60 words** at a sentence
boundary, and the checks score the capped text.

- **Deterministic checks** (pass-rate gate >= 0.8): length, sentence count, every number grounded in the gold article
  (format-tolerant; a derived figure counts as unsupported), gold entity named, not truncated.
- **Key-fact coverage**: each Opus key fact and each summary sentence is embedded with `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`; a fact
  is covered at a best cosine **>= 0.60** (primary), with 0.75 as the strict bound. In the hand-labelled spot check
  of 45 facts on 10 summaries ([`spotcheck.dev.json`](../../../evals/results/summary/spotcheck.dev.json)), 0.60
  matched 33 of 45 flags with 5 false "covered" and 0.55 matched 34 with 6, a near tie; 0.75 had no false "covered"
  but missed 20 stated facts (see the build-time findings in `01-decisions.md`).
- **Opus judges**, blind: per article the candidate summaries are anonymised as `S1..Sn` and shuffled
  ([`50-judge.md`](../../../evals/opus_prompts/50-judge.md)); each gets faithfulness 1-5, coverage 1-5, a list of
  hallucinations, and whether it leads with the market-moving fact. **Material error rate** = share at
  faithfulness <= 3.

Dev articles, n = 30 per row ([`summary/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)); length and sentence
count pass 100% by construction; CIs resample articles within their sentiment label.

| endpoint | model | pass | numbers | entity | key facts 0.60 / 0.75 | faithful [95% CI] | cover | halluc. flag | material [95% CI] | leads |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| summary | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 97% | 93% | 52% / 24% | 3.97 [3.67, 4.23] | 4.30 | 67% | 30% [17%, 47%] | 90% |
| summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 90% | 93% | 97% | 47% / 23% | 4.40 [4.17, 4.60] | 4.57 | 50% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 93% | 97% | 97% | 57% / 29% | 4.47 [4.20, 4.70] | 4.63 | 40% | 10% [0%, 20%] | 100% |
| analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 90% | 90% | 100% | 56% / 25% | 4.73 [4.53, 4.93] | 4.43 | 20% | 7% [0%, 17%] | 83% |
| analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | 77% | 80% | 97% | 45% / 19% | 3.77 [3.37, 4.20] | 4.27 | 63% | 40% [23%, 57%] | 80% |

**Hallucination flag vs material error.** The flag rate counts any summary with at least one entry in the judge's
hallucination list, including minor slips that still allow faithfulness 4 (a loosely worded or small unsupported
detail "a trader would shrug off"). The material error rate counts only faithfulness <= 3: a wrong key number, an
unsupported claim that matters, a misattribution, or worse. So `qwen3.5:4b` on `/summary` is flagged on half the
articles but has a material error on 10% [0%, 20%]; the material rate is the one to read as risk. The deterministic
number check agrees in direction: 1-3 unsupported numbers across 30 summaries for the qwen models, 8 for `ministral`.

## 7. Selection

Rules: [`selection/selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md). Accuracy filters come first (dev300
inversion <= 2%, articles dev not clearly over the cap, summary pass rate >= 0.8), then the native warm latency
budgets of R7 (measured in `05-latency.md`). Survivors rank on dev300 F0.5 then articles dev F0.5 (`/signal`,
`/analyze`) or on judge faithfulness then coverage (`/summary`). Budgets are reported, never moved; when nothing meets
one, the Pareto knee is used with the reason stated.

| endpoint | winner | deciding numbers | others |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (v2-label, tau 0.28) | only candidate inside the 500 ms lede budget: p50 178 ms, dev300 F0.5 0.730 | `clef-flash` 0.874 at 659 ms; `nimble` 0.843 at 1,061 ms |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v2) | faithfulness 4.40 vs 3.97, paired +0.43 [0.07, 0.77]; TTFT p50 1,128 ms, complete 2,199 ms | `qwen3.5:2b` faster (484 / 1,272 ms), more material errors (30%) |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (v1) | dev300 F0.5 0.752; TTFT p50 1,292 ms (limit 1,500), complete 2,584 ms | `ministral` 0.685; `qwen3-instruct` 0.647, though its summary faithfulness is best (4.73 vs 4.47, paired gap 0.27 [-0.07, 0.60], not significant) |

Bundled models (R8): `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` + `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, 4.34 GB against the 10 GB cap.

**The `/signal` trade-off.** `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` has the best dev300 F0.5 (0.874) but misses the 500 ms lede budget
(p50 659 ms), and its 10.58 GB file alone exceeds the 10 GB bundle cap. `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` (0.843, 1,061 ms) misses
the budget too. The selected `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` scores 0.730 at 178 ms: high dev300 precision (0.91 / 0.92), low
recall (it misses about half the directional articles on dev). The budget was not moved to fit the 9B models; both
stay on the allowlist and can be chosen per request with the `model` parameter on native Ollama. The holdout keeps
this picture: the 9B models still lead on the test articles and tweets ([section 8](#holdout-results)).

## 8. Holdout

Protocol of `uv run python -m veritrade_evals holdout {plan,run,analyze}` ([`holdout.py`](../../../evals/src/veritrade_evals/holdout.py)):

- Frozen rules at their frozen thresholds and prompts, no re-tuning, natural class priors (unweighted); a prompt that
  drifted since the freeze fails the run. `gap` = holdout F0.5 minus the dev F0.5 of the same rule (articles dev at
  the same scope for articles; dev300 for the tweet and cross-domain sets).
- 22 cells: the three `/signal` finalists on the test articles (lede and full) and `tfns_val`; the three `/analyze`
  finalists on the test articles (full) and `tfns_val`; the two winners also on `fpb_allagree` and
  `finentity_single`; the `qwen3.5:9b` ceiling on the test articles and both cross-domain sets. Then summaries from
  the `/summary` and `/analyze` winners on the 60 test articles go to the blind Opus judges.
- **Run once**: [`holdout_runs.json`](../../../evals/results/holdout_runs.json) is a guard keyed by the sha256 of
  `frozen.json`, recording the selection sha256, git sha, and start and completion times. An interrupted run resumes
  from its caches; a completed config refuses a second run unless `--force --reason` is passed, which is logged in
  the guard and must be disclosed. It also refuses a provisional selection (one made before the latency suite)
  without `--allow-provisional`; this selection was not provisional.
- `holdout analyze` only re-scores the cached predictions and never calls a model; the tables below come from the
```

```diff
 ## Limitations and next steps
 
 - **One model family labels and judges.** Article labels, gold bodies, key facts and summary judgements all come
-  from Claude Opus with no human check, and with 30 dev articles the served rules' CIs span about 0.2-0.5 F0.5.
-- **Precision costs recall.** The `/signal` default caught 10 of 20 directional dev articles, so users will see many
-  neutrals; the 9B decision models catch more but miss the latency budget.
-- **The inversion cap is unproven on articles.** On the 30 dev articles the `/signal` default inverts 1 of its 14
-  directional calls (7.1% against the 2% cap); selection passes it only because the 95% CI at n=30 reaches 0%, so
-  the holdout is the real check ([`selection.md`](evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
-- **Tuned on tweets.** Prompts and thresholds were tuned on 300 tweets and checked on balanced article sets; real
-  traffic is likely neutral-heavy, so served precision is likely lower ([threats](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#9-threats-to-validity)).
-- **Summaries still slip.** The `/summary` default has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% of dev
-  summaries and a material error in 10% [0%, 20%]; numbers are not re-checked against the source at serve time.
```
