```markdown
**Conditions.** One pass on 2026-10-19 from 15:40 local time, 50 warm samples, 0 errors. The laptop ran on
battery (67% at the start, 46% at the end), Low Power Mode off, no thermal warning. The 1-minute load average was
7.1 just before the pass and 35-75 during it, and that was the bundled Ollama itself: the Docker VM used about 11
to 16 cores' worth of CPU, and processes outside it stayed under about 3.7 cores (a watchdog flagged two brief
spikes of about 3.6 cores from ordinary desktop apps).

**Every budget is missed.** CPU-only Docker is 7.5 to 14.0 times slower than Metal on this machine: `/signal`
lede takes 2,291 ms against its 500 ms budget, and the 4B shows first text after 10 to 13 s and completes in 16 to
36 s. That is why native Ollama is the macOS default and the bundled profile is for Linux and CI: a portability
path, not a latency path.

**Per token**, docker-cpu is the warm p50 of the raw samples and Metal the ratio of the p50s in "Where the time
goes":

| model | prefill ms/token, docker-cpu / Metal | decode ms/token, docker-cpu / Metal |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | about 3.7 / 0.24 | about 35 / 6.1 |
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 11 to 14 / 1.0 to 1.2 | about 100 to 200 / 15.8 to 16.0 |

### Discarded passes and run-to-run variance

Two earlier passes were discarded, and neither is committed:

1. **Pass 1 found a prompt-cache bias.** The bundled Ollama has no host port, so the native unload was not
   available, and each JSON cell re-sent the prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles;
   those rows showed prompt eval of 118 to 171 ms. The reload hook above is the fix.
2. **Pass 2 had contention in one cell.** Other workloads ran during it (another container was starting). Its
   `/signal` cell decoded at about 2.4 s per token, against about 35 ms in the committed pass, and 4 `/analyze`
   JSON requests timed out; its 4B cells show the same per-token rates as the committed pass. The whole pass was
   discarded anyway. Its load average proves nothing either way, since a clean pass runs at 35-75 by itself.

Pass 1's rows that the cache bias did not touch (discarded, n=10, not committed) show how far one CPU run lands
from the next on the same protocol:

| cell | pass 1 p50 | committed p50 | committed / pass 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| /signal 0.8B lede JSON | 2,657 | 2,291 | 0.9x |
| /summary 4B SSE, complete | 14,405 | 20,820 | 1.4x |
| /analyze 4B SSE, complete | 12,106 | 30,145 | 2.5x |

CPU-only inference in Docker on a laptop varies about 2x from run to run: the power source, background load and
how the VM's 14 threads land on performance and efficiency cores all move it. The committed rows are one measured
run on battery, not a constant; pass 1 and the committed pass both miss every budget by a wide margin.

`OLLAMA_CPUS` in `compose.yaml` sets a `cpus:` quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota
below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower rather than just capped; a cpuset or `num_thread` is
the fix (backlog).
```

```markdown
5. **Resample the threshold choice.** Grid CIs hold the operating point fixed, so they are optimistic
   ([grid summary](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md)). A nested bootstrap or a separate threshold split would
   give honest CIs on the precision knobs.

   per-fact entailment check would track the Opus judge more closely and could gate summary prompts in CI.
7. **Latency on a dedicated host and under load.** Grid and extraction timings came from a shared workstation,
   contention stalled one cell of a discarded docker-cpu pass, and docker-cpu p50s varied about 2x between passes
   on the same laptop ([05](05-latency.md#discarded-passes-and-run-to-run-variance)). A dedicated runner plus a
   1 / 4 / 16 client sweep would give p95s fit for capacity planning.
8. **A label-noise pass.** 20 directional dev300 tweets get no correct call from any model
   ([grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)); review them before reading that recall loss as model error.
9. **A second vantage point for the source probe.** One EU residential IP chose the final 10, and datacenter IPs
   meet stricter bot management ([02](02-source-probe.md)). Probe from where the service would run.
```

```
The budget was reported, never moved; both 9B models stay selectable per request (`model`, native Ollama).

### Native vs docker-cpu

The bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp on CPU. `latency docker-cpu` measures the bundled defaults through the bundled
app over HTTP, warm n=10 per cell, fetch subtracted; x native divides each p50 by the native-metal p50 of the same
cell ([`latency.md`](evals/results/latency/latency.md#docker-cpu)):

| Endpoint | Transport | docker-cpu p50 | docker-cpu p95 | x native |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` 0.8B lede | JSON | 2,291 ms | 3,184 ms | 12.9x |
| `/summary` 4B | SSE | TTFT 10,169 ms, complete 20,820 ms | complete 34,195 ms | 9.0x / 9.5x |
| `/summary` 4B | JSON | 16,357 ms | 23,560 ms | 7.5x |
| `/analyze` 4B | SSE | signal 10,428 ms, TTFT 13,106 ms, complete 30,145 ms | complete 40,812 ms | 9.5x / 10.1x / 11.7x |
| `/analyze` 4B | JSON | 36,093 ms | 45,378 ms | 14.0x |

Conditions: one pass on 2026-10-19 from 15:40 local time, reload hook on, 0 errors; the laptop on battery (67% to
46%), Low Power Mode off, no thermal warning; 1-minute load average 7.1 before the pass and 35-75 during it, almost
all of it the bundled Ollama (processes outside the Docker VM stayed under about 3.7 cores).

CPU-only Docker is 7.5-14.0x slower than Metal on this machine and every p50 is over its budget, so the bundled
profile is for Linux and CI. Per token, the 4B prefills at 11-14 ms against 1.0-1.2 ms on Metal and decodes at
about 100-200 ms against about 16 ms. Read the rows as one run, not a constant: CPU inference in Docker on a laptop
varies about 2x between runs (power source, background load, how the VM's 14 threads land on performance and
efficiency cores). Two earlier passes were discarded, and neither is committed:

- **Pass 1**: the JSON rows were biased by Ollama's prompt cache (prompt eval 118-171 ms), because each JSON cell
  re-sent prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated. Fix: a reload hook (`container_reload` in
  [`latency.py`](evals/src/veritrade_evals/latency.py)) runs `docker exec ... ollama stop` before every warm phase.
  Its streaming cells completed in 14,405 ms (`/summary`) and 12,106 ms (`/analyze`), 1.4x and 2.5x faster than
  the committed pass on the same protocol: that spread is the run-to-run variance above.
- **Pass 2**: other workloads ran during it (another container was starting). Its `/signal` cell decoded at about
  2.4 s per token against about 35 ms in the committed pass, and 4 `/analyze` JSON requests timed out; its 4B cells
  match the committed pass per token, so contention hit the `/signal` cell and the timeouts, not every cell, but the
  whole pass was discarded. The load average is no evidence either way: a clean pass runs at 35-75 by itself.

## Evaluation

Full method and results: [`04-evals.md`](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md). The harness imports the serving code, so
what is measured is what is served.

- **Metric**: F0.5 macro over bullish and bearish, a 2% inversion cap, and an operating point at the best F0.5
  under the cap; 95% stratified bootstrap CIs (B = 1,000) on the headline metrics.
- **Tweets and sentences** ([`splits/`](evals/data/splits/), ids, hashes and labels only): `dev300` for tuning (100
  per class from Twitter Financial News train, reweighted to its 20.2 / 15.1 / 64.7% prior); Twitter FNS validation
  (2,388), Financial PhraseBank AllAgree (2,259) and FinEntity single-label paragraphs (851) held out.
- **Articles**: 90 recent articles from the 10 sources, 3 per class per source (Yahoo 4 bearish and BBC 2, keeping
```

> The prescreen is delivered, and CI passes on the final commit, e2e included: https://github.com/cleverjobs/veritrade-analytics.
> 
> The repo has the FastAPI service and Next.js UI, Docker Compose in native and bundled modes, the eval harness with committed results, the design docs, a README covering all four asks in the brief, and the redacted transcript with your note to the reviewers. All 28 commits are authored by you, and no private data is tracked. A fresh clone from GitHub builds and serves `/api/analyze` (JSON and streamed) and `/api/signal`.
> 
> **Results**
> 
> | Endpoint | Default model | Dev | One-time holdout (test articles) | Native p50 | Budget |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | `/signal` | qwen3.5:0.8b | F0.5 0.685 | F0.5 0.801, 1 of 30 calls inverted (3.3%) | 178 ms | met |
> | `/analyze` | qwen3.5:4b | F0.5 0.880 | F0.5 0.871, 0 inversions | 2.6 s complete | met |
> | `/summary` | qwen3.5:4b | faithfulness 4.40 | faithfulness 4.37 | 2.2 s complete | met |
> 
> The README states these weak spots openly:
> - **`/signal` inversions:** 3.3% on test is above the 2% cap as a point estimate. It inverted 1 of 14 calls on dev too.
> - **`/analyze` summaries degrade on unseen articles:** 25% have material errors on test, against 10% on dev.
> - **Tweets:** every model scores 0.03-0.09 below dev300.
> - **9B models:** the clef-flash and nimble decision models stay more accurate but miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget. They remain selectable per request.
> 
> **What happened along the way**
> - **Ollama hang:** native Ollama hung mid-holdout. I restarted it and resumed the run from its caches, so it still counts as the single holdout run (the guard logs the resume). The timed-out rows re-ran cleanly and every cell finished with 0 errors.
> - **Laptop crash:** only the judge-ingest step was lost, and I re-ran it. All 60 test judge outputs were still valid.
> - **Docker-cpu:** the bundled path measured 7.5-14x slower than Metal and misses every budget. It ran on battery, and CPU inference in Docker varied about 2x between passes, which the docs state. I also corrected an earlier claim in the docs that blamed one discarded pass's slowness on high load average; a clean pass reaches the same load by itself.
> - **CI fix:** CI failed once after the transcript commit because ruff formats code blocks inside the Markdown render. I excluded the transcript folder from ruff and CI is green again. That fix, and these final turns, are not in the exported transcript.
> - **Docker Desktop:** I started it for the docker pass and it's still running with no containers, so quit it if you don't need it.
> 
> **Rule slips**
> - **Me, twice:** an empty `python3 - <<'EOF'` heredoc in an earlier session, and a stray `uv run python -c "print(1)"` today while checking the transcript meta. Neither did anything.
> - **The docker agent:** ran `uv run python -c "print(1)"`.
> - **The extraction agent:** ran one `python3 -c` to read a JSON file.
> - **Judge agent on batch `ae`:** found the two candidate model names by dropping the models the error named and re-running. That was after its judging was done, and both candidates are the same 4B model, so it learned the pool but not which label is which.
> 
> **Restarting your stopped containers**

> docker start [redacted]-[redacted]-433-{postgres,redis,mailpit,api,scheduler,worker}-1 [redacted]330-postgres-1 [redacted]330-redis-1

```
# Serving config: allowlist, per-endpoint defaults, decoding options and frozen thresholds.
# `veritrade_evals freeze` writes the per-model thresholds and prompt versions from the eval results
# (evals/results/frozen.json); `select --write` owns [defaults]. Models it has not frozen keep provisional values.
#
# kind        generative (/api/chat) | decision (/v1/systemone)
# endpoints   endpoints the model may serve
# signal_schema   generative signal output: "label" (one of 3 labels) | "ordinal" (score -2..2)
# policy      probability | label-logprob | ordinal  (streaming and /analyze always use ordinal)
# min_p       decision/label-logprob threshold on the winning class probability; 0 never abstains
# directional_tau   optional, probability policies only: when neutral wins the argmax and the likelier
#             directional class has p >= tau, call that class; otherwise argmax + min_p applies
# ordinal_t   directional call only when |score| >= ordinal_t (always set: streaming fallback)
# field_order /analyze JSON order: sentiment-first (streams the score early) | summary-first
# prompt      frozen prompt version per endpoint, e.g. { signal = "v4" }; an endpoint left out serves
```

```
# Model selection

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals select` from committed results; numbers only.

## Rules

- **signal**: Candidates: the frozen /signal configs at the default lede scope. Filters: dev300 inversion rate <= 2% at the frozen operating point (n=300); the articles dev set must not fail the cap, meaning the 95% CI of its inversion rate reaches down to 2% (the freeze's clear-failure rule: at n=30 one inversion is about 5% of the calls); warm native p50 excluding fetch <= 500 ms at lede. Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro (primary, n=300), then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **analyze**: Candidates: the frozen /analyze configs (full scope, ordinal |score| >= t, sentiment-first). Filters: the same inversion rules as /signal; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s (warm, native, excluding fetch). Rank: dev300 F0.5 macro, then articles dev F0.5, then lower latency.
- **summary**: Candidates: the frozen /summary models. Filter: deterministic pass rate >= 0.8 on the dev articles; streamed TTFT p50 <= 1.5 s and complete p50 <= 4 s. Rank: Opus judge faithfulness, then judge coverage, then key-fact coverage (key-fact coverage leads while the judge is pending).
- **winner**: The best-ranked candidate inside every filter. When no accuracy-eligible candidate meets its latency budget, the Pareto knee (metrics.knee) of quality against budget utilisation (the worst measured metric divided by its limit) among the measured candidates, with the reason stated.
- **bundle**: R8: the per-endpoint winners when their model files total <= 10 GB (decimal), else the combination of accuracy-eligible candidates that fits with the fewest rank steps away from the winners (ties: signal, then summary, then analyze keeps its better pick; then the smaller total).
```

```
# Extraction matrix

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals.extraction_bench report` from local measurements; no article text is stored here.

- Data: the 90 committed articles (all splits) from 10 sources; stored HTML through the serving `veritrade.extract.registry.extract`; third-party extractors bring their own parser (parser column `(built-in)`).
- Quality: macro means over articles against the Opus gold body. Tokens are lowercased `\w+` runs; P/R/F1 are bag-of-words with multiplicity; a failed extraction scores 0. Leakage is the share of extracted tokens outside every 5-token window that also occurs in the gold body (successful extractions only). 95% CIs: bootstrap over articles (B=1000).
- Time: wall ms of one `extract` call (parse + extract), median of 5 runs per article after a warm-up, then p50/p95 over articles, failures included.
- Tokens: chars / 4 of the uncapped `full` input (title + body) at p50; lede = the `/signal` lede input at the decision model's budget.
- Install: decimal MB of the RECORD files a row adds to the backend core (its closure without any parser or extractor); own strategies add 0 beyond their parser.
- Signal: `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` v4 (grid best), served sentiment at p >= 0.8; agreement = share of articles whose verdict on the row's lede equals the verdict on the gold lede, title held at the gold headline; a failed extraction is a miss.
- Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, Python 3.13.12; Ollama had a model resident in 90/90 per-article samples (another eval was running), mean 1-min load average 6.1.
```

```
# Grid finalists on the articles dev set

Generated by `uv run python -m veritrade_evals finalists analyze` from the local prediction cache; counts and rates only, no article text.

- Data: the articles dev split, n=30 news articles labelled for their primary entity (bullish 10, bearish 10, neutral 10). Balanced and unweighted: unlike dev300, rates are not reweighted to a class prior.
- Inputs: the serving path. `cascade` extraction with `selectolax` on the stored HTML at the fetch's final URL, then the endpoint scope (headline + lede, or the full body) cut to each model's `max_input_tokens`. Extraction failures: 0 (no call; scored as abstentions).
- Thresholds: each config's dev300 operating point (max F0.5 with inversions <= 2%), never re-tuned here. A rule counts as clearly failing only when the whole 95% CI of its inversion rate is above the cap, or the whole coverage CI is below 50% of its dev300 coverage.
- CIs: 95% stratified bootstrap (B=1000). With 10 articles per class they are wide: a gap needs roughly 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most comparisons below are ties.
- Latency: wall ms per call on an Ollama 0.40.6 native-metal shared with other eval runs (client concurrency 1); indicative only.
```

```
# Default: the app uses native Ollama on the host (Metal on macOS; on Linux start it with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0).
#   docker compose up -d
# Bundled: CPU Ollama in a container, models pulled on first start (Linux, CI, no native install).
#   docker compose --profile bundled --env-file deploy/bundled.env up -d
# Either way the UI and API answer on http://localhost:8000 (VT_PORT changes the host port).
name: veritrade

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/app.Dockerfile
    image: veritrade-app:local
    ports:
      - "${VT_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BASE_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434}
      VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL: ${VT_OLLAMA_BACKEND_LABEL:-native-metal}
      # Empty values keep the models.toml allowlist and defaults.
      VT_MODELS: ${VT_MODELS:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SIGNAL:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SUMMARY:-}
      VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE: ${VT_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANALYZE:-}
      # Passed through only when set on the host; otherwise the app's public contact default applies.
      SEC_USER_AGENT:
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    depends_on:
      ollama-pull:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
        required: false

  ollama:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    # Unlimited by default. A quota does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a value below the
    # visible cores slows CPU inference rather than just capping it.
    cpus: ${OLLAMA_CPUS:-0}
    volumes:
      # OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR swaps the named volume for a host directory (CI caches it between runs).
      - ${OLLAMA_MODEL_DIR:-ollama-models}:/root/.ollama/models
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: 30m
      OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: "2"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
      OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE: q8_0
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "ollama", "list"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 30

  ollama-pull:
    profiles: [bundled]
    image: ollama/ollama:${OLLAMA_IMAGE_TAG:-0.40.6}
    depends_on:
      ollama:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
```

```
"""URL to Article: single-flight fetch, then extraction (off the event loop when it is slow)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import partial
from typing import Literal

from veritrade.extract.registry import extract
from veritrade.extract.types import PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS, Article, ExtractorName, ParserName
from veritrade.fetch import FetchResult, normalize_url
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime

FetchStatus = Literal["hit", "miss", "joined", "bypass"]
# Own strategies on these parsers take 0.4-4 ms on real pages, less than handing off is worth; bs4 and the
# third-party extractors take 5-60 ms of Python, which a thread lets concurrent streams interleave with.
INLINE_PARSERS: frozenset[ParserName] = frozenset({"selectolax", "lxml"})


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LoadedArticle:
    page: FetchResult
    article: Article
    fetch_status: FetchStatus
    fetch_ms: float
    consent_ms: float | None


async def load_article(
    runtime: Runtime, url: str, *, parser: ParserName, extractor: ExtractorName, no_cache: bool
) -> LoadedArticle:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    status: FetchStatus
    if no_cache:
        page, status = await runtime.fetcher.get(url), "bypass"
    else:
        fetch = partial(runtime.fetcher.get, url)
        shared = await runtime.fetch_cache.get_or_create(normalize_url(url), fetch)
        page, status = shared.value, shared.status
    if status in ("miss", "bypass"):
        fetch_ms, consent_ms = page.fetch_ms, page.consent_ms
    else:
        # A hit or join reports this request's own wait, not the download it reused.
        fetch_ms, consent_ms = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, None
    article = await extract_article(page, parser=parser, extractor=extractor)
    return LoadedArticle(page, article, status, fetch_ms, consent_ms)


async def extract_article(page: FetchResult, *, parser: ParserName, extractor: ExtractorName) -> Article:
    run = partial(extract, page.html, page.final_url, parser=parser, extractor=extractor)
    if extractor in PARSER_AWARE_EXTRACTORS and parser in INLINE_PARSERS:
        return run()
    return await asyncio.to_thread(run)
```

```
class HttpFetcher:
    """Fetcher protocol over one shared client whose cookie jar keeps Yahoo's reject-all answer."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Settings,
        *,
        resolver: Resolver = system_resolver,
        limiter: HostRateLimiter | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._settings = settings
        self._resolver = resolver
        self._allow_hosts = settings.ssrf_allow_hosts
        self._limiter = limiter or HostRateLimiter()
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            transport=_GuardedTransport(GuardedBackend(resolver=resolver, allow_hosts=self._allow_hosts)),
            follow_redirects=False,
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(settings.fetch_deadline_s, connect=settings.fetch_connect_timeout_s),
            # User-supplied URLs must never pick up .netrc credentials.
            trust_env=False,
        )

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self._client.aclose()

    async def get(self, url: str) -> FetchResult:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        host = _host(url)
        deadline = self._settings.fetch_deadline_s
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(deadline):
                return await self._fetch(url, started)
        except (TimeoutError, httpx.TimeoutException) as exc:
            raise UpstreamTimeout(
                f"{host} did not deliver the page within {deadline:g} s",
                hint="The publisher is slow or unreachable; retry, or try the story from another source.",
            ) from exc
        except httpx.InvalidURL as exc:
            raise InvalidUrl(f"malformed URL: {exc}") from exc
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise UpstreamHttp(
                f"request to {host} failed: {type(exc).__name__}",
                hint="The publisher could not be reached; retry shortly.",
            ) from exc

    async def _check(self, url: str) -> None:
```

```python
"""Fetch + extract every labelled article URL in-process, so the running app's caches stay cold."""

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path

from veritrade.config import get_settings
from veritrade.errors import VeritradeError
from veritrade.extract.registry import extract
from veritrade.fetch.client import HttpFetcher

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ARTICLES = ROOT / "evals/data/articles/articles.jsonl"
OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("urls.json")
EXTRA = [
    ("blocked", "https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news"),
    ("blocked", "https://apnews.com/hub/business"),
]


async def probe(fetcher: HttpFetcher, sem: asyncio.Semaphore, row: dict) -> dict:
    async with sem:
        try:
            page = await fetcher.get(row["url"])
            article = extract(page.html, page.final_url, parser="selectolax", extractor="cascade")
            words = len(article.text.split())
            return {**row, "ok": True, "title": article.title, "words": words, "fetch_ms": round(page.fetch_ms)}
        except VeritradeError as exc:
            return {**row, "ok": False, "error": type(exc).__name__, "detail": str(exc)[:120]}


async def main() -> None:
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in ARTICLES.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]
    keep = [
        {k: r[k] for k in ("id", "url", "source", "split", "label", "score", "entity", "published_at")}
        for r in rows
    ]
    keep += [{"id": f"extra-{i}", "url": u, "source": kind, "split": "-", "label": "-"} for i, (kind, u) in enumerate(EXTRA)]
    fetcher = HttpFetcher(get_settings())
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(6)
    try:
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(probe(fetcher, sem, r) for r in keep))
    finally:
        await fetcher.aclose()
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    for r in sorted(results, key=lambda r: (r["source"], r["label"])):
        status = f"ok {r['words']:5d}w {r['fetch_ms']:5d}ms" if r["ok"] else f"ERR {r['error']}"
        title = r.get("title") or r.get("detail", "")
        print(f"{r['source']:10s} {r['split']:5s} {r['label']:8s} {status:22s} {title[:70]}  {r['url']}")
    print(f"ok {sum(r['ok'] for r in results)}/{len(results)}")


asyncio.run(main())

```
</details>

### 🤖 Assistant: *\*\*What "abstained" means:\*\* the model's top…*

`15:30:17`

<details>
<summary>Thinking...</summary>

> 
</details>

> **What "abstained" means:** the model's top answer wasn't confident enough to act on, so the service gives no directional call and reports Neutral, with `abstained: true` so you can tell it apart from a confident Neutral. Precision over recall was the agreed objective, so a weak Bullish counts as no signal rather than a trade signal.
> 
> **Why Neutral when Bullish has the biggest bar:** for `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` the service only accepts the top class when its probability is at least **0.80** (`min_p = 0.8` in `backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml`). Here Bullish was the top class at 73.0%, which is below 0.80. The service therefore returns Neutral plus `abstained`, and the card adds "the model leaned Bullish" so the lean isn't hidden (`backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py:63-66`).
> 
> **Where 0.80 comes from:** the eval picked the threshold on the 300-tweet dev set. It's the cutoff that gives the highest F0.5 while keeping Bullish↔Bearish flips at or below 2%. Below 0.8, the extra directional calls lost more precision than the added recall was worth. The cost is that this model stays silent on 15-25% of articles: it made a call on 77% of the dev articles and 85% of the test articles.
> 
> **On this article, abstaining was the right outcome.** The Opus reference label is **Neutral**: opening an office is news, but it doesn't move a stock. The model saw a positive story, but not one positive enough to clear the bar.
> 
> **The 12.3 s time to signal** is a one-off. It's the first load of the 10 GB model, which I hadn't preloaded. Further requests with it should take about 0.7 s while it stays loaded, which is 30 minutes after its last use.
> 
> **One UI problem your screenshot shows:** the pill says "Neutral" while the biggest bar says Bullish. That reads like a contradiction until you read the note. I'd change the pill to show **"No signal"** when the call is abstained, and keep the "leaned Bullish" note. The API response would stay `sentiment: "neutral"` + `abstained: true`, so only the frontend changes. Want me to make that change?

```
"""Public API contract: request/response bodies, SSE event payloads and the error envelope."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from veritrade.errors import ErrorCode
from veritrade.extract.types import ExtractorName, ParserName, Scope
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint, FieldOrder, ModelKind, PolicyName, Sentiment


class _Strict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


# --- requests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _ArticleRequest(_Strict):
    url: AnyHttpUrl
    model: str | None = Field(None, description="Allowlisted Ollama tag; endpoint default when omitted.")
    parser: ParserName = "selectolax"
    extractor: ExtractorName = "cascade"
    no_cache: bool = Field(False, description="Bypass fetch and result caches (used by latency benchmarks).")


class SignalRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = Field("lede", description="lede = headline + opening paragraphs; full = whole article.")


class SummaryRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    pass


class AnalyzeRequest(_ArticleRequest):
    scope: Scope = "full"


# --- shared response parts ------------------------------------------------------------------


class CacheInfo(_Strict):
    fetch: Literal["hit", "miss", "joined", "bypass"]
    result: Literal["hit", "miss", "bypass"]


class InferenceTimings(_Strict):
    wall_ms: float
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    load_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_eval_ms: float | None = None
    eval_ms: float | None = None
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    eval_tokens: int | None = None


class Timings(_Strict):
    total_ms: float
    fetch_ms: float
    consent_ms: float | None = None
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    inference: InferenceTimings | None = None
    cache: CacheInfo


class ArticleMeta(_Strict):
    url: str
    final_url: str
    title: str
    source: str | None = Field(None, description="Key from sources.toml when the domain is a known source.")
    published_at: str | None = None
    endpoint: Endpoint
    model: str
    model_kind: ModelKind
    prompt_version: str
    parser: ParserName
    extractor: ExtractorName
    extraction_method: str = Field(description="Strategy that produced the body (cascade resolves to one).")
    scope: Scope
    input_chars: int
    word_count: int
    field_order: FieldOrder | None = None
    cached: bool
    backend: str = Field(description="Inference backend label, e.g. native-metal or docker-cpu.")


class SignalResult(_Strict):
    sentiment: Sentiment
    abstained: bool = Field(description="True when the call fell below the frozen confidence threshold.")
    policy: PolicyName
    confidence: float | None = None
    score: int | None = Field(None, ge=-2, le=2)
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float] | None = None


# --- responses ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SignalResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    timings: Timings


class SummaryResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class AnalyzeResponse(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    summary: str
    truncated: bool = Field(False, description="True when the summary was cut at the model's output limit.")
    timings: Timings


class ErrorBody(_Strict):
    code: ErrorCode
    message: str
    hint: str | None = None
    retryable: bool = False
    upstream_status: int | None = None


class ErrorResponse(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


class ModelInfo(_Strict):
    name: str
    kind: ModelKind
    endpoints: list[Endpoint]
    installed: bool
    size_bytes: int | None = None
    evaluated: bool = Field(True, description="False for plumbing-only models (e.g. the CI decision model).")


class ModelsResponse(_Strict):
    models: list[ModelInfo]
    defaults: dict[Endpoint, str]
    parsers: list[ParserName]
    extractors: list[ExtractorName]
    scopes: list[Scope]


class HealthResponse(_Strict):
    status: Literal["ok", "degraded"]
    ollama_reachable: bool
    ollama_version: str | None = None
    backend: str
    version: str


# --- SSE event payloads (event name -> data model) ------------------------------------------
# /summary/stream: meta -> summary_delta* -> done
# /analyze/stream: meta -> sentiment (exactly once, position follows field order) + summary_delta* -> done
# Any failure after the stream opens emits a single `error` event and closes.


class MetaEvent(_Strict):
    meta: ArticleMeta
    fetch_ms: float
    parse_ms: float
    extract_ms: float
    cache: CacheInfo


class SentimentEvent(_Strict):
    signal: SignalResult
    entity: str | None = None
    elapsed_ms: float = Field(description="Milliseconds since the request was received.")


class SummaryDeltaEvent(_Strict):
    text: str


class SummaryDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: SummaryResponse


class AnalyzeDoneEvent(_Strict):
    result: AnalyzeResponse


class ErrorEvent(_Strict):
    error: ErrorBody


SSE_EVENT_NAMES = ("meta", "sentiment", "summary_delta", "done", "error")
```

```
import type { PolicyName, Sentiment, SignalResult } from "@/lib/api";
import { capitalize, formatMs, formatPct } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./SignalCard.module.css";

const POLICY_NOTES: Record<PolicyName, string> = {
  probability: "threshold on the decision model's class probability",
  "label-logprob": "threshold on the label token probability",
  ordinal: "threshold on |score| of the -2..+2 scale",
};

const ORDER: readonly Sentiment[] = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

/** Direction the model leaned before the threshold turned it into an abstention. */
export function leaning(signal: SignalResult): Sentiment {
  if (signal.probabilities) {
    let best: Sentiment = signal.sentiment;
    for (const s of ORDER) {
      if ((signal.probabilities[s] ?? 0) > (signal.probabilities[best] ?? 0)) best = s;
    }
    return best;
  }
  if (typeof signal.score === "number" && signal.score !== 0) return signal.score > 0 ? "bullish" : "bearish";
  return signal.sentiment;
}

function formatScore(score: number): string {
  return score > 0 ? `+${score}` : String(score);
}

interface SignalCardProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity?: string | null;
  model?: string | null;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the signal arriving. */
  timeToSignalMs?: number | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on a combined stream. */
  serverMs?: number | null;
}

export function SignalCard({ status, signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: SignalCardProps) {
  const busy = !signal && (status === "pending" || status === "streaming");
  return (
    <section className={styles.card} aria-labelledby="signal-heading" aria-busy={busy}>
      <h2 id="signal-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Signal
      </h2>
      {signal ? (
        <SignalBody
          signal={signal}
          entity={entity}
          model={model}
          timeToSignalMs={timeToSignalMs}
          serverMs={serverMs}
        />
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.placeholder}>
          {busy
            ? "Waiting for the signal..."
            : status === "cancelled"
              ? "Cancelled."
              : "No signal: the request failed."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

type SignalBodyProps = Omit<SignalCardProps, "status" | "signal"> & { signal: SignalResult };

function SignalBody({ signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs }: SignalBodyProps) {
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <span
          className={styles.badge}
          data-sentiment={signal.sentiment}
          data-abstained={signal.abstained || undefined}
          data-testid="signal-badge"
        >
          {capitalize(signal.sentiment)}
        </span>
        {signal.abstained ? <span className={styles.abstainTag}>Abstained</span> : null}
        {entity ? <span className={styles.entity}>{entity}</span> : null}
      </div>
      {signal.abstained ? (
        <p className={styles.abstainNote}>
          Below confidence threshold: the call is not confident enough to trade on, so treat it as no
          directional signal.
          {lean !== signal.sentiment ? ` The model leaned ${capitalize(lean)}.` : null}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <dl className={styles.stats}>
        {typeof signal.confidence === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Confidence</dt>
            <dd>{formatPct(signal.confidence)}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof signal.score === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Score</dt>
            <dd>{formatScore(signal.score)} on -2..+2</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <div>
          <dt>Policy</dt>
          <dd>
            <code>{signal.policy}</code> <span className={styles.note}>({POLICY_NOTES[signal.policy]})</span>
          </dd>
        </div>
        {model ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Model</dt>
            <dd>
              <code>{model}</code>
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof timeToSignalMs === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Time to signal</dt>
            <dd>
              {formatMs(timeToSignalMs)}
              {typeof serverMs === "number" ? (
                <span className={styles.note}> (server {formatMs(serverMs)})</span>
              ) : null}
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </dl>
      {signal.probabilities ? (
        <ul className={styles.probs} aria-label="Class probabilities">
          {ORDER.map((s) => {
            const p = signal.probabilities?.[s] ?? 0;
            return (
              <li key={s} className={styles.prob}>
                <span className={styles.probLabel}>{capitalize(s)}</span>
                <span className={styles.probTrack} aria-hidden="true">
                  <span
                    className={styles.probFill}
                    data-sentiment={s}
                    style={{ width: `${Math.max(0, Math.min(1, p)) * 100}%` }}
                  />
                </span>
                <span className={styles.probValue}>{formatPct(p)}</span>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

```
"""Async Ollama client on httpx: the only Ollama path for the API, evals and probes."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Mapping, Sequence
from types import TracebackType
from typing import Any, Self

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, ValidationError

from veritrade.config import Settings, get_settings
from veritrade.errors import (
    InferenceTimeout,
    LlmUnreachable,
    ModelUnavailable,
    SchemaViolation,
    VtError,
)
from veritrade.inference.schemas import ollama_format
from veritrade.inference.types import (
    SENTIMENTS,
    ChatResult,
    DecisionResult,
    OllamaTimings,
    Sentiment,
    TokenLogprob,
)

Message = Mapping[str, str]
# Greedy and seeded so evals and serving see the same output for the same prompt. Penalties are neutralised
# because Modelfiles set them (qwen3.5: presence_penalty 1.5), which skews outputs away from recent tokens.
FIXED_OPTIONS: dict[str, Any] = {
    "temperature": 0,
    "seed": 0,
    "presence_penalty": 0,
    "frequency_penalty": 0,
    "repeat_penalty": 1,
}
SENTIMENT_QUESTION = "sentiment"


class OutputTruncated(SchemaViolation):
    """Generation hit num_predict before the JSON closed; `chat` keeps the partial output."""

    def __init__(self, model: str, chat: ChatResult) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"{model} reached its output token limit before the JSON closed")
        self.chat = chat


class _ChoiceAnswer(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")

    choice: Sentiment
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float]
    confidence: float


def _ms(value: Any) -> float | None:
    return value / 1e6 if isinstance(value, int | float) else None


def _int(value: Any) -> int | None:
    return value if isinstance(value, int) else None


def _str(value: Any) -> str | None:
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None


def parse_timings(body: Mapping[str, Any]) -> OllamaTimings:
    return OllamaTimings(
        load_ms=_ms(body.get("load_duration")),
        prompt_eval_ms=_ms(body.get("prompt_eval_duration")),
        eval_ms=_ms(body.get("eval_duration")),
        prompt_tokens=_int(body.get("prompt_eval_count")),
        eval_tokens=_int(body.get("eval_count")),
        total_ms=_ms(body.get("total_duration")),
    )


def parse_logprobs(raw: Any) -> tuple[TokenLogprob, ...] | None:
    if not isinstance(raw, list) or not raw:
        return None
    return tuple(
        TokenLogprob(
            token=entry["token"],
            logprob=float(entry["logprob"]),
            top=tuple((alt["token"], float(alt["logprob"])) for alt in entry.get("top_logprobs") or ()),
        )
        for entry in raw
    )


def _error_text(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
    try:
        body = response.json()
    except ValueError:
        return response.text[:300]
    error = body.get("error") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
    return error if isinstance(error, str) else response.text[:300]


def _status_error(status: int, text: str, model: str | None) -> VtError:
    name = model or "?"
    if status == 404 or "not found" in text.lower():
        return ModelUnavailable(
            f"Model {name} is not available in Ollama: {text}",
            hint=f"Pull it with `ollama pull {name}` or pick an installed model.",
            upstream_status=status,
        )
    return ModelUnavailable(
        f"Ollama rejected the request for {name} ({status}): {text}", upstream_status=status
    )


class OllamaClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url: str,
        *,
        timeout: float = 90.0,
        keep_alive: str | int = "30m",
        http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.keep_alive = keep_alive
        self._http = http or httpx.AsyncClient(
            base_url=self.base_url, timeout=httpx.Timeout(timeout, connect=min(5.0, timeout))
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_settings(cls, settings: Settings | None = None) -> OllamaClient:
        settings = settings or get_settings()
        return cls(
            settings.ollama_base_url,
            timeout=settings.inference_timeout_s,
```

```
"""Steps every article endpoint shares: resolve, check the result cache, load, describe."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeDoneEvent,
    AnalyzeRequest,
    AnalyzeResponse,
    ArticleMeta,
    CacheInfo,
    ErrorEvent,
    InferenceTimings,
    MetaEvent,
    SentimentEvent,
    SignalRequest,
    SignalResponse,
    SignalResult,
    SummaryDeltaEvent,
    SummaryDoneEvent,
    SummaryRequest,
    SummaryResponse,
    Timings,
)
from veritrade.extract.scope import build_input
from veritrade.extract.types import Scope
from veritrade.fetch import normalize_url
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, DecisionResult, Endpoint, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptSpec
from veritrade.services.article import LoadedArticle, load_article
from veritrade.services.cache import ResultKey
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer

ArticleRequest = SignalRequest | SummaryRequest | AnalyzeRequest
StreamPayload = (
    MetaEvent | SentimentEvent | SummaryDeltaEvent | SummaryDoneEvent | AnalyzeDoneEvent | ErrorEvent
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Job:
    """A request with its model and prompt resolved; nothing has touched the network yet."""

    runtime: Runtime
    endpoint: Endpoint
    request: ArticleRequest
    url: str
    scope: Scope
    spec: ModelSpec
    prompt: PromptSpec
    key: ResultKey | None
    clock: StageTimer

    @classmethod
    def resolve(
        cls, runtime: Runtime, endpoint: Endpoint, request: ArticleRequest, *, scope: Scope, clock: StageTimer
    ) -> Job:
        spec = runtime.registry.resolve(endpoint, request.model)
        prompt = runtime.prompt(endpoint, spec)
        url = str(request.url)
        key = None
        if not request.no_cache:
            key = ResultKey(
                endpoint=endpoint,
                url=normalize_url(url),
                model=spec.name,
                prompt_version=prompt.version,
                parser=request.parser,
                extractor=request.extractor,
                scope=scope,
            )
        return cls(runtime, endpoint, request, url, scope, spec, prompt, key, clock)

    def cached[R: (SignalResponse, SummaryResponse, AnalyzeResponse)](self, kind: type[R]) -> R | None:
        """The stored response marked as cached, with timings that describe this request."""
        hit = self.runtime.results.get(self.key) if self.key is not None else None
        if not isinstance(hit, kind):
            return None
        # A result hit runs no stage, so stage timings are zero and the article counts as a fetch hit.
        timings = Timings(
            total_ms=self.clock.elapsed_ms(),
            fetch_ms=0.0,
            parse_ms=0.0,
            extract_ms=0.0,
            cache=CacheInfo(fetch="hit", result="hit"),
        )
        meta = hit.meta.model_copy(update={"cached": True})
        return hit.model_copy(update={"meta": meta, "timings": timings})

    def remember(self, response: SignalResponse | SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse) -> None:
        if self.key is not None:
            self.runtime.results.put(self.key, response)

    async def prepare(self) -> Prepared:
        loaded = await load_article(
            self.runtime,
            self.url,
            parser=self.request.parser,
            extractor=self.request.extractor,
            no_cache=self.request.no_cache,
        )
        text = build_input(loaded.article, self.scope, self.spec.max_input_tokens)
        return Prepared(
            job=self,
            loaded=loaded,
            text=text,
            meta=self._meta(loaded, text),
            cache=CacheInfo(fetch=loaded.fetch_status, result="bypass" if self.key is None else "miss"),
        )

    def _meta(self, loaded: LoadedArticle, text: str) -> ArticleMeta:
        article = loaded.article
        return ArticleMeta(
            url=self.url,
            final_url=loaded.page.final_url,
            title=article.title,
            source=article.source,
            published_at=article.published_at,
            endpoint=self.endpoint,
            model=self.spec.name,
            model_kind=self.spec.kind,
            prompt_version=self.prompt.version,
            parser=self.request.parser,
            extractor=self.request.extractor,
            extraction_method=article.method,
            scope=self.scope,
            input_chars=len(text),
            word_count=article.word_count,
            field_order=self.spec.field_order if self.endpoint == "analyze" else None,
            cached=False,
            backend=self.runtime.settings.ollama_backend_label,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Prepared:
    """A job with its article loaded and the model input built; only inference is left."""

    job: Job
    loaded: LoadedArticle
    text: str
    meta: ArticleMeta
    cache: CacheInfo

    def timings(self, inference: InferenceTimings | None) -> Timings:
        loaded = self.loaded
        return Timings(
            total_ms=self.job.clock.elapsed_ms(),
            fetch_ms=loaded.fetch_ms,
            consent_ms=loaded.consent_ms,
            parse_ms=loaded.article.parse_ms,
            extract_ms=loaded.article.extract_ms,
            inference=inference,
            cache=self.cache,
        )

    def meta_event(self) -> MetaEvent:
        article = self.loaded.article
        return MetaEvent(
            meta=self.meta,
            fetch_ms=self.loaded.fetch_ms,
            parse_ms=article.parse_ms,
            extract_ms=article.extract_ms,
            cache=self.cache,
        )


def cached_meta_event(response: SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse) -> MetaEvent:
    timings = response.timings
    return MetaEvent(
        meta=response.meta,
        fetch_ms=timings.fetch_ms,
        parse_ms=timings.parse_ms,
        extract_ms=timings.extract_ms,
        cache=timings.cache,
    )


def signal_result(verdict: Verdict) -> SignalResult:
    return SignalResult(
        sentiment=verdict.sentiment,
        abstained=verdict.abstained,
        policy=verdict.policy,
        confidence=verdict.confidence,
        score=verdict.score,
        probabilities=verdict.probabilities,
    )


def inference_timings(raw: ChatResult | DecisionResult, *, ttft_ms: float | None = None) -> InferenceTimings:
    """ttft_ms is passed in by streams, which measure it from request receipt to the first summary text."""
    if isinstance(raw, DecisionResult):
        return InferenceTimings(wall_ms=raw.wall_ms, prompt_tokens=raw.input_tokens)
    t = raw.timings
    return InferenceTimings(
        wall_ms=raw.wall_ms,
        ttft_ms=ttft_ms,
        load_ms=t.load_ms,
        prompt_eval_ms=t.prompt_eval_ms,
        eval_ms=t.eval_ms,
        prompt_tokens=t.prompt_tokens,
        eval_tokens=t.eval_tokens,
    )
```

```
"""/signal: one non-streaming classification of the lede (or the full article)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from veritrade.api.contracts import SignalRequest, SignalResponse
from veritrade.inference.adapters import classify_signal
from veritrade.services.pipeline import Job, inference_timings, signal_result
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer


async def run_signal(runtime: Runtime, request: SignalRequest, clock: StageTimer) -> SignalResponse:
    job = Job.resolve(runtime, "signal", request, scope=request.scope, clock=clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(SignalResponse)) is not None:
        return hit
    prepared = await job.prepare()
    verdict, raw = await classify_signal(runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    response = SignalResponse(
        meta=prepared.meta,
        signal=signal_result(verdict),
        timings=prepared.timings(inference_timings(raw)),
    )
    job.remember(response)
    return response
"""/summary: a short summary of the full article, as one JSON body or as streamed deltas."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import aclosing

from veritrade.api.contracts import SummaryDeltaEvent, SummaryDoneEvent, SummaryRequest, SummaryResponse
from veritrade.inference.adapters import SummaryResult, summarize, summarize_stream
from veritrade.inference.incremental import SummaryText
from veritrade.services.pipeline import Job, Prepared, StreamPayload, cached_meta_event, inference_timings
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer


def _job(runtime: Runtime, request: SummaryRequest, clock: StageTimer) -> Job:
    return Job.resolve(runtime, "summary", request, scope="full", clock=clock)


async def run_summary(runtime: Runtime, request: SummaryRequest, clock: StageTimer) -> SummaryResponse:
    job = _job(runtime, request, clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(SummaryResponse)) is not None:
        return hit
    prepared = await job.prepare()
    result = await summarize(runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    response = _response(prepared, result, ttft_ms=None)
    job.remember(response)
    return response


async def open_summary_stream(
    runtime: Runtime, request: SummaryRequest, clock: StageTimer
) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    """Runs every step that can fail before the stream opens; the returned events only do inference."""
    job = _job(runtime, request, clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(SummaryResponse)) is not None:
        return _replay(hit)
    return _stream(await job.prepare())


async def _stream(prepared: Prepared) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    job = prepared.job
    yield prepared.meta_event()
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    events = summarize_stream(job.runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    async with aclosing(events):
        async for event in events:
            match event:
                case SummaryText(delta=delta):
                    if ttft_ms is None:
                        ttft_ms = job.clock.elapsed_ms()
                    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=delta)
                case SummaryResult():
                    response = _response(prepared, event, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)
                    job.remember(response)
                    yield SummaryDoneEvent(result=response)


async def _replay(hit: SummaryResponse) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    yield cached_meta_event(hit)
    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=hit.summary)
    yield SummaryDoneEvent(result=hit)


def _response(prepared: Prepared, result: SummaryResult, *, ttft_ms: float | None) -> SummaryResponse:
    return SummaryResponse(
        meta=prepared.meta,
        summary=result.output.summary,
        truncated=result.truncated,
        timings=prepared.timings(inference_timings(result.chat, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)),
    )
"""/analyze: sentiment, entity and summary from one generation, as JSON or as streamed events."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import aclosing

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeDoneEvent,
    AnalyzeRequest,
    AnalyzeResponse,
    SentimentEvent,
    SummaryDeltaEvent,
)
from veritrade.inference.adapters import AnalyzeResult, analyze, analyze_stream, score_verdict
from veritrade.inference.incremental import EntityClosed, ScoreClosed, SummaryText
from veritrade.services.pipeline import (
    Job,
    Prepared,
    StreamPayload,
    cached_meta_event,
    inference_timings,
    signal_result,
)
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer


def _job(runtime: Runtime, request: AnalyzeRequest, clock: StageTimer) -> Job:
    return Job.resolve(runtime, "analyze", request, scope=request.scope, clock=clock)


async def run_analyze(runtime: Runtime, request: AnalyzeRequest, clock: StageTimer) -> AnalyzeResponse:
    job = _job(runtime, request, clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(AnalyzeResponse)) is not None:
        return hit
    prepared = await job.prepare()
    result = await analyze(runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    response = _response(prepared, result, ttft_ms=None)
    job.remember(response)
    return response


async def open_analyze_stream(
    runtime: Runtime, request: AnalyzeRequest, clock: StageTimer
) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    """Runs every step that can fail before the stream opens; the returned events only do inference."""
    job = _job(runtime, request, clock)
    if (hit := job.cached(AnalyzeResponse)) is not None:
        return _replay(hit, clock)
    return _stream(await job.prepare())


async def _stream(prepared: Prepared) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    """Events follow generation order, so the frozen field order decides where `sentiment` lands."""
    job = prepared.job
    yield prepared.meta_event()
    entity: str | None = None
    ttft_ms: float | None = None
    events = analyze_stream(job.runtime.ollama, job.spec, job.prompt, prepared.text)
    async with aclosing(events):
        async for event in events:
            match event:
                case ScoreClosed(score=score):
                    yield SentimentEvent(
                        signal=signal_result(score_verdict(job.spec, score)),
                        entity=entity,
                        elapsed_ms=job.clock.elapsed_ms(),
                    )
                case EntityClosed(entity=name):
                    entity = name.strip() or None
                case SummaryText(delta=delta):
                    if ttft_ms is None:
                        ttft_ms = job.clock.elapsed_ms()
                    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=delta)
                case AnalyzeResult():
                    response = _response(prepared, event, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)
                    job.remember(response)
                    yield AnalyzeDoneEvent(result=response)


async def _replay(hit: AnalyzeResponse, clock: StageTimer) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamPayload]:
    yield cached_meta_event(hit)
    yield SentimentEvent(signal=hit.signal, entity=hit.entity, elapsed_ms=clock.elapsed_ms())
    yield SummaryDeltaEvent(text=hit.summary)
    yield AnalyzeDoneEvent(result=hit)


def _response(prepared: Prepared, result: AnalyzeResult, *, ttft_ms: float | None) -> AnalyzeResponse:
    return AnalyzeResponse(
        meta=prepared.meta,
        signal=signal_result(result.verdict),
        entity=result.entity,
        summary=result.output.summary,
        truncated=result.truncated,
        timings=prepared.timings(inference_timings(result.chat, ttft_ms=ttft_ms)),
    )
"""Process-wide objects, built once by the app lifespan and shared by every request."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.errors import LlmUnreachable
from veritrade.fetch import Fetcher, FetchResult, SingleFlightCache
from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec, Registry
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptRegistry, PromptSpec
from veritrade.services.cache import CachedResponse, ResultKey, TtlCache

# Installed Ollama tags -> size in bytes (None when Ollama does not report one).
InstalledTags = dict[str, int | None]
_TAGS_KEY = "tags"


def tag_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Ollama lists an untagged model as name:latest."""
    return name if ":" in name else f"{name}:latest"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Runtime:
    settings: Settings
    fetcher: Fetcher
    ollama: OllamaClient
    registry: Registry
    prompts: Mapping[tuple[Endpoint, str], PromptSpec]
    fetch_cache: SingleFlightCache[str, FetchResult]
    results: TtlCache[ResultKey, CachedResponse]
    tags: SingleFlightCache[str, InstalledTags]

    @classmethod
    def build(
        cls,
        settings: Settings,
        *,
        fetcher: Fetcher,
        ollama: OllamaClient,
        registry: Registry | None = None,
    ) -> Runtime:
        registry = registry or Registry.load(settings)
        prompt_registry = PromptRegistry()
        # Resolved up front so a broken prompt file fails startup instead of a request.
        prompts = {
            (endpoint, spec.name): prompt_registry.get(endpoint, spec.name, kind=spec.kind)
            for spec in registry.models
            for endpoint in spec.endpoints
        }
        return cls(
            settings=settings,
            fetcher=fetcher,
            ollama=ollama,
            registry=registry,
            prompts=prompts,
            fetch_cache=SingleFlightCache(
                max_entries=settings.cache_max_entries,
                ttl_s=settings.fetch_cache_ttl_s,
                error_ttl_s=settings.fetch_error_ttl_s,
                weigh=lambda page: len(page.html),
                max_weight=settings.fetch_cache_max_bytes,
            ),
            results=TtlCache(max_entries=settings.cache_max_entries, ttl_s=settings.result_cache_ttl_s),
            tags=SingleFlightCache(
                max_entries=1, ttl_s=settings.models_cache_ttl_s, error_ttl_s=settings.models_cache_ttl_s
            ),
        )

    def prompt(self, endpoint: Endpoint, spec: ModelSpec) -> PromptSpec:
        return self.prompts[(endpoint, spec.name)]

    async def installed_tags(self) -> InstalledTags:
        """Cached for models_cache_ttl_s, failures included, so a down Ollama is not probed per request."""
        result = await self.tags.get_or_create(_TAGS_KEY, self._list_tags)
        return result.value

    async def _list_tags(self) -> InstalledTags:
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(self.settings.ollama_probe_timeout_s):
                entries = await self.ollama.tags()
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            raise LlmUnreachable("Ollama did not list its models in time") from exc
        return {tag_name(str(entry.get("name", ""))): _size(entry) for entry in entries}


def _size(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> int | None:
    size = entry.get("size")
    return size if isinstance(size, int) else None
```

```
"""Confidence policies: raw model output -> Verdict, abstaining to neutral below the frozen threshold."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from veritrade.inference.schemas import LabelOut, OrdinalOut, score_sentiment
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, Endpoint, PolicyName, Sentiment, TokenLogprob, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec

# Ties resolve to the safe class first; also the criteria order sent to decision models.
TIE_ORDER: tuple[Sentiment, ...] = ("neutral", "bullish", "bearish")
# Share of first-token mass allowed on tokens that could start several classes before we give up.
AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX = 0.05

_VALUE_START = {
    "label": re.compile(r'"label"\s*:\s*"'),
    "score": re.compile(r'"score"\s*:\s*'),
}
_SCORE_HEAD = re.compile(r"^(?:-|-[12](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?|[012](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?)$")
_SCORE_KEY = re.compile(r'"score"\s*:')


def winner(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Sentiment:
    best = TIE_ORDER[0]
    for sentiment in TIE_ORDER[1:]:
        if probabilities.get(sentiment, 0.0) > probabilities.get(best, 0.0):
            best = sentiment
    return best


def normalise(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> dict[Sentiment, float]:
    total = sum(max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) for s in TIE_ORDER)
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("probabilities sum to zero")
    return {s: max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def _threshold(
    name: PolicyName,
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float],
    min_p: float,
    score: int | None = None,
    tau: float | None = None,
) -> Verdict:
    top = winner(probabilities)
    if tau is not None and top == "neutral":
        side: Sentiment = "bullish" if probabilities["bullish"] >= probabilities["bearish"] else "bearish"
        if probabilities[side] >= tau:
            return Verdict(
                sentiment=side,
                abstained=False,
                policy=name,
                confidence=probabilities[side],
                score=score,
                probabilities=probabilities,
            )
    confidence = probabilities[top]
    abstained = confidence < min_p
    return Verdict(
        sentiment="neutral" if abstained else top,
        abstained=abstained,
        policy=name,
        confidence=confidence,
        score=score,
        probabilities=probabilities,
    )


def label_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Labels a token's text could start; empty means the grammar would reject it."""
    return {s for s in TIE_ORDER if s.startswith(rest) or rest.startswith(s + '"')}


def sign_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Class implied by a token that starts an enum score (-2..2); empty when the grammar rejects it."""

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProbabilityPolicy:
    """Argmax unless its probability is below min_p (then neutral, abstained). With directional_tau, a
    neutral argmax still yields the likelier directional class when that class reaches tau: models that
    park most of their mass on neutral are otherwise never pushed into a call."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "probability"

    def decide(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, tau=self.directional_tau)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LabelLogprobPolicy:
    """The probability rule (min_p, directional_tau) on first-token label probabilities. On a label
    collision `decide` returns None and the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema; when its sign is
    unreadable too, the chain ends at the ordinal policy."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "label-logprob"

    def decide(self, out: LabelOut | OrdinalOut, chat: ChatResult) -> Verdict | None:
        if isinstance(out, LabelOut):
            probabilities = label_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
            return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities)
        probabilities = score_sign_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
        return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities, score=out.score)

    def threshold(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float], score: int | None = None) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(
            self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, score=score, tau=self.directional_tau
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrdinalPolicy:
    """Directional only when |score| >= t; a zero score is a confident neutral, not an abstention."""

    t: int
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "ordinal"

    def decide(self, score: int) -> Verdict:
        raw = score_sentiment(score)
        abstained = raw != "neutral" and abs(score) < self.t
        return Verdict(
            sentiment="neutral" if abstained else raw, abstained=abstained, policy=self.name, score=score
        )


Policy = ProbabilityPolicy | LabelLogprobPolicy | OrdinalPolicy


def _min_p(spec: ModelSpec) -> float:
    if spec.min_p is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{spec.name}: policy {spec.policy} needs min_p")
    return spec.min_p


def policy_for(spec: ModelSpec, streaming: bool = False, *, endpoint: Endpoint = "signal") -> Policy:
    """Streams and /analyze always threshold the ordinal score: it is read mid-JSON as soon as it
    closes, with no dependency on logprobs or on where the score sits in the output."""
    if spec.kind == "decision":
        return ProbabilityPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
    if streaming or endpoint == "analyze" or spec.policy == "ordinal":
        return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t)
    return LabelLogprobPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
```

```js
 (1) a /signal call with clef-flash:9b-q8_0 showed a "Neutral" pill + "Abstained" tag while the Bullish bar was the largest (73%),
     because clef-flash's frozen min_p is 0.80. The UI never shows the threshold, and nowhere in the UI can you see per-model thresholds.
 (2) "Time to signal 12.3 s" was a cold start (the 10 GB model was not loaded), and the UI gave no hint of that.
Goal: surface the frozen thresholds and cold starts in the API and the UI.

Hard rules for every agent:
- Never run inline Python (python -c, heredocs). Put any ad-hoc script in ${REPO}/.temp/ui-thresholds/ and run it with \`uv run python\`.
- No git commits, no git stash, no pushes. Leave changes in the working tree.
- Do not touch Docker containers, do not stop/unload/pull Ollama models, do not run evals or the latency suite (Kris is testing live).
- Terse WHY-only comments (<=3 lines, no Args/Returns blocks, no ticket refs), never an em-dash anywhere (code, comments, docs, UI copy).
- Match surrounding code style and idioms. Python 3.13, strict mypy, ruff line length 110.
- Quality gate: \`uv run python scripts/check.py --fast\` (unit) and \`uv run python scripts/check.py --full\` (integration, coverage floor,
  frontend lint/typecheck/prettier/vitest/build, openapi + type drift). --backend / --frontend narrow it.
`

const CONTRACT = `
AGREED CONTRACT (implement exactly; names are fixed so backend and frontend agree):

A. Thresholds on every verdict
 - veritrade.inference.types.Verdict gains \`threshold: float | None = None\` and \`directional_tau: float | None = None\`.
 - confidence._threshold sets threshold=min_p and directional_tau=tau (both on the tau-directional early return and the argmax path).
   OrdinalPolicy.decide sets threshold=float(self.t), directional_tau=None.
 - api/contracts.py SignalResult gains
     threshold: float | None = Field(None, description="Frozen cutoff this call was held to: the minimum winning-class probability
       (probability, label-logprob) or the minimum |score| (ordinal).")
     directional_tau: float | None = Field(None, description="When set, a neutral lead still yields the likelier directional class
       once that class reaches this probability.")
   services/pipeline.signal_result maps both.

B. Per-model rules on /api/models
 - New contract model \`SignalRule(_Strict)\`: policy: PolicyName; threshold: float; directional_tau: float | None = None.
 - ModelInfo gains \`signal_rules: dict[Endpoint, SignalRule] = Field(default_factory=dict, description=...)\`: the frozen rule for each
   endpoint of the model that returns a signal ("signal", "analyze"), built from confidence.policy_for(spec, endpoint=e)
   (non-streaming /signal; /analyze is always ordinal). A label-logprob rule still falls back to ordinal on a label collision;
   the listed rule is the primary one. Build it in services/system.py list_models.

C. Cold start
 - InferenceTimings gains \`cold_start: bool | None = Field(None, description="True when the model was not loaded in Ollama (or was
   loaded with another context size) as the request arrived, so the inference time includes loading it; null when unknown.")\`.
 - MetaEvent gains the same \`cold_start: bool | None = None\` so a stream can say "loading the model" before the first token.
 - Detection: Ollama GET /api/ps (OllamaClient.ps() already exists) returns entries like
   {"name":"clef-flash:9b-q8_0","model":"clef-flash:9b-q8_0",...,"context_length":16384}. A pure function (e.g. \`needs_load(spec, entries)\`
   in a small new module such as veritrade/inference/residency.py, or next to Runtime; your call, keep it idiomatic) returns True when no
   entry's name or model equals runtime.tag_name(spec.name); True when spec.kind == "generative" and the entry's context_length is an int
   different from spec.num_ctx (Ollama reloads on a num_ctx change; verified live); else False. Decision models (/v1/systemone) pick their
   own context size, so never compare context for them.
 - The probe runs CONCURRENTLY with the article fetch inside Job.prepare() (pipeline.py) so it adds no latency on a fetch miss: start it as a
   task, await load_article, then await the probe. If load_article raises, cancel the probe and re-raise the ORIGINAL exception (do not use
   TaskGroup/gather in a way that wraps VtError in an ExceptionGroup). The probe is bounded by settings.ollama_probe_timeout_s; on
   TimeoutError, VtError or httpx.HTTPError it yields None (unknown) and the request proceeds. Never catch bare Exception.
 - Prepared carries cold_start; Prepared.timings() puts it into InferenceTimings when inference is not None; Prepared.meta_event() includes it.
   Result-cache hits run no inference and keep cold_start null (cached_meta_event leaves it None).
 - load_ms stays as Ollama reports it (generative only; decision models report none).

D. Regenerate backend/openapi.json with \`uv run python scripts/export_openapi.py\` and frontend/src/lib/api-schema.d.ts with
   \`pnpm --dir frontend gen:api\` (then prettier if the drift check formats it).

E. UI (frontend)
 - SignalCard: when abstained the pill reads "No signal" (keep data-sentiment="neutral", data-abstained, data-testid="signal-badge"), the
   separate "Abstained" tag goes away, and the note explains it with numbers, e.g.
   "Abstained: the top class (Bullish, 73.0%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold, so there is no directional call."
   For ordinal abstentions use the score: "|score| 1 is below the threshold of 2".
 - SignalCard gets a "Threshold" stat rendered from signal.threshold / directional_tau / policy:
     probability or label-logprob with threshold > 0: "call needs >= 80.0%" (use the >= sign glyph);
     with directional_tau: add "bullish/bearish called at >= 28.0% even when neutral leads";
     threshold 0 and no tau: "none (top class wins)"; ordinal: "|score| >= 1". Absent threshold (older payload): omit the stat.
 - Probability bars: a visible threshold marker at threshold when > 0 (all three bars), and a tau marker on the bullish and bearish bars when
   directional_tau is set; markers are decorative for screen readers but the stat above carries the numbers.
 - Cold start: SignalCard "Time to signal" appends a "cold start" note when coldStart is true: "model loaded for this request (X s)" when a
   load time is known, else "includes loading the model into memory". Plumb from /signal JSON timings.inference.cold_start/load_ms and, on
   combined streams, from the meta event (same model) plus done timings. The summary lane: while streaming with no text yet and the meta
   event says cold_start, the placeholder says the model is being loaded into memory (cold start); after done, show the cold start (and load
   time when known) next to the lane's timings (LatencyBar or SummaryPanel; follow existing patterns).
 - Model pickers (AnalyzeForm): for the signal and analyze model selects, append the model's rule for that endpoint from
   /api/models signal_rules to each option label, e.g. "clef-flash:9b-q8_0 (p >= 0.80)", "qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0 (tau 0.28)",
   "qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M (|score| >= 1)". Use the >= glyph. Keep option values unchanged.
 - Update MSW fixtures/handlers in frontend/src/mocks so demo data carries the new fields.
 - Update tests: frontend/tests/unit/SignalCard.test.tsx, integration tests that assert on the badge, and frontend/e2e/analyze.spec.ts's
   SENTIMENT regex must also accept "No signal" (CI's tev1 plumbing model may abstain).
`

const IMPL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },

}

  type: 'object',

        type: 'object',

          fix: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['file', 'severity', 'summary', 'evidence', 'fix'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

phase('Backend')
const be = await agent(`${GROUND}\n${CONTRACT}\n
YOUR TASK: implement parts A, B, C and D (backend half) exactly as specified.
Read first: backend/src/veritrade/api/contracts.py, services/pipeline.py, services/system.py, services/runtime.py,
inference/confidence.py, inference/types.py, inference/ollama.py (ps), config.py (ollama_probe_timeout_s), backend/tests/integration/{conftest,fakes}.py,
and the existing unit tests under backend/tests/unit/inference and backend/tests/unit/services.
Tests to add/update (follow the existing style; each behaviour guarded once at the lowest useful altitude):
 - unit: policies fill threshold/directional_tau (probability with and without tau, label-logprob, ordinal); needs_load cases (absent,
   resident same ctx, resident other ctx generative, decision model with any ctx, ':latest' tag naming); signal_rules from policy_for.
 - integration: FakeOllama gets a /api/ps route (default: every requested model resident at its num_ctx, so existing tests see cold_start
   false) with a way to make a model absent or make ps fail; assert /api/signal carries threshold + cold_start, a stream's meta event carries
   cold_start, a cold model yields true, a ps failure yields null and the request still succeeds, a result-cache hit has no inference timings,
   /api/models lists signal_rules. Keep the coverage floor.
Then regenerate backend/openapi.json (part D, backend side only; do NOT touch frontend/) and run
\`uv run python scripts/check.py --full --backend\` until it passes. Report exact commands and outcomes.`,
  { label: 'backend', phase: 'Backend', schema: IMPL_SCHEMA, model: 'opus' })
log(`backend: ${be ? be.summary.slice(0, 300) : 'agent returned null'}`)

phase('Frontend')
const fe = await agent(`${GROUND}\n${CONTRACT}\n

${JSON.stringify(be)}
YOUR TASK: implement part D (frontend side: \`pnpm --dir frontend gen:api\`) and part E.

frontend/src/lib/{api,run-state,format,sse}.ts, frontend/src/mocks/*, frontend/tests/**, frontend/e2e/analyze.spec.ts.
```
