````markdown
| /analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | full | SSE | 30 | 2,242 | 3,976 | 1,051 | 802 | 3,253 | 2 | 2 | 2,236 | 713 | 1,361 | met (complete p50 2,242/4,000, TTFT p50 1,051/1,500) |
| /analyze | `ministral-3:3b` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,219 | 3,974 | - | 2,219 | 3,516 | 2 | 2 | 2,213 | 713 | 1,350 | met (complete p50 2,219/4,000) |
| /analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | full | SSE | 30 | 2,234 | 4,979 | 1,201 | 1,118 | 3,479 | 2 | 2 | 2,229 | 862 | 1,236 | met (complete p50 2,234/4,000, TTFT p50 1,201/1,500) |
| /analyze | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,243 | 4,969 | - | 2,243 | 3,403 | 2 | 2 | 2,237 | 868 | 1,242 | met (complete p50 2,243/4,000) |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | full | SSE | 30 | 2,584 | 4,627 | 1,292 | 1,098 | 3,570 | 1 | 2 | 2,578 | 992 | 1,539 | met (complete p50 2,584/4,000, TTFT p50 1,292/1,500) |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | full | JSON | 30 | 2,580 | 4,582 | - | 2,580 | 3,544 | 2 | 2 | 2,575 | 992 | 1,504 | met (complete p50 2,580/4,000) |

### What meets and what misses

- **Every generative candidate meets its budgets at p50.** The R7 sanity gate in 01 predicted a TTFT miss for
  `qwen3.5:4b` (2.4 s on ~1.6k-token synthetic inputs); real dev articles after the cascade are shorter (an
  825-token `/summary` prompt at p50), so its TTFT lands at 1,128 ms.
- **Both 9B decision models miss the `/signal` budget** (659 and 1,061 ms; see the trade-off section below).
- **The tails are outside the budgets, which bind only the p50.** Streamed TTFT p95 is 1,108 ms for the 2B and
  2,469 to 2,995 ms for the 3-4B models; complete p95 passes 4 s for `/summary` 4B (4,232) and for `/analyze` on
  both 4B models (4,627 and 4,979). The tail is the long articles: in the raw samples, the two slowest of 30
  requests in every full-scope cell carry about 2,550 to 2,980 prompt tokens (1,990 to 2,200 for `clef-flash`,
  whose article input is capped at 2,000 tokens) against 825 to 1,074 at p50, and write longer.
- In each `qwen3.5:2b` cell, 1 of 30 warm summaries hit `num_predict` and was served cut at a sentence with
  `truncated: true` (01); no other cell truncated. All 165 streamed samples, cold and warm, kept the event
  order (`meta` first, `done` last, one `sentiment` before `done` on `/analyze`).

### Where the time goes

Warm p50s from `latency.json`; per-token rates are ratios of p50s, so approximate.

| endpoint | model | prompt tokens | prompt eval ms | output tokens | eval ms | prompt eval share | decode ms/token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal lede | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 530 | 126 | 7 | 43 | 75% | 6.1 |
| /summary SSE | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M` | 825 | 423 | 92 | 827 | 34% | 9.0 |
| /summary SSE | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 825 | 1,029 | 68 | 1,075 | 49% | 15.8 |
| /analyze SSE | `ministral-3:3b` | 979 | 713 | 92 | 1,361 | 34% | 14.8 |
| /analyze SSE | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | 970 | 862 | 88 | 1,236 | 41% | 14.0 |
| /analyze SSE | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 963 | 992 | 96 | 1,539 | 39% | 16.0 |

- `/signal` is a prefill problem: 7 output tokens (label schema, `num_predict` 16), so prompt length decides
  the time. That is why the quick signal reads the lede (01, Q4).
- The summarisers differ. The 2B spends two thirds decoding; the 4B prefills at about 800 tokens/s against
  about 1,950 for the 2B, so prompt eval is half its time and almost all of its TTFT (1,029 of 1,128 ms).
  Shorter inputs move TTFT; shorter outputs move completion. Warm load is under 1 ms, and everything outside
  inference (parse, extract, input, response) is 3 to 6 ms.

### Streaming, JSON and field order

Same model, same articles: the transport does not change the total (SSE minus JSON is -2.9% to +1.1% at p50),
but SSE shows text at 38 to 54% of it (`/summary` 4B: 1,128 of 2,199 ms). The UI defaults to streaming.

**Sentiment-first field order** (R3) is what makes the streamed signal useful in `/analyze`. The incremental
scanner emits the `sentiment` event as soon as the score closes: 194 to 249 ms before the first summary text,
and 1.4 to 1.5 s before a JSON client would see it (signal 802 / 1,098 ms streamed against 2,219 / 2,580 ms JSON
for `ministral-3:3b` / `qwen3.5:4b`). `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` ignores schema property order and writes the
entity first (01), so its signal leads the summary by only 83 ms.

### Lede against full scope

| model | lede p50 / p95 | full p50 / p95 | prompt tokens lede / full |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 178 / 195 | 231 / 532 | 530 / 1,074 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 659 / 807 | 1,893 / 4,007 | 286 / 831 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 1,061 / 1,182 | 2,321 / 5,242 | 448 / 1,003 |

Full scope costs the 0.8B little at the median but widens every tail: its p95 crosses 500 ms, and the 9B tails
grow 4 to 5 times. Lede keeps `/signal` predictable as well as fast.

### Cold start, parse and extract

- **Cold**: the model load adds 0.7 to 1.3 s over warm for the generative models (load p50 785 to 1,328 ms),
  0.9 to 1.2 s for `nimble` and 5.4 to 6.2 s for `clef-flash` (a 10.58 GB file); n=3, so indicative. A cold 4B
  misses TTFT (2,132 ms for `/summary`). Every call sends `keep_alive` 30m, so only the first request after a
  start or 30 idle minutes pays it.
- **Parse and extract**: 1.2 to 1.6 ms and 1.6 to 2.5 ms at p50 in every cell, under 2% of even the fastest
  `/signal`, so the parser is not a latency lever (03: every parser yields the same body; `selectolax` is
  chosen for speed and footprint). The extractor matters through tokens instead: competent extractors send
  704 to 822 `full` tokens against 2,116 for `strip-tags` (03), and prompt eval scales with that.

## Network

The suite excludes fetch on purpose. Live cost from the source probe ([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md),
EU residential ISP, 2026-10-18): median of the per-source medians 148 ms, slowest 552 ms.

| source | fetch ms (median) | source | fetch ms (median) |
|---|---|---|---|
| bbc | 26 | globenewswire | 552 |
| cnbc | 161 | guardian | 116 |
| cnn | 35 | prnewswire | 34 |
| fool | 202 | sec | 135 |
| fortune | 367 | yahoo | 477 |

As a rough sum of medians (not measured end to end), a lede signal lands about 0.33 s after submit on a
typical source and about 0.73 s on the slowest; on 4 of the 10 sources the fetch takes longer than the signal.
What the service does about it:

- **One pooled HTTP/2 client** (`veritrade.fetch.client`): keep-alive connections (60 s) let a second article
  from the same publisher skip TCP and TLS setup. Deadline 8 s, connect 3 s.
- **Single-flight fetch cache** (`veritrade.fetch.cache`): split mode fires `/signal` and `/summary` at once,
  and the second request joins the first one's in-flight download (`timings.cache.fetch` is `"joined"`), so
  the page is fetched once. Pages live 10 minutes (512 entries, 200 MB); typed fetch errors live 60 s, so a
  refusing publisher is not hit per request.
- **Result cache** (`veritrade.services.cache`): finished responses keyed by (endpoint, url, model, prompt
  version, parser, extractor, scope) for 1 hour; a hit returns with zero stage timings and `meta.cached`.
- **Consent cookie**: the Yahoo reject-all form costs 857 ms once; the shared cookie jar skips it afterwards
  (about 120 ms, 02).

## Split against combined

The UI offers both, split by default. Defaults first, then the other combined candidates; each row measured
alone at concurrency 1.

| arrangement | signal | first summary text | summary complete | resident model files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| split: `/signal` 0.8B lede + `/summary` `qwen3.5:4b` SSE | 178 | 1,128 | 2,199 | 2 (1.02 + 3.32 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b` SSE (default) | 1,098 | 1,292 | 2,584 | 1 (3.32 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `ministral-3:3b` SSE | 802 | 1,051 | 2,242 | 1 (2.95 GB) |
| combined: `/analyze` `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507` SSE | 1,118 | 1,201 | 2,234 | 1 (2.50 GB) |

- **Split** gives the fastest signal, about 0.2 s, while the summary streams, at the cost of two prompts, two
  resident models and two prefills of the same article.
- **Combined** yields the signal at about 0.8 to 1.1 s and the summary by about 2.2 to 2.6 s, from one model
  and one prompt. Its signal is not worse: `qwen3.5:4b` scores dev300 F0.5 0.752 against 0.730 for the 0.8B,
  0.880 against 0.685 on the 30 dev articles (wide CIs, [selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)),
  and 0.871 against 0.801 on the 60 test articles ([holdout](04-evals.md#holdout-results)).
- **Not measured**: split mode's two requests running at once on one GPU; the split row joins two isolated
  measurements, so its summary times are a lower bound for real use.

## /signal: accuracy against latency

| model | dev300 F0.5 [95% CI] | articles dev F0.5 [95% CI] | lede p50 / p95 ms | cold p50 ms | file GB | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.730 [0.651, 0.795] | 0.685 [0.473, 0.833] | 178 / 195 | 992 | 1.02 | served default |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.874 [0.811, 0.937] | 0.848 [0.708, 0.963] | 659 / 807 | 6,064 | 10.58 | misses 500 ms; alone over the 10 GB bundle cap (R8) |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.843 [0.773, 0.901] | 0.895 [0.771, 0.976] | 1,061 / 1,182 | 2,219 | 5.63 | misses 500 ms |

The 9B decision models are 0.11 to 0.14 F0.5 better on dev300 and neither fits the budget, so the 0.8B wins as
the only candidate inside it. The budget was reported, not moved to admit them. Both stay on the allowlist: on
native Ollama a request picks one with the `model` parameter and trades about 0.5 to 0.9 s for a higher F0.5,
mostly recall. The lead holds on unseen tweets and narrows on the test articles, in the one-time holdout
([04-evals.md](04-evals.md#holdout-results), [`holdout.md`](../../../evals/results/holdout/holdout.md)):

| model | test articles lede F0.5 [95% CI] | inversion | coverage | `tfns_val` F0.5 [95% CI] | lede p50 ms |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | 0.801 [0.668, 0.886] | 1/30 | 100% | 0.648 [0.612, 0.679] | 178 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | 0.859 [0.784, 0.938] | 1/44 | 85% | 0.783 [0.761, 0.805] | 659 |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | 0.859 [0.755, 0.938] | 0/32 | 57% | 0.755 [0.730, 0.782] | 1,061 |

The 9B lead is about 0.06 F0.5 on the 60 test articles (overlapping CIs) and 0.11 to 0.14 on 2,388 tweets, where
the CIs separate. The trade-off stands: the 0.8B is the only candidate inside the budget, and the 9B models buy
their accuracy with 0.5 to 0.9 s more per signal.

## docker-cpu

Docker Desktop cannot pass Apple's GPU into a Linux container (01, Q1), so the bundled Ollama runs llama.cpp on
CPU. `latency docker-cpu` measures the bundled defaults over HTTP (`/signal` 0.8B lede JSON; `/summary` and
`/analyze` `qwen3.5:4b`, SSE and JSON), warm n=10 per cell; the app fetches live, so fetch and consent are
subtracted, and it warms up on an 11th dev article. Before every warm phase a reload hook (`container_reload` in
`latency.py`) runs `docker exec ... ollama stop <model>` and waits until `ollama ps` drops it, mirroring the
native unload.

Warm p50 / p95 in ms, copied from the `docker-cpu` section of
[latency.md](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md#docker-cpu); x native divides each docker-cpu p50 by the
native-metal p50 of the same cell above.

| endpoint | model | transport | n warm | p50 ms | p95 ms | TTFT p50 | to signal p50 | x native (complete / TTFT / signal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /signal | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` lede | JSON | 10 | 2,291 | 3,184 | - | 2,291 | 12.9x |
| /summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 10 | 20,820 | 34,195 | 10,169 | - | 9.5x / 9.0x |
| /summary | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | JSON | 10 | 16,357 | 23,560 | - | - | 7.5x |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | SSE | 10 | 30,145 | 40,812 | 13,106 | 10,428 | 11.7x / 10.1x / 9.5x |
| /analyze | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | JSON | 10 | 36,093 | 45,378 | - | 36,093 | 14.0x |

**Conditions.** One pass on 2026-10-19 from 15:40 local time, 50 warm samples, 0 errors. The laptop ran on
battery (67% at the start, 46% at the end), Low Power Mode off, no thermal warning. The 1-minute load average was
7.1 just before the pass and 35-75 during it, and that was the bundled Ollama itself: the Docker VM took most of
the 14 cores, and processes outside it stayed under about 3.7 cores (a watchdog flagged two brief spikes of about
3.6 cores from ordinary desktop apps).

**Every budget is missed.** CPU-only Docker is 7.5 to 14.0 times slower than Metal on this machine: `/signal`
lede takes 2,291 ms against its 500 ms budget, and the 4B shows first text after 10 to 13 s and completes in 16 to
36 s. That is why native Ollama is the macOS default and the bundled profile is for Linux and CI: a portability
path, not a latency path.

**Per token**, docker-cpu is the warm p50 of the raw samples and Metal the ratio of the p50s in "Where the time
goes":

| model | prefill ms/token, docker-cpu / Metal | decode ms/token, docker-cpu / Metal |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | about 3.7 / 0.24 | about 35 / 6.1 |
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | 11 to 14 / 1.0 to 1.2 | about 100 to 200 / 15.8 to 16.0 |

### Discarded passes and run-to-run variance

Two earlier passes were discarded, and neither is committed:

1. **Pass 1 found a prompt-cache bias.** The bundled Ollama has no host port, so the native unload was not
   available, and each JSON cell re-sent the prompts its SSE twin had just evaluated on the same articles;
   those rows showed prompt eval of 118 to 171 ms. The reload hook above is the fix.
2. **Pass 2 had contention in part of the pass.** Other workloads ran during it (another container was starting).
   Its `/signal` cell decoded at about 2.4 s per token, against about 35 ms in the committed pass, and 4
   `/analyze` JSON requests timed out; its 4B cells show the same per-token rates as the committed pass. The whole
   pass was discarded anyway. Its load average proves nothing either way, since a clean pass runs at 35-75 by itself.

Pass 1's rows that the cache bias did not touch (discarded, n=10, not committed) show how far one CPU run lands
from the next on the same protocol:

| cell | pass 1 p50 | committed p50 | committed / pass 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| /signal 0.8B lede JSON | 2,657 | 2,291 | 0.9x |
| /summary 4B SSE, complete | 14,405 | 20,820 | 1.4x |
| /analyze 4B SSE, complete | 12,106 | 30,145 | 2.5x |

CPU-only inference in Docker on a laptop varies about 2x from run to run: the power source, background load and
how the VM's 14 threads land on performance and efficiency cores all move it. The committed rows are one measured
run on battery, not a constant; pass 1 and the committed pass both miss every budget by a wide margin.

`OLLAMA_CPUS` in `compose.yaml` sets a `cpus:` quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota
below the visible core count can make CPU inference slower rather than just capped; a cpuset or `num_thread` is
the fix (backlog).

## Levers

Used:
- **Input and model size**: lede scope for `/signal` (half the tokens of full, p95 195 ms instead of 532); a
  cascade that sends about 720 `full` tokens where `strip-tags` sends about 2,100 (03); the smallest `/signal`
  model that clears the accuracy filters, answering in 7 tokens.
- **Perceived latency**: SSE, sentiment-first field order and an incremental JSON scanner.
- **Warm models**: `keep_alive` 30m on every call; `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` 3 native (2 bundled) keeps both
  split-mode models resident; flash attention and a q8_0 KV cache in the Ollama env.
- **Bounded generation**: `think: false`, greedy decoding, per-endpoint `num_predict`, and the served summary
  cap of 3 sentences / 60 words (01).
- **Network and hops**: pooled HTTP/2, single-flight fetch cache, result cache, consent cookie reuse; the UI is
  served by the same FastAPI process (R1), and the fast parsers extract inline, without a thread hand-off.

Left: the latency items in [90-optional-backlog.md](90-optional-backlog.md) (progressive `/signal`, split-mode
concurrency, a GPU compose profile, CPU threads for the bundled Ollama, latency under load), plus:
- Preload the default models at app start, so the first request does not pay 0.7 to 1.3 s of load.
- Trim the 4B prompts: prompt eval is half of `/summary` and nearly all of its TTFT.
- Start the fetch when a URL is pasted, before submit, to hide part of the network cost.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency preflight   # records the machine; fails while Docker containers run
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency run         # native suite, resumable; writes latency.{json,md}
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency docker-cpu --base-url http://localhost:8000   # bundled stack up first
uv run python -m veritrade_evals latency report      # re-aggregates the raw samples
```

The native run needs the private article HTML (`articles verify` passes) and an otherwise idle machine.
````

````markdown
# 00 - Overview

VeriTrade analysts lose minutes reading breaking news to gauge sentiment. This PoC takes a public financial-news
URL and returns a short summary plus a Bullish / Bearish / Neutral signal, optimised for latency and for
**precision of directional calls** (a wrong call costs a trade; a missed call costs little).

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

Two architectures are compared head to head:

- **Split**: a fast signal model (a decision model or a tiny LLM) answers `/signal` while a summariser streams
  `/summary` in parallel.
- **Combined**: one haiku-grade model produces score + summary in a single call (`/analyze`).

## Sources

Any public URL is accepted. The source profiles and the evaluation cover the final 10, chosen by a live probe
([02-source-probe.md](02-source-probe.md), [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml)):
Yahoo Finance, CNBC, The Motley Fool, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, SEC EDGAR 8-K EX-99.1, CNN Business, Fortune,
The Guardian Business and BBC Business. AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain client at
their CDN and are rejected rather than evaded.

## Outcome

The defaults were picked by the rules in [`selection.md`](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md): `/signal`
serves `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.730, lede p50 178 ms), and `/summary` and `/analyze` both serve
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (judge faithfulness 4.40 of 5; `/analyze` dev300 F0.5 0.752, complete p50 2,584 ms), so the
bundled profile pulls just those two models, 4.34 GB. The 9B decision models score higher
(`clef-flash:9b-q8_0` dev300 F0.5 0.874, mostly through recall: its bullish / bearish precision is 0.867 / 0.905
against 0.914 / 0.918 for the 0.8B) but miss the 500 ms `/signal` budget (p50 659 ms), so the default trades recall
for speed, and the 9B models stay selectable per request on native Ollama. Details:
[01 selection outcome](01-decisions.md#selection-outcome), [04-evals.md](04-evals.md), [05-latency.md](05-latency.md).

The one-time holdout on unseen test splits ([`holdout.md`](../../../evals/results/holdout/holdout.md)) leaves the
three defaults as frozen, with nothing re-tuned: test-article F0.5 0.801 for `/signal` (dev 0.685) and 0.871 for
`/analyze` (dev 0.880), and `/summary` judge faithfulness 4.37 (dev 4.40). Two weak spots remain: the
`/signal` default inverts 1 of 30 directional calls (3.3%, above the 2% cap as a point estimate, as on the dev
articles, 1 of 14), and `/analyze` summaries degrade on unseen articles (faithfulness 4.17, material errors 25%
against 10% on dev).
````

```markdown
# 90 - Optional backlog

What we would do with more time. This is a PoC and rigor was balanced per aspect (R2 in
[01-decisions.md](01-decisions.md)), so each item below marks a place where we stopped on purpose. Every item gives
the reason and the expected payoff; items are ranked by impact within their group, highest first. Items that an
earlier doc or a results file already names as future work link back to it.

## Accuracy

1. **A DSPy-style prompt optimiser instead of the hand grid** (Q7). The lean grid tried up to 8 configs per model
   with synthetic shots. An optimiser over instructions, shot selection and the decision rule, scored on dev300 F0.5
   under the 2% inversion cap, searches far wider. The largest lever found by hand was a decision rule
   (`directional_tau`, +0.218 F0.5 for `qwen3.5:0.8b`, [grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)).
2. **Distil the 9B decision model into the sub-second tier.** Label a large unlabelled stream of headlines and ledes
   with `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` (dev300 F0.5 0.874), then fine-tune `qwen3.5:0.8b` or a small classifier head on its
   calls. Payoff: part of the 0.874 vs 0.730 gap at the 178 ms tier, without a 10.58 GB model
   ([selection.md](../../../evals/results/selection/selection.md)).
3. **Logprob-weighted confidence for streamed `/analyze`.** Streams already carry logprobs (undocumented, see
   [01 build-time findings](01-decisions.md#build-time-findings-that-adjusted-the-plan)), so the ordinal
   `|score| >= 1` rule could become a tunable probability threshold like `/signal`'s. It needs a sign-safe score
   encoding: the qwen3.5 tokenizer fuses the space and minus sign, which hid the sign of negative scores in the
   0.8b grid.
4. **Serve the number-grounding check.** The summary eval already checks every number against the source; running
   it on each served summary and flagging sentences with unsupported numbers needs no model call. The `/summary`
   winner still has an unsupported detail (minor slips included) in 50% and a material error in 10% of dev summaries
   ([summary eval](../../../evals/results/summary/summary.md)), and numbers are the slips a trader acts on.
5. **A rubric for mixed results.** Earnings and guidance tweets hold the most wrong calls for their size (13 in 46,
   against 14 in 128 for the catch-all bucket), which fits a beat alongside a cut outlook. An aspect-level output
   (results vs outlook) or an explicit mixed rule targets the content type the brief names.
6. **Decide price moves before tuning for them.** The rubrics ask for economic impact, so the generative models miss
   33-38 of 57 directional price-move tweets, while the `/analyze` models miss only 0-1 of the 5 directional
   price-move headlines in the article dev set ([articles dev notes](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/notes.md)).
   Whether a reported move is directional is a product call; the rubric sentence the error pass left out is ready
   if the answer is yes.
7. **Revisit dropped candidates when their bugs close.** Gemma 4 (think + format bug) and `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`
   ignoring schema property order and `think:false` under a schema. Low effort, more combined-endpoint candidates.

## Latency and serving

1. **Analyse on publish, not on request.** The 10 sources already have `feeds` / `sections` in
   [`sources.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), and the evals' discovery code reads them.
   Polling them and analysing new articles ahead of time turns a request into a cache hit; the cost is inference on
   articles nobody opens.
2. **Progressive `/signal`.** Return the 0.8b verdict at 178 ms, then replace it when a 9B decision model answers
   (clef-flash lede p50 659 ms, [latency.md](../../../evals/results/latency/latency.md)). On the article dev set the
   default catches 10 of 20 directional articles and clef-flash 17 of 20, with 1 inversion each
   ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)).
3. **A GPU compose profile.** A `gpu` profile with a device reservation would give Linux hosts with a CUDA GPU the
   bundled path at native-like speed. CPU-only Docker measured 7.5-14.0x slower than Metal on the build machine
   and over every budget ([05](05-latency.md#docker-cpu)).
4. **Split-mode concurrency on one Ollama.** The latency suite runs at client concurrency 1, yet split mode fires
   `/signal` and `/summary/stream` at once against two resident models on one GPU. Measure that pair, then tune
   `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` and `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS` (3 native, 2 bundled). Payoff: the split-mode TTFT a user
   actually sees.
5. **A batching server for throughput.** Beyond a handful of analysts, a server with continuous batching (vLLM, or
   llama.cpp server with parallel slots) serves many concurrent streams per GPU. Cost: a second serving stack and
   model format beside Ollama.
6. **CPU threads for the bundled Ollama.** `OLLAMA_CPUS` in [`compose.yaml`](../../../compose.yaml) sets a CPU
   quota, which does not lower llama.cpp's thread count, so a quota below the visible cores can slow inference
   rather than cap it. Pin a `cpuset` or set `num_thread` to match. Payoff: predictable CPU latency in CI and on
   shared hosts.
7. **Trim the remaining story tails.** The cascade still leaks 13-15% of tokens on Yahoo, PR Newswire and
   GlobeNewswire, mostly after the story ([03](03-extraction.md)). That costs prompt-eval time and summary focus on
   the `full` scope, not the lede.
8. **Start `/signal` on a partial body.** The lede sits early in the HTML, so parsing a streamed prefix could start
   inference before the download ends. The payoff is bounded by transfer time, so mostly on large pages (CNN
   5.7 MB).

## Data and evaluation

1. **A human-checked article set and a larger test set.** The 90 articles are labelled by Opus only (two labellers
   and an adjudicator). With 10 per class on dev a gap needs about 0.2 F0.5 to clear zero, so most article
   comparisons are ties ([articles dev](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md)). A few hundred
   human-checked articles would separate finalists that tie today.
2. **Extraction beyond the top 10.** Any public URL is accepted, but the matrix covers only profiled sources; other
   publishers fall through to JSON-LD and `density`, unmeasured. A set of other publishers would show whether
   `trafilatura-precision`, the source-agnostic candidate in [03](03-extraction.md), should back the cascade there.
3. **Entity-level and multi-entity sentiment data.** Labels are for the article's primary entity, and the public
   sets are sentence- or headline-level (FinEntity only in its single-label rows). Entity-level data would measure
   the question an analyst asks ("bullish for whom?") and back entity-targeted requests.
4. **Fresh pages for the three tuned profiles.** GlobeNewswire, PR Newswire and Yahoo were tightened on the pages
   they are scored on, so the honest cascade F1 is 0.929 and 0.959 is in-sample ([03](03-extraction.md)).
5. **Resample the threshold choice.** Grid CIs hold the operating point fixed, so they are optimistic
   ([grid summary](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md)). A nested bootstrap or a separate threshold split would
   give honest CIs on the precision knobs.
6. **A sharper key-fact metric.** Embedding coverage agrees with hand labels on 33 of 45 facts at cosine 0.60. A
   per-fact entailment check would track the Opus judge more closely and could gate summary prompts in CI.
7. **Latency on a dedicated host and under load.** Grid and extraction timings came from a shared workstation,
   contention stalled the `/signal` cell and timed out 4 `/analyze` requests in a discarded docker-cpu pass, and
   docker-cpu p50s varied about 2x between passes on the same laptop
   ([05](05-latency.md#discarded-passes-and-run-to-run-variance)). A dedicated runner plus a 1 / 4 / 16 client sweep
   would give p95s fit for capacity planning.
8. **A label-noise pass.** 20 directional dev300 tweets get no correct call from any model
   ([grid notes](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)); review them before reading that recall loss as model error.
9. **A second vantage point for the source probe.** One EU residential IP chose the final 10, and datacenter IPs
   meet stricter bot management ([02](02-source-probe.md)). Probe from where the service would run.

## Product and API

1. **Entity-targeted requests.** Accept a ticker or entity and answer for it, and return per-entity calls for
   multi-entity articles, where one story can be bullish for one company and bearish for another. Depends on data
   item 3.
2. **Licensed feeds for the blocked sources.** AP News, Investing.com, Benzinga and Business Wire refuse a plain
   client at their CDN, and evasion is ruled out (Q19). Licensed APIs or feeds would add four widely read sources.
3. **A per-request precision knob.** Thresholds are frozen per model; an override of `min_p` / `directional_tau`
   within the dev300 operating curve would let a desk trade recall for precision without a redeploy.
4. **Non-HTML content.** PDF exhibits and attachments return `unsupported_content`, yet earnings decks and some
   filings arrive that way.
5. **Non-English news.** Discovery skips non-English items and every prompt is English; EU and Asian sources need
   multilingual prompts and their own labelled set.

## Operations

1. **Auth and inbound rate limiting.** The API has no authentication and no per-client limit; the only limiter is
   outbound, for EDGAR ([`client.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/fetch/client.py)). API keys or SSO plus per-key
   quotas come before it leaves localhost. The SSRF guard is already in place.
2. **Source DOM drift monitoring beyond the weekly live smoke.**
   [`live-smoke.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/live-smoke.yml) runs weekly and never gates. Profiles depend on selectors, and Guardian, BBC and Yahoo hash class names. A
   daily canary over fresh feed items that alerts when the cascade falls back from `profile` to `density`, body
   word counts drop, or `source_blocked` rises would catch silent degradation. No backup sources remain.
3. **Observability.** Every response already carries per-stage timings. Exported as traces and histograms
   (OpenTelemetry) with alerts on the R7 budgets, they make the latency report a live one.
4. **A shared cache (Redis) with distributed single-flight.** Fetch and result caches are in-process, so each
   replica fetches the same breaking story and a restart empties them. A shared store with a short lock keeps one
   fetch per URL across replicas.
5. **Quality monitoring.** Shadow-score a sample of served `/signal` calls with a 9B decision model and judge a
   sample of summaries offline; alert when agreement drops. It catches model, prompt or publisher drift that
   latency metrics miss.
6. **Pin models by digest and gate upgrades.** Eval manifests record model digests. Serving only digests that
   passed `freeze` and the holdout keeps served behaviour equal to measured behaviour across `ollama pull` and
   Ollama upgrades.

```

```
# Serving config: allowlist, per-endpoint defaults, decoding options and frozen thresholds.
# `veritrade_evals freeze` writes the per-model thresholds and prompt versions from the eval results
# (evals/results/frozen.json); `select --write` owns [defaults]. Models it has not frozen keep provisional values.
#
# kind        generative (/api/chat) | decision (/v1/systemone)
# endpoints   endpoints the model may serve
# signal_schema   generative signal output: "label" (one of 3 labels) | "ordinal" (score -2..2)
# policy      probability | label-logprob | ordinal  (streaming and /analyze always use ordinal)
# min_p       decision/label-logprob threshold on the winning class probability; 0 never abstains
# directional_tau   optional, probability policies only: when neutral wins the argmax and the likelier
#             directional class has p >= tau, call that class; otherwise argmax + min_p applies
# ordinal_t   directional call only when |score| >= ordinal_t (always set: streaming fallback)
# field_order /analyze JSON order: sentiment-first (streams the score early) | summary-first
# prompt      frozen prompt version per endpoint, e.g. { signal = "v4" }; an endpoint left out serves
#             the prompt file's `active` version

signal = "qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0"

analyze = "qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M"
```

```typescript
/** Compact frozen rule for an option label, e.g. "p ≥ 0.80", "tau 0.28" or "|score| ≥ 1". */
export function ruleLabel(rule: SignalRule | undefined): string | null {
  if (!rule) return null;
  if (rule.policy === "ordinal") return `|score| ≥ ${rule.threshold}`;
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (rule.threshold > 0) parts.push(`p ≥ ${rule.threshold.toFixed(2)}`);
  if (typeof rule.directional_tau === "number") parts.push(`tau ${rule.directional_tau.toFixed(2)}`);
  return parts.length ? parts.join(", ") : "no threshold";
}

/** Explains only the notations that appear in this picker. */
export function ruleHint(rules: readonly SignalRule[]): string | null {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (rules.some((r) => r.policy !== "ordinal" && r.threshold > 0)) {
    parts.push("p ≥ x means the top class needs probability x or more");
  }
  if (rules.some((r) => typeof r.directional_tau === "number")) {
    parts.push("tau x means bullish or bearish is called at x even when neutral leads");
  }
  if (rules.some((r) => r.policy === "ordinal")) {
    parts.push("|score| ≥ n means the -2..+2 score needs magnitude n or more");
  }
  return parts.length
    ? `In brackets, each model's frozen rule for a directional call. ${parts.join("; ")}.`
    : null;
}

function modelLabel(model: ModelInfo, endpoint: Endpoint, isDefault: boolean): string {
  const rule = ruleLabel(model.signal_rules?.[endpoint]);
  const name = rule ? `${model.name} (${rule})` : model.name;
  const notes = [
    isDefault ? "default" : null,
    model.installed ? null : "not installed",
    model.evaluated ? null : "CI plumbing, unevaluated",
  ].filter(Boolean);
  return notes.length ? `${name} (${notes.join(", ")})` : name;
}

interface ModelSelectProps {
  label: string;
  endpoint: Endpoint;
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  models: ModelsState;
}
```

```typescript
import type { PolicyName, Sentiment, SignalResult } from "@/lib/api";
import { capitalize, coldStartNote, formatMs, formatPct } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./SignalCard.module.css";

const POLICY_NOTES: Record<PolicyName, string> = {
  probability: "threshold on the decision model's class probability",
  "label-logprob": "threshold on the label token probability",
  ordinal: "threshold on |score| of the -2..+2 scale",
};

const ORDER: readonly Sentiment[] = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

/** Direction the model leaned before the threshold turned it into an abstention. */
export function leaning(signal: SignalResult): Sentiment {
  if (signal.probabilities) {
    let best: Sentiment = signal.sentiment;
    for (const s of ORDER) {
      if ((signal.probabilities[s] ?? 0) > (signal.probabilities[best] ?? 0)) best = s;
    }
    return best;
  }
  if (typeof signal.score === "number" && signal.score !== 0) return signal.score > 0 ? "bullish" : "bearish";
  return signal.sentiment;
}

// Non-breaking, so a wrapped line never strands the sign away from its number.
const AT_LEAST = "≥ ";

/** The frozen rule this call was held to, in words; null for payloads that predate thresholds. */
export function thresholdText(signal: SignalResult): string | null {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  if (typeof threshold !== "number") return null;
  if (signal.policy === "ordinal") return `|score| ${AT_LEAST}${threshold}`;
  const hasTau = typeof tau === "number";
  if (threshold <= 0 && !hasTau) return "none (top class wins)";
  const base = threshold > 0 ? `call needs ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(threshold)}` : "top class wins";
  return hasTau
    ? `${base}; bullish/bearish called at ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(tau)} even when neutral leads`
    : base;
}

/** Why the call abstained, with the numbers when the payload carries the threshold. */
export function abstainReason(signal: SignalResult): string {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  if (typeof threshold === "number") {
    if (signal.policy === "ordinal" && typeof signal.score === "number") {
      return `|score| ${Math.abs(signal.score)} (leaning ${capitalize(lean)}) is below this model's threshold of ${threshold}`;
    }
    const p = signal.probabilities?.[lean];
    if (typeof p === "number") {
      const reason = `the top class (${capitalize(lean)}, ${formatPct(p)}) is below this model's ${formatPct(threshold)} threshold`;
      // tau only rescues a neutral lead, so it is part of the reason only then.
      return lean === "neutral" && typeof tau === "number"
        ? `${reason}, and neither Bullish nor Bearish reached ${formatPct(tau)}`
        : reason;
    }
  }
  const leaned = lean === "neutral" ? "" : ` (it leaned ${capitalize(lean)})`;
  return `the call is below this model's confidence threshold${leaned}`;
}

function formatScore(score: number): string {
  return score > 0 ? `+${score}` : String(score);
}

// Rounded to 0.1% so float noise (0.28 * 100) never reaches the style attribute.
const share = (value: number) => `${Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value)) * 1000) / 10}%`;

interface SignalCardProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity?: string | null;
  model?: string | null;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the signal arriving. */
  timeToSignalMs?: number | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on a combined stream. */
  serverMs?: number | null;
  /** The model had to be loaded for this request. */
  coldStart?: boolean | null;
  /** Ollama's model load time; decision models report none. */
  loadMs?: number | null;
}

export function SignalCard({ status, signal, coldStart, ...rest }: SignalCardProps) {
  const busy = !signal && (status === "pending" || status === "streaming");
  return (
    <section className={styles.card} aria-labelledby="signal-heading" aria-busy={busy}>
      <h2 id="signal-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Signal
      </h2>
      {signal ? (
        <SignalBody signal={signal} coldStart={coldStart} {...rest} />
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.placeholder}>
          {busy
            ? coldStart
              ? "Waiting for the signal while the model loads into memory (cold start)..."
              : "Waiting for the signal..."
            : status === "cancelled"
              ? "Cancelled."
              : "No signal: the request failed."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

type SignalBodyProps = Omit<SignalCardProps, "status" | "signal"> & { signal: SignalResult };

function SignalBody({ signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs, coldStart, loadMs }: SignalBodyProps) {
  const rule = thresholdText(signal);
  const thresholdMark =
    signal.policy !== "ordinal" && typeof signal.threshold === "number" && signal.threshold > 0
      ? signal.threshold
      : null;
  const tauMark = typeof signal.directional_tau === "number" ? signal.directional_tau : null;
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <span
          className={styles.badge}
          data-sentiment={signal.sentiment}
          data-abstained={signal.abstained || undefined}
          data-testid="signal-badge"
        >
          {signal.abstained ? "No signal" : capitalize(signal.sentiment)}
        </span>
        {entity ? <span className={styles.entity}>{entity}</span> : null}
      </div>
      {signal.abstained ? (
        <p className={styles.abstainNote} data-testid="abstain-note">
          Abstained: {abstainReason(signal)}, so there is no directional call.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <dl className={styles.stats}>
        {typeof signal.confidence === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Confidence</dt>
            <dd>{formatPct(signal.confidence)}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof signal.score === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Score</dt>
            <dd>{formatScore(signal.score)} on -2..+2</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <div>
          <dt>Policy</dt>
          <dd>
            <code>{signal.policy}</code> <span className={styles.note}>({POLICY_NOTES[signal.policy]})</span>
          </dd>
        </div>
        {rule ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Threshold</dt>
            <dd data-testid="signal-threshold">{rule}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {model ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Model</dt>
            <dd>
              <code>{model}</code>
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof timeToSignalMs === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Time to signal</dt>
            <dd>
              {formatMs(timeToSignalMs)}
              {typeof serverMs === "number" ? (
                <span className={styles.note}> (server {formatMs(serverMs)})</span>
              ) : null}
              {coldStart ? (
                <span className={styles.cold} data-testid="signal-cold-start">
                  <span className={styles.tag}>Cold start</span> {coldStartNote(loadMs)}
                </span>
              ) : null}
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </dl>
      {signal.probabilities ? (
        <>
          <ul className={styles.probs} aria-label="Class probabilities">
            {ORDER.map((s) => {
              const p = signal.probabilities?.[s] ?? 0;
              return (
                <li key={s} className={styles.prob}>
                  <span className={styles.probLabel}>{capitalize(s)}</span>
                  <span className={styles.probTrack} aria-hidden="true">
                    <span className={styles.probFill} data-sentiment={s} style={{ width: share(p) }} />
                    {thresholdMark !== null ? (
                      <span
                        className={styles.probMark}
                        data-kind="threshold"
                        data-testid={`mark-threshold-${s}`}
                        style={{ left: share(thresholdMark) }}
                      />
                    ) : null}
                    {tauMark !== null && s !== "neutral" ? (
                      <span
                        className={styles.probMark}
                        data-kind="tau"
                        data-testid={`mark-tau-${s}`}
                        style={{ left: share(tauMark) }}
                      />
                    ) : null}
                  </span>
                  <span className={styles.probValue}>{formatPct(p)}</span>
                </li>
              );
            })}
          </ul>
          {thresholdMark !== null || tauMark !== null ? (
            <p className={styles.markLegend} aria-hidden="true">
              {thresholdMark !== null ? (
                <span>
                  <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="threshold" />
                  threshold {formatPct(thresholdMark)}
                </span>
              ) : null}
              {tauMark !== null ? (
                <span>
                  <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="tau" />
                  tau {formatPct(tauMark)} (bullish/bearish)
                </span>
              ) : null}
            </p>
          ) : null}
        </>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}

```

```markdown
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): first label-token probabilities, renormalised over the tokens the grammar
  accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still yields the likelier
  directional class when that class holds p >= tau; below tau the row is a served neutral, not an abstention. On a
  first-token label collision the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streams, fallback): a score from -2 to 2, directional only when \|score\| >= t. It is read
  mid-stream as soon as it closes and needs no logprobs (Q3); logprob-weighted streaming confidence is on the backlog.

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default (headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200
tokens); `lede` and `full` are both scored on articles. `/analyze` reads `full` and emits the sentiment field first,
so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error analysis and freeze.** One hand-written read of the grid counts
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)) drove the changes listed in section 5. The `freeze`
command then wrote [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json) and
[`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml):

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze` takes v5
unless the whole paired 95% CI of its gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles, which rejected v5 for
`qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first needed a dev300 win without an articles loss; it never
got one.
```

```markdown
## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` + `/summary`; the combined one `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells ([`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json)), all on
native Metal, Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0, sampling penalties neutralised; see the build-time
findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic shots =
  v1-v4; for `qwen3.5:0.8b` each runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: rubric or plain one-line question x described or bare criteria = v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the field-order
  check, on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): argmax of the native class probabilities; abstain when it is below `min_p`.
```

<details>
<summary><code>~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/README.md</code></summary>

````markdown
URL='https://...'   # any public article URL
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/signal -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
curl -sN http://localhost:8000/api/analyze/stream -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
```

**SSE order.** `meta` (article meta, fetch / parse / extract timings, `cold_start`) once extraction is done, so a
stream can say the model is loading before its first token; on `/analyze/stream`
one `sentiment` event as soon as the score closes (served field order: sentiment-first); `summary_delta` text
chunks; `done` with the full JSON response. A failure before the stream opens is a JSON error with its HTTP status,
after that one `error` event; a closed connection stops the upstream generation.

**Errors** share one envelope, `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "retryable", "upstream_status"}}`
([`errors.py`](backend/src/veritrade/errors.py), [`contracts.py`](backend/src/veritrade/api/contracts.py)); other
request-body validation errors, such as an unknown `parser`, `extractor` or `scope` or an extra field, return
FastAPI's standard 422 `{"detail": [...]}`.

| HTTP | Codes | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_url`, `blocked_destination`, `model_not_allowed` | Malformed URL; SSRF guard (private or reserved address, a port other than 80/443); model not on the allowlist or disabled by `VT_MODELS`, or not served on that endpoint |
| 422 | `paywalled`, `consent_required`, `extraction_empty`, `unsupported_content`, `too_large` | Fetched, but no usable article: paywall, consent wall, under 40 words, not HTML (PDF, feed), over 10 MB |
| 502 | `source_blocked`, `upstream_http`, `schema_violation` | Publisher refused (CDN bot wall, 401/403/429/451, with a hint to a syndicated copy); other upstream HTTP error; malformed model output |
| 503 | `model_unavailable`, `llm_unreachable` | Model not pulled (the hint gives the `ollama pull` command); Ollama down |
| 504 | `upstream_timeout`, `inference_timeout` | Fetch deadline (8 s); inference timeout (90 s) |

## Architecture
````

```diff
+### Thresholds and "No signal"
+
+Every model's confidence rule is frozen per model and endpoint. The served source of truth is
+[`models.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) (`policy`, `min_p`, `directional_tau`, `ordinal_t`),
+written by `veritrade_evals freeze`, with the evidence behind each value (dev300 and dev-article F0.5, inversions and
+coverage at that threshold) in [`frozen.json`](evals/results/frozen.json); the policies are explained in
+[04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#4-models-prompts-and-confidence-policies). As frozen:
+
+| Model | `/signal` rule | `/analyze` rule |
+|---|---|---|
+| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (`/signal` default) | label-logprob, `min_p` 0, tau 0.28 | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 |
+| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | probability, `min_p` 0.80 | - |
+| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | probability, `min_p` 0.97 | - |
+| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (`/analyze` default), `ministral-3:3b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | - | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 |
+| `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` (CI plumbing, never evaluated) | probability, `min_p` 0.50 (provisional) | - |
+
+- **Where to see them**: the signal and analyze pickers in the UI; the **Threshold** row and the threshold and tau
+  marks on every signal card; `GET /api/models`, whose `signal_rules` maps each signal endpoint of a model to its
+  `policy`, `threshold` and `directional_tau`; and every `signal` in a response, which carries the `threshold` and
+  `directional_tau` it was held to. A label-logprob rule falls back to ordinal \|score\| >= 1 on a first-token label
+  collision; `signal_rules` lists the primary rule.
+- **"No signal" is an abstention, by design** (precision over recall, Q2 and Q3): when the winning class is below
+  the model's frozen threshold, the service returns `sentiment: "neutral"` with `abstained: true` instead of a
+  directional call it is not confident in. The UI shows **No signal** and says why, e.g. "Abstained: the top class
+  (Bullish, 73.0%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold, so there is no directional call." A neutral with
+  `abstained: false` is a neutral verdict. With these rules only the 9B decision models abstain (dev300 coverage
+  72.9% for clef-flash, 26.3% for nimble); the defaults hold back by answering neutral
+  ([design decisions](#design-decisions)).
+
```

```markdown
## Design decisions

Every decision was settled in an interview before any code was written; the full table, with the question each one
answers, is in [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md).

- **Open-weight models on a local Ollama** ([Q1](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md#round-1)): everything runs and
  reproduces with no API key or paid service. Native Metal is the macOS default because Docker Desktop cannot reach
  the Apple GPU; a `bundled` CPU profile covers Linux and CI.
- **Precision first** (Q2): a wrong directional call costs a trade, a missed one little, so selection uses F0.5 macro
  over bullish and bearish with inversions capped at 2% ([04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#1-objective-and-metrics)).
- **Abstain rather than guess** (Q3): thresholds on decision-model class probabilities, on label-token probabilities
  (`/signal`, plus `directional_tau`) or on an ordinal -2..+2 score (`/analyze`, works mid-stream); every signal
  reports `abstained` and the threshold it was held to ([per model](#thresholds-and-no-signal)). The frozen
  defaults never abstain (dev300 coverage 100%): the 0.8B runs at `min_p` 0 with
  tau 0.28 and `/analyze` at \|s\| >= 1 on integer scores, so they hold back by answering neutral; only the 9B
  decision models abstain (dev300 coverage 72.9% and 26.3%).
- **Split and combined, both served** (Q8): a fast signal model next to a summariser, or one model for score, entity
  and summary; the UI switches and both were measured ([05](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md#split-against-combined)).
- **The quick signal reads the lede** (Q4): headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200 tokens; `/signal`
  answers in about 7 tokens, so prompt length is its latency.
- **Stream, sentiment first** (R3): the schema puts the score first and an incremental scanner emits it as it closes.
- **One origin** ([R1](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md#round-2)): FastAPI serves the static Next.js export; no
  proxy hop, no Node at runtime.
- **Extraction measured, not assumed** (Q10, R4): 22 parser x extractor rows on 90 real articles; the served
  `selectolax` + `cascade` is best or tied on quality and has the lowest tail of any row that finds bodies (p95
```

```
"""Steps every article endpoint shares: resolve, check the result cache, load, describe."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass

from veritrade.api.contracts import (
    AnalyzeDoneEvent,
    AnalyzeRequest,
    AnalyzeResponse,
    ArticleMeta,
    CacheInfo,
    ErrorEvent,
    InferenceTimings,
    MetaEvent,
    SentimentEvent,
    SignalRequest,
    SignalResponse,
    SignalResult,
    SummaryDeltaEvent,
    SummaryDoneEvent,
    SummaryRequest,
    SummaryResponse,
    Timings,
)
from veritrade.extract.scope import build_input
from veritrade.extract.types import Scope
from veritrade.fetch import normalize_url
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, DecisionResult, Endpoint, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptSpec
from veritrade.services.article import LoadedArticle, load_article
from veritrade.services.cache import ResultKey
from veritrade.services.runtime import Runtime
from veritrade.timing import StageTimer

ArticleRequest = SignalRequest | SummaryRequest | AnalyzeRequest
StreamPayload = (
    MetaEvent | SentimentEvent | SummaryDeltaEvent | SummaryDoneEvent | AnalyzeDoneEvent | ErrorEvent
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Job:
    """A request with its model and prompt resolved; nothing has touched the network yet."""

    runtime: Runtime
    endpoint: Endpoint
    request: ArticleRequest
    url: str
    scope: Scope
    spec: ModelSpec
    prompt: PromptSpec
    key: ResultKey | None
    clock: StageTimer

    @classmethod
    def resolve(
        cls, runtime: Runtime, endpoint: Endpoint, request: ArticleRequest, *, scope: Scope, clock: StageTimer
    ) -> Job:
        spec = runtime.registry.resolve(endpoint, request.model)
        prompt = runtime.prompt(endpoint, spec)
        url = str(request.url)
        key = None
        if not request.no_cache:
            key = ResultKey(
                endpoint=endpoint,
                url=normalize_url(url),
                model=spec.name,
                prompt_version=prompt.version,
                parser=request.parser,
                extractor=request.extractor,
                scope=scope,
            )
        return cls(runtime, endpoint, request, url, scope, spec, prompt, key, clock)

    def cached[R: (SignalResponse, SummaryResponse, AnalyzeResponse)](self, kind: type[R]) -> R | None:
        """The stored response marked as cached, with timings that describe this request."""
        hit = self.runtime.results.get(self.key) if self.key is not None else None
        if not isinstance(hit, kind):
            return None
        # A result hit runs no stage, so stage timings are zero and the article counts as a fetch hit.
        timings = Timings(
            total_ms=self.clock.elapsed_ms(),
            fetch_ms=0.0,
            parse_ms=0.0,
            extract_ms=0.0,
            cache=CacheInfo(fetch="hit", result="hit"),
        )
        meta = hit.meta.model_copy(update={"cached": True})
        return hit.model_copy(update={"meta": meta, "timings": timings})

    def remember(self, response: SignalResponse | SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse) -> None:
        if self.key is not None:
            self.runtime.results.put(self.key, response)

    async def prepare(self) -> Prepared:
        # The residency probe runs alongside the fetch; a fetch error still propagates as itself, unwrapped.
        probe = asyncio.create_task(self.runtime.cold_start(self.spec))
        try:
            loaded = await load_article(
                self.runtime,
                self.url,
                parser=self.request.parser,
                extractor=self.request.extractor,
                no_cache=self.request.no_cache,
            )
        except BaseException:
            probe.cancel()
            raise
        cold_start = await probe
        text = build_input(loaded.article, self.scope, self.spec.max_input_tokens)
        return Prepared(
            job=self,
            loaded=loaded,
            text=text,
            meta=self._meta(loaded, text),
            cache=CacheInfo(fetch=loaded.fetch_status, result="bypass" if self.key is None else "miss"),
            cold_start=cold_start,
        )

    def _meta(self, loaded: LoadedArticle, text: str) -> ArticleMeta:
        article = loaded.article
        return ArticleMeta(
            url=self.url,
            final_url=loaded.page.final_url,
            title=article.title,
            source=article.source,
            published_at=article.published_at,
            endpoint=self.endpoint,
            model=self.spec.name,
            model_kind=self.spec.kind,
            prompt_version=self.prompt.version,
            parser=self.request.parser,
            extractor=self.request.extractor,
            extraction_method=article.method,
            scope=self.scope,
            input_chars=len(text),
            word_count=article.word_count,
            field_order=self.spec.field_order if self.endpoint == "analyze" else None,
            cached=False,
            backend=self.runtime.settings.ollama_backend_label,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Prepared:
    """A job with its article loaded and the model input built; only inference is left."""

    job: Job
    loaded: LoadedArticle
    text: str
    meta: ArticleMeta
    cache: CacheInfo
    cold_start: bool | None

    def timings(self, inference: InferenceTimings | None) -> Timings:
        loaded = self.loaded
        if inference is not None:
            inference = inference.model_copy(update={"cold_start": self.cold_start})
        return Timings(
            total_ms=self.job.clock.elapsed_ms(),
            fetch_ms=loaded.fetch_ms,
            consent_ms=loaded.consent_ms,
            parse_ms=loaded.article.parse_ms,
            extract_ms=loaded.article.extract_ms,
            inference=inference,
            cache=self.cache,
        )

    def meta_event(self) -> MetaEvent:
        article = self.loaded.article
        return MetaEvent(
            meta=self.meta,
            fetch_ms=self.loaded.fetch_ms,
            parse_ms=article.parse_ms,
            extract_ms=article.extract_ms,
            cache=self.cache,
            cold_start=self.cold_start,
        )


def cached_meta_event(response: SummaryResponse | AnalyzeResponse) -> MetaEvent:
    timings = response.timings
    return MetaEvent(
        meta=response.meta,
        fetch_ms=timings.fetch_ms,
        parse_ms=timings.parse_ms,
        extract_ms=timings.extract_ms,
        cache=timings.cache,
    )


def signal_result(verdict: Verdict) -> SignalResult:
    return SignalResult(
        sentiment=verdict.sentiment,
        abstained=verdict.abstained,
        policy=verdict.policy,
        confidence=verdict.confidence,
        score=verdict.score,
        probabilities=verdict.probabilities,
        threshold=verdict.threshold,
        directional_tau=verdict.directional_tau,
    )


def inference_timings(raw: ChatResult | DecisionResult, *, ttft_ms: float | None = None) -> InferenceTimings:
    """ttft_ms is passed in by streams, which measure it from request receipt to the first summary text."""
    if isinstance(raw, DecisionResult):
        return InferenceTimings(wall_ms=raw.wall_ms, prompt_tokens=raw.input_tokens)
    t = raw.timings
    return InferenceTimings(
        wall_ms=raw.wall_ms,
        ttft_ms=ttft_ms,
        load_ms=t.load_ms,
        prompt_eval_ms=t.prompt_eval_ms,
        eval_ms=t.eval_ms,
        prompt_tokens=t.prompt_tokens,
        eval_tokens=t.eval_tokens,
    )
```

```
"""Process-wide objects, built once by the app lifespan and shared by every request."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import httpx

from veritrade.config import Settings
from veritrade.errors import LlmUnreachable, VtError
from veritrade.fetch import Fetcher, FetchResult, SingleFlightCache
from veritrade.inference.ollama import OllamaClient
from veritrade.inference.types import Endpoint
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec, Registry
from veritrade.prompts.registry import PromptRegistry, PromptSpec
from veritrade.services.cache import CachedResponse, ResultKey, TtlCache

# Installed Ollama tags -> size in bytes (None when Ollama does not report one).
InstalledTags = dict[str, int | None]
_TAGS_KEY = "tags"


def tag_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Ollama lists an untagged model as name:latest."""
    return name if ":" in name else f"{name}:latest"


def needs_load(spec: ModelSpec, entries: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> bool:
    """Whether Ollama must load the model before answering, given its /api/ps entries. Ollama reloads a
    generative model on a num_ctx change; decision models pick their own context size."""
    tag = tag_name(spec.name)
    for entry in entries:
        if tag not in {tag_name(str(entry.get(key) or "")) for key in ("name", "model")}:
            continue
        context = entry.get("context_length")
        if spec.kind == "decision" or not isinstance(context, int) or context == spec.num_ctx:
            return False
    return True


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Runtime:
    settings: Settings
    fetcher: Fetcher
    ollama: OllamaClient
    registry: Registry
    prompts: Mapping[tuple[Endpoint, str], PromptSpec]
    fetch_cache: SingleFlightCache[str, FetchResult]
    results: TtlCache[ResultKey, CachedResponse]
    tags: SingleFlightCache[str, InstalledTags]

    @classmethod
    def build(
        cls,
        settings: Settings,
        *,
        fetcher: Fetcher,
        ollama: OllamaClient,
        registry: Registry | None = None,
    ) -> Runtime:
        registry = registry or Registry.load(settings)
        prompt_registry = PromptRegistry()
        # Resolved up front so a broken prompt file fails startup instead of a request.
        prompts = {
            (endpoint, spec.name): prompt_registry.get(endpoint, spec.name, kind=spec.kind)
            for spec in registry.models
            for endpoint in spec.endpoints
        }
        return cls(
            settings=settings,
            fetcher=fetcher,
            ollama=ollama,
            registry=registry,
            prompts=prompts,
            fetch_cache=SingleFlightCache(
                max_entries=settings.cache_max_entries,
                ttl_s=settings.fetch_cache_ttl_s,
                error_ttl_s=settings.fetch_error_ttl_s,
                weigh=lambda page: len(page.html),
                max_weight=settings.fetch_cache_max_bytes,
            ),
            results=TtlCache(max_entries=settings.cache_max_entries, ttl_s=settings.result_cache_ttl_s),
            tags=SingleFlightCache(
                max_entries=1, ttl_s=settings.models_cache_ttl_s, error_ttl_s=settings.models_cache_ttl_s
            ),
        )

    def prompt(self, endpoint: Endpoint, spec: ModelSpec) -> PromptSpec:
        return self.prompts[(endpoint, spec.name)]

    async def installed_tags(self) -> InstalledTags:
        """Cached for models_cache_ttl_s, failures included, so a down Ollama is not probed per request."""
        result = await self.tags.get_or_create(_TAGS_KEY, self._list_tags)
        return result.value

    async def _list_tags(self) -> InstalledTags:
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(self.settings.ollama_probe_timeout_s):
                entries = await self.ollama.tags()
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            raise LlmUnreachable("Ollama did not list its models in time") from exc
        return {tag_name(str(entry.get("name", ""))): _size(entry) for entry in entries}

    async def cold_start(self, spec: ModelSpec) -> bool | None:
        """None when Ollama cannot say in time; the request goes ahead either way."""
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(self.settings.ollama_probe_timeout_s):
                entries = await self.ollama.ps()
        except (TimeoutError, VtError, httpx.HTTPError):
            return None
        return needs_load(spec, entries)


def _size(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> int | None:
    size = entry.get("size")
    return size if isinstance(size, int) else None
"""Confidence policies: raw model output -> Verdict, abstaining to neutral below the frozen threshold."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from veritrade.inference.schemas import LabelOut, OrdinalOut, score_sentiment
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, Endpoint, PolicyName, Sentiment, TokenLogprob, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec

# Ties resolve to the safe class first; also the criteria order sent to decision models.
TIE_ORDER: tuple[Sentiment, ...] = ("neutral", "bullish", "bearish")
# Share of first-token mass allowed on tokens that could start several classes before we give up.
AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX = 0.05

_VALUE_START = {
    "label": re.compile(r'"label"\s*:\s*"'),
    "score": re.compile(r'"score"\s*:\s*'),
}
_SCORE_HEAD = re.compile(r"^(?:-|-[12](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?|[012](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?)$")
_SCORE_KEY = re.compile(r'"score"\s*:')


def winner(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Sentiment:
    best = TIE_ORDER[0]
    for sentiment in TIE_ORDER[1:]:
        if probabilities.get(sentiment, 0.0) > probabilities.get(best, 0.0):
            best = sentiment
    return best


def normalise(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> dict[Sentiment, float]:
    total = sum(max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) for s in TIE_ORDER)
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("probabilities sum to zero")
    return {s: max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def _threshold(
    name: PolicyName,
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float],
    min_p: float,
    score: int | None = None,
    tau: float | None = None,
) -> Verdict:
    top = winner(probabilities)
    if tau is not None and top == "neutral":
        side: Sentiment = "bullish" if probabilities["bullish"] >= probabilities["bearish"] else "bearish"
        if probabilities[side] >= tau:
            return Verdict(
                sentiment=side,
                abstained=False,
                policy=name,
                confidence=probabilities[side],
                score=score,
                probabilities=probabilities,
                threshold=min_p,
                directional_tau=tau,
            )
    confidence = probabilities[top]
    abstained = confidence < min_p
    return Verdict(
        sentiment="neutral" if abstained else top,
        abstained=abstained,
        policy=name,
        confidence=confidence,
        score=score,
        probabilities=probabilities,
        threshold=min_p,
        directional_tau=tau,
    )


def label_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Labels a token's text could start; empty means the grammar would reject it."""
    return {s for s in TIE_ORDER if s.startswith(rest) or rest.startswith(s + '"')}


def sign_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Class implied by a token that starts an enum score (-2..2); empty when the grammar rejects it."""
    if not rest:
        return set(TIE_ORDER)
    if not _SCORE_HEAD.match(rest):
        return set()
    return {"bearish" if rest[0] == "-" else "neutral" if rest[0] == "0" else "bullish"}


def first_value_token(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob], key: str
) -> tuple[str, dict[str, float]] | None:
    """The generated token that starts the value of `key` (minus any text before the value) and its
    alternatives as {text after the same prefix: probability}; None if tokens do not tile the content."""
    match = _VALUE_START[key].search(content)
    if match is None:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end > offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset]
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            return tok.token[len(prefix) :], candidates
        pos = end
    return None


def _first_token_distribution(
    content: str,
    logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None,
    key: str,
    classes: Callable[[str], set[Sentiment]],
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    found = first_value_token(content, logprobs or (), key)
    if found is None:
        return None
    chosen, candidates = found
    if len(classes(chosen)) != 1:
        return None
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    ambiguous = 0.0
    for rest, p in candidates.items():
        # A token ending exactly where the value starts (e.g. a bare space) says nothing about the class.
        if not rest:
            continue
        hit = classes(rest)
        if len(hit) == 1:
            mass[next(iter(hit))] += p
        elif hit:
            ambiguous += p
    total = sum(mass.values())
    if total <= 0 or ambiguous > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + ambiguous):
        return None
    return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def label_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """First label-token probabilities renormalised over tokens the grammar accepts (Ollama reports
    pre-mask logprobs, so "positive" is dropped). None when the generated first token is shared by
    two labels or ambiguous tokens carry real mass."""
    return _first_token_distribution(content, logprobs, "label", label_classes)


def score_sign_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """Class probabilities of the score's sign ("-" bearish, "0" neutral, "1"/"2" bullish) from the tokens
    after the colon, whitespace-insensitive because tokenizers fuse " -". A generated bare space defers to
    the next token; a bare space that was not generated hides its sign and counts as ambiguous."""
    match = _SCORE_KEY.search(content)
    if match is None or not logprobs:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    hidden = 0.0
    path = 1.0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end >= offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset] if pos < offset else ""
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            chosen = tok.token[len(prefix) :]
            for rest, p in candidates.items():
                if rest == chosen:
                    continue
                if not rest.strip():
                    hidden += path * p
                elif hit := sign_classes(rest.lstrip()):
                    mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * p
            if chosen.strip():
                hit = sign_classes(chosen.lstrip())
                if len(hit) != 1:
                    return None
                mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * candidates[chosen]
                total = sum(mass.values())
                if total <= 0 or hidden > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + hidden):
                    return None
                return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}
            path *= candidates[chosen]
        pos = end
    return None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProbabilityPolicy:
    """Argmax unless its probability is below min_p (then neutral, abstained). With directional_tau, a
    neutral argmax still yields the likelier directional class when that class reaches tau: models that
    park most of their mass on neutral are otherwise never pushed into a call."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "probability"

    def decide(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, tau=self.directional_tau)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LabelLogprobPolicy:
    """The probability rule (min_p, directional_tau) on first-token label probabilities. On a label
    collision `decide` returns None and the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema; when its sign is
    unreadable too, the chain ends at the ordinal policy."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "label-logprob"

    def decide(self, out: LabelOut | OrdinalOut, chat: ChatResult) -> Verdict | None:
        if isinstance(out, LabelOut):
            probabilities = label_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
            return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities)
        probabilities = score_sign_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
        return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities, score=out.score)

    def threshold(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float], score: int | None = None) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(
            self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, score=score, tau=self.directional_tau
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrdinalPolicy:
    """Directional only when |score| >= t; a zero score is a confident neutral, not an abstention."""

    t: int
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "ordinal"

    def decide(self, score: int) -> Verdict:
        raw = score_sentiment(score)
        abstained = raw != "neutral" and abs(score) < self.t
        return Verdict(
            sentiment="neutral" if abstained else raw,
            abstained=abstained,
            policy=self.name,
            score=score,
            threshold=float(self.t),
        )


Policy = ProbabilityPolicy | LabelLogprobPolicy | OrdinalPolicy


def _min_p(spec: ModelSpec) -> float:
    if spec.min_p is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{spec.name}: policy {spec.policy} needs min_p")
    return spec.min_p


def policy_for(spec: ModelSpec, streaming: bool = False, *, endpoint: Endpoint = "signal") -> Policy:
    """Streams and /analyze always threshold the ordinal score: it is read mid-JSON as soon as it
    closes, with no dependency on logprobs or on where the score sits in the output."""
    if spec.kind == "decision":
        return ProbabilityPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
    if streaming or endpoint == "analyze" or spec.policy == "ordinal":
        return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t)
    return LabelLogprobPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
```
