```typescript
import type { PolicyName, Sentiment, SignalResult } from "@/lib/api";
import { capitalize, coldStartNote, formatMs, formatPct } from "@/lib/format";
import type { LaneStatus } from "@/lib/run-state";

import styles from "./SignalCard.module.css";

const POLICY_NOTES: Record<PolicyName, string> = {
  probability: "threshold on the decision model's class probability",
  "label-logprob": "threshold on the label token probability",
  ordinal: "threshold on |score| of the -2..+2 scale",
};

const ORDER: readonly Sentiment[] = ["bullish", "bearish", "neutral"];

/** Direction the model leaned before the threshold turned it into an abstention. */
export function leaning(signal: SignalResult): Sentiment {
  if (signal.probabilities) {
    let best: Sentiment = signal.sentiment;
    for (const s of ORDER) {
      if ((signal.probabilities[s] ?? 0) > (signal.probabilities[best] ?? 0)) best = s;
    }
    return best;
  }
  if (typeof signal.score === "number" && signal.score !== 0) return signal.score > 0 ? "bullish" : "bearish";
  return signal.sentiment;
}

// Non-breaking, so a wrapped line never strands the sign away from its number.
const AT_LEAST = "≥ ";

/** The frozen rule this call was held to, in words; null for payloads that predate thresholds. */
export function thresholdText(signal: SignalResult): string | null {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  if (typeof threshold !== "number") return null;
  if (signal.policy === "ordinal") return `|score| ${AT_LEAST}${threshold}`;
  const hasTau = typeof tau === "number";
  if (threshold <= 0 && !hasTau) return "none (top class wins)";
  const base = threshold > 0 ? `call needs ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(threshold)}` : "top class wins";
  return hasTau
    ? `${base}; bullish/bearish called at ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(tau)} even when neutral leads`
    : base;
}

/** Why the call abstained, with the numbers when the payload carries the threshold. */
export function abstainReason(signal: SignalResult): string {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  if (typeof threshold === "number") {
    if (signal.policy === "ordinal" && typeof signal.score === "number") {
      return `|score| ${Math.abs(signal.score)} (leaning ${capitalize(lean)}) is below this model's threshold of ${threshold}`;
    }
    const p = signal.probabilities?.[lean];
    if (typeof p === "number") {
      const reason = `the top class (${capitalize(lean)}, ${formatPct(p)}) is below this model's ${formatPct(threshold)} threshold`;
      // tau only rescues a neutral lead, so it is part of the reason only then.
      return lean === "neutral" && typeof tau === "number"
        ? `${reason}, and neither Bullish nor Bearish reached ${formatPct(tau)}`
        : reason;
    }
  }
  const leaned = lean === "neutral" ? "" : ` (it leaned ${capitalize(lean)})`;
  return `the call is below this model's confidence threshold${leaned}`;
}

function formatScore(score: number): string {
  return score > 0 ? `+${score}` : String(score);
}

// Rounded to 0.1% so float noise (0.28 * 100) never reaches the style attribute.
const share = (value: number) => `${Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value)) * 1000) / 10}%`;

interface SignalCardProps {
  status: LaneStatus;
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity?: string | null;
  model?: string | null;
  /** Client-measured time from submit to the signal arriving. */
  timeToSignalMs?: number | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on a combined stream. */
  serverMs?: number | null;
  /** The model had to be loaded for this request. */
  coldStart?: boolean | null;
  /** Ollama's model load time; decision models report none. */
  loadMs?: number | null;
}

export function SignalCard({ status, signal, coldStart, ...rest }: SignalCardProps) {
  const busy = !signal && (status === "pending" || status === "streaming");
  return (
    <section className={styles.card} aria-labelledby="signal-heading" aria-busy={busy}>
      <h2 id="signal-heading" className={styles.heading}>
        Signal
      </h2>
      {signal ? (
        <SignalBody signal={signal} coldStart={coldStart} {...rest} />
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.placeholder}>
          {busy
            ? coldStart
              ? "Waiting for the signal while the model loads into memory (cold start)..."
              : "Waiting for the signal..."
            : status === "cancelled"
              ? "Cancelled."
              : "No signal: the request failed."}
        </p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

type SignalBodyProps = Omit<SignalCardProps, "status" | "signal"> & { signal: SignalResult };

function SignalBody({ signal, entity, model, timeToSignalMs, serverMs, coldStart, loadMs }: SignalBodyProps) {
  const rule = thresholdText(signal);
  const thresholdMark =
    signal.policy !== "ordinal" && typeof signal.threshold === "number" && signal.threshold > 0
      ? signal.threshold
      : null;
  const tauMark = typeof signal.directional_tau === "number" ? signal.directional_tau : null;
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <span
          className={styles.badge}
          data-sentiment={signal.sentiment}
          data-abstained={signal.abstained || undefined}
          data-testid="signal-badge"
        >
          {signal.abstained ? "No signal" : capitalize(signal.sentiment)}
        </span>
        {entity ? <span className={styles.entity}>{entity}</span> : null}
      </div>
      {signal.abstained ? (
        <p className={styles.abstainNote} data-testid="abstain-note">
          Abstained: {abstainReason(signal)}, so there is no directional call.
        </p>
      ) : null}
      <dl className={styles.stats}>
        {typeof signal.confidence === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Confidence</dt>
            <dd>{formatPct(signal.confidence)}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof signal.score === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Score</dt>
            <dd>{formatScore(signal.score)} on -2..+2</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <div>
          <dt>Policy</dt>
          <dd>
            <code>{signal.policy}</code> <span className={styles.note}>({POLICY_NOTES[signal.policy]})</span>
          </dd>
        </div>
        {rule ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Threshold</dt>
            <dd data-testid="signal-threshold">{rule}</dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {model ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Model</dt>
            <dd>
              <code>{model}</code>
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
        {typeof timeToSignalMs === "number" ? (
          <div>
            <dt>Time to signal</dt>
            <dd>
              {formatMs(timeToSignalMs)}
              {typeof serverMs === "number" ? (
                <span className={styles.note}> (server {formatMs(serverMs)})</span>
              ) : null}
              {coldStart ? (
                <span className={styles.cold} data-testid="signal-cold-start">
                  <span className={styles.tag}>Cold start</span> {coldStartNote(loadMs)}
                </span>
              ) : null}
            </dd>
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </dl>
      {signal.probabilities ? (
        <>
          <ul className={styles.probs} aria-label="Class probabilities">
            {ORDER.map((s) => {
              const p = signal.probabilities?.[s] ?? 0;
              return (
                <li key={s} className={styles.prob}>
                  <span className={styles.probLabel}>{capitalize(s)}</span>
                  <span className={styles.probTrack} aria-hidden="true">
                    <span className={styles.probFill} data-sentiment={s} style={{ width: share(p) }} />
                    {thresholdMark !== null ? (
                      <span
                        className={styles.probMark}
                        data-kind="threshold"
                        data-testid={`mark-threshold-${s}`}
                        style={{ left: share(thresholdMark) }}
                      />
                    ) : null}
                    {tauMark !== null && s !== "neutral" ? (
                      <span
                        className={styles.probMark}
                        data-kind="tau"
                        data-testid={`mark-tau-${s}`}
                        style={{ left: share(tauMark) }}
                      />
                    ) : null}
                  </span>
                  <span className={styles.probValue}>{formatPct(p)}</span>
                </li>
              );
            })}
          </ul>
          {thresholdMark !== null || tauMark !== null ? (
            <p className={styles.markLegend} aria-hidden="true">
              {thresholdMark !== null ? (
                <span>
                  <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="threshold" />
                  threshold {formatPct(thresholdMark)}
                </span>
              ) : null}
              {tauMark !== null ? (
                <span>
                  <span className={styles.markSwatch} data-kind="tau" />
                  tau {formatPct(tauMark)} (bullish/bearish)
                </span>
              ) : null}
            </p>
          ) : null}
        </>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

```typescript
"use client";

import { useId, useState, type SubmitEvent } from "react";

import type { ModelsState } from "@/hooks/useModels";
import type { RunParams } from "@/hooks/useAnalysis";
import {
  EXTRACTORS,
  PARSERS,
  SCOPES,
  type Endpoint,
  type ExtractorName,
  type ModelInfo,
  type ParserName,
  type Scope,
  type SignalRule,
} from "@/lib/api";
import type { Mode } from "@/lib/run-state";
import { SOURCES } from "@/lib/sources";

import styles from "./AnalyzeForm.module.css";

// Third-party extractors bring their own HTML parser, so the parser picker does not apply.
const PARSER_AWARE: ReadonlySet<ExtractorName> = new Set(["cascade", "jsonld", "profile", "density"]);

export function isHttpUrl(value: string): boolean {
  try {
    const url = new URL(value);
    return url.protocol === "http:" || url.protocol === "https:";
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** Compact frozen rule for an option label, e.g. "p ≥ 0.80", "tau 0.28" or "|score| ≥ 1". */
export function ruleLabel(rule: SignalRule | undefined): string | null {
  if (!rule) return null;
  if (rule.policy === "ordinal") return `|score| ≥ ${rule.threshold}`;
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (rule.threshold > 0) parts.push(`p ≥ ${rule.threshold.toFixed(2)}`);
  if (typeof rule.directional_tau === "number") parts.push(`tau ${rule.directional_tau.toFixed(2)}`);
  return parts.length ? parts.join(", ") : "no threshold";
}

/** Explains only the notations that appear in this picker. */
export function ruleHint(rules: readonly SignalRule[]): string | null {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (rules.some((r) => r.policy !== "ordinal" && r.threshold > 0)) {
    parts.push("p ≥ x means the top class needs probability x or more");
  }
  if (rules.some((r) => typeof r.directional_tau === "number")) {
    parts.push("tau x means bullish or bearish is called at x even when neutral leads");
  }
  if (rules.some((r) => r.policy === "ordinal")) {
    parts.push("|score| ≥ n means the -2..+2 score needs magnitude n or more");
  }
  return parts.length
    ? `In brackets, each model's frozen rule for a directional call. ${parts.join("; ")}.`
    : null;
}

function modelLabel(model: ModelInfo, endpoint: Endpoint, isDefault: boolean): string {
  const rule = ruleLabel(model.signal_rules?.[endpoint]);
  const name = rule ? `${model.name} (${rule})` : model.name;
  const notes = [
    isDefault ? "default" : null,
    model.installed ? null : "not installed",
    model.evaluated ? null : "CI plumbing, unevaluated",
  ].filter(Boolean);
  return notes.length ? `${name} (${notes.join(", ")})` : name;
}

interface ModelSelectProps {
  label: string;
  endpoint: Endpoint;
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  models: ModelsState;
}

function ModelSelect({ label, endpoint, value, onChange, models }: ModelSelectProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const hintId = useId();
  const ready = models.status === "ready" ? models.data : null;
  const fallback = ready?.defaults[endpoint];
  const options = ready ? ready.models.filter((m) => m.endpoints.includes(endpoint)) : [];
  const fallbackRule = ruleLabel(options.find((m) => m.name === fallback)?.signal_rules?.[endpoint]);
  const hint = ruleHint(options.flatMap((m) => m.signal_rules?.[endpoint] ?? []));
  return (
    <div className={styles.field}>
      <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>
      <select
        id={id}
        value={value}
        onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)}
        aria-describedby={hint ? hintId : undefined}
      >
        <option value="">
          {fallback
            ? `Server default (${fallbackRule ? `${fallback}, ${fallbackRule}` : fallback})`
            : "Server default"}
        </option>
        {options.map((m) => (
          <option key={m.name} value={m.name} disabled={!m.installed}>
            {modelLabel(m, endpoint, m.name === fallback)}
          </option>
        ))}
      </select>
      {hint ? (
        <small id={hintId} className={styles.help}>
          {hint}
        </small>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}

interface AnalyzeFormProps {
  models: ModelsState;
  running: boolean;
  onSubmit: (params: RunParams) => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
}

export function AnalyzeForm({ models, running, onSubmit, onCancel }: AnalyzeFormProps) {
  const [url, setUrl] = useState("");
  const [urlError, setUrlError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<Mode>("split");
  const [streaming, setStreaming] = useState(true);
  const [signalModel, setSignalModel] = useState("");
  const [summaryModel, setSummaryModel] = useState("");
  const [analyzeModel, setAnalyzeModel] = useState("");
  const [parser, setParser] = useState<ParserName>("selectolax");
  const [extractor, setExtractor] = useState<ExtractorName>("cascade");
  const [scope, setScope] = useState<Scope>("lede");

  const ids = { url: useId(), urlHelp: useId(), parser: useId(), extractor: useId(), scope: useId() };
  const ready = models.status === "ready" ? models.data : null;
  const parsers = ready?.parsers.length ? ready.parsers : PARSERS;
  const extractors = ready?.extractors.length ? ready.extractors : EXTRACTORS;
  const scopes = ready?.scopes.length ? ready.scopes : SCOPES;
  const parserApplies = PARSER_AWARE.has(extractor);

  function handleSubmit(event: SubmitEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    const trimmed = url.trim();
    if (!isHttpUrl(trimmed)) {
      setUrlError("Enter a full http(s) URL, for example https://www.cnbc.com/2026/...");
      return;
    }
    setUrlError(null);
    onSubmit({
      url: trimmed,
      mode,
      streaming,
      parser,
      extractor,
      scope,
      signalModel,
      summaryModel,
      analyzeModel,
    });
  }

  const examples = SOURCES.filter((s) => s.exampleUrl);

  return (
    <form className={styles.form} onSubmit={handleSubmit} noValidate aria-label="Analyze an article">
      <div className={styles.urlRow}>
        <div className={styles.urlField}>
          <label htmlFor={ids.url}>Article URL</label>
          <input
            id={ids.url}
            name="url"
            type="url"
            inputMode="url"
            autoComplete="off"
            spellCheck={false}
            placeholder="https://..."
            value={url}
            onChange={(e) => setUrl(e.target.value)}
            aria-invalid={urlError ? true : undefined}
            aria-describedby={ids.urlHelp}
            required
          />
        </div>
        <div className={styles.actions}>
          <button type="submit" className={styles.primary}>
            {running ? "Restart" : "Analyze"}
          </button>
          {running ? (
            <button type="button" className={styles.secondary} onClick={onCancel}>
              Cancel
            </button>
          ) : null}
        </div>
      </div>
      <p id={ids.urlHelp} className={urlError ? styles.error : styles.help}>
        {urlError ?? "A public news article, press release or SEC 8-K exhibit."}
      </p>

      <div className={styles.sources}>
        <span className={styles.sourcesLabel}>Tested sources:</span>
        <ul className={styles.chips}>
          {SOURCES.map((s) => (
            <li key={s.key} className={styles.chip}>
              {s.name}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
        {examples.length ? (
          <div className={styles.examples}>
            {examples.map((s) => (
              <button
                key={s.key}
                type="button"
                className={styles.secondary}
                onClick={() => setUrl(s.exampleUrl ?? "")}
              >
                Example: {s.name}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.groups}>
        <fieldset className={styles.group}>
          <legend>Mode</legend>
          <label className={styles.choice}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              name="mode"
              value="split"
              checked={mode === "split"}
              onChange={() => setMode("split")}
            />
            <span>
              Split
              <small>/api/signal and /api/summary fire together; the signal lands first.</small>
            </span>
          </label>
          <label className={styles.choice}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              name="mode"
              value="combined"
              checked={mode === "combined"}
              onChange={() => setMode("combined")}
            />
            <span>
              Combined
              <small>One /api/analyze call generates sentiment and summary together.</small>
            </span>
          </label>
          <label className={styles.choice}>
            <input type="checkbox" checked={streaming} onChange={(e) => setStreaming(e.target.checked)} />
            <span>
              Streaming
              <small>Server-sent events; off uses the JSON endpoints.</small>
            </span>
          </label>
        </fieldset>

        <fieldset className={styles.group}>
          <legend>Models</legend>
          {mode === "split" ? (
            <>
              <ModelSelect
                label="Signal model"
                endpoint="signal"
                value={signalModel}
                onChange={setSignalModel}
                models={models}
              />
              <ModelSelect
                label="Summary model"
                endpoint="summary"
                value={summaryModel}
                onChange={setSummaryModel}
                models={models}
              />
            </>
          ) : (
            <ModelSelect
              label="Analyze model"
              endpoint="analyze"
              value={analyzeModel}
              onChange={setAnalyzeModel}
              models={models}
            />
          )}
          {models.status === "loading" ? <p className={styles.help}>Loading models...</p> : null}
        </fieldset>

        <fieldset className={styles.group}>
          <legend>Extraction</legend>
          <div className={styles.field}>
            <label htmlFor={ids.extractor}>Extractor</label>
            <select
              id={ids.extractor}
              value={extractor}
              onChange={(e) => setExtractor(e.target.value as ExtractorName)}
            >
              {extractors.map((name) => (
                <option key={name} value={name}>
                  {name}
                </option>
              ))}
            </select>
          </div>
          <div className={styles.field}>
            <label htmlFor={ids.parser}>Parser</label>
            <select
              id={ids.parser}
              value={parser}
              onChange={(e) => setParser(e.target.value as ParserName)}
              disabled={!parserApplies}
            >
              {parsers.map((name) => (
                <option key={name} value={name}>
                  {name}
                </option>
              ))}
            </select>
            {!parserApplies ? <small className={styles.help}>{extractor} uses its own parser.</small> : null}
          </div>
          {mode === "split" ? (
            <div className={styles.field}>
              <label htmlFor={ids.scope}>Signal scope</label>
              <select id={ids.scope} value={scope} onChange={(e) => setScope(e.target.value as Scope)}>

                  </option>
                ))}
              </select>
            </div>
          ) : null}
        </fieldset>
      </div>
    </form>
  );
}
```

```typescript
"use client";

import { useAnalysis } from "@/hooks/useAnalysis";
import { useModels } from "@/hooks/useModels";
import { capitalize } from "@/lib/format";
import {
  articleMeta,
  distinctErrors,
  laneById,
  type Lane,
  type LaneId,
  type RunState,
} from "@/lib/run-state";

import { AnalyzeForm } from "./AnalyzeForm";
import styles from "./AnalyzeApp.module.css";
import { ArticleMetaLine } from "./ArticleMetaLine";
import { ErrorBanner } from "./ErrorBanner";
import { LatencyBar, type LaneMark, type LatencyLane } from "./LatencyBar";
import { SignalCard } from "./SignalCard";
import { SummaryPanel } from "./SummaryPanel";

const LANE_LABELS: Record<LaneId, string> = { signal: "Signal", summary: "Summary", analyze: "Analyze" };

function toLatencyLane(lane: Lane): LatencyLane {
  const marks: LaneMark[] = [];
  if (lane.signalAtMs !== null) {
    marks.push({ kind: "signal", label: "time to signal", atMs: lane.signalAtMs });
  }
  if (lane.firstTokenAtMs !== null) {
    marks.push({ kind: "token", label: "time to first token", atMs: lane.firstTokenAtMs });
  }
  return {
    id: lane.id,
    label: LANE_LABELS[lane.id],
    status: lane.status,
    timings: lane.timings,
    endMs: lane.endAtMs,
    marks,
  };
}

function announcement(state: RunState): string {
  if (state.running && !state.signal) return "Analyzing...";
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (state.signal) {
    parts.push(
      state.signal.abstained
        ? "No signal: below this model's threshold."
        : `Signal ${capitalize(state.signal.sentiment)}.`,
    );
  }
  if (!state.running && state.summary) parts.push("Summary complete.");
  return parts.join(" ");
}

export function AnalyzeApp() {
  const models = useModels();
  const { state, start, cancel } = useAnalysis();

  const split = state.mode === "split";
  const signalLane = laneById(state, split ? "signal" : "analyze");
  const summaryLane = laneById(state, split ? "summary" : "analyze");
  const meta = articleMeta(state);
  const errors = distinctErrors(state);
  const showLatency = state.lanes.some(
    (l) => l.timings || l.signalAtMs !== null || l.firstTokenAtMs !== null,
  );

  return (
    <>
      <AnalyzeForm models={models} running={state.running} onSubmit={start} onCancel={cancel} />

      <p role="status" className="visually-hidden">
        {announcement(state)}
      </p>

      {models.status === "error" ? <ErrorBanner error={models.error} context="Model list" /> : null}
      {errors.map(({ lanes, error }) => (
        <ErrorBanner
          key={`${error.code}-${lanes.join("-")}`}
          error={error}
          context={lanes.map((id) => LANE_LABELS[id]).join(" and ")}
        />
      ))}

      {state.lanes.length ? (
        <div className={styles.results}>
          {meta ? <ArticleMetaLine meta={meta} /> : null}
          <div className={styles.cards}>
            {signalLane ? (
              <SignalCard
                status={signalLane.status}
                signal={state.signal}
                entity={state.entity}
                model={signalLane.meta?.model}
                timeToSignalMs={signalLane.signalAtMs}
                serverMs={state.serverSignalMs}
                coldStart={signalLane.coldStart}
                loadMs={signalLane.timings?.inference?.load_ms}
              />
            ) : null}
            {summaryLane ? (
              <SummaryPanel
                status={summaryLane.status}
                text={state.summary}
                truncated={state.summaryTruncated}
                model={summaryLane.meta?.model}
                streaming={state.streaming}
                firstTokenMs={summaryLane.firstTokenAtMs}
                coldStart={summaryLane.coldStart}
                loadMs={summaryLane.timings?.inference?.load_ms}
              />
            ) : null}
          </div>
          {showLatency ? <LatencyBar lanes={state.lanes.map(toLatencyLane)} /> : null}
        </div>
      ) : (
        <p className={styles.empty}>
          Results appear here. Split mode shows the signal as soon as /api/signal answers while the summary
          keeps streaming; combined mode gets both from one generation.
        </p>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

<details>
<summary><code>~/krisjobs/standalone/veritrade-analytics/README.md</code></summary>

````markdown
URL='https://...'   # any public article URL
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/signal -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
curl -sN http://localhost:8000/api/analyze/stream -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"url\": \"$URL\"}"
```

**SSE order.** `meta` (article meta, fetch / parse / extract timings, `cold_start`) once extraction is done, so a
stream can say the model is loading before its first token; on `/analyze/stream` one `sentiment` event as soon as
the score closes (served field order: sentiment-first); `summary_delta` text chunks; `done` with the full JSON
response. A failure before the stream opens is a JSON error with its HTTP status, after that one `error` event; a
closed connection stops the upstream generation.

**Errors** share one envelope, `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "retryable", "upstream_status"}}`
([`errors.py`](backend/src/veritrade/errors.py), [`contracts.py`](backend/src/veritrade/api/contracts.py)); other
request-body validation errors, such as an unknown `parser`, `extractor` or `scope` or an extra field, return
FastAPI's standard 422 `{"detail": [...]}`.

| HTTP | Codes | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_url`, `blocked_destination`, `model_not_allowed` | Malformed URL; SSRF guard (private or reserved address, a port other than 80/443); model not on the allowlist or disabled by `VT_MODELS`, or not served on that endpoint |
| 422 | `paywalled`, `consent_required`, `extraction_empty`, `unsupported_content`, `too_large` | Fetched, but no usable article: paywall, consent wall, under 40 words, not HTML (PDF, feed), over 10 MB |
| 502 | `source_blocked`, `upstream_http`, `schema_violation` | Publisher refused (CDN bot wall, 401/403/429/451, with a hint to a syndicated copy); other upstream HTTP error; malformed model output |
| 503 | `model_unavailable`, `llm_unreachable` | Model not pulled (the hint gives the `ollama pull` command); Ollama down |
| 504 | `upstream_timeout`, `inference_timeout` | Fetch deadline (8 s); inference timeout (90 s) |

### Thresholds and "No signal"

Confidence rules are frozen per model and endpoint. The served source of truth is
[`models.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) (`policy`, `min_p`, `directional_tau`, `ordinal_t`),
written by `veritrade_evals freeze`, with the evidence behind each value (dev300 and dev-article F0.5, inversions and
coverage at that threshold) in [`frozen.json`](evals/results/frozen.json); the policies are explained in
[04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#4-models-prompts-and-confidence-policies). As frozen:

| Model | `/signal` rule | `/analyze` rule |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (`/signal` default) | label-logprob, `min_p` 0, tau 0.28 | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | probability, `min_p` 0.80 | - |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | probability, `min_p` 0.97 | - |
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (`/analyze` default), `ministral-3:3b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | - | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 |
| `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` (CI plumbing, never evaluated) | probability, `min_p` 0.50 (provisional) | - |

- **Where to see them**: the signal and analyze pickers in the UI; the **Threshold** row and the threshold and tau
  marks on every signal card; `GET /api/models`, whose `signal_rules` maps each signal endpoint of a model to its
  `policy`, `threshold` and `directional_tau`; and every `signal` in a response, which carries the `threshold` and
  `directional_tau` it was held to. A label-logprob rule falls back to ordinal \|score\| >= 1 on a first-token label
  collision; `signal_rules` lists the primary rule.
- **"No signal" is an abstention, by design** (precision over recall, Q2 and Q3): when the winning class is below
  the model's frozen threshold, the service returns `sentiment: "neutral"` with `abstained: true` instead of a
  directional call it is not confident in. The UI shows **No signal** and says why, e.g. "Abstained: the top class
  (Bullish, 73.0%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold, so there is no directional call." A neutral with
  `abstained: false` is a neutral verdict. With these rules only the 9B decision models abstain (dev300 coverage
  72.9% for clef-flash, 26.3% for nimble); the defaults hold back by answering neutral
  ([design decisions](#design-decisions)).

## Architecture

```
browser ──► FastAPI (same origin: /api + static Next.js export)
              │ fetch (httpx, HTTP/2, SSRF guard, consent/paywall/block detection, single-flight cache)
              │ extract (parser x extractor registry, lede/full scope, token cap)
              ├─► /api/signal   decision model (/v1/systemone, class probabilities) or tiny LLM
              ├─► /api/summary  small LLM, JSON or SSE stream
              └─► /api/analyze  one small LLM -> {score, entity, summary}, JSON or SSE stream
                         ▼
                      Ollama (native Metal on macOS, or the bundled container)
```

A request is checked against the model allowlist; one pooled HTTP/2 client fetches the page behind an SSRF guard
that vets every resolved address and redirect hop, and bot walls, consent walls and paywalls become typed errors.
Extraction (default `selectolax` + `cascade`: JSON-LD `articleBody`, then the per-source profile in
[`sources.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/sources.toml), then a text-density fallback) cuts the `lede` or `full`
input. Ollama gets the model's frozen prompt with a JSON schema, greedy decoding and `think: false`, and the
model's confidence policy turns the answer into a label or an abstention against its frozen threshold
(`backend/src/veritrade/`). While the page downloads, a `/api/ps` probe asks Ollama whether the model is already
resident, so the response can flag a cold start.

## Design decisions

Every decision was settled in an interview before any code was written; the full table, with the question each one
answers, is in [`01-decisions.md`](.context/docs/design/01-decisions.md).
````

```typescript
import type { ApiError, ArticleMeta, SignalResult, Timings } from "./api";

export type Mode = "split" | "combined";
export type LaneId = "signal" | "summary" | "analyze";
export type LaneStatus = "pending" | "streaming" | "done" | "error" | "cancelled";

export interface Lane {
  id: LaneId;
  status: LaneStatus;
  meta: ArticleMeta | null;
  timings: Timings | null;
  error: ApiError | null;
  /** The model had to be loaded for this request; null when unknown or served from the result cache. */
  coldStart: boolean | null;
  // Client clock: milliseconds since the run started, from performance.now().
  signalAtMs: number | null;
  firstTokenAtMs: number | null;
  endAtMs: number | null;
}

export interface RunState {
  runId: number;
  mode: Mode;
  streaming: boolean;
  running: boolean;
  lanes: Lane[];
  signal: SignalResult | null;
  entity: string | null;
  /** Server-reported time to sentiment on the combined stream. */
  serverSignalMs: number | null;
  summary: string;
  /** The server cut the summary at the model's output limit. */
  summaryTruncated: boolean;
}

interface Tagged {
  runId: number;
  lane: LaneId;
  atMs: number;
}

export type RunAction =
  | { type: "start"; runId: number; mode: Mode; streaming: boolean; lanes: LaneId[] }
  | ({ type: "meta"; meta: ArticleMeta; coldStart?: boolean | null } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "signal"; signal: SignalResult; entity: string | null; serverMs: number | null } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "delta"; text: string } & Tagged)
  | ({
      type: "done";
      meta: ArticleMeta;
      timings: Timings;
      summary?: string;
      truncated?: boolean;
      signal?: SignalResult;
      entity?: string | null;
    } & Tagged)
  | ({ type: "error"; error: ApiError } & Tagged)
  | { type: "cancel"; runId: number; atMs: number };

export const initialRunState: RunState = {
  runId: 0,
  mode: "split",
  streaming: true,
  running: false,
  lanes: [],
  signal: null,
  entity: null,
  serverSignalMs: null,
  summary: "",
  summaryTruncated: false,
};

function newLane(id: LaneId): Lane {
  return {
    id,
    status: "pending",
    meta: null,
    timings: null,
    error: null,
    coldStart: null,
    signalAtMs: null,
    firstTokenAtMs: null,
    endAtMs: null,
  };
}

const isActive = (lane: Lane) => lane.status === "pending" || lane.status === "streaming";

function patchLane(state: RunState, id: LaneId, patch: (lane: Lane) => Partial<Lane>): RunState {
  const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) => (lane.id === id ? { ...lane, ...patch(lane) } : lane));
  return { ...state, lanes, running: lanes.some(isActive) };
}

export function runReducer(state: RunState, action: RunAction): RunState {
  if (action.type === "start") {
    return {
      ...initialRunState,
      runId: action.runId,
      mode: action.mode,
      streaming: action.streaming,
      running: true,
      lanes: action.lanes.map(newLane),
    };
  }
  // Late events from a superseded run must not leak into the current one.
  if (action.runId !== state.runId) return state;

  switch (action.type) {
    case "meta":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        meta: lane.meta ?? action.meta,
        coldStart: action.coldStart ?? lane.coldStart,
        status: lane.status === "pending" ? "streaming" : lane.status,
      }));
    case "signal":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({ signalAtMs: lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs })),
        signal: action.signal,
        entity: action.entity,
        serverSignalMs: action.serverMs,
      };
    case "delta":
      return {
        ...patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
          firstTokenAtMs: lane.firstTokenAtMs ?? action.atMs,
          status: "streaming",
        })),
        summary: state.summary + action.text,
      };
    case "done": {
      const next = patchLane(state, action.lane, (lane) => ({
        status: "done",
        meta: action.meta,
        timings: action.timings,
        coldStart: action.timings.inference?.cold_start ?? lane.coldStart,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
        signalAtMs: action.signal ? (lane.signalAtMs ?? action.atMs) : lane.signalAtMs,
      }));
      return {
        ...next,
        // The final payload is authoritative over the concatenated deltas.
        summary: action.summary ?? next.summary,
        summaryTruncated: action.truncated ?? next.summaryTruncated,
        signal: action.signal ?? next.signal,
        entity: action.entity !== undefined ? action.entity : next.entity,
      };
    }
    case "error":
      return patchLane(state, action.lane, () => ({
        status: "error",
        error: action.error,
        endAtMs: action.atMs,
      }));
    case "cancel": {
      const lanes = state.lanes.map((lane) =>
        isActive(lane) ? { ...lane, status: "cancelled" as const, endAtMs: action.atMs } : lane,
      );
      return { ...state, lanes, running: false };
    }
  }
}

export function laneById(state: RunState, id: LaneId): Lane | undefined {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.id === id);
}

/** Article-level meta from whichever lane reported first. */
export function articleMeta(state: RunState): ArticleMeta | null {
  return state.lanes.find((lane) => lane.meta)?.meta ?? null;
}

/** One banner per distinct failure; split lanes often fail identically on a shared fetch. */
export function distinctErrors(state: RunState): { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] {
  const out: { lanes: LaneId[]; error: ApiError }[] = [];
  for (const lane of state.lanes) {
    if (!lane.error) continue;
    const same = out.find((e) => e.error.code === lane.error?.code && e.error.message === lane.error.message);
    if (same) same.lanes.push(lane.id);
    else out.push({ lanes: [lane.id], error: lane.error });
  }
  return out;
}

```

```typescript
export function formatMs(ms: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (ms === null || ms === undefined || !Number.isFinite(ms)) return "-";
  if (ms >= 10_000) return `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`;
  if (ms >= 1000) return `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(2)} s`;
  return `${Math.round(ms)} ms`;
}

export function formatPct(value: number | null | undefined, digits = 1): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return `${(value * 100).toFixed(digits)}%`;
}

export function formatNum(value: number | null | undefined, digits = 3): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return value.toFixed(digits);
}

export function formatInt(value: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";
  return Math.round(value).toLocaleString("en-US");
}

/** Why a cold request was slow; decision models report no separate load time. */
export function coldStartNote(loadMs: number | null | undefined): string {
  return typeof loadMs === "number" && loadMs > 0
    ? `model loaded for this request (${formatMs(loadMs)})`
    : "includes loading the model into memory";
}

export function capitalize(value: string): string {
  return value ? value[0].toUpperCase() + value.slice(1) : value;
}

```
```
## 4. Models, prompts and confidence policies

**Roster** (R2 and its follow-ups). The split architecture serves `/signal` + `/summary`; the combined one `/analyze`.

| endpoint | models | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0`, `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | decision models (native class probabilities) |
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | generative baseline (label and ordinal schemas) |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | generative |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`, `ministral-3:3b` | generative, one call -> score + entity + summary |
| `/analyze` (holdout only) | `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` | quality ceiling, untuned (prompt v1, \|s\| >= 1) |

**Lean prompt grid** on dev300: 33 cells ([`grid/manifest.json`](../../../evals/results/grid/manifest.json)), all on
native Metal, Ollama 0.40.6, greedy (temperature 0, seed 0, sampling penalties neutralised; see the build-time
findings in `01-decisions.md`).

- Generative `/signal` and `/analyze`: rubric A (definitions) or B (impact questions) x 0 or 4 synthetic shots =
  v1-v4; for `qwen3.5:0.8b` each runs on both the label and the ordinal schema.
- Decision models: rubric or plain one-line question x described or bare criteria = v1-v4.
- `/analyze` follow-ups, paired against v1: v5 (the tightened summary rule) and `v1-summary-first` (the field-order
  check, on `qwen3.5:4b` and `ministral` only).

**Confidence policies** ([`confidence.py`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/inference/confidence.py)):

- **probability** (decision models): argmax of the native class probabilities; abstain when it is below `min_p`.
- **label-logprob** (generative `/signal`): first label-token probabilities, renormalised over the tokens the grammar
  accepts, with the same `min_p` rule. With **`directional_tau`**, a neutral argmax still yields the likelier
  directional class when that class holds p >= tau; below tau the row is a served neutral, not an abstention. On a
  first-token label collision the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema.
- **ordinal** (`/analyze`, streams, fallback): a score from -2 to 2, directional only when \|score\| >= t. It is read
  mid-stream as soon as it closes and needs no logprobs (Q3); logprob-weighted streaming confidence is on the backlog.

**Scope and field order.** `/signal` reads `lede` by default (headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200
tokens); `lede` and `full` are both scored on articles. `/analyze` reads `full` and emits the sentiment field first,
so the score streams after a handful of tokens (R3).

**Error analysis and freeze.** One hand-written read of the grid counts
([`grid/notes.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/notes.md)) drove the changes listed in section 5. The `freeze`
command then wrote [`frozen.json`](../../../evals/results/frozen.json) and
[`models.toml`](../../../backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml):

| endpoint | model | frozen prompt | policy | threshold | field order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/signal` | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `v2@ff82e957` (rubric A, 4 shots, label schema) | label-logprob + `directional_tau` | min_p 0, tau 0.28 (ordinal \|s\| >= 1 fallback) | - |
| `/signal` | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `v4@fcc93f1b` (plain question, bare labels) | probability | min_p 0.80 | - |
| `/signal` | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `v1@a1e34f63` (rubric, described criteria) | probability | min_p 0.97 | - |
| `/summary` | `qwen3.5:2b-q4_K_M`, `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v2@84ce3858` (tightened summary rule) | - | - | - |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` | `v1@7daf4f28` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |
| `/analyze` | `ministral-3:3b` | `v5@e2b57fc6` | ordinal | \|s\| >= 1 | sentiment-first |

Freeze rules: `/signal` keeps the dev300 best rule unless it clearly fails on the articles. `/analyze` takes v5
unless the whole paired 95% CI of its gap against v1 is below zero on dev300 or the articles, which rejected v5 for
`qwen3.5:4b` (articles -0.080 [-0.178, -0.014]). Summary-first needed a dev300 win without an articles loss; it never
got one.

## 5. Accuracy on dev

Frozen configs only. Articles use the dev300 threshold unchanged and the serving extraction (`selectolax` +
`cascade`). Sources: [`grid/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/grid/summary.md),
[`articles_dev/summary.md`](../../../evals/results/articles_dev/summary.md).
```

```
"""Confidence policies: raw model output -> Verdict, abstaining to neutral below the frozen threshold."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import ClassVar

from veritrade.inference.schemas import LabelOut, OrdinalOut, score_sentiment
from veritrade.inference.types import ChatResult, Endpoint, PolicyName, Sentiment, TokenLogprob, Verdict
from veritrade.models_registry import ModelSpec

# Ties resolve to the safe class first; also the criteria order sent to decision models.
TIE_ORDER: tuple[Sentiment, ...] = ("neutral", "bullish", "bearish")
# Share of first-token mass allowed on tokens that could start several classes before we give up.
AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX = 0.05

_VALUE_START = {
    "label": re.compile(r'"label"\s*:\s*"'),
    "score": re.compile(r'"score"\s*:\s*'),
}
_SCORE_HEAD = re.compile(r"^(?:-|-[12](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?|[012](?:[\s,}][\s\S]*)?)$")
_SCORE_KEY = re.compile(r'"score"\s*:')


def winner(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Sentiment:
    best = TIE_ORDER[0]
    for sentiment in TIE_ORDER[1:]:
        if probabilities.get(sentiment, 0.0) > probabilities.get(best, 0.0):
            best = sentiment
    return best


def normalise(probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> dict[Sentiment, float]:
    total = sum(max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) for s in TIE_ORDER)
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("probabilities sum to zero")
    return {s: max(0.0, probabilities.get(s, 0.0)) / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def _threshold(
    name: PolicyName,
    probabilities: dict[Sentiment, float],
    min_p: float,
    score: int | None = None,
    tau: float | None = None,
) -> Verdict:
    top = winner(probabilities)
    if tau is not None and top == "neutral":
        side: Sentiment = "bullish" if probabilities["bullish"] >= probabilities["bearish"] else "bearish"
        if probabilities[side] >= tau:
            return Verdict(
                sentiment=side,
                abstained=False,
                policy=name,
                confidence=probabilities[side],
                score=score,
                probabilities=probabilities,
                threshold=min_p,
                directional_tau=tau,
            )
    confidence = probabilities[top]
    abstained = confidence < min_p
    return Verdict(
        sentiment="neutral" if abstained else top,
        abstained=abstained,
        policy=name,
        confidence=confidence,
        score=score,
        probabilities=probabilities,
        threshold=min_p,
        directional_tau=tau,
    )


def label_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Labels a token's text could start; empty means the grammar would reject it."""
    return {s for s in TIE_ORDER if s.startswith(rest) or rest.startswith(s + '"')}


def sign_classes(rest: str) -> set[Sentiment]:
    """Class implied by a token that starts an enum score (-2..2); empty when the grammar rejects it."""
    if not rest:
        return set(TIE_ORDER)
    if not _SCORE_HEAD.match(rest):
        return set()
    return {"bearish" if rest[0] == "-" else "neutral" if rest[0] == "0" else "bullish"}


def first_value_token(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob], key: str
) -> tuple[str, dict[str, float]] | None:
    """The generated token that starts the value of `key` (minus any text before the value) and its
    alternatives as {text after the same prefix: probability}; None if tokens do not tile the content."""
    match = _VALUE_START[key].search(content)
    if match is None:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end > offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset]
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            return tok.token[len(prefix) :], candidates
        pos = end
    return None


def _first_token_distribution(
    content: str,
    logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None,
    key: str,
    classes: Callable[[str], set[Sentiment]],
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    found = first_value_token(content, logprobs or (), key)
    if found is None:
        return None
    chosen, candidates = found
    if len(classes(chosen)) != 1:
        return None
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    ambiguous = 0.0
    for rest, p in candidates.items():
        # A token ending exactly where the value starts (e.g. a bare space) says nothing about the class.
        if not rest:
            continue
        hit = classes(rest)
        if len(hit) == 1:
            mass[next(iter(hit))] += p
        elif hit:
            ambiguous += p
    total = sum(mass.values())
    if total <= 0 or ambiguous > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + ambiguous):
        return None
    return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}


def label_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """First label-token probabilities renormalised over tokens the grammar accepts (Ollama reports
    pre-mask logprobs, so "positive" is dropped). None when the generated first token is shared by
    two labels or ambiguous tokens carry real mass."""
    return _first_token_distribution(content, logprobs, "label", label_classes)


def score_sign_probabilities(
    content: str, logprobs: Sequence[TokenLogprob] | None
) -> dict[Sentiment, float] | None:
    """Class probabilities of the score's sign ("-" bearish, "0" neutral, "1"/"2" bullish) from the tokens
    after the colon, whitespace-insensitive because tokenizers fuse " -". A generated bare space defers to
    the next token; a bare space that was not generated hides its sign and counts as ambiguous."""
    match = _SCORE_KEY.search(content)
    if match is None or not logprobs:
        return None
    offset, pos = match.end(), 0
    mass = dict.fromkeys(TIE_ORDER, 0.0)
    hidden = 0.0
    path = 1.0
    for tok in logprobs:
        end = pos + len(tok.token)
        if content[pos:end] != tok.token:
            return None
        if end >= offset:
            prefix = content[pos:offset] if pos < offset else ""
            candidates: dict[str, float] = {}
            for text, logprob in ((tok.token, tok.logprob), *tok.top):
                if text.startswith(prefix):
                    candidates.setdefault(text[len(prefix) :], math.exp(logprob))
            chosen = tok.token[len(prefix) :]
            for rest, p in candidates.items():
                if rest == chosen:
                    continue
                if not rest.strip():
                    hidden += path * p
                elif hit := sign_classes(rest.lstrip()):
                    mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * p
            if chosen.strip():
                hit = sign_classes(chosen.lstrip())
                if len(hit) != 1:
                    return None
                mass[next(iter(hit))] += path * candidates[chosen]
                total = sum(mass.values())
                if total <= 0 or hidden > AMBIGUOUS_MASS_MAX * (total + hidden):
                    return None
                return {s: mass[s] / total for s in TIE_ORDER}
            path *= candidates[chosen]
        pos = end
    return None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ProbabilityPolicy:
    """Argmax unless its probability is below min_p (then neutral, abstained). With directional_tau, a
    neutral argmax still yields the likelier directional class when that class reaches tau: models that
    park most of their mass on neutral are otherwise never pushed into a call."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "probability"

    def decide(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float]) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, tau=self.directional_tau)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LabelLogprobPolicy:
    """The probability rule (min_p, directional_tau) on first-token label probabilities. On a label
    collision `decide` returns None and the adapter re-asks with the ordinal schema; when its sign is
    unreadable too, the chain ends at the ordinal policy."""

    min_p: float
    directional_tau: float | None = None
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "label-logprob"

    def decide(self, out: LabelOut | OrdinalOut, chat: ChatResult) -> Verdict | None:
        if isinstance(out, LabelOut):
            probabilities = label_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
            return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities)
        probabilities = score_sign_probabilities(chat.content, chat.logprobs)
        return None if probabilities is None else self.threshold(probabilities, score=out.score)

    def threshold(self, probabilities: Mapping[Sentiment, float], score: int | None = None) -> Verdict:
        return _threshold(
            self.name, normalise(probabilities), self.min_p, score=score, tau=self.directional_tau
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrdinalPolicy:
    """Directional only when |score| >= t; a zero score is a confident neutral, not an abstention."""

    t: int
    name: ClassVar[PolicyName] = "ordinal"

    def decide(self, score: int) -> Verdict:
        raw = score_sentiment(score)
        abstained = raw != "neutral" and abs(score) < self.t
        return Verdict(
            sentiment="neutral" if abstained else raw,
            abstained=abstained,
            policy=self.name,
            score=score,
            threshold=float(self.t),
        )


Policy = ProbabilityPolicy | LabelLogprobPolicy | OrdinalPolicy


def _min_p(spec: ModelSpec) -> float:
    if spec.min_p is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{spec.name}: policy {spec.policy} needs min_p")
    return spec.min_p


def policy_for(spec: ModelSpec, streaming: bool = False, *, endpoint: Endpoint = "signal") -> Policy:
    """Streams and /analyze always threshold the ordinal score: it is read mid-JSON as soon as it
    closes, with no dependency on logprobs or on where the score sits in the output."""
    if spec.kind == "decision":
        return ProbabilityPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
    if streaming or endpoint == "analyze" or spec.policy == "ordinal":
        return OrdinalPolicy(spec.ordinal_t)
    return LabelLogprobPolicy(_min_p(spec), spec.directional_tau)
```

```typescript
import { render, screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react";

async function submit(user: UserEvent, url = FIXTURE_URL) {
  const input = screen.getByLabelText("Article URL");
  await user.clear(input);
  await user.click(input);
  await user.paste(url);
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: /^(Analyze|Restart)$/ }));
}

  within(select)
    .getAllByRole("option")
    .map((o) => o.textContent);

        bodies.signal = (await request.json()) as SignalBody;
        return HttpResponse.json(signalResponse(bodies.signal));
      }),
      http.post(`${API}/summary/stream`, async ({ request }) => {
        bodies.summary = (await request.json()) as SummaryBody;

    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent("Try the company press release instead.");
    expect(screen.getAllByRole("alert")).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(screen.getByText(/No signal: the request failed/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveTextContent("Failed");
  });

  it("aborts the previous run on resubmit and on cancel", async () => {
    const hold = gate();
    let calls = 0;
    server.use(
      http.post(`${API}/summary/stream`, async ({ request }) => {
        calls += 1;
        const chunks = summaryStreamChunks((await request.json()) as SummaryBody);
        if (calls > 1) return sseResponse(chunks);
        return sseResponse(
          (async function* () {
            yield chunks[0];
            yield chunks[2];
            await hold.promise;
            yield* chunks.slice(3);
          })(),
        );
      }),
    );
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<AnalyzeApp />);
    try {
      await submit(user);
      await waitFor(() =>
        expect(screen.getByTestId("summary-text")).toHaveTextContent(SUMMARY_CHUNKS[0].trim()),
      );

      await submit(user);
      await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId("summary-status")).toHaveTextContent("Complete"));
      hold.open();
      await tick();
      expect(screen.getByTestId("summary-text").textContent).toBe(SUMMARY_TEXT);
      expect(calls).toBe(2);
    } finally {
      hold.open();
    }

    const stuck = gate();
    server.use(
      http.post(`${API}/signal`, async () => {
        await stuck.promise;
        return HttpResponse.json(signalResponse());
      }),
    );
    try {
      await submit(user);
      await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }));
      expect(screen.getByText("Cancelled.")).toBeInTheDocument();
      stuck.open();
      await tick();
      expect(screen.queryByTestId("signal-badge")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    } finally {
      stuck.open();
    }
  });

  it("rejects a non-http URL without calling the API", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<AnalyzeApp />);
    await submit(user, "ftp://example.com/file");
    expect(screen.getByText(/Enter a full http\(s\) URL/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Article URL")).toHaveAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("summary-status")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

```
----
  the Apple GPU; a `bundled` CPU profile covers Linux and CI.
- **Precision first** (Q2): a wrong directional call costs a trade, a missed one little, so selection uses F0.5 macro
  over bullish and bearish with inversions capped at 2% ([04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#1-objective-and-metrics)).
- **Abstain rather than guess** (Q3): thresholds on decision-model class probabilities, on label-token probabilities
  (`/signal`, plus `directional_tau`) or on an ordinal -2..+2 score (`/analyze`, works mid-stream); every signal
  reports `abstained` and the threshold it was held to ([per model](#thresholds-and-no-signal)). The frozen
  defaults never abstain (dev300 coverage 100%): the 0.8B runs at `min_p` 0 with tau 0.28 and `/analyze` at
  \|s\| >= 1 on integer scores, so they hold back by answering neutral; only the 9B decision models abstain (dev300
  coverage 72.9% and 26.3%).
- **Split and combined, both served** (Q8): a fast signal model next to a summariser, or one model for score, entity
  and summary; the UI switches and both were measured ([05](.context/docs/design/05-latency.md#split-against-combined)).
- **The quick signal reads the lede** (Q4): headline plus opening paragraphs, body capped at 200 tokens; `/signal`
  answers in about 7 tokens, so prompt length is its latency.
- **Stream, sentiment first** (R3): the schema puts the score first and an incremental scanner emits it as it closes.
```

```
String: // Non-breaking, so a wrapped line never strands the sign away from its number.
const AT_LEAST = "≥ ";

/** The frozen rule this call was held to, in words; null for payloads that predate thresholds. */
export function thresholdText(signal: SignalResult): string | null {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  if (typeof threshold !== "number") return null;
  if (signal.policy === "ordinal") return `|score| ${AT_LEAST}${threshold}`;
  const hasTau = typeof tau === "number";
  if (threshold <= 0 && !hasTau) return "none (top class wins)";
  const base = threshold > 0 ? `call needs ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(threshold)}` : "top class wins";
  return hasTau
    ? `${base}; bullish/bearish called at ${AT_LEAST}${formatPct(tau)} even when neutral leads`
    : base;
}

/** Why the call abstained, with the numbers when the payload carries the threshold. */
export function abstainReason(signal: SignalResult): string {
  const { threshold, directional_tau: tau } = signal;
  const lean = leaning(signal);
  if (typeof threshold === "number") {
    if (signal.policy === "ordinal" && typeof signal.score === "number") {
      return `|score| ${Math.abs(signal.score)} (leaning ${capitalize(lean)}) is below this model's threshold of ${threshold}`;
    }
    const p = signal.probabilities?.[lean];
    if (typeof p === "number") {
      const reason = `the top class (${capitalize(lean)}, ${formatPct(p)}) is below this model's ${formatPct(threshold)} threshold`;
      // tau only rescues a neutral lead, so it is part of the reason only then.
      return lean === "neutral" && typeof tau === "number"
        ? `${reason}, and neither Bullish nor Bearish reached ${formatPct(tau)}`
        : reason;
    }
  }
(note: Edit also tried swapping \uXXXX escapes and their characters; neither form matched, so the mismatch is likely elsewhere in old_string. Re-read the file and copy the exact surrounding text.)
```

```diff
@@ -1 +1,17 @@+/** Decimals for the card's percentages: more than one only when a missed threshold or tau would print as met. */
+export function pctDigits(signal: SignalResult): number {
+  const probs = signal.probabilities;
+  if (!probs) return 1;
+  const lean = leaning(signal);
+  let digits = 1;
+  if (signal.abstained && typeof signal.threshold === "number") {
+    digits = missDigits(probs[lean] ?? 0, signal.threshold);
+  }
+  if (lean === "neutral" && signal.sentiment === "neutral" && typeof signal.directional_tau === "number") {
+    const side = Math.max(probs.bullish ?? 0, probs.bearish ?? 0);
+    digits = Math.max(digits, missDigits(side, signal.directional_tau));
+  }
+  return digits;
+}
+
 // Non-breaking, so a wrapped line never strands the sign away from its number.
```

```
export function SummaryPanel({
  status,
  text,
  truncated,
  model,
  streaming,
  firstTokenMs,
  coldStart,
  loadMs,
  modelAnswered = false,
}: SummaryPanelProps) {
  const active = status === "pending" || status === "streaming";
  const loading = coldStart === true && !modelAnswered;
  const footer: ReactNode[] = [];
  if (model) {
    footer.push(
      <>
        Model <code>{model}</code>
      </>,
    );
  }
  if (typeof firstTokenMs === "number") footer.push(`first token ${formatMs(firstTokenMs)}`);
  // While nothing has streamed yet the status line already says the model is loading.
  if (coldStart && (text || !active || !loading)) {
    footer.push(<span data-testid="summary-cold-start">cold start: {coldStartNote(loadMs)}</span>);
  }
  return (
    <section className={styles.panel} aria-labelledby="summary-heading" aria-busy={active}>
      <div className={styles.header}>
        <h2 id="summary-heading" className={styles.heading}>
```

```
### Thresholds and "No signal"

Confidence rules are frozen per model and endpoint. The served source of truth is
[`models.toml`](backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml) (`policy`, `min_p`, `directional_tau`, `ordinal_t`),
written by `veritrade_evals freeze`, with the evidence behind each value (dev300 and dev-article F0.5, inversions and
coverage at that threshold) in [`frozen.json`](evals/results/frozen.json); the policies are explained in
[04](.context/docs/design/04-evals.md#4-models-prompts-and-confidence-policies). Rules that `freeze` never wrote
keep provisional values and are marked as such. As served:

| Model | `/signal` rule | `/analyze` rule |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` (`/signal` default) | label-logprob, `min_p` 0, tau 0.28 | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 (provisional, never evaluated on `/analyze`) |
| `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | probability, `min_p` 0.80 | - |
| `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | probability, `min_p` 0.97 | - |
| `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` (`/analyze` default), `ministral-3:3b`, `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | - | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 |
| `qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M` (holdout quality ceiling, untuned) | - | ordinal, \|score\| >= 1 (provisional) |
| `tev1:0.8b-q8_0` (CI plumbing, never evaluated) | probability, `min_p` 0.50 (provisional) | - |

- **Where to see them**: the signal and analyze pickers in the UI, which also repeat the selected model's rule
  under the picker; the **Threshold** row on every signal card, plus threshold and tau marks on the probability
  bars when the call has them; `GET /api/models`, whose `signal_rules` maps each signal endpoint of a model to its
  `policy`, `threshold` and `directional_tau`; and every `signal` in a response, which carries the `threshold` and
  `directional_tau` it was held to. A label-logprob rule falls back to ordinal \|score\| >= 1 on a first-token label
  collision; `signal_rules` lists the primary rule.
- **"No signal" is an abstention, by design** (precision over recall, Q2 and Q3): when the winning class is below
  the model's frozen threshold, the service returns `sentiment: "neutral"` with `abstained: true` instead of a
  directional call it is not confident in. The UI shows **No signal** and says why, e.g. "Abstained: the top class
  (Bullish, 73.0%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold, so there is no directional call." A neutral with
  `abstained: false` is a neutral verdict. With these rules only the 9B decision models abstain (dev300 coverage
  72.9% for clef-flash, 26.3% for nimble), plus the CI plumbing model `tev1` below its provisional 0.50; the
  defaults hold back by answering neutral
  ([design decisions](#design-decisions)).
```

> **Where the thresholds are right now.** The UI doesn't show them anywhere yet.
> 
> - **`backend/src/veritrade/data/models.toml`** is what the service actually uses. The `freeze` step wrote these values:
> 
>   | Model | Endpoint | Rule |
>   |---|---|---|
>   | `clef-flash:9b-q8_0` | `/signal` | top-class probability ≥ 0.80, else abstain |
>   | `nimble:9b-q4_K_M` | `/signal` | probability ≥ 0.97 |
>   | `qwen3.5:0.8b-q8_0` | `/signal` | never abstains (`min_p` 0); a neutral lead becomes Bullish/Bearish once that side reaches 0.28 |
>   | All generative models | `/analyze` | score must be at least 1 on the -2..+2 scale (in practice they never abstain) |
> 
> - **`evals/results/frozen.json`** has the evidence behind each threshold (dev F0.5, inversion rate, coverage).
> - **`evals/results/selection/selection.md`** and **`holdout/holdout.md`** show them inline, e.g. "probability @ 0.8".
> 
> **Why I didn't put them in the UI:** I added the probability bars and the policy name to the card but not the cutoff the bars are judged against. Without it, the card can't explain its own decision. That was a gap on my part.
> 
> **What's being built now** (one workflow: backend, then frontend, then docs, then three independent reviewers, then a fixer, all on Opus):
> - **Thresholds on every signal card:** a "Threshold" line (e.g. "call needs ≥ 80.0%") and a marker on the probability bars at the cutoff.
> - **"No signal" instead of "Neutral + Abstained":** the pill reads "No signal" and the note gives the numbers, e.g. "the top class (Bullish, 73.0%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold".
> - **Thresholds in the model pickers:** each signal and analyze option shows its rule, e.g. `clef-flash:9b-q8_0 (p ≥ 0.80)`, so you can compare models before running one. `/api/models` returns these rules too.
> - **Cold-start detection:** the backend asks Ollama which models are loaded, in parallel with the article fetch, so it costs nothing extra when the article has to be downloaded. A model that isn't loaded, or is loaded with a different context size, counts as a cold start. The response timings and the stream's first event carry a `cold_start` flag.
> - **Cold starts in the UI:** "Time to signal" adds "cold start: model loaded for this request (X s)". While a stream waits on a cold model, the summary panel says the model is being loaded instead of a plain wait.
> - **Docs:** the README and the latency doc will say where thresholds live and what cold starts cost. The committed measurements are about 0.7-1.3 s for the small models and 5.4-6.2 s for the 10 GB `clef-flash`.
> 
> When the workflow finishes, I'll check the reviewers' findings, rebuild the app and test both cold and warm requests in the browser. Then I'll ask you before committing and pushing.

```python
"""Print the review-relevant parts of the thresholds/cold-start workflow result file."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

raw = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
data = json.loads(raw[raw.index("{") : raw.rindex("}") + 1])
data = data.get("result", data)

for key in ("fe", "docs"):
    part = data.get(key)
    print(f"== {key}")
    if not part:
        print("(empty)")
        continue
    print(part["summary"])
    print("-- checks:", part["checks"])
    for issue in part["open_issues"]:
        print("-- open:", issue)
    print()

print("== findings", len(data["findings"]))
for f in data["findings"]:
    print(f"- [{f['severity']}] ({f['lens']}) {f['file']}:{f.get('line', '?')} | {f['summary']}")
    print(f"    evidence: {f['evidence'][:400]}")

fix = data.get("fix")
print("\n== fix")
if fix:
    for p in fix["per_finding"]:
        print(f"- {p['outcome']}: {p['summary'][:120]} | {p['why'][:300]}")
    print("final check:", fix["final_check"])
    print("files:", fix["files_changed"])
else:
    print("(empty)")
```

> Thresholds and cold starts now show in the UI and the API. I tested them live on the rebuilt app; nothing is committed yet.
> 
> **Thresholds**
> - **Model pickers:** each option carries its rule, e.g. `clef-flash:9b-q8_0 (p ≥ 0.80)`, `nimble (p ≥ 0.97)`, `qwen3.5:0.8b (tau 0.28)`. A line under the picker repeats the selected model's rule, because a closed dropdown cuts it off.
> - **Signal card:** a "Threshold" line ("call needs ≥ 80.0%") and a marker on the probability bars at the cutoff.
> - **Abstained calls:** the pill now reads **No signal**, with a note giving the numbers, e.g. "the top class (Neutral, 63.3%) is below this model's 80.0% threshold, so there is no directional call".
> - **API:** every signal response includes `threshold` and `directional_tau`, and `/api/models` lists each model's rules.
> - **README:** a new "Thresholds and No signal" section has a table of every model's rule and points to `models.toml` and `frozen.json`.
> 
> **Cold starts**
> - **Detection:** the backend asks Ollama which models are loaded while the article is downloading. A model that isn't loaded, or is loaded with a different context size, is a cold start. If Ollama doesn't answer within 2 s, the flag is left empty and the request carries on.
> - **UI:** "Time to signal" gets a **Cold start** tag. While a cold model loads, the summary says "Loading the model into memory (cold start)...", and when it finishes it shows the load time.
> - **Docs:** the README and the latency doc explain the 30-minute keep-alive and quote the measured load costs.
> 
> **Live results** (no models loaded at the start):
> 
> | Request | Result |
> |---|---|

```
def views_code_only(command: str) -> bool:
    """A read-only `cat`/`head`/`sed -n` over source files shows code, whatever tags it contains."""
    if not VIEW_CMD_RE.match(command) or "http" in command:
        return False
    files = [Path(f) for f in FILE_TOKEN_RE.findall(command)]
    return bool(files) and all(f.suffix.lower() in CODE_SUFFIXES or f.name.startswith(".") for f in files)


def result_text(content: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return "\n".join(str(i.get("text", "")) for i in content if isinstance(i, dict))
    return ""


def omission_reason(info: ToolInfo | None, text: str) -> str | None:
    """Why a tool result must not be published, or None to keep it."""
    name = info.name if info else ""
    if info and info.flag:
        return info.flag
    if len(text) > HTML_MIN_CHARS and is_html(text) and not (info and info.code_file):
        return "html"
    if WEB_TOOL_RE.search(name) and len(text) > WEB_MIN_CHARS:
        return "web_fetch"
    if info and info.fetch_like and len(text) > WEB_MIN_CHARS:
        return "web_fetch"
    if name not in MODEL_AUTHORED_TOOLS and PRIVATE_CONTENT_RE.search(text):
        return "private_mention"
    return None


@dataclass
class FileContext:
    san: Sanitizer
    tools: dict[str, ToolInfo]


def export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    denylist = load_denylist(args.denylist)
    project_dir, sid = resolve_session(args.projects_root, args.session)
    print(f"session {sid}")
    staging: Path = args.staging
    reset_staging(staging)
    session_root = staging / "projects" / PROJECT_NAME
    export_dir = staging / "export"
    san, harvest = Sanitizer(denylist=denylist), Harvest()
    stage_session(project_dir, sid, session_root, san, harvest)
    meta = build_meta(harvest, san, sid)
    shutil.copytree(session_root, export_dir / "raw")
    if not args.no_render:
        render(session_root / f"{sid}.jsonl", export_dir / "rendered", staging / "ccl-cache.db")
        scrub_rendered(export_dir / "rendered", Sanitizer(denylist=denylist))
    else:
        (export_dir / "rendered").mkdir(parents=True)
    (export_dir / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", "utf-8")
    note = (args.out / NOTE_NAME).exists()
    (export_dir / "README.md").write_text(readme(meta, note=note), encoding="utf-8")
    records = meta["records"]
    print(f"records kept {records['kept_total']}, dropped {records['dropped_total']}")
    print("redactions " + json.dumps(meta["redactions"]))
    for path in sorted((export_dir / "rendered").glob("*")):
        print(f"rendered {path.name}: {path.stat().st_size / 1_048_576:.1f} MB")
    if report_gate(scan_paths(export_dir, denylist)):
        print(f"export kept in {export_dir}; nothing moved to {args.out}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    publish(export_dir, args.out)
    print(f"published to {args.out}")
    return 0


def main() -> None:
```

```
def reset_staging(staging: Path) -> None:
    if staging.exists():
        if any(staging.iterdir()) and not (staging / STAGING_MARKER).exists():
            sys.exit(f"refusing to clear {staging}: not an export staging dir (no {STAGING_MARKER})")
        shutil.rmtree(staging)
    staging.mkdir(parents=True)
    (staging / STAGING_MARKER).touch()


def publish(export_dir: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name in OUTPUT_NAMES:
        target = out / name
        if target.is_dir():
            shutil.rmtree(target)
        elif target.exists():
            target.unlink()
        shutil.move(str(export_dir / name), str(target))


def export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
```

```
def render(session_file: Path, out_dir: Path, cache: Path) -> None:
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    env = {**os.environ, "CLAUDE_CODE_LOG_CACHE_PATH": str(cache)}
    for fmt, name in (("html", "transcript.html"), ("md", "transcript.md")):
        cmd = ["uvx", RENDERER, str(session_file), "-o", str(out_dir / name), "-f", fmt, *RENDER_FLAGS]
        try:
            subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, env=env, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc:
            sys.exit(f"render failed ({' '.join(cmd[:2])} -f {fmt}): {exc}; staging kept for inspection")


def scrub_rendered(out_dir: Path, san: Sanitizer) -> None:
```

```
    dates = meta["date_range"]
    pointer = f"\nStart with [`{NOTE_NAME}`]({NOTE_NAME}), a note from Kris to the reviewers.\n"
    pointer = pointer if note else ""
    return f"""# AI conversation transcript

Exported from the Claude Code session that built this repo (`{meta["session_id"]}`,
{dates["start"]} to {dates["end"]}), including every subagent and workflow run it spawned.
{pointer}
## Contents

- `rendered/transcript.html`, `rendered/transcript.md`: readable render ({RENDERER}, depth `tool`).
- `raw/`: the filtered, redacted JSONL in the original session layout (main thread, `subagents/**`,
  `workflows/**`); re-renderable with claude-code-log.
- `meta.json`: harness version, models, effort and thinking settings, modes, skills, workflows,
  subagent counts, token usage, record counts and redaction counts.

## What was removed, and why

- Harness plumbing: API request records, file-history snapshots, prompt snapshots, hook output,
  environment, listing and delta attachments. Noise for a reader, and some of it holds private configuration.
- Private context: the author's global instruction file, account and session context, credential data,
  harness reminder blocks inside messages and tool results, skill instruction bodies, and the output of
  tool calls that read local configuration (Claude config dirs other than this session's plan file,
  SSH/git/editor/env files, other session logs, listings above the repo) which becomes
  `[omitted: private local config, sha256=<prefix>, <n> chars]`.
- Thinking-block signatures, images and documents.
- Third-party content: tool calls touching `{PRIVATE_DATA}/`, raw HTML pages over 2 KB and fetched web
  content over 4 KB become `[omitted: publisher/web content, sha256=<prefix>, <n> chars]`.
- Redactions: home paths become `~`; emails other than the author's public address become
  `[redacted-email]`; credential-shaped strings become `[redacted-secret]`; private terms become `[redacted]`.

## How it was produced

`uv run python scripts/export_transcript.py`: allowlist filter and redaction into a staging dir,
render with `uvx {RENDERER}`, then a leak gate over every output file (paths, emails, secrets,
private markers, size). Only a passing export is moved here. The final turns that ran this export
and pushed it are not included.
"""
```

```python
"""Bytes of the staged main-thread JSONL per UTC date and hour, to pick an HTML split point."""

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

by_hour: Counter[str] = Counter()
for line in Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    ts = json.loads(line).get("timestamp") or "unknown"
    by_hour[ts[:13]] += len(line.encode())
total = sum(by_hour.values())
running = 0
for hour in sorted(by_hour):
    running += by_hour[hour]
    print(f"{hour}  {by_hour[hour] / 1e6:6.2f} MB  cumulative {running / total:5.1%}")
```

```
def test_export_publishes_only_when_gate_passes(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    write_jsonl(tmp_path / "proj" / f"{SID}.jsonl", [user("u1", None, f"see {HOME}/repo")])
    args = argparse.Namespace(
        out=tmp_path / "out",
        staging=tmp_path / "staging",
        projects_root=tmp_path / "proj",
        session=SID[:8],
        denylist=tmp_path / "missing.txt",
        no_render=True,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(et, "scan_paths", lambda *_: ["raw/x.jsonl:1: email"])
    assert et.export(args) == 1
    assert not args.out.exists()

    monkeypatch.undo()
    assert et.export(args) == 0
    assert sorted(p.name for p in args.out.iterdir()) == ["README.md", "meta.json", "raw", "rendered"]
    meta = json.loads((args.out / "meta.json").read_text())
    assert meta["session_id"] == SID
    assert meta["records"]["kept"] == {"user": 1}
    assert et.scan_paths(args.out, []) == []
    assert "NOTE.md" not in (args.out / "README.md").read_text()
```
